title: Senior Manager, Fleet & Transit Maintenance
description:
Join Our Campus Community!

Thank you for your interest in joining the University of Wyoming. Our community thrives on the contributions of talented and driven individuals who share in our mission, vision, and values. If your expertise and experience align with the goals of our institution, we would be thrilled to hear from you. We encourage you to apply and become a valued member of our vibrant campus community today!

Why Choose Us?

At the University of Wyoming, we value our employees and invest in their success. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to support your health, financial security, and work-life balance. Benefits include:

  • Generous Retirement Contributions: The State contributes over 15% of your gross salary. With your mandatory employee contribution, the total contribution toward your retirement plan exceeds 19%.
  • Exceptional Health & Prescription Coverage: Enjoy access to medical, dental, and vision insurance with competitive employer contributions, that include 4 deductible options to suit your needs.
  • Paid Time Off: Benefit from ample vacation, sick leave, paid holidays, and paid winter closure.
  • Tuition Waiver: Employees and eligible dependents can take advantage of tuition waivers, supporting continuous education and professional growth.
  • Wellness and Employee Assistance Programs: Stay healthy with wellness initiatives, counseling services, and mental health resources.

At the University of Wyoming, we are committed to creating a supportive and enriching workplace. To learn more about what we offer, please refer to UW’s Benefits Summary.

JOB TITLE:

Senior Manager, Fleet & Transit Maintenance

JOB PURPOSE:

Manage the daily automotive and transit service operations and personnel functions of the University of Wyoming Transportation Services department. Provide maintenance and repair for university vehicles ensuring proper safe operation and availability.

This position has been deemed essential as addressed in the University of Wyoming’s Employee Handbook. Employees in essential positions may be required to work during emergency closures and winter closures based on the nature of their job duties and the reasons for the closure.

This position is grant funded and considered at-will employment.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Direct and coordinate daily fleet and transit maintenance operations and scheduling to ensure availability of vehicles and equipment.
  • Establish procedures, standards, and guidelines for the maintenance and repair of all automotive and bus related mechanical equipment.
  • Prepare and implement preventive maintenance schedules for all University buses and vehicles. Ensure transit preventive maintenance program meets all standards set by DOT, FTA, and other policies as required.
  • Inspect, test, diagnose, and repair diesel and/or gas vehicles and equipment. Inspect vehicle components, parts, and accessories to ensure safe operation that is compliant with all DOT, FTA, and ADA regulations. Adhere to safety and preventative maintenance standards and procedures.
  • Use Fleet Management software to maintain record-keeping systems to reflect activities with inspection, maintenance, and repair of vehicles and buses.
  • Control and analyze maintenance costs and/or repairs and provide expert recommendations.
  • Assist in preparing budgetary projections for maintenance and repair; monitor and analyze budget vs. actuals.
  • Develop and maintain quality relationships with vendors and third-party services.
  • Prepare and maintain all work orders, defect reports, and warranty claims. Provide regular reports to management on repair and maintenance costs, miles, hours, etc. Perform associated accounting duties as required.
  • Oversee shop safety to ensure accident and incident-free environment and clean working conditions.
  • Supervise support staff including making hiring recommendations, training, evaluating, advising, and assisting with corrective action process.
  • Oversee operations of the University’s onsite fueling stations and resolve systems problems.

SUPPLEMENTAL FUNCTIONS:

  • Participate in performance-related goal setting and planning to meet personal and organizational goals and objectives.
  • Assist Assistant Director in preparing vehicle purchase specifications.
  • Serve as a member of various committees as required.
  • Assist with procurement and developing equipment specifications.
  • Travel occasionally as related to vehicle breakdowns, handle after-hours, out-of-town emergency breakdowns, and conferences/meetings.

COMPETENCIES:

  • Attention to Detail
  • Safety Awareness
  • Delegating Responsibility
  • Teamwork
  • Service Orientation
  • Work Prioritization & Management
  • Technical/Professional Knowledge
  • Judgment
  • Analysis/Problems Identification
  • Stress Tolerance

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

Education: Vocational School, On-the-Job Experience, or Associate’s degree

Experience: 5 years work-related experience

Required licensure, certification, registration, or other requirements:

  • Requires ASE Certifications in Medium/Heavy Truck and/or ASE Transit Bus
  • Valid Wyoming driver's license with a motor vehicle record (MVR) compliant with the Driving for University Business SAP.
  • Must be able to obtain a Wyoming commercial driver's license (CDL) after employment (within one year).
  • Must be able to pass all drug and/or alcohol screening(s) required by the UW Drug and Alcohol Policy .
  • 3-5 years of supervisory experience
  • 3-5 years of budget and expenditure experience

Experience Evaluation

Minimum experience requirements are evaluated on a full-time equivalent (FTE) basis. Relevant part-time experience will be prorated based on hours worked. For example, two years working an average of 20 hours per week is equivalent to approximately one year of full-time experience.

Applicants must include the average hours worked per week for all current and previous positions. Failure to provide this information may affect the evaluation of qualifications.

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Advanced knowledge of fleet and transit work order systems.
  • Advanced knowledge of OEM diagnostic and service software.
  • Experience developing reports and maintaining operational records.
  • Experience supervising and training employees.
  • Ability to provide a high level of customer service and support.
  • Ability to work effectively under limited supervision.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills and the ability to work effectively in a team environment.
  • Effective decision-making and problem-solving skills.
  • Strong time-management and organizational skills.
  • Experience managing parts, tires, bulk fuel, and lubricants.
  • Experience managing tools, shop equipment, and inventory, including inventory control and accountability.

REQUIRED APPLICATION MATERIALS:

Complete the online application. The department additionally requests candidates upload the following document(s) for a complete application:

  1. Cover letter
  2. Resume or C.V.
  3. Contact information for four work-related references (references will only be contacted if you are selected as a finalist for the position).

This position will remain open until filled. Complete applications received by 11/15/2026 will receive full consideration.

WORK LOCATION:

On-Campus: This position provides vital support to campus customers, and the successful candidate must be available to work and perform essential job functions on campus, understanding our location is at 7,220 feet above sea level.

WORK AUTHORIZATION REQUIREMENTS:

The successful candidate must be eligible to work in the United States, as sponsorship for any work authorization or work visas is not available for this position.

HIRING STATEMENT/EEO:

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran. In compliance with the ADA Amendments Act (ADAAA), if you have a disability and would like to request an accommodation to apply for a position, please contact us at 307-766-2377 or email jobapps@uwyo.edu.

ABOUT LARAMIE:

The University of Wyoming is located in Laramie, a charming town of 30,000 residents nestled in the heart of the Rocky Mountain West. The state of Wyoming continues to invest in its only 4-year university, helping to make it a leader in academics, research, and outreach with state-of-the-art facilities and strong community ties. We invite you to learn more about Laramie by visiting the About Laramie website.

Located in a high mountain valley near the Colorado border, Laramie offers both outstanding recreational opportunities and close proximity to Colorado’s Front Range and the metropolitan Denver area. Laramie’s beautiful mountain landscape offers outdoor enjoyment in all seasons, with over 300 days of sunshine annually. For more information about the region, please visit

title: Habitat Restoration Officer
description:
• Job grade: Executive Officer
  • Contract type: Fixed term

Location

The King’s House, Lyndhurst, Hampshire

About the job

Job summary

What you’ll do

The successful candidate will join the Higher-Level Stewardship (HLS) project team based in the New Forest. The team plans and delivers landscape-scale habitat restoration projects with external funding from the New Forest HLS scheme. The Verderer’s of the New Forest HLS scheme is focused on restoring and enhancing internationally-important habitats, renowned for their flora and fauna, and covering around 20,000 hectares. As a Habitat Restoration Officer you will play a vital role in planning and overseeing our habitat restoration projects.

Please see the job description below for more information and details about what we need from you.

Where you’ll work…

Based at The King’s House, Lyndhurst, Hampshire, SO43 7NH in the South District team.

Our South England Forest District team is made up of around 160 people, containing a diverse range of roles - from wildlife rangers and ecologists to marketing professionals, we all contribute towards the management of 46,000 hectares (ha) of public forest estate and national parks that stretch from Sussex to Dorset, and from Berkshire to the Isle of Wight.

Much of this forest is of high national importance for nature conservation and wildlife, and of international importance for biodiversity. South England Forest District is therefore responsible for land that includes Special Areas of Conservation (SACs), Special Protection Areas (SPAs), Ramsar sites, Areas of Outstanding National Beauty (AONB) and sites of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI).

Job description

Key responsibilities & accountabilities

The following provides an overview of the key responsibilities of the role. This list is not exhaustive, and additional duties may be assigned as required, consistent with the nature and level of the post

1. Plan work programmes to restore internationally important habitats in the New Forest by carrying out fieldwork and preparing practical plans to deliver works, including wetland and river restoration and terrestrial restoration work including tree felling, scrub removal, and ridge and furrow removal. This will include:

• Reviewing and updating HLS team databases to identify priorities for restoration.
• Carrying out walkover surveys to assess restoration work requirements.
• Preparing practical habitat restoration plans.
• Identifying constraints and implementing appropriate mitigation.

2. Engage with our staff and stakeholders, including leading consultation site visits, to get agreement for restoration proposals and to manage site-specific constraints (physical, ecological, archaeological etc):

• Work collaboratively across the HLS and Wider FE teams to integrate restoration work with other operational priorities.
• Liaise with Forestry England colleagues to guide the production of restoration Operational Site Assessments (OSAs).
• Engage with other stakeholders (e.g., Natural England, New Forest National Park Authority, EA, CDA, Verderers, etc.) on restoration proposals and secure approval to enable delivery of the HLS works programme.
• Work with the HLS Engagement Officer to engage with stakeholders such as Parish Councils, local landowners and other interested parties.

3. Deliver restoration projects on the ground by setting up and managing contracts, providing site-specific technical advice and liaising with contractors to ensure restoration is undertaken to agreed specifications with high standards of safety:

  • Follow procurement protocols to set up and manage contracts for the HLS programme of restoration projects.
  • Ensure contractors have the necessary information to undertake contracts safely, including all constraints maps and H&S documentation.
  • With guidance from the HLS Ecologist, communicate ecological constraints to contractors (toolbox talks, maps, pre-commencement meetings).
  • Liaise with contractors throughout the delivery phase and ensure restoration is undertaken to agreed specifications.

4. Report progress and monitor outcomes of habitat restoration projects:

• Update HLS team databases to enable accurate auditing and reporting.
• Report on progress quarterly to HLS Project Manager for updates to the HLS Board.
• Work with the HLS Communications Officer to keep relevant pages of the HLS website up to date.
• Provide verbal updates on work programmes at HLS team meetings and New Forest Operations meetings.
• Contribute to evaluating restoration effectiveness and recommend adjustments to future work proposals or methods.

5. Line management responsibilities

• This is a management role and, as such, there may be opportunities in the future to undertake line management responsibilities, including the supervision of a Works Supervisor and/or Volunteer Ranger.

And any other tasks, reasonably requested by your line manager.

Person specification

Skills, knowledge & experience

Essential professional and technical experience

• Experience working in the environmental management sector.
• Sound knowledge and understanding of delivering habitat restoration work within designated sites.
• Demonstrable experience in planning and delivering habitat restoration projects.
• Experience engaging with local stakeholder groups, including: landowners; non-governmental organisations; charities; local government.
• Experience in contract management.
• An effective communicator, both written and verbally.
• Competent in IT – Microsoft Office suite including Outlook, Word, Excel and Powerpoint.
• Sound knowledge of the application of environmental legislation to project planning and delivery.

Desirable

• Experience delivering river or wetland restoration.
• Knowledge of river and wetland ecology, hydrology and restoration techniques.
• Experience working within a designated site.
• Experience of budget management.
• Experience supervising or mentoring staff, volunteers or contractors.
• An understanding and knowledge of the New Forest and its habitats.
• Sound knowledge of the application of environmental legislation to project planning and delivery.

Qualifications

Essential

title: Associate Corporate Knowledge Information Manager

description:
• Job grade: Executive Officer
  • Contract type: Permanent
  • Business area: CPS - HQ Digital Information Directorate (DID)
  • Type of role: Digital, Knowledge and Information Management
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time, Job share, Part-time
  • Number of jobs available: 1

Location

This post can be based in any location within England and Wales where a Crown Prosecution Service office is located. You are expected to travel to Crown Prosecution Service locations as part of this role, based on business needs. The Crown Prosecution Service is a Disability Confident employer and all reasonable adjustments are considered in line with Equality Act of 2010.

About the job

Job summary

As a Corporate Knowledge & Information Manager (CKIM) practitioner, you contribute towards the Departments compliance with its obligations under the Data Protection Act 2018, UK GDPR, Freedom of Information Act 2000 (FOI) and the Public Records Act 1958.

Working with CKIM team leaders, you ensure that data processing operations are sufficiently transparent to meet statutory obligations and the expectations of the wider pubic

You work with Digital teams to ensure the development of new technologies and services are DPA, UK GDPR and DRA compliant.

You prepare and make recommendations on the disclosure of information for Right of Access Requests and FOI requests. You prepare reports to demonstrate compliance and performance against standards.

You provide advice and guidance to the organisation in respect of information handling, information lifecycle management, records retention and the interpretation of policy.

The Crown Prosecution Service is based in England and Wales. If you’re applying for this role and live in Scotland or Northern Ireland, you must let us know when accepting this offer as you need permission to work from your home address if hybrid working is part of your role. There’s no guarantee that we will grant this approval.

You must be aged 16 or over at the point of starting in this role. The expected start date is approximately 8–12 weeks after the application closing date. You are expected to commence employment as soon as possible following the expiry of your notice period. Requests for significantly later start dates may not be accommodated.

Job description

Your roles and responsibilities:

  • Working to the CKIM Manager, you have an important role in ensuring the delivery of CKIM services; with an understanding of information compliance principles and the statutory requirements of the Data Protection Act 2018 (DPA 2018), UK GDPR, Freedom of Information Act 2000 and the Public Records Act 1958 you are able to demonstrate how you have been able to contribute to departmental compliance.
  • You are able to use your skills and experience to review requests for information in order to advise on the disclosure/sharing of information. You are able to effectively explain the principles of information management best practice to internal and external stakeholders.
  • You are able to produce accurate and timely reports as directed by your manager, to demonstrate team performance and compliance with CPS data management objectives and legal compliance standards.
  • You provide up to date advice to CPS staff in relation to information management compliance or be able to direct them to the most appropriate subject matter expert.
  • You respond to requests for information and triage emails for the team mailboxes and will support the team in the planning, organisation and delivery of various governance and community of interest groups.

A copy of the full job description is attached.

Person specification

To be eligible to apply, you need:

  • working knowledge of DPA, GDPR, FOIA or PRA an advantage.
  • experience working with Excel.
  • experience working with PDF.

Behaviours

We'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:

  • Managing a Quality Service
  • Making Effective Decisions
  • Communicating and Influencing

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £31,840, Crown Prosecution Service contributes £9,224 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

Join the Crown Prosecution Service and find your purpose.

The Crown Prosecution Service is passionate about ensuring that we're a top performing organisation and a great place to work. We're a committed equal opportunities employer, creating a culture where you can bring your whole self to work, and individuality is truly appreciated.

This culture of inclusion is underpinned by our staff networks covering disability, faith and belief, LGBTQI+, race, social mobility alongside our mental health first aiders programme and wellbeing sessions.

The Crown Prosecution Service commits to offer its employees the following experience.

  • You can do impactful, purposeful work that’s making a difference to your local communities.
  • You are able to learn and grow, with access to the right opportunities and resources.
  • We care about your wellbeing.
  • We want you to feel valued, trusted and included.

We also offer the following range of benefits:

  • Civil Service contributory pension of up to 28.9%
  • 25 days’ leave, increasing to 30 days after 5 years
  • £350 each year to spend on personal development
  • lawyer training programme for all new prosecutors
  • an extra privilege day to mark the King's birthday
  • competitive maternity, paternity and parental leave
  • flexible working including flexitime, and a family friendly approach to work
  • Cycle2Work scheme, employee savings.

Diversity at the Crown Prosecution Service is about inclusion, embracing differences and ensuring our workforce truly reflects the communities we serve. We want you to feel that you belong and can thrive, whatever your background, identity or culture. As a Disability Confident employer, we're happy to support requests for reasonable adjustments and improve your recruitment experience. If you'd like any reasonable adjustments made to our recruitment process, let us know within your application or contact dimitra.siakavara@cps.gov.uk

The Crown Prosecution Service has fixed rates for its Executive Officer grade – a developing rate (the starting salary) and a spot rate (the maximum salary). Applicants typically join us on the developing rate and, after completing a 15-month development period, move to the spot rate if your line manager confirms you’re performing the role to a satisfactory standard.

If you’re joining the Crown Prosecution Service on a lateral transfer from another government department, you should contact us about the impact on your salary and the implications of any time you’ve already spent at that grade before applying or accepting an employment offer. Your salary may be adjusted if your location changes when you join us. This adjustment also takes into account any existing allowances that may have previously been consolidated into your basic pay – there’s no guarantee that you can retain these when you transfer.

We want to ensure our employees can thrive at work and home and offer a range of support to achieve a balance. This includes flexibility of working hours, flexibility to support caring responsibilities and a flexible approach to deployment. We offer a hybrid working policy. You must spend at least 40% of your contracted hours over a four-week period at court, in an office or another official workplace depending on business need and the kind of work you're doing.

Things you need to know

Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Selection process details

This vacancy is using Success Profiles (opens in a new window), and will assess your Behaviours, Strengths and Experience.

Recruitment process

The recruitment process consists of an online application and interview.

Personal statement

We ask you to complete a personal statement of no more than 750 words. You need to address the core behaviours for this role, which are:

  1. Managing a Quality Service (Lead Behaviour)
  2. Making Effective Decisions
  3. Communicating and Influencing

You also need to demonstrate the following experience required for this role:

  • working knowledge of DPA, GDPR, FOIA or PRA an advantage.
  • experience working with Excel.
  • experience working with PDF.

In addition, you need to demonstrate the Crown Prosecution Service or Civil Service values.

The panel has the right to assess the lead behaviour ‘Managing a Quality Service’ first. If the standard on this behaviour isn’t met, the other behaviours won’t be considered and your application won’t progress. The panel also has the right to raise the minimum standard pass mark. The panel may also refer to the lead behaviour at the interview stage to determine merit order.

CV

You’re not required to upload your CV. However, when submitting your application there is a ‘CV section’. You are required to provide information about your employment and/or academic history for the past three years. The CV section will be used as supporting evidence, it won’t be assessed.

It’s your responsibility to provide the specified information in the requested format to ensure that you're considered for the post.

If you're unable to cover three years through employment or academic history, you must provide a character reference for clearance purposes.

description:

About the job

Job summary

At DSIT we’re all about improving people’s lives by maximising the potential of science & technology.

We accelerate innovation, investment and productivity through world-class science, research and development.

We use technology for good by ensuring new and existing technologies are safely developed and deployed across the UK, with the benefits more widely shared.

We are driving forward a modern digital government which gives citizens a more satisfying experience and their time back.

We do all this to enable the Government’s 5 national missions: kickstarting economic growth, making Britain a clean energy superpower, taking back our streets, breaking down barriers to opportunity and building an NHS fit for the future.

Above all, we focus on improving people’s lives. Whether it’s researching new treatments for disease, developing better batteries, reducing burdens through better public services, keeping children safe online, and much more, outcomes for citizens are at the heart of what we do.

Our Inclusive Environment

We offer flexible working benefits, employee well-being support and a great pension. We are enormously proud to be a Disability Confident Leader employer. We support candidates with adjustments throughout our recruitment process. Information about disability confidence and just some examples of the adjustments that you can request can be found in the reasonable adjustment section below.

Please note

Former DSIT recruitment campaigns are continuing as usual, but candidates should be aware that following the Government’s announcement on the changes to some civil service departments, roles will be subject to the machinery of government moves and will ultimately be in one of the new departments. We will provide more information if you are selected for a role. This work remains of high importance to the civil service, and we thank you for your continued interest.

Job description

Role Overview

An excellent opportunity to join a unique, high-performing early-stage deep technology investment fund deploying up to £100m per annum within an exceptional National Security and Defence (NS&D) mission and values aligned culture.

As an Investment Manager, you will play a prominent role in the NSSIF investment team, working closely with the Senior Investment Partners and Analysts across core investment activities, owning the origination, evaluation, execution and management of investment opportunities. You will be part of a growing team that helps NSSIF identify and invest in cutting-edge technology capabilities aligned to HMG priorities.

About NSSIF

The National Security Strategic Investment Fund (NSSIF) is the UK’s Government’s dual-use deep-tech corporate venture capital fund for National Security and Defence (NS&D).

NSSIF’s mission is to ensure the UK NS&D community can access and adopt the most innovative technology at pace and scale, delivering strategic advantage to the UK as well as protecting the UK's security. We invest to accelerate UK NS&D’s access to cutting edge capability, nurture conversancy and alignment in the VC ecosystem with NS&D priorities, and provide value for UK taxpayers. NSSIF is differentiated by its unique end user and mission partner network, providing a direct link between early-stage tech teams and national security and defence missions.

NSSIF drives impact through:

- Direct investment into pioneering deep tech companies, predominantly UK based
- Indirect (LP) investment in relevant early stage and growth venture capital funds
- Delivering work programmes to end users across NS&D to accelerate technology readiness and provide insight across government.

Building on impressive performance, NSSIF is now scaling up to deploy up to £100m per annum. We have a direct portfolio of nearly 35 companies across AI, quantum, space and emerging technology, have to date have invested in 6 companies which have gone on to achieve unicorn status, and have achieved three exits. We have invested in over 20 other fund managers through our indirect investments, and enabled over 50 work programmes, 41% of which have resulted in contracts with NS&D customers.

NSSIF is a partnership between the NS&D community and the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT) that supports national security, accelerates technology development across DSIT’s frontier technologies and beyond, and drives growth in the UK economy. NSSIF investments are made through British Technologies Investments Limited (BTIL).

You can find more on NSSIF’s website www.nssif.gov.uk.

Person specification

1) Venture investment. Lead end-to-end direct investment activity within one or more of NSSIF’s technology themes, from origination through execution.
a) Engage across the dual-use technology ecosystem, including start ups, accelerators, incubators, universities and research organisations, to identify emerging technologies and investment opportunities.
b) Drive the development and triage of a pipeline of opportunities, leading investment evaluation and development of investment case papers for submission to the Investment Committee.
c) Support deal execution and syndicate engagement, working closely with co‑investors and counterparties.

2) Portfolio management and reporting. Be responsible for portfolio monitoring activities, tracking performance, strategic outcomes and portfolio data.
a) Monitor and analyse portfolio company performance, tracking progress against milestones and supporting companies through follow‑on financing, strategic inflection points and exit processes.
b) Own the capture and maintenance of portfolio performance data within the CRM, ensuring timely, accurate inputs to underpin internal reporting, external assurance and valuation activity.

3) External engagement and events. Engage externally on behalf of NSSIF to strengthen relationships with accredited fund managers and dual-use companies.
a) Attend key events, forums and industry engagements with a focus on building awareness of NSSIF’s mandate and investment approach.
b) Engage regularly with accredited fund managers and co‑investors to understand emerging market trends, technologies and deal-flow they are seeing.
c) Track and synthesise market insights from fund manager and event engagement, proactively flagging companies and themes of interest to support NSSIF pipeline development and connectivity across syndicates.

4) Market intelligence and insight. Build understanding of the dual‑use innovation landscape through market research, technology scouting and structured insight.
a) Develop and maintain an informed view of technology landscapes, market dynamics and investment trends across NSSIF priority sectors, drawing on external engagements and independent research.
b) Work closely with the NSSIF Insight function to support insight commissions that inform investment decision‑making, including contributing market perspectives, shaping research questions and translating findings into investment‑relevant outputs.
c) Capture and disseminate market intelligence and insights through NSSIF’s CRM, insight reports and shared team knowledge base.

5) Strategy formulation. Drive the evolution of NSSIF’s Investment Strategy, informing portfolio construction and exit considerations.

This is an outline description of the key responsibilities and accountabilities involved in the job. It is not exhaustive and aspects of the role may be revised/developed from time to time.

Essential Criteria

Essential:

· Experience of diligence, execution and management of VC direct investment deals.
· Excellent communications skills, and comfortable with public speaking.
· Highly collaborative and professional, with high integrity.
· Adaptable skill set which can be deployed across the NSSIF team as needed.
· Team-player and able to build excellent long-term relationships.
· Effective prioritisation skills and problem-solving capabilities.
· Able to deal with ambiguity and uncertainty.
· Strong analytical, strategic planning, and decision-making skills.
· Strategic thinker with the ability to balance risk management and early-stage investing.

Desirable Criteria

• Experience of working in UK NS&D and/or HMG environments.
• Experience of working with deep technologies, particularly in a technical role.
• Existing network of venture capital fund manager and wider ecosystem relationships.
• Experience of conducting early-stage investing.
• Experience of M&A and or other deep technology exits.
• Formal qualifications relevant to deep technology and or venture investing.

Behaviours:

• Ability to deliver results over the long term and see projects through
• Highly collaborative, with an open approach
• Highly professional, high integrity
• Self-starter, able to work effectively without close supervision
• Ability to produce effective reports and presentations

NSSIF offers flexible working arrangements, with the NSSIF office in central London.

About the job

Job summary

Information about the Command

The Strategy Directorate drives NCA strategic mission through rigorous intelligence insights, performance insights, risk management and communications. We shape priorities and build influence across government, law enforcement and the public.

Information about the Business Area

Communications plays a vital role in promoting and supporting NCA activity. We use our communications channels as an operational tool to disrupt serious and organised crime. Communications manage the Agency relationship with media outlets and journalists, issuing media releases and statements as well as interviews with Agency spokespersons. The team commission targeted audience research, developing, implementing, and evaluating marketing strategies for awareness raising or behaviour change. Communications lead a range of projects, channels and events to increase leadership visibility and boost Officer engagement.

Job description

The Senior Press Officer role provides an exciting opportunity to join the NCA’s high performing Communications Team.

You will use your knowledge of the media and skills as a professional communicator to build public and partner awareness of serious and organised crime, and confidence in the NCA’s response. Your work will also help to build the Agency’s intelligence picture of the most serious and complex crime threats facing the UK, and to disrupt the criminals presenting the greatest risk.


This is a full time role but we can consider flexibility in working hours to support a work-life balance that can be discussed upon offer

Role Description

The role of senior press officer is to engage with the media to inform the public and other identified audiences about the work of the NCA, to protect and improve our reputation, while also supporting the NCA’s mission of protecting the public from serious and organised crime.

As part of the wider communications team within the NCA’s Strategy Directorate, the press office is responsible for handling reactive queries from the media as well as proactive communications to promote the work of the Agency.

The Communications Team, which includes media, digital, internal comms, and campaigns specialists, work closely together and with a variety of internal and external partners to land our messages with target audiences.

The team’s activity has contributed directly to the capture of wanted international fugitives, the safeguarding of vulnerable people, and widespread public action to mitigate crime threats.


Duties & Responsibilities

Promote the NCA - Showcase the NCA’s unique role in UK law enforcement by delivering engaging, proactive stories on NCA activity, and working up ideas for content that supports communication objectives.

Professionalism - Provide a professional service for journalists by managing high-profile and sensitive media issues and answering enquiries in a timely and informative manner, including on an out-of-hours rotational basis.

Advise NCA officers on the media - Become a trusted source of communications support and counsel for NCA officers.

Build knowledge of the NCA - Develop expertise on the NCA’s wide remit and range of functions.

Engage across communications disciplines - Work with expert colleagues across the communications team – including digital, internal and campaigns - to share knowledge and maximise the impact of content across all audiences.

Build relationships - Develop and nurture excellent relationships with journalists and contacts (e.g. bloggers) in all forms of media, to improve story placement and check progress.

Media handling - Demonstrate techniques and strategies for handling journalists, respond quickly to media requests and agree points of escalation.

Audience - Understand how to optimise audience reach through a mix of media channels.

Person specification

Skills, Knowledge and Experience

Insight - Use insight to identify target audiences and stakeholders, support decision making and help inform the overall communication approach.

Engaging your audience - Communicate in a succinct and engaging manner using appropriate styles, methods and timing, including digital channels, to maximise understanding and impact to a range of stakeholders.

Communication skills - Demonstrate an ability to express ideas effectively, flexibly and creatively, both verbally and with strong writing skills, to develop innovative solutions.

Processing information - Demonstrate an ability to process complex information to produce effective content or recommendations.

Experience - Demonstrate solid experience of working in a busy press office or other news-focused environment where you used your communicating and influencing skills to deliver at pace while demonstrating awareness of the bigger picture.

On-call working

Officers take part in the on‑call rota covering evenings and weekends, with an allowance paid per session and enhanced pay for any work undertaken (x1.5 weekdays, x2 weekends).

Desirable criteria are only used for assessment in the event of a tie break.

Industry recognised communication qualification (such as CIPR) or equivalent

Experience of working in a busy press office or an equivalent track record of being able to multitask in a fast paced role that requires engaging with external stakeholders about the organisations' work.

title: Health Economist
description:
• Job grade: Senior Executive Officer
  • Contract type: Permanent, Loan, Secondment

Location

London (Canary Wharf)

About the job

Job summary

As an economist in UKHSA, you will be building the economic evidence base for the agency as well as the organisation’s economics capability. The role provides a great opportunity to develop and apply analytical skills, support evidence-based decision-making on critical health priorities and shape the organisation’s culture around the use of economics.

You will work with other experts (epidemiologists, data scientists and public health experts) to assess current and future economic costs and benefits of preparing for and responding to health threats and hazards and to help build our understanding of how health security interacts with the wider economy.

You will develop these cost and benefit estimates often either through literature reviews or your own primary research, including research using large-scale data assets held by UKHSA such as hospital records or microbiology results. Where needed, you will be supported through formal learning opportunities to develop data analysis skills, including programming or use of AI.

You will then incorporate these into economic evaluations for potential interventions as well as other ad-hoc pieces of work to support decision-making. Depending on the project, you may apply data analysis methods (including econometrics) as well as professional Government analytical standards, such as Green Book or Aqua Book.

Working for your organisation

We pride ourselves as being an employer of choice, where Everyone Matters promoting equality of opportunity to actively encourage applications from everyone, including groups currently underrepresented in our workforce.

UKHSA ethos is to be an inclusive organisation for all our staff and stakeholders. To create, nurture and sustain an inclusive culture, where differences drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our workforce and wider communities. We do this through celebrating and protecting differences by removing barriers and promoting equity and equality of opportunity for all.

Please visit our careers site for more information

Job description

You will be open to learning more about public health from other experts while demonstrating the value that economics can bring to public health questions. You will need to develop clear high-quality analysis and communicate it to a senior audience. As a small team, there will be some flexibility in the work undertaken but this also comes with the ability for the post-holder to shape the role towards their interests. However, the type of work you can expect to lead and support on includes:

  • Leading thinking on how health interventions impact health security and the economy, how we should assess associated costs and benefits to society and developing the evidence base for informing policymaking.
  • Producing cost-benefit, cost-effectiveness analysis and other economic outputs to guide UKHSA decision-making in policy-making, implementing interventions or supporting other bodies in their decision-making.
  • Developing robust economic cases, using the latest evidence for key UKHSA projects and programmes.
  • Developing the agency’s economic capacity

Your main responsibilities will include:

  1. Provide analysis and insight: You will apply economic techniques to estimate, analyse and communicate the costs of interventions or health threats to the UK. This includes carrying out cost-benefit, cost-of-illness and cost-effectiveness analysis, but may also extend to ad-hoc pieces of work to support decision-making. You are open to learning more about health security, climate threats and public health in general from other experts while demonstrating the value of economics. You will need to develop clear high-quality analysis, make recommendations and communicate effectively to a variety of audiences, including senior audiences.
  2. Lead a research programme. You will apply existing methods and identify new approaches to provide insight to difficult health questions. You will demonstrate an ability to manage projects and stakeholders across an organisation, and bring a strong intellectual curiosity with an interdisciplinary approach. There will be scope for the postholder to shape this work according to their interest, while also meeting the likely future demands of the organisation. It could include looking at how health security interacts with the wider economy or looking at new ways to value resilience.
  3. Build the Economic profession at UKHSA: All the while, you will be at the forefront of building the role and reputation of the economic profession within UKHSA in general, and providing leadership on economics. Working with experts across multiple fields, you will showcase the value of economics to all colleagues as well as contributing to building an inclusive and welcoming community of economics.

Recent project examples for the team include:

  • Estimating the burden and cost of infections and infectious diseases on NHS hospitals from routine administrative data
  • Supporting the Agency during Spending Review through developing evidence on the Agency’s Value for Money
  • Preparing a business case for pandemic preparedness to support allocation of resources.

In addition, you will also be central to building our understanding of how infectious disease and other hazards interact with the wider healthcare system and economy. You will support the Agency’s and Cabinet Office’s Risk Assessments and planning by estimating the potential economic impact of different health threats. Finally, as UKHSA has a responsibility to respond to mitigate the impact of health security threats, you may also feed into responses in the event of major public health incidents.

This is not an exhaustive list.

Person specification

Essential criteria

  • A first or second class honours degree in economics or related field (or equivalent qualification); or a postgraduate degree in a relevant numerate discipline (or equivalent qualification)
  • Ability to effectively communicate the results of analysis to senior stakeholders and decision makers
  • Good interpersonal skills and the ability to develop and maintain key stakeholder relationships
  • Excellent presentation skills

Desirable criteria

  • Knowledge of health economics and experience in applying it to provide insight into health problems.
  • Ability to work at pace to deadlines across multiple projects
  • Experience with developing Green Book-compliant business cases including knowledge of best practice.
  • Experience in cost-benefit and cost-effectiveness analysis, particularly relating to health interventions

Please note that for roles where specific qualifications or registrations are required, successful applicants will be asked to provide appropriate evidence. Employment cannot commence until satisfactory documentation has been received and verified.

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £46,310, UK Health Security Agency contributes £13,416 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).
  • Learning and development tailored to your role
  • An environment with flexible working options
  • A culture encouraging inclusion and diversity
  • A Civil Service pension with an employer contribution of 28.97%

This role is offered under Agenda for Change (AFC) Terms and Conditions. If you are already on AFC T&Cs or accept the role on a fixed-term contract, you will be enrolled in the NHS Pension Scheme or keep your current AFC Pension. If you take the role on a loan or temporary promotion, you will retain your existing substantive T&Cs. If the role is available under either AFC or Civil Service T&Cs depending on your registration, your pension scheme will align accordingly.

Things you need to know

Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Selection process details

This vacancy will be assessed using a competency-based framework which will assess your qualifications, knowledge and experience and / or skills and abilities outlined in the essential criteria.

Stage 1: Application & Sift

You will be required to complete an application form. You will be assessed on the listed 4 essential criteria, and this will be in the form of:

  • an application form (‘Employer/ Activity history’ section on the application)
  • a 1000 word supporting statement.

This should outline how you consider your skills, experience and knowledge provide evidence of your suitability for the role, with reference to the essential criteria.

You will receive a joint score for your application form and statement. (The application form is the kind of information you would put into your C.V –please be advised you will not be able to upload your CV. Please complete the application form in as much detail as possible). Please do not email us your CV.

Healthjobs UK has a word limit of 1500, but your supporting statement must be no more than 1000 words. We will not consider any words over 1000 words.

Longlisting: In the event of a large number of applications we will longlist into 3 piles of:

  • Meets all essential criteria
  • Meets some essential criteria
  • Meets no essential criteria

If used, the pile ‘Meets all essential criteria’ will proceed to shortlisting.

Shortlisting: In the event of a large number of applications we will shortlist on:

Desirable criteria may be used in the event of a large number of applications / large amount of successful candidates.

We offer great flexible working opportunities at UKHSA and operate using a hybrid working model where business needs allow. This provides us with greater flexibility about how and where we work, to get the best from our workforce. As a hybrid worker, you will be expected to spend a minimum of 60% of your contractual working hours (approximately 3 days a week pro rata, averaged over a month) on-site.

Our core HQ offices are modern and newly refurbished with excellent city centre transport link and benefit from benefit from co-location with other government departments such as the Department for Health and Social Care (DHSC).

If this role is fixed term and you are not currently a civil servant, you will take up the post on a Fixed Term appointment; you may be able to take this role up as a Secondment. Otherwise, roles are offered at the pay scale minimum for the grade, but in exceptional circumstances there may be flexibility if you are able to demonstrate you are already in receipt of an existing, higher salary. UKHSA is investing in a new state-of-the-art National Biosecurity Centre in Harlow, Essex, which will eventually bring together teams currently based at Canary Wharf, Colindale and Porton Down. For more details, please see: Huge biosecurity centre investment to boost pandemic protection - GOV.UK.

The new facilities will start becoming operational in the mid-2030s, with full completion by 2038. Staff will move in phases as facilities become available. If you're appointed to a role currently based at Canary Wharf, Colindale or Porton Down, please note that we'll continue investing in these sites for the next decade. As we get closer to the transition, we'll provide full information about relocation support available to staff.

Reasonable Adjustments

The Civil Service is committed to making sure that our selection methods are fair to everyone. company: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs
description:
• Job grade: Grade 6
  • Contract type: Permanent

About the job

Job summary

This is a high-profile opportunity to lead organisation design and development across the Defra Group at a time of significant organisational pressure and change. With the Permanent Secretary now established in the organisation, Defra is considering how its structures should evolve in response to political direction, including devolution and the future Civil Service, while ensuring the Group is organised to deliver Defra’s organisational outcomes.

As Head of Organisation Design & Development, you will bring deep professional expertise and practical leadership to the design and restructuring of Core Defra and its agencies and arm’s-length bodies. You and your team will work directly with Directors General, HR Directors and ALB leaders, offering trusted advice and constructive challenge and translating complex requirements into deliverable organisational solutions.

The role sits in the Workforce Strategy & Transformation directorate and will be central to enabling the Rightsizing pillar of the Workforce Strategy and Transformation Programme. Organisation design will be the strongest emphasis, alongside organisational development, culture and behaviour, team effectiveness, transformation and change, and wider workforce strategy.

You will lead a team of around seven Grade 7 practitioners, strengthen its bench strength and professional practice, manage demand across the Group and bring in specialist OD&D contractors where required. This is a practical, delivery-focused role for an experienced practitioner who can shape the organisation while building a strong, resilient and responsive OD&D service.

Job description

  • Lead organisation design and restructuring across the Defra Group, aligning structures with political direction, including devolution and the future Civil Service, and enabling delivery of Defra’s organisational outcomes.
  • Lead OD&D work in Core Defra, agencies and arm’s-length bodies, ensuring expert resource is deployed to the highest-priority organisational and transformation challenges.
  • Work confidently with Directors General, HR Directors and ALB leaders, providing trusted evidence-based advice, constructive challenge and practical organisational solutions.
  • Play a central role in the Workforce Strategy and Transformation Programme, particularly enabling the Rightsizing pillar through organisation design expertise and delivery.
  • Provide expert consultancy across organisation design, organisational development, culture and behaviour, team effectiveness, transformation and change, and workforce strategy, with organisation design as the principal focus.
  • Lead the central OD&D service and act as Head of Practice, setting professional standards, assuring quality and strengthening OD&D methods and capability across the Group.
  • Lead, coach and develop a team of around seven Grade 7 OD&D practitioners, building bench strength, professional confidence and a cohesive, inclusive and high-performing service.
  • Manage demand, priorities and practitioner deployment across the Group, balancing urgent restructuring activity with longer-term organisational development.
  • Commission and procure specialist OD&D contractors where needed, integrating them effectively into the team and ensuring quality, value and delivery.
  • Use organisational evidence, workforce insight and professional judgement to shape options, recommendations and implementation plans that are practical and sustainable.

Person specification

Essential experience and skills

  • Deep professional expertise in organisation design and development, with substantial experience of leading complex organisation design and restructuring.
  • A strong track record of operating in a large, complex organisation and translating strategic, political or operational requirements into practical organisational solutions.
  • Experience of influencing and advising at the most senior levels, including providing credible constructive challenge and building trusted relationships across organisational boundaries.
  • Demonstrable expertise across organisation design, organisational development, culture and behaviour, team effectiveness, transformation and change, and workforce strategy.
  • Experience of applying evidence-based OD&D practice, models, data and organisational insight with professional rigour.
  • Experience of leading an expert service and senior practitioners, developing capability and bench strength while managing competing demand and priorities.
  • Experience of commissioning or managing specialist external expertise and ensuring it is integrated effectively into delivery.
  • Excellent communication, facilitation and relationship-building skills, with the judgement to move between strategic advice and practical implementation.

description:

Location

HM Naval Base Devonport, Plymouth, PL2 2BG

About the job

Job summary

The Submarine Delivery Agency (SDA) is a part of the Ministry of Defence responsible for the procurement, in-service support, and disposal of the UK’s nuclear submarines. Our work is of unparalleled strategic importance nationally and internationally, ensuring the security of the UK’s continuous at-sea nuclear deterrent (CASD), and delivering some of the most technically complex programmes in defence. At least one of four nuclear-armed submarines, supported by smaller attack submarines, is on patrol at all times: 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.

At the SDA, we strive to Support, Deliver and Aspire and put our values at the heart of our recruitment process. We believe that everyone should feel comfortable to be themselves and be supported to do their best work. As part of a diverse and inclusive workforce, our team will find a community to belong to. We believe that, by celebrating different backgrounds and different perspectives, together we’ll achieve the extraordinary.

This position is advertised at 37 hours per week.

The primary delivery location for this position is Devonport , Plymouth.

Please note, due to the level of security, this role is reserved for UK nationals only.

If you need to contact Defence Business Services (DBS) regarding this vacancy, please indicate that your vacancy is being handled by the SDA Recruitment Team. If you experience any technical difficulties with the CS Jobs system, please contact the Support Team via the Help link.

Job description

Are you a Project Controls Manager interested in working with industry partners, providing through-life support for the UK’s fleet of submarines? The programme level schedules for each Major Submarines Disposal Projects containing key milestones and deliverables. The schedules are baselined as part of business case approvals and are reviewed monthly to understand the variances, review the forecasts, and discuss risks and opportunities against critical path activities. The outputs from these reviews inform monthly progress meetings and Project Boards.

The Project Controls Manager’s role is integral to enabling the successful delivery of these Submarine Disposal Projects.

You will be working as part of the Programme Management Office undertaking the following tasks:

  • Acting as the key contact for project controls and to integrate and co-ordinate all project controls activities within the project/programme.
  • Ensuring the quality and accuracy of all project controls data and artefacts is in-line with SDA policy, as well as ensure that these are utilised by the project team.
  • Develop the Performance Measurement Baseline (PMB), incorporating at an appropriate level both OPEX and CAPEX to aid effective performance analysis and project management. Analyse performance of projects against the PMB, and communicate it to the project teams to ensure effective delivery.
  • Work with the Project Manager and commercial teams to ensure that contractor and supplier data is received in a timely manner, in an appropriate format and to the required quality.
  • Work with and advise internal stakeholders (PM’s, CAM’s and OM’s) to ensure coherent, effective communication of project performance analysis (single version of the truth) and forecasted taskings and activities
  • Manage resource planning in line with the project schedule, ensuring resource demand is underpinned by robust BOE (driven by schedule activities)
  • Communicate complex project controls data to key stakeholders of the project, programme and SDDI Leadership Team, in a clear and audience appropriate manner.
  • To communicate and influence colleagues and Leadership Team within the SRRC project and supply chain on all aspects of project controls (drawing on sub-disciplines as required).
  • Establishing and maintaining the Submarine Disposal Programme drumbeat of PC processes whilst working across all project control functions to ensure consistency in project data.
  • Facilitate and manage changes to the Programme.
  • Working with Project Controls corporate function to implement PC processes (PC tailoring guide) within the Submarine disposal programme/projects
  • Facilitate the management of 4th order operating assumptions (4OA’s) and dependencies

Hybrid and flexible working can be considered for this post. Successful candidates are encouraged to discuss options with the recruiting line manager before starting the role.

As the post holder will have access to very sensitive information, there are limitations on travelling to a small number of countries and we will undertake additional security checks as part of the recruitment process. Applications from candidates with close connections to certain countries may take considerably longer to process, or in some cases result in a withdrawal of an offer of employment. Further details will be provided at the conditional offer stage.

Person specification

title: Network and Information Security Engineer Supervisor
description:
Essential Functions:

  • Supervise of Information Security Analysts, Security Engineers, Network Engineers, and Network Analysts in the day-to-day administration, service delivery, monitoring, and support of the LAN/WAN network and cybersecurity environment.
  • Coordinate and interface with network and information security managed service providers for operational support, incident response, and technology projects.
  • Collaborates with the IT Enterprise Architects and IT Program Managers to develop plans that ensure the network infrastructure and related security controls are available, reliable, secure, and scalable to meet current and future business demands.
  • Prioritize and respond to new work requests related to projects, break fix, and new technology installations. Delegate to team members to meet established service levels.
  • Ensure reliable network connectivity of servers, workstations, voice equipment, and other network appliances and work with other IT personnel to troubleshoot and resolve incidents.
  • Develop and maintain processes, procedures, standards, and technical documentation required for network administration, secure configuration, usage, vulnerability management, information security, incident response, and recovery.
  • Ensure network assets are maintained in accordance with recommended maintenance patches, security updates, and configuration standards; maintain accurate inventory with new and/or retired asset information; and track remediation of identified vulnerabilities.
  • Proactively monitor network availability, capacity, performance, and security events to ensure results comply with established service levels, risk tolerances, and performance metrics.
  • Lead and oversee daily information security operations, including security monitoring, alert escalation, threat analysis, vulnerability prioritization, and coordination of corrective actions.
  • Serve as the supervisory escalation point for significant network outages and cybersecurity incidents; coordinate containment, recovery, communications, documentation, and post-incident improvement activities.
  • Oversee the development, implementation, and periodic review of information security policies, standards, procedures, and technical controls aligned with District requirements and recognized guidance such as the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, CISA guidance, and CIS Critical Security Controls.
  • Oversee network and security architecture reviews and promote security-by-design, including appropriate network segmentation, identity and access controls, logging and monitoring, secure configurations, and resilient recovery capabilities.
  • Assess network and cybersecurity risks associated with new applications, technologies, projects, vendors, and managed services; recommend practical risk treatment and ensure agreed corrective actions are tracked to completion.
  • Develop and report operational, KPI, and risk metrics to IT leadership, including security and network service performance, vulnerabilities, security incidents, control effectiveness, project status, and resource needs.


Additional Responsibilities:

  • Assist in preparation and critique of purchase requisitions of related communications and equipment from user departments; provide information and communications technology consulting and support to the IT staff and user departments; prepare yearly performance appraisals of assigned staff; and coordinate technical project assignment as needed.
  • After-Hours Work: This position requires availability to work after regular business hours (evenings, nights, weekends) as needed for implementing system changes, updates, and maintenance activities. These activities are crucial for minimizing disruption to business operations and ensuring system stability.
  • On-Call Duty: The employee will participate in a rotational on-call schedule to provide technical support outside of regular business hours, including evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays.
  • Response Requirements: While on-call, the employee must be available to respond promptly to urgent issues, critical situations, and system alerts. This requires the ability to be contacted within a specified timeframe and initiate problem resolution as quickly as possible.
  • Troubleshooting & Incident Response: On-call duties involve identifying, diagnosing, and resolving technical problems, including system failures, security incidents, and application bugs.
  • Compensation: Compensation for on-call hours and after-hours work will be provided in accordance with Civil Service requirements and company policies. This includes any applicable overtime pay for non-exempt employees.
Training and Experience:
  • Bachelor's degree in Information Technology (or related field) or equivalent years of experience and
  • education.
  • Five or more years of experience in a network technical role supporting and configuring network technology.
  • At least three years of this experience should be in a senior level support position.
  • Professional certification ((e.g. Cisco Certified Internetwork Expert (CCIE)) is also highly desirable.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:
  • Knowledge and skills in Lan/Wan technologies, network security principles, and general network management best practices.
  • Excellent knowledge of Cisco data and voice networks.
  • Experience troubleshooting network performance issues and performing root cause analysis.
  • Effective skills in the area of project management and working with network managed service providers to complete infrastructure projects.
  • Ability to communicate effectively both in oral and written form.
  • Ability to take initiative and perform job functions with minimal supervision.

description:

About the job

Job summary

The Public Sector Reform Test, Learn and Grow (PSR TL&G) team is at the heart of the UK government’s initiative to drive innovation and reform in public service delivery. With the £100 million PSR Innovation Fund, our team collaborates with local authorities and government departments across the United Kingdom and with the Devolved Governments to design, test, and grow innovative solutions that enhance public service outcomes. By employing a ‘Test & Learn’ approach, we focus on creating evidence-based improvements while relieving pressures on public services. Our work involves piloting foundational programmes and place-based initiatives to accelerate mission delivery, support preventative measures, and foster a collaborative environment that encourages continuous improvement and innovation in public services.

The TLG programme uses place-based projects to prototype solutions to complex policy issues (these are known as ‘accelerators’). Examples of some of the accelerators in our portfolio include ‘violence against women and girls’ in Islington, ‘special educational needs and disabilities’ in Nottingham and Sandwell, ‘economic inactivity’ in Wakefield, and ‘neighbourhood health’ in Plymouth and Liverpool.

The ‘Grow’ element of the programme also aims to change the conditions across government so that it’s easier to work in a ‘test & learn’ way, as well as building the energy, networks and demand to sustain this work after the programme ends.

Job description

As the Lead Data Governance Manager for the TL&G team, you’ll work with colleagues from different multidisciplinary backgrounds in local government, central government and the wider public sector. You’ll help them identify data protection and data sharing issues early. You’ll support them in navigating complex data governance challenges, guiding them through the necessary processes, and ensuring proper join-up with the Cabinet Office Data Protection team. You’ll also make sure that any lessons learned around data governance, data protection and data privacy are shared with the ‘Grow’ part of the TLG team and support them in their work. This part of the team looks to identify and address systemic barriers that get in the way of those in central and local government taking iterative approaches to public services, and data sharing has already come up as a major area of work.

This role is mapped to the Lead Data Governance Manager role in the Government Digital and Data framework. This role may require some limited travel within the UK to work closely with local partners. This role is eligible for a DDaT allowance, the value of which will depend on an assessment of your skills and experience, as demonstrated at interview.

Main responsibilities

You will:

  • Ensure the adoption and implementation of the programme’s cross-organisational data governance framework, working closely with the Cabinet Office Data Protection team and our delivery partner–the transformation consultancy Public Digital (PD),
  • Develop, implement and manage additional data governance frameworks, policies, standards and agreements for work with our other stakeholders (including other central government departments, local government partners, other public sector bodies, and occasional private sector or third sector organisations),
  • Set principles for a data privacy-first approach, ensuring that data protection is embedded in the programme’s work and data risk is minimised,
  • Establish and oversee the programme’s data infrastructure,
  • Be responsible for understanding and managing the programme’s data risks and issues,
  • Explore creative solutions to data governance issues that meet Cabinet Office’s policies and standards,
  • Ensure that data governance issues are understood by seniors in the programme and by the Grow part of the TLG team,
  • Support the Grow part of the TLG team to understand good data practices established within our programme, identify opportunities to improve cross-government data governance and protection policy, and scope possible solutions where technical expertise is needed.

Person specification

It’s essential that you have the following skills:

Data ethics and privacy

  • Work with stakeholders to identify and address ethical and privacy concerns,
  • Research developments in data ethics and privacy to improve compliance and processes,
  • Assess and constructively challenge proposed data ethics policies.

Data governance

  • Implement and monitor data governance using standard methodology throughout the data life cycle.

Data innovation

  • Identify areas of innovation in data tools and techniques, and recognise appropriate timing for adoption.

Data life cycle

  • Understand and apply data governance structures and principles over a data life cycle, ensuring best practice at each phase,
  • Demonstrate knowledge of data governance industry standards,
  • Design and implement continuous improvements to optimise data governance over a data life cycle.

Data management

  • Monitor and improve data management practices,
  • Help define, develop and support the use of data management tools, procedures and methods in compliance with data governance policies.

Data maturity

  • Lead the implementation of data best practices,
  • Lead on monitoring and improving areas of data maturity.

Data standards

  • Create data standards for different subjects and ensure senior leaders understand them,
  • Monitor compliance with policies and standards in the Cabinet Office.

Communicating between technical and non-technical

  • Listen to and interpret the needs of technical and non-technical stakeholders, and manage their expectations,
  • Support or host difficult discussions within the team or with diverse senior stakeholders.

Stakeholder relationship management:

  • Identify and resolve issues, influence stakeholders and manage relationships effectively,
  • Build long-term strategic relationships and communicate clearly and regularly with stakeholders.

Logical and creative thinking

  • Ensure that the most appropriate actions are taken to resolve problems as they occur.

Inclusivity

  • Support equity and inclusion for your delivery work as well as in your team.

It’s desirable that you have:

Cross-sectoral experience

  • Experience across different organisation types would be valuable in this role (for example, experience in more than one of central government, local government, the private sector, and the third sector).

Policy influencing skills

  • Experience bringing different perspectives together to create policy change.

Data strategy and data policy development

  • Experience developing data strategy and data policy in complex environments.

Requirements to attend other locations for official business will also count towards this level of attendance.

  • Data governance
  • Data innovation

  • Communicating between the technical and non-technical
