About the job

Job summary

We are Ofwat, the Water Services Regulation Authority, a non-ministerial government department responsible for regulating the water sector in England and Wales.

We have an opportunity for a Principal Water Resources Planning Lead to join our Water Supply Team within the RAPID & Environmental Planning Directorate.

The water sector is entering a new chapter. The government has set out a bold new direction, bringing together expertise from across the sector to deliver better outcomes for customers and the environment. We are collaborating with fellow regulators to respond to recommendations in The Independent Water Commission Report, the Welsh Government’s response to the Green Paper, Shaping the Future of Water Governance in Wales, and the Government’s White Paper, A new vision for water.

Ofwat is working with the government and other regulators to help create a new body for England, bringing together our strengths with those of the Drinking Water Inspectorate, the Environment Agency and Natural England. We are also continuing to work with the Welsh Government to support decisions on the future arrangements for Wales.

While these changes take shape, our mission remains the same: to hold water companies to account, drive performance, and ensure the sector delivers real value for customers, communities, and the environment. If you’re passionate about making a difference, this is a unique moment to join us and help shape the future of water, and together we can continue to make a positive impact.

You can find out more about why you should join Ofwat, our strategy, values and our framework for success in the attached Information for Candidates Pack.

Job description

We're looking for a Water Resources Planning Lead to join our Water Supply team within the RAPID and Environmental Planning directorate at Principal level. The sector is facing unprecedented challenges, and we want someone who relishes the opportunity to apply their skills and experience to improve our water environment. Whilst there are specific policy areas you will lead on, you will also play an important role in driving the collaborative work programme across Governments and with other regulators to improve future water resources management.

The Water Resources Planning Lead role has an important and valuable contribution to enable us to deliver on our goals and regulatory commitments. You will lead our engagement with wider governments, regulators and a varied range of stakeholders on national water resources policy and investment policy, including delivery of current 2024 water resource management plans (WRMP24) and our preparations for WRMP29 and the 2029 price review (PR29). This includes bringing together partner regulators (Drinking Water Inspectorate, Environment Agency, Natural England and Natural Resources Wales) to agree on policy development and technical assessment outcomes. You will utilise forums such as the Technical Advisory Group (TAG) to present, communicate and consult with the industry on Ofwat's water resources policy decisions and technical issues. You will also have the opportunity to steer the development of new planning frameworks developed under Defra's White Paper on a new vision for water.

You will lead a technical team to undertake water resources work and their engagement with the water companies. You will be responsible for designing and planning the team's approaches to meeting our statutory responsibilities, and aligning our work across related and dependant regulatory frameworks and processes. This includes our involvement in the government's Water Delivery Taskforce; Ofwat's PR24 and PR29 teams including delivery plans and price control deliverables (PCDs); and interfacing with principal leads for the strategic resource options (SROs) in the RAPID programme. Your work on this area will hold companies to account on their delivery on behalf of customers and the environment.

Key deliverables:

In this role you will be expected to:

  • Lead on our statutory duties in water resources planning, including delivery oversight of current WRMPs and planning for future WRMPs, giving technical steer and making decisions on complex supply-demand balance and supply security issues.
  • Lead our strategy with our partner regulators and government on the evolving strategic planning frameworks, including WRMPs, business plan links, and new planning frameworks developed through Defra's White Paper on a new vision for water.
  • Support wider water resources efficiency policy and regulator guidance development working with government, other regulators, water companies and wider stakeholders.
  • Collaborate closely with other principals in the Water Supply team on cross-working issues and policies associated with WRMPs, demand management, and the positioning of the SROs within WRMPs.
  • Manage a small water resources team, supporting workload prioritisation, as well as their growth and professional development.
  • Contribute to the RAPID and Environmental Planning directorate strategy and the Price Review directorate more broadly as required.

Person specification

To be successful in this role you will need the below essential attributes, experience, skills and knowledge:

Experience, skills and knowledge

  1. Lead criterion: Relevant experience in water resources planning (including adhering to or designing planning frameworks, supply scheme development, water efficiency or environmental strategy). This can be regulatory, technical or policy experience gained within the water sector.
  2. Academic or professional experience of wider environmental issues and good knowledge/understanding of those related to the water industry.
  3. Significant experience of policy development and implementation, and/or designing and delivering programmes of work within a relevant field.
  4. Significant experience of building and maintaining constructive working relationships with internal and external stakeholders, influencing decisions and delivering outcomes across organisational boundaries.
  5. Highly numerate with significant experience of leading and completing complex technical analysis, critically evaluating the work of others and providing evidence-based recommendations.
  6. Excellent oral and written communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex concepts to technical and non-technical audiences in order to inform policy making, decision making or recommendations.

Attributes

Our people are at the heart of Ofwat, and our People Strategy defines the goals that keep this focus central to everything we do. Our 2025 People Survey highlights several key strengths. Nine in ten colleagues say that they are treated with respect and that Ofwat values individual differences. Location

About the job

Job summary

In the Department of Health and Social Care, we are proud of our purpose – to enable everyone to live more independent, healthier lives for longer. To achieve this, and create a great place to work, we have four values: we are inclusive, we constantly improve, we challenge, and we are agile. If this sounds like an environment you would like to work in, we would love to hear from you.

The DHSC Digital Transformation team works with the national health and care system to realise the benefits of digital, data and technology, to deliver better end to end services for their users and for the professionals who provide them.

We don’t manage live digital services; our role is more strategic. We partner with policy and commissioning teams to deliver user centred, design-led change, and to act as a bridge between policy and digital delivery teams. We support the Department and its arms' length bodies in a range of different ways - from providing short-term consultancy advice and digital training, to running full discoveries and alphas, and embedding team members in wider beta or live delivery teams.

We champion standards, user-centred design and accessibility in everything that we do.

Job description

As a Digital Business Partner, you will be responsible for building and maintaining strong relationships between DHSC and a range of external partner organisations. You will develop a detailed understanding of partner priorities, challenges and opportunities, acting as a trusted point of contact for digital leaders and helping identify opportunities for collaboration, alignment and shared learning.

Working closely with colleagues across DHSC and partner organisations, you will support shared priorities, facilitate collaboration across organisational boundaries, and help improve visibility of digital, data and technology priorities, risks and opportunities. You will play a key role in ensuring organisations are connected to the right expertise, communities and support mechanisms, helping to strengthen collaboration and deliver greater value across the wider system.

Person specification

Role responsibilities

We are looking for a proactive and collaborative individual who enjoys building relationships and working across organisational boundaries. You will be comfortable engaging with a wide range of stakeholders, understanding different perspectives and helping bring people together around shared challenges and opportunities.

You will have strong communication and organisational skills, the ability to manage competing priorities and an interest in how digital, data and technology can support organisational and system-wide improvement.

You will be motivated by helping others succeed, identifying opportunities for collaboration and supporting positive change across organisational boundaries.

Key Responsibilities

  • Build and maintain effective relationships with digital leaders and stakeholders across a range of external partner organisations.
  • Develop a strong understanding of organisational priorities, challenges and opportunities, helping identify areas for collaboration and shared learning.
  • Support delivery of shared digital, data and technology priorities, working with stakeholders across DHSC and partner organisations to drive progress.
  • Facilitate engagement across the wider system, including supporting forums, working groups, communities of practice and collaborative initiatives.
  • Identify, monitor and escalate emerging priorities, risks, dependencies and opportunities across your portfolio of organisations.
  • Produce high-quality briefings, reports and stakeholder communications to support decision-making, engagement and collaboration activities.
  • Please note this role may include line management responsibilities

Key skills and experience required for the role

Essential

  • Knowledge and understanding of the public sector, ideally with experience in business partnering, stakeholder engagement or relationship management
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and effectively with a range of audiences.
  • Strong interpersonal and networking skills, with experience building productive relationships with stakeholders at different levels of an organisation.
  • Experience supporting or enabling digital, data or technology delivery, with an understanding of the factors required for successful digital transformation.
  • Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities, coordinate activity and maintain attention to detail.
  • Ability to work independently, exercise sound judgement and deliver high-quality outcomes within a complex stakeholder environment.

Desirable

  • Relevant experience within digital, technology, health or wider government arms length bodies.
  • Experience working with public bodies, external partners or cross-organisational stakeholder groups.
  • Knowledge of the health and care system and the role of technology, digital and data in supporting organisational priorities.

  • Seeing the Big Picture
  • Communicating and Influencing
  • Working Together
  • Leadership

We only ask for evidence of these behaviours on your application form:

  • Seeing the Big Picture

Technical skills

We'll assess you against these technical skills during the selection process:

  • Knowledge of standards and ability to communicate technical concepts clearly

Alongside your salary of £58,462, Department of Health and Social Care contributes £16,936 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

About the job

Job summary

Working towards sustainable futures. Championing diversity in the workplace. At the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP), it’s all in a day’s work. From HR to Finance, Policy to Communications, this is work that sustains and supports, where everyone’s voice is heard, and our customers are at the heart of everything we do. For a career packed with possibility, a comprehensive benefits package, where we live by our values and have the opportunity to improve the lives of people across the country, look no further.

Supporting people who need it most. That’s our purpose. Start your own career today.

We are looking for an experienced, qualified finance professional to join our small team providing financial support to DWP’s Service Delivery, Change Finance and Shared Services, and Automated Buying, Business Services and External Resources Commercial functions covering a portfolio of c £2.8bn. The portfolio includes a wide variety of contracts in a number of areas including contact centres, banking, travel, logistics, and document management. It is a fast-moving and interesting role, and you will be in the heart of decision making for some of DWP’s most critical contracts.

The successful candidate will provide advice and insight on the financial implications of commercial contracts and commercial strategy decisions. Responsibilities will involve providing support throughout the commercial lifecycle, including procurement stages, pricing approaches, evaluation of bids, assessment of supplier viability, financial analysis and in-life management of contracts.

The role involves working in multi-disciplinary teams across the department and is a fantastic opportunity for anyone looking to hone their commercial skills. You will be joining a friendly, high performing, and engaged team, which offers opportunities for both personal growth and career development.

Places for Growth and Social Mobility

As part of the Places for Growth Programme, we are committed to delivering a more geographically diverse Civil and Public Service that will better serve the public and ministers.

As part of this initiative, we are continuously reviewing how we recruit into each location.

Job description

Working closely with Commercial and Business area experts you will be responsible for providing a wide range of analysis and activities to enable the department to achieve value for money on corporate contracts. Activities will include (but are not limited to):

  • Providing finance support to complex procurements including contributing to the development of payment mechanisms, drafting tender documents, and financial evaluation.
  • Providing ‘Should Cost’ analysis and contributing to Delivery Model Assessments to determine the most appropriate delivery method for the service.
  • Providing analysis of financial statements and opinion on the relative strength and ongoing financial viability of suppliers.
  • Reviewing and analysing Supplier financial and operational data on a regular and ad-hoc basis to ensure the department is gaining the maximum economic value from existing contracts.
  • Working collaboratively within a small team of finance professionals, contributing to joint team and corporate objectives.
  • Assisting in keeping DWP safe by reviewing commercial activity against financial accounting policies, and published guidance such as Managing Public Money, highlighting any concerns.
  • Providing advice and insight to support data driven decision making and working collaboratively with other functional experts at all levels to deliver shared objectives.
  • Demonstrating professional and personal credibility and generating confidence in senior stakeholders.

Hybrid working

This role may be suitable for hybrid working, which is where an employee works part of the week in their DWP office and part of the week from home. This is a voluntary, non-contractual arrangement and your office will be your contractual place of work.

If a hybrid working arrangement is suitable for the role and for you, you will normally be required to spend a minimum of 60% of your contracted working hours from your DWP office.

If you have a disability, caring responsibilities, or other circumstances that may affect your ability to meet the minimum office attendance requirement, please discuss this with us using the contact details in this advert.

This role can only be worked in the UK and not overseas.

Working Pattern

DWP are committed to flexible working patterns, and keen to support alternative working patterns where business needs allow. The working hours we can support will depend on which role you are offered (if there is more than one role now or in the future) and if there is capacity to operate the role part-time or job share.

Visas

Please note that while we consider sponsorship requests in accordance with current DWP guidance and Home Office policy, sponsorship cannot be guaranteed.

A strong candidate for this role should be able to demonstrate the following Essential Criteria:

  • [Lead criteria] Experience of analysing and modelling complex financial information in a commercial environment, using techniques such as value-for-money analysis, should-cost modelling and sensitivity analysis.
  • Experience of reviewing supplier proposals and underlying cost bases to develop pricing mechanisms or challenge contract costs.
  • Experience of working across boundaries with multidisciplinary teams and collaborating with subject matter experts towards a common goal.
  • Ability to communicate complex financial data, concepts and risks clearly to non-financial audiences demonstrating credibility to stakeholders at all levels.

This role is open to candidates who hold a full chartered level professional qualification awarded by a UK-recognised accountancy body: CIMA, ICAEW, ACCA, CIPFA, ICAS or Chartered Accountants Ireland (see advert for further eligibility criteria), or part-qualified accountants who are still studying. Please note the higher rate of pay is only available upon full qualification. Further information on your eligibility is listed on the application form. If you hold a chartered level accountancy qualification with an overseas body, you will not be eligible to apply for this role. Most of the UK-recognised accountancy bodies operate reciprocal agreements and pathways programmes which allow people with overseas qualifications to apply for membership. We would recommend pursuing this if you are interested in a career in UK government finance. You would then be eligible to apply for our future vacancies, once your membership became active.

Eligibility criteria for part-qualified accountants: You must be studying for a qualification with a UK-recognised accountancy body: CIMA, ICAEW, ACCA, CIPFA, ICAS or Chartered Accountants Ireland. You must have passed (or been awarded an exemption from) a minimum of 8 exams so far and your last exam sitting must have been within 12 months from the date you submit your application.

Please note that membership of AAT or other technician level qualifications does not satisfy the qualification criteria for this role. If you are invited to interview, you will be asked to provide evidence of both your exam passes/exemptions to date and your membership being active on the date you applied for the role. Please note that membership of AAT or other technician level qualifications does not satisfy the part-qualification criteria for this role. If you are unsure whether you meet the part-qualification criteria, you should confirm with our recruitment team before proceeding with your application. If you are successful in applying for the role, you will be expected to complete your studies and become a fully qualified accountant within a reasonable timeframe. If you do not achieve full qualification with your institute, you may in future be moved into a different role that does not require a professional finance qualification.

DWP have a broad benefits package built around your work-life balance which includes:

  • Working patterns to support work/life balance such as job sharing, term-time working, flexi-time and compressed hours.
  • Generous annual leave – at least 23 days on entry, increasing up to 30 days over time (pro–rata for part time employees), plus 9 days public and privilege leave.

About the job

Job summary

A cleaner, more secure energy future depends on the decisions we make today and the foundations we build. Ofgem is looking for a Manager, Offshore Cost Analyst to bring insight and independent thinking to major onshore and offshore electricity transmission projects.

Ofgem is Great Britain's independent energy regulator. We're at the forefront of change across the energy sector, driving toward Net Zero whilst protecting energy consumers, especially vulnerable people.

This is a permanent opportunity to work on major projects that will play a vital part in our future energy system. You'll get beneath the numbers, challenge assumptions and use your expertise to help ensure significant spending delivers genuine value for consumers.

You'll join our offshore cost assessment team within the Major Projects division at a fascinating time for the energy sector. With major projects moving forward and new approaches such as Multi-Purpose Interconnectors emerging, there's a lot happening – and you'll be right in the middle of it.

What's more, you'll have plenty of chances to grow and develop your skills, gaining new perspectives, tackling increasingly complex challenges, and broadening your existing knowledge base.

We're looking for someone with a proven ability to quickly assimilate, analyse and simplify a wide range of information, using their findings to identify trends and draw clear conclusions. You'll be a fantastic communicator with strong IT proficiency and the ability to present complex and technical analysis in a clear, concise way to different audiences. As confident presenting as engaging at a senior level, you'll be comfortable defending your analysis, debating and negotiating.

In return, you'll discover an outstanding rewards package, plenty of flexibility and a supportive environment that gives you the space to do your best work, whilst making a real impact in the future of energy in this country.

We have a critical purpose to protect consumers whilst supporting the development of a secure, sustainable energy system. Join us and use your analytical expertise to help make major projects count.

Job description

Key Outputs and Deliverables

The scope of work ranges from technical analysis and statistical/econometric modelling to report drafting and engaging with industry. Typical responsibilities include:

  • Leading on cost assessments specific infrastructure projects such as electricity interconnectors, onshore transmission assets and the transmission assets connecting offshore windfarms and supporting on the assessment of large infrastructure projects.
  • Detailed and robust analysis of submissions to help determine the economic and efficient costs associated with the development and delivery of these projects. This will include comparing costs across different projects, undertaking detailed analysis to inform and support our assessments, and helping to set appropriate incentives on project developers to manage their costs efficiently.
  • Presentation and discussion of analysis and resulting proposals to internal and external stakeholders, such as other team members, senior managers and project developers. In doing so you will support our objective to be fair, open and transparent.
  • Ensuring smooth and efficient assessments through clear project-planning, organisation of internal and external meetings, tracking key issues, management of external consultants and their contracts, and management of work packages and analysis allocated to other team members.
  • The ability to quickly review and draw conclusions from detailed cost and technical submissions.
  • Oversight and management of the team’s internal cost models and associated analysis, including reviewing and updating the models, as appropriate (dependent on candidate’s experience and/or skills).
  • A willingness to work flexibly within the Division is essential as role holders will be required to contribute where resources are most needed to achieve deliverables.

Key Responsibilities

  • Accountable to wider OFTO and Interconnector project teams for delivering cost valuations of the transmission assets at the agreed time for each project
  • Accountable to other teams for providing numerical/cost analysis as and when required
  • Budget accountability if managing an external contractor
  • May be responsible for line managing junior staff (e.g. graduate placement)

Responsible for 1-2 team management tasks such as resource planning or budget tracking.

  • Effective written and verbal communication skills, able to apply these in delivering internal and external documents and presentations. Ability to present and defend analysis, to the companies we regulate, in a confident and assertive manner. (LEAD)
  • Ability to present analysis in a clear, concise format and translate technical details to diverse stakeholders, and a proficiency in Microsoft Excel/Word/PowerPoint

title: Senior Software Development Engineer - UI/UX
description:
At Dragos, the mission is personal. The systems we protect deliver the water you drink, power your home, and keep the hospitals your community depends on running. Those critical infrastructure systems that power our civilization around the world are under attack every day by adversaries. When those systems fail, people are immediately at risk. We are the global leader in xOT cybersecurity, combining technology, threat intelligence, and expert services. The people here chose this work because they understand what is at stake. Here, you will find a remote-first mission-driven team across North America, Europe, the Middle East, and APAC built on authenticity, transparency, and trust. If safeguarding the systems that protect your family, friends, and community is the kind of work that matters to you, you are in the right place.

About the Role

We are growing the engineering team behind Dragos Software and Supply Chain Security product. As a Senior Software Engineer, you will build and run the web application, the GraphQL and gRPC APIs behind it, and the SDKs customers build on, so security teams and integrators can see which risks in their devices are actually exploitable.

This position reports to the Senior Director of Engineering, and our engineers work together by shipping code, troubleshooting problems, and listening to customers. You will own the production code you ship, work with real-time security data at scale, and turn dense binary-analysis output into something a security team can read under pressure.

What You'll Do

  • Build and ship features across the React and TypeScript frontend and the GraphQL and gRPC APIs behind it, from scoping through design, implementation, and deployment
  • Design and implement GraphQL schema and protobuf/gRPC contract changes with versioning and schema evolution, so existing customers and integrators keep working
  • Build and maintain client SDKs in Python, TypeScript, and Go, including the codegen pipelines, semantic versioning, and release automation that keep them in sync with the API
  • Define the contracts between your work and the backend team (mostly Go services), and work with Product and Design to turn customer needs into features
  • Improve frontend performance, accessibility, and observability in the code you own, write well-tested and secure code, and give constructive code reviews

You Should Have

  • 5+ years of professional experience building production web applications and the APIs behind them, taking work from idea to delivery with Product, Design, and Engineering. Equivalent experience is equally valued
  • React (hooks, Context, lazy loading, large component architectures) and TypeScript, with modern front-end tooling such as testing frameworks, state management, and build tools
  • GraphQL with Apollo Client and Apollo Server on Node.js, and gRPC with Protocol Buffers (client consumption at minimum, service design a plus)
  • Hands-on API design, versioning, and schema evolution, plus building and maintaining client SDKs in multiple languages (such as Python, TypeScript, and Go) with codegen, semantic versioning, and release automation
  • Auth0, OAuth 2.0, and JWT flows

You May Have

  • Data-heavy UIs, such as grids, charts, and virtualization, or shared UI component libraries and design systems
  • PostgreSQL (query patterns and data modeling), GCP (Cloud Run, GCS), and Protobuf schema design with buf tooling
  • OpenTelemetry, CI/CD with GitLab, feature flag systems such as OpenFeature, and Terraform
  • Cybersecurity, OT, or ICS experience, or SBOM knowledge (CycloneDX, SPDX, CVE)
  • Responsible use of AI-assisted development tools, and experience driving technical initiatives or improving engineering practices across teams

Compensation:

  • Salary: $165,000
  • Competitive Equity Package
  • Comprehensive Benefits Plan

About the job

Job summary

Please refer to Job Description

Job description

PIPEs are specifically designed environments where staff members have additional training to develop an increased psychological understanding of their work. This understanding enables staff to further develop a safe and supportive environment which facilitates an offender’s pathway either pre-treatment, through treatment, post-treatment, or on transition into the community. The service is aimed at supporting offenders to progress through the system in a planned and pathway based approach.

PIPEs are designed to have a particular focus on the environment in which they operate; actively recognising the importance and quality of relationships and interactions. They aim to maximise ordinary situations to support development, and to approach these in a psychologically informed way, paying attention to issues relating to Personality Disorder for example.

PIPEs form a significant part of the pathway for PD, and feature in a settings with different levels of security, both in custody and the community. The operating model for PIPEs is adaptable for the environment that it operates in and the purpose it is fulfilling. Whilst they can be considered as a ‘therapeutic environment’ they are not a treatment intervention themselves.

We’re looking for empathetic, patient, and organised people to join us in this varied role, which offers the chance to make a difference, gain new skills and build a rewarding career within the Probation Service.

If this sounds like you, apply now.

Job Title: Approved Premises Residential Worker

Directorate: Probation Service

Band: Band 3

Overview of the job

The job holder will work as part of a team providing 24 hour cover at an Approved Premises (AP) including security and monitoring services. The job holder will undertake a full range of work with the offender whilst resident at the Approved Premises. This will include; providing support in contributing to the risk management and sentence plan objectives and reporting any significant changes relating to risk and/or re-offending to any non-compliance within agreed enforcement procedures to ensure that offenders resident at an AP and the fabric of it are kept safe and secure throughout their shift.

Summary

The job holder will assist in the well-being and supervision of residents, maintaining discipline, adherence to AP rules, licence conditions, sentence plan objectives specific to residency in the Approved Premises and court orders. In addition, will contribute to the management of residents’ risk. This post will involve substantial out of hours work, both waking night duty and weekend work. The post holder may be required to cover duties at other Approved Premises at times of staff absence.

In line with PS policies and procedures, the job holder must at all times demonstrate a commitment to equality and inclusion and an understanding of their relevance to the work they do.

The post holder must adhere to all policies in respect of the sensitive/confidential nature of the information handled whilst working in this position.

Responsibilities, Activities & Duties

The job holder will be required to carry out the following responsibilities, activities and duties:

  • Contribute to effective team practice, communicate and collaborate effectively with colleagues to ensure consistency of work practices and positive working environment.
  • Effectively communicate key risk issues to colleagues at handover and throughout the shift. It will also, at times, require communicating with Offender Managers, Stand-by Manager and partner agencies e.g. Police, Health professionals and drug/alcohol services.
  • Undertake regular inspections of the building, including cellars and grounds throughout the period of duty, recording any occurrences/damage or defects, and monitor CCTV equipment.
  • Maintain an active presence in the AP at all times. Regularly engage with residents in a pro-social manner. Contribute towards the protection of the residents through observation to ensure adherence to their risk management plans and general wellbeing.
  • Actively engage with and monitor behaviour of high risk residents and motivate residents to ensure compliance. Challenge and manage appropriately abusive or aggressive behaviour.
  • Contribute to the risk management plans of residents by observing and reporting any significant changes relating to risk and/or re-offending to any non-compliance within agreed enforcement procedures.
  • Contribute to the sentence plan objectives of the residents through active engagement in purposeful activities as agreed by the AP Manager and Offender Manager.
  • Ensure that the AP is locked and secure during curfew period. Confirm the presence and wellbeing of all residents overnight.
  • Facilitate the function of the AP as a first/emergency point of contact out of hours.
  • Through observation and/or engagement with residents, provide accurate information, analysis of situation and risk assessment to the Offender Manager and/or escalate to Out of Hours Manager, which may lead to enforcement and/or compliance with court orders, licences, AP rules.
  • Support, create and maintain a safe working environment for staff, residents and visitors by adhering to Health and Safety legislation, ensuring Safe Systems of Work (SSOW) and Risk Assessments are followed reporting incidents to Manager.
  • Undertake Health and Safety, fire alarm, curfews and room curfew checks in line with procedures.
  • Undertake pre-arranged or initiate room searches based on concerns around risk.
  • Pack up residents’ possessions as directed.
  • Set up and /or deliver purposeful activities linked to residents’ sentence plan objectives as agreed by the Offender Manager and AP Manager.
  • Supervise residents’ meals.
  • Undertake effective induction of residents.
  • Follow prescribed medication procedures including the issuing of medication to residents and both weekly and nightly audit of medication sheets.
  • To carry out drug and alcohol tests in line with risk management plan which may include times when job holder believes that the resident maybe under the influence and therefore increase in risk.
  • Undertake First Aid if a resident is injured or self-harms.
  • Maintain Approved Premises records and files as required, including data entry as necessary and contribute to the completion of incident reports.
  • Carry out safeguarding children duties in accordance with the PS statutory responsibilities and agency policies.
  • Deal with visitors and telephone calls, and monitor the work of visiting contractors in accordance with health and safety.
  • Demonstrate pro-social modelling skills by consistently reinforcing pro-social behaviour and attitudes and challenging anti-social behaviour and attitudes.
  • To work within the aims and values of PS and HMPPS.

The duties/responsibilities listed above describe the post as it is at present and is not intended to be exhaustive. The job holder is expected to accept reasonable alterations and additional tasks of a similar level that may be necessary. Significant adjustments may require re-examination under the Job Evaluation Scheme and shall be discussed in the first instance with the job holder.

description:

About the job

Job summary

Do you have a background in science and/or engineering? Could you bring your technical expertise to our diverse team, supporting the UK military air safety? If so, 1710 Naval Air Squadron wants to hear from you.

Within Navy Command, we support and sustain the Royal Navy Fleet Air Arm across every theatre of operations. Based in Portsmouth Naval Base, with a heritage dating back to the 1930s, 1710 Naval Air Squadron is a mixed Civil Service and Military team of technical specialists from multidisciplinary backgrounds, using scientific and engineering reasoning to overcome UK MOD aircraft operational issues.

As part of our Condition Monitoring Department, the Wear Debris Section ensure the safe operation of helicopter and fixed wing aircraft. Analysis of Wear Debris can identify early signs of failure in engines and gearboxes, improving air safety and preserving aircraft to help sustain UK air capability.

This position is advertised at 37 hours per week.

Job description

In this exciting and vital role, you will acquire and develop the expertise to enable you to analyse, interpret and present Wear Debris analysis evidence to both aircraft operators and manufacturers. This will result in the ability to provide airworthiness recommendations for a range of aircraft, both in the UK and around the globe.

As part of the mixed Civil Service and military team of scientists and engineers, you will primarily provide expert specialist support to monitor aircraft engine and gearbox wear processes. This is achieved using a multitude of specialist equipment including scanning electron microscopes and x-ray fluorescence instruments within a laboratory / office hybrid setting.

Additionally, there will be opportunities to explore and exploit other health condition monitoring approaches including novel data analysis approaches. Your expertise will enable you to collaborate with wider condition monitoring partners, both national and international, assuring the provision of expert scientific and engineering advice and risk-based judgements to the Military Air Commands.

The role also offers variety beyond the office, with occasional travel to UK locations and opportunities to attend conferences and visit external partners, and occasional necessary travel to satellite locations with the UK. These experiences can support your continuing professional development, broaden your professional network and help you build valuable leadership, auditing and stakeholder-management skills.

As a key partner in NATO and other strategic alliances, the UK maintains a global military presence to provide security and humanitarian aid. As a Condition Monitoring Specialist, you may occasionally be called upon to work out of hours in the laboratory to support these crucial operations.

Responsibilities

As a Condition Monitoring Specialist within our team, you will be responsible for:

  • Analysing Aircraft Transmission and Engine wear debris samples.
  • Interpreting sample data and providing airworthiness advice to Delivery Teams and Aircraft Operators.
  • Operating and maintaining scientific equipment.
  • Generating fault reports for repair and overhaul organisations.
  • Reviewing repair and overhaul organisations investigation reports to confirm accurate fault detection.
  • Data trending and analysis of fleet data sets.
  • Liaising with MOD Delivery Teams and Aircraft operators to ensure best practice and effective monitoring programs are upheld.
  • Keeping meticulous records of samples to build trends for future analysis.

Desirable Criteria

  • Relevant technical knowledge of systems health monitoring.
  • Relevant experience of data analysis

Job summary

Discover a career in your hands at HMRC. Whether you're seeking purpose, growth, or a workplace that gives you a true sense of belonging, hear from some of our employees as they share their story about what it’s really like to work at HMRC.

Visit our YouTube channel to watch the full series and come and discover your potential.

This national, field-based role is within HMRC Debt Management’s Field Collections Team, collecting overdue tax to fund UK public services. Select the nearest advertised location when applying. Separate merit lists will be maintained for each location, with appointments made in merit order according to business need.

Geographical Vacancy locations are: Aberdeen; Brighton; Bristol; Chelmsford; Chester; Coventry; Cumbria; Doncaster; East London; Enniskillen; Harrow; Hemel Hempstead; Hereford; Kingston upon Thames; Lake District; Leicestershire; Londonderry; Luton; North London; North West London; Northamptonshire; Omagh; Perthshire; Peterborough; Reading and Slough (Berkshire); Somerset; Southall; Stevenage; Swindon (Wiltshire); Watford (Hertfordshire); and Worcester.

This is an exciting time to join a modern digital Field Collections Team within HMRC Debt Management, whose core purpose is to collect money to fund UK public services. Field Collections are responsible for pursuit and collection of overdue taxes.

You will visit company directors, sole traders, partnerships and other customers at homes and business premises, often without an appointment. You will establish their circumstances, secure payment and take appropriate recovery action, including authorised enforcement under the legislation applying in England, Northern Ireland or Scotland.

Close to 90% of your working time will be spent travelling within your allocated area and visiting customers, although wider travel and occasional overnight stays may be required. You will receive mobile-working and lone-worker safety equipment and may be eligible to apply for an HMRC company-car scheme. A structured 12-week full time training programme and ongoing peer support will be provided.

This public-facing role requires you to speak English fluently so you can communicate clearly, confidently and effectively when explaining requirements, gathering information, negotiating payment arrangements and taking appropriate action. This job-related requirement will be assessed at interview.

Candidate webinars will be held on Teams at 10:00 on 27th Oct 2026 at 10am.

Candidate Information Session - Field Collections Team - Tues 27th Oct 26 @ 10am – Fill in form

Job description

  • Plan and manage an allocated caseload, prioritising work to achieve timely and effective outcomes.
  • Visit customers unannounced at homes and business premises, including unannounced visits, in accordance with operational instructions and personal-safety requirements.
  • Gather, verify and analyse relevant information to understand customer circumstances and inform make proportionate decisions.
  • Communicate clearly and confidently, balancing empathy and fairness with the need to explain HMRC requirements and secure compliance.
  • Collect payments and negotiate payments arrangement where appropriate.
  • Identify relevant assets and progress authorised enforcement activity in line with the legislation and procedures applicable to the location.
  • Maintain accurate digital records, complete administrative work and use Office 365 and other HMRC systems effectively.
  • Work flexibly across the operational area, including occasional overnight stays or varied attendance where business needs require this and appropriate notice is given.
  • Represent HMRC professionally and uphold the Civil Service values in every customer and stakeholder interaction.
  • This is a field-based role and 90% of your working time is spent travelling and visiting customers.
  • You will work within an allocated geographical area, but wider travel may be required to meet operational needs.
  • Occasional overnight stays may be required for work or training, with notice provided and expenses handled under the applicable policy.
  • The role is not suitable for contractual homeworking because of its mobile and customer-facing requirements.
  • Approved equipment will be provided to support mobile working. Vehicle arrangements and eligibility will be explained during the recruitment or onboarding process.

Successful candidates will receive a structured training programme and ongoing workplace support. The training will cover the knowledge, systems, customer-handling skills, safety requirements and operational procedures needed for the role. You will undertake a bespoke 12-week training and development programme, when full-time working is required.

Person specification

As an influential officer of the Field Collections Team, you will need to be organised, driven, manage your own time effectively, and communicate successfully. At times you will be an empathic civil servant and at other times an authoritative, assured and confident debt collection officer. Under challenging circumstances, you will operate fairly in your dealings with members of the public and with external and internal stakeholders.

Be part of a large and extremely engaged nationwide team who are inclusive, flexible, adaptable and creative in solving problems and dealing with change.

Whilst on the road, which is 90% of your time, you will be an ambassador for HMRC. You will take customer service, etiquette and fairness seriously and demonstrate it professionally. You will be self-motivated and always looking to develop your expertise.

Use your knowledge to remind customers about relevant laws, including Taking Control of Goods (England), Levy Distraint (Northern Ireland), and Summary Warrant actions (Scotland).

Use available digital platforms and apply good judgement to make decisions to progress each case and deal with associated queries.

Field Collections operates flexibly to maximise contact with customers and 90% of the working day is spent “on the road” calling at premises unannounced. Advance notice will be provided regarding any overnight stays required for business purposes or training, and all applicable expenses will be reimbursed.
Field Collections Team operates across the United Kingdom with a flexible working setup, allowing colleagues to work remotely during the week.

Essential Criteria:

  • Strong planning and organisational skills to deliver consistently high outputs in a fastpaced environment.
  • Flexibility and ability to deliver a great customer experience with internal and external exposure across many levels of seniority.
  • Adaptable and capable of operating in dynamic, fast-paced environments; comfortable working within tight deadlines and under pressure.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills with a proven ability to influence and engage others effectively.
  • Skilled in gathering and analysing data to make sound, evidence-based decisions (including when they are unpopular).
  • Highly observant, ensuring all relevant information is considered.
  • Proficient in Office 365.
  • Manage your own caseload and undertake related administrative tasks.
  • Strong time management and communication skills.
  • A Full UK Driving Licence.

Location

About the job

Job summary

Across government, service design plays a critical role in ensuring that digital services are user-centred, accessible and effective. As organisations adopt enterprise platforms such as Salesforce, there is an increasing need to design end-to-end services that are not only technically robust but also intuitive, inclusive and aligned with user needs. Ofgem plays a vital role in the UK’s energy system, protecting consumers and enabling a more secure, fair and sustainable energy future, and well-designed digital services are essential to delivering this mission.

Ofgem is on an ambitious transformation journey. Within the Digital, Data and Security Services (DDSS) directorate, we are delivering a range of digital, data and AI initiatives, including the expansion of Salesforce-based services. As part of this, we are strengthening our service design capability to ensure that solutions are coherent, scalable and deliver consistent user experiences across the organisation.

As a Senior Service Designer (Salesforce), you will lead the design of end-to-end Salesforce-enabled services. You will work across multidisciplinary teams to shape service journeys, workflows and interactions, ensuring they meet user needs while aligning with technical constraints and organisational priorities. You will act as a bridge between business stakeholders and technical teams, ensuring that design intent is clear, feasible and effectively delivered.

This is a senior role requiring strong experience in service design, user-centred design approaches and the ability to influence across complex delivery environments.

Job description

You will be responsible for:

  • Leading the design of end-to-end Salesforce services, ensuring consistent, user-centred experiences across multiple touchpoints.
  • Working closely with stakeholders to understand business requirements and translate them into effective service designs and user journeys.
  • Facilitating workshops and design sessions to align stakeholders, gather insight and drive collaborative design approaches.
  • Producing clear design artefacts, including journey maps, service blueprints and documentation to support delivery teams.
  • Ensuring that designs are accessible, inclusive and aligned with government standards and best practice.
  • Collaborating with architects, developers and systems integrators to ensure that designs are technically feasible and aligned with platform capabilities.
  • Driving continuous improvement through iterative design, using user research, analytics and feedback to refine services.
  • Providing design assurance, ensuring that solutions meet organisational standards and deliver intended outcomes.
  • Mentoring and supporting other designers, contributing to capability building and embedding user-centred design practices across teams.
  • Championing service design within the organisation, promoting its value in delivering effective digital services.

Person specification

Essential Criteria

  • Deep experience of designing end-to-end Salesforce service journeys using user- centered design methods (Lead Criteria)
  • Deep understanding of Government Service design frameworks (Lead Criteria)
  • Strong ability to clearly explain complex problems and ideas to teams or stakeholders outside of design
  • Strong experience acting as liaison between business teams and technical delivery partners
  • Background in creating clear documentation of design decisions, research findings, and reusable service patterns for delivery and implementation teams.

Holds or can obtain the following certifications or equivalent within 6 months:

  • Salesforce Strategy Designer
  • Salesforce UX Designer

Desirable Criteria

  • Service design across other automation PaaS solutions.

title: Sr. Director, Compliance and Ethics
description:
Your Role

As Senior Director, Compliance & Ethics at Ascendiun you will lead the enterprise-wide compliance and ethics program across all affiliates, business units, products, services and activities.

You will oversee preventive, detective and remedial controls; policies and procedures; workforce training and communications; testing, auditing, monitoring and reporting; and remediation of control deficiencies. Program areas include the Code of Conduct, compliance policies and investigations, anti-bribery, anti-kickback and anti-corruption, exclusion lists, conflicts of interest and other compliance and ethics initiatives.

Reporting directly to Ascendiun’s Chief Risk and Compliance Officer, you will primarily lead the enterprise-wide program and may take on additional responsibilities or support the Chief Compliance & Ethics Officer’s other initiatives as needed.

Your Work

In this role, you will:

  • Lead, implement, and maintain an effective enterprise-wide Corporate Compliance and Ethics Program, including but not limited to managing compliance Whistleblower programs, anti-corruption programs, maintaining effective compliance policies and procedures, effective compliance training, awareness, and communications programs.
  • Manage and conduct enterprise-wide compliance investigations. Maintain a clear, comprehensive, and integrated enterprise compliance investigation protocol. Oversee all internal and external hotline and compliance reporting channels. Prepare comprehensive investigation summary reports. Ensure proper corrective action and remedial measures are taken once investigations are completed.
  • Build, develop, and lead teams of Compliance & Ethics professionals to ensure robust and effective, preventive, detective and remedial programs and controls throughout the Company’s operations.
  • Lead and model collaborations with compliance resources across the Ascendiun Family of Companies (e.g., Human Resources Employee Relations, IT Security, Legal, Internal Audit) and operational areas to promote the C&E Program and encourage ethical behavior at all levels.
  • Provide regulatory and compliance industry standards support and guidance, develop and implement enterprise-wide compliance policies, procedures, and develop training programs to effect compliance with legal and regulatory standards.
  • Research, identify, review, and summarize new and existing regulations; maintain awareness of industry trends and regulatory actions; and communicate impact of these changes to the Ascendiun Family of Companies and the Chief Risk and Compliance Officer (CRCO).

Your Knowledge and Experience

  • Requires bachelor’s degree or High School Diploma/GED and 4 years of additional relevant experience in lieu of a degree
  • Requires 12 years of legal, or health care compliance and ethics experience with increasingly progressive responsibility including Director-level Compliance experience
  • Requires functional subject matter expertise in compliance investigations, compliance hotlines/reporting, compliance training and communications, anti-corruption/anti-bribery/anti-kickback, government contracting, exclusion lists, corporate ethics, business partner and third-party risk management, and applicable laws and regulations
  • Requires 6 years of prior people management experience with direct responsibility for supervising, coaching, and evaluating direct reports
  • Require Director-level, Deputy Chief Compliance Officer, and/or Federal Law Enforcement experience
  • Requires excellent verbal and written communication and relationship building skills to effectively interact with senior management team, board members, providers, or federal and state regulators.
  • Requires strong independent judgment, problem-solving, critical, and analytical thinking skills, including a “moral compass” and high integrity
  • Juris Doctor (JD) from an ABA accredited law school and admission to practice law in one or more U.S. States (CA strongly preferred) preferred
  • Certified Healthcare Certification (CHC) or Certified Compliance and Ethics Professional Certification (CCEP), and experience and knowledge of compliance or risk incident management software preferred
  • Experience with writing and implementing policies and procedures, performing risk assessments, documenting controls and control gaps, remediating control gaps, and delivering and maintaining a robust and effective compliance and ethics program preferred

Hybrid

This role requires employees to be in-office based on our hybrid workplace model, balancing purposeful in-person collaboration with flexibility. For most teams, this means coming into the office two days each week.

Employees living more than 50 miles from an office location will work with their manager to determine in-office time based on business need.

title: Voids Officer
description:
Organisation: London Borough of Waltham Forest

Salary: £40,182 - £42,060

Contract Type: Fixed Term

Working hours per week: 36

Application Deadline: 15/11/2026

Proposed Interview Date(s): TBC

Reference: 2396

About Us:

Bursting with culture, energy, and opportunity, the London Borough of Waltham Forest is a fantastic and exciting place to work.

We are a highly ambitious borough. Driven by culture and the innate creativity of our residents, we have developed new and innovative ways to build our communities. Our Council is relentlessly resident-focused, insight-led, digitally driven and commercially minded; a Council focused on meeting the needs of our existing and future residents.

London Borough of Waltham Forest is one of the Mayor of London’s Good Work Standard employers. This accreditation is a proof of our commitment to creating a healthy, fair and inclusive workplace. This includes fair pay and conditions, workplace well-being, skills and progression and diversity and recruitment.

About the role:

We are looking for an enthusiastic and proactive Voids Officer (Downsizing & Mutual Exchange) to join our Central Voids Team on a 12-month fixed-term basis.

This is an exciting opportunity to be part of a new pilot programme designed to tackle under-occupation, reduce overcrowding and help make better use of the Council's housing stock. Working at the heart of our Voids Service, you will provide intensive, end-to-end support to tenants who are looking to downsize or move through Mutual Exchange, helping them navigate what can often be a complex and emotional process.

You will proactively engage with tenants, carry out home visits, identify suitable housing options and provide practical support throughout the moving journey. By helping residents move into homes that better meet their needs, you will play a key role in freeing up larger family homes, reducing reliance on temporary accommodation and improving housing outcomes for local residents.

This role is ideal for someone with a strong customer-focus, excellent organisational skills and a passion for helping residents achieve positive housing outcomes. You will work closely with colleagues across Voids, Allocations, and Tenancy Management and services to deliver ambitious targets and measurable results.

This is a fixed-term appointment for 12 months and forms part of a pilot programme focused on increasing downsizing and Mutual Exchange activity across the borough.

>> Click here to download the Role Profile <<

Key Responsibilities:

  • Proactively identify and engage with tenants who are under-occupying their homes and may benefit from downsizing.
  • Manage a caseload of downsizing and Mutual Exchange applications from initial enquiry through to successful move completion.
  • Undertake home visits and housing needs assessments to understand tenants' circumstances and housing requirements.
  • Provide practical, personalised support to residents throughout the moving process, including bidding, viewings, sign-ups, removals and utility transfers.
  • Support and facilitate Mutual Exchange opportunities for residents in our council stock wanting to downsize, including supporting tenants to register on HomeSwapper and identify suitable matches.
  • Ensure Mutual Exchange applications are processed efficiently and within statutory timescales.
  • Work closely with Allocations, Tenancy Management and Repairs teams to maximise housing mobility and minimise delays.
  • Support the allocation of suitable void properties to downsizing households and help maximise use of available housing stock.
  • Maintain accurate records, monitor performance data and contribute to the achievement of pilot outcomes and service KPIs.
  • Provide high-quality advice, guidance and customer service to residents, partners and stakeholders.
  • Contribute to reducing overcrowding, releasing larger family homes and supporting the Council's wider housing objectives.

Skills, Experience and Qualifications:

  • Experience of working within a housing, lettings, allocations, tenancy management, voids, housing options or customer service environment.
  • Experience of managing customer cases and delivering positive outcomes within challenging timescales.
  • Strong customer service skills with the ability to build trust and engage effectively with a diverse range of residents.
  • Excellent communication, negotiation and influencing skills, both written and verbal.
  • Experience of working with vulnerable residents and understanding the barriers they may face when moving home.
  • Good organisational and time management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and meet performance targets.
  • The ability to work independently whilst also contributing positively to team objectives.
  • Strong IT skills, including experience of using housing management systems and Microsoft Office applications.
  • Experience of maintaining accurate records, analysing information and producing reports.
  • An understanding of housing management, allocations, lettings, downsizing or Mutual Exchange processes would be advantageous.
  • GCSE English and Mathematics (or equivalent) and/or relevant housing-related qualification.

Terms and conditions:

The below terms and conditions apply to this role:

  • Satisfactory employment references and CIFAS identity checks;
  • Satisfactory declaration of interest;

  • As a public authority, we must ensure that members of staff in public-facing roles are able to speak fluent English. This means that they must have a command of spoken English, with confidence and accuracy, sufficient for the effective performance of their role. This requirement does not refer to any particular English language qualifications, regional or international accents, dialects, speech impediments or the tone of conversations. It does not require staff to speak only in English.

How to Apply:

Interested candidates are invited to submit their applications online by pressing the ‘Apply’ button below. This includes a supporting statement that outlines to us how your skills and experience make you a good candidate for this vacancy.

We reserve the right to close this vacancy early if we receive sufficient applications for the role. Therefore, if you are interested, please submit your application as early as possible.

Equal Opportunity Employer:

Waltham Forest is a diverse borough where diversity is valued and is integral to both, service delivery and employment of its staff. The Council is proud of its rich mix of communities and as the largest employer in the area, it works hard to respond to the changing needs of its population. We use our statutory duties on race, gender and disability equality and best practice in respect of age, faith and sexual orientation to ensure equality of opportunity in the workplace. The Council is committed to meeting its 4 equality objectives: - Promoting equality of opportunity - Opposing all forms of discrimination, intolerance and disadvantage - Ensuring our workforce reflects the diverse communities of Waltham Forest at all levels. - Providing fair, appropriate, accessible and excellent Services to all. Respecting Diversity is a core Council value.

title: 4254 Head of Knowledge, Information and Records Management
description:
• Job grade: Grade 6
  • Contract type: Permanent
  • Business area: Operational Effectiveness Group
  • Type of role: Knowledge and Information Management
  • Working pattern: Full-time, Job share, Part-time
  • Number of jobs available: 1

Location

Wales

About the job

Job summary

Head of Knowledge, Information and Records Management leads four teams providing information, knowledge, records and library services to Welsh Government.

The postholder acts as Departmental Records Officer (DRO) ensuring compliance with the public records act and that policies and systems are in place to manage our records in line with the regulation. The postholder works with others across the organisation and with Arms Length Bodies (ALBs) to ensure effective information management and provide advice on compliance, systems and support with issues. The postholder provides advice to inquiry response teams and e-discovery services to ensure that evidence is carefully selected and transferred.

As DRO the postholder ensures the secure transfer of records in or out of the organisation as part of machinery of government change. This includes engagement with the other party at all levels, providing advice and training as well as ensuring that the body has appropriate systems and mechanisms in place to manage the transferred records.

The DRO is responsible for the operational elements of records management who support the Electronic Records and Document Management System (EDRMS) and also manage the archiving of paper records and ongoing storage. DRO has oversight of the work to ensure compliance with Public Records act and Freedom of Information Act section 46. This role also ensures that all records work is aligned and that teams work together to achieve common goals as required.

Job description

As Head of Profession, the postholder is responsible for developing and leading the Knowledge and Information Management (KIM) profession across Welsh Government, providing advice and guiding and supporting recruitment for KIM posts. This includes providing advice and support on professional issues to KIM professionals in Culture Division as well as advice to senior leaders in Culture Division on KIM recruitment and professional matters.

The Head of Profession also represents Welsh Government in cross Civil Service groups and on professional groups. The postholder interacts on a regular basis with colleagues in other administrations, e.g. Government Digital Services, to share knowledge, benefit from expertise and ensure that records management in particular is aligned with National Archives requirements.

Also responsible for the Departmental Knowledge and Information Managers (DKIMs) network and ensuring that DKIMs have good communication both ways to support their work in championing good practice and resolving business issues. This forms part of wider work to promote good practice and develop better understanding of the importance of information management cross government.

Provide senior level KIM input on Security Board, Collaboration Scrutiny and Solution Design Authority (SDA).

As Chief Librarian the post is leads the development of the library services and oversees the WG Publications Archive in compliance with Re-use of Public Sector Information (PSI). The postholder also advises on copyright matters and use of the Open Government Licence.

Person specification

  1. Head of KIM Profession in Welsh Government. Leading and developing the profession, providing advice across the profession. Recruitment and continuous professional development of KIM teams. Identifying areas individuals and teams need to deliver, building KIM skills, capability and talent across the department.
  2. Carry out the responsibilities of the Departmental Records Officer (DRO) as set out in Annex C of the Code of Practice on the management of records issued under section 46 of the Freedom of Information Act 2000
  3. Set the strategic direction for Welsh Government’s digital information, including on new platforms, initiating new KIM programmes as required
  4. Persuading and influencing senior leaders about the importance of good information and knowledge management.
  5. Strategic business ownership and contract management for Welsh Government digital and paper records system, ensure compliance with procurement rules, value for money and fitness and flexibility for the future
  6. Manage KIM budget which includes staff costs for a team of around 35 at present, contract management for records and e-discovery systems and library. Negotiate funding to ensure the organisation is compliant and escalate any risk arising from the budget.
  7. Working with Inquiry response teams to ensure KIM responds to their eDiscovery needs and timescales, providing e-discovery services and information management expertise.
  8. Lead on the strategic development of library services, including the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and KIM.
  9. Working with other organisations in Government on mutually beneficial KIM work, representing the Welsh Government in UK KIM fora and other professional bodies and learning from best practice across the UK and beyond.
  10. Leading on the Copyright and Re-use of Public Sector Information, including the re-use of data. Policy lead in discussions with The National Archive (TNA) on Crown Copyright.
  11. Act as lead contact with TNA as set out in the Memorandum of Understanding.
  12. Compliance with section 46 of the Freedom of Information Act which defines the DRO role.

title: Airside Experience Specialist
description:
As an Airside Experience Specialist, you are the face of our private aviation terminal, delivering a seamless, personalized, and welcoming experience for every guest, crew member, and aircraft in our care. In this dynamic role, you'll combine exceptional hospitality with hands-on operational support to ensure our guests feel cared for, from wheels down to wheels up.

You’ll operate ground service equipment and perform aircraft ground services while engaging guests with professionalism and a service-first mindset. This role requires schedule flexibility, including nights, weekends and holidays, and the ability to thrive in outdoor environments around active aircraft and in varying weather conditions.

If you enjoy creating memorable guest experiences in a fast-paced, luxury-driven environment – and you're excited by the energy of the runway – this is the role for you.

(Other duties may be assigned)

  • Work as part of a team to conduct airside operations safely and efficiently in accordance with established policies and standard operating procedures (SOPs) ensuring efficient and accurate communication through various methods to accomplish operational tasks.
  • Collaborate, cooperate, and work closely with all team members, guests, clients, vendors, and aircraft crewmembers to ensure service needs are met. Services include, but are not limited to, fueling, de-icing, lavatory, ground power and potable water services, parking, marshalling, wing walking, delivering catering and towing.
  • Proactively prepare for arriving/departing aircraft, identify and perform open job tasks, and immediately speak up and/or point out observed safety concerns to all stakeholders.
  • Operate and drive ground service equipment such as fuel trucks, de-icing trucks, ground power units, tugs, stair trucks, etc.
  • Load and unload luggage and other cargo into/out of aircraft and from/into the PAT, guest vehicle, or other mode of transportation.
  • Provide professional and friendly guest service while exhibiting a positive and helpful attitude to everyone at all times ensuring guests always receive an exceptional experience.
  • Offer safe, convenient, and courteous transportation when driving shuttle vehicle to transport guests, luggage and cargo.
  • Maintain safe, clean, and secure ramps and operations.
  • Fuel handling, including fuel quality control, fuel receipt, inventory and maintaining accurate related documentation.
  • Understand, comply with, and enforce all operational, safety, and guest service requirements for all aspects of the job.
  • Stop work when an unsafe condition or act is likely to cause harm to people, the environment, Company or guest assets, or the Company’s reputation if the work continues. Report concerns to the appropriate manager and cooperate in addressing the unsafe act or condition.
  • Follow emergency response procedures during critical events.
  • Understand, comply with, and enforce all security (physical, cyber and data) protocols as dictated by both Signature Aviation and the airport.
  • Create accurate records pertaining to time worked and activities and services performed.

Minimum Education and/or Experience:

  • High School Diploma or General Education Degree (GED).
  • Minimum of 18 years of age.
  • Ability to pass company background checks (criminal and motor vehicle), drug tests, meet airport background check requirements to receive and maintain an airport security badge, and be insurable by the Company's applicable insurance policies.
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the jurisdiction of employment.
  • Excellent vision and coordination to move and/or direct aircraft and visually inspect aircraft fuel. Ability to pass a color vision test for purposes of inspecting aviation fuel.
  • Must possess a valid state driver’s license. In some locations a commercial driver’s license (CDL) is required as dictated by local regulations and business needs.
  • Must be able to exercise good judgment and follow directions/directives from supervisor/management.
  • Preferred: Three (3) to six (6) months experience and/or training in aviation, customer service or other related field; or equivalent combination of education and experience and/or training.

Additional knowledge and essential skills:

  • Hospitality Skills: Excellent guest service skills with an energetic, outgoing, and guest-obsessed personality. Must be able to anticipate guest needs and prioritize guest requests and job responsibilities by exhibiting a keen ability to multi-task in a fast-paced environment. Must be able to maintain professionalism and confidentiality.
  • Language Skills: Ability to read and comprehend documents such as safety rules, operating instructions, and procedure manuals, and for safety-sensitive tasks, in English. Clearly communicate in English with others in person, via telephone, radio communicators, and in writing.
  • Math Skills: Ability to perform simple arithmetic (e.g., addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, percentages, fractions, angles, degrees, time).
  • Physical Ability: Must be able to physically enter/exit and operate motor vehicles and ground support equipment such as fuel trucks, vans, tugs, and cars. Must be able to perform various functions safely and efficiently (e.g., fueling, de-icing) from elevated heights.
  • Critical Thinking / Reasoning Ability: Ability to carry out multi-step instructions. Ability to deal with standardized situations with only occasional or no variables.
  • Interpersonal Skills: Ability to get along and work well with others. Excellent interpersonal skills for effective collaboration with team members and service to guests.
  • Multitasking: Ability to handle multiple tasks simultaneously while maintaining attention to detail.
  • Computer Skills: Ability to use a computer and email, learn necessary company software, and pass computer-based training modules.
  • Task Management: Ability to successfully and timely complete Signature’s training programs.

Pay ranges vary based on multiple factors, including, without limitation, skill sets, education, shift worked, responsibilities, seniority, geographical market, merit, output, productivity, prior training or experience, and travel. The pay range for this position is $23.00 / hour.
