title: Environmental Response Specialist
description:
Classification: Grid 27, BCGEU Membership

Office Location: Fort St John

Salary: $88,386.22 – $100,776.50 – Permanent Full-Time, based on a 35-hour work week.
An additional 20.75% Job Family Market Multiplier will be added to the posted salary.
An additional 3% Location Allowance will be added to posted salary for northern location.

About the Job:
The Environmental Response Specialist (Specialist) protects the environment and the public by providing authoritative and technical expertise on the management, assessment and remediation associated with spillage and discharges from oil and gas activities. This is achieved through administration and enforcement of the Energy Resource Activities Act (ERAA), the Environmental Management Act (EMA), and other applicable regulations.

The Specialist works through the Supervisor, Environmental Management & Restoration Verification to enhance systematic approaches, policies, and procedures to ensure consistent and appropriate management and documentation of spillage from oil and gas activities. The Specialist also works to ensure and maintain coordinated approaches and interaction with other related agencies.

Organization Chart:
Commissioner, Chief Executive Officer
Executive Vice President, Safety & Compliance
Vice President, Compliance & Operations
Executive Director, ALP & Operations
Supervisor, Environmental Management & Restoration Verification
Environmental Response Specialist

Ensure consistent management and follow up to incident reports involving spills or releases.

Conduct follow up investigation as required which may involve site visits to determine that the appropriate response actions were taken and follow up at sites with longer term remediation issues.

Gather evidence for legal proceedings and testifying in court where required.

Provide operational support for BCER ambient air quality monitoring systems including equipment deployment, filter and gas canister replacement, etc.

Provide technical support for BCER ambient air quality monitoring equipment involving the use of specialized hardware and software.

Provide authoritative, technical direction to industry, environmental consultants, governments, staff, stakeholders and the public for acceptable waste management policy, legislation, handling, storage, disposal or discharge for the upstream oil and gas industry.

Prepare technical recommendation and directions to the Supervisor, regarding, environmental impacts, based upon technical review and analysis of preliminary and detailed site investigation reports, remediation plans and confirmation of remediation reports.

Audit, or investigate non-compliance of a statutory authorizations, evaluate and characterize environmental impacts and summarize information in report form and determines the most effective method to mitigate environmental impacts of a non-compliance through technical assessment, negotiations and problem resolution.

Review, assess and provide technical advice and recommendations to environmental protection plans produced by QEP’s.

Provide technical assessment on reports submitted on environmental issues, identify concerns of others (agencies, stakeholders and elected officials) resolving differences and formulating strategies on proposed discharges.

Perform and support environmental monitoring actions undertaken by the BCER.

Answer queries from and provides technical advice to, BCER staff, Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy, Ministry of Energy, Mines and Low Carbon Innovation, other government agencies, QEP’s, the public and stakeholders regarding oil and gas field operations waste management.

Plan, organize and represent the BCER at technical seminars, stakeholder events, staff training and development opportunities.

Maintain and update a comprehensive knowledge of oil and gas field waste materials, water, well drilling/completion/workover fluids, gases, and other wastes as well as mitigative and remediation technologies through independent research and attending conferences, seminars, and training courses.

Education:
Bachelor’s Degree from a recognized post-secondary institution in a related field such as such as Chemistry, Biology, Earth Sciences, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Protection, Spill Response, Emergency Management and three years of relevant experience; or

Diploma from a recognized post-secondary institution in a relevant field such as such as Chemistry, Biology, Earth Sciences, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Protection, Spill Response, Emergency Management and five years of relevant experience.

An equivalent combination of education, training and experience may be considered.

Experience:
Demonstrated experience in environmental emergency response under the Environmental Management Act including attending or responding to hazardous materials spills, assessing spill related hazards or threats to health or the environment, determining if spill response actions are necessary to address hazards or threats, and monitoring or supervising spill response actions.

Demonstrated experience in environmental protection and pollution prevention under the Environmental Management Act including assessing environmental impacts or pollution associated with discharges of waste to the environment and characterizing and managing waste materials.

Demonstrated experience in emergency management (hazmat emergency response, spill response, cleanup and remediation, fire department suppression activities, transportation of dangerous goods, spill contingency planning, oil spill response).

Key Competencies
Conflict Management
The ability to effectively identify, address, and work to resolve conflicts within the organization or externally. It involves managing risks, fostering positive working relationships, and promoting a collaborative and productive work environment.

Influence
The ability to guide and shape others’ understanding of key issues and priorities to achieve corporate goals while appreciating cultural and political nuances. It involves using strategic communication and relationship building to effectively influence and align others to support organizational objectives.

Problem Solving and Judgement
The ability to systematically analyze problems, identify root causes, evaluate potential solutions, and make sound decisions to address challenges and achieve desired outcomes.

Team Building
The ability to develop group identity, facilitate decision-making, and foster open and effective communication within diverse teams across the organization. It involves building and sustaining trust through integrity, concern for others, consistent behaviour, following through on commitments, and promoting open communication.

If you are interested in applying for this role and meet the minimum selection criteria, please select “Apply Now” and submit your application prior to the closing date. title: Embedded Software Engineer II / III - Flight Deck Avionics
description:
When you join Honeywell Aerospace, you become a member of our global team of thinkers, innovators, dreamers and doers who make the things that make the future.

Honeywell Aerospace's Anthem™ Integrated Flight Deck is the Future of Flight

Honeywell's Anthem™ Integrated Flight Deck is the industry's 1st Cloud-Connected "Always-On" Integrated Cockpit system, featuring cloud-native communications, navigation, and surveillance systems, powered by a flexible software platform that can be customized for virtually every type of aircraft, from passenger planes and business aircraft to defense, general aviation and the rapidly emerging class of Advanced Air-Mobility (AAM) vehicles.

Honeywell Aerospace’s newest and most advanced Flight Deck will herald a new age of aviation where connectivity will help enable true autonomy.

Honeywell Anthem™ is breaking new ground in Avionics design and pilot-machine interface, with the goal of making pilots’ jobs easier, safer and more intuitive. Anthem allows pilots to configure their own cockpit based on mission and phase of flight.

The revolutionary Anthem™ Integrated Flight Deck delivers unparalleled levels of connectivity, a modern and intuitive user interface, and a highly scalable, customizable design — bringing flexibility, clarity, and simplicity to an industry that demands precision. #Anthem

It’s not just an upgrade—it’s the next era of flight.

As a Software Engr, within our Next-Generation Avionics (NGA) group, you will join a team responsible for the design, architecture and deployment of cutting-edge Avionics Display System solutions. As part of the Flight Displays software team, you will have responsibilities across the design, development, software integration and verification of Core Displays to be hosted on the Anthem Next Generation Avionics Platform.

The Next Generation Avionics (NGA) Flight Displays team is at the forefront of developing innovative solutions that enhance the situational awareness and decision-making capabilities of pilots.

As a flagship product, the Anthem Integrated Flight Deck System is not just another avionics product; it is a visionary endeavor that employs cutting-edge technologies to redefine how pilots interact with flight information and aircraft systems.

Key Responsibilities

  • You will work closely with a passionate team of engineers and designers to create and implement forward-thinking software solutions for our cutting-edge Avionics Flight Display Systems.
  • Support the design, development and implementation of robust, high-quality software solutions for cutting-edge Flight Display System platforms, services and/or applications, ensuring high performance, reliability, and functionality
  • Craft and implement high-level code, ensuring our technology is both robust and user-friendly
  • Create test cases for software based upon use cases derived from the system and software requirements
  • Participate in the complete software development lifecycle, from concept through implementation and verification
  • Enjoy increasing ownership of software modules, deliver innovative features, implement functionalities and contribute to the overall advancement of technology.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure seamless integration of software with existing avionics systems.
  • Feature Definition
  • Stay curious and engaged with the latest advancements in avionics technology and software engineering practices

Our team welcomes those with expertise in either low-level embedded software development OR expertise in high-level embedded, user application, and/or graphics areas of focus, as well as engineers possessing experience across both domains

YOU MUST HAVE

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in a technical discipline such as Engineering, Software, or Computer Science degree
  • Embedded software development experience ~1.5-2+ years (Engr II), ~4-5 years (Advanced/Engr III)
  • Our team welcomes those with expertise in either low-level embedded software development OR expertise in high-level embedded, user application, and/or graphics/displays areas of focus, as well as engineers possessing experience across both domains
  • Competence in programming, with preference to languages such as C/C++, Python, Open GL, Vulkan etc.

WE VALUE

  • Understanding of software development lifecycles, methodologies and tools.
  • Experience with Avionics products is of a PLUS i.e. Displays & Graphics, Flight Mgmt, Flight Planning, Flight Controls, Flight Displays (PFD), Traffic Collision Avoidance (TCAS), Crew Alert Messaging (CAS), Terrain, Radios, etc
  • Experience developing software in a Real-Time Operating System (RTOS)
  • Object oriented development experience
  • Knowledge of software change management practices
  • Knowledge of software certification requirements and documentation
  • Experience with DO-178C is of value
  • Passion for innovation and continuous learning
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills

BENEFITS

Beyond a performance-driven salary, you'll work alongside dedicated experts on technology that's advancing aviation. As a Honeywell Aerospace employee, you're eligible for a comprehensive benefits package that includes:

  • Employer-subsidized medical, dental, vision and life insurance
  • Short-term and long-term disability coverage
  • 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts and health savings accounts
  • Employee assistance program and educational assistance
  • Parental leave and 12 paid holidays
  • Paid time off for vacation, personal and sick time

Explore your benefits:

U.S. PERSON REQUIREMENTS

Due to compliance with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidate must be a U.S. Person, which is defined as, a U.S. citizen, a U.S. permanent resident, or have protected status in the U.S. under asylum or refugee status or have the ability to obtain an export authorization.​

ABOUT HONEYWELL AEROSPACE

Join a company that's reintroducing itself to the aviation community we've helped advance for more than a century. At Honeywell Aerospace (NASDAQ: HONA), we're launching as an independent, publicly traded aerospace and defense company built on a legacy of operational excellence and mission-focused execution.

Our new brand identity pairs that heritage with real momentum, as we build technology that helps pilots navigate with confidence, aircraft operate more efficiently, and operators stay ahead of change. With our systems on board 90% of the world's aircraft, your work here has reach that's rare to find anywhere else.

Focusing on our customers, investing in innovation, and building a culture of accountability and performance is how we're shaping what comes next.

Every horizon. Every mission. Every day.

ABOUT ELECTRONIC SOLUTIONS

Honeywell Aerospace products and services are found on aircraft across commercial aviation, defense and space — from engines and cockpit electronics to cabin systems, mechanical components and connectivity solutions. Our technology helps operators fly more safely, reduce fuel consumption, improve on-time performance and deliver a better experience for the people on board.

As aviation continues to evolve, we're also developing systems to support autonomous and supersonic platforms, bringing the same focus on safety and efficiency to the next era of flight. With approximately 36,000 employees worldwide and net sales of $17.4B in 2025, Honeywell Aerospace is one of the largest dedicated aerospace companies in the world. Explore our businesses:

Electronic Solutions develops the avionics, navigation systems, sensors and electromagnetic defense technology that help aircraft perform safely and with precision. Our systems are on board 90% of the world's aircraft — serving commercial aviation, defense and space operators from integrated flight deck platforms with 30-plus years in service to radiation-hardened systems trusted for human spaceflight.

title: Building Inspector
description:
• $113k - $128k + 12% Superannuation

  • Permanent Full Time

  • Based at our Civic Centre in Nunawading

At Whitehorse City Council, community is at the heart of everything we do. To stay ahead of and best respond to the evolving changes and needs of the community, the organisation is undertaking an exciting journey that will transform ways of working and will empower employees to be innovative and constantly striving towards providing excellent customer experience at all times. The five pillars of our organisation focus on:

  • Excellent Customer Experience and Service Delivery
  • Great Organisational Culture
  • Innovation and Continuous Improvement
  • Good Governance and Integrity
  • Long Term Financial Sustainability

The role:

This position has a strong customer service ethos and will require a proactive and solution orientated approach to all matters to achieve high-quality outcomes. As a Building Inspector you will be responsible for providing information and assistance to members of the community including clients about policies and legislation, including; Building Control responsibilities of Council and the Building Regulations.

To manage enforcement of Building Regulations for building safety and regulatory compliance within the Whitehorse Municipality including mandatory & building enforcement inspections

The Building Services Team has a primary function within the Whitehorse Municipality to ensure ongoing legislative and statutory process for building safety, building enforcement and building related permitting and record keeping.

The team looks after Building enforcement functions, high risk buildings, Public Protection, Swimming pool and Spa safety, building permitting service, Reports and Consents, Essential Safety Measures, Places of Public Entertainment permitting, building investigations, customer enquiry response, emergency response and issuing Building Notices and Orders for both the organisation and the community.

This enables team members to be exposed to all facets of the Building Surveying profession, encouraging growth, continuous improvement, learning and upskilling. In this diverse role.

About you:

To be considered for this position you will have:

  • Victorian Building & Plumbing Commission, Registration as Unlimited Building Inspector.
  • Minimum 2 years in mandatory building and audit site inspection experience.
  • Minimum 2 Years Local Government Building Services experience including Inspections, Report and Consent, Pool Compliance, Place of Public Entertainment, ESSMs Audits & Public Protection.
  • Ability to undertake swimming pool and spa safety inspections, mandatory building and building enforcement inspections and associated enforcement functions
  • Well-developed interpersonal & IT skills in Pathway, CM, including verbal and written communication, negotiation, facilitation, and problem-solving skills.

In return, we will offer:

The ability to make a difference - Working at Whitehorse City Council you contribute to making a real difference in the lives of the community and those that live, learn, work or visit Whitehorse. Every day you really will see how the work you're involved in benefits the diverse community.

Career opportunities – engaging work and the opportunity to apply your skills and experience.

Reward & Recognition - extensive reward and recognition program, corporate learning offerings, study assistance and comprehensive leadership development programs.

Building Inspector

location: London and East Kilbride (followed by overseas placement)
description:

About the job

Job summary

A dynamic and impactful career at the forefront of world events.

Job description

Join the Diplomatic and Development (DD) Fast Stream at a pivotal moment in world affairs.

The DD Fast Stream, aimed at nurturing the next generation of leaders in diplomacy and development, operates within the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO). Our mission is to lead the Government’s diplomatic, development, and consular efforts worldwide. We champion the interests of British citizens, safeguard the UK’s security, uphold our values, combat poverty, and address global challenges alongside our international partners.

The FCDO is committed to recruiting a talented and diverse workforce that truly reflects the society we serve. As a dynamic and inclusive organisation, we work at the heart of global affairs, tackling complex international challenges and shaping the UK’s role on the world stage. The Fast Stream offers a demanding and rewarding entry point into this work. The programme will stretch your skills, expose you to fast-paced and high-impact roles, and give you the opportunity to make a real contribution from the outset.

From 2026, the FCDO will introduce a China Pathway as part of the DD Fast Stream which reflects the need to develop future leaders with a strong understanding of China’s political system, economy, language, culture, and global influence. The China Pathway complements the broad, generalist leadership development that sits at the heart of the DD Fast Stream. DD Fast Streamers will be able to apply for and join the China Pathway in their first two years. Fast Streamers will continue to develop core diplomatic and policy skills, while gaining more sustained experience in China-facing roles and, where appropriate, language capability. This approach allows the FCDO to strengthen its long-term capability in a critical policy area, while maintaining the flexibility, breadth and resilience expected of future FCDO leaders.

Please note: The Final Selection Board for the DD Fast Stream will be conducted in person in London on selected dates. Candidates must be in the UK and available to attend their allocated assessment in person during January and February 2027. While assessments are expected to conclude within this period, a small number may extend into early March. Flexibility to attend in person is therefore essential.

Person specification

You must be a British citizen (those with dual nationality may apply)
Resided in the UK for at least 5 of the previous 10 years, including a consecutive 12-month period
You need to have or be on track to receive a 2:2 degree, degree apprenticeship or higher in any subject
Existing civil servants can apply without a degree

Seize the unique opportunity to work on critical issues at the heart of global events. This scheme lays the perfect foundation for promotion and long-term career growth.

Joining as a permanent employee of the FCDO, benefits include the Civil Service Pension Scheme, recognised language qualifications, season ticket loans, sports and social activities, childcare assistance, diversity support/networks/forums and more.

Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Selection process details

Application Process

There are several phases in the Fast Stream application process. Some of these assessments are multimedia in that they present information in video, audio, graphical or visual formats, as well as text. We hope you find it an engaging process and one that gives you a real insight into the role of a fast streamer.

At the initial application stage you will be asked to complete some background information which will include some diversity questions - which are for monitoring purposes only and will have no bearing on selection outcomes - along with the opportunity to identify your preferences in terms of the different Fast Stream schemes. You can choose up to three.

When you apply please register with a personal email address, and not a work or university email address.

Assessment Phases

Work-based scenarios - This test measures interpersonal skills, utilising video based scenarios and you are required to assess the effectiveness of various responses.

Case Study assessment - In this test you are required to take work based scenarios on an imaginary role, learning and responding to a series of challenges and situations and adapting to the changes you are presented with.

More information on the schemes that require additional information can be found https://www.civil-service-careers.gov.uk/fast-stream/fs-how-to-apply/fs-additional-information/

Fast Stream Assessment Centre - if you pass the above stages you'll be invited to attend a half day assessment centre. This will be conducted virtually online. The Fast Stream Assessment Centre (FSAC) reflects some of the key elements of a Fast Stream role and will consist of a written exercise, oral briefing exercise and a personal development conversation. Information will be presented via an app that you will be able to access remotely.

Final Selection Board - most schemes will then require a Final Selection Board . We'll ask you to attend this final assessment if you reach the required standard at FSAC. More information on the Final Selection Boards can be found https://www.civil-service-careers.gov.uk/fast-stream/fs-how-to-apply/fs-final-selection-board/

Location

Belfast Regional Centre - Erskine House, Birmingham, Bristol, Cardiff, Edinburgh, Glasgow, Leeds, Liverpool, Manchester, Nottingham, Newcastle Upon Tyne, Portsmouth, Worthing.

About the job

Job summary

Explore the world of HMRC Estates, where we lead the way in government property transformation. As a key player in one of the UK's largest property programmes, HMRC Estates offers safe, inclusive workplaces and exceptional career development opportunities. Our team is dedicated to delivering high-quality, user-friendly services that enable our colleagues to thrive in an environment where they truly belong. Watch the video below to meet some of our team and come and discover a career in your hands at HMRC.

Build a Career in Property with HMRC Estates

Professional Services & Estates Assurance is a Deputy Director (SCS1) led team of subject matter experts and specialist engineers covering, Construction, Digital, Data & Analytics and the Professional Services Team (Fire, H&S, Security, BIM, Sustainability & Building Services). Providing specialist advice, guidance, assurance and statutory compliance.

The Head of Physical Security & Resilience is responsible for the Physical Security specialism across Estates, anticipating challenges, providing strategic direction, driving performance and building the capability required to ensure the security of HMRC’s assets (staff, information, estate) and assuring HMRC is aligned to Government Security Minimum Standards. The role is also the Head of Security Profession for Estates.

Job description

This a critical role in Estates, responsible for the following: -

  • Threat & Risk Assurance (TaRA) process.
  • Physical Security Design Standards (PSDS).
  • Departmental Security Health Check (DSHC) Physical section.
  • Strategic direction for physical security improvements.
  • Level 2 Physical Security Assurance.

Physical Security and Resilience encompasses setting the standards across HMRC for: -

Physical measures

  • Hostile Vehicle Mitigation – HVM.
  • Walling & Door Systems.
  • Glazing.
  • Perimeter measures (Fencing & PID systems).

Electronic measures

  • Access Control Systems (AACS).
  • Intruder Detection Systems (IDS).
  • Video Surveillance Systems (VSS).
  • Integration of systems.

Person specification

The role will require an individual from a Security and/or Engineering background who is able to work alone or as part of a team, while exhibiting diplomacy, honesty and integrity.

They will require academic / professional qualifications / accreditation as follows:

  • Degree or equivalent in relevant subject(s).
  • Member or Fellow of a relevant security professional body such as CSyP; Security Institute; RSES.

The successful candidate will have to undertake the role of subject matter expert, and so applicants must already have the requisite knowledge and experience as they will not be afforded time to learn on the job.

Travel requirements:

  • Ability to travel UK wide in role.

Essential Criteria:

  • Applied physical security - Expert.
  • Risk understanding and mitigation - Expert.
  • Protective security - Practitioner.
  • Threat understanding - Practitioner.
  • Legal & regulatory environment and compliance - Working.
  • BIM; REVIT; CAD - Working.
  • Capable of operating efficiently across a wide variety of differing business areas.

Desirable Criteria:

The ideal candidate will be able to demonstrate they have successfully developed and implemented Physical Security Strategies within large / complex organisations, and will have circa:

  • Extensive General Security experience.
  • Built Environment Security experience.
  • Hold a Security/ Engineering qualification such as CEng / IEng.

Additional Security Information

This role requires the successful candidate to hold or be willing to hold Security Check (SC) clearance.

Further Location Information

Please ensure that you only apply for a location that you are willing and able to work from, as we will only make one offer of employment. Any additional notes included in a ‘Further Location Preferences (optional)’ field within the application form, will not be considered. Please be aware that you cannot change your location preference after submitting your application.

Office closures

For more information on where you might be working, review this information on our locations.

If your location preference is for one of the following sites, it’s important to note that these are not long-term sites for HMRC and we will require you to move to a new building in the future, subject to our location strategy and the applicable employee policies at that time.

These sites are:

  • Benton Park View, Newcastle - moving to Pilgrims Quarter, Newcastle
  • Lynx House, Portsmouth – moving to an alternative office in Portsmouth

You will be given more information about what this means at the job offer stage.

Leeds Locations

Qualifications

Degree or equivalent in relevant subject(s).

Memberships

Member or Fellow of a relevant security professional body such as CSyP; Security Institute; RSES.

Technical skills

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £58,541, HM Revenue and Customs contributes £16,959 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

HMRC operates both Flexible and Hybrid Working policies, allowing you to balance your work and personal commitments. We welcome applications from those who need to work a more flexible arrangement and will agree to requests where possible, considering our operational and customer service needs.

We offer a generous leave allowance, starting at 25 days and increasing by a day for every year of qualifying service up to a maximum of 30 days.

  • Pension - We make contributions to our colleagues’ Alpha pension equal to at least 28.97% of their salary.
  • Family friendly policies.

Hybrid working at HMRC

HMRC is an office-based organisation, and colleagues are expected to spend 60% of their working time in the office. Our offices provide opportunity for interaction, collaboration which aids learning and development and a sense of community. You will normally need to meet the minimum UK residency period as determined by the level of vetting being undertaken, which for SC is 5 years UK residency prior to your vetting application. Terms and Conditions

Customer facing roles in HMRC require the ability to converse at ease with members of the public and provide advice in accurate spoken English and/or Welsh where required. Where this is an essential requirement, this will be tested as part of the selection process.

HMRC has a presence in every region of the UK. For more information on where you might be working, review this information on our locations.

title: Director of Operational Excellence - Control Systems
description:
Join a company that's reintroducing itself to the aviation community we've helped advance for more than a century. At Honeywell Aerospace (NASDAQ: HONA), we're launching as an independent, publicly traded aerospace and defense company built on a legacy of operational excellence and mission-focused execution.

Our new brand identity pairs that heritage with real momentum, as we build technology that helps pilots navigate with confidence, aircraft operate more efficiently, and operators stay ahead of change. With our systems on board 90% of the world's aircraft, your work here has reach that's rare to find anywhere else.

Focusing on our customers, investing in innovation, and building a culture of accountability and performance is how we're shaping what comes next.

Every horizon. Every mission. Every day.

Honeywell Aerospace products and services are found on aircraft across commercial aviation, defense and space. We operate through three business areas:

Electronic Solutions develops the avionics, navigation systems, sensors and electromagnetic defense technology on board 90% of the world's aircraft

Engines & Power Systems provides the propulsion, auxiliary power and electrical systems that keep those aircraft flying

Control Systems supplies the thermal and motion control systems that support takeoff, landing and the safety of everyone on board

The AOS Leader serves as the strategic program coordinator for the SBG, Channel, or Function. This senior role is responsible for driving the expansion, adoption, and execution of the Aerospace Operating System (AOS) across the organization. The AOS Leader aligns leadership teams, coordinates improvement initiatives, embeds Lean and Agile methodologies, and fosters a culture of continuous improvement.

This position plays a critical part in enabling scalable, repeatable performance by coaching leaders, orchestrating strategic improvement processes, and ensuring the AOS framework becomes deeply institutionalized throughout the enterprise.

Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership & Coordination

  • Drive AOS expansion, including roadmap definition and coordination of activities across the unit.
  • Align with respective leadership teams to ensure adoption of AOS priorities, methods, and templates.
  • Coordinate, prioritize, and organize Improvement Events.
  • Manage or lead strategic business challenges to deliver on performance and improvement targets.

Continuous Improvement & Hoshin Kanri

  • Foster a continuous improvement mindset with practical Lean and Agile methods.
  • Support and/or orchestrate the Hoshin Kanri process.
  • Coach peers and key managers on the promotion and usage of AOS; serve as a mindset-change champion.

Community Building & Coaching

  • Advance AOS through recognition of success stories and role models of Lean and Agile leadership.
  • Coach and lead the AOS community and key enablers across the unit.
  • Drive, motivate, and manage AOS qualifications for employees.
  • Collaborate with the global AOS community to execute enterprise-wide strategy.

Organizational Impact

  • Act as an active member of the companywide AOS network.
  • Help establish and grow the AOS team (1 FTE per SBG/Channel/Function).
  • Ensure that improvement methodology is applied consistently and effectively across the business.

YOU MUST HAVE

  • Strong methodical knowledge of Lean and Agile Management methods, including AOS elements and practical application.
  • Proven project management expertise, preferably across both strategic and tactical initiatives.
  • Strong leadership skills aligned to Honeywell’s Aerospace People and Leadership Practices framework.
  • Deep competence in organizational change management.
  • Excellent communication skills appropriate for executive leadership environments.
  • Demonstrated success leading without formal authority and driving results.
  • Proven ability to motivate, coach, and develop diverse teams.
  • Skilled facilitator of Improvement Events and complex problem solving sessions.
  • Active and empathetic listener.
  • Capable of inspiring and influencing leaders without direct authority.
  • Convincing and proactive change driver.
  • Strong results and quality orientation.
  • Highly methodical, structured thinker with solid strategic insight.

WE VALUE

  • Experience establishing and sustaining networks or communities of practice.
  • Prior cross organizational leadership preferred.
  • Passionate about Lean, AOS Core Methods, and developing organizational capability.
  • Able to build networks that support AOS adoption.

Due to compliance with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidate must be a U.S. Person, which is defined as, a U.S. citizen, a U.S. permanent resident, or have protected status in the U.S. under asylum or refugee status or have the ability to obtain an export authorization.

BENEFITS

Beyond a performance-driven salary, you'll work alongside dedicated experts on technology that's advancing aviation. As a Honeywell Aerospace employee, you're eligible for a comprehensive benefits package that includes:

  • Employer-subsidized medical, dental, vision and life insurance
  • Short-term and long-term disability coverage
  • 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts and health savings accounts
  • Employee assistance program and educational assistance
  • Parental leave and 12 paid holidays
  • Paid time off for vacation, personal and sick time

Explore your benefits:

The application period for the job is estimated to be 40 days from the job posting date; however, this may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates.

title: Chief of Staff, Cyber Security and Digital Identity
location: Birmingham, Bristol, Cardiff, Darlington, Edinburgh, London, Salford
description:
• Job grade: Grade 7
  • Contract type: Permanent
  • Business area: Digital Foundations - Cyber Security & Digital Identity
  • Type of role: Business Management and Improvement, Policy, Senior leadership, Strategy
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time, Job share, Part-time

Location

Birmingham, Bristol, Cardiff, Darlington, Edinburgh, London, Salford

About the job

Job summary

At DSIT we’re all about improving people’s lives by maximising the potential of science & technology.

We accelerate innovation, investment and productivity through world-class science, research and development.

We use technology for good by ensuring new and existing technologies are safely developed and deployed across the UK, with the benefits more widely shared.

We are driving forward a modern digital government which gives citizens a more satisfying experience and their time back.

We do all this to enable the Government’s 5 national missions: kickstarting economic growth, making Britain a clean energy superpower, taking back our streets, breaking down barriers to opportunity and building an NHS fit for the future.

Above all, we focus on improving people’s lives. Whether it’s researching new treatments for disease, developing better batteries, reducing burdens through better public services, keeping children safe online, and much more, outcomes for citizens are at the heart of what we do.

Our Inclusive Environment

We offer flexible working benefits, employee well-being support and a great pension. We are enormously proud to be a Disability Confident Leader employer. We support candidates with adjustments throughout our recruitment process. Information about disability confidence and just some examples of the adjustments that you can request can be found in the reasonable adjustment section below.

Please note

Former DSIT recruitment campaigns are continuing as usual, but candidates should be aware that following the Government’s announcement on the changes to some civil service departments, roles will be subject to the machinery of government moves and will ultimately be in one of the new departments. We will provide more information if you are selected for a role. This work remains of high importance to the civil service, and we thank you for your continued interest.

Job description

The Cyber Security and Digital Identity directorate sits at the heart of the UK’s efforts to strengthen cyber resilience, drive growth through cyber and digital technologies, and ensure citizens and organisations can thrive in an increasingly digital world.

Our work spans cyber resilience, digital identity, technology innovation, growth and national security priorities. We work closely with Ministers, senior officials, industry, regulators, the National Cyber Security Centre and partners across government.

As Chief of Staff to the Director, you will operate as the Director’s principal strategic adviser, helping to lead and coordinate a large, complex and high-profile directorate. Working across policy, programme delivery and corporate functions, you will ensure the Director and Senior Leadership Team remain focused on their highest priorities, while driving organisational effectiveness, accountability and delivery.

This is a highly visible leadership role requiring exceptional judgement, strategic thinking and the ability to influence at senior levels. You will have significant autonomy and responsibility for coordinating activity across multiple teams, ensuring decisions are implemented, risks are managed and priorities are aligned.

You will act as the connective tissue between the Director, Senior Leadership Team, the directorate and the wider department, helping the directorate operate as a coherent, high-performing organisation. The role is suited to someone who combines strategic thinking with strong operational delivery skills and enjoys working at pace across a diverse and challenging portfolio.

Person specification

  • Act as principal adviser and trusted partner to the Director on strategic, operational and organisational matters.
  • Lead the Director’s Office and ensure effective coordination across all directorate priorities.
  • Drive implementation of Director and Senior Leadership Team decisions, ensuring delivery remains on track.
  • Lead directorate governance arrangements, including Senior Leadership Team and senior management forums.
  • Lead cross-directorate initiatives and priority projects on behalf of the Director.
  • Support organisational design, transformation and continuous improvement across the directorate.
  • Build strong relationships across DSIT, government, industry and delivery partners to advance directorate objectives.
  • Ensure the Director’s engagement with Ministers, senior officials and external stakeholders is strategically coordinated and effective.
  • Line manage staff within the Director’s Office.

As a line manager, you will be responsible for working with your members of staff to define their objectives, as well as managing their development and performance.

Essential Criteria

  • Excellent strategic thinking, with the ability to understand complex issues quickly and give clear advice.
  • Outstanding communication, briefing and drafting skills.
  • Strong leadership and influencing skills, with the ability to work effectively with senior stakeholders.
  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities.
  • Experience of driving delivery through others and holding teams to account for outcomes.
  • High levels of resilience, discretion and personal integrity.

Desirable Criteria

  • Experience in cyber security, digital, national security, technology or regulatory policy environments.
  • Experience supporting a Director General, Director or equivalent senior leadership team.

Behaviours

We'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:

  • Communicating and Influencing
  • Leadership
  • Making Effective Decisions

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £58,275, Department for Science, Innovation & Technology contributes £16,882 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

The Department for Science, Innovation and Technology offers a competitive mix of benefits including:

  • A culture of flexible working, such as job sharing, homeworking and compressed hours.
  • Automatic enrolment into the Civil Service Pension Scheme, with an employer contribution of 28.97%.
  • A minimum of 25 days of paid annual leave, increasing by 1 day per year up to a maximum of 30.
  • An extensive range of learning & professional development opportunities, which all staff are actively encouraged to pursue.
  • Access to a range of retail, travel and lifestyle employee discounts.

Office attendance

The Department operates a discretionary hybrid working policy, which provides for a combination of working hours from your place of work and from your home in the UK. The current expectation for staff is to attend the office or non-home based location for 40-60% of the time over the accounting period.

title: Incident Control and Business Continuity Manager
description:
• Job grade: Higher Executive Officer
  • Contract type: Permanent
  • Business area: HMRC - PPG - Estates
  • Type of role: Administration / Corporate Support, Analytical, Audit, Business Management and Improvement, Conflict Advisers, Estates, Governance, Health and Safety, Internal Audit, Investigation, Knowledge and Information Management, Legal Services, Operational Delivery, Planning, Policing, Property, Risk Management, Security
  • Working pattern: Full-time
  • Number of jobs available: 1

Location

Portsmouth - Lynx House

About the job

Job summary

Explore the world of HMRC Estates, where we lead the way in government property transformation. As a key player in one of the UK's largest property programmes, HMRC Estates offers safe, inclusive workplaces and exceptional career development opportunities. Our team is dedicated to delivering high-quality, user-friendly services that enable our colleagues to thrive in an environment where they truly belong. Watch the video below to meet some of our team and come and discover a career in your hands at HMRC.

Build a Career in Property with HMRC Estates

We are seeking an experienced Incident Control and Business Continuity Manager to join our Estates Workplace Operation team in Portsmouth, Hampshire.

This critical role will oversee day-to-day Incident Control and Business Continuity readiness for our HM Government Hub site, ensuring all HMRC Lines of Business and Other Government Departments can effectively respond to incidents and recover operations swiftly.

This role is central to the Estates Workplace Operation team, with responsibility for maintaining resilience and safety across government estates.

The Government Hubs Incident Control and Business Continuity Manager ensure sites are prepared to respond immediately and effectively to incidents, and that business continuity plans are embedded across the region.

Job description

  • Collaborate with Estates colleagues to ensure fire safety plans and emergency procedures for the Portsmouth Region meet all departmental and legal requirements.
  • Determine and communicate evacuation routes before and during incidents, instructing the Incident Control Team to direct staff and visitors accordingly.
  • Act as the lead during emergency situations, making critical decisions and ensuring instructions are followed to safeguard building occupants.
  • Liaise with and support emergency services, making informed decisions based on real-time information.
  • Lead the development and ongoing support of the incident team, including Incident Marshals and deputy ICOs, providing training as required.
  • Oversee and resource counter-terrorism activities in line with departmental standards, working in partnership with the Regional Security Manager and Head of Counter Terrorism.
  • Ensure all Lines of Business have comprehensive Business Continuity Plans (BCP), assisting in their development as necessary.
  • Prepare for and lead local Business Continuity and Counter Terrorism exercises.
  • Work with the Building Manager and Health and Safety Officer to prepare and maintain fire safety and emergency procedures.
  • Work with HMRC Estates colleagues to gain the assurances required; that any Fire Risk Assessments or Occupied Building Risk Assessments action points are completed by the appropriate owners of those tasks.
  • Collate and manage Personal Evacuation Plans (PEPs) for staff and visitors, integrating them into site evacuation procedures.
  • Resolve issues related to emergency procedures, such as staffing for Incident Marshal roles or implementation of risk assessment recommendations.
  • Conduct weekly building safety checks and address identified issues.
  • Serve as a liaison with business area managers, occupiers, and external agents involved in emergency procedures.
  • Ensure regular testing and documentation of fire alarm call points are conducted by service providers.
  • Oversee bi-annual evacuation drills, ensuring realistic and effective arrangements.
  • Report the status of emergency incidents to the Business Continuity Command and Control Team and provide timely updates.
  • Provide guidance to all Other Government Departments within the building on incident control and business continuity matters.
  • Monitor safe occupancy levels in collaboration with the Head of Estate.
  • Work alongside the Regional Security Manager to assure senior management that staff and assets are adequately protected against terrorist threats and are trained to respond effectively to emergencies.
  • Provide training to on-site suppliers supporting staff and visitors in the event of an emergency situation.
  • Support the wider Workplace Operations team and carry out other tasks to contribute towards the day to day running of the Estate as directed by the Building Manager or Head of Estates.

Person specification

The following skills, knowledge and experience are required for this role. Prospective candidates must be able to clearly demonstrate their capability in these areas during the application process:

  • Responsibility and Organisation: The successful candidate will be highly responsible and able to work in a structured and organised manner, ensuring tasks are prioritised and completed efficiently.
  • Stakeholder Engagement: Strong skills in engaging with stakeholders at all levels are essential. Candidates should be able to build effective working relationships, communicate clearly, and manage expectations in challenging situations.
  • Incident Management Experience: Substantial, recent, and relevant experience in incident management is required. Candidates must be able to demonstrate their involvement in managing incidents, coordinating responses, and implementing solutions.
  • Business Continuity Knowledge: Experience in business continuity planning and execution is essential. This includes developing, testing, and maintaining business continuity plans, as well as responding to disruptions and ensuring organisational resilience.
  • Problem Solving and Decision Making: The ability to analyse complex situations, identify key issues, and make effective decisions under pressure is crucial for success in this role.
  • Communication Skills: Excellent verbal and written communication skills are required, with the ability to convey information clearly and concisely to a variety of audiences.
  • Attention to Detail: A keen eye for detail is necessary to ensure accuracy in incident records, reports, and business continuity documentation.

Essential Criteria

  • Demonstrable experience of working in an operational, resilience, incident management, or business continuity environment.
  • Experience of coordinating activities, managing competing priorities and communicating effectively with a range of stakeholders.
  • Ability to make sound decisions and remain calm under pressure during incidents or time-critical situations.
  • Knowledge of business continuity, incident management and organisational resilience principles and practices.
  • An understanding of relevant standards, legislation and regulatory requirements associated with resilience, business continuity, or incident management.

Desirable Criteria

  • L3 Award Passive Fire Protection.
  • NEBOSH General Certificate.
  • Experience in operational or resilience-focused environments.

Additional Security Information

The successful candidate must hold or be willing to obtain National Security Vetting level at Security Check before starting the role.

Working Pattern

Due to operational needs, these posts are full-time; however, applicants who need to work a more flexible arrangement are welcome to apply. We cannot guarantee that we can meet all requests to work flexibly as any agreement will be subject to business ability to accommodate. Any request to work a more flexible arrangement should be made prior to your acceptance of the provisional offer.

Office Closures

If your location preference is for the following site, it’s important to note that this is not long-term site for HMRC and we will require you to move to a new building in the future, subject to our location strategy and the applicable employee policies at that time.

For more information on where you might be working, review this information on our locations (opens in a new window)

This site is:

  • Lynx House, Portsmouth – moving to an alternative office in Portsmouth

HMRC operates both Flexible and Hybrid Working policies, allowing you to balance your work and personal commitments. We welcome applications from those who need to work a more flexible arrangement and will agree to requests where possible, considering our operational and customer service needs.

We offer a generous leave allowance, starting at 25 days and increasing by a day for every year of qualifying service up to a maximum of 30 days.

Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. How to Apply

As part of the application process, you will be asked to provide the following:

  • A 500-word Personal Statement. Your Personal Statement should be used to describe how your skills and experience would be suitable for the advertised role, and how they meet the Essential Criteria and Person Specification outlined in the advert.

“It is often said that the customer's needs should come first. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?”

There is no expectation or requirement for you to prepare for the strengths-based questions in advance of the interview, though you may find it helpful to spend some time reflecting on what you enjoy doing and what you do well.

title: Sr. Mission Integration Engineer, Mission and Ground Systems - Top Secret Clearance
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SR. MISSION INTEGRATION ENGINEER, MISSION AND GROUND SYSTEMS - TOP SECRET CLEARANCE

As a member of our Mission Management team, you will help tackle new technical problems from initial requirements verification through rapid prototyping, integrated test, and operational deployment.

You’d work within a team of other Mission Integration Engineers and Mission Managers, on the same program and across related efforts, to ensure total alignment of your work. You would also work closely with disciplines across SpaceX such as software, information technology, and payload integration to ensure safe and successful mission completion.

You’ll contribute to the performance and execution of programs within the special programs portfolio while specifically focusing on the mission specific systems that drive, manage, and provide user insight into those programs. Based on customer requirements and SpaceX’s system capabilities, you’ll develop system specifications, interface control documentation, and infrastructure plans. This work will cover a number of technical disciplines including space system command and control, operational planning, data processing, compute and networking infrastructure, integrated mission planning, payload integration, and the secure implementation and execution of each of these discipline areas. Our ideal candidate is a self-starter and is hungry to do work that matters.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Serve as the customer interface at meetings, tests, and reviews to develop operations plans, design missions, and participate in real world operations.
  • Ensure contract deliverables are completed on-time and distill customer requirements into actionable development objectives.
  • Work with internal and external stakeholders to drive development. Collaborate with subsystem representatives across team boundaries to consider all necessary trades and ensure end-to-end mission success.
  • Ownall phases of the program from development, initial proposal, through successful test, flight, and on-orbit commissioning. This will include educating the customer on our designs and methodologies.
  • Own ground segment interface and architecture design, including compute infrastructure, network architecture, and software systems.
  • Lead in-person integration efforts (forward deployed engineering) with external stakeholders and customers.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in a engineering or science discipline.
  • 5+ years of software engineering or electrical engineering, working hands-on with hardware or software technical projects.
  • 3+ years of technical project management experience.
  • Professional experience working with spacecraft, with a broad understanding of spacecraft command and control systems and ground segment architectures.
  • Active Top Secret, Top Secret SCI, or DOE Level Q Clearance.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Familiarity with USG processes and software systems.
  • Experience coordinating hardware or infrastructure deployments, including in classified or government-controlled environments.
  • Familiarity with networking fundamentals (e.g. IP networking, switching/routing concepts, etc).
  • Demonstrated ability to work under pressure and deliver reliable and expeditious results across multiple parallel priorities.
  • Highly detail oriented, hardworking, and professional with excellent written and verbal technical communication skills.
  • Spacecraft mission design, development, integration, and/or test experience. Strong penchant for innovation in process improvement and system design.
  • Capacity to balance conflicting opinions and manage expectations between multiple teams and customers.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay Range:
Level 3: $135,000.00 - $215,000.00

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees accrue paid sick leave pursuant to Company policy which satisfies or exceeds the accrual, carryover, and use requirements of the law.

Those with an active clearance will receive a 10% differential, up to an additional $20,000 annually, once officially briefed into a classified program.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

  • To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to EEOCompliance@spacex.com.

We are MHCLG

Here at the Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government (MHCLG), we work on things that make a real difference to people's lives. We have ambitious and far-reaching outcomes to achieve this year and, if you' re thinking of joining us, there's never been a more exciting time.

The Digital Planning Programme is a multidisciplinary team within the MHCLG Leasehold, Private Rental, and Digital Directorate who work with policy colleagues, local government, planning software developers, and planners, shaping the product roadmap and delivering value for our users.

Find out more about our Digital teams and what they are working on through our MHCLG Digital blog. Please note that MHCLG do not offer visa sponsorship and applicants will need a valid visa for the duration of your employment.

Job description

As a Senior Content Designer, you'll:

  • Be involved in the creation of, or change to, a transaction, product or single piece of content that stretches across digital and offline channels
  • Make things easier for people to understand and use. This can involve working on a single piece of content or on the end-to-end journey of a service
  • Make sure appropriate content is shown to a user in the right place and in the best format
  • Start from discovery and work closely with user researchers, service designers and interaction designers
  • Take responsibility for content quality, manage small teams and mentor content colleagues • write and map user stories
  • Review the work of others to assure quality

  • Extensive experience writing clear and easy to understand content in plain English that meets user needs and achieves the right outcomes

Watch our Webinar on the above link and gain valuable insight into GCA and our recruitment processes.

Ready to move beyond system design and drive a strategic roadmap that delivers true value for the nation? We are seeking a Senior Enterprise Architect to translate high-level strategy into a resilient, scalable digital estate for the public good.

If you’re prepared to own the architectural governance for products impacting millions of citizens, we want to hear from you. In this role, you will navigate the critical trade-offs between speed, cost, and quality—ensuring that every technical decision maximises efficiency and delivers public value across the organisation.

Job Summary

We are seeking a visionary Senior Enterprise Architect to act as the defining authority for our enterprise-wide DDaT strategy and architecture. In this high-impact role, you will perform as a versatile Enterprise Architect while bringing deep specialisation in data and integration—translating high-level strategic goals into coherent, resilient technical roadmaps and leading critical governance on investments and technical debt to ensure secure, scalable public service delivery. You will lead, mentor, and grow a unified team of Enterprise and Technical Architects, establishing the technical guardrails and maintaining strategic control while steering our complex digital transformation journey and managing preferred delivery partners.

Job description

Key Accountabilities:

  • Strategic Vision & Roadmap Delivery - Convert the annual business plan into a clear, step-by-step blueprint for the future technology environment (Target State Architecture or TSA). You will manage the plans for moving from the current system to the future one, specifically for major initiatives, to make sure all projects are connected and support the overall business strategy.
  • Governance & Assurance Leadership - You will be the technical voice on the Architecture Review Board (ARB). Your role is to manage the 'Front Door' review process, making sure new projects are checked for architectural soundness and fit before budget approval.
  • Investment & Technical Debt Management - Ensure strategic bids allocate a dedicated remediation budget (15–20%) to mitigate technical debt.
  • Senior Leadership Communication - Maintain the "Level Zero" Architecture Map as a streamlined executive view of the GCA technology estate for Board and ExCo decision-making.
  • Blueprinting & Business Alignment - Partner with Business Architecture to create Enterprise Blueprints. You will take high-level strategic goals (e.g. "Improve SME Spend") and map them to specific technical capabilities and data flows required to deliver that outcome.
  • Technical Standards & Principles - You will establish and enforce the Secure by Design and Data First architectural principles. You will set the non-negotiable rules that product teams must follow to ensure technical consistency, interoperability, and security across the organisation.
  • Strategic Consultancy & Mentorship - Provide Architecture-as-a-Service to senior stakeholders, moving from "activity-based" updates to "outcome-based" advice. You will mentor a team of up to 1-2 architects, establishing a formal competency framework to elevate the team’s strategic influence.
  • Architectural Steering & High-Level Design (HLD) - Author Architecture Steer papers to align stakeholders on major investments, and personally develop High-Level Designs for critical, complex initiatives to ensure long-term resilience and strategic alignment.

Person specification

Essential Criteria (to be assessed at application stage):

  • Enterprise Architecture & Roadmap Delivery: Proven experience converting abstract business strategies into Target State Architecture (TSA) blueprints and managing transition roadmaps for complex digital estates.
  • Strategic Governance & Assurance: Experience leading technical assurance (e.g., an Architecture Review Board) and defining architectural principles, such as Secure by Design and Data First.
  • Risk & Technical Debt Management: Proven track record of identifying architectural risks and successfully articulating, managing, and securing investment to remediate technical debt.
  • Executive Stakeholder Communication: Ability to translate complex technical problems into simplified executive views (like a "Level Zero" map) to influence Board and ExCo-level decision-making.
  • Leadership & Technical Mentorship: Experience leading, mentoring, and developing the strategic capabilities of architecture teams while managing the technical guardrails for external delivery partners.

  • Leadership

Andover SP11 8HJ, Glasgow G2 8EX, Whittington WS14 9TJ and Wyton PE28 2EA.

This is a non-contractual arrangement where all office-based employees will be expected to spend a minimum of 60% of their working time in office, subject to capacity and any required workplace adjustments. Requirements to attend other locations for official business (i.e., detached duty) or work in another MOD office, will also count towards this level of attendance. Applicants can request further information regarding how this may work in their team from the Vacancy Holder (see advert for contact details). Defence Business Services cannot respond to any questions about working arrangements.

About the job

Job summary

About the National Armaments Director Group (NAD Group)

We are the National Armaments Director Group (NAD Group). Part of the Ministry of Defence (MOD), we bring together a wide range of expertise to develop, deliver, and sustain the UK’s national defence capabilities. Working closely with industry, international partners, and allies, we provide the equipment, technology, and support services that enable our armed forces to operate effectively and respond to the challenges of today and tomorrow.

View our YouTube video to see more about our work.

This position is advertised at 37 hours per week.

Job description

About our United States Visiting Forces (USVF) team

Within the Commercial team this role supports the United States Visiting Forces (USVF) which are permanently located at MOD sites across the UK. The team is divided into 4 work streams by location and Commercial Activity.

The teams which these roles sit within deliver major construction projects at bases around the UK covering both Procurement and Contract Management activities, ensuring the development and continuity of the United States Air Force’s (USAF) critical strategic mission in Europe. Each team is headed up by a Grade 7 with considerable Procurement experience and an SEO to whom you would report.

The team are based around the UK with small hubs around Wyton (Cambridge), Whittington (Lichfield), Andover and Glasgow and have all adopted a hybrid approach to working, with some travel to sites throughout England required.

Why join the USVF team?

USVF Commercial is a dynamic and talented, friendly team working at the heart of some of the most exciting and interesting infrastructure projects in the UK, in support of the United States Air Force mission in Europe. You will be working closely with both US military & civilian personnel and UK colleagues to deliver operational capability across the USVF sites within the UK, on a wide variety of infrastructure projects, many of considerable strategic importance. The scale and scope of these will ensure you develop your career in a demanding and varied environment which will further hone your procurement and contract management skills, build your market knowledge, and allow you to make a contribution to maintaining national security.

The size and nature of Commercial and Industry (C&I) ensures that, for the right candidate, onward career prospects are excellent.

Person specification

As a Commercial Practitioner in the USVF Commercial team

You will have a Commercial background to support and deliver capital projects preferably within construction, which may range from cost management to programme delivery.

You will be willing to work across different phases of the commercial life cycle, from leading or support key sourcing activities to contract management with the aim to meet project goals while minimising risk and ensuring value for money is considered on a sound Commercial basis. You will be accountable for ensuring adherence to and conformity with all agreed C&I processes and operating procedures, and particularly those which are detailed under the key infrastructure process for Commercial and relate to end to end project management.

You will work with Project Managers, the US customer and a wide range of stakeholders to provide commercial advice and assurance to the many infrastructure projects within the portfolio.

A typical day could involve:

  • Assist in writing a Commercial Strategy
  • Working with project managers to develop a forthcoming requirement for a new military installation
  • Joining a project call with the customer and delivery team to give updates on the project
  • Assisting with drafting criteria for evaluating a future procurement and evaluating bid proposals for a new construction project
  • Drafting an options paper to support your manager in a negotiation
  • Approving a contract variation or attending a meeting with team members and the US customer at one of the base sites

You will have the opportunity to further develop your skills in researching supplier markets, commercial strategies, contract drafting and contract management. The scale and scope of USVF projects mean you will have the opportunity to liaise with many other teams, including legal, finance, risk management, cyber security, technical service providers who support our projects and of course, the contractors with whom we are working.

Although some of the workload is programmed, the nature of the work we do in USVF means that the successful candidate can expect to work in a dynamic and rapidly changing environment.

Responsibilities

  • Provide input to Commercial Strategy and associated contracting strategy as required following RIBA 2020 stages and NEC contracting models
  • Support commercial relationships with suppliers, with a principal objective of achieving optimal cost and performance
  • Undertake end to end contract management and offer commercial advice and guidance
  • Comply with regulations and policy affecting procurement and adopt commercial best practice and maintain auditable records of commercial activities
  • Support fundamentals of sourcing and supplier engagement activities including tendering, spend pattern analysis, contract analysis, bid evaluation, negotiations, and supplier consolidation
  • Collaborate with members of the team including project, technical, finance and specialist staff, to deliver Customer requirements

Essential Criteria

  • You must become a qualified Commercial Officer to Practitioner Level. This means you must already be in possession of CIPS Level 4 (as a minimum) or work towards it within 2 years or as soon as practically possible
  • You will be required to undertake mandated pre-requisite training to be issued with a Commercial Licence as soon as practicably possible following appointment
  • You will be required to travel to relevant UK MOD locations on occasion
  • You will possess excellent communication, written, verbal, and stakeholder management skills
  • You will have the ability to manage multiple simultaneous projects requiring frequent communication, organisation, time management, and problem-solving skills
  • You will possess relevant sourcing experience conducting end-to-end procurement process across an area of responsibility ideally with a background in projects and construction
  • You will possess relevant Contract Management experience across an area of responsibility ideally with a background in projects and construction
  • You will be a passionate self-starter with the highest integrity and ethics

Desirable Experience and Skills

Situation: Describe the situation you found yourself in. You must describe a specific event or situation. Be sure to give enough detail for the job holder to understand. Where are you? Who was there with you? What had happened?

Task: The recruitment panel will want to understand what you tried to achieve from the situation you found yourself in. What was the task that you had to complete and why? What did you have to achieve?

Action: What did you do? The recruitment panel will be looking for information of what you did, how you did it and why. Keep the focus on you. Try to use “I” rather than “we” to explain your actions that lead to the result. Be careful not to take credit for something that you did not do.

Result: Don’t be shy about taking credit for your behaviour. Quote specific facts and figures easily understandable. What results did the actions produce? What did you achieve through your actions, and did you meet your goals? Was it a successful outcome? If not, what did you learn from the experience? Keep the situation and task parts brief.

Concentrate on the action and the result. If the result was not entirely successful describe what you learned from this and what you would do differently next time. Make sure you focus on your strengths. When providing your evidence please ensure that you avoid acronyms and company specific jargon.
