title: Lead Program Manager
description:
About the Team

The Sensors Division within STR focuses on the development and analysis of advanced sensor systems in the RF, acoustic, and electro-optical domains. This includes the design and development of novel sensors and advanced information processing techniques from ideation to prototype implementations. The Subsea and Seabed Systems (SSS) Group develops and delivers advanced undersea sensor and signal processing systems related to intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) and counter-ISR applications.

The Role

The SSS Group is seeking a Lead Program Manager with a highly technical, undersea warfare background to manage a portfolio of programs focused on future undersea systems. This portfolio spans concept generation and prototype development with the goal that programs will continue into low-rate initial production (LRIP) or production. As such, we are looking for applicants with experience traversing that span of technology readiness and an ability to adaptively scale process. In this role you will lead small, highly capable, multidisciplinary teams of researchers, scientists, and engineers across STR campuses, coordinating electrical and mechanical design, software development, system construction, integration, testing, and field execution to meet cost, schedule, and performance objectives on innovative, complex, and challenging national security programs.

A central responsibility is the financial planning and execution of fast-paced, complex programs: developing credible budgets and resource plans, maintaining current forecasts, and making timely cost, schedule, and staffing decisions as technical priorities evolve. Your areas of specific focus will also include building and executing programmatic baselines, including personnel, deliverables, and subcontractor/contract manufacturer management plans while anticipating risks, resolving resource, security, and contracting challenges, and meeting or managing customer, sponsor, and leadership expectations.

A successful candidate will have recent and significant program manager experience building fieldable systems and a working knowledge in several of the following areas: undersea warfare, sonar systems, ocean engineering, modeling and simulation, test and evaluation, hardware design, software architecture, uncrewed underwater vehicles, resource management, signal processing, and/or communications. This position requires competency in leading and managing multidisciplinary teams, briefing senior leadership, cultivating positive, collaborative, and productive work environments, and a strong proficiency in all aspects of program management. Strong interpersonal, communication, mentorship, and peer-leadership skills are also required.

What you will do:

  • Execute multiple fast-paced, complex programs against cost, schedule, and technical objectives, with accountability for financial planning and performance
  • Develop and maintain program budgets, time-phased spending plans, staffing and resource allocations, and estimates to complete and at completion across labor, materials, travel, subcontractors, and contract manufacturers
  • Manage financial execution by reviewing actual costs and commitments, monitoring burn rates and funding availability, analyzing variances, and updating forecasts as program needs change
  • Work with technical leads, finance, and contracts to assess cost and schedule tradeoffs, implement corrective actions, and communicate financial risks and resource needs to leadership and sponsors
  • Lead proposals by providing expertise in proposal development while ensuring adherence to a gated capture process
  • Create subcontractor statements of work and managing and tracking subcontractors to ensure proper execution
  • Work with contract manufacturers to build up to LRIP and then meet LRIP milestones with high quality
  • Lead multidisciplinary teams through design, build, integration, test readiness, and field execution, coordinating interdependent engineering activities to deliver fieldable systems
  • Oversee preparation, planning, and execution of advanced undersea system testing, including test objectives, personnel and resource coordination, readiness activities, at-sea execution, and post-test assessment
  • Provide regular program briefs to group and division leadership.
  • Create and maintain an environment that fosters collaboration by giving clear direction and constructive feedback to the team
  • Monitor progress against goals, anticipating risks, resolving issues, and initiating corrective actions as appropriate

Who you are:

  • Active clearance (Current TS/SSBI with SCI preferred) with ability to gain and keep SCI/SAP accreditations required, for which U.S citizenship is needed by the U.S government
  • Technical degree and 8+ years of prior relevant experience in government contracting, research and development (R&D), or advanced technology production. Equivalent experience will be considered
  • Program manager or control account manager experience in a design and development and/or build contract, including work breakdown structure (WBS) definition, schedule generation, financial analysis and reporting, and resource management
  • Demonstrated experience planning and executing the finances of fast-paced, complex programs, including budget development, resource planning, financial forecasting, cost and variance analysis, and timely corrective action to meet program objectives within available funding
  • Experience in proposal management, including planning and cost estimation
  • Experience managing projects larger than $10M for the Department of War
  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills
  • Experience leading small, highly capable, multidisciplinary teams executing complex advanced-technology programs spanning electrical and mechanical design, software development, system construction, integration, test, and field execution
  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate interdependent engineering disciplines and drive systems from design and build through integration, readiness, and successful execution in operationally relevant environments
  • Strong presentation and organizational skills

Desired Qualifications

  • Experience with advanced undersea warfare system concepts, signal processing, underwater acoustics, and ocean engineering
  • Experience with sonar systems
  • Experience preparing, planning, and executing testing and fielding of advanced undersea systems and vehicles, including development of test objectives, coordination of personnel and resources, test readiness activities, at-sea execution, and post-test assessment.
  • Experience conducting operationally representative testing of advanced undersea systems in realistic maritime environments, working with operators, engineers, and government sponsors to translate mission needs and operating conditions into test scenarios and performance measures, and using results to inform system design, performance improvements, operational employment, and transition toward fieldable capability
  • Work experience in government, FFRDC, or defense industry companies and sponsors
  • Earned value management system (EVMS) experience
  • Contract manufacturing experience
  • Risk and opportunity management experience
  • Experience managing research and development programs
  • Proficiency in all Microsoft Office applications, including but not limited to Microsoft Project, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint

Why Join Us

This is an opportunity to contribute to the development of groundbreaking undersea systems that will shape the future of undersea defense. You will work alongside a passionate and talented team, tackling some of the most challenging and rewarding problems in the field. If you are passionate about managing programs that deliver advanced undersea technology that sailors depend on working, we want to hear from you.

Pay Information
Full-Time Salary Range: $147,000 - $200,000

The salary range listed is based on external market data. Offers are based on factors, such as but not limited to, the candidate’s experience, education, training, key skills/critical skills, security clearances, and prevailing market and business conditions.

STR is a growing technology company with locations near Boston, MA, Arlington, VA, near Dayton, OH, Melbourne, FL, Carlsbad, CA, Atlanta, GA, and Denver, CO. We specialize in advanced research and development for defense, intelligence, and national security in: cyber; next generation sensors, radar, sonar, communications, and electronic warfare; and artificial intelligence algorithms and analytics to make sense of the complexity that is exploding around us.

STR is committed to creating a collaborative learning environment that supports deep technical understanding and recognizes the contributions and achievements of all team members. Our work is challenging, and we go home at night knowing that we pushed the envelope of technology and made the world safer.

STR is not just any company. Our people, culture, and attitude along with their unique set of skills, experiences, and perspectives put us on a trajectory to change the world. We can't do it alone, though - we need fellow trailblazers. If you are one, join our team and help to keep our society safe! Visit us at for more info.


STR is an equal opportunity employer. We are fully dedicated to hiring the most qualified candidate regardless of race, color, religion, sex (including gender identity, sexual orientation and pregnancy), marital status, national origin, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

If you need a reasonable accommodation for any portion of the employment process, email us at appassist@str.us and provide your contact info.

Pursuant to applicable federal law and regulations, positions at STR require employees to obtain national security clearances and satisfy the requirements for compliance with export control and other applicable laws.

Job summary

The post holder(s) will work as part of a large team which supports the Welsh Tribunals Unit and the 6 devolved tribunals. Mental Health Tribunal for Wales (MHRTW), Education Tribunal Wales (ETW) Residential Property Tribunal (RPT) Agriculture land Tribunal (ALT) Welsh Language Tribunal (WLT) and the Adjudication Panel Wales.

Job description

These are independent tribunals that provide appeal processes and access to justice.

The posts provide an opportunity to develop operational skills by ensuring that tribunal hearings are scheduled, and any follow up action is delivered in compliance with statutory requirements and within specified timescales.

The post holder(s) will be responsible for their own caseload.

  • Communicating both verbally and in writing with a range of stakeholders ensuring that accurate records are maintained.
  • Collating and distributing tribunal reports and tribunal hearing decisions to a range of stakeholders within the required timescales.
  • Recording accurate information which is used to monitor the number of hearings that take place and how many tribunal members take part in the hearings.
  • Clerking and admitting panel members to virtual hearings. Welcome attendees and support the tribunal hearing panel by dealing with any queries during the hearing.
  • Ensuring that information given is accurate and complies with information security policies; escalating complex queries to the Business Managers.

About the job

Job summary

On the Cyber Fast Stream, you will have a unique opportunity to protect government systems, data and its staff and help make the UK the safest place to be online.

Job description

Cyber Security is the practice of protecting systems (hardware, software and their associated infrastructure) networks, programmes, the data on them, and the services they provide, from unauthorised access, digital attacks, harm or misuse.
On the Cyber Fast Stream programme, you will have the opportunity to work in various areas across the UK Civil Service. You will have the chance to develop your leadership and management capabilities while developing skills and experience through a number of postings. During your postings, Cyber Fast Streamers have the opportunity to work in collaboration with wider business departmental colleagues. You may be:

Advising senior management on cyber strategy and policies.
Providing critical advice and guidance to ensure secure systems are being delivered effectively.
Investigating indicators of potentially malicious activity, escalating incidents or initiating responses.
Performing detailed reviews of digital services in order to provide security assurance and prevent and mitigate against potential cyber risks.
Setting direction and leading teams responsible for the detection and response to cyber incidents and the technology and processes required to keep pace with the evolving cyber threat.

Person specification

You must be eligible to work in the UK

title: Guest Experience Specialist
description:
As a Guest Experience Specialist, you are often the first and last impression our guests have – making you an essential part of the Signature Aviation experience. In this highly visible, hospitality-driven role, you’ll warmly welcome guests and crew members with professionalism, care, and a genuine commitment to creating exceptional moments.

Whether you’re greeting a VIP traveler, supporting a flight crew, or coordinating services behind the scenes, you bring grace under pressure and attention to detail that ensures every visit is smooth, comfortable, and memorable. Your reliability and pride in service directly reflect the Signature standard our guests trust.

This is a dynamic, hands-on position that requires flexibility to work varied schedules, including nights, weekends, and holidays, and the ability to operate in both indoor and outdoor environments, often near active aircraft and ground service equipment.

If you love delivering thoughtful service, working in a fast-paced setting, and being part of a high-end hospitality team, you’ll thrive in this role.

(Other duties may be assigned)

  • Meet and greet guests and crews as they arrive at our facility and provide a warm, friendly greeting while escorting them to the front entrance, aircraft, or vehicles.
  • Effectively collaborate, cooperate, and work closely with all team members, guests, and other visitors to ensure services are promptly and correctly handled in a professional and courteous manner. This includes ensuring an efficient and accurate transfer of information through various methods between and among guests, the private aviation terminal (PAT), other Company departments, and external parties.
  • Accurately receive, dispatch, and completely process guest purchases and fuel transactions in accordance with Company procedures. May assist with some general accounting work and financial record keeping.
  • Provide visitors with a wide array of concierge services including arranging reservations for hotel stays, ground transportation or rental cars, catering, and customs appointments as requested.
  • Manage guest, crew, and/or visitor inquiries, resolve requests, handle billing disputes, and address concerns in an efficient and effective manner.
  • Maintain a working knowledge of Signature’s facilities, services, website, surrounding areas, and other information commonly asked about by guests.
  • Monitor arriving and departing flights and communicate with aircraft to coordinate services and assign to the Airside Experience Team. Use real-time system management (SIGops/SIGnet) to log and schedule requested services, change service status, and supervise the operation’s flow by appropriately prioritizing services. Ensure all departing aircraft have all requested amenities such as catering, coffee, ice, and newspaper.
  • Maintain and stock amenities in guest areas and ensure that lobby, pilot facing spaces, and restrooms are clean and free of debris.
  • Promote and sell the Company’s services and products to aircraft passengers and crew.
  • Assist crews and guests with luggage, provide transportation from the facility to commercial terminal, hotel, or other nearby locations as required, and fulfill special requests. Assist pilots with access to weather information, portals, and computers.
  • Identify crewmembers, passengers, visitors, and vendors in accordance with all security procedures.
  • Stop work when an unsafe condition or act is likely to cause harm to people, the environment, Company or guest assets, or the Company’s reputation if the work continues. Report concerns to the appropriate manager and cooperate in addressing the unsafe act or condition.
  • Abide by emergency response procedures during critical events.
  • Understand, comply with, and enforce all Signature and airport security (physical, cyber and data) protocols.
  • Create accurate records pertaining to time worked and activities and services performed.
  • Use the Company contact management system to review, capture, and update customer preferences to provide a more personalized service experience.
  • Assist the Airside Experience team to ensure our guests receive an exceptional experience. Services include without limitation, valeting customer vehicles, wing walking, placing chocks and cones, and positioning stairs/jetway to aircraft.
  • Assist airlines with passenger service functions in certain locations as needed.

Minimum Education and/or Experience:

  • High School Diploma or General Education Degree (GED).
  • At least 1 year of customer experience-related work in retail, hospitality, or sales is preferred.
  • Must possess a valid state driver’s license.
  • Minimum of 18 years of age.
  • Ability to pass company background checks (criminal and motor vehicle), drug tests, meet airport background check requirements to receive and maintain an airport security badge, and be insurable by the Company's applicable insurance policies.
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the jurisdiction of employment.
  • Must be able to exercise good judgment and follow directions/directives from supervisor/management.
  • Ability to drive standard and automatic transmission vehicles is preferred.

Additional essential knowledge and skills:

  • Hospitality Skills: Excellent guest service skills with an energetic, outgoing, and guest-obsessed personality. Must be able to anticipate and act on guest needs and prioritize guest requests and job responsibilities by exhibiting a keen ability to multi-task in a fast-paced environment. Must be able to maintain professionalism and confidentiality. Experience with conflict resolution in a hospitality environment is preferred.
  • Language Skills: Clearly communicate in English with others in person, via telephone, radio communicators, and in writing for purposes of performing certain job duties and safety-sensitive tasks. Ability to read and comprehend documents such as safety rules, operating instructions, and procedure manuals.
  • Math Skills: Ability to perform simple arithmetic (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, percentages, and fractions).
  • Communication Skills: Able to use telephone, fax, two-way radio, email, or text messaging to contact guests, crew members, team members, or emergency personnel.
  • Critical Thinking / Reasoning Ability: Ability to use rational thought to analyze and evaluate information, and to make informed decisions in a fast-paced environment.
  • Interpersonal Skills: Ability to get along and work well with others. Excellent interpersonal skills for effective collaboration with team members and service to guests.
  • Multitasking: Ability to handle multiple tasks simultaneously while maintaining attention to detail. High level of concentration is required to ensure accuracy in a busy setting.
  • Computer Skills: Ability to use a computer, learn necessary company software and timely complete Signature’s training programs.

Pay ranges vary based on multiple factors, including, without limitation, skill sets, education, shift worked, responsibilities, seniority, geographical market, merit, output, productivity, prior training or experience, and travel. The pay range for this position is $22.00 to $25.00 / hour.

About the job

Job summary

The Future Rural Payments Service (FRPS) is one of Defra Group’s largest transformation programmes, reshaping how grants and payments are delivered through a simpler, more resilient and adaptable service. With a programme budget of approximately £100 million, FRPS will replace six legacy systems, helping customers access £2.5 billion of funding each year while creating a platform capable of supporting future grants and payments services across Defra Group. The programme is now entering a critical phase, moving from design and early delivery towards testing, business readiness and transition to live service. Leading this programme means ensuring that essential funding continues to reach those who depend on it, while creating a service equipped to support the rural sector for years to come.

Job description

We are seeking a proven leader of major transformation programmes to lead FRPS through its next phase of delivery. Working closely with the Rural Payments Agency (RPA) Chief Executive, the programme’s Senior Responsible Owner, you will set strategic direction, maintain delivery momentum and ensure that investment delivers lasting benefits.

This is one of the most significant delivery leadership roles in Defra Group. You will bring together leaders from RPA, Defra policy teams and Defra’s Digital, Data, Technology and Security group to align policy, operations and digital delivery around a shared objective. You will resolve competing priorities and keep the programme on track while balancing delivery pace with risk, cost and scope. You will oversee implementation and transition from legacy systems while protecting the continuity of payments on which customers depend.

The successful candidate will bring a strong track record in major transformation and large-scale digital service delivery, alongside the judgement and resilience to lead through complexity. You will build confidence among Ministers, senior leaders and assurance bodies, establish clear governance and accountability, and lead high-performing, inclusive teams.

This is a rare opportunity to lead a nationally significant transformation at a pivotal moment. FRPS will become a cornerstone of Defra Group's future delivery landscape, enabling funding, grants and payments to be delivered through services that are simpler, more resilient and more adaptable to future needs. As Programme Director, you will play a central role in shaping that future.

Person specification

We’re looking for a senior leader who can operate at pace, bring clarity to complexity, and deliver consistently through others.


Major programme delivery:
A proven track record of leading large, complex transformation programmes and delivering successful outcomes in demanding environments. Experience of recovering momentum, managing interdependencies and delivering against challenging milestones would be advantageous.


Digital service delivery:
Significant experience of leading the delivery of large-scale digital services, platforms or business-critical technology programmes. Experience of operating within complex legacy technology environments and delivering change whilst maintaining service continuity would be advantageous.


Strategic leadership and judgement:
Able to provide clear direction in complex environments, make difficult decisions and balance pace, risk, cost and value. Demonstrates sound judgement and resilience when operating under pressure and scrutiny.

Stakeholder leadership:
Experience of building confidence and alignment across diverse stakeholder groups, including senior leaders, delivery partners, assurance bodies and government sponsors. Able to influence effectively in environments where outcomes depend on collaboration rather than direct authority.

Implementation and service transition:
Experience of leading organisations through testing, business readiness, implementation and transition to live
service. Able to maintain operational performance and stakeholder confidence while managing delivery risk and
organisational change.


People leadership:
A track record of building high-performing teams and fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement. Committed to developing people and creating an inclusive environment in which teams can thrive.

About the job

Job summary

This is an exciting opportunity to lead community, stakeholder and public engagement across Greater Cambridge, helping to ensure that the voices of residents, partners and communities are at the heart of shaping the area's future. You will develop and deliver engagement strategies that build trust, strengthen relationships and create meaningful opportunities for people to influence decisions and projects that affect them.

Job description

Working closely with colleagues, government partners, local authorities and a wide range of stakeholders, you will champion innovative and inclusive approaches to engagement. You'll help ensure that engagement activity supports the Greater Cambridge Development Corporation's vision and values, delivering social value, positive community outcomes and a strong sense of place.

The role combines strategic leadership with practical delivery. You will oversee engagement and consultation activity, provide expert advice and guidance, commission and manage specialist support where required, and work with project teams to design and deliver targeted engagement programmes. You will also help identify and mitigate risks, share best practice across the organisation and ensure a consistent and effective approach to stakeholder and community engagement.

This is a highly visible role that requires a confident and collaborative leader, able to navigate complex environments, influence a diverse range of stakeholders and deliver engagement that makes a genuine difference to communities across Greater Cambridge.

This role is being recruited by Homes England to support the establishment and operation of the Greater Cambridge Development Corporation. The successful candidate will initially be employed by Homes England and will work predominantly on matters relating to the Greater Cambridge Development Corporation and its activities.

We're looking for an experienced engagement professional who is passionate about involving communities, partners and stakeholders in shaping the future of places. You will have a strong track record of leading stakeholder and community engagement activity on complex development, regeneration, infrastructure or place-based programmes, and be comfortable working with senior leaders across government, local authorities and the private sector.

You will bring a solid understanding of planning, housing and public policy, with an appreciation of the challenges and opportunities involved in delivering sustainable growth. Knowledge of the funding, economics and infrastructure required to support large-scale development will help you engage confidently with a wide range of stakeholders and partners.

You will understand what good engagement looks like and be able to apply best practice approaches to build trust, encourage participation and deliver meaningful outcomes.

The successful candidate will be a skilled collaborator and influencer, capable of bringing together diverse interests and building consensus around complex proposals and decisions. You will be confident navigating challenging stakeholder environments, balancing competing priorities and maintaining productive relationships across multiple organisations.

Experience of working within the development, planning, housing, regeneration or public sector environment, particularly alongside government bodies, will be highly valued. Above all, you will be motivated by making a positive difference, helping to create places that reflect the needs and aspirations of the communities they serve.

About the job

Job summary

Discover a career in your hands at HMRC. Whether you're seeking purpose, growth, or a workplace that gives you a true sense of belonging, hear from some of our employees as they share their story about what it’s really like to work at HMRC.

Visit our YouTube channel to watch the full series and come and discover your potential.

At HMRC, we are committed to creating a great place to work for all our colleagues; an inclusive and respectful environment that reflects the diversity of the society we serve. We want to maximise the potential of everyone who works for us, and we offer a range of flexible working patterns and support to make an exciting career at HMRC accessible to you.

Diverse perspectives and experiences are critical to our success, and we encourage applications from all people from all backgrounds with the experience and skills needed to perform this role.

Job description

HMRC is currently undertaking some of the largest digital transformation programmes across Government and other sectors. Our user researchers are at the core of keeping user needs central to design and implementation, providing an opportunity to shape and improve Services that impact millions of users daily.

You will be joining a thriving and supportive User Researcher community, with regular opportunities for insight sharing, training and discussion. Our team draws together expertise from a wide variety of backgrounds and sectors and welcomes new ideas on how we can continue to conduct robust research with real-world impact. You will be based at one of our CDIO Centres across the UK with access to research labs and facilities.

This is an exciting time to join an organisation that is at the forefront of cutting-edge user research. Our blog tells you a bit more about what we do and how we do it. User Research in HMRC (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u3_5uDUBh0I)

If this sounds like the sort of thing which excites you, this is the job for you.

Person specification

As a Senior User Researcher, your responsibilities include:

  • Leading on planning, recruiting and conducting user research in larger teams and on more complex services, including playing back user research to stakeholders and digital teams.
  • Understanding the service problem then aligning user research activities to influence and support decision-making.
  • Applying a range of techniques to analyse and synthesise user research insights, creating research outputs in an actionable way.
  • Advocating for, and including, all kinds of users in appropriate research activities to help teams design accessible services for all users.
  • Contributing to the user research community at HMRC.
  • Managing and/or mentoring User Researchers.
  • Participating in HMRC’s cross-government research and conferences.

Essential Criteria

  • Extensive experience in senior user research, improving digital services and applying GDS standards to meet user needs.
  • Skilled in tackling complex problems, aligning research activities to guide decisions and deliver practical solutions.
  • Expert in a wide range of research methods, including usability testing, surveys, ethnographic techniques, and data analysis, producing clear, actionable insights.
  • Strong advocate for user-centred design, influencing stakeholders and embedding research practices into agile workflows.
  • Excellent communicator, able to present complex ideas clearly and persuasively; supported by a relevant degree or equivalent experience.
  • Demonstratable experience in coaching and mentoring of team members.

About the job

Job summary

Working in a team with our Heads of Housing & Infrastructure Funding Portfolio Management, the Senior Manager will play a critical role in managing a range of complex grant investments. Youn will be joining our experienced, multi-disciplinary team, who are committed to making positive changes in supporting housing and infrastructure delivery and unlocking hundreds of thousands of homes across England. Our Senior Managers look after some of the largest funding investments Homes England makes (up to £350m at a project level), with significant complexity, political interest and stakeholder management responsibilities. Therefore, we are looking for a mixture of technical skills, experience, stakeholder management and a calm, professional approach to getting the job done.

Job description

We are a flexible, national team that works locally; with Homes England moving to a regional delivery model, we now form part of Chief Regional Delivery Officer’s directorate’s central technical team. A key part of the role will involve working collaboratively with regional Homes England colleagues primarily across the South, as well as external partners, to drive forward our housing and regeneration priorities locally.

The Team believes in delivering a first-class customer service, resolving project delivery issues informally wherever possible, taking an innovative and creative approach. They believe in working in a collaborative and flexible way to foster good decision making and problem solving within their team.

This is a rare chance to shape the future of infrastructure and housing delivery in a national organisation with real social purpose. Working with key stakeholders and a professional team you will ensure efficient, consistent and effective resolution of complex contractual and delivery issues directly helping to create new communities.

The role will support partners and the delivery of key strategic projects around England. There are some ambitious projects to get involved with and this is an excellent opportunity to balance contract management with day-to-day delivery whilst bringing innovative solutions to the funding required to unlock housing.

Person specification

Whilst our day job is to deliver first class customer service to our stakeholders, you will be used to "spinning several plates" at once and will always be looking for ways to improve and innovate.

You'll be comfortable supporting the Housing & Infrastructure Grants business with complex project delivery issues, aiming to ensure that projects are performing in line with expectations. You will be proficient in project and portfolio management, assurance and monitoring in the built environment with a background in capital projects and programmes in the housing and infrastructure (e.g. funding projects with viability challenges, transport, utilities, public buildings, land assembly, site remediation, communications and green/blue infrastructure) sectors and hold a relevant professional qualification.

Delivering on a mission as bold as ours isn’t always easy. You will be resilient and comfortable managing stakeholders at a senior level and your discussions will always be shaped by a good understanding of the commercial and operational impact of what we do as a team. You will enjoy working in an innovative, fun and engaging way and be able to negotiate and persuade.

As an experienced housing & infrastructure professional, you’ll understand how to manage colleagues and be able to demonstrate you can work with others as part of a team in a collaborative, inclusive way.

• Experience of risk management & business administration.

Location

Bristol, Darlington, Manchester, Wolverhampton

About the job

Job summary

We are MHCLG

Here at the Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government (MHCLG), we work on things that make a real difference to people’s lives. Whether it's through the homes we live in, the work of local councils, or the communities we are part of, our work is at the top of the political agenda. We have ambitious and far-reaching outcomes to achieve and, if you’re thinking of joining us, there’s never been a more exciting time.

We're looking for Senior User Researchers to join teams delivering some of the department's most important digital services. Opportunities are available across both the Funding Service and Elections Digital.

The Funding Service is transforming how MHCLG delivers grant funding to councils, community organisations and local services. Our aim is to design digital solutions so that grant delivery is faster, more consistent, cost-effective and user-centred across the lifecycle, from fund design through assessment, payments and monitoring. Our service supports programmes worth billions of pounds, and if you want your research to shape real-world decisions and improve outcomes, this is a great place to do it.

We are also growing our user research capability within Elections Digital, which sits within the Elections Directorate. The Directorate is responsible for how elections are run and who participates, delivering the government's elections strategy including votes for 16 and 17-year-olds, improvements to voter registration and changes to voter identification. Our digital services support millions of users each year and include Register to Vote, Apply for a Postal Vote, Apply for a Proxy Vote and services used by Electoral Registration Offices in local authorities.

As a Senior User Researcher, you will lead high-quality user research to inform the design, delivery and continuous improvement of the Funding Service or Elections Services. You will work closely with a multidisciplinary team to embed user insight into decision making, shape service direction, and improve user outcomes. You will also support the development of user research capability across the team and wider department. You can find out more about the Funding Service in our MHCLG Digital Blog [Search Results for “funding service” – MHCLG Digital].

Find out more about our Digital teams and what they are working on through our MHCLG Digital blog. Please note that MHCLG do not offer visa sponsorship and applicants will need a valid visa for the duration of your employment.


Job description

As a Senior User Researcher, you'll:

  • Lead the planning, design and delivery of user research using a variety of research methods at different design phases, from discovery through to live services
  • Carry out user research activities from recruiting participants, preparing discussion guides, and moderating research sessions
  • Analyse and synthesise research data to develop findings, insights and recommendations
  • Work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team and with wider stakeholders to inform user-centred decision making
  • Use inclusive research practices with a focus on accessibility needs
  • Advocate for the user by sharing research insights and user needs regularly and consistently
  • Maintain user needs, playbacks, and insights so that designers can easily find and act on research findings
  • Line manage and/or mentor junior researchers

Person specification

As a Senior User Researcher, you'll have:

  • Senior-level experience planning, preparing, and carrying out user research activities for complex services, with demonstrable experience in qualitative (for example, usability testing, contextual interviews) and quantitative methods (for example, surveys, A/B testing)
  • Proven ability to analyse and synthesise complex research data into clear, actionable findings and insights
  • Ability to collaborate effectively within multidisciplinary teams to action user research findings and inform decision making

On occasion, some individuals may need to move location. We aim to align postings with your preferences whenever possible; however, final decisions must support our wider business needs. Please note that Fast Streamers cannot choose their department or their specific role.

About the job

Job summary

On the Government Policy Fast Stream, you will work at the heart of the Civil Service. You’ll design, develop and oversee delivery of appropriate courses of action to help meet key government priorities, ministerial objectives, and positively impact citizen’s lives.

Job description

Policy professionals play a pivotal role in helping ministers navigate complex policy issues and make the commitments of the government a reality.

You will work with ministers, other Civil Service professions and stakeholder networks to propose, design and oversee delivery of government policy.

You will develop agility of thought, and learn how to approach issues strategically, tactically and creatively to develop ideas that will achieve objectives.

You will have opportunities to learn the systems of government, support ministers with objective and impartial advice, navigate the complexities of Parliament. You may also work with other governments both in the UK and overseas.

You will understand how to take a broad view to ensure you’ve weighed up the implications and deliverability of your proposals. You will also work closely with Operational Delivery colleagues to monitor, manage and adapt policies over time to ensure they remain effective in practice.

You will learn how to develop strong working relationships and build productive networks in order to bring a range of perspectives to bear in developing effective policy proposals. You will also develop the skills to feel comfortable working in a complex, fast paced and dynamic environment.

There will be lots to learn on the job, but you will be working within a supportive environment to help you develop both the softer and more technical skills required of policy professionals. You will have access to a carefully structured curriculum as well as the opportunity to build and learn from a constructive network of current and future leaders.

Work at the heart of government is always changing, but your three years on the Fast Stream scheme will be shaped to ensure you hone your skills and gain a breadth of experience to support you on your journey to becoming a future leader.


We aim to put all successful candidates through Security Clearance (SC). However, if you are ineligible for SC, please do not be deterred from applying; we have plenty of exciting roles available that only require standard Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) pre-employment checks. You can find more information about vetting clearance levels here: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/united-kingdom-security-vetting-clearance-levels

You need to have or be on track to receive, a 2:2 or higher in any degree subject, including degree apprenticeships
Existing civil servants can apply without a degree

Alongside your salary of £31,554, Fast Stream and Emerging Talent contributes £9,141 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

The programme provides a solid foundation for promotion and long-term career progression within the profession and offers many advantages, which include:

Responsibility and autonomy in a variety of roles at the heart of the Civil Service
Excellent training and development opportunities including a professional qualification
Close contact with senior civil servants and the opportunity to join a valuable network of future leaders
Possible opportunity for international work
Enhanced support as you off-board from the scheme into your permanent policy role
Potential earning opportunities between £45k and £62k upon successful completion of the scheme

Further employment benefits include a generous annual leave offer starting at 25 days plus national holidays, access to the highly competitive Civil Service Pension Scheme, flexible working opportunities, season ticket loans, sports and social activities, childcare assistance and more.

There are several phases in the Fast Stream application process. Some of these assessments are multimedia in that they present information in video, audio, graphical or visual formats, as well as text. We hope you find it an engaging process and one that gives you a real insight into the role of a fast streamer.

At the initial application stage you will be asked to complete some background information which will include some diversity questions - which are for monitoring purposes only and will have no bearing on selection outcomes - along with the opportunity to identify your preferences in terms of the different Fast Stream schemes. You can choose up to three.

When you apply please register with a personal email address, and not a work or university email address.

Assessment Phases

There are 2 online tests:

Work-based scenarios - This test measures interpersonal skills, utilising video based scenarios and you are required to assess the effectiveness of various responses.

Case Study assessment - In this test you are required to take work based scenarios on an imaginary role, learning and responding to a series of challenges and situations and adapting to the changes you are presented with.

Location

About the job

Job summary

Please refer to Job Description

Job description

Proud to serve. Proud to keep justice going.

Our Delivery Managers play a critical role helping deliver justice. If you’re customer focussed, intent on delivering excellent service, enthusiastic about leading and motivating a team, then this role gives you the opportunity to play a pivotal role within HM Courts & Tribunals Service (HMCTS).

About us

HMCTS is an agency of the Ministry of Justice and is responsible for the administration of criminal, civil and family Courts and Tribunals in England and Wales. Our roles support our service users and colleagues within HMCTS, where people and businesses access potentially life-changing justice. We’re looking for individuals who are committed to public service and making a difference in people’s lives to deliver justice. If you are interested in developing a career with a real purpose, please apply.

Your role

Leading your team, you’ll support your Operations Manager(s) to meet operational needs, deliver performance objectives and provide a consistent and customer-focused service.

You’ll maintain positive and effective working relationships with the judiciary, supporting agencies, and user groupsand strive for continuous improvement to improve operational efficiency. You’ll need to be familiar with work environments that are process and compliance driven and able to constructively manage complaints and complete corrective actions within set timescales. You’ll understand the importance of Health and Safety, IT/Workstation compliance and identifying and escalating any Court facilities issues.

About you

Are you a hands-on problem solver with the ability to engage with people at all levels and deliver excellent service through effectively leading a team? Are you able to reflect on an issue and take a collaborative and diplomatic approach to your work? If you do, this varied and challenging role is for you.

A confident communicator, you will use your skills and abilities to effectively work and engage with all court users, lead your team and set local priorities and objectives aligned to national/regional strategies and plans. Driven by your enthusiasm to provide excellent customer service through your team, you’ll know that employee engagement, morale and motivation is key to delivering a highly effective performance. You’ll be able to give direction and close support to Team Leaders to develop their team plans to form part of the overall business plan for the region. You’ll make sure that targets are met and the team is resourced and trained effectively to meet your allocated budget, identifying and implementing solutions to local problems.

For a full job description, please read the supporting document before applying.

Further details

New recruits to the Civil Service joining MoJ are expected to join at the band minimum.

These operational roles are customer facing, requiring successful applicants to be office based to provide HMCTS services to the public.

Non-contractual hybrid working may be available. Hybrid working arrangements will be determined by the business and will only be available when it has been established that delivering the service from home can be done effectively. We cannot facilitate requests for a particular work from home/working in the office schedule.

Standard full time working hours are 37 hours per week.

HMCTS welcomes part-time, flexible and job-sharing working patterns, where they meet the demands of the role and business needs and are agreed prior to appointment. All applications for part-time, flexible and job-sharing working patterns will be considered in accordance with the MoJ’s Flexible Working policy.

Applications for part-time working will be considered however due to the nature of the role the minimum hours would be 30 hours per week over 5 days.

Travel to other courts

For this post, you will be based in Preston Crown Court and Family Court (Sessions House), The Family Court, Sessions House, Lancaster Road, Preston, PR1 2PD. With regular travel to Leyland Family Hearing Centre, Lancastergate, Leyland, PR25 2EX.

Skilled Worker Visa

This role is not eligible for new Skilled Worker visas in accordance with the current immigration rules.

From 22 July 2025, the Government introduced changes to the Skilled Worker visa route. The department cannot consider sponsoring you for this role unless you have held a Skilled Worker visa prior to the 22 July 2025 changes. If you have held a Skilled Worker visa continuously, please raise this during your vetting checks and eligibility will be assessed in accordance with the immigration rules and transitional provisions in place.

If you are applying for this role and you have not held a Skilled Worker visa prior to the 22 July 2025 changes, you will need to consider your options for obtaining and/or maintaining your right to work in the UK in light of these changes. Successful applicants must ensure they have and maintain the legal right to live and work in the Civil Service and in the United Kingdom.

The Department will continue to comply with UK Immigration Rules applied in the UK and Civil Service. You can read more about Skilled Worker visas and the eligibility criteria here.

Person specification

Please refer to Job Description

Behaviours

We'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:

  • Leadership
  • Managing a Quality Service

Technical skills

We'll assess you against these technical skills during the selection process:

  • Could you provide us with an experience where you improved performance on your team. What did you do and what was the result?

description:

About the job

Job summary

The Honours & Awards team of nine, led by Meg Taylor (G6), is part of the Public Bodies, Appointments and Honours team within Corporate Strategy.

The honours team manage honours nominations from across DCMS sectors, two rounds per year: New Year’s Day and the King’s Birthday. The dedicated team delivers each element of the process and works closely with Cabinet Office as well as the independent honours committees, SCS and Ministers. This is an exciting time to be working within the honours system, as a high priority for both our Secretary of State and our Permanent Secretary.

DCMS plays an active role in Arts & Media, Sport, and Community & Voluntary Service lists, as well as contributing to Public Service, Economy and Science Technology and Research lists. DCMS is the biggest departmental contributor of nominations to the Honours system.

Job description

This is a new, high-profile role at the heart of the Department's honours work. It offers a unique opportunity to lead strategic reform of the DCMS honours system and help ensure that honours better reflect the diversity, achievements and contribution of people across the whole of the UK. Improving the honours system is a key ministerial priority. Following an internal review of DCMS honours processes, you will lead work to implement a programme of reform and drive improvements across the department. You will also play a central role in shaping DCMS's contribution to ongoing improvements to the honours system led by the Cabinet Office.

You will lead two major workstreams:

  • Deliver honours system reform within DCMS. Implementing the recommendations from the departmental honours review; developing policies and processes that strengthen the quality, diversity and regional representation of honours nominations; designing and leading engagement with senior stakeholders, including Ministers, the Permanent Secretary, Honours Committee Chairs; and driving cultural and organisational change to improve understanding and participation in the honours system across the department.
  • Lead DCMS engagement on the cross- government honours review. Coordinating DCMS’ contribution to the cross-Government honours review; providing strategic advice to ministers and senior leaders.

You will manage and be supported by an HEO analyst, who will provide data, insight and demographic analysis to support policy development and drive improvements in the diversity of nominations.

Person specification

The ideal candidate would have the following key skills and experience:

Essential requirements:

  • Exceptional ability to work at pace operationally, to deliver on strategic priorities whilst meeting deadlines;
  • Strong political awareness: the ability to build credibility and trust with ministers and officials at the highest levels of government;
  • Excellent communication skills: adept at advising verbally and in writing;
  • Significant experience of working in ambiguity, particularly in self-starting and developing iterative work and a strategic way forward with limited parameters;
  • Significant experience engaging multiple stakeholders with a wide range of seniority, including across Whitehall and external to Government;
  • Experience of using CRM software and AI for reporting and streamlining of processes and data;
  • Confident using data to inform evidence-based decision making and recommendations.

Desirable Skills:

  • Previous experience delivering strategic recommendations on a high priority and high profile area;
  • Previous experience working with Cabinet Office, No10 or the Royal Palace.

title: Assistant, Digital Content (Part-Time/Seasonal)
description:
Monumental Sports & Entertainment (MSE) is one of the leading integrated sports and entertainment companies globally. MSE’s portfolio spans premier professional sports teams, world-class venues, and next-generation media properties, with marquee assets including the NHL’s Washington Capitals, NBA’s Washington Wizards, WNBA’s Washington Mystics, NBA G League’s Capital City Go-Go, Capital One Arena, and Monumental Sports Network, along with an investment in Team Liquid.

Rooted in the nation’s capital, MSE brings Washington, D.C's distinct influence, ambition, and leadership to the global sports and entertainment landscape. The company harnesses the power of its platform to drive continuous innovation and deliver extraordinary experiences that inspire and unite our community, our fans, and our people.

Our success is powered by talented people who bring passion, creativity, and collaboration to everything they do. If you're looking to build your career in a dynamic, fast-paced organization that's shaping the future of sports and entertainment, we'd love to hear from you.

Position Overview

The Digital Content Publisher supports the publishing, programming, and presentation of content across Monumental Sports Network’s digital platforms. This role helps ensure live events, original programming, podcasts, highlights, and other video content are published accurately, on time, and optimized for the best fan experience. The ideal candidate is organized, meticulous, comfortable working within digital content platforms, and able to prioritize tasks in a fast-paced sports media environment. They will support live programming and adapt to evolving content needs.

Are you passionate about digital media, sports content, and creating engaging experiences for fans? If so, we'd love to hear from you!

Responsibilities

  • Support the daily publishing and scheduling of video content across Monumental+, Monumental Sports Network digital properties, YouTube, and other owned and operated platforms.
  • Plan, distribute, revise, and manage live events, full episodes, highlights, clips, podcasts, trailers, promotional content, and other digital video and audio assets.
  • Build and maintain content pages, collections, trays, playlists, and other merchandising placements within Monumental+.
  • Curate content placement across digital platforms to improve discoverability, support programming priorities, and build a consistent user experience.
  • Add and preserve accurate titles, descriptions, artwork, thumbnails, tags, categories, availability windows, and other publishing-related information inside content management systems.
  • Perform quality assurance checks before and after publishing to confirm content, metadata, artwork, links, and playback experiences are accurate.
  • Support digital programming related to the Capitals, Wizards, Mystics, Go-Go, and other Monumental Sports Network live events and seasonal highlights.
  • Work closely with Content Strategy, Production, Product, Marketing, and other internal teams to collect assets and complete publishing plans.
  • Assist in managing programming calendars, publishing trackers, content inventories, and other operational documents employed by the Content Strategy team.
  • Aid in the upkeep and arrangement of the network’s digital content library.
  • Troubleshoot publishing issues and bring up technical problems to the appropriate Product, Engineering, or platform teams when necessary.
  • Monitor digital platforms for outdated, duplicated, incorrectly merchandised, or improperly published content and assist with ongoing platform cleanup.
  • Provide support for publishing requirements during evenings, weekends, and holidays as needed by the network’s live sports and programming schedule.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Keen focus on accuracy and excellent organizational abilities.
  • Capacity to handle several publishing projects and deadlines at the same time.
  • Comfortable adapting to and operating within content management systems and other digital publishing tools.
  • Strong written communication skills and editorial judgment.
  • Familiarity with digital video, streaming platforms, YouTube, or sports media is preferred.
  • Experience with CMS platforms, digital publishing, video operations, or content management is preferred.
  • Ability to work independently while communicating clearly with a collaborative, cross-functional team.
  • Interest in sports, streaming, digital media, or content programming is strongly preferred.
  • Availability to commit around 25 hours weekly, with adaptability for live broadcasts and urgent content requirements.

Pay Rate: $25.00 USD/hour

We are an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

title: Senior DevOps Engineer
description:
Who we are

DigiCert is a global leader in intelligent trust. We protect the digital world by ensuring the security, privacy, and authenticity of every interaction. Job summary

We are seeking a Senior DevOps Engineer who will play a role in updating the state of our infrastructure, automation, and operational excellence. This role requires a deep understanding of systems, networking, monitoring, and security, with a strong bias toward automation, reliability and scale. The ideal candidate will be a technical leader, helping to shape the direction of infrastructure and tooling.

What you will do

  • Implementation of infrastructure automation, monitoring, and system reliability practices committed to providing 100% service availability.
  • Able to perform forensic system administration, troubleshooting unfamiliar Linux systems and services.
  • Demonstrates a SecOps mindset with a focus on secure automation and hardened Linux system administration.
  • Champion the use and advancement of DevOps best practices including CI/CD, infrastructure as code, and zero-touch provisioning.
  • Utilize best practices in release management, incident management, capacity planning, and operational readiness.
  • Instrumentation of services with visualization to speed triage (lower MTTR) allowing no direct access to systems.
  • Exerts technical influence horizontally—up and laterally to fellow seniors, and down to the team.
  • Acts as a mentor to DevOps and engineering team members; share knowledge and foster a culture of learning and continuous improvement.
  • Proactively identify and implement opportunities to increase system resiliency.
  • Implement technical direction around infrastructure, cloud, networking (BGP), and automation strategy.
  • Participate in on-call rotation, demonstrating strong customer empathy and responsiveness to incidents.
  • Own and improve standard operating procedures and system documentation.
  • Research, prototype, and implement new technologies across cloud, virtualization, and hardware platforms.

What you will have

  • Strong Linux systems administration background with a deep understanding of how Linux interacts with hardware (CPU, memory, disk, networking).
  • Advanced proficiency in scripting and automation using Ansible, Bash, Python, Packer, and Terraform.
  • Hands-on experience with AWS services (EC2, IAM, VPC, etc.) and provisioning tools like Terraform and Packer.
  • Experience with datacenter operations including racking, stacking, and remote system management.
  • Proven ability to manage and configure systems at scale with zero-touch provisioning approaches.
  • Experience managing monitoring systems and developing custom dashboards for observability.
  • Solid understanding of networking within a linux environment (Router -> Switch -> Server -> Virtualization -> Linux -> Service) ; BGP and DNS experience is a plus.
  • Passion for operational excellence, security, and performance.
  • Ability to self-manage, communicate effectively, and collaborate with diverse technical teams.
  • Willingness and ability to learn new technologies as required.

Nice to have

  • Experience with Kentik, Splunk, or similar network visibility and observability platforms.
  • Familiarity with modern CI/CD tools and pipeline architecture.
  • Willingness and ability to learn new languages as required.
  • Experience in designing, developing, and maintaining RESTful APIs following coding best practices.
  • Understanding of release management processes in large-scale environments.

Benefits

  • Competitive compensation and comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage
  • Retirement savings programs with company matching (401(k) or RRSP)
  • Generous paid time off, including holidays, and vacation
  • Paid parental leave and family support benefits
  • Life and disability coverage
  • Flexible spending and health savings options (where applicable)

  • Employee Assistance Program with 24/7confidential support for employees and families
  • Education assistance and professional development opportunities
  • Access to LinkedIn Learning and continuous learning resources
  • Employee referral bonus program and additional company perks and discounts

title: Senior Director, Strategy and Growth, Electromagnetic Defensive Solutions
description:
Reporting to the President, Electromagnetic Defensive Solutions (EDS), Honeywell Aerospace, the Senior Director, Strategy and Growth is responsible for developing and executing the enterprise growth strategy across the global defense, commercial aerospace, and international markets. This executive will identify and capture new business opportunities, expand strategic customer relationships, and lead market development initiatives that accelerate sustainable revenue growth.

The leader will drive strategic pursuits across Electronic Warfare, Radar and Sensor Systems, Advanced RF technologies, Advanced Computing, AI-enabled mission systems, and emerging commercial applications. The role is accountable for achieving Annual Operating Plan (AOP) growth commitments while shaping and executing EDS’s three-year and five-year Strategic Plan (STRAP).
Partner with Offering Management to identify, prioritize, and commercialize high-growth opportunities across unmanned platforms, autonomous systems, advanced RF technologies, AI-enabled mission systems, and adjacent commercial markets; ensuring alignment between customer demand, portfolio investments, product strategy, and growth execution.

The position partners closely with Honeywell Aerospace leadership, business units, Engineering, ISC, Product Management, Finance, and Honeywell Aerospace international and commercial organizations to accelerate growth through organic expansion, international partnerships, adjacent market entry, and portfolio development.

This role has broad executive engagement across DoD service branches, direct customers, and will also interface with Honeywell Aerospace executive management.

This role has a Hybrid work arrangement (at least three days per week in office) and can be based at one of the following locations: San Diego, CA; San Jose, CA; Lansdale, PA; Phoenix, AZ; Clearwater, FL; Minneapolis, MN; Washington, DC.

Key Responsibilities:
Enterprise Growth Strategy:
• Develop and execute EDS’s global growth strategy supporting defense, adjacent commercial industries, and international expansion.
• Identify, qualify, and capture new opportunities within Electronic Warfare, Radar, RF Systems, Mission Computing, Software, Space, and emerging technology markets.
• Expand Honeywell EDS presence into international defense markets through internal Honeywell Aerospace strategic partnerships
• Drive commercial market expansion by identifying dual-use technologies and adjacent commercial applications.
• Lead market assessments to identify emerging technologies, customer needs, competitive positioning, and investment priorities.
• Develop market entry strategies for new countries, commercial sectors, and strategic growth platforms.
• Partner with Offering Management to define the long-term EDS growth portfolio and investment roadmap.
• Build multi-year growth pipelines that support Annual Operating Plan (AOP) and long-range strategic objectives.
• Validate and execute the 3-year and 5-year Strategic Plan (STRAP).

Strategic Capture & Business Development:
• Lead enterprise capture strategy for major domestic and international pursuits.
• Develop customer-specific value propositions that differentiate Honeywell EDS technologies.
• Partner with Product Management to shape next-generation aligned with market demand.
• Lead cross-functional pursuit teams from opportunity identification through contract award.
• Increase pipeline conversion, win rates, bookings, and profitable revenue growth.

International & Commercial Expansion
• Develop strategic relationships with foreign governments, international OEM’s, adjacent commercial customers, and global partners.
• Identify exportable technologies and support international licensing and compliance strategies.
• Partner with Honeywell Aerospace international and commercial business teams to leverage existing global customer relationships and accelerate market penetration.
• Expand participation in international trade shows and strategic industry events.

Customer & Executive Engagement:
• Build executive-level relationships across DoD, allied governments, prime contractors, and strategic commercial customers.
• Represent Honeywell EDS at executive customer meetings, industry forums, and strategic planning sessions.
• Improve customer loyalty, Voice of Customer (VOC) metrics, and long-term strategic partnerships.

Leadership & Organizational Development:
• Lead and develop a high-performing Growth organization focused on business development, capture excellence, strategic planning, and market development.
• Build organizational capability supporting international growth, commercial expansion, and advanced technology markets.
• Develop talent and succession plans supporting long-term organizational growth.

Key Success Factors:
• Revenue Growth
• Orders & Bookings
• Pipeline Growth
• Win Rate Improvement
• International Revenue Expansion
• Commercial Market Revenue
• AOP Financials (Revenue, Margin Achievement)
• Customer Satisfaction (VOC)
• Strategic Partnership Development
• Portfolio Expansion

SECURITY CLEARANCE
This position requires U.S. citizenship and the ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government security clearance in accordance with 32 CFR Part 117 (NISPOM.) Non-U.S. citizens are not eligible for clearance processing for this role. All applications are reviewed in compliance with national security requirements.

Job summary

Do you want to work on one or the most exciting transformation projects in the public sector?

The Defence Housing Service (DHS) is being created through the Armed Forces Bill to deliver a step-change in housing for the UK’s Armed Forces and their families following the publication of the Defence Housing Strategy on 3 November 2025, which marked the most significant change to Armed Forces housing in over 50 years. DHS will bring a dedicated focus to improving the homes, communities and lived experience of Service personnel, placing families firmly at the heart of everything it does.

This is one of the most ambitious housing transformation programmes in the UK today. Backed by a £9.2 billion investment, DHS will modernise tens of thousands of homes, introduce a more proactive and customer-focused approach to maintenance, and unlock new opportunities to develop housing on Defence land. DHS will have the focus and agility to deliver change at pace, combining public service values with greater flexibility to build the skills, systems and partnerships needed for the future.

This is a rare opportunity to be part of shaping its culture, influencing how it works, and helping deliver lasting improvements for Service families across the UK.

The Defence Housing team is currently part of the Defence Infrastructure Organisation (DIO), who respond to the evolving needs of our military personnel, and the ways in which they live, work, train and deploy. We are proud to be the expert partner Defence needs for all their infrastructure requirements. From large scale infrastructure projects such as runways for the F35 fighter jets to net carbon-zero accommodation for our Service families, our activities focus relentlessly on our customers, and our outputs are unique in the UK and across the globe!

DIO , What we deliver every day.

The future delivery model for this team is currently under review and may change as part of potential organisational developments. Job description

As Assistant Head, Strategy Development, you’ll will work closely with the Deputy Head of Strategy, cross-cutting stakeholders and experts, to translate strategic priorities into clear, deliverable outputs.

You’ll bring together evidence, insight and a range of perspectives, to tackle complex cross-cutting strategy challenges, whilst enhancing business capabilities and driving performance. You’ll lead on a variety of interesting strategic areas, which are likely to include the Corporate Strategy, Annual Report and bespoke cross-cutting projects, that ensure Service Personnel and their families are at the heart of defence development activities.

You’ll need to hit the ground running, with strong strategic thinking, leadership capabilities and a track record of seeing the bigger picture, turning complex issues into clear, practical recommendations. You’ll be passionate about building strategy from the ground up and dedicating time and resources to develop team capability, to make DIO Accommodation Strategy a great place to work.

Responsibilities

  • Support delivery of key DIO strategies, such as the Corporate Strategy, to provide a clear vision, evidence-based objectives and deliverable outputs for the organisation.

  • Bring together stakeholder perspectives, to address gaps and opportunities to support clear decision making, against Strategy deliverables.

  • Lead monitoring and reporting against The Defence Housing Strategy recommendations, identifying key risks and areas for improvement.

  • Lead and line-manage a small Strategy team, providing guidance and mentorship as required, to ensure alignment with strategy development and delivery.

  • Lead high-profile, cross cutting projects on behalf of senior leaders, to help drive forward delivery of Defence Housing Strategy recommendations and wider organisational priorities.

  • Provide clear strategic outputs that influence tangible operational and policy change, putting Service Personnel and their families at the heart of areas for improvement.

  • Ensure recommendations from strategic projects have clear owners and implementation arrangements to drive successful delivery; establishing project structures, plans and governance to maintain momentum, managing risk and dependencies to deliver high-quality outcomes.

  • Build and maintain strong working relationships with a wide range of stakeholders including internal DIO teams, wider MOD colleagues, external partners and serving personnel/families and their representatives.

Person specification

1. Demonstrable experience of strategic thinking, strategy development and delivery. (personal statement)

2. Strong leadership capabilities, able to work with and bring together a wide range of individuals and teams to work on shared objectives. (personal statement)

3. Experience of project and/or programme management, including structure, governance and risk management.

4. Line management experience, including building capability and developing high performing teams.

5. Able to demonstrate ability to analyse evidence, evaluate options and make strategic recommendations.

6. Excellent stakeholder management skills, able to build strong working relationships, to influence and deliver objectives.

Additional information

We have a strong learning and development ethos, supporting you to fulfil your potential by providing learning and development tailored to your role, professional skills development, access to thousands of training courses through Civil Service Learning and the ability to obtain industry recognised qualifications, supported by MOD.

This role can be based at London SW1A 2HB, Whittington WS14 9PY, Andover SP11 8HJ, Wyton PE28 2EA or Bristol BS34 8QW. Work location will be agreed once the successful candidate has been selected.
