About the job

Job summary

Do you want to use your analytical skills to make a real difference across government?

Are you curious, detail-focused and keen to improve the models behind important public decisions?

This varied role will see you lead reviews of government models, providing advice to improve their clarity, robustness and reliability while shaping how we deliver and develop our model quality assurance services. Our current and recent work includes assuring analysis included in ministerial submissions and departmental business cases, and models used in implementation of key policies supporting the government’s missions. We are advising on policies supporting the circular economy, cover for clinical negligence, managing the costs of nuclear decommissioning, education spending, healthcare funding and payment models and more.

About us

At the Government Actuary’s Department (GAD) our vision is to be bold and trusted partners in risk and finance, enhancing decision making for lasted benefits to society. We work closely with clients to understand their needs, develop solutions together and deliver high-quality advice. We continually look for innovative and efficient ways to increase our impact and provide greater value. The department’s work covers quality assurance of analysis, financial modelling, and policy support in relation to insurance and contingent liabilities, pension schemes, financial risk, and social security.

For further information about the role and GAD, please see the following pack: Analytical Model Quality Assurance Lead - Analytical Model Quality Assurance Lead

Job description

About the role

The role sits within the Analytical Solutions Team (AST) which comprises around 80 analysts and actuaries and works across a wide and growing range of analytical areas. You will be part of the Models, Development & Assurance team whose mission is to deliver high-quality models and systems that help government make better decisions.

Models often sit at the heart of major financial, policy and operational decisions. As our Model Quality Assurance Lead, you will help ensure that the analytical models used by the clients we work with that inform important government decisions are robust, transparent and, fit for purpose and have appropriate governance and controls. You will also provide thought leadership to develop and strengthen our model quality assurance service offering.

This role would suit an experienced professional with a strong track record in model quality assurance and experience across a range of analytical methods and technical tools and environments. You will be comfortable leading analytical work, providing oversight and direction to others, and drawing on specialist expertise from across the wider organisation. Experience of consulting or working in / with government or public sector organisations and the analytical challenges they face, would be particularly valuable.

What does the role involve?

You will lead a varied portfolio of projects reviewing complex analytical models. While much of the team’s current work focuses on Excel-based financial models, it increasingly covers models built in tools such as R and Python and using statistical methods. Regardless of the tool, each project involves some element of validation (checking the model is fit for purpose), verification (checking the model has been correctly) or providing advice on governance, controls and good practice depending on the clients need. A key part of the role is bringing together and managing the right blend of skills and expertise to deliver high-quality assurance work, ensuring projects meet client requirements and are delivered on time and within budget. Alongside project delivery, you will help develop model assurance capability across the organisation, champion high standards, and contribute to the growth of our model QA offering. This is a varied role that combines technical challenge, stakeholder engagement and strategic influence. As such you will become an integral part of the Analytical Solutions Team with broad influence throughout the organisation.

Working closely with our client-facing Risk & Assurance team, you will help shape and develop our model QA portfolio, identifying opportunities where our expertise can add value and ensuring we are delivering the right solutions to client needs. You will directly manage two SEO specialists who support the delivery of model QA projects, while also drawing on a wider network of analysts and actuarial staff from across the department. This gives you access to a broad range of technical skills and expertise, allowing you to assemble and lead the right teams for each engagement.

Your primary responsibility will be ensuring the successful execution of diverse and sometimes unpredictable model QA projects undertaken by the team. This role requires the capability to adapt existing knowledge to novel and unfamiliar circumstances. As the analytical context within which we operate evolves we are also seeking you to provide thought leadership about how the organisation approaches its model QA offering and how we can adapt to meet new and emerging needs, such as Large Language Models.

Person specification

Managing delivery

  • Lead the delivery of model quality assurance projects, ensuring work meets client requirements and is delivered on time and within budget.
  • Build and manage project teams by drawing on expertise from across the department to deliver high-quality outcomes.
  • Provide clear and practical advice on model risks, controls and good practice.
  • Work with clients and stakeholders to understand their needs and ensure our services deliver value.

Building capability

  • Lead and promote best practice in the quality assurance of analytical models across the organisation.
  • Develop and maintain guidance, tools and resources to support effective project delivery.
  • Plan and deliver training and knowledge-sharing activities to strengthen model QA capability.
  • Drive continuous improvement in the quality and efficiency of model QA delivery.

Providing leadership

  • Lead and develop a small team, providing coaching, support and direction.
  • Help shape and grow the organisation's model QA offering, working closely with colleagues across the business.
  • Act as a senior point of contact for model QA, providing leadership on complex or high-profile work.
  • Build strong relationships and promote a collaborative, inclusive and high-performing culture

Other

  • To ensure effective and agile co-operation with other teams within AST, including flexible working across teams as required to meet client demand.

Please note: Applications for part-time working will be considered; however, the minimum part-time working arrangement available for this role is 80% of full-time hours.

Behaviours

We'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:

  • Working Together
  • Delivering at Pace
  • Communicating and Influencing
  • Leadership

Technical skills

We'll assess you against these technical skills during the selection process:

  • Experience of identifying model risks, errors, weaknesses or limitations, and making practical recommendations to improve quality, transparency and control. (Essential)
  • A broad knowledge of applying modelling techniques (e.g. statistical, mathematical or financial modelling) to real world problems, use cases and potential impact, as well as tools and technologies. (Essential)
  • Experience with Excel/VBA for analytical and financial modelling. (Essential)
  • Experience with Python or R for data science including the core Python framework (pandas, numpy, matplotlib etc) or R framework (base-R, tidyverse, data.table etc) for data science and visualisation. (Essential)

location: The locations for this role are Newport, Titchfield (Fareham).
description:

Location

The locations for this role are Newport, Titchfield (Fareham).

This role is aligned to ONS hybrid working principles, which are based on attending the office with purpose. The postholder will be expected to contribute to the organisation’s overall 40% office attendance, in line with business and role requirements.​

The induction process for the role will be conducted in person.

About the job

Job summary

The Office for National Statistics (ONS) is the UK’s largest producer of official statistics, covering a range of key economic, social and demographic topics. These include measuring changes in the value of the UK economy, estimating the size, geographic distribution and characteristics of the population, and providing indicators of price inflation, employment, earnings, crime and migration.

The last few years has seen an extensive overhaul of security and information management to meet the challenges of corporate and statistics transformation in technology, methods and practice, the Digital Economy Act and organisational risk appetite. The capability is evolving and expanding to address changes in threat and business direction.

This Cyber Security Threat Hunting Principal role sits within the Security and Information Management (SaIM) Directorate, which operates six key services across ONS: Security Risk Advice and Management; Knowledge and Information Management (KIM); Physical Security and Business Continuity; Security Compliance and Audit (SCA); Cyber Security; and Security Culture Services.

Job description

The role will lead in delivering the Cyber Security Threat Hunting function which is part of the Cyber Security division, within the Security and Information Management directorate.

This will involve having a detailed understanding of the methods used to malicious attackers as well as business understanding to be able to identify unusual and malicious activity. The role will lead on complexity threat hunts to proactively identify potential malicious activity present in the ONS IT estate and vulnerabilities that could be used for malicious activity. Findings from these threat hunts will be reported to the senior leaders in Security and Information Management, Cyber Security Threat Hunting Principal will advice and lead on remediation steps against identified findings and vulnerabilities.

In addition, the role holder will assist in major incident response providing highly skilled resource to the Cyber Security Incident Response Principal when required.

Typical assignments

  • Delivering strategic objectives for Cyber Security Threat Hunting function over the three-year Security and Information Management (SaIM) strategy period.
  • Conduct Cyber Security Threat Hunting aligned to the cyber threat faced by ONS, scope the threat hunts hypothesis and report the findings to the Head of Cyber Security.
  • Identify opportunities to improve the quality of security alerts and work with the cyber analytics to implement changes to alerting, ensuring all teams involved are briefed and appropriate and high-quality documentation is created.
  • Identify misconfiguration and other vulnerabilities present in the ONS network, leading the remediation, working with the stakeholders in Vulnerability Management and Digital Services.
  • Liaise with other government departments to assist in the identification and remediation of cyber security threats.

Responsibilities

  • Lead the Cyber Security Threat Hunting function, developing the function and integrating it into the cyber security division.
  • Define and advising on techniques and procedures to undertake Cyber Security Threat Hunting activity.
  • Create Cyber Security Threat Hunting hypothesis, undertake testing and produce detailed reports.
  • Report the findings and management information of the Cyber Security Threat Hunts to the Head of Cyber Security.
  • Identifying opportunities to improve protective monitoring and vulnerability management.
  • Support the remediation of high-priority cyber security incidents.

Government Security Profession Career Framework (opens in another Window)

Person specification

Essential Criteria:

  • Experience in developing and implementing cyber security strategy across people, process, and technology.
  • Lead large-scale, cross-functional or highly complex cyber security threat hunts to proactively hunt for malicious activity not identified by protective monitoring or vulnerability management.
  • Disseminate the implications of Cyber Security Threat Hunting findings and explain the potential business impact if findings are exploited to senior level leadership across government.
  • Lead engagement with senior internal and external stakeholders to manage and provide appropriate Cyber Security assurance to the required standard and in accordance with policy and regulations.
  • Advise on complex issues and mitigation options to appropriate stakeholders or governance forums, acting as an SME across government, the public sector, and industry.
  • Be the key decision maker on reports, overseeing the remediation of vulnerabilities identified during Cyber Security Threat Hunts.
  • Proven track record of analysing complex information associated with Cyber Security.

Desirable

About the job

Job summary

We have an exciting opportunity for an experienced Lead Business Analyst to join our Business Analysis team!

The role is key in the identification, analysis, and delivery of requirements for our service teams whilst working in an Agile way using Scrum framework.

We are looking for an enthusiastic and motivated team player with a passion for driving change, who can use their business analysis skills and expertise to coach and mentor others.

For this role, you will:

  • Have expert Business Analysis skills.
  • Be required to lead and coach others to increase professionalism.
  • Be a confident communicator, able to clearly describe complex concepts to stakeholders across the organisation.
  • Work with aligned professional communities.
  • Oversee senior business analysts, their role, their assignments, development and performance.

If you are interested in this role and enjoy working in a fast-paced development environment, please keep reading to find out more!

Watch this video to find out more about working in Digital at Companies House

Companies House offers a flexible and welcoming culture that promotes a healthy work life balance as well as a proactive approach to wellbeing that allows us to be our best at work. We recognise that people are the key to our success so offer a fantastic benefits package including flexible working with no core hours, 30 days annual leave, 8 bank holidays and 1 privilege day as well as enrolment into the Civil Service Pension scheme with a contribution rate averaging 28%.

Find out more about what a great place Companies House is to work

Please note:

  • Companies House cannot offer Visa sponsorship to candidates through this campaign.
  • Security Clearance (SC) is an essential requirement for this campaign. You'll need to have been in the UK for at least 3 out of the last 5 years to be eligible to apply for SC.
  • The BCS International Diploma in Business Analysis is an essential requirement for this role. We cannot accept alternatives or part qualifications.

Job description

As a Lead Business Analyst, you would work across a range of multi-disciplinary scrum teams and collaborate with a variety of professions including, Agile Delivery Management, Product Management, User Centred Design, Project Management, Architecture and Software Development.

We have multiple scrum teams within Companies House who develop and maintain digital services for our core service lines – Filing/Get Company Information/Intelligence and Enforcement/Common Services. Your role within these teams would be to:

  • Work within a core service line and report to the Head of Business Analysis.
  • Contribute to the agile community at Companies House.
  • Play an active role in the South Wales BA community of practice. Organise events hosted by Companies House and attend and participate in events hosted by other organisations.
  • Lead the business analysis of the projects within a service line and ensure that solutions comply with the Companies House and Digital strategy.
  • Lead the business analysis input into business improvements and service iteration as well as the resolution of live issues to ensure continuity of the service line is maintained.
  • Train and mentor other analysts within the Business Analysis profession to develop their business analysis knowledge and experience.
  • Influence stakeholders across the organisation, and act as an escalation point for business analysts and stakeholders.
  • Champion our vision, mission, strategy, goals, and values within the Business Analysis profession
  • Work within the squad in an agile setting, facilitating, and providing analysis representation during squad activities.
  • Provide advice to external partner scrums to help adherence with CH and Digital strategy.
  • Work with colleagues and contribute to business testing strategies to ensure that testing coverage is achieved across Business Improvement and project work.
  • Develop the strategies for the documentation of process and data flow models. Develop knowledge and experience of using BA tools to model enterprise level processes.
  • Create strategies around developing and storing requirements/reference material for use during/after development.
  • Work with Scrum teams, Developers, Senior BA’s, BA’s and Junior BA’s, Architects and User centric teams to establish best technical solutions for projects/Business Improvement work. Consider changes in technology/systems and how this impacts processes within and across the service lines.
  • Develop networks and relationships with key stakeholders in business teams that make up the service lines.
  • Use your strong written and oral communication skills to clearly describe complex concepts to stakeholders across the organisation.
  • Develop expert knowledge and experience of the organisation and its services to support analysis input into strategic decisions on development of the services.
  • Use Business Analysis knowledge and experience to advise and challenge portfolios of work to ensure it fits with CH and Digital strategy.

Our Lead Business Analysts play a key role in the identification, analysis, and delivery of requirements for these service teams whilst working in an Agile way using Scrum framework. We would love you to be part of our team.

Office Location

You will be aligned to our Cardiff office, where you will be expected to attend on a regular basis. For the first few weeks you will be required to attend the office full time for training.

We use a hybrid approach to the way we work which provides opportunities for you to be adaptable in the way you work so that you can achieve a healthy balance between your work and home life. The degree of choice you have will depend on your role and your day-to-day work activities. Your manager will agree regular patterns of attendance with you; however you may be required to make yourself available to attend the office more frequently when required to meet business needs.

Due to the nature of this role and team structure, this is a full time only role of 37 hours per week.

Security Clearance

To gain (SC) you will need to have been a UK resident for a minimum of 3 years out of the last 5 years.

We are looking for someone who:

  • Has experience in contributing to delivery plans to support strategic aims.
  • Has experience of working on business/service improvements.
  • Has experience of mapping business processes and systems modelling including skills to mentor others in business modelling.
  • Can build good relationships with business teams.
  • Has experience of discussing requirements with diverse user groups to establish deliverables.
  • Will be a role model to define, drive and support change.

About the job

Job summary

On the Finance Fast Stream, you’ll make your mark on some of the most important economic and financial issues facing the UK.

Job description

As a Finance fast streamer, you will work in some of the most fascinating, high profile environments in government and will be part of a 10,000-strong Government Finance Function community based all over the UK. Strong financial management and placing finance at the heart of senior decision making is vitally important in the Civil Service.

You’ll help shape the government’s financial policy and make sure that public services are delivered effectively and efficiently. You will also gain a professional accountancy qualification to equip you with the knowledge and skills for a career in government finance.


We aim to put all successful candidates through Security Clearance (SC). description:

  • Contract type: Permanent
  • Business area: DVLA - Strategy, Policy and Communications Directorate
  • Type of role: Architecture and Data, Governance, Knowledge and Information Management
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time, Job share, Part-time

Swansea

About the job

Job summary

Can you provide expert leadership and guidance to help shape effective data and AI governance?

Have you got experience working with stakeholders to navigate governance, assurance, data protection or organisational change?

Are you passionate about using data responsibly and helping organisations respond to emerging priorities, policies and standards?

If so, we’d love to hear from you!

This role sits within the Government Digital and Data Profession and offer an opportunity to play a key part in strengthening data governance and assurance across DVLA.

Working across Information Assurance and Governance (IAG), you will help ensure teams, projects and initiatives are supported by effective governance and assurance. The role, will involve you developing capability, providing strategic advice on data protection, data and AI governance, and helping DVLA respond to emerging government policy, standards and guidance.

This role will support DVLA in maintaining effective governance while keeping pace with the evolving data and AI landscape.

Joining our department comes with many benefits, including:

  • Employer pension contribution of 28.97% of your salary. Read more about Civil Service Pensions here
  • 25 days annual leave, increasing by 1 day each year of service (up to a maximum of 30 days annual leave), plus 8 bank holidays and a privilege day for the King’s birthday
  • Flexible working options where we encourage a great work-life balance.

Read more in the Benefits section below!

Find out more about what it's like working at DVLA – Home, Civil Service Careers

Job description

This role offers the opportunity to make a meaningful contribution within a collaborative and evolving environment. You’ll work alongside colleagues and stakeholders, bringing your expertise, ideas and enthusiasm to help deliver positive outcomes. It’s a great opportunity for someone who enjoys variety, values teamwork and is keen to continue developing their skills and experience.

Your responsibilities will include, but aren’t limited to:

  1. Serve as a key member of the Information Assurance & Governance Senior Management Team by providing strategic leadership for the Agency's data governance, data management and AI governance agenda.
  2. Work closely with the Chief Data Officer and senior business leaders to develop, implement and continuously improve the Agency's data governance, ensuring alignment with organisational priorities, business transformation and digital ambitions.
  3. Lead the development, implementation and oversight of data governance and AI governance frameworks, policies, standards and operating models, ensuring effective stewardship, accountability and compliance across the organisation.
  4. Lead the identification, assessment and management of organisational data risks, ensuring appropriate controls, mitigations and assurance mechanisms are in place to address risks arising from data processing, sharing, retention, emerging technologies and AI-enabled solutions.
  5. Build and maintain strong relationships with senior stakeholders across the Agency and wider government landscape, influencing decision-making and promoting best practice in data governance, AI assurance and responsible data use.
  6. Horizon-scan emerging legislation, government policy, technologies and best practice relating to data governance, information management and artificial intelligence, assessing organisational impacts and recommending appropriate actions.
  7. Lead, develop and motivate a high-performing team of specialists by developing professional capability within the Government Digital & Data Profession and promoting the adoption of data governance best practice.

Great line management is important to us as an organisation, and we will equip and support line managers to develop the skills set out in the Civil Service Line Management Standards.

For further information on the role, please read the role profile. Please note that the role profile is for information purposes only - whilst all elements are relevant to the role, they may not all be assessed during the recruitment process.

Person specification

To be successful in this role you will need to have the following experience:

  • Experience of considering the bigger picture, recognising wider organisational priorities and strategies and translating them into prioritised data or governance deliverables that support operational delivery and decision-making.
  • Experience in creating, applying or contributing to data and/or AI governance, ensuring appropriate standards, controls and responsible practices are considered.
  • Experience of managing or working with data effectively, including its, accessibility, use, ongoing management and protection.
  • Experience of advising or influencing senior leaders and technical and non-technical audiences on data related issues, ensuring decisions are evidence-based, proportionate, and aligned to organisational objectives.

Additional Information

All successful candidates will need to either hold, or be willing to work towards, the following qualifications once in post:

  • Certificate in Information Security Management Principles
  • An industry-recognised Data Protection qualification

We welcome applications from candidates who can speak Welsh and English. Welsh language skills could be useful in this role, but it is not an assessment criterion, so it won’t put you at any disadvantage during recruitment if you aren’t a Welsh speaker. Please note that the application and assessment process will be held in English.

Working hours, office attendance and travel requirements

Full-time roles consist of 37 hours per week.

Whilst we welcome applications from those looking to work with us on a part-time basis, there is a business requirement for the successful candidate to be able to work at least 35 hours per week.

This role is suitable for hybrid working, which is a non-contractual arrangement where a combination of workplace and home-based working can be accommodated subject to business requirements.

The expectation at present is a minimum of 60% of your working time a month will be spent at either your designated workplace (one of the locations cited in the advert) or, when required for business reasons, in another office/work location/visiting stakeholders. Your designated workplace will be your contractual place of work. There may be occasions where you are required to attend above the minimum expectation.

Occasional travel to other offices may be required, which could also involve overnight stays.

If you have a question about hybrid working, part time/job share hours, flexible working, travelling for work, or require a reasonable adjustment, please contact the Vacancy Holder during the recruitment process to avoid possible disappointment later in the process should your working arrangements not be compatible with the requirements of the role (see below for contact details).

If your application is successful but you have been dismissed from the Civil Service, your application could be removed at the pre-employment checking stage depending on the nature of the dismissal.

Applicants who are successful at interview will be, as part of pre-employment screening, subject to a check on the Internal Fraud Database (IFD). This check will provide information about employees who have been dismissed for fraud or dishonesty offences. This check also applies to employees who resign or otherwise leave before being dismissed for fraud or dishonesty had their employment continued. Any applicant’s details held on the IFD will be refused employment. A candidate is not eligible to apply for a role within the Civil Service if the application is made within a 5-year period following a dismissal for carrying out internal fraud against government.

All external applicants and current employees of accredited non-departmental public bodies (NDPBs) will be required to undergo a Social Media Check. A Social Media Check is a review of your publicly available online activity, typically across platforms like LinkedIn, Facebook, X (formerly Twitter), Instagram, and others. The purpose is to identify any public posts or content that could raise concerns for employers, such as:

  • Hate speech or discriminatory behaviour
  • Threats or acts of violence
  • Illegal activity or substance misuse
  • Sexually explicit material
  • Extremist views or affiliations

Importantly, this check does not involve hacking into your accounts or accessing private messages. It only considers content you have chosen to make public. Employers use this kind of screening to help ensure their workplace remains safe, inclusive, and aligned with company values. It’s not about judging your personality or lifestyle - it’s about checking for potential red flags that might affect the role or company culture. If you have questions or concerns about the social media check, we would be happy to explain in more detail what’s being looked at and how your data is handled securely and fairly.

description:
POSITION SUMMARY

Instruct group fitness classes (e.g., aerobics, spinning, strength training) at all ability levels. Provide advice to individuals on the correct method of exercising with fitness equipment. Assess individual's current exercise program and level of fitness to develop personalized exercise programs and provide fitness counseling. Promote a fun and relaxing atmosphere for guests. Observe activity in the recreational facility and respond appropriately/in accordance with local operating procedure in the event of an emergency. Provide assistance to injured guests until the arrival of emergency medical services. Clean and maintain recreational area, equipment, and supplies. Call Maintenance or an outside service company if machines require service.

Report accidents, injuries, and unsafe work conditions to manager; complete safety training and certifications. Follow company policies and procedures; ensure uniform and personal appearance are clean and professional; maintain confidentiality of proprietary information; protect company assets. Welcome and acknowledge all guests according to company standards; anticipate and address guests’ service needs; assist individuals with disabilities; thank guests with genuine appreciation. Speak with others using clear and professional language. Develop and maintain positive working relationships with others; support team to reach common goals; listen and respond appropriately to the concerns of other employees. Comply with quality assurance expectations and standards. Read and visually verify information in a variety of formats (e.g., small print). Visually inspect tools, equipment, or machines (e.g., to identify defects). Stand, sit, or walk for an extended period of time or for an entire work shift. Move, lift, carry, push, pull, and place objects weighing less than or equal to 50 pounds without assistance and objects weighing in excess of 75 pounds with assistance. Grasp, turn, and manipulate objects of varying size and weight, requiring fine motor skills and hand-eye coordination. Move through narrow, confined, or elevated spaces. Move over sloping, uneven, or slippery surfaces as well as up and down stairs and/or service ramps. Reach overhead and below the knees, including bending, twisting, pulling, and stooping. In addition some states may have additional licensing/registration requirements to be considered for this position. Perform other reasonable job duties as requested.

Education: High school diploma or G.E.D. equivalent.

Related Work Experience: At least 1 year of related work experience.

Supervisory Experience: No supervisory experience.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

License or Certification: CPR Certification

First Aid Certification

Fitness Equipment

Fitness Instruction

Any certification or training required by local and state agencies.

description:

About the job

Job summary

The Defence Nuclear Organisation (DNO) is responsible for the provision of the nuclear deterrent, encompassing our submarines and nuclear warheads, while also advising on UK nuclear planning and fostering international co-operation on nuclear matters. With a multidisciplinary team of over 700 professionals, the DNO brings together expertise in science, engineering, finance, policy, programme delivery, and more. We work in partnership with the Royal Navy, the Submarine Delivery Agency and the Atomic Weapons Establishment as the Defence Nuclear Enterprise (DNE).

Here at DNO we strongly believe that diversity and inclusion is not only the right thing to do but is also essential for a thriving and successful organisation. We have a culture where differences are celebrated, and our people feel supported, included and empowered. Join us and be part of an organisation that truly values diversity and inclusion and makes a positive impact on the world.

Integrated Stockpile Management (ISM) is responsible for the development, delivery and support of both the current in-service Re-Entry System (RES), Future Technologies and the replacement RES. These programmes are owned by Director Warhead Integrated Stockpile Management who maintains the responsibility for delivery of these programmes, provides direction on prioritisation and ensures joint ways of working. The WISM has two parts, the ISM A21/Mk7 and the ISM Mk4A team which share the responsibility for the MOD intelligent customer role across the entire CADMID cycle for the RES (inc. applicable support equipment) and future RES technologies.

Deputy Head Safety & Quality Assurance supports Director WISM in their roles as the Authoriser with Design Authority Responsibilities for Nuclear Weapons, and Nuclear Weapons Transport by providing independent safety advice, management of the audit programme and maintenance of the Warhead Group Quality Management System.

This post is advertised at 37 hours per week.

Job description

The Assistant Head Safety & Quality Assurance (SQA) plays a key leadership role within the Warhead Group (WHG), providing independent assurance to senior leaders on the safety, quality and regulatory compliance of the UK's nuclear warhead programme and defence nuclear material transport operations. Working closely with the Deputy Head SQA, the post holder ensures that nuclear safety cases, operational activities, quality management systems and regulatory arrangements meet policy and regulatory requirements.

Key Duties and Responsibilities

  • Lead and coordinate independent technical assurance activities for nuclear warhead systems and defence nuclear material transport operations, ensuring compliance with regulatory, legislative and safety requirements.
  • Provide advice and assurance to the Nuclear Warhead Approving Authority (NWAA), Life Cycle Phase 2 Authoriser and Managing Director Warhead on nuclear safety and quality matters.
  • Manage and develop a multidisciplinary assurance team, including direct line management of senior assurance specialists and oversight of wider quality and regulatory assurance staff.
  • Lead the assessment and review of nuclear safety cases, safety justifications and operational submissions, ensuring that risks are appropriately identified, managed and reduced to ALARP.
  • Act as Deputy Chair of key nuclear safety committees, facilitating robust technical scrutiny and providing consolidated assurance and recommendations to senior duty holders.
  • Maintain oversight of the Warhead Group Quality Management System, ensuring continued compliance with ISO 9001, Defence Nuclear Safety Regulations and MOD policy.
  • Develop productive relationships with regulators, industry partners and stakeholders, supporting regulatory engagement and ensuring that emerging safety, quality and compliance issues are effectively managed.
  • Champion a strong safety culture across the Warhead Group, promoting high standards of governance, assurance, quality management and continuous improvement.

As the post holder will have access to very sensitive information, there are limitations on travelling to a small number of countries and we will undertake additional security checks as part of the recruitment process. Applications from candidates with close connections to certain countries may take considerably longer to process, or in some cases result in a withdrawal of an offer of employment. Further details will be provided at the conditional offer stage.

title: Recruitment Officer
location: Successful candidates may be based in any of our office locations – Cardiff, Glasgow, or London. We especially welcome applicants from Cardiff and Glasgow.
description:

  • Length of employment: 6 Months
  • Business area: OFGEM - Corporate Services
  • Type of role: Human Resources
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time

Location

Successful candidates may be based in any of our office locations – Cardiff, Glasgow, or London. We especially welcome applicants from Cardiff and Glasgow.

About the job

Job summary

At Ofgem, we are committed to building a workforce that reflects the diverse communities we serve while helping to deliver a cleaner, more affordable and secure energy future for Great Britain. As a Recruitment Officer, you will play a vital role in attracting talented people to our organisation by providing high-quality administrative and coordination support across the full recruitment lifecycle. Working closely with Recruitment Advisors, hiring managers and key stakeholders, you will ensure recruitment campaigns are delivered efficiently, compliantly and with an excellent candidate experience at their heart.

This is a fast-paced and varied role where organisation, attention to detail and customer service are essential. You will be responsible for setting up vacancies and adverts, coordinating candidate communications, arranging interviews and assessments, managing recruitment documentation and maintaining accurate records within our Applicant Tracking System. You will help ensure campaigns progress smoothly, meet agreed service levels and comply with Civil Service Recruitment Principles, data protection requirements and governance standards.

The successful candidate will be a proactive and highly organised administrator who can manage competing priorities while maintaining accuracy and professionalism. You will be confident communicating with candidates, hiring managers and colleagues, handling sensitive information with discretion and supporting reasonable adjustments to create an inclusive recruitment process. Experience within recruitment, HR administration or a regulated environment will be valuable, alongside strong IT skills and a commitment to delivering excellent service.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone looking to develop or build a career in recruitment within a supportive and purpose-driven organisation. You will contribute directly to Ofgem’s success by ensuring we attract and appoint talented individuals who will help deliver our mission, while also identifying opportunities to improve processes, enhance candidate experience and support continuous improvement across the recruitment function.

Ofgem has a culture of inclusion that encourages, supports and celebrates the diverse voices and experiences of our colleagues. It fuels our innovation and helps ensure we can best represent the consumers and the communities we serve. Everyone is welcome - as an inclusive workplace, our employees are comfortable bringing their authentic selves to work.

We are currently recruiting for two opportunities within the team: one permanent position and one fixed-term contract initially for a period of six months. Candidates will be assessed against the role requirements, with appointments made in merit order.

Job description

Key Responsibilities:

Campaign Administration & Candidate Co-Ordination:

  • Set up requisitions and adverts in the ATS, publish to approved channels, manage candidate communications, collate eligibility/right‑to‑work documents and support offer/PECS admin.
  • Ensure prompt, accurate responses to candidate queries.

Interview & Assessment Scheduling:

  • Coordinate panel availability, book rooms/virtual links, issue interview packs and scoring sheets, confirm reasonable adjustments, send invites and confirmations and record outcomes.

Data Quality & Compliance:

  • Maintain complete, audit‑ready records.
  • Follow naming/versioning conventions and data protection requirements. Resolve data gaps and discrepancies.
  • Ensure HR documentation meets legal and policy standards, supporting audits and governance requirements.

Advert Preparation & Content Support

  • Draft and proof adverts using approved templates and language, ensure brand/policy compliance and track response volumes.
  • MI Reporting & Continuous Improvement
  • Analyse routine status reports flag bottlenecks to the Recruitment Advisor and suggest template/process improvements.

Key Outputs and Deliverables:

  • Ensure accurate and timely entry, maintenance and integrity of data in systems.
  • Live, error‑free adverts posted to agreed channels.
  • Accurate interview schedules, complete packs and documented outcomes within agreed timelines.
  • Audit‑ready ATS records across each stage (requisition to offer/checks), with consistent data quality.
  • Clear, timely candidate and panel communications, including reasonable adjustment confirmations.
  • Routine pipeline/status reports that enable advisors and managers to act quickly on risks and delays.

Key Skills and Capabilities

  • Proven administrative experience in recruitment or HR, with strong organisation and attention to detail.
  • Working knowledge of Success Profiles and Civil Service Recruitment Principles, or willingness to learn quickly.
  • Confident user of ATS systems, MS Office and scheduling tools; committed to data accuracy and audit standards.
  • Clear, professional written and verbal communication; customer‑focused and responsive.
  • Ability to manage competing deadlines, reprioritise and maintain composure during peaks.
  • Discretion and integrity in handling confidential and sensitive information.
  • Inclusive mindset and practical handling of reasonable adjustments for candidates and panels.
  • Continuous improvement Mindset. Spots issues early and proposes simple, workable fixes.

Person specification

Essential Criteria:

  • Proven experience providing administrative support within recruitment or HR processes or regulated environment (Lead Criteria)
  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to prioritise tasks and meet agreed SLAs. (Lead Criteria)
  • Strong communication skills, both written and verbal, with a customer-focused approach.
  • Ability to work collaboratively within a team and with hiring managers to progress campaigns effectively.

Desirable Criteria:

  • Experience working within the UK Civil Service or wider public sector, with knowledge of recruitment governance and controls.
  • Experience using applicant tracking systems to maintain accurate data and robust audit trails.

Behaviours

We'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:

  • Delivering at Pace

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £26,694, OFGEM contributes £7,733 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

title: Group Product Manager, Data/ML
description:
Discord has a highly engaged community of millions of daily active users who use the platform for many different reasons, but there’s one thing that nearly everyone does: play video games. Discord plays a uniquely important role in the future of gaming, and we are focused on making it easier and more fun for people to hang out before, during, and after playing games.

As Group Product Manager for Data/ML, you'll drive the vision, strategy, and roadmap for Discord's Machine Learning Platform and its applications, particularly to Advertising, while also championing how the broader company uses data to make product decisions. This is a horizontal role reporting to the VP of Product, Business that touches nearly every product team at Discord, as well as core technical teams, so you'll need to be comfortable driving alignment across stakeholders whose goals are sometimes in tension.

What you'll be doing

  • Guide the product philosophy, vision, and roadmap for Discord's ML Platform and its key use cases (Personalization, Notifications, Safety, Advertising, Recommendations).
  • Own performance against key data and ML business metrics, and proactively report progress to stakeholders across the company.
  • Collaborate deeply with Applied ML, ML Platform, and Data Science to build and prioritize the ML roadmap for our Advertising products.
  • Advise product teams across Discord on how to build and instrument their products with data-first capabilities from the start.
  • Drive cross-functional execution across all product areas, working with engineers/MLEs, security, legal, and policy partners as needed.

What you should have

  • 8+ years of combined experience in data science and product management, including direct, hands-on experience as a data scientist or in a similarly quantitative role before moving into product.
  • 3-5+ years of product management experience owning algorithmic, data-driven systems (e.g., bidding, ranking, personalization, and/or recommendations systems), including responsibility for prioritization, trade-offs, and timelines.
  • Proven ability to analyze and synthesize data directly, not just interpret it secondhand, including comfort with the statistical and quantitative fundamentals behind modern ML systems.
  • Demonstrated technical proficiency working closely with ML/data engineers, including familiarity with ML fundamentals, enough to cut through the buzz and separate what's practical at scale from what isn't.
  • Experience operating across international or distributed teams and stakeholders.

Bonus Points

  • Experience in performance advertising and real-time bidding specifically.
  • Proficiency in modern BI tooling (Looker, Tableau, or similar).
  • Passion for games, gaming, or online communities.

Candidates must reside in or be willing to relocate to the San Francisco Bay Area (Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, Solano, and Sonoma counties). Relocation assistance may be available.

For this role, the Hiring Manager would like folks to be in the office 3 days a week.

The base salary range for this full-time position is listed below. This position will also be eligible for equity and benefits. Our salary ranges are determined by role and level. Within the range, individual pay is determined by additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Please note that the compensation details listed in role postings reflect the base salary only, and do not include equity, or benefits.

Base Salary
$304,000—$380,000 USD

Why Discord?

Discord plays a uniquely important role in the future of gaming. We're a multiplatform, multigenerational and multiplayer platform that helps people deepen their friendships around games and shared interests, and helps developers build and grow their businesses. We believe games give us a way to have fun with our favorite people, whether listening to music together or grinding in competitive matches for diamond rank. Join us in our mission! Your future is just a click away!

Discord is committed to inclusion and providing reasonable accommodations during the interview process. We want you to feel set up for success, so if you are in need of reasonable accommodations, please let your recruiter know.

Please see our Applicant and Candidate Privacy Policy for details regarding Discord’s collection and usage of personal information relating to the application and recruitment process by clicking HERE.

title: Quality/Risk Director
description:
Quality/Risk Director Career Opportunity


Highly regarded and valued for your Quality/Risk Director expertise
Are you seeking a career that not only utilizes your skills but also aligns with your personal values, providing a profound sense of belonging and the opportunity to make a meaningful difference in patients' lives? Look no further than Encompass Health, the nation's leader in in-patient rehabilitation care. As a Quality/Risk Director, you will oversee a hospital-wide quality management program, collaborating with various stakeholders to monitor and enhance the quality of patient care services. Join a team that values collaboration, support, and inclusivity, and embark on a rewarding career close to home and close to your heart, complete with access to cutting-edge equipment and technology and a comprehensive benefits package from day one.


A Glimpse into Our World
At Encompass Health, you'll experience the difference the moment you become a part of our team. Being at Encompass Health means aligning with a rapidly growing national inpatient rehabilitation leader. We take pride in the growth opportunities we offer and how our team unites for the greater good of our patients. Our achievements include being named one of the "World’s Most Admired Companies" and receiving the Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For® Award, among other accolades, which is nothing short of amazing.

Starting Perks and Benefits
At Encompass Health, we are committed to creating a supportive, inclusive, and caring environment where you can thrive. From day one, you will have access to:

  • Affordable medical, dental, and vision plans for both full-time and part-time employees and their families.
  • Generous paid time off that accrues over time.
  • Opportunities for tuition reimbursement and continuing education.
  • Company-matching 401(k) and employee stock purchase plans.
  • Flexible spending and health savings accounts.
  • A vibrant community of individuals passionate about the work they do!

Become the Quality/Risk Director you've always aspired to be

  • Ensure compliance with regulatory agencies, accrediting bodies, corporate and hospital policies, and procedures. Develop, implement, and maintain quality assessment and improvement programs.
  • Assess compliance with federal, state, and industry regulatory and accreditation standards, facilitating processes to remediate and/or maintain compliance. Provide organizational education related to regulations and standards and coordinate local, state, federal, and accreditation surveys.
  • Use a variety of applications (including, but not limited to, PatCom, UDS, ORYX, and Press Ganey) to identify improvement opportunities, generate reports, research issues, identify resources, and access external databases.
  • Ensure the update and maintenance of hospital plans, including the Provision of Care/Scope of Services, Leadership, Information Management, Utilization Review, Infection Control, and Patient Safety plans. Oversee risk management activities, including completion of incident reports, notice of potential claims, corrective action planning, and incident reporting to the Corporate Risk Manager.
  • Coordinate the review, development, and implementation of hospital policies.
  • .Communicate and collaborate with other departments to coordinate care and promptly resolve patient concerns or complaints.
  • Celebrate the accomplishments and successes of our dedicated employees along the way.

Qualifications

  • A bachelor's degree in healthcare or a related field is preferred.
  • License or Certification as required by state regulations.
  • Experience in Quality and/or Risk Management, including primary responsibility for performance improvement activities, regulatory compliance, conflict resolution, leadership, and risk management activities.

title: Director, Enforcement
description:
Classification: Management Band B, Excluded - Pending Exclusion Review

Office Location: Fort St John

Salary: $119,211 - $156,045 – Permanent Full-Time, based on a 35-hour work week.
An additional 3% Location Allowance will be added to posted salary for northern location

About the Job:
The Director, Enforcement (Director) is accountable for the leadership and delivery of the BCER’s provincial enforcement program in accordance with the BCER’s Compliance Policy, regulatory framework, and organizational priorities.

The Director establishes program direction, priorities, risk-based decision-making approaches, performance expectations, and quality assurance processes to support consistent, transparent, and defensible enforcement outcomes. The role provides oversight and authoritative advice on complex and contentious enforcement matters and ensures regulatory, legal, operational, public safety, environmental, and reputational risks are appropriately identified and managed. The Director works collaboratively with leaders and staff throughout the organization in the design, operation and continuous improvement of the BCER’s enforcement program.

The Director leads a geographically dispersed team and is accountable for allocating resources, building organizational capability, and continuously improving BCER’s enforcement approaches in response to emerging risks, regulatory requirements, industry activity, and organizational priorities. In addition, the Director provides expert advice and input into ongoing enforcement investigations and actions under various provincial legislation.

This role represents the BCER with regional agencies and ministry representatives (mining/forestry/environment), regulatory, industry, and other external representatives to enhance the integration of multi-agency services, evaluate implementation of regulatory harmonization, and monitor ongoing industry expansion projects. The Director provides expert advice on the design, implementation and continuous improvement of regulatory approaches including compliance processes assessing company performance against clear, relevant standards. A detailed list of accountabilities, education and experience is outlined in the job description.

Organization Chart:
Commissioner, Chief Executive Officer
Executive Vice President, Safety & Compliance
Vice President, Compliance & Operations
Executive Director, Compliance & Enforcement
Director, Enforcement

Lead the BCER’s provincial enforcement program, establishing program direction, priorities, objectives, standards, and risk-based decision-making approaches to support consistent, effective, and defensible enforcement of regulatory requirements and the protection of public safety and the environment.

Lead and develop a geographically dispersed team, establishing program priorities, allocating resources, managing performance, building capability, and leading organizational change and modernization initiatives to achieve program outcomes and respond to evolving regulatory demands.

Lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of the Enforcement Program Framework, including governance structures, policies, procedures, standards, and guidelines, ensuring the enforcement program responds effectively to evolving legislation, regulatory requirements, industry practices, and organizational priorities.

Provide strategic oversight and authoritative advice on complex or contentious enforcement matters, and determining or recommending enforcement approaches based on regulatory requirements, risk assessments, and potential impacts to operations, public safety, and the environment.

Provide strategic advice and recommendations to Executive and senior leadership on significant enforcement matters, emerging risks, program performance, and opportunities for regulatory or policy improvement.

Establish and oversee program performance measures, quality assurance processes, and service standards to evaluate enforcement effectiveness, monitor provincial trends, assess adherence to enforcement policies and decision-making frameworks, identifying risks, inconsistencies, and opportunities for program improvement.

Provide strategic enforcement expertise and direction in corporate regulatory development and improvement initiatives, ensuring new and evolving regulatory requirements are enforceable and supported by effective enforcement approaches.

Represent the BCER in senior-level discussions with government, regulatory agencies, industry, and other external organizations on enforcement matters.

Provide strategic level input into the BCER risk-based C&E approaches and develop and maintain relationships with strategic staff within other regulatory agencies and Government.

Education:
A degree from a recognized post-secondary institution in a relevant field such as Business Administration, Engineering, Environmental Management, Law, Planning, Public Administration, or Science, or a related field, and seven or more years of directly related experience.

An equivalent combination of education, training, and experience may be considered.

Experience:
Demonstrated experience in a progressively responsible management role within regulatory enforcement, compliance, natural resource regulation, or a related field.

Demonstrated experience leading complex regulatory programs or functions, including establishing program priorities, allocating resources, and overseeing program performance.

Demonstrated experience managing the administration and/or regulation of oil & gas, pipelines, or natural resources.

Demonstrated experience leading professional and/or technical teams, building organizational capability, and managing performance in a complex regulatory or operational environment.

Demonstrated experience developing, implementing, and improving regulatory policies, governance frameworks, standards, guidelines, or risk-based decision-making approaches.

Demonstrated experience interpreting and applying legislation and regulations, including enforcement of legal requirements in administrative and/or prosecutorial contexts.

Demonstrated experience leading organizational change, program modernization, or continuous improvement initiatives to improve regulatory or organizational outcomes.

Demonstrated experience providing strategic oversight or advice on complex, high-risk, or contentious regulatory or enforcement matters.

Demonstrated experience establishing and maintaining effective working relationships with government agencies, regulatory partners, industry, and other stakeholders.

Key Competencies:
Accountability
The ability to take ownership and responsibility for the behaviours and outputs of oneself and others while instilling a sense of motivational ownership through guidance and support.

Communicating Effectively
The ability to convey information clearly, accurately, and appropriately to the intended audience. It involves utilizing multiple forms of communication channels and techniques, such as verbal and written communication, active listening, and nonverbal cues, to ensure a message is understood and received as intended. It involves being mindful of the audience’s needs, preferences, and cultural backgrounds, adapting the message and delivery style accordingly to facilitate mutual understanding and engagement.

Leadership
The ability to inspire and motivate others to maximize their efforts to achieve organizational goals while modelling its values. Effective leaders build a culture based on trust and collaboration, guiding teams towards a common objective and fostering an environment where everyone can thrive.

Performance Management
The ability to measure performance against the plan and continuously improve to achieve organizational goals. It involves developing the knowledge, skills, and abilities of people to support their development and succession management. It also includes the ability to take timely and appropriate corrective action to ensure that performance remains aligned with the organization’s objectives and drives results.

If you are interested in applying for this role and meet the minimum selection criteria, please select “Apply Now” and submit your application prior to the closing date. Applicants should review the education and experience listed in the job requisition and clearly articulate how their work experience and skills are aligned with the requirements. Please note, applicants will only be contacted if they are selected to proceed further in the process.

title: User Researcher
location: Birmingham, Leeds, Liverpool or London (Canary Wharf)
description:
• Job grade: Senior Executive Officer
  • Contract type: Fixed term, Loan, Secondment
  • Length of employment: until 31.12.2027
  • Type of role: Digital, Science
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time, Job share, Part-time
  • Number of jobs available: 2

Location

Birmingham, Leeds, Liverpool or London (Canary Wharf)

About the job

Job summary

UKHSA’s readiness to respond to all threats and hazards. We focus on Agency capability, putting external stakeholder and customer needs at the centre of designs for the future. We identify opportunities to improve public health outcomes through better user experiences.

The team are responsible for:

  • embedding UCD approaches into UKHSA ways of working
  • UCD expertise in project delivery
  • ensuring user needs are understood and designed for, advocating for all users, to achieve equitable outcomes
  • ensuring our products are accessible and developed to the Government Service Standard and use appropriate style guides and patterns
  • leading the UKHSA-wide UCD community of practice to support organisational and in-profession development
  • standards for UCD professionals

Working for your organisation

We pride ourselves as being an employer of choice, where Everyone Matters promoting equality of opportunity to actively encourage applications from everyone, including groups currently underrepresented in our workforce.

UKHSA ethos is to be an inclusive organisation for all our staff and stakeholders. To create, nurture and sustain an inclusive culture, where differences drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our workforce and wider communities. We do this through celebrating and protecting differences by removing barriers and promoting equity and equality of opportunity for all.

Please visit our careers site for more information

Job description

As a user researcher, you’ll work as part of a multidisciplinary squad collaborating with teams across UKHSA. Through effective user research you’ll ensure design projects are rooted in a deep understanding of users and their needs.

Together with other UCD professions, you’ll ensure quality, innovation, and creativity in how we approach all aspects of design and how we bring concepts to life for stakeholders to effect change.

You’ll embody inclusive behaviours. You’ll understand the importance of inclusive research practices, taking pride in ensuring research is representative of a wide range of people and communities.

You’ll be an active part of the UCD community sharing insights and practices within the community and across the organisation.

Your work will help UKHSA to solve problems, improve public health outcomes and address health inequalities.

As a user researcher, you’ll:

  • carry out user research activities, creating research plans, recruiting participants, preparing discussion guides, creating information gathering artefacts, running and moderating user research sessions
  • analyse and synthesise user research data to present clear and engaging user insights and actionable findings, using creative approaches to storytelling
  • contribute to the improvement of user research practice and ways of working by adhering to and embedding consistent and high-quality professional standards
  • drive awareness of user research practices, advocating for user needs and user research to be embedded within strategy, policy and service design
  • work collaboratively and in an inclusive manner by involving teams and colleagues from across UKHSA in user research to help everyone develop a deep understanding of UKHSA’s users’ needs
  • act as the voice of users in the design of our services, make actionable recommendations based on insights and communicate these to stakeholders clearly and confidently
  • ensure research practice is high quality and meets government and NHS standards and industry best practice – using peer reviews and critique processes to gather feedback and share best practice
  • actively contribute to the UKHSA’s community of practice, advocate for user research and support the creation of the right environment and processes to establish the profession within UKHSA

This is not an exhaustive list.

Person specification

Essential criteria

  • Experience of using user-centred design methods and practices in complex organisations
  • Experience of designing and delivering inclusive user research with a range of users
  • Experience of qualitative research methodologies and knowing how to apply different methods to different research projects
  • Experience of using basic techniques to analyse and synthesise findings
  • To be able to create actionable, evidenced-based insights using a variety of techniques to tell compelling stories.
  • Experience of developing user research practices and a good understanding of the key standards in assuring the quality of user research
  • To be able to explain the value of research practice. navigate stakeholder landscapes and gain support for research plans, findings, and ways of working
  • To be able to work as part of a multidisciplinary team, working directly with other professions to ensure effective and timely delivery

Desirable criteria

  • Government service assessments
  • Working in an agile environment
  • Coaching and mentoring other user researchers

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £41,983, UK Health Security Agency contributes £12,162 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).
  • Learning and development tailored to your role
  • An environment with flexible working options
  • A culture encouraging inclusion and diversity
  • A Civil Service pension with an employer contribution of 28.97%

Things you need to know

Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Selection process details

This vacancy is using Success Profiles and will assess your technical skills and experience.

Stage 1: Application & Sift

You will be required to complete an application form. You will be assessed on the listed 8 essential criteria, and this will be in the form of:

  • an application form (‘Employer/ Activity history’ section on the application)
  • a 750 word supporting statement.

This should outline how you consider your skills, experience and knowledge provide evidence of your suitability for the role, with reference to the essential criteria.

You will receive a joint score for your application form and statement. (The application form is the kind of information you would put into your C.V – please be advised you will not be able to upload your CV. Please complete the application form in as much detail as possible). Please do not email us your CV.

Healthjobs UK has a word limit of 1500, but your supporting statement must be no more than 750 words. We will not consider any words over 750 words.

Longlisting: In the event of a large number of applications we will longlist into 3 piles of:

  • Meets all essential criteria
  • Meets some essential criteria
  • Meets no essential criteria

Only those meeting all essential criteria will be taken through to shortlisting.

Shortlisting: In the event of a large number of applications we will shortlist on:

  • Carry out user research activities, creating research plans, recruiting participants, preparing discussion guides, creating information gathering artefacts, running and moderating user research sessions

Desirable criteria may be used in the event of a large number of applications / large amount of successful candidates.

If you are successful at this stage, you will progress to interview and assessment.

Feedback will not be provided at this stage.

Stage 2: Interview

You will be invited to a remote interview via MS Teams.

Technical skills and experience will be tested at interview.

You’ll be invited to a 60-minute remote video interview. This will include a presentation on your understanding of user-centred design and user research, to help us understand more about you and your skills and experience.

For this role we’ll assess your experience and specialist technical skills against the government technical skills for a user researcher.

User researcher - Government Digital and Data Profession Capability Framework

Candidates should expect questions on the following technical skills during the interview:

  • Analysis and synthesis
  • Research management, leadership and assurance
  • User research methods

title: Engineer II - Materials Engineering
description:
As an Engineer II - Materials Engineering here at Honeywell Aerospace, you will support production and engineering teams across electronics assemblies, sealants, coatings, adhesives, chemical processing, and engineering substantiation/source approval.


You will collaborate with cross‑functional teams to provide intermediate‑level materials and process expertise to Production, Design, and Quality. You will develop test plans, perform hands‑on evaluations of nonmetallic materials, and support receiving inspection, process development, failure analysis, and engineering investigations.

You will report directly to our Senior Engineering Manager, and you’ll work out of our Minneapolis, MN location on a hybrid work schedule.

• Perform and interpret thermal analysis laboratory techniques (DMA, TGA, DSC, TMA, TG‑IR).
• Lead failure analyses using SEM/EDS, FTIR, CT X‑ray, microscopy, XRF, and mechanical testing.
• Characterize adhesives (epoxies, polyurethanes, silicones, acrylics).
• Select materials and develop processes for potting, bonding, staking, underfilling, and conformal coating in electronic assemblies.
• Draft and maintain material/process specifications and inspection procedures.
• Identify alternates/replacements to mitigate materials obsolescence.
• Validate materials and perform lab testing for production and receiving inspection.
• Lead technicians and engineers to resolve process challenges.
• Collaborate with suppliers to diagnose issues and provide robust guidance.

YOU MUST HAVE
• Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in a technical discipline such as science, technology, engineering, mathematics
• 3 or more years of experience across Materials & Process, Design & Applications, and laboratory testing supporting engineering and production.

WE VALUE
• Experience with adhesives, conformal coatings, sealants, paints, wires, chemical processing, and printed board assemblies.
• Process development for potting, bonding, staking, and underfilling in electronic assemblies.
• Knowledge of coatings and their process applications.
• Experience leading laboratory activities and failure analyses.
• Experience identifying alternate materials to address obsolescence.
• Strong cross‑functional communication and collaboration.
• Self‑motivated; drives on‑time execution and positively influences others.
• Excels in fast‑paced environments with shifting priorities and multiple concurrent projects.

Due to compliance with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidate must be a U.S. person, which is defined as, a U.S. citizen, a U.S. permanent resident, or have protected status in the U.S. under asylum or refugee status.

SPONSORSHIP
We are currently not sponsoring applicants for work visas for this job. Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis.

BENEFITS
Beyond a performance-driven salary, you'll work alongside dedicated experts on technology that's advancing aviation. As a Honeywell Aerospace employee, you're eligible for a comprehensive benefits package that includes:

Employer-subsidized medical, dental, vision and life insurance
Short-term and long-term disability coverage
401(k) match, flexible spending accounts and health savings accounts
Employee assistance program and educational assistance
Parental leave and 12 paid holidays
Paid time off for vacation, personal and sick time
Explore your benefits: https://honeywellaerospacebenefits.com/

The annual base salary range for this position is $84,800 -$105,900. Please note that this salary information serves as a general guideline. Honeywell Aerospace considers various factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate’s work experience, education and training, key skills, as well as market and business considerations.

ABOUT HONEYWELL AEROSPACE

Join a company that's reintroducing itself to the aviation community we've helped advance for more than a century. At Honeywell Aerospace (NASDAQ: HONA), we're launching as an independent, publicly traded aerospace and defense company built on a legacy of operational excellence and mission-focused execution.

Our new brand identity pairs that heritage with real momentum, as we build technology that helps pilots navigate with confidence, aircraft operate more efficiently, and operators stay ahead of change. With our systems on board 90% of the world's aircraft, your work here has reach that's rare to find anywhere else.

Focusing on our customers, investing in innovation, and building a culture of accountability and performance is how we're shaping what comes next.

Every horizon. Every mission. Every day.

At FCDO Services we protect the UK’s interests at home and overseas. We design and construct secure government buildings and courier diplomatic packages worldwide, safeguard government tech and a whole lot more. Our work is as varied and vital as it gets, but we never lose sight of our people. Their skills, aspirations and growth mean as much as the global mission we’re on. In our world, it all matters.
