title: Activities Instructor
description:
Title: Activities Instructor (Boxing)

CHARACTERISTICS OF THE CLASS: Under general supervision, plans, promotes, organizes, conducts and provides instruction in a specialized athletic, recreation or leisure activity including, but not limited to tennis, aerobics, yoga, boxing, sailing and skating. Conducts classes, controls specialized equipment and recruits volunteers. Performs other related duties as assigned.

EXAMPLES OF DUTIES:

  • Plans and implements a course curriculum for the instruction of a specialized athletic, recreation or leisure activity.
  • Provides instruction and supervision for Chicago Park District patrons involved in a specialized athletic, recreation or leisure activity.
  • Demonstrates proper techniques and skills in specialty area. Adapts programs to reflect differing levels of participant skill development.
  • Provides instruction in advanced competitive strategies of specialty area.
  • Provides information on the rules and regulations governing competition in specialty area.
  • Promotes sportsmanship and encourages creativity in participants.
  • Communicates constructively with participants, parents, volunteers and the community.
  • Enforces and promotes safety guidelines for specialized activity.
  • Resolve conflicts among participants.
  • Issues and maintains an inventory of specialized equipment and supplies.
  • Sets up special apparatus and equipment.
  • Supervises unorganized plan and enforces Chicago Park District rules and regulations.
  • Determines tournament eligibility requirements and verifies dates and other standards.
  • Establishes schedules for tournaments, leagues and competitions.
  • Conducts meetings on competitions and other special events.
  • May officiate at competitions in assigned specialty area.
  • Performs general administrative duties such as assisting in course registration, collecting fees, answering routine inquiries in person or by phone and routine record keeping.
  • Conducts and attends workshops and in-service training seminars.
  • May work with a special population, including but not limited to senior citizens and populations with physical, sensory and other disabilities.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:
Training and Experience: Associate of Arts degree or completion of two (2) full years of course work at an accredited college or university which included a minimum of twenty (20) credit hours in one (1) or more of the following areas: Recreation, Leisure Studies, Physical Education or related discipline and one (1) year of closely related instructional, practical or sanctioned competitive (i.e. IHSA, NCAA or AAU) experience in the specialty area; or a high school diploma or GED and 5 years of closely related instructional, practical or sanctioned competitive experience (examples include: IHSA, NCAA or AAU) in the specialty area or an equivalent combination of education and experience is required.
Knowledge, Skills and Abilities: Knowledge of athletic, leisure and recreation theories and principles; technical knowledge and skill in an area of specialization; skill in teaching the full range of skills and techniques in an area of specialization; effective oral and written communication skills; ability to evaluate skill levels in the specialty area.

BENEFITS: As a part-time Chicago Park District employee in a position covered by the District’s Agreement with SEIU Local 73, eligible employees receive a comprehensive benefits package including:

  • +$1.00/hour increase on 1/1/2027.
  • 1 day of personal leave at the commencement of each quarter, accrued on a pro rata basis.
  • 2 days of sick leave at the commencement of each quarter, accrued on a pro rata basis.
  • After one year of employment, employees who work 1,040 hours or more in the previous year are typically eligible for between 7-10 workdays of paid vacation time annually, and additional time after first 5 years of employment.
  • 12 weeks of paid parental leave (upon meeting FMLA eligibility requirements).
  • Pension plan through the Park Employees' and Retirement Board Employees' Annuity and Benefit Fund, a system covered by the State of Illinois' Reciprocal Act.
  • Free Admission to most Chicago Museums.

RATE OF PAY: $26.63 per hour

BUDGETED HOURS: Budgeted up to 25 hours per week

description:

  • Contract type: Permanent

Location

Bristol, Lichfield, Andover

About the job

Job summary

Do you want to work on one of the most exciting transformation projects in the public sector?

The Defence Housing Service (DHS) is being created through the Armed Forces Bill to deliver a step-change in housing for the UK’s Armed Forces and their families following the publication of the Defence Housing Strategy on 3 November 2025, which marked the most significant change to Armed Forces housing in over 50 years. DHS will bring a dedicated focus to improving the homes, communities and lived experience of Service personnel, placing families firmly at the heart of everything it does.

This is one of the most ambitious housing transformation programmes in the UK today. Backed by a £9.2 billion investment, DHS will modernise tens of thousands of homes, introduce a more proactive and customer-focused approach to maintenance, and unlock new opportunities to develop housing on Defence land. DHS will have the focus and agility to deliver change at pace, combining public service values with greater flexibility to build the skills, systems and partnerships needed for the future.

This is a rare opportunity to be part of shaping its culture, influencing how it works, and helping deliver lasting improvements for Service families across the UK.

The Defence Housing team is currently part of the Defence Infrastructure Organisation (DIO), who respond to the evolving needs of our military personnel, and the ways in which they live, work, train and deploy. We are proud to be the expert partner Defence needs for all their infrastructure requirements. From large scale infrastructure projects such as runways for the F35 fighter jets to net carbon-zero accommodation for our Service families, our activities focus relentlessly on our customers, and our outputs are unique in the UK and across the globe! DIO , What we deliver every day.

The future delivery model for this team is currently under review and may change as part of potential organisational developments. This could include the team or function transferring to a different employer or organisational structure in the future. Should activities transfer out of the Ministry of Defence existing employees transferring with those activities will maintain the same or substantially the same terms and conditions of employment.

Job description

Reporting to the DHS HR Director, this role will help shape the People Strategy to drive and underpin people transformation across DHS. You will be responsible for leading the delivery and performance of the HR Services team, ensuring services align with organisational priorities and support the achievement of DHS strategic objectives. You will act as a key HR contact for the Ministry of Defence (MOD), Defence Business Services (DBS) and Civil Service Commission, building influential relationships and maintaining an awareness of the wider government people agenda.

You will lead a multi-functional team spanning Talent Acquisition, Employee Relations, Diversity & Inclusion, Wellbeing, HR Policy, and People Data and Reporting. You will provide the strategic frameworks, tools and processes required to ensure HR services are delivered effectively, efficiently and in line with business needs.

Working closely with senior stakeholders across DHS, you will support the development and delivery of people strategies that enable organisational transformation and cultural change. The role will play a key part in shaping strategic workforce planning, building housing capability, enhancing colleague engagement, and delivering an effective employee lifecycle experience.

What you’ll be doing;

  • Lead and develop the HR Services team, ensuring the effective delivery of talent acquisition, employee relations, wellbeing, diversity and inclusion, HR policy, and people data services.
  • Provide strategic leadership for HR service delivery, ensuring the function is appropriately resourced, skilled, and equipped to meet organisational priorities and service standards.
  • Work closely with HR Business Partners and senior stakeholders to deliver strategic workforce planning, ensuring DHS has the capability, capacity, and structures required to meet current and future business needs.
  • Lead the development and implementation of HR policies, frameworks, and processes, ensuring compliance with employment legislation, Civil Service requirements, and organisational objectives.
  • Provide expert advice and oversight on complex employee relations matters, working collaboratively with DBS, Trade Unions, HR colleagues, and external partners where required.
  • Lead the Diversity & Inclusion and wellbeing agendas, driving initiatives that support an inclusive, engaged, and high-performing workforce.
  • Use people data, workforce insight, and performance metrics to inform decision-making, identify trends, and drive continuous improvement across HR services.
  • Build and maintain effective relationships with key stakeholders, including the Ministry of Defence (MOD), Defence Business Services (DBS), Civil Service Commission, and Trade Unions.
  • Ensure effective governance of HR services, including oversight of contracted services, compliance obligations, and value-for-money considerations.
  • Manage departmental resources and budgets to ensure the efficient and effective delivery of HR services.

Whilst this role is advertised as a full-time position of 37 hours per week, we recognise the benefits of flexible working and are open to discussing part-time hours, job share arrangements, or other flexible working patterns with suitable candidates. Regular in person attendance is required (this is expected to be approximately 60% of your working week) to promote the benefits of face-to-face collaboration alongside flexibility of hours to support work-life balance and business need. Initially, you may be expected to attend more frequently to familiarise yourselves with the site, the team, and your role.

Person specification

To be successful with your application, you'll need to show that you meet the following essential criteria:

  • Proven experience of leading multi-functional HR teams, setting strategic direction and delivering organisational people strategies, driving continuous improvement and high-quality service delivery.
  • Significant experience across a broad range of HR disciplines, including workforce planning, resourcing, employee relations, organisational development, and the development and implementation of HR policies and strategies.
  • Strong understanding of Diversity, Equity and Inclusion principles, with experience of developing and implementing initiatives to build a diverse and inclusive workforce.
  • Strong commercial and business acumen, with the ability to align people strategies to organisational objectives and balance growth, performance and cost management priorities.
  • Experience of using workforce data, insights and evidence-based analysis to support strategic decision-making and inform HR policy and people strategy.
  • Comprehensive knowledge of employment legislation, HR best practice and employee relations, with experience leading on complex and high-risk cases and managing relationships with external legal advisers.

If so, this is an exciting opportunity to join the Food Standards Agency (FSA) as our Senior Intelligence Analyst, and we’d love to hear from you!

Your work will provide decision-makers with clear, credible intelligence that supports both operational activity and longer-term priorities. You will lead and develop a small analytical team in a role offering significant professional scope, varied partnerships and exposure to complex intelligence challenges.

The FSA is a non-ministerial department of over 1600 people. We play a critical role in protecting public health and consumers’ wider interests in food across England, Wales and Northern Ireland. Our vision is an important one - to drive change, delivering “food you can trust” and working towards a healthier and more sustainable food system.

Job description

You will agree the purpose, scope and timescales of analytical commissions, distribute work fairly and monitor progress while keeping customers informed. Alongside overseeing team delivery, you will undertake complex assignments and produce robust strategic and tactical assessments that translate information into useful conclusions and recommendations.

You will review analytical products for accuracy, relevance and compliance with professional standards, including outputs prepared for investigations or potential court proceedings. You will engage with law enforcement bodies, government organisations, local authorities and other partners to strengthen understanding of priority threats. You will also support individual and team performance, encourage professional development and assess colleagues against relevant professionalisation standards.

About the job

Job summary

Can you lead transformational people change and improve organisational effectiveness through a systems-thinking approach?

Have you successfully partnered with employees, representatives and trade unions to build engagement and resolve complex people issues?

Are you experienced in shaping reward, employee experience and people policies that drive performance, retention and fairness?

If so, we’d love to hear from you!

This role sits within the People and Places Directorate and plays a key role in shaping DVSA’s culture, employee engagement and overall colleague experience. Working closely with senior leaders, HR Business Partners, trade union representatives and wider Civil Service colleagues, the team uses workforce insight and employee feedback to drive organisational effectiveness, support strategic change and improve business performance.

The team leads on employee engagement, culture and capability, employee relations, reward and benefits, and the employee value proposition, ensuring colleagues feel valued, supported and able to perform at their best. Through a systems-thinking approach, the team develops people strategies, policies and services that enable effective decision-making, strengthen organisational performance and help attract, retain and develop talented people across DVSA.

Joining our department comes with many benefits, including:

  • Employer pension contribution of 28.97% of your salary. Read more about Civil Service Pensions here
  • 25 days annual leave, increasing by 1 day each year of service (up to a maximum of 30 days annual leave), plus 8 bank holidays a privilege day for the King’s birthday
  • Flexible working options where we encourage a great work-life balance.

Read more in the Benefits section below!

DVSA roles: Working for the Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency , Civil Service Careers

Job description

In this role, you will translate insight into clear priorities, lead a team of subject matter experts and work across organisational boundaries to deliver practical, evidence-led improvements. Your work will help senior leaders and managers respond confidently to people issues, strengthen consultation and engagement routes, and make decisions that are fair, consistent and aligned to DVSA’s priorities.

Your responsibilities will include, but aren’t limited to:

  1. Lead a specialist portfolio that connects organisational effectiveness, employee relations, engagement, reward and colleague voice to improve colleague and manager experience.
  2. Use workforce evidence, colleague feedback, employee relations intelligence, organisational diagnosis and systems thinking to identify patterns, risks and opportunities for improvement.
  3. Develop approaches that strengthen engagement, colleague voice and visible action from feedback.
  4. Support constructive employee and industrial relations, including effective engagement with trade unions, representatives and wider Civil Service HR colleagues.
  5. Develop clear guidance, tools and improvement activity that help managers identify and address people issues early, fairly and consistently.
  6. Lead work on reward, benefits and the employee value proposition so the employee offer supports attraction, retention, fairness and organisational performance.
  7. Work with senior leaders, HR Business Partners, trade union representatives and People & Places colleagues to translate insight into clear priorities, advice and evidence-led action.
  8. Lead and develop a team of subject matter experts, setting clear direction, prioritising work and supporting high-quality delivery.

Great line management is important to us as an organisation, and we will equip and support line managers to develop the skills set out in the Civil Service Line Management Standards.

For further information on the role, please read the role profile. About the job

Job summary

This advert is for year-long statistics university student placements, to commence in summer 2027. There are multiple posts available.

Please note that this scheme is only open to undergraduate students currently in their second year of study, looking to undertake a year-long placement commencing Summer 2027 before returning to complete their degree OR to postgraduate students who have a year-long placement built into their postgraduate degree scheme which they are looking to undertake Summer 2027-Summer 2028. Graduates should not apply.

Job description

The role of Welsh Government statisticians is to support decision-making, resource allocation, research and debate within government and the wider community by providing reliable and efficient statistical services. A wide range of topics are covered by Welsh Government statisticians including education, health, housing, poverty, social justice, industry, the economy, local government, transport, the environment, agriculture, demography and the Welsh language. Most of our statisticians work together in a central hub of analysts known as Knowledge and Analytical Services; however, there are also a small number of statistical teams “outbedded” within Welsh Government policy departments.

The general purpose of the role of our statistics placement students is to provide support for Welsh Government’s Knowledge and Analytical Services in respect of statistical needs and projects.

We encourage you to browse our website to understand the work that we do and the types of statistical publications successful applicants may be involved in producing.

Person specification

The key tasks will be defined by the specific projects that the successful candidate is required to carry out. Examples will include the following:

  • Preparation of statistical reports, drawing out key messages, identifying trends and writing insightful commentary that tells the story with data.
  • Development of data visualisations and statistical tables to help illustrate messages in data.
  • Answering requests for data and analysis from a variety of internal and external sources.
  • Data management and manipulation, including efficient storage of data and automation of statistical processes.
  • Data validation and quality assurance of statistical outputs

Behaviours

We'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:

  • Communicating and Influencing
  • Working Together
  • Delivering at Pace

Technical skills

We'll assess you against these technical skills during the selection process:

  • A good working knowledge of at least one statistical package or programming language e.g. R, Python, SQL.
  • A university student studying for a degree in a numerate discipline (such as statistics, mathematics, economics, psychology or geography) whose degree contains a statistical element.
  • Ability to develop and apply knowledge in the analysis and quality assurance of data and the production of statistical outputs.

  • An environment with flexible working options
  • A culture encouraging inclusion and diversity
  • A Civil Service pension with an employer contribution of 28.97%

  • Communicating and Influencing – Communicate clearly and concisely both orally and in writing (assessed via application form and presentation at interview).
  • Technical 1 – A good working knowledge of at least one statistical package or programming language (e.g. SQL, R, Python) (assessed via application form and interview question).
  • Technical 2 – A university student studying for a degree in a numerate discipline (such as statistics, data science, mathematics, economics, psychology or geography) whose degree contains a statistical element. You must either be an undergraduate student, currently in your second year of study, looking to undertake a year-long placement commencing Summer 2026 OR a postgraduate student with a year-long placement built into your postgraduate degree scheme which you are looking to undertake Summer 2026 – Summer 2027 (assessed via application form and statistics and numeracy ability test).

As a guide, we recommend that you aim to write 250 words for each. Using the “STAR technique” may help you to structure your evidence. For “Technical 2”, you should state the name of your degree scheme and describe the statistical elements you have studied.

To reduce bias within the application process, we will be sifting candidate evidence without identifiers, so please do not include any information that could identify you within your evidence. This includes your name and the name of the institution where you are studying.

  • All candidates who have submitted an application by the deadline will be invited to undertake a multiple choice test at 14:00 on 11/11/2026. The test is designed to test your numeracy and statistical knowledge. You will be sent an email with the test. It is a timed test and must be completed and returned via email by 15:00 on 11/11/2026. Only those who pass the test will progress to the application form sift. It is not expected that you will need to revise for the test. If you do not receive a copy of the test at the time specified, please email statscareers1@gov.wales immediately.
  • Those candidates who pass both the multiple choice test and application sift will be invited to an online interview. The online interview will take place over Microsoft Teams. The interview will be using various assessment techniques aligned to the Civil Service Success Profiles framework. This gives us the best possible chance of finding the right person for the job. Situational style questions (what would you do if… ?) and past experience style questions (can you give me an example of time when…?) will be used to assess the specified civil service behaviours. In addition, you will also be asked technical questions relevant to the role.
  • Five working days before the interview, you will be sent some data to analyse. You will be required to draw out key messages from the data and deliver these in the form of an oral presentation at the beginning of your interview. This presentation will be used to assess the behaviour Communicating and Influencing – Communicate clearly and concisely. The presentation should last no more than 5 minutes and you will remain seated during the presentation.

A reserve list may be held for this opportunity. Any candidate who is successful in being offered a reserve status, will remain on the reserve list for 12 months.



Feedback will only be provided if you attend an interview or assessment.

Security

title: Open Rank-Rheumatology
description:
The Department of Internal Medicine, Division of Rheumatology, at the University of South Florida Morsani College of Medicine is seeking a fellowship-trained, board-certified/board-eligible rheumatologist at the rank of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor (Open Rank) with specialized clinical expertise in Myositis (idiopathic inflammatory myopathies). This recruitment will establish and grow a dedicated Myositis program, expand patient access to specialized care across the Tampa Bay region, strengthen multidisciplinary clinical services, and advance the Division's clinical, educational, and research missions.
The successful candidate will provide comprehensive care for patients with dermatomyositis, polymyositis, inclusion body myositis, immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy, antisynthetase syndrome, overlap myositis, and myositis-associated interstitial lung disease (ILD), as well as general rheumatologic conditions. This is a full-time, 12-month salaried faculty appointment with attending staff privileges at Tampa General Hospital (TGH) and affiliated hospitals. Practice locations may include the Morsani Center for Advanced Healthcare, USF South Tampa Center, TGH Health Park, and Tampa General Hospital.

  • Clinical-A typical schedule may include:
    • Outpatient Rheumatology clinics with a dedicated Myositis focus
    • Participation in multidisciplinary clinics and care conferences (e.g., ILD/Rheumatology with Pulmonary, Derm/Rheum, Neurology/Neuromuscular)
    • Inpatient rheumatology consult coverage as assigned
    • Coordination of advanced and immunomodulatory therapies (e.g., IVIG, biologics, emerging cellular therapies)
    Scheduling may be tailored based on faculty interests and divisional needs.
  • Teaching-Participate in the teaching of medical students, internal medicine residents, and rheumatology fellows in clinic, inpatient consult, and conference settings. Contribute to divisional didactics, case conferences, and Grand Rounds, including education on the diagnosis and management of inflammatory myopathies. Supervise and mentor trainees in accordance with ACGME and Morsani College of Medicine requirements.
  • Research-Participate in clinical research and scholarly activity commensurate with rank, with an emphasis on Myositis and related autoimmune diseases. Opportunities include developing a Myositis patient registry and biorepository, participating in industry-sponsored and investigator-initiated clinical trials, collaborating on multidisciplinary research with Pulmonary (ILD), Neurology, and Dermatology, and disseminating findings through peer-reviewed publications and national presentations.
  • Administrative-Serve as clinical lead for the development and growth of the Myositis program, including care pathways, referral relationships, and community and physician outreach. Protected time for administration, research, and/or education is consistent with holding specific leadership roles and fulfilling said responsibilities. Should you no longer hold those leadership roles (for any reason), the protected time may be removed and will be made up by an increase in cFTE assignments related to clinical patient care. Complete clinical obligations such as chart completion and patient follow-up.
  • Call responsibilities are shared among division faculty and generally include inpatient rheumatology consultation coverage on a collegial and equitable call schedule. Participate in divisional, departmental, and hospital committees as assigned. Specifics of call frequency and responsibilities will be discussed with candidates during the recruitment process.
  • Responsible to a Chair or other appropriate higher-level administrator of a State university.
  • Responsible for teaching, research, service, and related administrative activities.
  • Responsible for academic advising and related activities.
  • May represent the university, college/school, or department.

Minimum:

Medical degree from an accredited institution or the highest degree appropriate in the field of specialization with a demonstrated record of achievement in teaching, academic research, and service. Must meet university criteria for appointment to the rank of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor. For Associate/Full Professor - Normally will have produced creative work, professional writing or research in refereed and other professional journals, and be a recognized authority in the field of specialization.

Preferred:

Must hold or be eligible for a full, unrestricted Florida Medical License or foreign equivalent required. To perform this position, the candidate will need to obtain and maintain a full un-restricted FL Medical License, maintain credentials in the USF Health faculty practice plan, and be a medical staff member in good standing at the hospitals he/she is assigned to perform clinical duties. The candidate will participate in the teaching of residents, fellows, and medical students in clinical medicine.

Must be board certified/eligible in Internal Medicine/Rheumatology

The University of South Florida is a top-ranked research university serving approximately 50,000 students from across the globe at campuses in Tampa, St. Petersburg and USF Health. In 2025, U.S. News & World Report recognized USF with its highest overall ranking in university history, as a top 50 public university for the seventh consecutive year and as one of the top 15 best values among all public universities in the nation. U.S. News also ranks the USF Health Morsani College of Medicine in the highest tier, placing it as one of the top 16 medical schools in the nation and inside the top 10 among public universities. USF is a member of the Association of American Universities (AAU), a group that includes only the top 3% of universities in the U.S. With an all-time high of $750 million in research funding in 2025 and as a top 20 public university for producing U.S. patents, USF uses innovation to transform lives and shape a better future. The university generates an annual economic impact of nearly $10 billion for the state of Florida. USF’s Division I athletics teams compete in the American Conference. Learn more at .

title: Product Manager, Associate, Stellarus
description:
Your Role

The Product Management team drives the strategy and delivery of digital solutions that empower members to make informed healthcare decisions. Your work will shape how millions of members access and understand their healthcare benefits. The Product Manager, Associate will report to the Sr. Director, Product Management.

In this role, you will help advance Stellarus’ mission by delivering solutions that meet the needs of our health plan customers. You will ensure digital experience components such as Benefit Coverage, Cost Transparency, Provider navigation and Claims are clear, transparent, and easy to use for members. This position focuses on helping to build scalable, member-centric solutions that reinforce Stellarus’ value to payer customers and drive innovation in healthcare. You will support initiatives to integrate AI and machine learning into digital products, creating intuitive, predictive and personalized member experiences for all Stellarus customers

Our leadership model is about developing great leaders at all levels and creating opportunities for our people to grow – personally, professionally, and financially. We are looking for team members that are energized by creative and critical thinking, building and sustaining high-performing teams, getting results the right way, and fostering continuous learning.

Your Work

In this role, you will:

  • Support execution of the product lifecycle for a defined product area or squad, assisting in requirements development, backlog management, and delivery coordination under guidance
  • Contribute to user discovery and validation activities by gathering inputs on personas, workflows, and user needs to support product decision-making
  • Assist in translating customer, business, and regulatory needs into user stories and acceptance criteria, ensuring clarity and completeness
  • Collaborate with cross-functional partners (engineering, design, data) to support delivery activities and ensure alignment on priorities and timelines
  • Track product performance metrics and supports data analysis efforts to inform product improvements and reporting
  • Support product launches and adoption efforts through coordination, documentation, and feedback collection
  • Apply foundational understanding of product tools, processes, and agile practices to contribute to team effectiveness
  • Build knowledge of compliance, risk, and security requirements, supporting adherence across product activities

Your Knowledge and Experience

  • Requires a bachelor’s degree or High School Diploma/GED and 4 years of additional relevant experience in lieu of a degree
  • Requires experience delivering digital products in cross-functional environments, partnering with engineering, design, and business stakeholders
  • Requires experience using data and metrics to evaluate product performance and inform decision-making
  • Requires familiarity with modern product and technology environments, including tools, workflows, and basic system understanding

title: Farm Assistant - Fall/Spring Semester
description:
***APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS***

Professional resume

Cover letter describing why you are applying, the skills you bring to the position, your career area(s) of interest, and what you hope to professionally achieve from the internship. Submit when asked for additional documents.*

To apply, you MUST submit a resume and a cover letter to this application as an attachment. *Students who do not submit a resume and cover letter will not be considered for this position.

The Farm at Butler is a one-acre diversified farm located on Butler’s campus that produces a large variety of food crops for the Butler community and serves as an example of sustainable urban agriculture to the community at large. The Farm also provides an opportunity for place-based learning for various classes and groups centered around food systems, agro-ecology and sustainability. Student assistants will perform a variety of farm and garden related tasks as needed to further the farm’s daily operations and contribute to these goals. Students will have the opportunity to practice and enhance their attention to detail, initiative-taking, observation skills, systems-thinking, resilience, and responsibility to a team as they pursue their tasks.

Work Schedule

​​8-10 hours/week, tbd based on class schedule​, plus availability to work an hour or so every 2-3 weekends.

Position Responsibilities

  • ​​​Harvest, wash, record, and package produce as appropriate for its end-use. ​
  • Manage weeds and soil, by hand and through the use of appropriate farm tools. ​
  • Amend beds—for example, load, transport and unload wheelbarrows full of compost. ​
  • Clean and organize—wash farm containers and tools as needed and store neatly. Wash, clean and/or organize farm spaces as needed. ​
  • Mow grassy walkable areas of the farm. ​
  • Manage pests through cultural practices such as physical exclusion or through hand-picking as needed ​
  • Plant—transplanting or direct-seeding.
  • ​Prepare beds—may include removal of old crop material, measuring and re-forming permanent beds, weed management and amendment as mentioned above. ​
  • Complete other tasks as identified by the farm manager​​

Required Qualifications

  • Availability to work 8-10 hours/week, plus availability to work an hour or so every 2-3 weekends.
  • Commitment to the job schedule
  • Willingness to work hard physically to meet the demands and deadlines of the job in potentially all types of weather, and be prepared with appropriate clothing and footwear
  • Capacity for detail-oriented tasks and creative problem solving..

Preferred Qualifications

  • ​​Individuals who have an appreciation for food production in the context of enhancing the ecological quality of the space.
  • Individuals who would like to feel a shared ownership of and responsibility to the farm.
  • Individuals who will notice and be concerned with a broader view than the specific task they’ve been assigned.
  • Individuals who value providing sustainably grown food to Butler dining grown right here on campus..

Other Expectations

  • Maintain regular and punctual attendance.
  • Comply with University standards and policies.
  • Ensure confidentiality of information.

title: Policy Lab Project Producer - 2 roles
description:
• Job grade: Higher Executive Officer
  • Contract type: Permanent
  • Business area: DfE - Strategy & Operations Group
  • Type of role: Digital, Policy, Project Delivery, Social Research
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time, Job share, Part-time
  • Number of jobs available: 2

Location

Bristol (BS2 0EL), London (SW1P 3BT), Manchester (M1 2WD)

About the job

Job summary

IMPORTANT - This vacancy is using the Civil Service Numerical and Verbal tests. The deadline for completing the tests is the same as the vacancy closing date. Please ensure you complete the tests with sufficient time to complete the written application.

Policy Lab improves the lives of people in the UK by designing policies that respond directly to their needs. We work across government using innovative, participatory approaches that make policies more efficient and effective. Since 2014, we have involved many thousands of people in policymaking. Our mission is to radically improve policymaking through design, innovation and people-centred approaches.

We are looking for two exceptional Higher Executive Officer (HEO) candidates with strong design, research and technological skills. These roles are integral to delivering Policy Lab’s portfolio of policy innovation projects.

Both roles require a similar core set of experience and strengths, particularly in project delivery, design expertise, creative practice, and working and communicating effectively with varied stakeholders. The successful candidates may be appointed to either role depending on campaign outcomes, business need and candidate preference.

The successful candidate for the Project Producer, Design role will provide design and visualisation skills across Policy Lab’s portfolio of work. This role is central to ensuring and communicating high-quality design research and design outputs in our policy projects, resulting in better designed policy outcomes for teams across government and better outcomes for citizens and communities.

The successful candidate for the Project Producer, Creative Technology role will help develop and integrate emerging technology into Policy Lab’s practice. The postholder will use their creativity and knowledge of digital technology, artificial intelligence and varied forms of data to enhance Policy Lab’s existing suite of software applications, and to develop new ones, through our portfolio of policy innovation projects.

Policy Lab has over a decade of experience working openly and collaboratively to address some of the UK’s most complex policy challenges. Our team brings together expertise in policy, lived experience research, design, systems thinking, futures, and technology. We work on a cost-recovery basis with a wide range of commissioners.

Job description

We are recruiting 2 roles which will provide high-quality design and technology support in a fast-paced, multidisciplinary environment.

Role 1: Project producer, design

Project Delivery

  • Work as part of a multidisciplinary, design and research-led project team, providing essential support across project operations and delivery and cross-government engagement.
  • Work confidently in a fast-paced, agile environment, managing competing priorities and adapting to changing requirements.
  • Support research, design and delivery activity, including logistics for user research, workshops, sprints and events (online and in person), ensuring smooth research and design delivery.
  • Work closely with policy, technology and research colleagues, as well as external partners and commissioners, to ensure projects are well run, inclusive and effective.
  • Support engagement and business development activity, including coordinating meetings with commissioners, contributing to proposals, and maintaining clear, professional communications.

Design and creative practice

  • Support and deliver day-to-day design processes within Policy Lab projects, ranging from visual design tasks, creating communication materials, workshop design and delivery, and report design
  • Run creative research activities using a range of material and virtual facilitation techniques to capture people’s lived experience and new ideas.
  • Manage diary, travel and meeting arrangements where required, ensuring clear information flows.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement by contributing to reviews and refinements of design processes.
  • Support communications activity of project work to demonstrate how Policy Lab’s work results in better policy outcomes for people in the UK.

Role 2: Project Producer, Creative Technology

Project Delivery

  • Work as part of a multidisciplinary, design and research-led project team, providing essential support across project operations and delivery and cross-government engagement.
  • Work confidently in a fast-paced, agile environment, managing competing priorities and adapting to changing requirements.
  • Support research, design and delivery activity, including logistics for user research, workshops, sprints and events (online and in person), ensuring smooth research and design delivery.
  • Work closely with policy, technology and research colleagues, as well as external partners and commissioners, to ensure projects are well run, inclusive and effective.
  • Support engagement and business development activity, including coordinating meetings with commissioners, contributing to proposals, and maintaining clear, professional communications.

Creative technology

  • Work flexibly across multiple coding languages, programming environments and cloud services to iterate existing Policy Lab software prototypes
  • Develop innovative new software applications using emerging technologies including AI and vibecoding within Policy Lab projects, to meet commissioner needs
  • Support the building of capability around the use and creation of creative technology prototypes within Policy Lab and across wider government
  • Help run and analyse user research, prototype testing and show-and-tell sessions to inform the iteration of Policy Lab’s emerging technology practice.
  • Support communications activity of project work to demonstrate how Policy Lab’s work results in better policy outcomes for people in the UK.

Working Pattern

We welcome applications from candidates seeking part time or compressed working pattern. However, due to the nature of the work and the shift coverage required, the minimum number of contracted hours for this role is 30 hours per week over a 4 day period.

Person specification

Candidates must be able to demonstrate the following essential criteria:

  • High-quality project delivery: You have experience supporting ambitious projects or programmes that achieve impactful outcomes, maintaining a strong attention to detail.
  • Cutting-edge design or creative technology skills: You have experience applying excellent design and/or creative technology skills across multiple projects in a fast-paced, agile environment, resulting in high-quality products and outcomes. Including communicating project outcomes to different groups.
  • Working in multidisciplinary teams: you have experience managing competing priorities and different ways of working; maintaining effective working relationships across a wide range of stakeholders.
  • Innovative approaches to policymaking: Experience and or proven interest in applying design and/or creative technology skills to policy design challenges, through methods such as people-centred research, co-design, speculative design or other participatory methods.

Experience may come from a range of sectors and does not need to be from a policy role, provided relevant transferable skills are demonstrated.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree such as design, technology or visual subject (e.g. illustration) or equivalent.

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £37,260, Department for Education contributes £10,794 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

Applicants currently holding a permanent post in the Civil Service should note that, if successful, their salary on appointment would be determined by the Department’s transfer / promotion policies.

As a member of the DfE, you will be entitled to join the highly competitive Civil Service Pension Scheme, which many experts agree is one of the most generous in the UK.

You will have 25 days leave, increasing by 1 day every year to a maximum of 30 days after five years’ service. In addition, all staff receive the King’s Birthday privilege holiday and 8 days’ bank and public holidays.

We offer flexible working arrangements, such as job sharing, term-time working, flexi-time and compressed hours.

Most DfE employees will be working a hybrid pattern, spending at least 60% of their time in an office or work setting. Changes to these working arrangements are available in exceptional circumstances but must be agreed with the line manager and in line with the requirements of the role.

Travel to your primary office location will not be paid for by DfE, but costs for travel to an office which is not your main location will be covered.

As an organisation, which exists to support education and lifelong learning, we offer our staff excellent professional development opportunities.

Things you need to know

Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Selection process details

This vacancy is using Success Profiles (opens in a new window), and will assess your Strengths and Experience.

To apply for this role, please select 'Apply Now' at the top or bottom of this advert. CV details need to be included in the template within the application form; attached or emailed CVs will not be considered.

Stage 1: Civil Service Numerical Test (CSNT)

When you have completed your personal information, you will be asked to complete the CSNT. You must achieve the minimum pass mark to progress to the next stage.

Stage 2: Civil Service Verbal Test (CSVT)

When you have completed the CSNT, you will be asked to complete the CSVT. You must achieve the minimum pass mark to progress to the next stage.

It is important you allow enough time to complete the test online (within 24-48 hours is recommended), and obtain the results before you can complete your full application online prior to the test closing date and time.

Do not leave completing the tests until the last minute in case you experience any access or technical issues. There may not be technical support available after business hours.

While the tests should work on most operating systems and modern browsers with a good internet connection, we cannot guarantee that every combination will work. At the beginning, the test will check which browser you are using, and alert you if it is likely to be incompatible.

It is highly recommended that you complete the online tests on a desktop computer, not a mobile phone or tablet.

If candidates require reasonable adjustments during the application process, or online test process, please allow sufficient time (at least 5 working days prior to the closing date) to allow us to review and progress your application to the next stage of the process.

Please note that there is no candidate support available from Friday 5pm until Monday 9am.

If you are unsuccessful in passing the online tests you will be unable to continue any further in the application process. If you successfully pass the tests, you will then progress to stage 3 of completing the full application.

Stage 3: Written Application

At sift stage, you will be assessed on your Experience in line with the essential criteria listed in the person specification section of the job advert.

To apply for this role, please provide:

  1. A Short CV setting out your career history, highlighting specific responsibilities and achievements that are relevant for this role.
  2. Your Statement of Suitability – In no more than 500 words, provide examples of how your personal skills, qualities and experience meet the essential criteria.
  3. You will also need to upload a two page spread portfolio of your work - ensuring that no detail shows your name or personal identity.

To confirm, the maximum word count for the statement of suitability is 500 words. Please adhere to this limit as anything over 500 words will not be taken into account.

The sift will be restricted to just assessing personal statements and your portfolio in the event of a large volume of applications.

We reserve the right to increase the minimum pass mark for the CSNT and CSVT where there is a high volume of applications or a particularly strong field of candidates. Where this occurs, candidates who do not meet the revised pass mark will not progress further, and their written application will not be assessed.

Please note, CV details must be contained within the template on the application form. Any CV or Statement of Suitability that has been emailed to our team will not be considered.

Once you have submitted your application it cannot be amended; only submit your application when you have completely finished, answered all the relevant questions and reviewed the information entered.

Application sifting will take place 05 November 2026 onwards. Please note these dates are subject to change.

If you are successful at application sift stage, your application will be progressed onto Stage 4 part of the Selection process.

Stage 4: Presentation/Interview

The interview will be a 2-part process:

Part 1: Candidates invited to interview need to prepare a 5-minute presentation referencing their portfolio which will cover the following essential criteria:

Cutting-edge design or creative technology skills: You have experience applying excellent design and/or creative technology skills across multiple projects in a fast-paced, agile environment, resulting in high-quality products and outcomes. Including communicating project outcomes to different groups.

Candidates will be asked the following follow up question:

"Referring to your portfolio can you tell us how your skills and experience would contribute to Policy Lab's mission to radically improve policymaking through design, innovation and people-centred approaches"

Part 2: At interview you will be asked questions to assess your experience in line with the three remaining essential criteria (listed below). Candidates will also be asked some strength based questions.

  • High-quality project delivery: You have experience supporting ambitious projects or programmes that achieve impactful outcomes, maintaining a strong attention to detail.
  • Working in multidisciplinary teams: you have experience managing competing priorities and different ways of working; maintaining effective working relationships across a wide range of stakeholders.
  • Innovative approaches to policymaking: Experience and or proven interest in applying design and/or creative technology skills to policy design challenges, through methods such as people-centred research, co-design, speculative design or other participatory methods.

Experience is the knowledge or mastery of an activity or subject by involvement in or exposure to it. When looking at your experience we are looking for/;

  • Previous examples of what you have achieved.
  • Your knowledge in a particular field which is relevant to the job role.
  • How you performed in a particular field – not how long you served

Sometimes experience from outside work can be transferable from a non-work context. Skills gained through voluntary work or a hobby can show the experience you may need for a role. For example, teamwork or communication.

Strengths are a way for Hiring Managers to understand what motivates you and what you enjoy doing, which helps the panel to understand your areas of strength. Evidence shows that people do better work when a job aligns well with what they enjoy and find motivating. We don’t advertise which strengths we are going to assess you on as we want to be able to assess your first, natural response to the questions.

Interviews will take place towards the end of November 2026. Please note these dates are subject to change. If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact us.

Interviews will be held over video conferencing using MS Teams. If you are invited to interview, please ensure that you have access to this software and that you have your video turned on. If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact us.

We receive many applications, and unfortunately we’re not able to provide feedback for candidates who aren’t shortlisted. Feedback will only be provided if you attend an interview or assessment.

All communications will be electronic therefore it is vitally important that you check your Civil Service Jobs account regularly, as well as your spam/junk email folder.

Important Information

If you fail to complete the tests before the deadline, your application will be withdrawn. Guidance will be available when you are invited to take the test. The tests are untimed, administered via Civil Service Jobs, and applicant guidance is available during the test and online on GOV.UK Online Tests guidance.

Applicants must complete the test on their own, without help, and Departments reserve the right to retest applicants under supervised conditions at later stages of the selection process. Doing this can provide reassurance to recruiters who are concerned about the authenticity of one or more test results.

Please ensure you allow yourself sufficient time to complete both assessments and submit your application before the advertised deadline.

Reasonable adjustments & test accessibility:

See our reasonable adjustments guide for candidates (online tests), or some example case studies, to act as a guide. You can use these to help you decide whether to ask for help or take the test without help.

More information about online tests can be found here: Preparing for the Civil Service Verbal and Numerical tests - GOV.UK. You will also find practice tests on this page if you would find them helpful prior to completing the live test.

Other Information

Interviews may be via Microsoft teams or face to face; the vacancy manager will confirm prior to the Interview.

In your application, please don’t include personal information that identifies you.

This means we can recruit based on your knowledge and skills, and not background, gender or ethnicity - it's called name blind recruitment (opens in a new window).

Please ensure that you remove from your application, all references to your:

  • name/title
  • educational institutions
  • age
  • gender
  • email address
  • postal address
  • phone number
  • nationality/immigration status

We reserve the right to raise the minimum pass mark in the event of a high volume or strong field of candidates.

Please be aware that this role can only be worked in the UK from the location options provided and not from overseas.

The government is committed to supporting apprenticeships, enabling people to learn and progress in a role whilst earning. We want to monitor the number of people who have completed apprenticeships who are now applying to progress further in their career and are asking this question to all candidates, on all vacancies. You will be asked a question as part of the application process about any previous apprenticeships you have completed. Your response to this question will not affect your application and it is not a requirement of the role to have completed a previous apprenticeship.

If successful and transferring from another Government Department a criminal record check may be carried out.

In order to process applications without delay, we will be sending a Criminal Record Check to Disclosure and Barring Service on your behalf. However, we recognise in exceptional circumstance some candidates will want to send their completed forms direct. title: Systems Engineer (Senior) Job #560
description:
Systems Engineer (Senior)

Clearance Required: TS/SCI

Springfield, VA

Minimum Years’ Experience: 12 years

Overall Assignment Description:

National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency is modernizing their GEOINT Reporting and Workflow Orchestration to a service architecture requiring support in guiding the architecture and development activities moving forward. This position is in support of our Analysis Integrated Program Office (IPA) customer, where our team provides engineering services to assist the team in defining the to-be architecture, decomposing capabilities into solution/program epics, documenting and prioritizing the development baseline, integrating new customers and sources as required, and working with the development vendor to achieve the planned baseline. While we primarily support the IPA leadership team, we also provide services to the various projects dealing with intelligence and geospatial analysis capabilities provided to the intelligence community. Areas that our team is involved with include: Structured Observation Management Services, Analytic Modernization Services, Exploitation Services, Orchestration Services, Advanced Geospatial Services, as well as requirements, architecture, and integration with a number of sensor-related programs.

Primary Duties include:

  • Guides the planning, analysis/traceability of user requirements, architectures traceability, procedures, and problems to automate or improve existing systems and review cloud service capabilities, workflow, and scheduling limitations.
  • Assists the Government in the capture and translation of mission and customer requirements/needs into systems/capability requirements and solutions.
  • Coordinates between Government Program Manager customer and DevOps teams utilizing Agile methodologies, Scrum and Agile Planning Tools.
  • Supports the analyses and allocation of requirements to systems architecture components and executing programs.
  • Assists the Government in performing systems integration activities, strategic technical planning, project management, performance engineering, risk management and interface design.

Secondary Duties include:

  • Operates at the level of integrating multiple systems, services, processes, and interfaces within a Major Systems Acquisitions across organizational and agency boundaries.
  • Guides Mid-level and Junior-level system engineers performing requirements engineering, solutions engineering, scheduling, reliability, resiliency, services development, integration, test and evaluation, maintainability and analysis across the National System of Geospatial-intelligence (NSG), Allied System of Geospatial-intelligence (ASG) and Federal Agencies.
  • Conducts Analysis of Alternatives (AoAs), Course of Actions (CoAs), Trade Studies, and Engineering Assessments.

Required:

  • Bachelor’s degree or higher in Systems Engineering or in related technical or scientific fields such as engineering, physics, mathematics, operations research, engineering management, Computer Science, Information Technology, Management Information Systems, or related STEM degree program.
  • 12 years of experience as a Systems Engineer may be considered in lieu of a degree.
  • TS/SCI clearance adjudication or ability to obtain SCI and pass a poly
  • 12 years of experience in government or industry in relevant work areas including: DoD/IC Acquisition Process, Requirements Process, PPBES Process or system engineering of large complex System of Systems or Service Oriented Architecture/Cloud environments.
  • Experience with and strong understanding of systems engineering lifecycle.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of the current NSG/ASG and NRO enterprises.
  • Experience with Agile development processes and tools (e.g., Jira, Confluence)

Desired:

  • Experience engineering solutions using Cloud Based Technology such as: Service Orientated Architecture (SOA), On-demand self-service, Broad network access, Resource pooling, Rapid elasticity, Measured Service, Software as a Service (SaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS), and Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS).
  • Experience engineering solutions using structured and unstructured Big Data.
  • Experience engineering solutions using Automation, Augmentation and Artificial Intelligence technologies.
  • Experience in Geospatial-Intelligence Analysis systems, tools and processes. eg. NGA analyst workflow and reporting methods.
  • Experience coordinating, and strong communication skills, between customers, developers, users and/or other teams.
  • Familiarity with development and integration of metadata catalogs and collections orchestration.
  • Familiarity with GEOINT reporting systems as a developer or user is a plus.
  • Master’s degree in Systems Engineering or in related technical or scientific fields such as engineering, physics, mathematics, operations research, engineering management, Computer Science, Information Technology, Management Information Systems, or related STEM degree program.
  • Working knowledge of Model Based Systems Engineering, processes, tools and languages.
  • Working knowledge of Software Development Frameworks.
  • INCOSE Certified System Engineering Professional (CSEP) certification.
  • Documented work experience in the field of geospatial intelligence.
  • Licensure as a professional engineer.
  • Demonstrated expertise in photogrammetry, remote sensing, image science, information sciences, geographic information systems, geomatics, or related fields.

title: Advanced Mechanical CAD Engineer
description:
As an Advanced Mechanical CAD Engineer here at Honeywell Aerospace, you will be a key contributor and subject matter expert (SME), or a developing SME, in PTC Creo Parametric, Model-Based Definition (MBD), and engineering drafting. You will model complex aerospace hardware, including cast and machined parts, cable and harness assemblies, and printed board assemblies, and produce definition data that flows cleanly from CAD into PLM.

You will set the modeling and documentation standard for the mechanical team. That means applying ASME Y14.5, Y14.41, Y14.47, Y14.100 and related standards correctly, and helping peers do the same.

You will report directly to our Mechanical Engineering Design Manager and you’ll work out of our Clearwater, FL location, with a hybrid work option available after an initial 90-day period.

  • Create robust, design-intent-driven 3D models and assemblies in PTC Creo Parametric for complex aerospace hardware.
  • Model cast and machined parts, including draft, parting lines, machining allowances, and casting-to-machined family relationships.
  • Design and document cable and harness assemblies using Creo Cabling, including routing, connector definition, and formboard or nailboard drawings.
  • Develop printed board assembly (PBA) models through ECAD-MCAD collaboration, covering board outline, keep-outs, component placement, and mechanical interfaces.
  • Author Model-Based Definition data per ASME Y14.41 and Y14.47, including semantic PMI, annotation planes, combination states, and model organization.
  • Produce 2D engineering drawings where required, with correct GD&T per ASME Y14.5 and drawing practices per ASME Y14.100.
  • Manage CAD data in PLM (e.g., Teamcenter), including check-in and check-out, lifecycle states, BOM structure, part numbering, and change management (ECR/ECO).
  • Perform and support tolerance stack-up analysis to confirm fit, form, and function.
  • Review models and drawings from peers and suppliers for standards compliance, manufacturability, and design intent.
  • Develop and maintain CAD best practices and modeling guidelines; mentor engineers and designers.
  • Work with manufacturing, quality, suppliers, and electrical and systems engineering to resolve design and producibility issues.
  • Support the transition from drawing-based to model-based enterprise workflows.

YOU MUST HAVE

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in a technical discipline such as the sciences, technology, engineering or mathematics
  • Minimum 5 years of hands-on experience in Creo Parametric modeling, MBD, and drafting of complex hardware (cast and machined parts, cable assemblies, printed board assemblies), including CAD-to-PLM integration; aerospace, defense, or other regulated industry preferred.
  • Advanced proficiency in PTC Creo Parametric, including complex part modeling, top-down assembly design, skeletons, family tables, and parameters and relations.
  • Demonstrated experience modeling cast and machined parts and designing cable assemblies.
  • Working knowledge of printed board assembly design and ECAD-MCAD data exchange.
  • Hands-on experience authoring MBD data and 2D engineering drawings.
  • Strong working knowledge of GD&T and the ASME Y14 standards listed below.
  • Experience with CAD-to-PLM integration, including BOM management and engineering change processes.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain any required export-control or security eligibility.
  • Clear written and verbal communication; able to explain standards and modeling decisions to engineers at all levels.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance.

WE VALUE

  • Master's degree in a relevant engineering discipline.
  • ASME GDTP certification (Technologist or Senior level).
  • PTC Creo certification or equivalent demonstrated expertise.
  • Experience with Teamcenter, Windchill, or other PLM.
  • Experience with Creo Cabling and Creo ECAD-MCAD Collaboration (e.g., with Altium, Cadence, or Mentor).
  • Experience with Model-Based Enterprise (MBE) initiatives, including supplier acceptance of MBD data.
  • Familiarity with castings and machining processes.
  • Experience developing CAD standards, templates, or training material.
  • Experience with sensors, guidance, or navigation hardware.

U.S. PERSON REQUIREMENTS

  • Must be a US Citizen due to contractual requirements

BENEFITS

Beyond a performance-driven salary, you'll work alongside dedicated experts on technology that's advancing aviation. As a Honeywell Aerospace employee, you're eligible for a comprehensive benefits package that includes:

  • Employer-subsidized medical, dental, vision and life insurance
  • Short-term and long-term disability coverage
  • 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts and health savings accounts
  • Employee assistance program and educational assistance
  • Parental leave and 12 paid holidays
  • Paid time off for vacation, personal and sick time

Explore your benefits:

ABOUT HONEYWELL AEROSPACE

Join a company that's reintroducing itself to the aviation community we've helped advance for more than a century. At Honeywell Aerospace (NASDAQ: HONA), we're launching as an independent, publicly traded aerospace and defense company built on a legacy of operational excellence and mission-focused execution.

Our new brand identity pairs that heritage with real momentum, as we build technology that helps pilots navigate with confidence, aircraft operate more efficiently, and operators stay ahead of change. With our systems on board 90% of the world's aircraft, your work here has reach that's rare to find anywhere else.

Focusing on our customers, investing in innovation, and building a culture of accountability and performance is how we're shaping what comes next.

Every horizon. Every mission. Every day.

THE BUSINESS UNIT

Honeywell Aerospace products and services are found on aircraft across commercial aviation, defense and space — from engines and cockpit electronics to cabin systems, mechanical components and connectivity solutions. Our technology helps operators fly more safely, reduce fuel consumption, improve on-time performance and deliver a better experience for the people on board.

As aviation continues to evolve, we're also developing systems to support autonomous and supersonic platforms, bringing the same focus on safety and efficiency to the next era of flight. With approximately 36,000 employees worldwide and net sales of $17.4B in 2025, Honeywell Aerospace is one of the largest dedicated aerospace companies in the world. Explore our businesses:

Electronic Solutions develops the avionics, navigation systems, sensors and electromagnetic defense technology that help aircraft perform safely and with precision. Our systems are on board 90% of the world's aircraft — serving commercial aviation, defense and space operators from integrated flight deck platforms with 30-plus years in service to radiation-hardened systems trusted for human spaceflight.

The application period for the job is estimated to be 40 days from the job posting date; however, this may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates. Posting date, October 23, 2026.
