title: Hospital Clinical Educator
description:
Hospital Clinical Educator Career Opportunity


Acknowledged for your expertise in Hospital Education
Are you passionate about shaping the educational landscape in a hospital setting? Join us as the Hospital Educator, where you'll play a pivotal role in planning, developing, and coordinating in-service education programs for all staff. Beyond the professional aspects, this position offers a chance to build a career close to home and close to your heart, serving as a point-person for local schools and fostering partnerships with students on clinical rotations. Collaborate with hospital leadership to assess educational needs, strategize effective plans, and contribute to policy development and equipment integration. You'll be a knowledge hub within the hospital, making a lasting impact on healthcare excellence and community education.

A Glimpse into Our World
At Encompass Health, you'll experience the difference the moment you become a part of our team. Working with us means aligning with a rapidly growing national inpatient rehabilitation leader. We take pride in the growth opportunities we offer and how our team unites for the greater good of our patients. Our achievements include being named one of the "World’s Most Admired Companies" and receiving the Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For® Award, among other accolades, which is nothing short of amazing.


Starting Perks and Benefits
At Encompass Health, we are committed to creating a supportive, inclusive, and caring environment where you can thrive. From day one, you will have access to:

  • Affordable medical, dental, and vision plans for both full-time and part-time employees and their families.
  • Generous paid time off that accrues over time.
  • Opportunities for tuition reimbursement and continuous education.
  • Company-matching 401(k) and employee stock purchase plans.
  • Flexible spending and health savings accounts.
  • A vibrant community of individuals passionate about the work they do!

Become the Hospital Educator you always knew you could be

  • Coordinate staff completion of BLS and ACLS certifications.
  • Manage the equipment and skills stations needed for BLS and ACLS training.
  • Assist in coordination of clinical rotations and student orientation packet completion.
  • Train staff in new hire orientation and assist in general hospital orientation.
  • Assist with staff training.
  • Coordinate preceptor program.
  • Facilitate the implementation of new competencies and equipment.
  • Provide education on compliance with federal and state regulations.
  • Ensure training requirements and standards for Joint Commission and other regulatory agencies are met.

Qualifications

  • Active clinical license.
  • Minimum Qualifications:
    • Appropriate education to obtain and maintain required licensure.
  • Preferred: Previous experience as an Educator.
  • CPR certification.
  • If a Registered Nurse, CRRN certification preferred.
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills
  • Strong organizational and time management abilities
  • Critical thinking and problem-solving skills
  • Ability to work independently.
  • Flexibility to work varying shifts, including weekdays, weekends, evenings, or nights as needed.

title: Data Analyst
location: This role is being offered as hybrid working based at any of our Core HQs.
description:
• Job grade: Senior Executive Officer
  • Contract type: Permanent, Loan, Secondment
  • Length of employment: Permanent
  • Type of role: Analytical
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time, Job share, Part-time
  • Number of jobs available: 2

Location

This role is being offered as hybrid working based at any of our Core HQs.

We offer great flexible working opportunities at UKHSA and operate using a hybrid working model where business needs allow. This provides us with greater flexibility about how and where we work, to get the best from our workforce. As a hybrid worker, you will be expected to spend a minimum of 60% of your contractual working hours (approximately 3 days a week pro rata, averaged over a month) working at one of UKHSA's core HQs (Birmingham, Leeds, Liverpool, and London).

Our core HQ offices are modern and newly refurbished with excellent city centre transport links and benefit from co-location with other government departments such as the Department for Health and Social Care (DHSC).

About the job

Job summary

The CMA Assurance, Planning and Performance division delivers a group function to stakeholders across CMA Group and UKHSA. As a Data Analyst you work across the team to create and optimise solutions in data monitoring and reporting that stretch across the Chief Medical Advisor group. You will support regular outputs where necessary but primary focus will be developing the reporting capabilities.

The post holder may work with colleagues who are based across the country at different sites and/or who work remotely.

This role involves the collation, analysis, interpretation and presentation of information across the Chief Medical Advisor group. You will be required to have good working knowledge of the practical application of analytical methods and technical skills to present information in an efficient and insightful manner.

The role will be an ambassador for continuous improvement, and be able to work with stakeholders to design and recommend changes in process and the way of using data, to increase automation and impact. This includes appropriate use of AI tools, in line with policy and where they provide a discernible benefit.

Working for your organisation

We pride ourselves as being an employer of choice, where Everyone Matters promoting equality of opportunity to actively encourage applications from everyone, including groups currently underrepresented in our workforce.

UKHSA ethos is to be an inclusive organisation for all our staff and stakeholders. To create, nurture and sustain an inclusive culture, where differences drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our workforce and wider communities. We do this through celebrating and protecting differences by removing barriers and promoting equity and equality of opportunity for all.

Please visit our careers site for more information https://gov.uk/ukhsa/careers

Job description

  • Lead the planning, management and delivery of a range of projects requiring potentially complex analytic input, including influencing stakeholder decisions as to the most appropriate data output, initiating and planning workloads and upskilling users.
  • Lead the development of structured and low maintenance data flows.
  • Lead the development of dashboards for data visualisation, using tools such as Power BI.
  • Contribute to the continuous improvement in the team on the Delivery of the “business as usual” production of insights.
  • Lead, develop and promote quality assurance procedures. Check for data anomalies prior to and during analyses and perform corrective actions as required, including liaising with internal and external data providers.
  • Exercise judgement in interpreting statistics appropriately, especially where the data indicates a negative or contentious situation.
  • Communicate and present complex analytical/statistical information to non-analytical/statistical professionals at differing levels across the organisation.
  • Build stakeholder relationships at all levels and assist embedding best practice across the group on KPI performance reporting.
  • Ensure personal compliance and promote this within the team on corporate policies in relation to security, confidentiality and release of information.
  • An understanding of and commitment to equality of opportunity and good working relationships.

Person specification

Essential Criteria:

  • Experience of using data visualisation (e.g. Power BI) to share information with stakeholders
  • Analyse and use a range of relevant, credible information from internal and external sources to support decisions, communicating in the most appropriate style
  • Experience of building strong relationships with stakeholders at all levels and encouraging collaborative working both within and outside of own team
  • Able to deliver analysis in a way to meet the needs of a varied group of stakeholders
  • Experience of quality assuring complex data and analytical products, including quality assuring outputs and introducing and improving quality assurance procedures
  • Highly competent in the use of a variety of software applications including Word, Excel, Outlook and PowerPoint
  • Make it clear to all team members that bullying, harassment and discrimination are unacceptable.

Desireable Criteria:

  • Experience of coding (e.g. SQL, R, Python) or use of advanced excel methods such as powerapps
  • Experience of working with multiple sets of health-related data and information systems in health-related organisations
  • Knowledge of data security and confidentiality issues

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £41,983, UK Health Security Agency contributes £12,162 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).
  • Learning and development tailored to your role
  • An environment with flexible working options
  • A culture encouraging inclusion and diversity
  • A Civil Service pension with an employer contribution of 28.97%

Things you need to know

Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Selection process details

This vacancy is using Success Profiles and will assess your Behaviour, Strengths, and Technical skills.

Stage 1: Application & Sift

Success Profiles - GOV.UK

You will be required to complete an application form. You will be assessed on the listed 7 essential criteria, and this will be in the form of a:

  • Application form (‘Employer/ Activity history’ section on the application)
  • 1,000 word supporting statement.

This should outline how you consider your skills, experience and knowledge provide evidence of your suitability for the role, with reference to the essential criteria.

You will receive a joint score for your application form and statement. (The application form is the kind of information you would put into your C.V –please be advised you will not be able to upload your CV. Please complete the application form in as much detail as possible). Please do not email us your CV.

Healthjobs UK has a word limit of 1500, but your supporting statement must be no more than 1,000 words. We will not consider any words over 1,000 words.

Longlisting:
In the event of a large number of applications we will longlist into 3 piles of:

  1. Meets all essential criteria
  2. Meets some essential criteria
  3. Meets no essential criteria

If used, the pile(s) ‘Meets all essential criteria’ will proceed to shortlisting.

Shortlisting:

In the event of a large number of applications we may conduct an initial sift, on the lead criteria of:

  • Experience of using data visualisation (e.g. Power BI) to share information with stakeholders
  • Able to deliver analysis in a way to meet the needs of a varied group of stakeholders

Desirable criteria may be used in the event of a large number of applications/large amount of successful candidates.

If you are successful at this stage, you will progress to interview & assessment.

Feedback will not be provided at this stage.

Stage 2: Interview

You will be invited to a single remote interview .

Behaviours, Strengths and Technical skills will be tested at interview.

The Behaviours tested during the interview stage will be:

  • Changing and Improving (Lead behaviour)
  • Delivering at Pace

Interview dates are yet to be confirmed.

Once this job has closed, the job advert will no longer be available. You may want to save a copy for your records.

Location

This role is being offered as hybrid working based at any of our Core HQs.

We offer great flexible working opportunities at UKHSA and operate using a hybrid working model where business needs allow. This provides us with greater flexibility about how and where we work, to get the best from our workforce. As a hybrid worker, you will be expected to spend a minimum of 60% of your contractual working hours (approximately 3 days a week pro rata, averaged over a month) working at one of UKHSA's core HQs (Birmingham, Leeds, Liverpool, and London).

Our core HQ offices are modern and newly refurbished with excellent city centre transport links and benefit from co-location with other government departments such as the Department for Health and Social Care (DHSC).

Security Clearance Level Requirement

Successful candidates must pass a basic disclosure and barring security check before they can be appointed.

Successful candidates must meet the security requirements before they can be appointed. The level of security needed is Basic Personnel Security Standard.

Eligibility Criteria – External

This vacancy is open to all external applicants (anyone) from outside the Civil Service as well as internal applicants.

Salary Information

If you are successful at interview, and are moving from another government department, NHS, or Local Authority, the relevant starting salary principles for level transfers or promotions will apply. Otherwise, roles are offered at the pay scale minimum for the grade, but in exceptional circumstances there may be flexibility if you are able to demonstrate you are already in receipt of an existing, higher salary. Pay increases are through the relevant annual pay award for the role and terms.

Please be aware that the salary is based on the office location.

Senior Executive Officer (SEO)

  • £41,983- £48,128 (National)
  • £44,148- £50,121 (Outer London)
  • £46,310- £52,113 (Inner London)

If this role is fixed term and you are not currently a Civil Servant, you will take up the post on a Fixed Term appointment; you may be able to take this role up as a Secondment. If you are an existing Civil Servant, based outside of UKHSA, you will take up the post as a loan which you will need your department to agree. Loans are normally agreed for a period of two years. However, this may be extended where required, subject to agreement between UKHSA and your home department. You cannot take the post up as a fixed term. If you are an existing UKHSA member of staff, you will take up the post as either a level transfer or a temporary promotion as per the UKHSA’s Pay policy. If this role is permanent, it may also be available as a loan (for existing Civil Servants only) or secondment arrangement, subject to business need and agreement from the hiring manager and, where applicable, the employee's home organisation.

Reserve List

If more than the required number of suitable candidates pass the interview criteria, you may be kept on a reserve list for 12 months subject to your agreement. You may be contacted, in merit-order, if similar roles with closely matching essential criteria become available and the department choose to appoint from a reserve list.

The panel will assess if candidates meet the requirement of the role first, using a specific benchmark system. If you are interviewed for the post and do not meet the required threshold for the specified grade, your application may be assessed against a similar, lower grade role and you may be offered the post should one be available.

Incident Response Activity

From time to time, the role holder may be required to support UKHSA’s incident response activity by contributing their appropriate expertise within an Incident Cell; during such periods, supported by the line manager, this work will take priority over normal day‑to‑day responsibilities, commensurate with their grade, skills and experience.

Qualifications and Registrations

For roles where specific qualifications or registrations are required, successful applicants will be asked to provide appropriate evidence. Employment cannot commence until satisfactory documentation has been received and verified.

Future location

UKHSA is investing in a new state-of-the-art National Biosecurity Centre in Harlow, Essex, which will eventually bring together teams currently based at Canary Wharf, Colindale and Porton Down. For more details, please see: Huge biosecurity centre investment to boost pandemic protection - GOV.UK.

About the job

Job summary

What you’ll do

As Recreation Ranger - Facilities you will support the Recreation Manager in the day to day running of a busy Forest Centre. The Recreation Ranger will plan, deliver, and supervise work programmes for contractors and staff to ensure compliance, safety and high standards of visitor experience across the busy site.

Your main responsibilities include making sure we have seamless day-to-day visitor operations, our visitors are having excellent experiences and maintaining a welcoming and safe environment for our customers.

You will supervise the Craftsperson team to ensure all maintenance and forest management work is undertaken alongside answering visitor enquiries and supporting your direct colleagues on site. A large part of the role is working in partnership with Dorset Council.

You will contribute to the overall safety of the visitor experience, drive efficiencies and income generation opportunities.

Please see the job description below for more information and details about what we need from you.

Where you’ll work

Moors Valley Country Park and Forest is jointly owned and managed by Dorset Council and Forestry England, working closely with several onsite concessions. The Park has previously won Gold for Large Visitor Attraction in the Southwest Tourism Excellence Awards and is one of two popular visitor centres in the south district for Forestry England.

Moors Valley is one of the most visited attractions in the south with more than 1,000,000 visitors annually enjoying its lakeside walks and bike rides, innovative forest play structures, Tree Top Trail, steam railway, Go Ape, Segways, Nets Adventure and Golf Course. Prized as much by the local community as visiting tourists the park also offers stimulating play facilities, nationally recognised green exercise initiatives, locally sourced resta­­­urant food and an extensive year-round events programme.

Job description

Key Responsibilities & Accountabilities

In this role, you'll have the opportunity to maintain our recreational facilities focusing on health and safety and forest management. Here's a snapshot of your responsibilities:

• Be the face of Forestry England: you'll provide a visible presence for visitors. Maintain a safe and enjoyable Forest Centre: carry out regular inspections of car parks, cycle routes, recreational facilities, and litter management, to ensure a safe and enjoyable environment for all. Ensure defects are properly recorded and add findings to work plans. Build and maintain good relationships with on site partners and third party businesses.

• Ensure health and safety compliance: coordinate emergency procedures, complete accident and incident reports, undertake tree safety checks and adhere to health and safety guidelines. Work with the Recreation Manager to ensure risk assessments are being adhered to and that building management procedures and monitoring are in place. Ensure personal safety by using Peoplesafe (lone working) and by carrying out PPE and safety checks, in compliance with policy guidance. Input incidents into the reporting system, collating all relevant information.

• Working with others: work closely with volunteers, the wider Forest Centre team, partner organisations and Forestry England colleagues to ensure the smooth day to day running of the site.

• Delivering at pace: Working alongside the Recreation Manager and other Recreation Ranger, coordinate and monitor progress of tasks for the craftsperson team and contractors to ensure work is delivered in a timely and safe manner. Carry out maintenance to a variety of facilities including but not limited to play equipment, tracks, fencing, signage and general vegetation management.

And any other tasks, reasonably requested by your line manager in line with the business need.

Person specification

Essential Professional and Technical experience

• Experience working in a public facing role delivering high-quality customer service
• Experience of practical work in countryside / forest management
• Willingness and ability to work outdoors in all weathers and to carry out manual tasks
• Excellent team working skills and the ability to work with dispersed team members.
• Practical understanding of Health & Safety best practices and a commitment to a positive health and safety culture in an outdoor environment.
• Competent IT user with experience in MS Office suite of applications.

Desirable Professional and Technical experience

• Carpentry skills
• Prior experience managing work plans for a team
• Experience with brushcutter / strimmer and chainsaw operations
• Experience in working around tractors and / or machinery

Qualifications

Essential

Desirable

• Qualifications in Brushcutter / strimmer and chainsaw operations
• Qualifications in 4 x 4 driving and tractor driving in a forest environment.
• First Aid
• Health and safety qualification / Site Safety and Supervision qualification

About the job

The Government Digital Service (GDS) is the digital centre of government. We are responsible for setting, leading and delivering the vision for a modern digital government.

Our priorities are to drive a modern digital government, by:

  1. joining up public sector services
  2. harnessing the power of AI for the public good
  3. strengthening and extending our digital and data public infrastructure
  4. elevating leadership and investing in talent
  5. funding for outcomes and procuring for growth and innovation
  6. committing to transparency and driving accountability

We are home to the Incubator for Artificial Intelligence (I.AI), the world-leading GOV.UK and at the forefront of coordinating the UK’s geospatial strategy and activity. We lead the Government Digital and Data function and champion the work of digital teams across government.

We’re part of the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT) and employ more than 1,000 people all over the UK, with hubs in Manchester, London and Bristol.

The Government Digital Service is where talent translates into impact. From your first day, you’ll be working with some of the world’s most highly-skilled digital professionals, all contributing their knowledge to make change on a national scale.

Join us for rewarding work that makes a difference across the UK. You'll solve some of the nation’s highest-priority digital challenges, helping millions of people access services they need.

The Government Data Team is helping transform how government manages, shares and uses data. We are building the foundations that enable data to be treated as a strategic asset across the public sector, including common standards, secure access models, interoperable data infrastructure and the capabilities needed to support AI and data-driven services. Working across departments, local government and wider public sector partners, we are developing the shared approaches that make it easier to find, access and use data safely, ethically and at scale.

Job description

Former DSIT recruitment campaigns are continuing as usual, but candidates should be aware that following theGovernment’s announcement on the changes to some civil service departments, roles will be subject to the machinery of government moves and will ultimately be in one of the new departments. We will provide more information if you are selected for a role. This work remains of high importance to the civil service, and we thank you for your continued interest.

This is a rare opportunity to shape how data flows across government. As Head of Data Interoperability, you'll:

  • lead the development and adoption of the patterns and technical approaches that enable organisations to share and use data consistently
  • drive adoption of APIs, interoperable data exchange standards and federated data-sharing approaches across government
  • build consensus and influence senior stakeholders to adopt common approaches to data sharing and interoperability
  • work with architects, engineers and policy teams to deliver the foundations needed for modern public services and AI-enabled government
  • play a leading role in delivering the UK Public Data Infrastructure vision and enabling trusted data sharing at scale

Person specification

We’re interested in people who:

  • can turn data standards, API specifications and interoperability frameworks into practical approaches that delivery teams can adopt at scale
  • have established data integration standards, design patterns or API architectures that enable secure and interoperable data sharing across organisational boundaries
  • have successfully built consensus and driven the adoption of standards, mandates or common technical approaches across organisations and stakeholder groups
  • can provide strategic leadership on complex interoperability challenges, identifying and describing problems, navigating trade-offs and providing technical assurance on complex integration and data-sharing designs
  • can anticipate future developments in data interoperability, APIs and data-sharing technologies, and can advise on how to adopt new approaches to realise better value from data

title: DBS-Estates North Regional Manager and Health, Safety & Environmental Protection Lead
description:
• Job grade: Senior Executive Officer
  • Contract type: Permanent
  • Business area: MOD - National Armaments Directorate - DBS
  • Type of role: Estates, Health and Safety
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time, Job share, Part-time
  • Number of jobs available: 1

Location

Tomlinson House, Norcross, Blackpool, Lancashire

About the job

Job summary

Are you a dedicated person who is passionate about making a difference?

Would you like to work for the Ministry of Defence?

Defence Business Services (DBS) is one of the largest shared service organisations in Europe that provides a wide range of corporate services, to over 1.2 million end users, including serving and past military and families, as well as MoD civil servants and industry.

DBS delivers large scale administration and smaller specialist services to enable the wider MOD to focus on its core aims, maintaining the UK’s Defence and Security. Services include Human Resources, Pay, Veterans, Finance and Procurement.

The 2025 – 2030 Corporate Plan came up with a new mission and vision which are now:

Vision

To be the best shared service centre in Government

Mission

Proudly delivering excellence in shared services, through customer centric solutions to enable Defence outcomes

DBS is committed to creating a great place to work for all our colleagues. We are building an inclusive culture and respectful environment that reflects the diversity of the society.

We want to maximise the potential of everyone who chooses to work for us through opportunities to develop your skills and experience. We also offer a range of flexible working patterns and support to make a fulfilling career accessible to you and offer a Civil Service pension with an average employer contribution of 28.97%. Where your role permits, we support a blended working approach alternatively known as hybrid working.

DBS is part of The National Armaments Directorate (NAD) Group which is at the heart of delivering and sustaining the UK’s defence capability. Bringing together organisations responsible for developing, procuring, supporting and modernising Defence equipment, infrastructure and services, the Directorate works closely with industry, international partners and academia to ensure the Armed Forces have the capabilities they need to deter threats, protect the nation and succeed on operations. NAD drives innovation, operational readiness and value for money while supporting economic growth and strengthening the UK’s defence industrial base.

Between April & September 2027 the role you are applying for will move from Tomlinson House Norcross to the new MOD building at Station View, Talbot Gateway, Blackpool. For successful external/new candidates to DBS please note this post does not qualify for relocation allowances.

Come and join the DBS community today!

https://youtu.be/gUw0ToaRGgk

Job description

Exciting Leadership Opportunity – Estates, Infrastructure, Physical Security and Health, Safety & Environmental Protection

We are seeking a dynamic, proactive, and self-motivated individual with strong leadership and collaboration skills, who is passionate about driving continuous improvement and delivering exceptional service and customer experience.

Reporting directly to the DBS Estates Assistant Head, the successful candidate will take full accountability for the effective management and delivery of DBS Estates, Infrastructure, Physical Security, and Safety, Health & Environmental Protection (HS&EP) functions across the North region. This includes leading the corporate DBS HS&EP team and overseeing policy-driven management systems, assurance processes, and comprehensive reporting activities.

You will lead and inspire a dedicated team of seven personnel located across two key DBS sites: Norcross and the Glasgow workspace at Kentigern House. Your role will be pivotal in fostering a culture of excellence, innovation, and continuous improvement within Estates and HS&EP operations.

The ideal candidate will bring relevant knowledge and experience in one or more of these areas, coupled with the confidence and communication skills to engage effectively with stakeholders at all levels, both internally and externally.

While the primary duty station is DBS Norcross, Blackpool, this role requires flexibility to travel as needed. The expectation is to spend at least 60% of your working time at Norcross, with a higher presence during the initial induction and learning phase. Further details regarding working arrangements can be discussed during the interview.

Please note: DBS Estates team is currently within an organisational restructure as we transition into the new National Armaments Directorate (NAD). This presents an excellent opportunity for the team, working with the same professions across other enabling organisations, whilst maintaining essential services to DBS. Additionally, the Norcross site will be closing, with a planned move to Station View in Blackpool town centre scheduled for May 2027.

A key initial responsibility for this role during the first 12 months will be to work collaboratively with relevant stakeholders to ensure a smooth transition to Station View. This includes establishing all listed Estates services at the new location and managing the orderly closure of the Norcross site.

If you are a driven self-starter eager to lead, innovate, and make a tangible impact during this exciting period of change, we would love to hear from you.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Tactical and operational planning for DBS Estates in the North region, encompassing both business-as-usual activities and organisational change initiatives.
  • Lead and collaborate with Defence Infrastructure Organisation (DIO) and industry partners to deliver efficient, effective hard and soft facilities management services across the DBS estate.
  • Support operational requirements by scrutinising all Estates-related needs to ensure value for money and adherence to control totals; act as the focal point with delegated authority for Estates procurements via the Contracting, Purchasing and Finance (CP&F) system.
  • Own and maintain the Site Business Continuity Plan, actively participating as a key stakeholder in incidents and exercises.
  • Serve as the senior Estates lead and provide support to the DBS Head of Establishment at the Norcross site (Station View from May 27'), ensuring managed Estates and facilities management services underpin operational capability.
  • Line manage the DBS Estates Projects role, overseeing delivery of function-focused projects related to operational change, continuous improvement, and the transition to new facilities.
  • Lead the planning and execution of the transition from Norcross to Station View, including the establishment of all Estates services at the new location and the orderly closure of the Norcross site.
  • Drive continuous improvement of all DBS Estates processes, including flexible resourcing across sites to maintain service excellence and support operational needs.
  • Ensure compliance with all statutory, mandatory, and assurance reporting requirements related to Estates functions in the North region, including Health, Safety & Environmental Protection (HS&EP) and Physical Security.
  • Oversee Physical Security to ensure the estate and supporting contracts operate within Defence policy frameworks.
  • Collaborate closely with the DBS FCS Estates Regional Manager (South) and the Estates senior leadership team to promote coherence and best practice across national operations.

Corporate HS&EP Responsibilities:

About the job

Job summary

The Met Office is delighted to open our advertising for Industrial Placements 2027.

This is an exciting opportunity to join the Met Office on a 12-month Year in Industry placement, commencing at the start of July 2027, developing your skills and knowledge and ensuring you gain the most value possible from your experience with us.

You will have the opportunity to network with our cohort of Industrial Placements all over the Met Office and understand what career opportunities are on offer at the Met Office after you graduate.

We’re looking for Observations Research & Development Industrial Placement to help us make a difference to our planet.

As our Observations Research & Development Industrial Placement, the job may be suitable for hybrid working, which is where an employee works part of the week in the office and part of the week from home. This is a voluntary, non-contractual arrangement and the location advertised will be your contractual place of work. As an Industrial Placement, we would expect you to attend the office once a week as a minimum.

Our opportunity is full time, 37 hours per week. Our people are at the heart of what we do and we'll do our best to agree a working pattern that works for everyone.

World changing work

From science to technology, from meteorology to management, and from planning to communication, our expertise helps us stand out as the authority on weather accuracy and climate prediction. We help individuals, industries and government to make better decisions to stay safe and thrive. This is the Met Office. This is who we are.

  • We’re a force for good - focusing on our environmental and social impact
  • We’re experts by nature - always learning and developing to do things better
  • We live and breathe it - putting our purpose at the heart of decision-making
  • We’re better together - understanding partnerships and inclusivity make us greater
  • We keep evolving - pushing boundaries to make tomorrow better for our customers

Job description

Our Industrial Placement scheme offers ambitious and capable undergraduates the opportunity to gain valuable experience working alongside diverse and highly skilled experts in their field. You’ll be working on projects that really matter and will make a difference.

Observations of the atmosphere, oceans and land underpin everything we do at the Met Office. You’ll be working in the Observations Research & Development team to support the application of scientific research to enhance our Observations Capability. This will involve working on data to contribute to protecting our weather radar network from interference from wind turbines. You will be part of a wider team exploring engineering and data-processing solutions to this real-world challenge. There may also be opportunities to engage in work on other observations networks.

Your key duties

  • Work with observations scientists, radar specialists and network protection experts to evaluate case studies of real-world impacts to the radar network.
  • Apply geospatial, statistical and visualisation techniques to a variety of datasets to extract meaningful information and metrics.
  • Develop knowledge and skills associated with observations network analysis.
  • Produce regular technical verbal and written briefings for internal colleagues on the findings and recommendations.

Person specification

  1. Lead Criteria: You can select and apply appropriate geospatial and/or data science tools to analyse datasets, interpret the results and draw well-supported conclusions.
  2. You have effective analytical and problem-solving skills (Expert by Nature).
  3. You can write code in python or a similar coding language, with a desire to enhance your skills (Keep Evolving).
  4. You are interested in how real-world environmental data is collected and used, and you understand the importance of quality assurance (Force for Good).
  5. You work effectively as part of a wider team and can clearly communicate technical ideas and results to peers and team leaders (Better Together).

The panel may perform a preliminary sift of the lead criteria as indicated above.

Job summary

Job description

Overview of the job

The job holder will lead the management and assessment of selected low to medium risk prisoners and prepare, implement, review and evaluate their sentence plans with them. The job holder will build effective, appropriate and supportive relationships with prisoners, with the aim of reducing re- offending.
The job holder will act in a supportive role only to probation officers in the case management of high risk prisoners. The job holder will have undergone selection and additional training to carry out this specialist delivery job as a Prison Offender Manager to prisoners.
This is a non-operational job with no line management responsibilities. This role is rotational.
Will have regular prisoner facing activities/duties.

Summary

Typical tasks associated with this role include:
• Supervise, Manage, Signpost and advise prisoners decently, safely and securely while carrying out all activities.
• Understand, apply and conform to national and local policies.
• Establish, develop and maintain professional relationships with prisoners and staff.
• Maintain and update systems in line with local agreements.
• Prepare relevant documentation to managers for verification/quality checking purposes.
• Attend and contribute to relevant meetings as required.
• To assess and manage the risk posed by offenders to protect victims of crime and the general public by:
o Providing information and advice to other criminal justice agencies and partner organisations.
o Supervise offenders during custodial sentences.
o Contribute to the management of risk.
o Work with other agencies and groups to prevent reoffending and meet the needs of victims and offenders.

Responsibilities, Activities and Duties

The job holder will be required to carry out the following responsibilities, activities and duties:
• To undertake the full range of offender management tasks with low to medium risk cases.
• No ownership of high risk cases will be held, but support to probation officers in the case management of high risk prisoners will be given when required.
• As Prison Offender Manager, be involved in all relevant processes in the prison such as ACCT and violence reduction/anti-bullying for those within your case load, if this is applicable.
• Act as the ACCT Case Manager for individuals if appropriate (Prison Offender Managers should not routinely be used as ACCT Case Managers, only when appropriate to do so).
• Interview prisoners within prescribed timescales of their arrival. Set and review targets with prisoners and update case management notes on PNOMIS or relevant IT systems.
• Use the Offender Assessment System (OASys) to identify risks and manage offenders appropriately.
• Obtain further information if required from outside agencies to complete a comprehensive OASys report.
• Lead the sentence planning meeting in order to prepare and review appropriate plans.
• Coordinate the activities within the sentence plan through liaison with prisoners and other departments and agencies, including gathering and exchanging information and understanding/investigating conflicting opinions on prisoner progress.
• Encourage and support prisoner to participate in education, interventions and workshops as defined within the sentence plan. Develop strategies to assist prisoners to overcome reluctance to attend.
• To provide professional advice and assessment, including written reports to criminal justice agencies and partner organisations.
• Liaise with the Community Offender Managers regarding Release on Temporary Licence (ROTL) and Home Detention Curfew (HDC). Make recommendations to the Governor on suitability for early release. Inform relevant agencies of release dates and address of prisoners considered a risk on release.
• Support Community Offender Managers with the delivery of plans to enable recalled prisoners to be re-released.
• Complete all paperwork for the cases, including lifer and ISP specific paperwork in line with relevant policies, standards and set timescales.
• Highlight any prisoner who gives significant concerns by their behaviour to the Heads of Offender Management or Orderly Officer. Concerns may be for a variety of issues, for example, any prisoner who has presented in the past risk of suicide or self harm, or if there are any outstanding concerns with regards to victims or further offences and racial harassment.
• Contribute to and attend Multi-Agency Public Protection Arrangements (MAPPA) Boards and work with all relevant external agencies to protect the public when releasing prisoners under MAPPA.
• Liaise with the Foreign National Department or UK Border Agency regarding foreign national prisoners, as appropriate.
• Instigate public protection child contact checks and share relevant safeguarding information with authorities.
• Undertake the role of the resettlement advisor for prisoners in the specific caseload. Forge, develop and maintain the links between the programmes, the progress, or otherwise, made by the participants and the prisoner’s ongoing path through their sentence.
• To work collaboratively with colleagues and maintain effective team relationships, in particular with Key Workers.
• Demonstrate pro-social modelling skills by consistently reinforcing pro-social behaviour and attitudes and challenging anti-social behaviour and attitudes.
• To use computer based systems to produce, update and maintain records and other documentation within agreed timescales.
• To work within the aims and values of HMPPS.
The duties/responsibilities listed above describe the post as it is at present and is not intended to be exhaustive. The job holder is expected to accept reasonable alterations and additional tasks of a similar level that may be necessary. Significant adjustments may require re-examination under the Job Evaluation Scheme and shall be discussed in the first instance with the job holder.
An ability to fulfil all spoken aspects of the role with confidence through the medium of English or (where specified in Wales) Welsh.

• Ability to communicate clearly verbally and in writing with offenders, professionals, and at hearings such as Parole Boards.
• Ability to empathise constructively with people from diverse backgrounds.
• The ability to complete all mandatory training as required to support the job role.

Experience

• Experience of working with a diverse range of people who have experienced a range of social/personal difficulties, and of using tact and discretion when dealing with confidential and sensitive issues.
• Understanding of factors related to offending, e.g. substance misuse, accommodation issues.
• Understanding of and commitment to the principles of case management.
• Knowledge and understanding of risk management/risk assessment pertaining to offenders and the impact on victims of crime.
• Experience in planning and coordinating work.
• Experience of working with groups or individuals in order to motivate and change behaviour.
• Experience of working with diverse communities including promoting equality and valuing diversity.

The Met Office is delighted to open our advertising for Industrial Placements 2027.

This is an exciting opportunity to join the Met Office on a 12-month Year in Industry placement, commencing at the start of July 2027, developing your skills and knowledge and ensuring you gain the most value possible from your experience with us.

You will have the opportunity to network with our cohort of Industrial Placements all over the Met Office and understand what career opportunities are on offer at the Met Office after you graduate.

We’re looking for Ocean Forecast Verification Industrial Placement to help us make a difference to our planet.

As our Ocean Forecast Verification Industrial Placement, the job may be suitable for hybrid working, which is where an employee works part of the week in the office and part of the week from home. This is a voluntary, non-contractual arrangement and the location advertised will be your contractual place of work. As an Industrial Placement, we would expect you to attend the office once a week as a minimum.

Our opportunity is full time, 37 hours per week. Our people are at the heart of what we do and we'll do our best to agree a working pattern that works for everyone.

World changing work

From science to technology, from meteorology to management, and from planning to communication, our expertise helps us stand out as the authority on weather accuracy and climate prediction. We help individuals, industries and government to make better decisions to stay safe and thrive. This is the Met Office. This is who we are.

  • We’re a force for good - focusing on our environmental and social impact
  • We’re experts by nature - always learning and developing to do things better
  • We live and breathe it - putting our purpose at the heart of decision-making
  • We’re better together - understanding partnerships and inclusivity make us greater
  • We keep evolving - pushing boundaries to make tomorrow better for our customers

Job description

Your world of expertise

Our Industrial Placement scheme offers ambitious and capable undergraduates the opportunity to gain valuable experience working alongside diverse and highly skilled experts in their field. You’ll be working on projects that really matter and will make a difference.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is having a rapidly growing impact in many aspects of our lives. Weather and ocean forecasting is no different. Exciting advances are being made in the use of Agentic AI tools to assist and improve the ways we work. Working alongside members of our Ocean Forecast Verification team, you will develop a prototype Agentic AI capability for Operational Ocean Monitoring and Event Attribution. The overall aim is to create an intelligent monitoring assistant that can automatically monitor daily marine forecasts, detect anomalies and explain likely causes, and contextualise the forecasts against current and upcoming weather and oceanic events such as El Niño, tropical cyclones, and marine heatwaves.

Your key duties

  • Working alongside marine experts on quality assurance and anomaly detection for monitoring marine forecast models and observations
  • Developing an Agentic AI-driven monitoring workflow that replicates existing manual monitoring
  • Training AI Agent(s) to assess model outputs to detect missing or erroneous diagnostics and highlight marine climate anomalies
  • Training the Agent(s) to summarise system status in natural language for end users

Person specification

  1. Lead Criteria: A clear interest in AI and machine learning, with a strong motivation to build skills in this area (Keep Evolving).
  2. Studying for a degree in a mathematical or physical science, with an industrial placement year included.
  3. Experience with programming or scientific computing tools such as Fortran, Python, or MATLAB, showing a commitment to continuous learning and technological development.
  4. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  5. Ability to communicate technical information clearly and concisely, while working effectively and collaboratively with others as part of a team (Better Together).

The panel may perform a preliminary sift of the lead criteria as indicated above.

Alongside your salary of £27,170, Met Office contributes £7,871 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

Our work is life-changing, often life-saving and always life-enhancing. The Met Office is Great Place to Work UK certified. We are also featured on their ‘Best Workplaces in Tech’ 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026 lists, as well as their ’54 Best Workplaces for Women’ 2023 list.

About the job

Job summary

On the Science and Engineering Fast Stream (SEFS), you will use your science and engineering skills to support government policy development and decision-making. The scheme is not designed to place you in roles based solely on your scientific or engineering experience; instead, you will be placed in roles where your skills strengthen and inform policy.

Society faces many challenges that science and engineering can help solve. The Civil Service needs talented, adaptable science and engineering leaders to deliver complex work that makes a difference to people across the UK. The government’s focus on science and innovation to drive the UK’s growth, prosperity and security highlights the vital role of scientists and engineers in decision-making. Their expertise helps ensure policy is informed by the best available evidence and that scientific advice is communicated clearly.

You might be a science or engineering graduate, an experienced postgraduate researcher, a professional from industry, or an existing civil servant with a technical background. Join the Science and Engineering Fast Stream and you’ll become part of a modern, vibrant community of professionals with a shared goal: improving outcomes for the public.

The specific towns and cities depend on the department you are posted to and its office locations. The Fast Stream evolves continually, so postings can vary from year to year.

As an indication, in 2026 new fast streamers were posted to government offices in the following regions: Greater London, North West, South West, West Midlands, and Yorkshire and the Humber.

On occasion, some individuals may need to move location. We aim to align postings with your preferences whenever possible; however, final decisions must support our wider business needs. Please note that Fast Streamers cannot choose their department or their specific role.

Job description

Over three years, you will complete a range of stretching but rewarding postings across the Civil Service. These could include supporting the MOD Chief Scientific Adviser, working on earth observation policy in DEFRA, or advising on materials in the Department of Business, Innovation, Science and Trade These postings are designed to broaden your experience and build your leadership capability, including in areas outside your previous technical specialism. The scheme also offers a unique interchange placement, which may include opportunities in local government, charities or the private sector.

Across your postings, you will help build and apply evidence so government can respond to major challenges such as climate change or sustainable housing. You might analyse complex datasets, model public health risks, or develop evidence to inform clean energy decisions. You may also help shape legislation and regulation, or work with industry on compliance with statutory requirements (for example, food safety standards or transport emissions).

You will draw on your scientific background to develop and communicate robust evidence, working with experts across government, academia and industry.

You will be passionate about science and engineering and, throughout the programme, you will advocate for the use of evidence in the Civil Service and help promote the Government Science and Engineering Profession.

As a future leader, you will be expected to lead work from an early stage, including (but not exclusively) technical work. This might involve managing research projects, or working with policy teams to develop solutions for ministers and senior officials. By acting as an intelligent customer, you could oversee technical delivery for programmes such as a major transport project or research into artificial intelligence. You will work strategically with academics, industry experts and delivery partners inside and outside government.

You may also contribute to horizon scanning to identify emerging trends and technologies, such as autonomous vehicles or genomics, and apply systems thinking to help address complex cross-government challenges. Your combination of technical expertise and leadership potential, and your ability to work in both technical and non-technical environments, will make you deployable across the Civil Service at the end of the programme. When you finish after three years, you may choose to specialise in a policy area and take on technical leadership roles, or apply your skills in policy or operational delivery, bringing fresh perspectives to teams. Alternatively, you may focus on leadership and management roles, while remaining affiliated to the profession and continuing to champion science and engineering across government.

Whatever path you take, the Science and Engineering Fast Stream will develop you into a confident and inspiring future leader, supporting our ambition to put science and engineering at the heart of government decision-making.


We aim to put all successful candidates through Security Clearance (SC). However, if you are ineligible for SC, please do not be deterred from applying; we have plenty of exciting roles available that only require standard Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) pre-employment checks. You can find more information about vetting clearance levels here: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/united-kingdom-security-vetting-clearance-levels

Person specification

You must be eligible to work in the UK
You need to have or be on track to receive a 2:1 or higher undergraduate degree in any subject, including degree apprenticeships before you start the programme.
You must also hold a postgraduate degree in a science or engineering discipline, or be a chartered engineer or scientist registered with a professional institution licensed by the Engineering Council or the Science Council. For integrated master’s degrees, you need (or expect to have) a 2:1 or higher.
We expect you to have secured your postgraduate degree before you start the programme

Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Selection process details

Application Process

There are several phases in the Fast Stream application process. Some of these assessments are multimedia in that they present information in video, audio, graphical or visual formats, as well as text. We hope you find it an engaging process and one that gives you a real insight into the role of a fast streamer.

At the initial application stage you will be asked to complete some background information which will include some diversity questions - which are for monitoring purposes only and will have no bearing on selection outcomes - along with the opportunity to identify your preferences in terms of the different Fast Stream schemes. You can choose up to three.

When you apply please register with a personal email address, and not a work or university email address.

Assessment Phases

There are 2 online tests:

Work-based scenarios - This test measures interpersonal skills, utilising video based scenarios and you are required to assess the effectiveness of various responses.

Case Study assessment - In this test you are required to take work based scenarios on an imaginary role, learning and responding to a series of challenges and situations and adapting to the changes you are presented with.

Additional information - depending on the schemes you have chosen, there may be additional information to be completed, or an intermediate sift process. More information on the schemes that require additional information can be found https://www.civil-service-careers.gov.uk/fast-stream/fs-how-to-apply/fs-additional-information/

Fast Stream Assessment Centre - if you pass the above stages you'll be invited to attend a half day assessment centre. This will be conducted virtually online. The Fast Stream Assessment Centre (FSAC) reflects some of the key elements of a Fast Stream role and will consist of a written exercise, oral briefing exercise and a personal development conversation. Information will be presented via an app that you will be able to access remotely.

Final Selection Board - most schemes will then require a Final Selection Board . We'll ask you to attend this final assessment if you reach the required standard at FSAC. More information on the Final Selection Boards can be found https://www.civil-service-careers.gov.uk/fast-stream/fs-how-to-apply/fs-final-selection-board/

At Dstl, our vision is to have a modern way of working efficiently, accommodating and enabling our people to create, collaborate and deliver. To do this successfully in this job will require attendance at a Dstl location, Government Departments including wider MoD or Delivery and Mission Partner premises for at least 80% of your working time.

About the job

Job summary

Are you passionate about understanding how software and systems really work? Do you enjoy taking apart complex technologies, uncovering vulnerabilities and solving challenging technical problems that others cannot?

Why join us?

Dstl is seeking a Senior Cyber Vulnerability Researcher to join a specialist team delivering world-class vulnerability research, reverse engineering and technical analysis in support of national security and defence outcomes. In this role, you will apply advanced technical skills to analyse software, firmware and embedded systems, identifying vulnerabilities, assessing risks and providing expert advice that directly informs critical decision-making.

Working alongside experts from a range of scientific, engineering and cyber disciplines, you will investigate complex technologies, develop innovative research techniques and contribute to some of the most challenging technical problems in the cyber domain. You will combine deep technical expertise with strong analytical thinking to understand system behaviour, identify weaknesses and develop evidence-based assessments that stand up to rigorous scrutiny.

As a senior member of the team, you will also help shape future capability, providing technical leadership, mentoring colleagues and sharing knowledge to strengthen the organisation's cyber research expertise. This role offers a unique opportunity to work at the forefront of cyber vulnerability research while contributing to work of national importance.

Job description

What you'll do;

  • Conduct software reverse engineering, vulnerability research and technical assessments across software, hardware and embedded systems.
  • Apply static and dynamic analysis techniques to understand system functionality and identify vulnerabilities.
  • Investigate emerging technologies, products and capabilities to understand technical risks, opportunities and potential mitigations.
  • Provide authoritative technical advice and evidence-based assessments to customers and stakeholders.
  • Develop and enhance tools, techniques and methodologies to improve vulnerability research capability and efficiency.
  • Lead technical work packages and coordinate complex research activities, ensuring high-quality outputs are delivered to agreed standards and timescales.
  • Produce clear technical reports, briefings and documentation for both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Work collaboratively across multidisciplinary teams and partner organisations to solve complex technical challenges.
  • Mentor and support the development of less experienced engineers and researchers, helping to build organisational capability.

Person specification

What we're looking for

  • A degree in a STEM subject such as Electronic Engineering, Embedded Systems, Computer Science, Physics or Mathematics, or equivalent experience.
  • Experience using reverse engineering tools such as Ghidra or IDA.
  • Practical experience applying static and dynamic analysis techniques.
  • Knowledge of at least one assembly language such as ARM or x86.
  • Strong programming skills in C and/or C++.
  • A sound understanding of common software vulnerabilities and experience identifying them.
  • Experience solving complex technical problems and making robust technical assessments from incomplete or disparate information.
  • Experience leading or contributing to multidisciplinary teams delivering challenging technical outcomes.
  • Experience coaching, mentoring and supporting the development of others.
  • Excellent analytical, communication and problem-solving skills.

description:
As an Advanced systems Engineer here at Honeywell Aerospace, you will support key Performance and Operability engine programs, Model Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) initiatives, and Ensemble Digital Transformation efforts.


The Performance & Operability (P&O) and Methods group within the Systems Engineering organization is seeking an Advanced Engineer who will support key Performance and Operability engine programs, Model Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) initiatives, and Ensemble Digital Transformation efforts. As an Advanced Systems Engineer here at Honeywell Aerospace, you will play a critical role in the design, implementation, and management of complex systems and solutions within the System Engineering department. You will work within cross-functional global teams on cutting-edge projects that transform the way businesses operate.

You will report directly to our Systems Engineering Manager you will work out of our Phoenix, AZ on a Hybrid work schedule.

Hybrid Work Schedule Note: For the first 90 days, New Hires must be prepared to work 100% onsite M-F.

This position requires the individual to have knowledge of turbine engines, requirements-based engineering, test, validation, and MBSE (intro level). The individual will mentor and develop less-experienced engineers. The Engineer will be responsible for supporting Performance/Operability modeling and analysis, MBSE, and Ensemble efforts within P&O. You will have the opportunity to use your unique skills to accelerate innovation and engineering productivity, teaming with the world’s most talented engineers!

  • Provide Performance & Operability modeling, test coverage, and data reduction to support gat turbine engine development, cert/qual, and production
  • Provide MBSE support to P&O to drive INCOSE 2.0 and 3.0 deliverables
  • Provide Ensemble Digital Transformation support to better connect data and models to support customers
  • Perform test cell correlations
  • Prepare detailed test plans, including instrumentation, data acquisition and test schedules
  • ISC support, including test cell support, production margin tracking, diagnostics, PETS Online maintenance
  • Requirements analysis & requirements decomposition
  • Proposal support and customer interaction
  • Support customers with fielded engine systems
  • Mentor less-experienced engineers

Travel domestically and internationally: 10%

YOU MUST HAVE

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in a technical discipline such as the sciences, technology, engineering or mathematics
  • 4 years of experience working in the turbine engine field

WE VALUE

  • Understanding of turbine engines and how they operate
  • MBSE basic knowledge
  • Familiarity with Cameo, and IBM DOORS
  • Experience with Agile Methodologies and JIRA
  • Individuals that quickly analyze, incorporate and apply new information and concepts
  • Diverse and global teaming and collaboration
  • Self-motivated, able to work with little supervision and take the initiative to get things done
  • Ability to adapt dictated by project changes
  • Multi-tasking and can manage a variety of complicated tasks
  • Mentor less-experienced engineers
  • Proficient technical report writing and presentation skills.

Beyond a performance-driven salary, you'll work alongside dedicated experts on technology that's advancing aviation. As a Honeywell Aerospace employee, you're eligible for a comprehensive benefits package that includes:

· Employer-subsidized medical, dental, vision and life insurance

· Short-term and long-term disability coverage

· 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts and health savings accounts

· Employee assistance program and educational assistance

· Parental leave and 12 paid holidays

· Paid time off for vacation, personal and sick time

Explore your benefits: https://honeywellaerospacebenefits.com/

ABOUT HONEYWELL AEROSPACE

Join a company that's reintroducing itself to the aviation community we've helped advance for more than a century. At Honeywell Aerospace (NASDAQ: HONA), we're launching as an independent, publicly traded aerospace and defense company built on a legacy of operational excellence and mission-focused execution.

Our new brand identity pairs that heritage with real momentum, as we build technology that helps pilots navigate with confidence, aircraft operate more efficiently, and operators stay ahead of change. With our systems on board 90% of the world's aircraft, your work here has reached that's rare to find anywhere else.

Focusing on our customers, investing in innovation, and building a culture of accountability and performance is how we're shaping what comes next.

Every horizon. Every mission. Every day.

title: Health Protection Practitioner (Level 1)
location: Horsham, West Sussex or Ashford, Kent
description:
• Job grade: Higher Executive Officer, Other
  • Contract type: Permanent, Loan, Secondment
  • Length of employment: Permanent
  • Type of role: Science
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time, Job share, Part-time
  • Number of jobs available: 3

Location

Horsham, West Sussex or Ashford, Kent

About the job

Job summary

We are seeking to recruit a Health Protection Practitioner (HPP) to work as part of the South East Region health protection team in our Kent, Surrey & Sussex team.

We are looking for Environmental Health Practitioners, Registered Nurses, Registered Midwives or Allied Healthcare Professionals who are seeking to develop their role within the field of health protection.

The post holder will be part of the multi-disciplinary team providing the day-to-day health protection function, including the management of infectious and environmental hazards and supporting response to major incidents.

The post is an entry level Health Protection development post, and the post holder will develop specialist knowledge and skills to undertake case management, liaise with, and provide health protection advice and response across a range of partner organisations, professionals and the public.

Candidates holding NMC registration will be appointed on NHS terms and conditions at NHS AfC Band 6. Candidates without NMC registration will be appointed on Civil Service terms and conditions at HEO grade.

Salary bands:

  • AfC Band 6: £39,959 - £48,117 per annum, pro rata
  • CS HEO (Outer London): £35,587 - £43,244 per annum, pro rata

Working for your organisation

We pride ourselves as being an employer of choice, where Everyone Matters promoting equality of opportunity to actively encourage applications from everyone, including groups currently underrepresented in our workforce.

UKHSA ethos is to be an inclusive organisation for all our staff and stakeholders. To create, nurture and sustain an inclusive culture, where differences drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our workforce and wider communities. We do this through celebrating and protecting differences by removing barriers and promoting equity and equality of opportunity for all.

Please visit our careers site for more information

Job description

Your main duties will include:

  • Under supervision, contribute to day to day running of the acute response function to ensure high quality, safe and effective delivery of the health protection service.
  • Provide first point of contact for specialist knowledge, support and advice to health professionals on health protection matters.
  • Undertake initial assessment and management of routine acute response work and non-complex incidents.
  • Escalate and refer challenging or complex incidents, outbreaks of infectious diseases and non-infectious environmental hazards to senior managers.
  • Manage and carry out continuing responsibility for caseload ensuring accurate, up to date records of contacts/action by completion of relevant records and compliance with
    team handover procedures, in line with UKHSAs standards for record keeping.
  • Utilise an evidence-based approach to manage clinical/professional advice and discussions within team, seeking senior advice as/when appropriate.
  • Support and participate in the team's formal case review process.
  • Contribute to and where required lead under supervision the ongoing longer-term management of issues relevant to a defined geographical area.
  • Contribute to UKHSA response during incidents in line with UKHSAs Emergency Planning and Resilience Response (EPRR) arrangements as part of the region's responsibilities
    under the Civil Contingencies Act.
  • Will be required to participate in a local on call rota at regional level.

Detailed job description and main responsibilities

  • Surveillance
    • Contribute to the development and maintenance of effective systems for the surveillance of communicable disease and environmental hazards.
    • Contribute to the use of surveillance outputs to inform and influence local and national Public Health actions, policies and strategies.
    • Support identification and reporting of health needs, health inequalities and health impact assessment.

  • Partnership Working
    • Through activities delegated/supported by line management, contribute to the development of effective relationships with a range of individuals and stakeholders.
    • With support and guidance from line management, may need to deal with difficult and/or conflicting subject matter problems in day-to-day workload.
    • Contribute to and support the development and implementation of initiatives for public health action and improvement.

  • Research, Teaching & Training
    • Contribute to research activity to complement the health protection evidence base.
    • Contribute to the development and delivery of teaching resources and activities across a range of audiences with support from senior manager as appropriate.
    • Support the training programmes for Faculty of Public Health, Foundation Year Doctors and Specialist Trainees in the training scheme as appropriate and to the training of
      public health and health care professionals and practitioners within the locality as requested by line management.

  • Management & Leadership
    • Act as role model adhering to team professional standards.
    • Contribute to the development of policies and protocols for a wide range of health protection issues.
    • Contribute to and undertake audit as part of a wider programme of quality/service improvement activity.
    • Undertake projects on defined areas of work as agreed with the line manager.
    • Contribute to specified quality improvement and governance initiatives as agreed.
    • Ensure compliance with all confidentiality and governance requirements within the team.
    • Proactively contribute to wider organisational development.
    • Contribute to the strategic work of the locality/patch-based health protection team and deputise where appropriate.
    • Contribute pro-actively to the development and testing of the regions business continuity plan.

  • Personal & Professional Development
    • Participate in organisational and professional appraisal and revalidation as appropriate.
    • Pursue a programme of CPD, including statutory and mandatory training, in accordance with the relevant regulatory body and UKHSA requirements.
    • Agree individual clinical / professional supervision or mentorship arrangements with line manager.
    • Undergo a programme of on-going development and education to build on existing knowledge and develop skills to meet competencies required to undertake the role.

  • Communication & Key Working Relationships
    • Develop working relationships and communicate regularly with a wide range of individuals, clinical and non-clinical, internal and external to UKHSA.

The above is only an outline of the tasks, responsibilities and outcomes required of this role. You will carry out any other duties as may reasonably be required. The job description and person specifications may be reviewed on an ongoing basis in accordance with the
changing needs of the organisation.

Person specification

Essential criteria

  • First degree (Health Related) or demonstrable equivalent experience; OR Registered General Nurse or Allied Health Professional in relevant clinical discipline with current professional registration e.g. NMC
  • Working towards registration with an appropriate health or science related professional body
  • Post registration experience as a practitioner in a related field
  • An understanding of and ability to work under the current Health and Social Care Act (e.g. safe guarding vulnerable adults; data protection, information governance)
  • Effective verbal and written communication skills including report writing and presentations
  • Ability to work independently, manage and prioritise own workload and cope with competing demands
  • Ability to problem solve whilst working in an unpredictable environment, often under pressure and to tight timescales

Please note that for roles where specific qualifications or registrations are required, successful applicants will be asked to provide appropriate evidence. Employment cannot commence until satisfactory documentation has been received and verified.

Healthjobs UK has a word limit of 1500, but your supporting statement must be no more than 1000 words. We will not consider any words over 1000 words.

  • Meets some essential criteria
  • Meets no essential criteria

If used, the pile ‘Meets all essential criteria’ will proceed to shortlisting.

Open to all external applicants (anyone) from outside the Civil Service (including by definition internal applicants).

The new facilities will start becoming operational in the mid-2030s, with full completion by 2038. Staff will move in phases as facilities become available. Job summary

We are looking for a Building Services Assistant to help ensure our building remains safe, efficient, and welcoming for all users. Supporting the delivery of building operations, you will assist with a wide range of activities, including visitor management, contractor coordination, routine inspections, and maintaining building standards.

Every day will bring variety as you work closely with colleagues, building users, contractors, and stakeholders to support the smooth day-to-day running of the site. You will help maintain compliance with health and safety requirements, contribute to fire safety arrangements, and assist in creating a safe and professional environment.

This is an excellent opportunity to develop your skills and experience in building operations and facilities management while being part of a supportive team that values professionalism, customer service, and continuous improvement. Your contribution will help ensure our building remains a safe, efficient, and productive place to work.

Please note that this is a Reserved post and therefore it is important that applicants consider whether or not they are eligible to work in a reserved post before they apply. Eligibility includes sole British nationals who do not have any ties to any other nations.

Office attendance details

This is an office-based role based in Taunton, Somerset and is not eligible for hybrid working.

The postholder will be part of a weekly rota to provide office coverage between 07:00 and 19:00, Monday to Friday.

  • Act as first point of contact and escalation for building and facilities issues.
  • Ensure statutory compliance across facilities, health & safety, and fire safety, under guidance from the Facilities Management team.
  • Oversee contractor management, audits, and inspections.
  • Support senior leadership with building operations and risk management

description:

  • Contract type: Permanent
  • Type of role: Digital
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time, Job share, Part-time
