About the job

Job summary

BIST provides personnel security support across its customer departments. This role offers an exciting opportunity to work within an innovative, professional and evolving unit as the dedicated DDaT vetting and aftercare contact, supporting the delivery of effective personnel security services across DDaT.

The successful applicant will be responsible for providing DDaT with advice and support on vetting, aftercare and wider personnel security matters, ensuring that appropriate policies and processes are applied efficiently, consistently and effectively.

As an HEO in a developing and dynamic environment, you will play an active role in delivering these services on behalf of BIST. You will act as the dedicated DDaT support person for vetting and aftercare, contribute to the Personnel Security Strategy, support insider threat activity and review personnel security requirements across all DDaT roles, including role mapping and determining appropriate clearance levels.

This will also include briefing staff on security vulnerabilities. You will also need to be aware of and consider where security risks to the business can be managed in post.

You will be trusted with highly sensitive and personal information, which you must handle securely in line with data protection rules whilst maintaining a professional and understanding approach with applicants, considering the sensitive nature of the information being shared.

As a manager you will provide advice and direction to others within the team to support the timely and efficient delivery of decisions and actions. This role is highly suited to a person who can make difficult risk-based decisions, conduct investigations in a sensitive way, and motivate and build the capabilities of staff under challenging circumstances.

This is an interesting and varied role the successful applicant will manage casework by assessing personal vulnerabilities for individuals with access to sensitive government assets, to assist them in maintaining their National Security Vetting clearance.

You may be required to manage a member of staff, proactively monitoring the performance and delivery of the risk management team, to ensure that personal information and issues are handled sensitively, and that MI is recorded accurately.

You will also be responsible for implementing and conducting risk-based Aftercare for those holding National Security Vetting levels and taking forward appeals processes for those who appeal decisions for Vetting. You will support decision makers within the team including senior managers where Aftercare or appeals actions are required.

Job description

Your duties will include but will not be limited to:

  • You will build professional and supportive relationships with colleagues across BIST, DDaT, the wider security community, recruitment partners and suppliers to support the continuous development of effective personnel security processes.
  • You will champion vetting policy, procedure and process with colleagues at all levels, using various communication media.
  • You will provide advice on how to handle insider threat issues, providing personnel security advice
  • You will act as the primary DDaT contact for vetting and aftercare support, manage relevant casework and mailbox activity, and monitor the performance and delivery of staff within your line management.
  • You will investigate and assess vetting cases, making decisions on individual’s ability to hold security clearance, escalating high risk cases where appropriate. This will include conducting briefings and investigative interviews.
  • You will be responsible for implementing Aftercare measures, working closely with the Aftercare Lead and other stakeholders. You will update databases to ensure accurate records are maintained.
  • You will review personnel security requirements across all DDaT roles, working with the Aftercare Lead and DDaT stakeholders to map roles, determine appropriate clearance levels and deliver presentations and information sessions to participating teams.
  • Line management and supervision of EO and AO team members.

This is not an exclusive or exhaustive list, and the post-holders will be required to perform any additional duties reasonably expected of them within the scope of the grade and within the limits of their skill, competence and training.

Person specification

It is essential that you have:

  • Experience of making vetting decisions and managing complex vetting and aftercare casework within a personnel security environment, including gathering and assessing sensitive information to inform decisions. (LEAD)
  • Practical knowledge of personnel security, risk management, information and records management, and UK GDPR requirements when handling sensitive information.
  • Experience of managing stakeholders in relation to sensitive or complex cases, communicating decisions and advice clearly and appropriately.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to produce clear, evidence-based case documentation and recommendations.
  • Ability to build trust and rapport while asking challenging and probing questions about personal and sensitive matters.
  • Strong attention to detail, with good Microsoft 365 skills, particularly Word and Excel, and the ability to quickly learn and confidently use new systems.

It is desirable that you have:

  • Experience of working within, or alongside, a digital, data and technology function, with an understanding of how security and vetting services support a complex organisation.

description:

About the job

Job summary

We’re looking for 3 exceptional Climate Monitoring Foundation Scientists to help us make a difference to our planet.

As our Climate Monitoring Foundation Scientist, the job may be suitable for hybrid working, which is where an employee works part of the week in the office and part of the week from home. This is a voluntary, non-contractual arrangement and the location advertised will be your contractual place of work.

Our opportunity is full time, 37 hours per week, but we would also consider applicants wishing to work a minimum of 30 hours per week and we will also try our best to consider those intending to work a job share. Our people are at the heart of what we do and we'll do our best to agree a working pattern that works for everyone.

World changing work

From science to technology, from meteorology to management, and from planning to communication, our expertise helps us stand out as the authority on weather accuracy and climate prediction. We help individuals, industries and government to make better decisions to stay safe and thrive. This is the Met Office. This is who we are.

  • We’re a force for good - focusing on our environmental and social impact
  • We’re experts by nature - always learning and developing to do things better
  • We live and breathe it - putting our purpose at the heart of decision-making
  • We’re better together - understanding partnerships and inclusivity make us greater
  • We keep evolving - pushing boundaries to make tomorrow better for our customers

Job description

Your world of expertise

The Climate Monitoring and Attribution group (CMA) at the Met Office Hadley Centre is an internationally recognised group that specialises in working with observations to monitor and understand our climate.

We work closely with experts both within and outside of the Met Office, and with international agencies and initiatives, such as the World Meteorological Organisation (WMO), the European Space Agency and EUMETSAT, the European meteorological satellite agency, and we provide climate information to customers and end users, including the UK government and the public

We are recruiting into three different positions in CMA:

  • Global Surface Temperature Climate Monitoring Scientist: This position sits within the ‘Observing Climate: Marine and Cross-Domain Analysis’ team. In this role, you will develop global observational data sets and use them to monitor and report on the Earth’s climate across land, ocean and ice, with a focus on temperature change at the Earth’s surface. You will use your data analysis skills to combine current and historical instrumental data to quantify observed changes, assess uncertainty in those changes, and put current observed climate into historical context. You will develop data sets that have a wide range of applications in climate science and that are relevant to informing international climate policy and agreements.
  • Satellite Climate Observations Scientist: This position sits within the ‘Observing Climate: Land and Atmosphere’ team. The role is primarily focused on using satellite data for UK and global climate monitoring. This includes development of novel satellite-based climate indicators to characterise and track impactful climatic events, such as extreme heat, drought, vegetation stress and wildfires, and combining satellite and station data to produce new ‘blended’ datasets for key variables. This role provides the opportunity to contribute new satellite-based metrics to our Met Office Climate Dashboard, which is used internationally as a trusted source of global climate monitoring information.
  • UK Climate Scientist: This position sits within The National Climate Information Centre (NCIC) team. We are looking for a scientist with strong data management and communication skills to work closely with the existing team developing the flagship climate data sets HadUK-Grid and HadCET and supplying UK climate information to a variety of users. We communicate our analysis through regular reports and media output, most notably the high-profile annual State of the UK Climate report.

Through your work and through collaboration with experts both within and outside of the Met Office, you will utilise observational data to quantify climate change and variability by applying your analytical and scientific software skills. This role will include opportunities to apply cutting edge research such as ML approaches and new data gridding/mapping methods.

We welcome applications for all three roles from candidates with a range of scientific backgrounds. We are particularly interested in individuals who are motivated to apply their scientific and analytical skills to climate observations and climate monitoring, and who are enthusiastic about developing a career in this area.

Your key duties:

  • Working with data from a variety of sources, including UK and global weather stations, satellites, ships and buoys to create new observational climate data sets and update existing data sets.
  • Effectively conveying confidence in results through robust quantification of observational uncertainty and evaluation.
  • Analysing new and existing observational data sets to characterise and monitor global, regional and UK climate change.
  • Documenting and disseminating scientific findings via peer-reviewed papers, reports, webpages, press releases and through presentations at national/international meetings and conferences. Providing guidance to internal and external users of climate observation data.
  • Working collaboratively within a team of scientists and scientific software engineers to deliver and communicate high-quality scientific output.

Person specification

  1. Lead Criteria: Evidence of experience in processing, analysing and interpreting scientific or other complex data sets, including, for example, investigating patterns, variability or trends. Evidence of carefully checking your results. (We’re experts by nature)
  2. An undergraduate degree in physical, environmental, computational, or mathematical science or demonstration of equivalent experience, with evidence of a proactive approach to developing new skills. (We’re experts by nature, We keep evolving)
  3. Demonstrated experience of writing computer code in Python (or a similar programming language) to process and analyse data. (We’re experts by nature)
  4. Evidence of good communication skills (written, oral, presentation and listening), conveying scientific/technical information clearly, accurately and concisely. (We’re experts by nature)
  5. Evidence of the ability to balance competing demands on your time and to work in a collaborative team to successfully deliver a common goal. (We live and breathe it, We’re better together)

The panel may perform a preliminary sift of the lead criteria as indicated above.

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £28,600, Met Office contributes £8,285 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

Our work is life-changing, often life-saving and always life-enhancing. The Met Office is Great Place to Work UK certified. We are also featured on their ‘Best Workplaces in Tech’ 2023, 2024 and 2025 lists, as well as their ’54 Best Workplaces for Women’ 2023 list.

As our Climate Monitoring Foundation Scientist, your total reward package will be up to £40,524 annually, which includes:

  • £28,600 base pay
  • An outstanding Civil Service pension, with an average employer contribution of 28.97%
  • Annual Leave starting at 27.5 days (plus Bank Holidays) rising to 32.5 days (plus Bank Holidays) after 5 years and option to buy or sell up to 5 days per year of annual leave

About the job

Job summary

Senior Governance Manager

£80,000 per annum

Bedford

Permanent

Hybrid Working

Ready to make a real difference? Join us at the Money and Pensions Service (MaPS) as our Senior Governance Manager. This is your chance to play a meaningful role in helping people across the UK build stronger financial futures and to do it as part of a supportive, energetic team.

Why This Role Matters

In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to lead and own the development, implementation and continuous improvement of MaPS’ corporate governance framework, ensuring it is robust, proportionate, strategically aligned and consistently embedded across MaPS’ Non-Executive and Executive governance structures. The role will provide senior leadership on governance design, decision-making, accountability and assurance, ensuring MaPS has effective arrangements in place to support organisational delivery, manage risk and meet public sector accountability expectations.

A key priority will be to lead the integration of the National Dashboard Connection Service into MaPS’ governance framework, ensuring that appropriate governance, assurance, compliance and accountability arrangements are established for the Executive, Board and DWP. The role will act as a senior governance adviser to Chairs, the CEO, Executive Team and senior leaders, providing authoritative advice, constructive challenge and practical solutions on complex governance, compliance, regulatory and public sector accountability matters, working closely with MaPS’ legal advisers where required.

The role will provide strategic leadership to the governance team, setting standards for high-quality governance advice, secretariat support and corporate governance practice across MaPS. It will be accountable for ensuring that Board, Committee and Executive governance processes operate effectively, support high-quality decision-making and enable the organisation to demonstrate transparency, accountability and good governance. The postholder will deputise for the Head of Governance and Data Protection as required and will play a key role in shaping the future direction, maturity and impact of the governance function. Shaping work that genuinely improves people’s financial wellbeing.

You’ll join a team that’s passionate, collaborative, and driven by the belief that financial confidence should be something everyone can access.

Job description

  • Lead and be accountable for the continuous improvement of MaPS’ Corporate Governance Framework, ensuring appropriate decision-making processes are in place across the business and that MaPS has a consistent and holistic approach to governance aligned with external best practice.
  • Provide senior governance leadership and expert advice to Chairs, Non-Executive Directors, the CEO, Executive Team and senior leaders on governance, decision-making, accountability, compliance and public sector requirements.
  • Lead the governance integration of the National Dashboard Connection Service, ensuring that appropriate decision-making, assurance, risk, compliance and accountability mechanisms are embedded and effective.
  • Shape and influence governance and approvals arrangements with DWP and other government stakeholders, ensuring MaPS’ decision-making processes are clear, efficient, robust and capable of withstanding external scrutiny.
  • Lead the business case governance framework, ensuring business cases are well-governed, evidence-based, appropriately assured and aligned with government approval expectations.
  • Provide strategic oversight of Board, Committee, Executive and sub-committee governance processes, ensuring agendas, papers, minutes, actions and decisions support effective oversight, accountability and delivery.
  • Set standards for governance advice, secretariat practice and corporate governance support across MaPS, ensuring consistency, quality and continuous improvement in the service provided to senior forums.
  • Lead and develop a team of Governance Managers and Advisers, building capability, setting clear expectations, supporting professional development and fostering a high-performing, trusted governance function.
  • Provide senior oversight of MaPS’ corporate policy framework and governance-related policies, ensuring key policies are reviewed, maintained and embedded effectively, including conflicts of interest, whistleblowing, gifts and hospitality and related governance procedures.

description:

Location

Addenbrookes Hospital, Cambridge

About the job

Job summary

UKHSA provides strategic leadership and vision for protecting and improving the nation’s health. Its ambition is to lead nationally, and enable locally, a transformation in the health expectations of all people in England, regardless of where they live and the circumstance of their birth. It will achieve this through the application of research, knowledge and skills. UKHSA is an executive agency of the Department of Health. It is a distinct delivery organisation with operational autonomy to advise and support government, local authorities and the NHS in a professionally independent manner.

The Microbiology laboratory at Cambridge is the East of England Region for UKHSA currently providing services to Addenbrooke’s, Royal Papworth, and the E&N Herts Hospitals, the surrounding district and other NHS Laboratories. It has active research and epidemiological interests. Set on the outskirts of the university city of Cambridge, Addenbrooke’s Hospital is one of the top hospitals in the UK and a thriving NHS Foundation Trust. Addenbrooke’s is closely associated with leading educational providers including the University of Cambridge and is a major centre for biomedical research and education.

Job description

Supervises bench work of a team within the laboratory in processing of microbiological specimens and related tasks including isolation, identification, interpretation and reporting of results in accordance with agreed polices and standard operating procedures. As a member of the management team, take a specialised lead role within the department.

Communication and key working relationships

Internal

  • Supervises BMS, Trainee, Support workers and other junior grade staff within a team.
  • Liaise with more senior grade BMS and medical staff concerning microbiological investigations and other tasks to be performed, including explanation of results to ward and other clinical staff.
  • Liaise with Quality Manager and Training Officer for quality and training issues.

External

  • Liaise with external bodies including NHS staff and commercial companies.

Detailed job description and main responsibilities

Staff managed

  • Biomedical Scientists and support staff team

Technical and scientific

  • Advises staff regarding technical difficulties.
  • Participates in implementing and suggesting changes to work practices and procedures.
  • Selection of appropriate test profiles according to agreed protocols.
  • Analysis of cultures, determination of antibiotic susceptibility and biomedical identification of micro-organisms
  • Performance of immunological and other assays to investigate microbial infection and management of therapeutic agents.
  • Screen and interpret test results (including those from regional specialties within the hospitals served) and communicate findings to senior colleagues and medical microbiology staff.
  • Technical validation of reports for clinical authorisation
  • Under strict protocols authorisation of reports for release to other departments, wards, general practitioners and other customers.
  • Participate in provision of out of hours on-call service (lone working).
  • Participate in Senior BMS rotation through all sections of the department.
  • Contribute to preparation of documents and SOPs
  • Contribute to incident and outbreak investigations
  • Participate in and support relevant R&D activities of the laboratory and UKHSA, including epidemiological characterisation of organisms by alternative technologies.
  • Provide technical advice to internal and external laboratory users

Health & Safety

In collaboration with the Laboratory Safety Team:Ensure that all tasks are carried out to the required safety standards

  • Report all accidents and incidents or near misses, dangerous situations or shortcomings in health and safety training instructions
  • Maintain competence to work to containment level 3 standards
  • Participate in risk assessment

Your attention is drawn to the Health & Safety Act of 1974 which requires you to take reasonable care for yourself and others who may be affected by your acts and omissions at work; and to co-operate with your employer on any matters of health and safety.
Quality/Clinical Governance

In collaboration with Laboratory Quality manager:

  • Participate in quality management audits.
  • Maintain a high standard of work and comply with departmental quality policy
  • Contribute to internal and external quality assurance programmes
  • Ensure compliance with UKAS and other accreditation and certification standards
  • Contribute to internal and external audit programmes and corrective actions
  • Participate in review of Standard Operating Procedures take every effort to suggest quality improvements

Information Technology

  • Record test results on live computer systems in accordance with agreed standard operating procedures
  • Use databases and software packages.

Staff management and training

  • Manages and allocates work to BMS, Healthcare Science Support workers and other junior grade staff of the laboratory to comply with agreed laboratory turn around times.
  • With other team leaders plans day-to-day of the work of the laboratory.
  • Plans the day-to-day training activities of staff
  • Responsible for internal communication to staff
  • Participate in training and supervision of trainee BMS and Healthcare Science Support staff.
  • Participate in skills development of other BMS.
  • Participate in training of junior medical staff in microbiological techniques.

Support services & Equipment

  • Participate in management of stock levels within the laboratory
  • Monitor and maintain laboratory equipment.

Strategy, Policy and Service development

  • Actively participate as a member of the Senior BMS Committee
  • Work with others to improve working practices.

General employment responsibilities

  • Ensure confidentiality and conformance to Data Protection Act in collaboration with designated Caldecott Guardian, Data Protection Officer and Security of information Officer.
  • Actively participate and maintain a continuing professional development programme
  • Develop professional/management expertise by undertaking further appropriate training

Working Environment:

  • This job will involve frequent exposure to unpleasant bodily fluids including sputum, faeces, blood etc. and to Micro-organisms likely to cause disease.
  • To work within the UKHSA and Laboratory policies, codes of practice and professional guidelines.
    This list is not exhaustive

Please note that UKHSA is exploring options for the future of the Clinical Network Laboratories service and that further information will be shared as the review progresses.

Person specification

Essential Criteria:

  • FIBMS (Fellow of the institute of Biomedical Science) or equivalent
  • State HCPC Registration
  • Understands quality assurance principles and procedures
  • Knows and understands laboratory safety requirements and procedures
  • Relevant experience of working in a microbiology laboratory
  • Aptitude for managing people and assessing performance
  • Able to convey ideas and opinions clearly, concisely, orally and in writing

Benefits

  • Learning and development tailored to your role
  • An environment with flexible working options
  • A culture encouraging inclusion and diversity
  • A Civil Service pension with an employer contribution of 28.97%

UKHSA ethos is to be an inclusive organisation for all our staff and stakeholders. Location

East Midlands (England), East of England, London (region), North East England, North West England, Scotland, South East England, South West England, Wales, West Midlands (England), Yorkshire and the Humber

About the job

Job summary

This position is based Nationally

Job description

Role: Strategic Engagement Manager

Business: Office of Public Guardian (OPG)

Location: National

Grade: HEO

Salary: £35,335 - £37,847

Contract Type: Permanent

Minimum Hours: Full time. Requests for flexible, part-time working and job share will be considered, taking into account the operational needs of the Department.

Organisational Overview

The Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) protects people in England and Wales who may not have the mental capacity to make certain decisions for themselves, such as about their health and finance. We are an Executive Agency of the Ministry of Justice (MoJ), set up in 2007 following the introduction of the Mental Capacity Act of 2005.

OPG is responsible for registering lasting powers of attorney (LPA) and enduring powers of attorney (EPA) and supervising deputies who are appointed by the Court of Protection.

OPG is a fantastic place to work offering a range of development opportunities. The OPG is a disability confident employer and is committed to developing a supportive and inclusive environment that reflects the diverse community we serve.

OPG is currently delivering an ambitious transformation programme. This will change the way we provide services and help us meet the growing needs of our users, partners and our stakeholders. It will make sure our users experience a better level of support and will help us to respond to the changing needs of society. Transformation will ensure we can better support adults at risk and create high-quality services that are accessible and affordable.

Team Overview

The Strategic Engagement team leads and co-ordinates OPG’s engagement with key external stakeholders, helping the organisation explain its plans and priorities, listen to stakeholder insight, and use feedback to improve services. The team supports strategic relationships across OPG, develops engagement approaches for priority audiences, and produces tailored briefings and communications material to support effective stakeholder activity.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Support improvements to the quality of stakeholder engagement across OPG and assist with strategic advice to OPG senior leaders on handling high-profile and sensitive issues.
  • Support work to maintain effective and proactive relationships with OPG’s key stakeholders at senior level to support delivery of strategic objectives.
  • Support OPG’s business and customer transformation programmes by assisting with stakeholder handling and engagement strategies for inclusion in project and programme delivery plans.
  • Manage the co-ordination of business-as-usual stakeholder engagement activity across OPG to support consistent messaging and corporate memory.
  • Make clear recommendations to senior leaders in response to engagement invitations and support delivery of a proactive engagement calendar.
  • Manage the delivery of high-quality briefings and communications material for key stakeholder audiences, promoting better understanding of OPG issues and initiatives.
  • Support the planning and delivery of engagement activity such as webinars.
  • Support the gathering of intelligence and analysis of external engagement effectiveness to inform current and future engagement strategies.

Agreed Expectations

The successful candidate will be expected to work from their base location on a weekly basis in line with current Civil Service requirements, outside of any reasonable adjustments.

The role may require engagement with a diverse range of stakeholders, including at senior levels, and occasional travel to other offices or stakeholder locations may be required in line with business need.

Skills & Qualifications

Essential Skills

  • Ability to establish, build and maintain constructive working relationships with a diverse, sometimes challenging, range of key stakeholders at a senior level. (Lead Criteria)
  • Excellent organisational and planning skills.
  • Strong written and oral communication skills, with experience of delivering high-quality tailored briefings and other products to support successful stakeholder engagement activity. (Lead Criteria)
  • Knowledge and understanding of stakeholder engagement principles and experience of supporting the delivery of stakeholder engagement strategies and plans to deliver strategic organisational objectives.
  • A strong team player, with proven ability to collaborate with others to deliver key objectives, projects and programmes of work.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office products including Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams and PowerPoint.

Desirable Skills

The below criteria are desirable only. These will not be assessed throughout the recruitment process but will be used in the event of tied scores between candidates.

  • Experience of working on a project and the ability to use project management principles.

Application process

This recruitment will follow the Civil Service Success Profile process. Candidates will be expected to complete the following as part of the application:

  • CV (up to 2 pages of A4) and Statement of Suitability of no more than 1000 words, to demonstrate your experience against the essential skills required for this role.

In the event that we receive a large number of applications, we will conduct an initial sift based on the lead criteria:

  • Ability to establish, build and maintain constructive working relationships with a diverse, sometimes challenging, range of key stakeholders at a senior level.
  • Strong written and oral communication skills, with experience of delivering high-quality tailored briefings and other products to support successful stakeholder engagement activity.

Interview Process

If you are successful at sift, you will be invited to an interview which will use the Civil Service Success Profiles. At interview, candidates should expect questions on:

  • Strengths relevant to the role
  • The following Behaviours:
  • Delivering at Pace
  • Working Together
  • Managing a Quality Service
  • Communicating and influencing (10-minute presentation)

All interviews will be held remotely via MS Teams.

Feedback will only be provided if you attend an interview.

Reasonable Adjustments

title: Business Optimization Analyst
description:
Om oss

På E.ON Regionnät är vi mitt i energiomställningen. Elektrifieringen går snabbt och tillsammans med ökad efterfrågan på kapacitet och nya kundbehov skapar det både spännande möjligheter och komplexa utmaningar. För att fatta kloka beslut behöver vi förstå våra kunder, vårt nät och vår omvärld, och använda data på ett sätt som skapar verkligt värde.

Inom teamet Marknads- & Affärsrelationer använder vi data, analys och affärsförståelse för att utveckla smartare prissättning, abonnemang och digitala lösningar som skapar konkret affärsvärde. Nu söker vi en Business Optimization Analyst som vill bidra med nyfikenhet, analys och nya perspektiv.

Din roll

Som Business Optimization Analyst hjälper du oss att omvandla data och komplex information till tydliga insikter och användbara beslutsunderlag. Du får en varierad roll där analys möter verksamhetsutveckling och där du får möjlighet att både fördjupa dig i data och se till helheten.

Du samarbetar nära kollegor och experter inom olika delar av verksamheten, samtidigt som du får utrymme att ta ansvar för och driva egna förbättringsinitiativ. Tillsammans utvecklar vi våra analyser, arbetssätt och verktyg för att skapa ännu bättre förutsättningar för datadrivna beslut.

I rollen kommer du bland annat att:

  • Automatisera och vidareutveckla analyser och rapporter

  • Kvalitetssäkra och strukturera data

  • Utveckla dashboarder och beslutsstöd

  • Genomföra analyser inom kund, abonnemang och kapacitet

  • Bygga och utveckla prognos- och scenariomodeller.

Dina erfarenheter

Vi tror att du tycker om att utforska data, hitta samband och göra komplex information mer begriplig. Du är strukturerad och nyfiken och motiveras av att tillsammans med andra utveckla arbetssätt och hitta smartare lösningar.

Du har en akademisk examen inom exempelvis teknisk fysik, industriell ekonomi, energisystem eller liknande men även annan relevant kvantitativ utbildning är av intresse.

Vi ser gärna att du har ett intresse för dataanalys, modellering, verksamhetsutveckling och energibranschen. Har du erfarenhet av SQL, Python eller liknande verktyg är det värdefullt, men vi är också intresserade av dig som har en relevant grund och vill fortsätta utvecklas inom området.

För att trivas i rollen tror vi också att du tycker om att kommunicera och göra analyser och insikter tillgängliga för andra. Du har förmåga att se samband mellan kunder, nät, kapacitet, ekonomi och reglering och kan omsätta dem till konkreta rekommendationer.

Hur är det hos oss?

Hos oss blir du en del av ett sammanhang där analys och data används för att lösa verkliga utmaningar i energiomställningen. Du får arbeta tillsammans med kollegor med olika perspektiv och kompetenser, dela kunskap och samtidigt utveckla din egen expertis.

Vi tror på värdet av samarbete, nyfikenhet och olika perspektiv. Du behöver därför inte kunna allt från början. Det viktiga är att du har en stark analytisk grund, tycker om att lära dig och vill bidra till att vi tillsammans utvecklar både verksamheten och framtidens energisystem.

På E.ON arbetar vi aktivt med inkludering - det är avgörande för att driva energiomställningen framåt. Vi vill att just du ska känna dig välkommen! Vi strävar efter att skapa en trygg arbetsmiljö med meningsfulla arbetsuppgifter och goda möjligheter till utveckling. Vi fortsätter hela tiden att utmana oss själva för att skapa en välkomnande arbetsplats, där vi hoppas att du kommer att trivas.

Vi arbetar för ett mer hållbart energisamhälle, men det är minst lika viktigt att våra medarbetare har förutsättningar att värna om sin egen hållbarhet. Vi erbjuder därför bra förmåner för att du ska må bra och ha god balans mellan arbete och fritid. Några av dessa är t.ex. arbetstidsförkortning som är högre än branschens standard, hälsoförsäkring, fri sjukvård och mer därtill!

Varmt välkommen att söka och var med oss på vägen mot ett mer hållbart samhälle! Sista ansökningsdag är 6 november.

description:

Location

This role is available on a remote, hybrid, or office basis.
Initially, all DBS employees' contracts are office-based at one of our two sites. Employees can apply for remote or hybrid work from day one. If approved, the arrangement will start after six months for transfers from Home Office or after completing probation for new joiners. Requests will be considered based on business needs and role requirements. Informal hybrid working arrangements are also available from day one, subject to business needs and role requirements and will be discussed further following any job offer.

About the job

Job summary

The Workforce Modelling Manager will deliver workforce modelling and capacity planning across DBS, translating demand forecasts into optimised workforce strategies that ensure resources, skills and deployment are aligned to operational and strategic requirements.

The role is accountable for delivering robust modelling that supports efficient, effective and sustainable service delivery, identifying capacity risks, informing workforce strategy and enabling evidence‑based decisions on resource allocation and organisational design.

The postholder will drive continuous improvement in modelling approaches and tools, ensuring workforce insight is fully integrated into business planning, performance frameworks and delivery of DBS priorities.

The postholder will also lead DBS's compliance with the Government Functional Standard for Analysis, organisational data maturity, and delivery of the DBS Data Strategy, overseeing assessments and driving cross‑business improvement to strengthen capability, data quality, resilience and risk management.

The successful applicant will initially need to attend office in Liverpool and Darlington for desk training, thereafter the role can be hybrid (remote/office based).

In the case of system outages and business needs, attendance in the office will be required.

Job description

Key Responsibilities:

  • Manage and develop the DBS Workforce Modelling function (including Operational resources and wider DBS resources) to deliver a high-quality, trusted service, supporting DBS service delivery and decision-making.
  • Translate demand forecasts into resource requirements (FTE, skills, deployment).
  • Develop and maintain workforce models covering productivity, utilisation, and throughput.
  • Support resource allocation, work distribution, and demand management processes.
  • Identify gaps between capacity and demand and recommend solutions.
  • Extend resource planning across end-to-end processes and new service areas.
  • Contribute to workforce strategy, including skills planning and organisational design inputs.
  • Support SLA and KPI development through understanding of capacity constraints.
  • Work with Operations to assess impact of demand changes on workforce requirements.
  • Drive continuous improvement in workforce modelling techniques and tools.
  • Manage compliance with the Government Functional Standard for Analysis, including organisation‑wide assessments and delivery of improvement actions to support continuous improvement in analytical practice.
  • Manage organisational data maturity improvement, including maturity assessments and delivery of improvement actions to strengthen data capability and reduce risk.
  • Manage and drive delivery of the DBS Data Strategy action plan, coordinating activity across business areas and ensuring progress against agreed priorities to improve data quality, resilience and use.
  • Ensure that work processes and approaches, comply with Government Functional Standard 010 (Analysis).
  • Build strong, collaborative relationships across DBS and with customers.
  • Work collectively to ensure end-to-end service delivery across teams.
  • Identify and deliver continuous improvement in quality, efficiency, and processes.
  • Ensure accuracy, integrity, and timeliness of data, analysis, and outputs.
  • Contribute to business planning, operational delivery, and strategic decision-making.
  • Provide clear narrative, insight, and implications alongside data outputs and draw out the 'So What' to enable confident decision making.
  • Ensure risks are identified, communicated, and mitigated.
  • Support organisational objectives including service transition, LTER, and new products.
  • Lead and develop a multi-grade team, setting objectives, managing performance and workload, and building the capability required to deliver current priorities and adapt to future business needs.
  • Contribute to governance reporting (Executive Team, Board, committees, Ministers).
  • Deputise for the Head of Service as required.

Corporate Responsibilities:

  • Support the Head of Service in their role as a member of the Directorate Leadership Team (DLT) and by engaging in and helping to drive change as required.
  • From time to time, the postholder may be asked to support corporate activity with duties that are commensurate with the grade (e.g. supporting other parts of the business with HR related matters).

Person specification

Essential Criteria:

  • Ability to lead the development of Workforce Modelling tools.
  • Understanding of workforce planning within a large business/operational setting.
  • Strong analytical capability, with the ability to interpret complex data and identify key insights.
  • Ability to communicate complex data and insight clearly to a range of audiences, including senior management.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills.
  • Ability to lead others and deliver under pressure.
  • Ability to prioritise work effectively against competing demands.
  • Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office tools.
  • Experience of producing, interpreting, and presenting data and Forecasts.
  • Experience of developing Forecasting and MI products (including dashboards) and prioritising requirements in line with user needs.
  • Proven experience in developing and applying data collection, analysis, and performance reporting approaches to support both operational delivery and strategic decision-making.
  • Experience operating in a large, complex business/operational environment (ideally central government or similar).
  • Track record of managing performance and providing clear direction to teams.
  • Experience of delivering outcomes under pressure, prioritising competing demands and meeting challenging deadlines.
  • Experience of building effective strategic relationships across a wide range of internal and external stakeholders.

Desirable Criteria:

  • Advanced Microsoft Excel skills including practical ability in using Power Query in Excel.
  • Expert, current knowledge of Business Intelligence tools and technologies and their practical application.

title: Lead DevOps Engineer
description:
• Job grade: Grade 7
  • Contract type: Permanent
  • Business area: DSIT - Corporate Services - Analysis
  • Type of role: Digital, Information Technology
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time, Job share, Part-time
  • Number of jobs available: 1

Location

Bristol, London, Salford

About the job

Job summary

At DSIT we’re all about improving people’s lives by maximising the potential of science & technology.

We accelerate innovation, investment and productivity through world-class science, research and development.

We use technology for good by ensuring new and existing technologies are safely developed and deployed across the UK, with the benefits more widely shared.

We are driving forward a modern digital government which gives citizens a more satisfying experience and their time back.

We do all this to enable the Government’s 5 national missions: kickstarting economic growth, making Britain a clean energy superpower, taking back our streets, breaking down barriers to opportunity and building an NHS fit for the future.

Above all, we focus on improving people’s lives. Whether it’s researching new treatments for disease, developing better batteries, reducing burdens through better public services, keeping children safe online, and much more, outcomes for citizens are at the heart of what we do.

Our Inclusive Environment

We offer flexible working benefits, employee well-being support and a great pension. We are enormously proud to be a Disability Confident Leader employer. We support candidates with adjustments throughout our recruitment process. Information about disability confidence and just some examples of the adjustments that you can request can be found in the reasonable adjustment section below.

Please note

Former DSIT recruitment campaigns are continuing as usual, but candidates should be aware that following the Government’s announcement on the changes to some civil service departments, roles will be subject to the machinery of government moves and will ultimately be in one of the new departments. We will provide more information if you are selected for a role. This work remains of high importance to the civil service, and we thank you for your continued interest.

Job description

We are building a modern, unified analytical tooling and data platform, giving analysts across the department access to tools and data quickly and securely. The platform is based on the Ministry of Justice’s open-source Analytical Platform, widely recognised as a leading model across government. The team have completed user acceptance testing and are preparing to migrate analysts onto the platform, however there are plenty of new features to be added and we are setting up a short feedback cycle with our users, to rapidly iterate the platform.

The project is led by the Head of Platforms and Engineering, and the team brings expertise across data engineering, dev ops and software development. We are a small team with lots of autonomy and work collaboratively to tackle problems and decide on the best ways of working. For the right candidate, there will be the opportunity to take on a leadership role within the team.

The platform is made up of several components, divided into two sections:

  1. Analytical tooling – delivering the secure, scalable tools analysts need, such as JupyterLab, RStudio, and VS Code, GitHub integration, and cloud-based workflow orchestration.
  2. Data platform – delivering the pipelines, storage, and ingestion processes that ensure analysts can find and use trusted data efficiently.

The role is part of the central Data Science and Engineering team, in the department’s Analysis function. This team plays a key role in shaping the department’s analytical capability. By sitting within Analysis, the team ensures the platform is developed with analysts’ needs front and centre, owned by the analytical community and built to serve it.

As a G7 Lead DevOps Engineer in the analytical tooling strand of the project, you will own and extend the infrastructure and tools that enable analysts to work securely, reproducibly and efficiently. You’ll take forward the platform to ensure it is a secure, cloud-based environment for analysis at scale, drawing on best practice across government. Your work will directly improve evidence-based policymaking, unlock efficiency savings across the department, and create the foundations for future innovation and AI based policymaking.

The team are led by the needs of our users, and initially this role will focus on strengthening and extending the analytical tooling infrastructure. As the platform matures, you’ll also have opportunities to tackle broader DevOps challenges across the department, including data science and AI applications that improve operational efficiency and widen access to data for non- technical users.

Person specification

  • Manage secure, scalable deployments of key analytical tools, including JupyterLab, RStudio and VS Code.
  • Ensure authentication, access controls, monitoring, and audit capabilities are in line with DSIT and cross-government security standards.
  • Ensure robust CI/CD (GitHub) and environment management processes are in place.
  • Work closely with Data Engineers and wider digital colleagues to ensure seamless integration between tooling and data systems.
  • Extend the analytical platform, developing new features to meet user requirements such as dashboard hosting and AI applications.
  • Support onboarding of users and act on feedback to refine the platform for wider rollout.

Essential Criteria

  • Strong experience designing and delivering secure cloud-based infrastructure (AWS preferred).
  • Proficiency in containerisation and orchestration (e.g. Docker, Kubernetes, AWS ECS/Fargate).
  • Proficiency setting up infrastructure-as-code (Terraform preferred).
  • Ability to set up CI/CD pipelines.
  • Knowledge of information security and access control in cloud services.
  • A collaborative approach to working with data engineers, software developers, service designers and users to shape fit-for-purpose tools.

Desirable Criteria

  • Experience with Python and Django applications.
  • Familiarity with analytical user requirements and how to build user-friendly analytical platforms.
  • Familiarity with analytical tools (e.g. JupyterLab, RStudio, VS Code) and how they are deployed in cloud environments.

Technical skills

We'll assess you against these technical skills during the selection process:

  • Competency: Systems design (practitioner)
  • Modern development standards (expert)
  • Troubleshooting and problem resolution (expert)

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £58,275, Department for Science, Innovation & Technology contributes £16,882 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

The Department for Science, Innovation and Technology offers a competitive mix of benefits including:

  • A culture of flexible working, such as job sharing, homeworking and compressed hours.
  • Automatic enrolment into the Civil Service Pension Scheme, with an employer contribution of 28.97%.
  • A minimum of 25 days of paid annual leave, increasing by 1 day per year up to a maximum of 30.
  • An extensive range of learning & professional development opportunities, which all staff are actively encouraged to pursue.
  • Access to a range of retail, travel and lifestyle employee discounts.

Office attendance

The Department operates a discretionary hybrid working policy, which provides for a combination of working hours from your place of work and from your home in the UK. The current expectation for staff is to attend the office or non-home based location for 40-60% of the time over the accounting period.

Things you need to know

Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Selection process details

This vacancy is using Success Profiles (opens in a new window), and will assess your Experience and Technical skills.

As part of the application process you will be asked to complete a CV and personal statement. Further details around what this will entail are listed on the application form.

Please use your personal statement (in no more than 500 words) to describe how you meet the essential criteria for this role.

Applications will be sifted on CV and Personal Statement.

In the event of a large number of applicants, applications will be sifted on the CV only.

Candidates who pass the initial sift may be progressed to a full sift, or progressed straight to assessment/interview.

Former DSIT recruitment campaigns are continuing as usual, but candidates should be aware that following the Government’s announcement on the changes to some civil service departments, roles will be subject to the machinery of government moves and will ultimately be in one of the new departments. We will provide more information if you are selected for a role. This work remains of high importance to the civil service, and we thank you for your continued interest.

Reasonable Adjustment

We are proud to be a disability confident leader and we welcome applications from disabled candidates and candidates with long-term conditions.

Information about the Disability Confident Scheme (DCS) and some examples of adjustments that we offer to disabled candidates and candidates with long-term health conditions during our recruitment process can be found in our DSIT Candidate Guidance. If you are experiencing accessibility problems with any attachments on this advert, please contact the email address in the 'Contact point for applicants' section.

New entrants are expected to join on the minimum of the pay band.

A location based reserve list of successful candidates will be kept for 12 months. Should another role become available within that period you may be offered this position.

Candidates who meet the minimum benchmark may be placed on a Reserve List for consideration for similar roles, including those at a lower grade. Candidates who narrowly miss the benchmark and are not placed on the Reserve List may still be considered for an offer in a similar role at a lower grade.

Please note terms and conditions are attached. Please take time to read the document to determine how these may affect you.

Any move to the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology from another employer will mean you can no longer access childcare vouchers. This includes moves between government departments. You may however be eligible for other government schemes, including Tax Free Childcare; for further information visit the Childcare Choices website.

DSIT does not normally offer full home working (i.e. working at home); but we do offer a variety of flexible working options (including occasionally working from home).

DSIT cannot offer Visa sponsorship to candidates through this campaign. DSIT holds a Visa sponsorship licence but this can only be used for certain roles and this campaign does not qualify.

In order to process applications without delay, we will be sending a Criminal Record Check to Disclosure and Barring Service on your behalf.

However, we recognise in exceptional circumstances some candidates will want to send their completed forms direct. If you will be doing this, please advise Government Recruitment Service of your intention by emailing Pre-EmploymentChecks.grs@cabinetoffice.gov.uk stating the job reference number in the subject heading.

Applicants who are successful at interview will be, as part of pre-employment screening, subject to a check on the Internal Fraud Database (IFD). This check will provide information about employees who have been dismissed for fraud or dishonesty offences. This check also applies to employees who resign or otherwise leave before being dismissed for fraud or dishonesty had their employment continued. Any applicant’s details held on the IFD will be refused employment.

A candidate is not eligible to apply for a role within the Civil Service if the application is made within a 5 year period following a dismissal for carrying out internal fraud against government.

For further information on National Security Vetting please visit the Demystifying Vetting website.

Security

About the job

Job summary

This is an exciting opportunity to join the CB Reachback Modelling Capability, a team that provides urgent scientific advice and emergency response support to MOD and homeland security operations. Working as part of a specialist team, you will deliver Chemical and Biological hazard assessment advice, using mathematical models to evaluate the potential impact of toxic materials released into the atmosphere. Your work will directly inform decision-making at the highest levels of government and contribute to the development of current and future policy.

This is a dynamic and fast-paced role, often requiring responses to time-critical and high-priority requests. Success in the role will depend on your ability to communicate complex technical information clearly, manage competing priorities and remain calm and effective under pressure while delivering high-quality scientific outputs.

Why Join Us?

Dstl recognises the importance of diversity and inclusion as people from diverse backgrounds bring fresh ideas. We are committed to building an inclusive working environment in which each employee fulfils their potential and maximises their contribution.

Job description

In this role you will deliver deliver scientific analysis at pace, using modelling and your expert knowledge to generate robust evidence. You will use your judgement to reach evidence based conclusions and contribute scientific expertise to our customers through a variety of communication methods. The successful candidate will also actively contribute to capability development to improve the quality and pace of our future responses.

For further details, please see the job profile at the bottom of this advert.

Person specification

We looking for someone who has:

Chemistry / Engineering / Mathematics / Physics

About the job

Job summary

The Met Office is delighted to open our advertising for Industrial Placements 2027.

This is an exciting opportunity to join the Met Office on a 12-month Year in Industry placement, commencing at the start of July 2027, developing your skills and knowledge and ensuring you gain the most value possible from your experience with us.

You will have the opportunity to network with our cohort of Industrial Placements all over the Met Office and understand what career opportunities are on offer at the Met Office after you graduate.

We’re looking for two Data Engineer Industrial Placements to help us make a difference to our planet.

As a Met Office Data Engineer Industrial Placement, the job may be suitable for hybrid working, which is where an employee works part of the week in the office and part of the week from home. This is a voluntary, non-contractual arrangement, and the location advertised will be your contractual place of work. As an Industrial Placement, we would expect you to attend the office once a week as a minimum.

Our opportunity is full-time, 37 hours per week. Our people are at the heart of what we do, and we'll do our best to agree a working pattern that works for everyone.

World changing work

From science to technology, from meteorology to management, and from planning to communication, our expertise helps us stand out as the authority on weather accuracy and climate prediction. We help individuals, industries, and government to make better decisions to stay safe and thrive. This is the Met Office. This is who we are.

  • We’re a force for good - focusing on our environmental and social impact
  • We’re experts by nature - always learning and developing to do things better
  • We live and breathe it - putting our purpose at the heart of decision-making
  • We’re better together - understanding partnerships and inclusivity make us greater
  • We keep evolving - pushing boundaries to make tomorrow better for our customers

Job description

Your world of expertise

Our Industrial Placement scheme offers ambitious and capable undergraduates the opportunity to gain valuable experience working alongside diverse and highly skilled experts in their field. You’ll be working on projects that really matter and will make a difference.

As a part of the Machine Learning Operations team, you will be a part of a growing group of people who are building the services the Met Office will reply upon to power the next generation of forecasting. Our team comprises Software, DevOps and Data Engineers, Product and Delivery experts, Cloud Solutions Architects and Mathematicians. We come from different backgrounds, but we all share a passion for data and building amazing services. We are at the centre of the Met Office's plans to embrace AI and Machine Learning to inform our Weather and Climate models, and you would be joining at a crucial time as we move from experimentation to real-world operations.

Our team are all multidisciplinary, we turn our hands to multiple tasks to help deliver on the Met Office's and Team' objectives. We get involved in conversations spanning Technology, Product and Science to support our colleagues - we aim to be the first port of call for people who want to make the move from small-scale experimentation to large-scale data processing and service creation.

Your key duties

An Industrial Placement Data Engineer learns on the job, and you will develop skills while working under supervision to deliver stories in a multidisciplinary team to:

  • Understand and be proficient in different data types used in the Met Office
  • Understand the scripts/methods used to transform our data
  • Be able to share with others in the importance of data engineering

Person specification

  1. Lead Criteria: Studying towards a degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Data Engineering, or a related field which must incorporate a placement year.
  2. Demonstrable experience with programming languages such as Python, Java, Scala, or R (Expert by Nature).
  3. Understanding data flows, data structures, algorithms, data engineering principles, and business intelligence (BI) systems.
  4. Good communication and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently and as part of a team (Better Together).
  5. An interest in weather and climate science.

The panel may perform a preliminary sift of the lead criteria as indicated above.

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £27,170, Met Office contributes £7,871 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

Our work is life-changing, often lifesaving and always life-enhancing. The Met Office is a Great Place to Work UK certified. We are also featured on their ‘Best Workplaces in Tech’ 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026 lists, as well as their ’54 Best Workplaces for Women’ 2023 list.

Your package includes:

  • Your salary will be £27,170
  • Annual Leave starting at 27.5 days
  • Access to discounted shopping, inclusive of retail, leisure and lifestyle brands

Whilst this is a temporary position until July 2028, there may be an opportunity to apply for our Graduate Development scheme upon completion of your university studies. However, this is not guaranteed and would be subject to programme availability and a successful application.

Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. We recommend candidates use the CARL method (Context, Action, Result and Learning) for presenting evidence of experience and skills. Please also look at the Early Careers Programmes Application Guidance at the bottom of this advert.

About the job

Job summary

IMPORTANT - This vacancy is using the Civil Service Numerical and Verbal tests. The deadline for completing the tests is the same as the vacancy closing date. Please ensure you complete the tests with sufficient time to complete the written application.

As an interaction Designer at the Apprenticeship service, you will be a confident and competent designer who can develop designs based on evidence of user needs and organisational outcomes. You will work out the best ways to let users interact with our services, both in terms of the overall user journey and at the level of individual design elements. You will join our growing User-Centred Design Team, reporting to the Senior Interaction Designer and collaborating with other interaction designers, content designers, user researchers, and service designers.

Job description

An interaction designer is a confident and competent designer who can develop designs based on evidence of user needs and organisational outcomes.

At this role level, you will:

  • Design and prototype high-quality user interfaces aligned to user needs and business goals
  • Interpret research and data to make informed design decisions
  • Collaborate across disciplines to shape end-to-end service experiences
  • Ensure designs meet strict accessibility standards and inclusive design principles
  • Contribute to and help maintain design systems, patterns and components
  • Communicate design decisions clearly and influence stakeholders
  • Manage and iterate designs independently within agile teams

Person specification

Essential Criteria:

It is essential that you can demonstrate the following:

  • Strong prototyping skills across multiple fidelities including wireframes, Figma and code using HTML, CSS and JavaScript
  • Working knowledge of GitHub or version control systems
  • Ability to use research and data to drive design decisions
  • Confident stakeholder communication and facilitation skills
  • Experience designing accessible services (WCAG and inclusive design)
  • Experience contributing to design systems, components and patterns
  • Ability to work effectively in agile, multidisciplinary teams

Desirable Criteria:

It is desirable if you can demonstrate the following:

  • Strong analytical skills to identify and resolve service design issues
  • Experience measuring design impact and outcomes

Desirable criteria will only be assessed at interview, in the event of a tie break situation, to make an informed decision.

Behaviours

We'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:

  • Working Together
  • Delivering at Pace
  • Making Effective Decisions

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £44,305, Department for Education contributes £12,835 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

Applicants currently holding a permanent post in the Civil Service should note that, if successful, their salary on appointment would be determined by the Department’s transfer / promotion policies.

As a member of the DfE, you will be entitled to join the highly competitive Civil Service Pension Scheme, which many experts agree is one of the most generous in the UK.

You will have 25 days leave, increasing by 1 day every year to a maximum of 30 days after five years’ service. In addition, all staff receive the King’s Birthday privilege holiday and 8 days’ bank and public holidays.

We offer flexible working arrangements, such as job sharing, term-time working, flexi-time and compressed hours.

Most DfE employees will be working a hybrid pattern, spending at least 60% of their time in an office or work setting. Changes to these working arrangements are available in exceptional circumstances but must be agreed with the line manager and in line with the requirements of the role.

Travel to your primary office location will not be paid for by DfE, but costs for travel to an office which is not your main location will be covered.

Part‑time hours available, from a minimum of 0.8 FTE.

As an organisation, which exists to support education and lifelong learning, we offer our staff excellent professional development opportunities.

Things you need to know

Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Selection process details

This vacancy is using Success Profiles (opens in a new window), and will assess your Behaviours, Strengths and Experience.

Stage 1: Civil Service Numerical Test (CSNT)

When you have completed your personal information, you will be asked to complete the CSNT. You must achieve the minimum pass mark to progress to the next stage.

Stage 2: Civil Service Verbal Test (CSVT)

When you have completed the CSNT, you will be asked to complete the CSVT. You must achieve the minimum pass mark to progress to the next stage.

Stage 3: Written Application

To apply for this role you will be asked to provide:

  • Your CV, which should include details of your employment history including the roles held and the skills and experience gained from those roles.
  • Your personal statement, which should be no longer than 750 words and display how your experience meets the essential criteria of the role (listed in the person specification section above).

More guidance on personal statements can be found here – completing your application.

Stage 4: Sift

We reserve the right to increase the minimum pass mark for the CSNT and CSVT where there is a high volume of applications or a particularly strong field of candidates. Where this occurs, candidates who do not meet the revised pass mark will not progress further, and their written application will not be assessed.

Applications will be sifted by a panel who will assess the evidence provided against the essential criteria listed in the advert. The evidence included in the CV and statement will be evaluated in line with the DfE Design Skills Framework, including:

  • Iterative design
  • Evidence-based design
  • Designing together
  • Design communication
  • Design for everyone
  • Leading design

In the event of a large volume of applications, the sift will be restricted to just assessing personal statements.

Stage 5: Interview

Candidates who are successful at sift will be invited to a 2-part interview process, typically held on the same day. This will last up to 2 hours.

Part 1: Technical Assessment

The first stage is a technical design assessment, led by a Senior Interaction Designer.

Format:

  • 40-minute practical task, assessed against the first essential criteria
  • Followed by up to 10-minute discussion
  • Followed by a 10-minute break before Part 2

Part 2: Interview questions

This part of the interview will involve two types of questions – Behaviour-based and Strength-based.

Strengths are a way for Hiring Managers to understand what motivates you and what you enjoy doing, which helps the panel to understand your areas of strength. Evidence shows that people do better work when a job aligns well with what they enjoy and find motivating. We don’t advertise which strengths we are going to assess you on as we want to be able to assess your first, natural response to the questions.

Behaviours are the actions and activities that people do which result in effective performance in a job. We want to get an understanding of the actions and activities that you have done (or would do) that result in effective performance.

We will assess you against the following behaviours during the selection process:

  • Working Together
  • Delivering at Pace
  • Making Effective Decisions

Important Information

If you fail to complete the tests before the deadline, your application will be withdrawn. Guidance will be available when you are invited to take the test. The tests are untimed, administered via Civil Service Jobs, and applicant guidance is available during the test and online on GOV.UK Online Tests guidance.

Applicants must complete the test on their own, without help, and Departments reserve the right to retest applicants under supervised conditions at later stages of the selection process. Please ensure you allow yourself sufficient time to complete both assessments and submit your application before the advertised deadline.

More information about online tests can be found here: Preparing for the Civil Service Verbal and Numerical tests - GOV.UK. You will also find practice tests on this page if you would find them helpful prior to completing the live test.

Other Information

Interviews may be via Microsoft teams or face to face; the vacancy manager will confirm prior to the Interview.

In your application, please don’t include personal information that identifies you.

This means we can recruit based on your knowledge and skills, and not background, gender or ethnicity - it's called name blind recruitment (opens in a new window).

  • age

  • email address

  • phone number
  • nationality/immigration status

Please be aware that this role can only be worked in the UK from the location options provided and not from overseas.

The government is committed to supporting apprenticeships, enabling people to learn and progress in a role whilst earning. Your response to this question will not affect your application and it is not a requirement of the role to have completed a previous apprenticeship.
