title: Manchester Digital Campus, Deputy Information and Documents Manager
location: Birmingham, Bristol, Cardiff, Leeds, Manchester, Nottingham, Swindon The MDC team are all expected to have a significant presence in Manchester (averaging at least 2-days a week). Regular travel is expected
description:
• Job grade: Senior Executive Officer
  • Contract type: Permanent, Loan
  • Length of employment: All MDC roles are being offered on a choice of permanent or initial 2 year loan basis to allow you to retain an initial link with your home department if preferable. The programme completes in 2032.
  • Business area: GPA - Capital Projects - MDC
  • Type of role: Administration / Corporate Support, Business Management and Improvement, Governance, Information Technology, Knowledge and Information Management, Policy, Project Delivery
  • Working pattern: Full-time
  • Number of jobs available: 1

Location

Birmingham, Bristol, Cardiff, Leeds, Manchester, Nottingham, Swindon
The MDC team are all expected to have a significant presence in Manchester (averaging at least 2-days a week). Regular travel is expected to attend GPA offices, and partner locations, especially London and occasionally Birmingham.

The role involves hybrid working with an expectation of office/meeting attendance on three days a week or more as the project demands.

About the job

Job summary

The Government Property Agency is the largest property holder in government, with more than £2.1 billion in property assets and over 55% of the government’s office estate.

We are transforming the way the Civil Service works by creating great places to work, leading the largest commercial office programme in the UK, working towards halving carbon emissions from government offices, and achieving greater value for taxpayers. And we are looking for innovative, solutions-focused people to join our team.

Representing the best covenant in the UK – His Majesty’s Government – we are leading significant transformational programmes. We are also delivering cost-effective property services such as asset management, lifecycle replacement and workplace services.

Innovation and progress underpin our behaviours. We foster a culture of lifelong learning, where curiosity and self-improvement are encouraged. Our four core values are at the heart of everything we do. They shape our culture and guide how we work, lead and grow together:

  • Striving for excellence- We always aim to deliver great results
  • Empowering through respect- We insist on fair treatment for all, always
  • Acting with integrity- We consistently do the right thing
  • Succeeding together- We rely on each other to achieve success

We are committed to representing the communities we serve by making Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion (EDI) part of everything we do. Our strong emphasis on EDI is not just about driving inclusion across our organisation, it is also about ensuring our services meet the needs of government departments and the civil servants who use our spaces. To ensure that we are always recruiting and retaining a diverse mix of talent, we are particularly inviting applications from candidates who are disabled, ethnically or gender diverse, and people who identify as being part of the LGBTQ+ community.

Join our dynamic and diverse team that leads with purpose, improving sustainability, nurturing social value, driving inclusivity and flexibility, and kickstarting economic growth. We are driven by purpose, and you can be part of it too: where you make a meaningful impact; where you influence; where your voice really matters; where you help to shape our future direction.

Job description

The Manchester Digital Campus (MDC) is part of the Government’s Major Projects Portfolio (GMPP), and is an exciting transformation across multiple Government departments, with significant ministerial, public, industrial and media interest. MDC is GPA’s biggest delivery programme yet.

The campus will comprise of two Government Hubs, built on a 5.5acre brownfield site in central Manchester. It will become a vibrant workplace for well over 8,000 people (including ministers and senior officials) from the digitally focused departments. The new, bespoke buildings will be designed to support the transformation objectives, collaborative working across government and with industry, academia and the local community. MDC will strengthen HMG’s skills, innovation and enable multi-department careers, whilst learning from and contributing to the exciting digital/AI sector in Manchester and the North West. It will directly support economic growth, skills, Civil Service reform (PAS) and the UN Sustainable Development Goals. It is an exciting vision!

MDC is overseen by its policy sponsors (including Places for Growth and Government Digital/Data – in Cabinet Office and DCMS) and delivered by the GPA, together with the Departmental Partners transforming to use the new site. Having completed our Outline Business Case approval, and approaching our RIBA3 milestone (design complete), we are expanding the dedicated MDC team to match the growing workload. The MDC team is multi-disciplinary and all are dedicated to and passionate about our amazing programme. We pride ourselves on our inclusivity, curiosity to explore and solve problems, our openness to challenge and our commitment to delivering what's needed for the Civil Service’s future.

SC is the minimum vetting requirement to start in MDC posts. MDC may subsequently offer the opportunity to sponsor your DV application in specific roles.

If you are interested at all in this role, but have a question, do please reach out.

As the Manchester Digital Campus (MDC) develops, you will play a pivotal leadership role in establishing robust information governance and security standards, ensuring the programme realises its objectives effectively.

As Deputy Information and Documents Manager (Deputy IDM), you will be at the heart of a major government programme, driving integration across all workstreams and taking end-to-end ownership of the secure management and strategic governance of critical data and information assets throughout the lifecycle of the project.

MDC uses electronic document management systems (EDRMS) to store and exchange OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE information. You will provide strategic oversight to assure that data and information is securely generated, stored, and shared across networks and between partners and supply chains. This includes managing client requirements, and setting standards for information management across the design, build, and operational transition phases of the project.

As part of a supportive, collaborative team, you will engage with senior managers across the programme to champion information governance and influence key stakeholders to maintain rigorous security compliance. You will act as an authoritative lead, guiding decision-making, proactively mitigating risks, and adapting information frameworks to match the changing and expanding needs of the MDC programme.

You will report to the MDC Information and Documents Manager and have line management responsibility for an HEO Document Controller, collectively ensuring robust information governance and assurance across the entire MDC programme.

Key Responsibilities

  • Day-to-day management of data and information to ensure it’s appropriately and securely received, stored, organised, retrieved and distributed.
  • Engage with senior stakeholders to coordinate training and action plans in line with the project schedule and subject to audit compliance.
  • Deliver regular information handling inductions and briefings to GPA teams, delivery partners, and supply chain contractors, to ensure the correct and controlled management of and access to secure information .
  • Line manage one HEO.
  • Administer the MDC document control systems and maintain the security of sensitive documents, including commercial and financial information.
  • Securely receive, store, maintain, and distribute data and information between stakeholders.
  • Establish and maintain document control workflows to ensure correct and up-to-date procedures for safe data and information exchange.
  • Manage user accounts and control access to the secure repositories.
  • Perform regular compliance checks to ensure all documents and records are correctly stored and referenced, acting as the department’s Library Manager and assisting Corporate Services.
  • Quality assure documents for accuracy, completeness and compliance.
  • Report any breach immediately and where appropriate escalate.

Person specification

  • Self-starter, willingness to help others and challenge
  • Able to engage with a wide range of stakeholders

We encourage applications from people from all backgrounds and aim to have a workforce that represents the communities and wider society that we serve. We pride ourselves on being an employer of choice. We champion diversity, inclusion and wellbeing and aim to create a sense of belonging in a workplace where everyone feels valued.

Experience & Technical Skills

Desirable criteria:

  • Experience in managing a document lifecycle using an EDRMS system
  • Understanding of 19650-2
  • Experience in data analysis and data quality checks
  • Experience working in a project / programme environment

title: Litigation Assistant
location: Jersey City, New Jersey, United States
description:
At Morgan & Morgan, the work we do matters. For millions of Americans, we’re their last line of defense against insurance companies, large corporations or defective goods. From attorneys in all 50 states, to client support staff, creative marketing to operations teams, every member of our firm has a key role to play in the winning fight for consumer rights. Our over 6,000 employees are all united by one mission: For the People.

Summary

We are seeking a qualified Litigation Assistant to join our team. As a Litigation Assistant, you will be responsible for managing the law firm's day-to-day operations, including carrying out administrative services and supporting the legal team. This position's ideal candidate has a strong work ethic, exceptional problem-solving skills, and comfortable working in a fast-paced dynamic workplace.

Responsibilities

  • Perform administrative duties (scheduling calendar hearings and deadlines, organize case files, manage logistics)
  • Maintain pleadings and discovery indexes
  • Organize exhibits, documents, evidence, briefs, and appendices
  • Implement and improve upon administrative processes for more efficient workflow.
  • Collect, examine, and organize evidence and other legal documents for attorney review and case preparation
  • Draft and proofread correspondence and legal documents, such as pleadings and contracts
  • Research regulations, laws, and legal articles to assist with the preparation of reports, case files, and legal advice
  • Manage client billing by preparing, finalizing, and sending out bills, as well as resolving billing issues in cooperation with the billing attorney
  • Communicate with clients and witnesses to schedule meetings, interviews, and depositions
  • Manage, organize, and maintain documents in paper or electronic filing systems
  • Performs other related duties as assigned to meet the needs of the business

Qualification

  • High school diploma or general education degree (GED) required
  • Associates degree in paralegal studies, a paralegal certificate, or a bachelor's degree is preferred
  • Bilingual English and Spanish (preferred)
  • At least 2 years of experience as an administrative assistant (preferably in a law firm or in a corporate legal department), legal assistant, legal secretary, or paralegal
  • Experience in Personal Injury, WC, Premises, or other injury related practice areas. (preferred)
  • Must possess the ability to multi-task, prioritize, handle a fast-paced environment, and manage workload with a great attitude and minimal supervision
  • Great written and communication skills, be proficient in calendar depositions, mediation, and hearings
  • Applicable knowledge of motions, discovery, evidence, litigation documentation, court rules, and procedures, practices, etc.
  • Highly organized with the ability to juggle multiple deadlines in a fast-paced environment
  • Strong writing and communication skills along with attention to detail
  • Extensive computer and database expertise, Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, and type no less than 35 wpm
  • Remote and/or hybrid not eligible

#LI-AP2

$30—$30 USD

Benefits

Morgan & Morgan is a leading personal injury law firm dedicated to protecting the people, not the powerful. This success starts with our staff. For full-time employees, we offer an excellent benefits package including medical and dental insurance, 401(k) plan, paid time off and paid holidays.

Every horizon. Every mission. Every day.

title: Senior Internet Intelligence & Investigations Officer
description:
• Job grade: Senior Executive Officer
  • Contract type: Permanent
  • Type of role: Analytical, Digital, Information Technology, Intelligence, Investigation
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time, Part-time
  • Number of jobs available: 1

Location

London

About the job

Job summary

Are you an experienced intelligence professional with the skills to uncover critical insights in an increasingly complex digital world? The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) is seeking a Senior Internet Intelligence & Investigations (III) Officer to join our specialist Internet Investigations Laboratory, the CMA's Centre of Excellence for Internet Intelligence & Investigations.

In this influential role, you will lead the delivery of high-quality intelligence products derived from both open and closed online sources, supporting some of the CMA's most impactful work across competition enforcement, consumer protection, digital markets and market studies. Combining advanced digital tradecraft, innovative investigative tools and strategic insight, you'll help drive evidence-based decision making and deliver meaningful outcomes for consumers and businesses across the UK.

As a senior member of the team, you will play a key role in shaping the CMA's internet intelligence capabilities, advancing the use of Open Source Intelligence (OSINT), and exploring the opportunities presented by emerging technologies and AI. Working closely with colleagues across the organisation, you will contribute to the development of cutting-edge investigative approaches and strengthen the UK's wider intelligence capability.

This is a unique opportunity to apply your expertise in a role that combines strategic leadership, technical innovation and operational impact. Your work will support the CMA's mission to promote competition, protect consumers and foster economic growth, while helping ensure the organisation's priorities are delivered with efficiency, clarity, balance and transparency.

About the CMA

The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) is the UK’s principal competition and consumer protection authority. We promote competition and protect consumers with a clear end goal in mind: to drive economic growth and improve household prosperity. The CMA has a range of powers, which it uses to undertake a wide variety of cutting-edge, high profile and complex work, spanning merger and market inquiries, competition and consumer law enforcement, our role in the digital markets competition regime, subsidy advice, and internal market advice.

You can read more about working at the CMA including our office locations in our candidate pack

Job description

As a Senior Internet Intelligence & Investigations (III) Officer, you will act as the lead intelligence specialist on high-profile cases and strategic projects, delivering sophisticated online investigations and intelligence products that support the CMA's work across competition enforcement, consumer protection, digital markets and market studies. Working closely with case teams and senior stakeholders, you'll ensure intelligence insights are delivered at critical points in the investigative lifecycle, helping to inform operational decisions and deliver successful outcomes.

As a recognised subject matter expert, you will evaluate emerging technologies, develop new investigative methodologies, and champion the use of advanced OSINT and digital investigation techniques. You'll collaborate with colleagues across the CMA, UK Government, law enforcement and international partners, sharing expertise and representing the CMA's Internet Intelligence capability through briefings, training and specialist advice. Your work will help shape the future direction of III and contribute to wider government thinking on digital investigations and intelligence.

Beyond delivering intelligence, you will play a key role in building organisational capability by providing technical leadership, coaching and oversight to junior colleagues. You'll help maintain specialist software, hardware and virtual environments, support the development of policies and best practice, and ensure intelligence activity is accurately recorded and managed. The role involves acquiring and analysing information from a diverse range of digital environments, including websites, restricted-access platforms, mobile devices, computers, gaming consoles and emerging technologies, ensuring the CMA remains at the forefront of modern digital investigations.

Person specification

It is essential that you can provide evidence and examples for each of the following selection criteria in your application. For tips on how to make the most your application, please have a look at our guidance document.

Essential Criteria

  • Extensive experience with the application of OSINT specific toolsets, platforms, scripts and web extensions used in III work. Technical knowledge of the structure of the Internet and websites, including knowledge of emerging technologies used in the OSINT sphere with the ability to generate and modify scripts - particularly Python (Lead Criteria).
  • Extensive practice in conducting and leading in OSINT or internet-based investigations within a specialist intelligence/investigation environment with proven ability to make logical and timely decisions, cutting through complexity and seeing the big picture to achieve outcomes (Lead Criteria).
  • Strong relationship management skills to build and maintain effective working relationships within the team and other business units.
  • Extensive experience of conducting and overseeing complex OSINT tasking, including identifying and managing associated operational risks and assessing the relevance, reliability and value of information obtained from online sources – including data from web scraped information.
  • Strong analytical skills and ability to produce clear, actionable intelligence reports.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to produce documents that can be tailored to a wide variety of audiences and brief stakeholders across all levels of seniority.
  • Ability to effectively prioritise competing demands, work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment and deliver high-quality outcomes in a fast-paced and constantly changing environment.
  • Understanding of relevant related legislation parameters, for example, Human Rights Act 1998 (HRA 1998), Regulation of Investigatory Powers Act 2000 (RIPA 2000), General Data Protection Regulation 2016 (GDPR), UK Data Protection Act 2018 (DPA) and Guidance on Internet Intelligence & Investigations (NPCC).

      We'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:

      • Making Effective Decisions
      • Communicating and Influencing
      • Working Together
      • Changing and Improving
      • Developing Self and Others

      Technical skills

      We'll assess you against these technical skills during the selection process:

      • Data collection
      • Python Scripting (within Internet Investigations)

      Benefits

      Alongside your salary of £49,400, Competition & Markets Authority contributes £14,311 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

      You’ll also get:

      • 25 days leave (increasing to 30 days over five years), plus 8 public holidays and an additional day off for the King’s birthday. In addition, you’ll be able to access a wide range of other types of leave as and when you need it, including generous maternity, paternity, shared parental leave and adoption options, as well as paid special leave for volunteering.
      • Access to our benefits platform which includes retail discounts, cycle to work scheme and payroll giving. Employees can also sign up for season ticket loans.
      • Access to the Civil Service Sports & Leisure, giving discounted gym membership, high street discounts, free access to UK wide attractions and a free Tastecard.
      • A range of wellbeing benefits, including an employee assistance programme, flu vaccinations and eye tests. We also have flexible working options and family friendly policies.

      You can read more about our benefits in our candidate pack.

      Our Values

      We are Ambitious and Evidence-based, and always strive for Excellence.​ We treat everyone with Respect and are Collaborative and Inclusive.​

      Everything we do is underpinned by the Civil Service values: Honesty, Integrity, Impartiality and Objectivity.

      You can read more about life at the CMA in our candidate pack.

      Artificial intelligence

      Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

      Selection process details

      This vacancy is using Success Profiles (opens in a new window), and will assess your Behaviours, Experience and Technical skills.

      Application and sift stage

      • As part of the application process you will be asked to complete a CV, personal statement and an online application form. Further details about application requirements are listed on the application form.
      • In addition, candidates will also need to provide answers to the following 3 questions. Responses must not exceed 500 words.

      1. Provide an example of how you have applied technical knowledge, internet investigations tradecraft using OSINT specific toolsets (including the use of scripting) to solve a complex investigative problem.

      2. Describe a time when you took the lead an internet intelligence (OSINT) investigation in support of an operational, regulatory, enforcement or intelligence objective.

      3. Describe a time when you were responsible for delivering internet intelligence support throughout the lifecycle of a case, project or investigation involving multiple stakeholders.

      • At the sift stage, your application (CV, personal statement and above questions) will be reviewed and assessed against the essential criteria listed under the Person Specification of the role profile.
      • Please note that it is essential that your personal statement is aligned to provide evidence that you have the knowledge and experience for each of the essential criteria (as included on the role profile attached and listed above under 'Person Specification') in your application. Your personal statement should be no more than 1250 words.

These vacancies are Residential Worker annualised hours working pattern, with the opportunity to work flexibly for either 625 or 1250 hours per year, the equivalent of one or two 12 hour shifts each week. Approved Premises - Residential Worker

Helping to keep the public safe. Giving people the chance to turn their lives around. Building a rewarding professional career. It’s an extraordinary role. There are many reasons to join the Probation Service. What will yours be?

About Approved Premises

Approved Premises are primarily for offenders who have been released on licence and who require a high level of supervision.

About the role

As a residential worker in an Approved Premises, you will play a crucial role in supporting the management of offenders in their transition from custody into the community, to achieve successful resettlement. You will assist with the well-being and supervision of Approved Premises residents, helping them to stick to their license conditions and supporting them to keep themselves and others safe. You will carry out inspections, monitor behaviour and positively engage with residents, working closely with colleagues and partner agencies.

The role will entail working at one main Approved Premise with the requirement to work across additional sites should the need arise.

Residential Workers are required to work regular unsocial hours which attract premium rates of pay in addition to advertised annual salary.

  • Monday to Friday: 7pm to 8am premium payment of 30%
  • Weekend: 8am Saturday – 8am Monday premium payment of 50%
  • Public/Bank Holidays :8am to 8am premium payment of 50%: in addition, time off in lieu for actual hours worked is applicable

Overview of the approved premises role - Prison and Probation Jobs

You do not need a degree for this role. We are much more interested in your personal qualities. Ideally, with experience of working with people who have social or personal difficulties, you will be empathetic, patient, and resilient. A good level of numeracy and literacy is also required as the role involves some report writing.

The Probation Service works with offenders who are pre-release or post-release from prison or serving community sentences. Our role is to support their rehabilitation and protect the public. People come from all walks of life to form one team in the Probation Service.​ Join us and you will be part of a supportive team that thrives on sharing knowledge and expertise.

description:

At Whitehorse City Council, community is at the heart of everything we do. To stay ahead of and best respond to the evolving changes and needs of the community, the organisation is undertaking an exciting journey that will transform ways of working and will empower employees to be innovative and constantly striving towards providing excellent customer experience at all times. The five pillars of our organisation focus on:

  • Excellent Customer Experience and Service Delivery
  • Great Organisational Culture
  • Innovation and Continuous Improvement
  • Good Governance and Integrity
  • Long Term Financial Sustainability

A fantastic opportunity exists for a motivated and enthusiastic team player to join the City Services Department. The successful applicant will be provided with training and will work within a supportive team environment.

The role:

The role involves performing a range of maintenance works including asphalting, stormwater drainage maintenance, installation and repair of signage and roadside furniture.

You will carry out regular inspections of Council’s road network and undertake various maintenance activities in accordance with Council’s Road Management Plan as well as working in accordance with the OHS Act and Council’s OHS Policies to provide a safe working environment.

About you:

To be considered for this position you will have:

  • Hands on experience in maintenance works and ideally experience in asphalting, drain cleaning, minor concrete construction
  • Good verbal and written communication skills.
  • An ability to deal with all parties including the general public in a courteous manner and to resolve minor problems with residents, traders and contractors.
  • An ability to work as part of team and support team objectives.
  • A flexible approach and ability to respond to changing work methods, equipment and procedures.

In return, we will offer:

The ability to make a difference - Working at Whitehorse City Council you contribute to making a real difference in the lives of the community and those that live, learn, work or visit Whitehorse. Every day you really will see how the work you're involved in benefits the diverse community.

Great working conditions – a professional environment, friendly and supportive teams and a flexibility program that promotes employee work life balance.

An extensive Health and Wellbeing offering – Employee assistance program, private health insurance benefits, health checks (skin, hearing and vaccinations), discounted gym membership and facilities (e.g. Theatre, Arts, Leisure) and an active health and wellness program (e.g. stretching, healthy eating demonstrations and health challenges.

Career opportunities – engaging work and the opportunity to apply your skills and experience.

Transformation - We are in a time of transformation to stay ahead of the evolving changes and needs of our community. Together, we are on an exciting journey to empower all of our employees to be innovative, and constantly strive towards continuous improvement.

Reward & Recognition - extensive reward and recognition program, corporate learning offerings, study assistance and comprehensive leadership development programs.

Further Information

Further information is available from Arthur Makris on 9262 6205. To apply, please submit a copy of your resume (max 5 pages) and one page statement addressing the selection criteria and what you would bring to the role by Sunday 8 November 2026.

Infrastructure Maintenance Officer

City of Whitehorse is a culturally and linguistically diverse community. We are proud of the diversity of our workforce and recognise the strength this provides in meeting the needs of our community. We are committed to upholding a safe, inclusive and respectful workplace that values the contribution of all.

Whitehorse City Council is committed to being a child safe organisation. We recognise our responsibilities to keep children and young people safe from harm and have established policies, procedures and training to achieve these commitments.

ABOUT US

The City of Whitehorse, located 15 kilometres east of the Melbourne CBD, is a culturally diverse community of almost 177,000 people. Whitehorse includes the suburbs of Box Hill, Burwood, Nunawading, Blackburn, Mitcham, Forest Hill and Vermont and is characterised by quiet tree-lined residential streets, an abundance of parks, gardens and natural bushland reserves, bustling shopping centres and a diverse range of arts, cultural, sports and leisure facilities.

Whitehorse City Council provides more than 100 services and facilities across a range of areas within our community services, city development, infrastructure, corporate services and transformation directorates. Whitehorse is one of Melbourne’s largest metropolitan councils with a workforce of approximately 1300 employees and aspires to foster an inclusive, vibrant, prosperous and sustainable community. Our employees help us achieve these goals!

At Whitehorse, employee health, wellbeing and development are paramount, and we aim for everyone to become the best they can be in the workplace. Benefits of working with us include:

  • Salary sacrifice options for gym / swim memberships, childcare and superannuation; and access to novated vehicle leases.
  • Competitive terms and conditions of employment
  • Ample onsite parking at most facilities with ready access to public transport

About the job

Job summary

About the role...

The Research Manager role is part of an ambitious, multidisciplinary team that delivers high-quality research and analysis to help the Agency address knowledge gaps and make evidence-led decisions.

Playing a crucial role in supporting the team, the role will:

• Support the delivery of the team's research programme, contributing to both established analytical products and exploratory research projects, and applying own initiative to identify and develop new insights.

• Support the production and continuous development of the team's market insight products, including market overviews and forecasts, using complex data analysis, interpretation and written reporting to generate robust and actionable insights.

• Undertake research and analysis across a broad range of economic, housing market, finance and place-based topics, from national trends and forecasts to localised projects, as well as sub-sector trends (Build to Rent, SME development, affordable housing, emerging tenures and other priority sectors where the Agency invests), generating insights that support the Agency's strategic decision-making.

Job description

• Apply critical thinking and analytical judgement to explore, interpret and quality assure complex datasets, identifying and resolving methodological, data quality and analytical issues.

• Contribute to a varied programme of research projects, including exploratory and data discovery work, using a range of methods such as statistical analysis, literature reviews, stakeholder engagement and evidence synthesis.

• Translate complex findings into clear, concise and accessible insights through reports, briefings, presentations and other communications for a range of stakeholders, including senior colleagues.

• Support the development and continuous improvement of the Agency's self-service insight products and analytical resources, helping colleagues access and use data and evidence effectively.

• Build effective and collaborative working relationships with colleagues and stakeholders across the Agency, contributing expertise and insight to achieve shared objectives.

The role will support the wider team to complete their outputs to the highest standard, working collaboratively and supportively across the wider Research, Economics and Geospatial (REG) function.

Person specification

About you…

You’ll have existing experience or interest in UK or European real estate research. Specialist knowledge of the UK housing development or investment markets would be an added benefit.

You'll be interested in regeneration and housing and ambitious in delivering high-quality research and analysis. Additionally, you’ll have experience delivering commercially-focussed research and insight programmes.

You'll be resilient and used to "spinning several plates" at once with demonstrable experience of working across teams and managing internal and external stakeholders in a collaborative, inclusive way.

You’ll be able to synthesise complex concepts and findings and communicate them effectively to stakeholders with varying levels of technical expertise.

You'll be comfortable working on a range of projects as well as helping the team to implement our varied and exciting research and analysis programme – all to ensure the agency's decision making is informed by market evidence and empirically sound, helping to deliver maximum value for money.

We are a government agency working in partnership with the private sector and want to employ and retain great people. In return we offer a range of excellent benefits, some of the key benefits include:

Holiday - Homes England offers all staff 33 days annual leave per year in addition to 8 statutory bank holidays.

Working Flexibly - At Homes England we have a strong culture of flexible working and encourage all employees to have a healthy work/life balance. We offer a wide range of potential working patterns, including part time, job share and compressed hours.

Health and Wellbeing - We offer health screening with Nuffield Proactive Health Clinics, a free Employee Assistance Programme which offers confidential support 24 hours a day, 7 days a week as well as access to Occupational Health.

Professional Development - At Homes England we are committed to your continued professional and personal development with learning as one of our core values. We pay for one job-related professional membership subscription per year for our employees.

We also offer an excellent range of family friendly benefits, for example, maternity, paternity, shared parental leave.

title: Defence Nuclear Organisation - Nuclear Fuels Programme – Radioactive Material Packaging Project Manager
description:
• Job grade: Senior Executive Officer
  • Contract type: Permanent
  • Business area: MOD - Defence Nuclear - DNO
  • Type of role: Project Delivery
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time, Compressed hours
  • Number of jobs available: 1

Location

MOD Abbey Wood, Bristol

About the job

Job summary

The Defence Nuclear Organisation (DNO) is responsible for the provision of the nuclear deterrent, encompassing our submarines and nuclear warheads, while also advising on UK nuclear planning and fostering international co-operation on nuclear matters. With a multidisciplinary team of over 700 professionals, the DNO brings together expertise in science, engineering, finance, policy, programme delivery, and more. We work in partnership with the Royal Navy, the Submarine Delivery Agency and the Atomic Weapons Establishment as the Defence Nuclear Enterprise (DNE).

Here at DNO we strongly believe that diversity and inclusion is not only the right thing to do but is also essential for a thriving and successful organisation. We have a culture where differences are celebrated, and our people feel supported, included and empowered. Join us and be part of an organisation that truly values diversity and inclusion and makes a positive impact on the world.

The Nuclear Fuels Programme (NFP) sits within the newly established 3* area within the DNO. The programme’s purpose is to re-establish a nuclear fuel cycle for reactor fuel for defence purposes, underpinning the UK’s nuclear deterrent. The programme operates as a blended team of MOD civil servants, UKGI, and external specialists, working across multiple locations and in partnership with industry, regulators and international stakeholders. This role sits within a high-profile, sensitive and strategically important programme, delivered within a complex and highly regulated environment.

The NFP Radioactive Material Packaging Project Manager will lead the planning, acquisition and through-life management of specialist transport packaging required to support the safe and compliant movement of materials. The role will bring together project delivery, logistics and regulatory considerations, translating complex technical requirements into practical delivery plans.

This is an opportunity to take ownership of a specialist and strategically important area of delivery, influence emerging plans and help establish an enduring capability within a growing programme.

This post is advertised at 37 hours per week.

Job description

As the Radioactive Material Packaging Project Manager, you will lead the development and delivery of the programme’s approach to specialist transport packaging for a range of uranium products across the nuclear fuel cycle. You will act as the programme’s focal point for packaging requirements, bringing together technical, regulatory, commercial and delivery considerations to ensure that suitable solutions are available when needed.

You will work with internal and external specialists to evaluate packaging options, plan future demand and manage the acquisition, certification, testing and through-life management of packaging. You will also provide clear reporting and advice to senior leaders, supporting informed decisions and effective management of delivery risks, issues and dependencies.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Managing the through-life stewardship of transport packaging, including maintenance, reuse, inventory management, refurbishment, disposal and end-of-life disposition.
  • Developing and maintaining the programme’s transport packaging strategy, covering both on-site and off-site movements.
  • Defining, managing and maintaining packaging requirements across the programme lifecycle.
  • Assessing material characteristics and operational requirements to identify suitable, compliant packaging solutions.
  • Developing the packaging demand forecast, including package quantities, availability and inventory management.
  • Leading the acquisition and delivery of specialist transport packaging, working with commercial colleagues, suppliers and technical specialists.
  • Managing packaging certification, testing and regulatory approval arrangements.
  • Integrating packaging activity with wider programme schedules, delivery plans and dependencies.
  • Identifying and managing packaging-related risks, issues, assumptions and dependencies.
  • Engaging with regulators, assurance bodies, international authorities and logistics providers to support approvals and delivery.
  • Auditing and assuring supplier capability against relevant regulatory and programme requirements.
  • Producing and coordinating transport plans, regulatory submissions, risk assessments and logistics procedures.
  • Providing timely reporting, analysis, advice and decision support to senior programme leadership.
  • Advising programme teams and stakeholders on packaging requirements, regulatory responsibilities and through-life management considerations.
  • Maintaining awareness of relevant legislation, policy and regulation and assessing how changes may affect programme delivery.

NFP is a growing area operating within a dynamic and evolving environment. As the organisation develops, new priorities and responsibilities may emerge, and the post holder may be required to work flexibly across the area to support successful programme delivery.

Due to the pace of delivery and requirement for regular workplace attendance this role is not suitable for part-time or job share candidates.

Hybrid and flexible working can be considered for this post but will need regular workplace attendance due to security constraints. Candidates are encouraged to discuss options with the recruiting line manager before submitting an application.

This post is on the MOD Civilian Nuclear Post Control List (PCL) and may attract the Nuclear Recruitment and Retention Allowance (RRA). This is a discretionary allowance. The post being listed on the PCL does not mean that the post holder will have an automatic entitlement to receive the RRA. The NSQEP RRA is not a contractual allowance and can be amended or withdrawn without notice in line with MOD Main and Submarine Delivery Agency policy.

As the post holder will have access to very sensitive information, there are limitations on travelling to a small number of countries and we will undertake additional security checks as part of the recruitment process. Applications from candidates with close connections to certain countries may take considerably longer to process, or in some cases result in a withdrawal of an offer of employment. Further details will be provided at the conditional offer stage.

Person specification

We are looking for an organised and proactive project delivery professional who can bring structure and momentum to a technically complex area. You will be comfortable working across organisational boundaries, managing competing priorities and translating specialist information into clear plans, recommendations and decisions.

You do not need to be an expert in every aspect of the role from the outset. However, you will need relevant experience of delivering projects involving regulated, hazardous or technically complex activities, together with the ability to build effective relationships with technical specialists, suppliers and regulatory stakeholders.

Essential Skills: Experience of delivering projects involving radioactive material, hazardous materials or another comparably regulated and technically complex environment.

  • Demonstrable project delivery experience, including managing scope, schedule, cost, risk and dependencies.
  • Experience of working with technical specialists, suppliers, regulators or assurance bodies to deliver agreed outcomes.
  • Strong planning and organisational skills, with the ability to coordinate multiple activities and maintain delivery momentum.
  • The ability to analyse complex technical or regulatory information and turn it into clear recommendations, plans and decision-support material.
  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, including the confidence to influence across organisational and professional boundaries.
  • Experience of identifying and managing delivery risks, issues, assumptions and dependencies.
  • The ability to produce clear, accurate reporting and provide proportionate advice to senior stakeholders.

Essential Qualifications:

A recognised project management qualification, such as PRINCE2, APM or equivalent

Desirable Qualifications:

A qualification or accredited training relating to logistics, supply-chain management, dangerous goods or radioactive material transport.

  • Relevant nuclear-awareness or nuclear-safety training.
  • Training in the transport regulations applicable to radioactive or hazardous materials.

Desirable Skills:

  • Experience of radioactive material transport packaging or the movement of radioactive materials.
  • Knowledge of packaging certification, testing or regulatory approval arrangements.
  • Experience of transport and storage within a nuclear, defence, hazardous-material or similarly regulated environment.
  • Experience of international logistics, cross-border movements or working with international approval authorities.
  • Knowledge of relevant dangerous-goods or radioactive-material transport regulations.
  • Experience of managing specialist equipment or packaging inventories through their lifecycle.
  • Experience of supplier assurance, audits or assessments of technical delivery capability.

Qualifications

A recognised project management qualification, such as PRINCE2, APM or equivalent

Technical skills

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £46,040, Ministry of Defence contributes £13,337 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

About the job

Job summary

The Office for National Statistics (ONS) is the UK’s largest producer of official statistics, covering a range of key economic, social and demographic topics. These include measuring changes in the value of the UK economy, estimating the size, geographic distribution and characteristics of the population, and providing indicators of price inflation, employment, earnings, crime and migration.

This role supports the delivery of legal and data services across the UK Statistics Authority (the Authority), including the ONS and the Office for Statistics Regulation (OSR). The Authority is an independent body at arm’s length from government and has the statutory objective of promoting and safeguarding the production and publication of official statistics that ‘serve the public good’.

The Legal and Data Services (LDS) team provides expert guidance and operational support in areas such as legal advice, Freedom of Information (FOI), Data Protection, ethics, accreditation for the purposes of statistical research, and complaints handling. You will work within the LDS branch within the Strategy & Policy division. The branch plays a critical role in ensuring the organisation operates within legal frameworks, maintains public trust, and upholds high standards of transparency and accountability.

The primary focus for the LDS is to support the National Statistician, Permanent Secretary, senior executives, and the wider organisation to manage the governance of the access, use and sharing of data for research and statistical purposes, whilst ensuring compliance with relevant legislation.

Working within LDS, you will be part of a multidisciplinary team at the forefront of legal and data governance. You will provide practical and administrative support across a wide range of areas, including data ethics, Digital Economy Act accreditation, and other legal services. The role will see you supporting collaborative working and engagement with the National Statistician's Data Ethics Advisory Committee, the Research Accreditation Panel and the wider data research community.

This is a fast-paced and varied role, offering the opportunity to work flexibly across the LDS team.

Job description

Key Responsibilities

The Legal and Data Services Policy Assistant role will carry out a variety of supporting tasks which may include:

  • Coordinating communications with relevant stakeholders, management of correspondence and research tracking systems within the team.
  • Providing administrative and secretariat support for the National Statistician's Data Ethics Advisory Committee and the Research Accreditation Panel.
  • Support with the development of strong effective relationships with key stakeholders across the Authority and wider researcher community.
  • General branch support for the LDS team.

Person specification

Essential Criteria

  • Experience of operating flexibly and working at pace, planning and prioritising to meet tight and competing deadlines.
  • Possess excellent communication skills, with the ability to adapt communication appropriately to a diverse range of colleagues, stakeholders, and members of the public.
  • Able to work well alone, managing your own time and work as part of a team, encouraging the participation of others when necessary.

Across government, analytics engineering is playing an increasingly important role in transforming how organisations use data to inform decisions, deliver insight and enable digital services. By structuring, modelling and optimising data for analysis, analytics engineers ensure that data is accessible, reliable and aligned with business needs. Ofgem plays a vital role in the UK’s energy system, protecting consumers and enabling a more secure, fair and sustainable energy future, and strong analytics engineering capability is central to unlocking the value of data.

Ofgem is on an ambitious transformation journey. Within the Digital, Data and Security Services (DDSS) directorate, we are building modern data platforms and analytical capabilities that support data-driven decision-making across the organisation. As our data maturity grows, there is an increasing need to ensure that data is structured effectively, enabling analytics, AI and business intelligence at scale.

As a Lead Analytics Engineer, you will play a key role in shaping how data is structured, modelled and consumed across Ofgem. You will lead the design and implementation of analytical data models, working closely with stakeholders and multidisciplinary teams to ensure data supports both operational and strategic needs. You will define standards, drive best practice and contribute to the continuous improvement of data transformation and modelling processes.

This is a senior, hands-on technical role that combines data engineering, analytics and stakeholder engagement. You will work across complex data environments, ensuring that data is optimised for use while maintaining quality, consistency and governance.

Job description

You will be responsible for:

  • Leading the design, build and maintenance of analytical data models that support reporting, analytics, AI and business intelligence.
  • Working with stakeholders to understand business processes and translate requirements into effective data structures and models.
  • Developing and maintaining data transformation standards across platforms such as Azure Data Factory, Azure Synapse and related technologies.
  • Ensuring data quality, consistency and interoperability, enabling reuse and effective analysis across the organisation.
  • Collaborating with data engineers, data scientists and analysts to ensure alignment between platform design and analytical needs.
  • Driving continuous improvement in data modelling, transformation and analytics engineering practices.
  • Establishing and maintaining standards for documentation, ensuring transparency and maintainability of data solutions.
  • Supporting metadata management, ensuring that data assets are discoverable, well-defined and effectively governed.
  • Identifying and resolving issues within data pipelines and models, implementing preventative measures and optimisations.
  • Providing technical leadership and guidance to colleagues, promoting best practice and building capability across teams.

We are looking for:

A technically strong and analytically minded professional who can lead the development of robust, scalable data models in a modern cloud environment. You will bring experience in analytics engineering or data engineering, alongside the ability to work closely with stakeholders to deliver practical solutions.

You may come from a data engineering, analytics or BI background, but you will demonstrate:

  • Experience designing and optimising complex data models in a cloud-based environment
  • Strong experience with tools such as Azure Data Factory, Azure Synapse Analytics or equivalent platforms
  • Experience working with programming languages such as Python and SQL
  • Knowledge of data transformation, modelling and metadata management practices
  • The ability to balance technical design with business needs and stakeholder requirements
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to translate technical concepts into clear, actionable insights
  • Experience in government or regulated environments, and in supporting analytics, AI or business intelligence use cases, would be beneficial.

This is an opportunity to play a key role in shaping how Ofgem uses data to support decision-making and innovation. You will ensure that data is structured and accessible in a way that enables insight, driving value across the organisation at a time when data capability has never been more important.

Person specification

Essential Criteria

  • Knowledge and experience of optimising complex data models in a modern cloud environment (Lead Criteria)
  • Practical experience of working with OFGEMs primary toolset (e.g. Azure Data Factory, Azure Synapse Analytics) (Lead Criteria)
  • Knowledge and experience of continuous improvement techniques for complex systems
  • Experience of metadata management
  • Experience of coding programs, scripts and/or components for a complex platform/codebase using Python. Experience with SQL is desirable.

Desirable Criteria

  • Experience of communicating technical concepts in a non-technical language.

title: Sr Advanced Hardware Engineer
description:
As a Senior Advanced Test Hardware Engineer, you will be responsible for the architecture, design, development, integration, and qualification of electronic test hardware supporting new product introduction, verification, production, and repair operations. You will develop innovative test solutions for Circuit Card Assemblies (CCAs), Printed Board Assemblies (PBAs), subassemblies, and Line Replaceable Units (LRUs).

In this role, you will collaborate closely with Systems, Hardware, Software, Manufacturing, Quality, and Test Engineering teams to ensure robust, cost-effective, and scalable test solutions throughout the product lifecycle.

You will report directly to our Senior Engineering Manager and you’ll work out of our Phoenix, Arizona location on a hybrid work schedule. Note: For the first 90 days, New Hires must be prepared to work 100% onsite M-F.

• Design and develop test hardware for engineering development, qualification and production environments.
• Develop schematic designs and support PCB layout activities.
• Define test architectures for digital, analog, power, FPGA, and mixed-signal products.
• Support board bring-up, verification, validation, and troubleshooting activities.
• Drive Design for Testability (DFT) requirements into product development.
• Support Automated Test Equipment (ATE) integration and deployment.
• Collaborate with manufacturing and repair organizations to improve fault isolation and test coverage.
• Participate in technical reviews, root-cause investigations, and corrective action activities.
• Lead test hardware efforts across multiple concurrent development programs.
• Mentor junior engineers and provide technical leadership.

YOU MUST HAVE

  • Extensive experience in advanced hardware design and development for aerospace or related industries
  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in a technical discipline such as the sciences, technology, engineering or mathematics
  • Strong knowledge of schematic capture, PCB layout, and hardware validation techniques
  • Proficiency with hardware simulation and analysis tools to optimize design performance
  • Experience with aerospace industry standards and compliance requirements
  • Ability to lead complex hardware projects from concept through production
  • Experience designing electronic circuits and developing hardware verification solutions

WE VALUE

  • 7+ years of experience in hardware engineering with a focus on aerospace or high-reliability systems
  • Strong problem-solving skills and innovative mindset
  • Experience mentoring and leading engineering teams
  • Familiarity with emerging hardware technologies and industry trends
  • Experience designing test equipment for avionic, aerospace, defense, or safety-critical products.
  • Experience supporting qualifications and environmental testing.

U.S. PERSON REQUIREMENT

Due to compliance with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidate must be a U.S. Person, which is defined as, a U.S. citizen, a U.S. permanent resident, or have protected status in the U.S. under asylum or refugee status or have the ability to obtain an export authorization.

BENEFITS

Beyond a performance-driven salary, you'll work alongside dedicated experts on technology that's advancing aviation. As a Honeywell Aerospace employee, you're eligible for a comprehensive benefits package that includes:

  • Employer-subsidized medical, dental, vision and life insurance
  • Short-term and long-term disability coverage
  • 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts and health savings accounts
  • Employee assistance program and educational assistance
  • Parental leave and 12 paid holidays
  • Paid time off for vacation, personal and sick time

Explore your benefits:

ABOUT HONEYWELL AEROSPACE

Join a company that's reintroducing itself to the aviation community we've helped advance for more than a century. At Honeywell Aerospace (NASDAQ: HONA), we're launching as an independent, publicly traded aerospace and defense company built on a legacy of operational excellence and mission-focused execution.

Our new brand identity pairs that heritage with real momentum, as we build technology that helps pilots navigate with confidence, aircraft operate more efficiently, and operators stay ahead of change. With our systems on board 90% of the world's aircraft, your work here has reach that's rare to find anywhere else.

Focusing on our customers, investing in innovation, and building a culture of accountability and performance is how we're shaping what comes next.

Every horizon. Every mission. Every day.

ABOUT THE BUSINESS UNIT

Honeywell Aerospace products and services are found on aircraft across commercial aviation, defense and space — from engines and cockpit electronics to cabin systems, mechanical components and connectivity solutions. Our technology helps operators fly more safely, reduce fuel consumption, improve on-time performance and deliver a better experience for the people on board.

As aviation continues to evolve, we're also developing systems to support autonomous and supersonic platforms, bringing the same focus on safety and efficiency to the next era of flight. With approximately 36,000 employees worldwide and net sales of $17.4B in 2025, Honeywell Aerospace is one of the largest dedicated aerospace companies in the world. Explore our businesses:

Electronic Solutions develops the avionics, navigation systems, sensors and electromagnetic defense technology that help aircraft perform safely and with precision. Our systems are on board 90% of the world's aircraft — serving commercial aviation, defense and space operators from integrated flight deck platforms with 30-plus years in service to radiation-hardened systems trusted for human spaceflight.

title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
• Job grade: Higher Executive Officer
  • Contract type: Permanent
  • Type of role: Engineering
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time, Part-time, Compressed hours
  • Number of jobs available: 1

Location

Cheltenham, Manchester

About the job

Job summary

GCHQ is an intelligence, cyber and security agency with a mission to keep the UK safe. We use cutting-edge technology, ingenuity and partnerships to identify, analyse and disrupt threats. Working with our intelligence partners, MI5 and MI6, we protect the UK from terrorism, cyber attacks, and espionage. At GCHQ, you’ll do varied and fascinating work in a supportive and inclusive environment that emphasises teamwork.

Flexible working

We recognise the importance of a healthy work-life balance and offer a range of working patterns, including full-time, part-time, and compressed hours. Hybrid working, which combines working on-site and from home, may be more limited due to the nature of the work. However, some homeworking may be available depending on business needs. We also support flexible start and finish times, where possible, to help you manage your personal and professional commitments.

Find out more about flexible working on our website.

Job description

As a Senior Software Engineer, you’ll play a pivotal role in solving mission-critical challenges. You’ll contribute to the architecture and design of both new and existing systems, establish and promote best practices, and deliver high-quality software solutions. Drawing on your expertise in a range of software engineering methodologies, you’ll introduce fresh ideas and innovative approaches that make a real impact at the core of our mission: keeping the UK safe, both in the real world and online.

This is a practical, impact-driven role with plenty of opportunities to develop yourself and others. Operating at a deep technical level, you’ll apply your expertise across a variety of software engineering frameworks and technologies, working with languages such as JavaScript, Java, Node.js, Python, Rust and Go. Alongside hands-on engineering, you’ll help shape how teams build and deliver software by defining code review, branching and deployment strategies, and reviewing pull requests to support high-quality, maintainable solutions.

For our Cheltenham roles, we are particularly interested in candidates with experience in technologies and practices such as C++, Golang, Python, Rust, CMake, HELM, YAML, JSON, containerisation, VCPkg, observability, DevOps, Kubernetes, systems administration and Linux. However, we also welcome applications from candidates whose experience aligns with any of the technologies and disciplines outlined above.

You’ll bring a pragmatic approach to adopting new software engineering practices, using them to improve quality, productivity and delivery, and helping others do the same. As part of a wider network of peers, you’ll collaborate and learn from others. With your experience, you’ll set the standard, introduce innovative ways of working, and help shape technical priorities.

Whether leading and mentoring a team or acting as the technical expert within a high-performing group, you’ll draw on your knowledge of diverse methodologies to deliver impactful solutions. Confidently engaging with both technical and non-technical stakeholders, you’ll make a positive contribution to the wider engineering community.

Training and development
At GCHQ, we’re committed to your growth and development. From the moment you join, a comprehensive induction will introduce you to our organisation, providing insight into how we operate and the collaborative environment you’ll be part of. This lays the foundation for a learning journey tailored to your goals and preferred learning style.

From day one, access to mentors and subject matter experts will help you settle into the role. You can continue to have a mentor for as little or as long as you choose throughout your career. We invest in your development and adapt to the way you like to learn. Support and encouragement are provided every step of the way, as you become an integral part of our innovative team. We’ll provide the space and resources for continuous learning and improvement, with up to 30% of your time dedicated to personal development, giving you the freedom to explore new technologies, build professional skills, or pursue areas of growth that interest you.

From books, online courses, and conferences to real-world projects supported by your team, we’ll provide the resources you need to grow. Learning and development opportunities tailored to your role cover a wide range of software disciplines including front-end design, site reliability engineering, data engineering, solution architecture, machine learning operations, UX, Agile, cloud engineering and security. We’ll even support formal qualifications through dedicated funding and provide subscriptions to platforms like Cloud Academy, Pluralsight, and O’Reilly to help stay ahead.

Our culture embraces a growth mindset and values equality, encouraging teams and leaders to bring their best every day. Whether you’re exploring advanced software engineering patterns, gaining certifications like AWS Developer or Certified Scrum Master, or developing leadership skills through internal training, we’ll help you build the career you want. As your expertise grows, you’ll also have opportunities for skill reviews that can lead to recognised additional skills payments, supporting both your development and progression within the organisation.

Person specification

As a Senior Software Engineer, you will bring expertise in the frameworks and technologies mentioned above, along with experience working with cloud platforms AWS, Azure, and GCP. You’ll have successfully led Agile project teams, evaluated customer business requirements, and delivered high-quality software solutions that make a real impact.

Strategic and self-driven, you’ll serve as a bridge between teams, communicating technical information with clarity and confidence. You’ll thrive in a fast-paced, innovative environment where creativity is key to solving complex and unprecedented challenges.

Experience of generative AI would be advantageous, whether through using AI assisted software development tools, understanding agentic patterns, or developing applications that use large language models. An awareness of how to evaluate AI-generated outputs and use these technologies responsibly, securely and effectively would also be beneficial. What matters most is your curiosity and willingness to develop your knowledge as these technologies evolve.

We welcome experienced professionals from a variety of related fields, including security engineering, site reliability engineering and data engineering. Your genuine enthusiasm for software engineering, combined with your ability to mentor others, collaborate effectively, and stay ahead of emerging technologies, makes you a valuable contributor to a forward-thinking engineering community.

We’re Disability Confident
GCHQ is proud to have achieved Leader status within the Department for Work and Pensions’ Disability Confident scheme. This initiative encourages employers to think differently about disability and take action to improve how they recruit, retain, and develop disabled people. As a Disability Confident Leader, we aim to ensure that a fair and proportionate number of disabled applicants who best meet the essential minimum criteria for this position, will be offered an interview, if it is practical for us to do so. This is known as the Offer of an interview.

To secure an interview for this role, you will need to meet the minimum criteria assessed during the application sift. The minimum criteria in order of application process are:

  • You'll be required to reach the minimum pass mark for the online Situational Judgement Test (SJT), which assesses criteria important for all roles in our organisation.
  • Able to demonstrate evidence of where you’ve taken ownership of a technical project or piece of work.
  • Able to demonstrate the ability to understand several modern languages/frameworks, such as Golang, Java, JavaScript, Node.js, Python, Rust.
  • Able to demonstrate experience working in an Agile technical project team.
  • Able to demonstrate the practical application of software engineering principles to deliver, maintain and improve software solutions in a complex technical environment.

Equal opportunities
At GCHQ diversity and inclusion are critical to our mission. To protect the UK, we need a truly diverse workforce that reflects the society we serve. This includes diversity in every sense of the word: people of different backgrounds, ages, ethnicities, gender identities, sexual orientations, ways of thinking, and those with disabilities or neurodivergent conditions. We therefore welcome and encourage applications from everyone, including individuals from groups that are under-represented in our workforce, such as women, people from ethnic minority backgrounds, individuals with disabilities, and those from low socio-economic backgrounds.

Find out more about our culture, working environment and diversity on our website here.

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £50,354, GCHQ contributes £14,587 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

You’ll receive a starting salary of £50,354 to £60,036. This includes a basic salary, skills payment, and a concessionary payment of £2,758. The final amount will depend on your skills and experience. You’ll also receive a one-off recruitment bonus of £3,500, split into two payments: £1,750 on joining and £1,750 upon successful completion of your probation period. Other benefits include:

    • 25 days of annual leave, automatically increasing to 30 days after 5 years' service, plus 10.5 days of public and privilege holidays
    • opportunities for recognition through our employee performance scheme
    • interest-free season ticket loan
    • excellent pension scheme
    • cycle to work scheme
    • on-site facilities such as a gym, restaurant, and coffee bars (available at some locations)
    • paid parental and adoption leave

Things you need to know

Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Selection process details

Our recruitment process is fair, transparent, and based on merit.

Here is a brief overview of each stage, in order:

  1. An initial online application form including pre-screening questions to ensure you meet the eligibility criteria.
  2. Online Situational Judgement Test (SJT) in which you rate the appropriateness of responses to a series of short scenarios.
  3. Technical and competency-based interview, including a presentation.
  4. If successful, you’ll receive a conditional offer of employment, subject to vetting.

Please note you must successfully pass each stage of the process in order to progress to the next. Your application may take around 6 to 9 months to process, including vetting, so we advise you to continue any current employment until you have received your final job offer.

Before you apply
To work at GCHQ, you must be a British citizen or hold dual British nationality. Read the full eligibility criteria.

This role requires the highest level of security clearance, known as Developed Vetting (DV). It’s something everyone in the UK Intelligence Community undertakes. Find out more about the vetting process.

Please note we have a strict drugs policy. Once you start your application, you must not take any recreational drugs, and you’ll need to declare any previous drug usage at the relevant stage.

Before applying, we recommend setting up a separate email address for your contact with us to ensure your personal and application correspondence remain separate. Try to avoid including identifying features in your email address, such as your first and/or surname and date of birth. This is good practice and will help you manage your application with us more securely.

The role is based in Cheltenham or Manchester, so you’ll need to live within a commutable distance. Please consider any financial implications and practicalities before submitting your application.

We offer reasonable reimbursement of travel costs for candidates attending in person interviews or assessments during the recruitment and vetting process. Full details will be provided with your interview or assessment invitation.

Reimbursement is discretionary and will only be made in line with the Candidate Expenses Policy, as amended from time to time. Candidates must book their own travel, using the most economical option, and provide original hard copy receipts for reimbursement.

Please note, you should only launch your application from within the UK. If you are based overseas, you should wait until you visit the UK to launch an application. Applying from outside the UK will impact on our ability to progress your application. You should not discuss your application, other than with your partner or a close family member.

Right to close applications early:
Please be aware that we reserve the right to close applications once a certain number have been received. Please submit your application as soon as possible to avoid missing out. If you have a disability (as defined under the Equality Act 2010) and need additional time to complete your application. Then, contact us via the email provided as soon as possible, using the subject line “Reasonable Adjustments Extension” and briefly outline the support you require.



Feedback will only be provided if you attend an interview or assessment.

Location

About the job

Job summary

Please refer to Job Description

Job description

Proud to serve. Proud to keep justice going.

Our Team Leaders in HMCTS National Services play a critical role in helping deliver justice, this role will enable you to demonstrate and develop your leadership skills. You will be responsible for making sure your team deliver business objectives through providing excellent administrative support and customer service to service users and key stakeholders.

About us

HM Courts & Tribunals Service (HMCTS) is responsible for the administration of criminal, civil and family Courts and Tribunals England and Wales as well as the reserved unified tribunals across the United Kingdom. Our roles support our service users and colleagues within HMCTS, where people and businesses access potentially life-changing justice. We’re looking for individuals who are committed to public service and making a difference in people’s lives to deliver justice.

National Services provides centralised support through Courts and Tribunals Service Centres, Business Centres and Enforcement Offices. We handle case administration, customer queries by phone, email, and webchat and enable self-service in our digital services.

About your role

The role of a manager is at the heart of HMCTS operations, shaped by the Civil Service Line Management Standards. It’s rewarding, challenging, and essential to our success.
