title: Sr Advanced Hardware Engineer
description:
As a Sr. Advanced Hardware Design Engineer at Honeywell Aerospace, you will play a key role in designing and developing sophisticated hardware solutions that advance the future of aerospace technology. You will apply deep technical expertise to create innovative, high-reliability hardware that contributes to safer, more efficient, and more dependable aerospace products.

In this role, you will support Honeywell’s Integrated Flight Deck Systems (IFS) organization and contribute to the development of the next generation Head-Up Display (HUD). Working under minimal supervision, you will collaborate with world-class engineers to design, test, validate, and transition complex hardware from prototype through production. You will also serve as a technical mentor, supporting the growth of junior engineers and contributing to the success of complex engineering programs.

You will report directly to our Sr Engineering Manager, and you’ll work out of our Phoenix, AZ location on a Hybrid work schedule. External hires will begin with 90 days on site before transitioning to a 3/2 hybrid schedule.

  • Lead the design and development of advanced hardware systems from concept through production.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to define hardware requirements and ensure seamless integration with software and systems engineering.
  • Perform schematic capture, PCB design support, and comprehensive hardware validation to ensure performance, reliability, and compliance.
  • Conduct troubleshooting, debugging, and root-cause analysis during development and qualification phases.
  • Provide technical leadership and mentorship to junior engineers and support continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Interface with internal and external stakeholders to ensure products meet customer and regulatory requirements.
  • Stay current with emerging hardware technologies and aerospace industry trends to drive innovation in product designs.

YOU MUST HAVE

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in a technical discipline such as the sciences, technology, engineering or mathematics
  • U.S. citizenship or permanent residency due to export control and ITAR requirements.
  • Strong expertise in schematic capture, hardware testing methodologies, and design verification.
  • In-depth knowledge of analog and digital circuit design, signal integrity, and power management.
  • Experience with hardware validation, debugging tools, and compliance with aerospace standards.

WE VALUE

  • Experience with modern processing technologies, including microprocessors, FPGAs, memory, and high‑speed I/O.
  • Experience designing module-level analog/linear circuits such as signal conditioning and data conversion (ADC/DAC).
  • Demonstrated experience performing Product/LRU and Printed Board Assembly (PBA) design verification and qualification.
  • Working knowledge of DO‑254 (Design Assurance for Airborne Electronic Hardware) and RTCA DO‑160 qualification guidelines.
  • Proven ability to design, simulate, analyze, and verify hardware performance against requirements.
  • Proficiency with Mentor Graphics Xpedition (or similar design tools), Mathcad, LTspice, and Microsoft Excel.
  • Test engineering experience, including requirements‑based verification.
  • Familiarity with the avionics development lifecycle and strong troubleshooting/debug capabilities.

U.S. PERSON REQUIREMENT

Due to compliance with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidate must be a U.S. Person, which is defined as, a U.S. citizen, a U.S. permanent resident, or have protected status in the U.S. under asylum or refugee status or have the ability to obtain an export authorization.

BENEFITS

Beyond a performance-driven salary, you'll work alongside dedicated experts on technology that's advancing aviation. As a Honeywell Aerospace employee, you're eligible for a comprehensive benefits package that includes:

  • Employer-subsidized medical, dental, vision and life insurance
  • Short-term and long-term disability coverage
  • 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts and health savings accounts
  • Employee assistance program and educational assistance
  • Parental leave and 12 paid holidays
  • Paid time off for vacation, personal and sick time

Explore your benefits:

ABOUT HONEYWELL AEROSPACE

Join a company that's reintroducing itself to the aviation community we've helped advance for more than a century. At Honeywell Aerospace (NASDAQ: HONA), we're launching as an independent, publicly traded aerospace and defense company built on a legacy of operational excellence and mission-focused execution.

Our new brand identity pairs that heritage with real momentum, as we build technology that helps pilots navigate with confidence, aircraft operate more efficiently, and operators stay ahead of change. With our systems on board 90% of the world's aircraft, your work here has reach that's rare to find anywhere else.

Focusing on our customers, investing in innovation, and building a culture of accountability and performance is how we're shaping what comes next.

Every horizon. Every mission. Every day.

ABOUT THE BUSINESS UNIT

Honeywell Aerospace products and services are found on aircraft across commercial aviation, defense and space — from engines and cockpit electronics to cabin systems, mechanical components and connectivity solutions. Our technology helps operators fly more safely, reduce fuel consumption, improve on-time performance and deliver a better experience for the people on board.

As aviation continues to evolve, we're also developing systems to support autonomous and supersonic platforms, bringing the same focus on safety and efficiency to the next era of flight. With approximately 36,000 employees worldwide and net sales of $17.4B in 2025, Honeywell Aerospace is one of the largest dedicated aerospace companies in the world. Explore our businesses:

Electronic Solutions develops the avionics, navigation systems, sensors and electromagnetic defense technology that help aircraft perform safely and with precision. Our systems are on board 90% of the world's aircraft — serving commercial aviation, defense and space operators from integrated flight deck platforms with 30-plus years in service to radiation-hardened systems trusted for human spaceflight.

About the job

Job summary

Heritage is all around us, it is valued by people, and it drives pride in place and wellbeing. It is a key part of the Government’s place and community agenda, and a brilliant place to come and make a difference. Our preserved heritage tells our national story - from monuments such as Stonehenge, to our industrial landscapes to local pubs.

The Heritage team does everything from listing buildings to designing and operationalising grant schemes, from sponsorship to developing heritage policy and potential bill measures. We are a flexible team and work to ensure the best outcomes for our Secretary of State’s priorities:

  • Growth and good jobs in every place
  • A more socially cohesive country with an inclusive national story
  • Richer lives with choices and opportunities for all

Job description

You will lead the heritage protection team alongside your job-share partner (an existing G7 who works 3 days a week) to deliver the government’s responsibilities to protect buildings and monuments through the listing and scheduling processes.

The heritage protection team oversees the department’s statutory duties to protection the historic environment through the designation of listed buildings, scheduled monuments, and protected wreck sites. It also manages a non-statutory review process for listing decisions, and powers for the upkeep and repair of historic buildings.

Key deliverables include:

  • Managing a fascinating caseload across different heritage protection regimes
  • Steering complex casework, with close engagement with legal colleagues, Historic England, and ministers
  • Ensuring correspondence is drafted in a timely way and to a high standard
  • Contributing to policy preparation for a potential heritage bill.

The protection team sits within the wider heritage team in VEHLAC and you will be expected to make a strong corporate contribution to the life of the team and the wider directorate.

Person specification

  • Line management: The role manages 1 SEO, 1 HEO and 2 EOs. You will be able to set a positive, supportive team culture in line with DCMS values. You will be an experienced line manager, capable of setting direction in your team, taking responsibility for team performance and the timely delivery of work. You will coach your team to develop new skills in line with priorities and support their wider learning and development.

title: Cyber Security Architect
description:
• Job grade: Senior Executive Officer
  • Contract type: Permanent
  • Business area: IPO - DDaT

  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time, Part-time

Location

Newport, NP10 8QQ

About the job

Job summary

Cyber Security Architect

The Security Architect works closely with the Chief Security Officer, Head of Cyber, Lead Security Architect and the wider security team to develop an IPO vision for security and evolution of the security strategy and supporting roadmaps.

The role of IPO Security Architect is part of the IPO Secure team at the Intellectual Property Office. Playing a key part in an established team, the individual is responsible for ensuring the continued compliance with key security standards, such as PCI, ISO27001, secure by design, GovAssure etc.

It is essential that this role ensures that security architecture alongside compliance are understood and therefore the role will include championing security by design.

The Security Architect is essential in shaping security solutions and controls across multiple platforms (on-premises, cloud, hybrid) providing oversight, support, and advice to enable technical teams to make security decisions.

They ensure that common tools and patterns are used effectively to deliver secure systems, whilst implementing proportionate controls to enable positive business outcomes thereby safeguarding the IPO’s data, essential services and the supporting infrastructure.

They ensure Secure by Design principles are adopted, and coordinate on assurance against the National Cyber Security Centre’s Cyber Assessment Framework with the Government’s GovAssure framework.

Working Style

This role will be carried out in-line with IPO Hybrid working arrangements where staff are currently expected to spend at least 20% of their time working onsite from one of our offices. This role is based in our Newport Office.

The requirement for attendance at an office location can vary by role so we would encourage candidates to discuss working arrangements with the recruiting manager to agree a reasonable balance between working from home and the office.

The IPO holds a visa sponsor licence however; this role is not eligible for sponsorship under the Skilled Worker route. Candidates will therefore need to have an existing right to work in the UK at the time of application.

Job description

Main duties consist of but are not limited to:

  • Ensure security architecture aligns with wider Gov security policies and frameworks, legal frameworks, industry regulations and best practise (e.g ISO 27001, NCSC Standards, GDPR, PCI DSS, GovAssure, Secure by Design)
  • Support the secure by design champion in building awareness and understanding of secure by design framework across DDaT.
  • Develop and manage the security architecture roadmap, ensuring activities are organised and planned in with relevant teams in an efficient manner, ensuring it aligns closely with the IPO Secure Team’s strategic direction and any recommendations from audits
  • Continuously keep up to date with changing compliance legislation and initiatives to assess new opportunities for educating colleagues on relevant security standards.
  • Recommend security controls and identify security solutions that support business objectives.

Job description

We look forward to reading your application for the role of Public and Personal Safety Training (PPST) Subject Matter Expert.

This is an exciting opportunity for a Police Constable or Staff equivalent to join the Public and Personal Safety Training (PPST) team and assist in driving the work forward. The PPST team forms part of the broader Public Order, Public Safety team where you will be able to bring new ideas and build relationships with the UK forces as well as other teams within the College.

You will play a vital part in supporting forces with the transition to the National Trial as well as embedding the scenario-based methodology. This is an opportunity for a PPST subject matter expert to bring their knowledge into the College for the benefit of all forces. You will ensure knowledge and good practice is shared, set standards and support professional development.

The successful candidate must be able to work proactively and use their own initiative to manage competing priorities, identify solutions, and drive tasks forward. Equally important is the ability to work collaboratively as part of a team, building positive relationships with colleagues and stakeholders, sharing knowledge and expertise, and contributing to the achievement of common objectives.

Person specification

Some of your responsibilities will include:

  • Design and maintain a national PPST curriculum derived from empirical research, industry best practice, and lessons learned.
  • Develop engaging learning materials, including written guides.
  • Facilitate CPD events-design agendas, arrange guest speakers, deliver interactive learning sessions.
  • Provide expert guidance at national meetings and practitioner working groups, advocating for PPST standards.
  • Collaborate closely with College colleagues, police forces, academic partners, and external organisations to ensure standardised delivery and continuous improvement.

To be successful in this role you’ll need:

  • Qualified as a Public and Personal Safety Trainer.
  • Certified Trainer in Police Sector Trainer Standards.
  • Evidence of commitment to continual professional development.
  • Qualified assessor i.e. Assessing Competence in the Workplace or equivalent qualification/ award including College assessing awards.

Belfast, Bristol, Cardiff, Edinburgh, Glasgow, Leeds, Manchester, Newcastle- upon- Tyne, Stratford, Telford, Worthing.

Please note that due to workforce controls, Newcastle- upon- Tyne and Stratford are only available to existing HMRC staff in these locations. HMRC staff based in Reading can also apply to move to Stratford in line with Migration path. HMRC staff based in 100PS can also apply to move to Stratford, however, please note that selecting “London” on your location preference choices refers to 100 Parliament Street and not the wider London area.

About the job

Job summary

Discover a career in your hands at HMRC. Whether you're seeking purpose, growth, or a workplace that gives you a true sense of belonging, hear from some of our employees as they share their story about what it’s really like to work at HMRC.

Visit our YouTube channel to watch the full series and come and discover your potential.

Candidates who wish to work an alternative working pattern are welcome to apply. The preferred working pattern may or may not be available and will be considered in line with business need. Any request to work an alternative working pattern should be discussed with the vacancy holder following the selection process.

Please note that, if you are applying for roles on a part-time basis, the salary agreed will be pro-rata, reflective of the working hours agreed within your contract.

Job description

This role is an exciting opportunity to join HMRC’s CDIO Borders and Trade (B&T) working as a leader for the Business Analysis Practice in CDIO B&T.

You will lead and build capability across a multi-grade, geographically dispersed Team of around 35 BA’s.
Within CDIO, BA professionals play an essential role in delivering high-quality analysis using different methodologies and techniques to define technical requirements. You will be responsible for leading the BA function in CDIO B&T, setting standards, managing resourcing and ensuring quality analysis within the technical delivery function.

You will use your knowledge and experience of Business Analysis to coach and mentor teams and colleagues, use OKRs, KPIs, AI capability and other leadership and management techniques to drive delivery and improvement. You will encourage and facilitate continuous improvement and identify and remove blockers to delivery. You will help ensure that CDIO applies the latest in innovation and ways of working and help spread those practices across the wider estate. In particular, you will define the BA role and set direction for the team as we transition to product ways of working.

You will be comfortable parachuting into priority deliveries to either lead remediation of complex issues and put product deliveries on a ‘path to green’, and or driving early life cycle delivery to establish product delivery teams on sound foundations to deliver outcomes successfully.

For those who thrive in a fast-paced, exciting, and motivational environment, we offer unique and unparalleled opportunities to work with some of the latest technologies and make a real, lasting difference.

Person specification

  • Directly manage a team of BA’s ensuring effective deployment to meet demand as well as managing performance, setting direction and role-modelling inclusive Leadership.
  • As a member of Senior Leadership Group, you will support the Deputy Director in wider leadership activities which support the needs and priorities of BSD, including People, financial, commercial and risk management where appropriate.
  • Supporting CDIO B&T Product ways of working transformation through application of new BA resource model and roles, impacting and landing Change through visible leadership
  • Building relationships and collaboration with B&T Guilds and the wider BA community, sharing best practice to enable alignment on GDD Standards and tooling, Delivery and functional integration
  • Developing and shaping strategies to drive awareness of the BA profession, promoting the BA Service Offer, building the influence of the team and supporting services across the organisation by embedding the practice.
  • Responsible for shaping the Business Analysis practice and improving ways of working by embedding a consistent and high-quality professional framework and standards, utilising AI capabilities.
  • Overall Accountability for BA work across CDIO Borders and Trade, including Quality Assurance, including driving a data and evidence led approach using OKRs, KPIs and tooling to improve performance, delivery and quality outcomes.
  • Managing relationships with delivery leads to ensure business analysis is contributing to successful delivery, stepping in to support where required.
  • Accountable for workforce planning and capability development to ensure the BA profession meets current and future organisational needs.
  • Champion professional development, mentoring, and career progression for BAs, ensuring alignment with GDD capability frameworks.
  • Establish and maintain governance for BA standards and assurance across all delivery portfolios.
  • Use data and insight to measure BA contribution to delivery outcomes and continuously improve practice.
  • Represent HMRC in cross-government and industry BA communities to share learning and influence best practice.
  • Act as a visible leader for cultural change, embedding product-centric ways of working across BSD.

Essential Criteria

  • Significant experience in a BA role and leading teams of geographically dispersed BAs within an Agile and Product-led environment, with a track record of direction setting, building capability, working practically and strategically, resolving challenges, pursuing opportunities, anticipating and mitigating risks and finding creative solutions.
  • A track record of working collaboratively with others, identifying and analysing stakeholder views, providing constructive challenge and successfully influencing decisions using data and insight.
  • Degree level qualification or equivalent experience
  • Experience in workforce planning and capability development, ensuring alignment with organisational priorities and future skills needs.
  • Experience in establishing and maintaining governance for professional standards and quality assurance across multiple programmes, including use of OKRs and KPIs.
  • Proven ability to lead cultural and behavioural change, embedding new ways of working across complex organisations.
  • Experience in engaging with cross-government or industry professional communities to share best practice and influence standards.
  • Ability to use data and insight to measure professional impact and drive continuous improvement.
  • Understanding of financial and commercial considerations in a digital delivery context

Desirable Criteria

  • Understanding of Borders and Trade Sub regimes, services and Products and Platforms
  • Balancing multiple priorities and employing techniques to deal with ambiguity.
  • Leading a community of practice.
  • Understanding of customs and trade regulations and policies

title: Advanced Materials Engineer
description:
Honeywell Aerospace is seeking a highly skilled Advanced Materials and Process Engineer specializing in materials development, testing, and characterization to join our innovative engineering team.

The ideal candidate will have a strong background in materials science and demonstrated experience with processing-microstructure-property relationships for at least one of the Ni-based, Fe-based, or Ti-based alloy families. This role offers the opportunity to work on cutting-edge projects in a collaborative environment, contributing to the development of high-performance components for various demanding applications.

You will report directly to our Mechanical Design Engineering Manager in our Phoenix, AZ site on a hybrid work schedule. Note: For the first 90 days, New Hires must be prepared to work 100% onsite M-F.

• Materials Science: Possess strong materials science fundamentals with education/experience focused on metallurgy, materials engineering, and/or materials science.
• Material Characterization: Lead comprehensive materials development and qualification projects that require a wide breadth of knowledge in techniques such as microstructure analysis, mechanical testing, and data modeling to understand the properties and behaviors of materials used in mechanical designs.
• Mechanical Testing: Conduct experimental testing to understand material performance under various loading conditions, ensuring compliance with industry standards and safety regulations.
• Design Guidance: Integrate insights gained from material characterization to develop guidance for the design process to optimize the mechanical properties and overall performance of components, ensuring durability and reliability in challenging environments.
• Troubleshooting: Investigate material performance issues to identify root causes, leveraging advanced analytical techniques. Recommend solutions to mitigate risks and enhance material reliability.
• Interdisciplinary Collaboration: Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including design, manufacturing, and quality assurance, to ensure successful integration of material characteristics into product design and development processes.
• Documentation and Reporting: Prepare detailed documentation and reports outlining findings from material characterization studies, testing results, and recommendations for design improvements. Present findings to stakeholders in a clear and concise manner.
• Continuous Improvement: Drive initiatives focused on improving material characterization methods and techniques to enhance accuracy, efficiency, and effectiveness in the engineering design process.
• Mentorship: Provide technical mentorship to junior engineers and team members in the areas of material characterization and mechanical design principles, fostering a culture of knowledge sharing and professional development.

Must Haves:
• Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in a technical discipline such as the sciences, technology, engineering or mathematics
• Minimum of 3 years of experience in material characterization, preferably in aerospace, automotive, or related industries.

We Value:
• Master’s degree in Materials Science, or a related field
• Proficient in material characterization techniques such as mechanical testing, microscopy, and computational modeling tools.
• Experience with mechanical testing (tensile, creep, fatigue) and the ability to interpret testing results.
• Understanding of common failure modes in metals (e.g. creep, LCF, HCF, etc.).
• Knowledgeable in material manufacturing methods such as castings, forgings, additive manufacturing, or composites manufacturing.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, with a proven track record in assessing material performance and implementing improvements.
• Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to effectively convey technical information to diverse audiences.
• Strong understanding of materials science fundamentals with an emphasis in metallurgy, composites, or material processing methods.
• Experience working in a team-oriented environment, demonstrating strong collaboration skills and the ability to influence cross-functional teams.
• Expertise in material behavior under dynamic loading conditions and an understanding of fatigue and fracture mechanics.
• Familiarity with design control processes, risk assessment, and reliability engineering practices.

BENEFITS

Beyond a performance-driven salary, you'll work alongside dedicated experts on technology that's advancing aviation. As a Honeywell Aerospace employee, you're eligible for a comprehensive benefits package that includes:

  • Employer-subsidized medical, dental, vision and life insurance
  • Short-term and long-term disability coverage
  • 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts and health savings accounts
  • Employee assistance program and educational assistance
  • Parental leave and 12 paid holidays
  • Paid time off for vacation, personal and sick time

Explore your benefits:

ABOUT HONEYWELL AEROSPACE

Join a company that's reintroducing itself to the aviation community we've helped advance for more than a century. At Honeywell Aerospace (NASDAQ: HONA), we're launching as an independent, publicly traded aerospace and defense company built on a legacy of operational excellence and mission-focused execution.

Our new brand identity pairs that heritage with real momentum, as we build technology that helps pilots navigate with confidence, aircraft operate more efficiently, and operators stay ahead of change. With our systems on board 90% of the world's aircraft, your work here has reach that's rare to find anywhere else.

Focusing on our customers, investing in innovation, and building a culture of accountability and performance is how we're shaping what comes next.

Every horizon. Every mission. Every day.

Due to compliance with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidate must be a U.S. Person, which is defined as, a U.S. citizen, a U.S. permanent resident, or have protected status in the U.S. under asylum or refugee status or have the ability to obtain an export authorization.​

We are currently not sponsoring applicants for work visas for this job. Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis.

About the job

Job summary

Can you solve the puzzles of government?

Can you be the architect of a better tomorrow?


If you enjoy applying statistical theories to assess risks and estimate the odds of future outcomes—and have a passion for presenting your findings—a rewarding career as a Graduate Trainee Actuary in the heart of government could be the perfect fit for you!

About us

The Government Actuary’s Department (GAD) are at the centre of actuarial expertise within government. We enable government to better understand and quantify risk and uncertainty and in turn help shape better outcomes for the UK public. We do this on our core work by diving into client challenges and ensuring our advice enables success. We identify critical challenges to co-create solutions with our partners so that actuarial expertise can have more impact on significant policy initiatives.

We are an inclusive organisation that values the unique perspectives and strengths of a diverse team, supported through our staff networks and active Diversity and Inclusion strategy, we ensure everyone has the opportunity to thrive. We are seeking motivated individuals to join our analytical team, where your contributions will be valued, and your voice heard.

Job description

As a Graduate Trainee Actuary, we will support your development to become a future Actuary in Government who is able to produce high quality, impactful advice and analysis for government and adapt to emerging societal challenges.

This will include participation in our rotation programme which includes:

Analytical Focussed Placement: Apply theoretical actuarial concepts and modern techniques to actuarial processes to deliver accurate analysis efficiently. As time progresses, take on more responsibility for the validity of your work and others as well as delegating and developing junior colleagues.

Consulting Focussed Placement: Work with actuaries to turn analysis into impactful advice through drafting communications and presenting to clients. Build relationships with stakeholders (internal and external) to support effective delivery of advice. As time progresses, build relationships with clients, support scoping of actuarial advice and business development.

Specialised Focussed Placement: Build upon experience of previous placements to try a new actuarial area in GAD or continue specialising within a certain domain to take on more ownership of advice and/or analysis.

Throughout the rotation programme, secondment opportunities exist to work directly with clients in government.

A significant proportion of GAD’s actuarial advice is either pensions or emerging policy areas. Therefore, during the rotation programme, all trainees will be exposed to typical pensions work (such as delivering actuarial valuations and other pension calculations, managing costs and risks associated with public service pension schemes or providing advice on funded pension schemes) as well as working in a different area to develop adaptability to new problems.

GAD works across a wide range of actuarial areas and we would look to provide opportunities for you to get involved in areas of interest where business needs allow.

Person specification

  1. Have an inquisitive and open mind to learn and apply new concepts
  2. Produce actuarial analysis to inform GAD’s advice to government departments, across areas of insurance, investments, pensions, and risk.
  3. Consider the validity of your, or others’, analysis through self-checks and communicate areas of concerns to senior colleagues.
  4. Support client engagement by drafting reports and advice as well as providing support in meetings and presentations.
  5. Manage your time to deliver your work to time and budget. You may also be responsible for assisting with broader project management and development of junior staff.
  6. Proactively develop your knowledge and understanding of actuarial methods and analysis, data science, the issues and risks facing government as well as how GAD can best provide advice to our clients.
  7. Identify and suggest new ways of working, innovative solutions, modern outputs and new areas where GAD can provide advice.
  8. Work within GAD’s and Actuarial professional standards and departmental procedures and guidance notes.
  9. Use MS Office and advanced tools like R, Python or our Pension Valuation Software to carry out analysis and prepare advice for clients.
  10. With materials and time provided, independently work towards actuarial qualification through exams and Personal Professional Development requirements.

  • Making Effective Decisions
  • Delivering at Pace
  • Communicating and Influencing

  • Staff reward and recognition bonuses that operate throughout the year.

About the job

Job summary

Protect Great Britain's Critical Energy Infrastructure

At Ofgem, we work on behalf of energy consumers to ensure every household and business across Great Britain can rely on a safe, affordable and environmentally sustainable energy supply.

As Great Britain's energy system continues to evolve, cyber resilience plays a critical role in maintaining secure and reliable services. Through our responsibilities under the Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations, Ofgem acts as the Competent Authority for the Downstream Gas and Electricity (DGE) sector, helping ensure operational systems and networks remain resilient against cyber and related security threats.

We're looking for two experienced Regulatory Cyber Assurance Principals to join our Cyber Regulation team on a permanent basis. This is an opportunity to play a leading role in protecting critical national infrastructure, working directly with Operators of Essential Services (OES), government partners and industry stakeholders to strengthen cyber resilience across the energy sector.

Job description

As Ofgem's Cyber Assurance expert, you will lead and maintain relationships across a designated portfolio of Operators of Essential Services (OES), delivering a regulatory model that is engaging, collaborative and focused on improving cyber resilience.

You will provide leadership on cyber assurance activities across the Downstream Gas and Electricity sector, assessing compliance with the NIS Regulations, making expert compliance determinations and advising on appropriate regulatory responses where concerns or breaches are identified.

Working at the intersection of cyber security, regulation and critical national infrastructure, you will conduct assurance activities including inspections, review audit, exercising and technical testing outcomes, while influencing improvements that help safeguard services relied upon by millions of consumers across Great Britain.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead and maintain relationships across a designated portfolio of Operators of Essential Services (OES).
  • Provide expert advice and guidance to the DGE sector on compliance with the NIS Regulations.
  • Lead and support regulatory assurance and engagement activities, ensuring alignment with regulatory expectations.
  • Contribute to and lead NIS inspections, including evidence reviews, on-site assessments and the production of high-quality inspection reports.
  • Review and assess compliance documentation, including assurance reports, audit findings, exercising and testing outcomes, remediation plans and incident reports.
  • Assess and make expert determinations on compliance with the NIS Regulations.
  • Document inspection outcomes, assurance findings and regulatory decisions accurately and consistently.
  • Escalate compliance concerns where appropriate and collaborate with Enforcement teams to support the application of regulatory tools and drive improvements.
  • Provide expert advice regarding enforcement action where NIS Regulations have been breached.
  • Lead the development and continuous improvement of cyber assurance policies, products, methodologies and regulatory approaches.
  • Work collaboratively with government departments, other Competent Authorities, industry stakeholders and external assurance providers to support resilience objectives.
  • Provide inclusive leadership through knowledge sharing, coaching and support across the Cyber Regulation team, contributing to Ofgem's values and culture.

Person specification

Essential Criteria:

  • Relevant professional qualification in cyber security, such as: CISSP, CISA, CISM, ISO 27001 Lead Auditor, GICSP, ISA/IEC 62443 Cybersecurity Expert, or a related degree. Equivalent experience in a cyber regulatory environment will also be considered. (LEAD)
  • Expert in understanding cyber risk assessments and methodologies in relation to OT and IT of Critical National Infrastructure environments, and the application of appropriate and proportionate controls across people, process, and technology to mitigate risk.
  • Practitioner in advising on the implementation of cyber regulation and policy, promoting good security practice within the sector.
  • Proven experience of inspecting, auditing, or testing with an information security role.
  • Strong technical author skills.
  • Good understanding of the NIS Regulations and the NCSC Cyber Assessment Framework (CAF), with practical experience applying these eg in either policy, process, assurance, inspection, and/or enforcement activities.

We'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:

  • Making Effective Decisions
  • Communicating and Influencing
  • Delivering at Pace

Ofgem can offer you a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes; 30 days annual leave after 2 years; Excellent training and development opportunities; The opportunity to join the generous Civil Service pension which also includes a valuable range of benefits; hybrid working (currently 1 day a week in the office but this is kept under review), flexible working hours and family friendly policies. Plus lots of other benefits including clean and bright offices based centrally, engaged networks and teams and an opportunity to contribute to our ambitious and important targets of establishing a Net Zero energy system by 2050. title: Senior Electrical Power Systems Engineer I
description:
Voyager is an innovative space, defense, and national security technology company committed to advancing and delivering transformative, mission-critical solutions. We tackle the most complex challenges to unlock new frontiers for human progress, fortify national security, and protect critical assets to lead in the race for technological and operational superiority from ground to space.

Forge the Future: Join Voyager Technologies

The future belongs to those who build it. At Voyager Technologies, we’re building technologies that protect lives, expand frontiers and prepare us for what’s next. And we’re doing that with people who are wired to solve, build, adapt and lead. These roles are not for the faint of heart.

You’ll help lay the foundation for humanity's future. Join a culture where innovation thrives, curiosity is rewarded, and impact is real. We’re a company of doers, thinkers and builders, united by purpose and grounded in reality.

If you want to put your skills to work where the stakes are real and the mission is bigger than any one person, forge the future with Voyager.

The Senior Electrical Power Systems Engineer I for Voyager Lunar Systems is responsible for performing avionics and power system analysis for spacecraft missions to assess design margin, risk, and system compatibility.

The position reports to the Electronic Systems Manager and is part of Voyager Lunar Systems based in Pittsburgh, PA. This role is hybrid based in Pittsburgh, PA.

In this role, the essential functions are:

  • Perform power and avionics design and analysis for all mission concepts, right-sizing the power architecture to meet end-to-end mission objectives and requirements.
  • Develop and perform trade studies to support technical, business, and/or programmatic actions and decision-making.
  • Support development of component specifications and system-level requirements
  • Support spacecraft power component testing and system integration
  • Coordinate between technical partners, vendors, and peer engineers of other disciplines to assess design progress, schedule, and risks through the full systems engineering development cycle
  • Provide real-time operational support from mission control center

If your experience aligns with our basic qualifications and you are inspired by our mission, we’d like to connect. If you don’t see the right role right now, Join Our Talent Community and stay connected as we continue to build what’s next.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • 4-7 years of professional experience in power systems development for mission-critical, aerospace, defense, or other high reliability industry.
  • Demonstrated ability to carry out complicated analysis tasks, including developing the necessary tools/methodology and synthesizing results into higher level conclusions.
  • B.S. in Electrical or Computer Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Systems Engineering, similar related discipline or equivalent work experience.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Familiar with solar photovoltaic and lithium-ion battery technology
  • Experience with power budgeting process and system level energy balance analysis
  • Familiarity with surface charging related to space environments
  • Experience using SPICE for circuit analysis/modeling and familiarity with power electronics
  • Hands on experience working with electronics and lab equipment
  • Familiarity with power system telemetry measurement and processing
  • Experience with FMEA process and interfacing with software teams to develop system FDIR
  • Ability to build analytical tools using Microsoft VBA and MATLAB
  • Knowledge of spacecraft environmental tests
  • Knowledge of Range Safety and Ground Safety compliance
  • Familiarity with NASA-STD-4001, NASA-STD-4003, and MIL-STD-461

Travel, Physical, and/or Government Mandated Requirements:

  • Travel up to 10%, including the possibility of overnights, both foreign and domestic, to launch sites, customer facilities, and NASA/Government centers
  • Ability to lift, move or carry items or equipment up to 10 pounds

The position may be eligible for lump-sum bonus upon hire.

Voyager offers a highly competitive total compensation package designed to support the well-being, growth, and success of our employees. Employees benefit from a flexible and comprehensive rewards program that supports both professional and personal well-being.

  • Flexible Time Off (FTO), empowering employees to take the time they need to recharge and maintain a healthy work-life balance
  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and their families, with a significant portion of premiums covered by the company and many benefits paid at 100% for employees
  • Flexible, affordable gym memberships with 12,700+ options nationwide, including 24 Hour Fitness, EoS Fitness, Crunch Fitness, Anytime Fitness, Blink Fitness, Chuze Fitness, and more! No long-term contracts and FREE on-demand workout videos before you enroll
  • 401(k) retirement plan with a 50% company match on contributions up to 8%, supporting long-term financial security
  • Company wellness programs that support physical and mental well-being
  • Additional voluntary benefits and employee support resources
  • The opportunity to work alongside a highly talented team in an innovative, mission-driven environment

Voyager is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status, or other characteristics protected by law.

  • Support in the development and writing of operational procedures and reviewing procedures from other business areas.

Approved Premises - Residential Worker

Helping to keep the public safe. Giving people the chance to turn their lives around. Building a rewarding professional career. It’s an extraordinary role. There are many reasons to join the Probation Service. What will yours be?

About Approved Premises

Approved Premises are primarily for offenders who have been released on licence and who require a high level of supervision.

About the role

As a residential worker in an Approved Premises, you will play a crucial role in supporting the management of offenders in their transition from custody into the community, to achieve successful resettlement. You will assist with the well-being and supervision of Approved Premises residents, helping them to stick to their license conditions and supporting them to keep themselves and others safe. You will carry out inspections, monitor behaviour and positively engage with residents, working closely with colleagues and partner agencies.

The role will entail working at one main Approved Premise with the requirement to work across additional sites should the need arise.

Residential Workers are required to work regular unsocial hours which attract premium rates of pay in addition to advertised annual salary.

The Probation Service works with offenders who are pre-release or post-release from prison or serving community sentences. Our role is to support their rehabilitation and protect the public. At Dstl, our vision is to have a modern way of working efficiently, accommodating and enabling our people to create, collaborate and deliver. About the job

Job summary

The MOD is responsible for ensuring that it understands and demonstrates legal compliance regarding the environmental impact of the operations it conducts. Due to the broad nature of operations, these can involve explosive, Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) or other hazardous materials. Decisions on whether and how these operations proceed depend on understanding the potential environmental impact of these materials.

Working as a senior member of a specialist team, you will lead the delivery of environmental impact assessments and scientific advice that inform decision-making at the highest levels of Defence and Government. You will provide technical leadership across environmental assessment activities, ensuring that operational objectives are achieved whilst environmental risks and wider consequences are appropriately understood and managed.

Dstl recognises the importance of diversity and inclusion as people from diverse backgrounds bring fresh ideas. We are committed to building an inclusive working environment in which each employee fulfils their potential and maximises their contribution.

Job description

You will act as a recognised environmental specialist, providing technical oversight and assurance of assessment outputs, developing capability and supporting the professional development of colleagues. You will work closely with customers, stakeholders and multidisciplinary experts to ensure the Environmental Impact capability remains effective and responsive to current and future operational requirements.

Your responsibilities will include leading the delivery of environmental impact assessments that enable informed Defence operational and strategic decision making as well as giving authoritative scientific advice on the environmental consequences and risks associated with hazardous, explosive and CBRN material release scenarios.

For more information on the job responsibilities, please see the job profile attached below.

You will have experience of applying environmental, ecological or related scientific knowledge to complex operational or policy challenges. At FCDO Services, we protect the UK’s interests at home and overseas. We design and construct secure government buildings, courier diplomatic packages worldwide, safeguard government tech, and a whole lot more. Our work is as varied and vital as it gets, but we never lose sight of our people. Their skills, aspirations and growth mean as much as the mission we're on. In our world, it all matters.

Job description

    Our Digital and Data technology team is at the forefront of digital innovation. They provide best-in-class solutions for our clients, helping to shape and support a data driven future for the UK’s government. Whether it’s creating bespoke, secure software, offering programme and application support or moving an entire embassy’s servers to a Cloud platform. No matter the task, they’re on hand to provide support. Now, you’ve got the opportunity to join them.

    An inspirational coach and mentor with a challenging and enquiring mind, you’re committed to ensuring the products and services we offer to our customers are of the highest quality. Join us and you’ll have the opportunity to use all your skills as you work to support and enhance our global mission.

    Providing innovation to government partners

    Delivering best-in-class solutions

    Working at the cutting-edge of technology

    It all matters

    Manage the test solutions that contribute to the success of our global mission

    When you join us in this vital role it’ll be your task to define and implement test strategies that meet the relevant ISO standards, and use our business and operational requirements to construct test solutions for a range of more complex projects. You’ll be responsible for the improvement and optimisation of the tests we perform, and in addition to agreeing with stakeholders on proposed solutions, we’ll expect you to produce the required supporting documentation. You’ll also put your interpersonal skills to good use as you manage a team of testers and ensure their work is successful and signed off by the end user, and liaise with your colleagues to confirm that our defect management processes reflect operational priorities.

    Use all your design, delivery and management skills

    With a creative and analytical approach to your work, and excellent verbal and written communication skills, you’ll be capable of designing test models that meet all our requirements. With this in mind you should have well developed experience of using automation testing and defect tracking tools to manage and facilitate the following types of testing: functional, system integration, regression, non-functional, user acceptance and operational acceptance. You should hold Agile and ITIL Foundation level certification, advanced ISTQB certification, and basic knowledge of the SQL scripts used to interrogate databases. In addition, we’ll look for a good understanding of AWS, Azure and other MS programmes, and some knowledge of Virtual Machine management tools.

    Discover the support you need to grow your career further

    But we’re always looking to improve – just like you. That’s why when you join us, expect to receive a competitive salary, generous holiday entitlement and a Civil Service Pension. Along with this, you’ll also have access to training and other development opportunities to help grow your career with us. Our offices have an on-site gym, nursery, café, and restaurant, and we offer interest-free loans on season tickets and bikes to help you get there. It's a great set of benefits made to support all you do, and all you need.

    Want to see your future team’s work in action? Step into our Virtual Embassy and select a guide to take you round to see how we deliver for government customers and how you could help. Explore the embassy now at virtual-embassy.fcdoservicescareers.co.u

    Every single colleague must be security cleared before joining us. If you’re successful in your application, we’ll ask you to undergo our vetting process to achieve Developed Vetting (DV) clearance. This role is a reserved post and applications are only being accepted from single nationality candidates and not dual nationals. You can find out more about vetting on our website:

    It takes a diverse team to protect a diverse world.

    The vital work we do takes an incredible community of colleagues, with different skills, backgrounds, cultures and identities. The HR Officer is a key member of GAD’s HR team, providing a responsive, professional and inclusive first-line HR service to colleagues and managers. The role will coordinate core employee lifecycle processes, provide clear guidance on routine people matters, and ensure HR activity is completed accurately, consistently and on time.

Working across the full range of HR services, plus other GAD teams, you will maintain accurate workforce data and records, resolve routine enquiries and escalate more complex or higher-risk matters appropriately.

Job description

Providing 1st level proactive operational professional advice to colleagues & managers for the whole of the employee life cycle, predominantly in an administration context, but with the expectation of an advisory context as well.

The first point of call for basic employee relations and wellbeing queries, escalating where necessary. Ensuring that HR administrative tasks are carried out on time, to a high standard.

The post holder will use a full mixture of professional skills and integrity built on from enthusiasm, initiative and hands-on experience, to support predominantly the HR Business Partners, but also other members of the HR team, in relation to employee relations cases, wellbeing initiatives, recruitment & onboarding approaches delivering efficient day to day HR advice & administration, supporting the other HR Officers.

The role will require full support in ensuring key recruitment data cleanse and transition to a new HRIS model as required by the Project and senior leadership.

Person specification

People Services and customer experience

  • Manage first-line HR enquiries through agreed channels and within agreed service standards.
  • Provide clear, accurate and accessible advice on routine policy and employee lifecycle matters.
  • Take ownership of enquiries through to resolution, keeping customers informed and escalating appropriately.
  • Monitor response times, recurring enquiries and customer feedback to improve the service.

Employee lifecycle delivery

  • Coordinate recruitment, pre-employment checks, onboarding, contractual changes, family leave, probation and leaver processes.
  • Ensure transactions are completed accurately, on time and with clear audit trails.
  • Work with Payroll, Finance, IT and Security to manage dependencies and prevent delays.
  • Provide colleagues and managers with a consistent and inclusive experience at key moments in the employee lifecycle.

HR systems, data and controls

  • Maintain accurate and timely records across HR systems, SharePoint and relevant trackers.
  • Carry out scheduled data-quality checks and resolve discrepancies.
  • Produce regular management information on recruitment, workforce changes, absence, probation and service performance.
  • Support reconciliation of HR, payroll, finance and establishment information.
  • Apply data-protection, retention, information-handling and audit requirements consistently.

First-line employee relations and wellbeing support

  • Provide first-line procedural guidance on absence, probation, flexible working, family leave and other routine matters.
  • Coordinate meetings, correspondence, records and agreed actions.
  • Recognise matters requiring specialist advice and escalate them promptly to an HR Business Partner.
  • Handle sensitive personal information with discretion, empathy and appropriate professional boundaries.
  • Administer occupational health referrals and signpost colleagues to appropriate support.

Service improvement and change

  • Support mapping and improving HR processes, removing unnecessary hand-offs and duplication.
  • Develop clear guidance, templates, checklists and standard operating procedures.
  • Support new HR systems implementation and improvement.
  • Use enquiry, case and workforce data to identify recurring problems and recommend improvements.
  • Contribute to projects as appropriate
  • Help embed a culture of continuous improvement, shared ownership and learning.

Team contribution and professional standards

  • Work flexibly across the HR team, sharing knowledge and providing appropriate cover.
  • Build constructive relationships while being prepared to challenge incomplete or inaccurate information.
  • Demonstrate impartiality, discretion, sound judgement and commitment to inclusion.
  • Maintain professional knowledge and take responsibility for personal development.

Behaviours

We'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:

  • Changing and Improving
  • Delivering at Pace
  • Working Together
  • Managing a Quality Service

Technical skills

We'll assess you against these technical skills during the selection process:

  • Demonstrable experience of delivering a responsive administrative, HR or customer service in a busy, fast-paced environment (Lead Criteria) - Essential
  • Strong digital literacy, including use of Microsoft packages, systems and AI. (Lead criteria) - Essential

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £34,543, Government Actuary's Department contributes £10,007 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

As well as competitive salaries, we offer a substantial package of benefits:

  • Exceptional learning and development opportunities that you can explore alongside your day-to-day work.
  • 25 days annual leave per year, increasing to 30 days after 5 years’ service. In addition, we offer 9 days public and privilege days leave per year (pro rata for part time staff)
  • A Civil Service pension with an employer contribution of 28.97%
  • 5 days of paid volunteering leave
  • Up to 9 months maternity leave on full pay + generous paternity and adoption leave
  • Staff reward and recognition bonuses that operate throughout the year.
  • Occupational sick pay
  • Family-friendly policies such as help with caring responsibilities, special leave, generous paid maternity, paternity, and adoption leave.
  • Access to employee assistance programme which offers staff 24/7 confidential support and resources such as counselling, debt guidance and management advice.
  • The opportunity to join a trade union.
  • A working culture which encourages inclusion and diversity.
  • Salary advances for travel costs, including annual season tickets and cycle-to-work schemes.
  • Access to the Edenred employee benefits system which offers discounts to popular retailers and access to various useful resources such as financial and savings advice.
  • Complimentary BUPA health check.

Job description

Please note: This role is based at Weston Approved Premises in Weymouth and is not suitable for home working.
About you
You don’t need a degree for this role. We’re much more interested in your personal qualities. Ideally with experience of working with people who have social or personal difficulties, you’ll be empathetic, patient and resilient. Good writing skills are also essential. You must be able to produce clear and accurate reports to tight deadlines.
Additional Information
Approved Premises (AP) provide critical community-based service to accommodate and closely supervise high-risk offenders on release from prison, for the purposes of public protection. AP are staffed 24 hours per day, with staff enforcing an overnight curfew, and other monitoring and reporting requirements. Probation Services Officers lead on the key interventions and rehabilitative activities with the resident group, working regular hours Monday to Friday but also covering at weekends as required. The provision of suitable accommodation on release is a key factor in reducing reoffending and supporting transition into the community.
Helping to keep the public safe. Giving people the chance to turn their lives around. Building a rewarding professional career. There are many reasons to join the Probation Service. What will yours be?
We’re looking for empathetic, patient, and organised people to join us in this varied role, which offers the chance to make a difference, gain new skills and build a rewarding career within the Probation Service.
If this sounds like you, apply now.
If you are successful in the recruitment process to join the Probation Service, your starting salary will be £28,064.
The Probation Service offers the opportunity for annual pay progression through a Competency Based Framework (CBF), which if eligible, will see your pay increase. CBF is designed to enable you to move up through the pay band range as your competence grows.
New entrants are expected to join on the minimum of the pay band.
Probation Service also increase their pay band ranges annually in line with Civil Service Pay guidance, which will also apply an increase to band pay ranges where applicable.
Overview of the job
The job holder will undertake the full range of work with people on probation before and after sentence. This will include assessment, sentence implementation, offender management and producing reports. The job holder will provide case management support to a full range of people on probation utilising service procedures and practice directions that underpin professional judgement.
For further information on the summary, responsibilities, activities, duties of the role and the Civil Service Success Profile Criteria which will be used in the assessment process, please refer to the full Job Description Attachment.

Skilled Worker visa changes from 22 July 2025
In accordance with current immigration rules, this role is not eligible for a new Skilled Worker visa.
From 22 July 2025, the Government introduced changes to the eligibility criteria for Skilled Worker visas. As a result:
HM Prison and Probation Service (HMPPS) cannot consider sponsoring you to work as a probation services officer unless you have held a Skilled Worker visa prior to the 22 July 2025 changes.
If you have held a Skilled Worker visa continuously, please raise this during your pre-employment checks and your eligibility will be assessed in accordance with the immigration rules and transitional provisions in place.
If you apply to be a probation services officer and you have not held a Skilled Worker visa prior to 22 July 2025, you will need to consider your options for obtaining and/or maintaining your right to work in the UK in light of these changes.
If your application is successful, you will need to ensure that you have and maintain the legal right to live and work in the Civil Service and in the United Kingdom.
HMPPS will continue to comply with UK Immigration Rules applied in the UK and Civil Service. You can read more about Skilled Worker visas and the eligibility criteria here.

About us:
By managing offenders in the community, the Probation Service protects the public from the effect of crime and gives offenders the chance to turn their lives around. Join us and you’ll be part of a supportive team that thrives on sharing knowledge and expertise.
Successful applicants may be based a wide variety of office, court, team, or prison locations within the Probation Service region. Allocations will be made according to business need.
To find out more about working as a Probation Service Officer please click here
About the Recruitment Process
To apply to this role you will be required to complete a short application form and detail responses to Civil Service Behaviours and Experience based question.
As part of this application, you will also be required to sit the Civil Service Judgement test (CSJT). The CSJT is a two-part test which looks at your ability to make decisions in relation to specific civil service behaviours.
The CSJT is stage one of your application process and you will have the option to complete a practice test immediately before taking the test, to give you an insight of what to expect before you start.
If you would like more information relating to reasonable adjustments and the CSJT, please see more details here. You can also watch a short a video here.
You can find out more about the CSJT and complete a practice test now here.
If you are successful in passing this stage, your full application will be sifted once the application deadline has closed. You will then receive further instruction on the progress and outcome of your application.
If we receive a high volume of applications, we may assess and progress candidates through the recruitment process in stages (tranches). Candidates who meet the required standard at sift may be held pending future assessment stages rather than progressing immediately. Interview invitations and subsequent offers will be managed in line with the tranche in which candidates are assessed and their position in merit order
If you apply for multiple vacancies for the same role, only one of your applications will be progressed. Any assessment scores achieved will be applied consistently across all applications for that role, this will be valid for 6 months.
Candidates who do not meet the minimum benchmark at either the Sift or Interview stage will not be eligible to reapply for the same role for six months from the date their assessment scores are progressed. There is also no guarantee that you will progress to the next stages of the recruitment process; however, we will keep you informed at each stage.
Take a look at a short video about Probation Service Officer Role here
About the role
Probation services officers can help make a real difference to peoples’ lives. It’s not always easy to help someone turn their life around, but it can be immensely rewarding.
Probation services officers are required to work within a variety of settings. There may be opportunities for positions within Probation Delivery Units (PDU), Courts, Prisons, Approved Premises etc. depending on business requirement.
Probation services officers are based in a wide variety of settings, listed below:
  • Accredited Programmes
  • Structured Interventions & Attendance Centres
  • Community Accommodation Services
  • Community Integration and Contracts
  • Contracts
  • Courts
  • Integrated Offender Management
  • Performance & Quality
  • Personality Disorder Projects
  • Prisons
  • Public Protection (Custody)
  • Public Protection (Community)
  • The Homeless Prevention Taskforce
  • Service Centre
  • Unpaid Work (community payback)
We’re looking for empathetic, patient and resilient people to join us as probation services officers. As well as making a difference to others, the role offers plenty of on-the-job training and a real chance to build a career in the Probation Service.
As a PSO, you’ll have a similar job to a fully qualified probation officer. The main difference is you’ll work with medium and lower risk people of probation. That’s not to say it’ll be easy. There’s no doubt this is a challenging role.
Day-to-day, you’ll manage a caseload of offenders before and after sentence. We’ll look to you to assess and manage risks, provide information to courts and work closely with agencies throughout the justice system. You’ll also do everything you can to support offenders. This could involve everything from providing practical advice about housing and employment to simply listening and empathising.

About the job

Job summary

On the Commercial Fast Stream, you’ll learn how to negotiate contracts ranging from hundreds of thousands right up to millions of pounds. You will help to keep UK citizens safe, build important public assets such as schools, railways, roads and hospitals – and support delivery of essential frontline public services.

The specific towns and cities depend on the department you are posted to and its office locations. The Fast Stream evolves continually, so postings can vary from year to year.

As an indication, in 2026 new fast streamers were posted to government offices in the following regions: East Midlands, London, North West, Scotland, South East, West Midlands, and Yorkshire and the Humber.

On occasion, some individuals may need to move location. We aim to align postings with your preferences whenever possible; however, final decisions must support our wider business needs. Please note that Fast Streamers cannot choose their department or their specific role.

Job description

Every year, we invest in excess of £300 billion to provide public services to the UK. The central Government alone invests over £49 billion each year on goods and services. Therefore, effective management of commercial activities is incredibly important. As a Commercial Fast Streamer, you’ll play a vital role ensuring the Civil Service achieves value for money for the public.

You’ll be joining us at an exciting time as our teams work to transform public procurement to maximise innovation and deliver wider economic benefits for the UK.

Commercial capability is increasingly recognised as the top skill sought by employers across all sectors. Building commercial expertise and skills is one of the top priorities for the Civil Service. You will learn how to negotiate substantial contracts and ensure the government is in tune with its markets. You may also be responsible for managing relationships between the Civil Service and some of the biggest companies in the world.

The commercial activity carried out by the Civil Service attracts a huge amount of press and political attention. Applying sound judgement in commercial matters is vital in protecting the government’s reputation.

We aim to put all successful candidates through Security Clearance (SC). However, if you are ineligible for SC, please do not be deterred from applying; we have plenty of exciting roles available that only require standard Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) pre-employment checks. You can find more information about vetting clearance levels here: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/united-kingdom-security-vetting-clearance-levels

Existing civil servants can apply without a degree

Benefits include the Civil Service Pension Scheme, flexible working arrangements, season ticket loans, sports and social activities, childcare assistance and more.

Selection process details

Application Process

There are several phases in the Fast Stream application process. Some of these assessments are multimedia in that they present information in video, audio, graphical or visual formats, as well as text. We hope you find it an engaging process and one that gives you a real insight into the role of a fast streamer.

At the initial application stage you will be asked to complete some background information which will include some diversity questions - which are for monitoring purposes only and will have no bearing on selection outcomes - along with the opportunity to identify your preferences in terms of the different Fast Stream schemes. You can choose up to three.

When you apply please register with a personal email address, and not a work or university email address.

Assessment Phases

There are 2 online tests:

Work-based scenarios - This test measures interpersonal skills, utilising video based scenarios and you are required to assess the effectiveness of various responses.

Case Study assessment - In this test you are required to take work based scenarios on an imaginary role, learning and responding to a series of challenges and situations and adapting to the changes you are presented with.

Additional information - depending on the schemes you have chosen, there may be additional information to be completed, or an intermediate sift process. More information on the schemes that require additional information can be found https://www.civil-service-careers.gov.uk/fast-stream/fs-how-to-apply/fs-additional-information/

Fast Stream Assessment Centre - if you pass the above stages you'll be invited to attend a half day assessment centre. This will be conducted virtually online. The Fast Stream Assessment Centre (FSAC) reflects some of the key elements of a Fast Stream role and will consist of a written exercise, oral briefing exercise and a personal development conversation. Information will be presented via an app that you will be able to access remotely.

Final Selection Board - most schemes will then require a Final Selection Board . We'll ask you to attend this final assessment if you reach the required standard at FSAC. More information on the Final Selection Boards can be found https://www.civil-service-careers.gov.uk/fast-stream/fs-how-to-apply/fs-final-selection-board/

Join our vessel crew and help support the important work that protects Scotland's seas and advances marine science.

The Marine Directorate is the Scottish Government's lead marine management organisation, bringing together scientific research, compliance, policy and management to support the sustainable use and protection of Scotland's marine environment. We are recruiting Seaman 1A positions to join our Marine Research Vessel fleet, working at sea as part of a professional onboard team that enables the successful delivery of scientific research programmes across Scottish waters.

As a Seaman 1A, you will play a key role in supporting deck, fishing and scientific operations aboard our research vessels, working closely with vessel officers, crew and scientific staff. Your contribution will help ensure the safe and effective operation of the vessel and the successful collection of the scientific data and evidence that underpins marine science, policy development and decision-making in Scotland.

This role will be based on-board MRV Scotia or MRV Alba na Mara, operating primarily in Scottish waters as part of a marine working pattern aligned to vessel operations.

  • Assist with the loading, stowing, deploying, recovery, discharging and the maintenance of fishing and science equipment.
  • Undertake all aspects of deck maintenance, including cleaning, painting, greasing, storing, ropework, etc as required by Commanding Officer or First Officer (Executive) and directed by CPO (Deck).

description:
Additional Information: This hotel is owned and operated by an independent franchisee, GVA Hospitality. The franchisee is a separate company and a separate employer from Marriott International, Inc. The Santa María, A Luxury Collection Hotel & Golf Resort, is seeking a motivated and experienced Assistant Director of Food & Beverage to support the Director of Food & Beverage in managing the hotel’s Food & Beverage operations.
This position is responsible for assisting with daily operations, supervising and developing associates, maintaining high service standards, and ensuring exceptional guest experiences in accordance with the hotel’s luxury service expectations.

* Assist the Director of Food & Beverage in overseeing and coordinating daily operations across restaurants, bars, banquets, and other Food & Beverage outlets.

* Monitor guest satisfaction, address service concerns, and implement improvement initiatives.
* Support associate training, coaching, performance management, and professional development.
* Assist with budget monitoring, cost control, inventory management, and operational performance.
* Collaborate with the Culinary, Events, and other hotel departments to ensure seamless operations and memorable guest experiences.
* Promote teamwork, accountability, continuous improvement, and a culture of personalized service.

* Conversational English proficiency, with the ability to communicate effectively with guests and associates.
