title: 202610: Prison Officer - HMP Manchester
description:
• Job grade: Administrative Officer
  • Contract type: Permanent
  • Type of role: Operational Delivery, Other
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time, Job share, Part-time
  • Number of jobs available: 20

Location

Manchester, North West England, M60 9AH

About the job

Job summary

Please see job description

Job description

Prison officer - HMP Manchester

HMP Manchester, 1 Southall St, Cheetham Hill, Manchester M60 9AH

Starting salary: £36,816 (for a 39 hour week inc 20% unsocial)

City/Town: Manchester

Region: North East

Vacancy type: Merit

Sponsorship is not guaranteed, and applicants are responsible for ensuring they have, and can maintain, the appropriate right to work in the UK.

Skilled Worker visa sponsorship may be available for this role, subject to eligibility and in line with the UK Immigration Rules in force at the time of application. However, due to current immigration requirements and recruitment timescales, candidates who require Skilled Worker visa sponsorship are unlikely to be sponsored if applying to this campaign.

Applicants are strongly encouraged to consider their right to work in the UK carefully before applying. You can read more about Skilled Worker visas and eligibility criteria at .

The Department will continue to comply with UK Immigration Rules applied in the UK and Civil Service.

Due to the security status of this prison a Counter-Terrorism Check (CTC vetting) will need to be undertaken. Proof that you have been a resident in the UK for the last 3 years is needed to complete the CTC vetting process. Applicants who do not meet the residency requirement will not be able to take up post at this prison. (please refer to CTC section below)

An extraordinary job. Done by someone like you.

Prison officers protect the public and help make an impact on prisoners' lives.

If you have the integrity, skills and strength of character we’re looking for, this fast-paced role could be the start of a successful career.

Someone like you

There’s no such thing as a typical prison officer. Our officers come from different walks of life, just like the offenders they work with. Whether you’re a parent, a teacher, have worked in retail, the armed forces, or just feel like you’re a natural people person, you’ll have the empathy, self-confidence, great communication skills and resilience we want.

No matter the challenge, you’ll take the time to build constructive, positive and professional relationships with prisoners who could be at the lowest point in their lives.

Teamwork plays a vital role in this environment, so you’ll need to be fully committed to supporting your colleagues and understand the importance of acting as one team to keep the prison, and everyone who works here safe. You will be required to work various shifts and some weekends.

An extraordinary job

In this unique career, you’ll have the opportunity to carry out many different roles in any one day. One minute you’re a peacekeeper, the next you’re a counsellor or a teacher. You’ll work directly with prisoners in a unique environment, helping to protect the public and make a positive impact.

Find out more about this varied role and day-to-day life as a prison officer.

Job details

Eligibility

To become a prison officer, you will need to:

  • be at least 18 years old at the point you commence employment
  • meet the Civil Service Nationality requirements (see nationality requirements section below)
  • as this is a physically active job, you will need to pass a medical and fitness assessment as part of the application process
  • meet the required eyesight standard in both eyes (both with and without corrective lenses)
  • For safety reasons, everyone training to be a prison officer needs a suitable standard of hearing (without the use of hearing aids)
  • Whilst tattoos are permitted, including those that are visible, they must not be deemed as offensive, discriminatory, violent, or intimidating in any way. Facial tattoos are generally not acceptable, except where this is for cultural, religious, or medical reasons.

Due to the security status of this prison a Counter-Terrorism Check (CTC vetting) will need to be undertaken. Proof that you have been a resident in the UK for the last 3 years is needed to complete the CTC vetting process. Applicants who do not meet the residency requirement will not be able to take up post at this prison. (please refer to CTC section below)

Travel to Work

Some prison establishments are situated in rural locations with limited public transport options; therefore a driving licence and own transport is beneficial but is not an essential requirement of the role (unless specified). Please note that shift start, and finish times are fixed, and it is your responsibility to get to and from your place of work on time for the start of your shift. Please carefully consider the location of this vacancy and your transport options before applying.

Nationality requirements

This job is broadly open to the following groups:

  • UK nationals
  • nationals of the Republic of Ireland
  • nationals of Commonwealth countries who have the right to work in the UK
  • nationals of the EU, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein and family members of those nationalities who have made a valid application for settled or pre-settled status under the European Union Settlement Scheme (EUSS)
  • individuals with limited leave to remain or indefinite leave to remain who were eligible to apply for EUSS on or before 31 December 2020
  • Turkish nationals, and certain family members of Turkish nationals, who have accrued the right to work in the Civil Service

Further information on nationality requirements .

Essential skills

You don’t need qualifications to become a prison officer. Personal qualities are more important. You need to show:

  • communication and influencing skills
  • commitment to quality
  • effective decision-making
  • care and understanding

Pay

The initial training is 37 hours a week. After training, you can choose to work 37, 39 or 41 hours a week. Your annual salary will reflect your weekly hours.

  • · 37 hours a week = £34,928 a year
  • · 39 hours a week = £36,816 a year
  • · 41 hours a week = £39,334 a year

All salary figures quoted include any additional allowances that at applicable to the role/location.

Prisons operate 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. This means you will have to cover various shift patterns that will include evenings, some nights, weekends and public holidays (these days are added to your holiday allowance). Most prisons work with a changing shift pattern of 39 hours a week.

You may also have opportunities to work additional paid hours.

Benefits

  • 25 days’ annual holiday (rising to 30 days after 10 years’ service)
  • paid time off for public holidays and 1 extra privilege day
  • Civil Service pension with employer contributions of 28.97%
  • cycle to work scheme, travel loans and other benefits

Read more about prison officer benefits.

Assessment Process

During the recruitment process you will be assessed on the behaviours, strengths and abilities you need to become an effective prison officer. These include:

  • communicating and influencing
  • managing a quality service
  • making effective decisions
  • caring

Your natural strengths are assessed to find out what motivates and energises you. We will also assess your numerical, written English and spoken English abilities.

Online Tests

Once you have completed your initial application form, you will be invited to complete stage 1 of the online test, to see if you have the basic judgement and numerical skills expected of a prison officer.

If you are successful, we will invite you to the stage 2 online test (values-based assessment). We use this assessment to understand how well you demonstrate the values needed to be an effective prison officer.

If you successfully pass the Values Based Assessment (VBA), you'll be eligible to progress to the Online Assessment Centre (OAC), where we'll assess the behaviours, strengths and abilities needed to become a Prison Officer.

As demand for assessment places can vary, candidates who achieve a higher pre-determined VBA score may be invited to the OAC sooner. This approach is applied consistently and fairly to all applicants within the campaign.

If you meet the required VBA pass mark but are not selected for an initial invitation, you will remain under consideration and may be invited to attend an OAC as additional assessment capacity becomes available.

If you were unsuccessful at the stage 2 online test in the last 6 months, you can now re‑apply.

The online assessment centre (OAC)

On successful completion of the online test, we will invite you to an online assessment centre where we test to see if you have the abilities, behaviours and strengths to be a prison officer.

Read more about the application process.

Following the successful completion of your online assessments, you may be invited to attend HMP Manchester to complete your medical and fitness assessments. This will cover an eyesight test, hearing test and basic health screening, including a blood pressure check.

Available dates are 7th, 8th and 9th December 2026.

If you are invited to complete your Medical and Fitness test at HMP Manchester you will also:

· Take a guided tour and gain an insight into working within the Prison environment.

· Meet and speak with serving Prison Officers about the role.

· Complete your medical and fitness assessments.

· Begin your pre-employment checks if you successfully pass the required assessments.

Please note: Places at HMP Manchester are limited and cannot be guaranteed. If no local appointments are available, you may be required to attend one of our National Fitness Assessment Centres to complete your assessments

Please note we are not able to facilitate medical and fitness assessments outside of the UK. Applicants will be required to attend a UK based medical and fitness assessment centre to progress their application.

Find out more about the medical assessment and fitness test on the application information centre


High security prisons requiring CTC vetting

If your application is successful, you will need to undergo and clear pre-employment checks. This will include His Majesty’s Prison and Probation Service Enhanced Level 2 vetting, and due to the security status of the establishment Counter-Terrorism Check (CTC vetting) is also required. Proof that you have been a resident in the UK for the last 3 years is needed to complete the CTC vetting process. The residency requirements refer to the period immediately before an application is made, and not any other three-year period, or any other accumulation of time spent in the UK.

If you have been out of the country for a significant period of time (usually up to one year) and maintained your UK residency you may still be considered for vetting clearance. For example:

  • to return in the future
  • taken a gap year before or following university
  • travelled for a year
  • spent time overseas visiting family

This is not an exhaustive list.

Candidates must be able to provide correct and up to date documentation when requested during the application process.

Job offers: merit vacancy

This is a merit job vacancy. If you are successful at the online assessment centre, you will be added to a merit list based on your score.

When all applicants have completed the assessment centre, the prison will make job offers to individuals with the highest scores first when positions become available.

You can stay on the merit list for 12 months. After this, you’ll need to apply again.

If your application is unsuccessful at the sift/Interview stage, a six month waiting period will be applied during which time you will not be allowed to submit any further applications for prison officer positions.

Operational Support Grade Role

Our Online Assessment Centre (OAC), will not only assess you against the key criteria to become a prison officer but will also determine your suitability for appointment as an operational support grade OSG If following attendance at your OAC, you are unsuccessful in your application to become a prison officer, we may instead offer you an alternative role as an OSG.


Medical and Fitness

Once we identify a vacancy for you, we will invite you to complete a medical and fitness test. This will cover an eyesight test, hearing test and basic health screening, including a blood pressure check.

Please note we are not able to facilitate medical and fitness assessments outside of the UK. Applicants will be required to attend a UK based medical and fitness assessment centre to progress their application.

Find out more about the medical assessment and fitness test on the application information centre

Working for the Civil Service

The Civil Service Code sets out the standards of behaviour expected of Civil Servants.

We recruit by merit on the basis of fair and open competition, as outlined in the Civil Service Commission's recruitment principles. If you feel the recruitment process has breached the recruitment principles you can raise a formal complaint in the following order:

  1. Shared Services Connected Ltd: call 0845 241 5358 (Monday to Friday 8am - 6pm) or email Moj-recruitment-vetting-enquiries@gov.sscl.com
  2. Ministry of Justice Resourcing
  3. The Civil Service Commission.

Diversity & Inclusion

The Civil Service is committed to attract, retain and invest in talent wherever it is found. To learn more please see the Civil Service People Plan and the Civil Service Diversity and Inclusion Strategy

Reasonable Adjustment Support

As a Disability Confident employer, the MoJ is committed to ensuring that everyone can demonstrate their skills, talent, and abilities. Offering reasonable adjustment support to candidates when they apply for one of our jobs is just one way, we do this.

Before completing online tests or attending an online assessment centre, it is essential to arrange reasonable adjustment support. Due to practical and logistical constraints, our assessors cannot accommodate requests on the day of the assessment centre. Therefore, we kindly request that you let us know in plenty of time if adjustments are required. This will help ensure the right support is in place for you when you need it.

Applying for reasonable adjustment support has been made simple. Just select ‘yes’ in the application form when it asks if you think you might need it.

The jobholder must be able to fulfil all spoken aspects of the role with confidence in English or (when specified in Wales) Welsh.

Allowance Details

Additional Information

title: Software Engineer I – Flight Management Systems – m/f/d
description:

Our new brand identity pairs that heritage with real momentum, as we build technology that helps pilots navigate with confidence, aircraft operate more efficiently, and operators stay ahead of change. With our systems on board 90% of the world's aircraft, your work here has reach that's rare to find anywhere else.

Focusing on our customers, investing in innovation, and building a culture of accountability and performance is how we're shaping what comes next.

Every horizon. Every mission. Every day.

Electronic Solutions develops the avionics, navigation systems, sensors and electromagnetic defense technology that help aircraft perform safely and with precision. Our systems are on board 90% of the world's aircraft — serving commercial aviation, defense and space operators from integrated flight deck platforms with 30-plus years in service to radiation-hardened systems trusted for human spaceflight.

We have an opportunity for a Junior Software Engineer - Flight Management Systems to join our Honeywell Aerospace team in Brno. You will become a part of the Flight Management Systems (FMS) team that designs, develops, and integrates a flight management system for the civil and defense customers, allowing you to develop knowledge in an exciting industry segment.

title: Assistant Investigator
description:
• Job grade: Executive Officer

About the job

Job summary

Are you an organised and inquisitive individual with experience applying investigative skills and techniques to achieve positive outcomes?

Do you thrive in a fast-paced environment, enjoy analysing information and evidence, and have the confidence to manage competing priorities?

Would you like to play a key role in investigations that help protect lives, support environmental protection and uphold maritime legislation across the United Kingdom?

If so, we’d love to hear from you!

As an Assistant Investigator within the Regulatory Compliance Investigation Team (RCIT), you will work alongside experienced investigators and regulatory compliance professionals supporting criminal and regulatory investigations into significant breaches of maritime legislation. This is a unique opportunity to contribute to high-profile investigations, support enforcement outcomes and help improve safety, environmental protection and compliance across the maritime sector.

No two days are the same. You could be gathering evidence, supporting interviews, reviewing intelligence, assisting with financial lines of enquiry, undertaking compliance assurance activity, or helping prepare evidential case files for enforcement action and prosecution.

The Maritime and Coastguard Agency (MCA) implements the government’s maritime safety policy in the United Kingdom and works to prevent the loss of life and occurrence of pollution on the coast and at sea.

Safer lives. Safer Ships. Cleaner Seas.

Our vision is to be a world-leading organisation, accelerating the transition to sustainable shipping with non-negotiable safety standards. We put our people, our customers and our planet at the heart of everything we do.

Joining our department comes with many benefits, including:

  • Employer pension contribution of 28.97% of your salary. Read more about Civil Service Pensions here
  • 25 days annual leave, increasing by 1 day each year of service (up to a maximum of 30 days annual leave), plus 8 bank holidays a privilege day for the King’s birthday.
  • Flexible working options where we encourage a great work-life balance.

Read more in the Benefits section below!

Find out more about what it's like working at MCA roles: MCA Homepage , Civil Service Careers

Job description

Working within the direction of Lead Investigators, you will support all aspects of the investigative process and contribute to ensuring investigations are conducted professionally, lawfully and in accordance with regulatory requirements.

You will support regulatory compliance investigations into significant breaches of maritime legislation, contributing to enforcement action and prosecutions where authorised. You may also assist with the preparation of evidence for court proceedings and support Lead Investigators throughout the prosecution process where required.

Your responsibilities will include, but aren’t limited to:

  • Assist in investigations by undertaking a wide range of tasks under the direction of supervisor/line manager.
  • Assisting in interviewing of suspects under caution.
  • Assisting in the completion of criminal files of evidence by undertaking allocated.
  • To aid the RCIT’s Lead Investigators by obtaining statements of evidence for criminal investigations.
  • To assist in the examination, preservation and continuity of evidence and exhibits such as CCTV recovered during an investigation in accordance with procedure.

For further information on the role, please read the role profile. Please note that the role profile is for information purposes only - whilst all elements are relevant to the role, they may not all be assessed during the recruitment process. This job advert will detail exactly what will be assessed during the recruitment process.

Person specification

Essential qualifications/licenses:

  1. A valid passport for international travel
  2. A full UK driving license

You will be required to provide evidence that you hold any essential licenses at some point during the recruitment process. If you cannot provide evidence, your application will be withdrawn.

Required experience:

To be successful in this role you will need to have the following experience:

  1. Strong investigative skills with experience interviewing suspects under caution
  2. Interest in applying investigative expertise within the maritime industry
  3. Team player with excellent interpersonal and communication skills
  4. Confident in handling challenging situations and adapting communication style accordingly
  5. Highly organised with strong IT skills, particularly in Microsoft Excel and MS Teams
  6. Detail-oriented, producing clear and high-quality documents and reports
  7. Able to manage a demanding workload and prioritise effectively in a fast-paced environment
  8. Knowledge and experience of legislation including Police and Criminal Evidence Act (PACE) and Criminal Procedure and Investigations Act (CPIA).

Additional Information

Operational Delivery Profession (ODP) is the largest and most diverse professional community across the Civil Service. Many of us will have an association with several professional communities or specialisms, ODP applies to all public facing roles / or a role that is primarily aligned to supporting the work of those with public facing roles. All critical to the delivery of UK public services.

Working hours, office attendance and travel requirements

Full time roles consist of 37 hours per week.

Whilst we welcome applications from those looking to work with us on a part time basis, there is a business requirement for the successful candidate to be able to work at least 30 hours per week.

This role is suitable for hybrid working, which is a non-contractual arrangement where a combination of workplace and home-based working can be accommodated subject to business requirements.

The expectation at present is a minimum of 60% of your working time a month will be spent at either your designated workplace (one of the locations cited in the advert) or, when required for business reasons, in another office/work location/visiting stakeholders. Your designated workplace will be your contractual place of work. There may be occasions where you are required to attend above the minimum expectation.

This role follows a compressed working pattern of 74 hours over two weeks, with every other Friday off. You'll work 8.22 hours per day, across five days in week one and four days in week two.

Regular travel to other offices will be required, which may involve overnight stays.

If you have a question about hybrid working, part time/job share hours, flexible working, travelling for work, or require a reasonable adjustment, please contact the Vacancy Holder during the recruitment process to avoid possible disappointment later in the process should your working arrangements not be compatible with the requirements of the role (see below for contact details).

Please note that we will only offer sponsorship for a skilled worker visa where a role has been deemed to be business critical. This role does not meet that category, and we will not sponsor a visa. Therefore, this role is not open to applications from those who require sponsorship – candidates must ensure they have the appropriate right to work in the UK before applying. Should you apply for this role and be found to require sponsorship, your application will be rejected and any provisional offer of employment withdrawn.

This check will provide information about employees who have been dismissed for fraud or dishonesty offences. This check also applies to employees who resign or otherwise leave before being dismissed for fraud or dishonesty had their employment continued. Any applicant’s details held on the IFD will be refused employment. A candidate is not eligible to apply for a role within the Civil Service if the application is made within a 5-year period following a dismissal for carrying out internal fraud against government.

All external applicants and current employees of accredited non-departmental public bodies (NDPBs) will be required to undergo a Social Media Check. A Social Media Check is a review of your publicly available online activity, typically across platforms like LinkedIn, Facebook, X (formerly Twitter), Instagram, and others. The purpose is to identify any public posts or content that could raise concerns for employers, such as:

  • Hate speech or discriminatory behaviour
  • Threats or acts of violence
  • Illegal activity or substance misuse
  • Sexually explicit material
  • Extremist views or affiliations

Importantly, this check does not involve hacking into your accounts or accessing private messages. It only considers content you have chosen to make public. Employers use this kind of screening to help ensure their workplace remains safe, inclusive, and aligned with company values. It’s not about judging your personality or lifestyle - it’s about checking for potential red flags that might affect the role or company culture. About the job

Job summary

About Cabinet Office Digital:

Cabinet Office Digital sits at the heart of UK government, delivering user-centred digital services, robust technology infrastructure, and progressive digital capability across the Cabinet Office and beyond. Our mission is to make government work better for citizens by modernising legacy systems, championing innovative technologies including secure cloud and AI, and embedding world-class security into every phase of service delivery. We foster an inclusive, collaborative, and agile environment where technical excellence and public value go hand in hand.

The Role:

As the Information Security Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC) Manager, you will serve as the departmental subject matter expert on cyber risk management, security policy, and enterprise assurance. Reporting directly to the Head of Information Security, you will lead and develop the GRC team to drive the departmental cyber governance strategy, ensuring critical systems and digital services remain resilient against evolving threats.

Bridging the gap between executive strategy and technical implementation, you will provide authoritative risk advice to System Owners, Senior Information Risk Owners (SIROs), and Risk Committees. You will oversee central compliance with the Government Functional Standard for Security (GovS 007), lead the GovAssure programme across the department, and embed Secure by Design (SbD) principles across all digital initiatives, while leveraging frameworks such as the NCSC Cyber Assessment Framework (CAF), ISO/IEC 27001, and NIST.

This role offers an exceptional opportunity to shape cyber resilience at the centre of government, leading high-impact assurance initiatives and fostering a culture of proactive risk management across dynamic digital transformation programmes.

Job description

Strategic Delivery & Governance

Drive the delivery of the departmental cyber security governance strategy, establishing frameworks that support the organisational risk appetite while ensuring direct alignment with GovS 007 and the NCSC CAF.

Manage GovAssure across the Cabinet Office, directing the central programme for the whole department and providing practical support and guidance to service owners.

Embed Secure by Design (SbD), ensuring security is integrated across the entire lifecycle of departmental digital and data projects.

Represent Cyber Security on key governance boards (e.g., Departmental Risk Committee), presenting complex risk trade-offs to non-technical leadership.

Manage commercial requirements, owning the allocated budget and acting as the contract manager for all GRC tooling and security education platforms.

Risk Assessment & Management

Own the cyber risk framework, defining and maintaining the methodologies, standards, and thresholds that departmental teams must work within.

Lead GRC platform engineering, driving the administration, configuration, and continuous maturity of the central GRC tool to automate workflows and improve risk visibility.

Mature the departmental Cyber Risk Register, ensuring risk owners accurately identify, accept, or treat exposures in a timely manner.

Drive third-party and supply chain assurance, establishing cyber risk protocols across the enterprise and high-value procurement contracts.

Provide actionable risk intelligence, delivering regular insights on threat trends and control effectiveness to the Head of Information Security and senior leadership.

Facilitate risk workshops, leading regular sessions with technical and business leads to identify emerging threats and maintain high-quality risk data.
Compliance, Policy & Assurance.

Author and enforce departmental cyber security policies, ensuring they remain practical and mapped against GovS 007, CAF, ISO 27001, and NIST CSF.

Track and integrate audit findings, working closely with operational security teams to record outputs from IT Health Checks (ITHCs), penetration tests, and external audits, ensuring remediation is tracked.

Govern cyber compliance and threat frameworks, leading on cyber-specific legislation and enterprise vulnerability management standards. Work alongside Data

Privacy to support UK GDPR/DPA 2018, ensuring operational alignment with CIS Controls and MITRE ATT&CK.

Lead the security awareness programme, ensuring staff understand current threats and secure data handling practices through effective, metrics-driven education.

Team Leadership & Stakeholder Management

Line manage and mentor a team of security specialists, supporting continuous technical development and professional growth.

Build strategic partnerships with external bodies, including the Government Security Group, DCMS, the NCSC, and partner agencies.

Practice inclusive leadership, building a culture of shared accountability and continuous improvement in security outcomes.

Person specification

Essential Criteria (Mandatory)

  • Information Security Leadership: Extensive experience managing Information Security, GRC, or risk functions within the public sector or large, highly regulated organisations.

  • Risk Management in Digital Change: Proven experience governing risk management principles for complex digital transformation programmes, including AI integrations, automated decision-making systems, or legacy migrations.

  • Stakeholder Communication: Strong ability to translate technical cyber vulnerabilities and risks into clear, business-focused narratives for non-technical senior leaders.

  • Supply Chain Assurance: Practical experience creating, establishing, and managing security risk frameworks for supply chains and third-party vendors.

  • Core Certifications: Must hold one of the following: CISM, CRISC, ISC2 CGRC, or CISSP.

  • Core Framework Mastery: Deep, practical knowledge of GovS 007, the NCSC CAF, GovAssure, Secure by Design, and ISO/IEC 27001/27005.

Desirable Criteria

  • GRC Platforms: Hands-on experience administering, configuring, and maturing enterprise GRC software tools.

  • Supplementary Frameworks: A good working knowledge of the NIST CSF, CIS Controls, and MITRE ATT&CK.

  • Cloud Security: Familiarity with cloud security risk management (e.g., CSA CCSK or CSP specific certifications).

  • Enterprise Architecture: Awareness of enterprise architecture methodologies (e.g., TOGAF).

  • Data Privacy: Working knowledge of DPA 2018 / UK GDPR principles in an information security context.

  • AI Governance: Practical knowledge of AI risk management frameworks (e.g., NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001).

Additional information:

Cabinet Office policy is that a minimum 60% of your working time should be spent at your principal workplace. For some roles, due to their nature and the business need, this may be up to 100%. Requirements to attend other locations for official business will also count towards this level of attendance.

Qualifications

Proven Track Record: Extensive experience managing information security, GRC, or risk functions within the public sector or large, highly regulated enterprises.

Risk Decision-Making: Demonstrable experience governing risk management principles across complex digital transformation programmes, specifically including AI integrations, automated decision-making systems, and legacy migrations.

GRC Platform Engineering (Desirable): Practical experience administering, configuring, and maturing enterprise GRC tooling.

Senior Stakeholder Engagement: Proven ability to translate technical cyber vulnerabilities into plain-English, business-focused risk narratives.

Supply Chain Security: Hands-on experience establishing supply-chain risk assurance frameworks.

About the job

Job summary

Working at HM Treasury puts you at the heart of government, making a difference to the UK economy and ultimately to people’s lives right across the UK.

Jobs at the Treasury are fast-paced, fun and can offer unparalleled perspective – not least the opportunity to advise Ministers on the decisions which directly determine the UK’s prosperity. Deep in our DNA is a commitment to empowering our people: maximising individual and collective impact, with interesting work no matter your role or seniority.

Day-to-day you could be supporting Ministers to decide the right level of a specific tax or line of government spending; helping maintain the stability of financial markets; analysing the long-term trends impacting the future of the economy; or enabling this work as part of our vital corporate functions.

We are a high-performing department and proud to have outstanding staff from a wide range of backgrounds. We are also a friendly, inclusive and sociable workplace that prides itself on fostering great team spirit. Our two largest offices are 1 Horse Guards Road in London, opposite St James’ Park, and the Darlington Economic Campus, which also contains eight other departments. We work seamlessly across all our sites, including Norwich, Birmingham and Leeds, as one Treasury.

We are both a 1,000-year-old institution and dynamic, forward-looking economics and finance ministry, with a strong direction set by our organisational strategy, the Future Treasury Vision. The 21st century offers huge opportunities and poses new challenges for the UK. Working at the Treasury is your chance to help the country chart the right course.

Job description

This is an exciting role leading HM Treasury’s strategic sponsorship of the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR). The OBR is an independent body responsible for producing the official economic and fiscal forecasts on which government policy is based. By supporting the OBR to fulfil it’s remit and advising Ministers on its role, the postholder therefore plays an important role delivering HMT’s objectives for growth and sustainable public finances.

The role will provide the postholder with the opportunity to directly advise Ministers and senior officials on sensitive issues, work across different teams and be at the heart of the Budget and forecast process. It would suit candidates who thrive when working independently across a varied workload.

The key accountabilities are:

  1. Lead HM Treasury’s sponsorship of the OBR, acting as the departmental expert on the OBR’s remit and legislation and providing regular reporting to the Executive Management Board (EMB) such as on risks to the organisation.
  2. Provide high-quality advice to Ministers and senior officials on all OBR-related issues, using judgement to provide balanced advice on politically sensitive, high-profile and fast-moving developments
  3. Lead oversight of the OBR’s budget, working closely with HMT Finance to scrutinise performance against spending plans, advise senior leaders on financial risks and prepare for negotiations on the OBR’s budget at the next Spending Review.
  4. Build and maintain strong relationships with OBR counterparts, driving effective collaboration across HMT and the OBR, including as joint Secretariat for weekly meetings between senior officials at the OBR and HMT.
  5. Lead on the government’s public narrative with regards to the OBR, including briefing Ministers ahead of parliamentary appearances, drafting government responses to inquiries and responding to urgent press queries.
  6. Coordinate cross-cutting fiscal event and forecast processes, working across HM Treasury and with the OBR to agree the forecast timetable, deliver key briefing products and ensure an effective process for factchecking the OBR’s ‘Economic and Fiscal Outlook’.
  7. Contribute to Fiscal Statistics and Policy (FSP) team and the wider Fiscal Group. The post holder will help to ensure Fiscal Group is an excellent place to work, including contributing to corporate workstreams.

Location

Birmingham, Bristol, Cambridge, Canary Wharf, Cardiff , Carmarthen, Colchester, Croydon, Durham, Eastbourne, Exeter, Folkestone, Hull, Lancaster, Leeds, Liverpool, Manchester, Newcastle-upon Tyne, Norwich, Nottingham, Oxford, Plymouth, Preston, Sheffield, Southampton, St Austell, Stoke-on-Trent, Swansea, Wembley and Wrexham.

About the job

Job summary

Discover a career in your hands at HMRC. Whether you're seeking purpose, growth, or a workplace that gives you a true sense of belonging, hear from some of our employees as they share their story about what it’s really like to work at HMRC.

Visit our YouTube channel to watch the full series and come and discover your potential.

This role is part of HMRC Valuation Office, formerly known as the Valuation Office Agency. We have recently integrated into HMRC.

HMRC Valuation Office are the public sector’s property valuation experts and advisers with a vision to be a world-leading provider of public sector valuations. Our work is vital to the collection of over £60 billion of revenue which goes back into communities, touching every citizen and every business across England and Wales.

For further information about our Development Programmes please click here HMRC – Valuation Office , Civil Service Careers

Job description

Role Overview

We are looking for graduates who have completed, or are due to complete, a RICS-accredited degree aligned to the RICS Valuation pathway or any of the pathways listed in the Essential Criteria section below. Our graduate training programme offers the opportunity to develop your professional skills and gain practical experience across a range of property and valuation work and includes structured support through the RICS Assessment of Professional Competence (APC) programme, enabling you to work towards achieving Chartered Surveyor (MRICS) status.

The Valuation Office (VO) offers a dynamic and fast-paced working environment where no two days are the same. As a Graduate Surveyor, you will undertake property inspections, collect and analyse property, rental and market evidence, and apply valuation principles, legislation and professional judgement to support accurate valuation and taxation decisions. Working as part of a supportive and knowledgeable team, you will manage your own case load, prioritising activities to ensure compliance with statutory timescales and organisational commitments.

The work you undertake is subject to business need and will see you play an active role in delivering valuation outcome as part of a high-quality surveying and valuation service. Working alongside Chartered Surveyors will strengthen your technical and professional capabilities along with providing the opportunity to build professional networks.

You can find out more about our Graduate Programme and how to apply by attending one of our live events prior to the closing date click here to view dates, times and sign up . Please note bookings will close at midday the day before each event. The link will be sent by 9:30am on the day of the event. Please check your spam or junk folder before contacting us.

Key responsibilities

  • Undertake property inspections, measurements and data collection activities to support accurate valuation and casework decisions.
  • Research, analyse and interpret property, rental and market evidence to inform valuations and recommendations.
  • Progress valuation and taxation cases, reviewing evidence and reaching reasoned conclusions supported by legislation, valuation practice, and professional judgement.
  • Prepare reports, case notes and valuation documentation to support decision making and maintain accurate records.
  • Communicate effectively with customers, professional representatives and colleagues to gather information, explain decisions and resolve queries.
  • Support the preparation of appeals and tribunal cases, including compiling evidence and, where appropriate, attending tribunals as an advocate or expert witness.
  • Collaborate with colleagues and specialist teams to deliver high-quality surveying and valuation services.
  • Manage and prioritise a varied workload, ensuring deadlines are met.
  • Maintain and develop technical knowledge of valuation principles, legislation and professional standards relevant to the role.
  • Actively participate in the RICS Assessment of Professional Competence (APC) programme and undertake continuous professional development activities to achieve Chartered Surveyor (MRICS) status.

Person specification

To be successful in this role, you will be naturally curious, motivated to learn, and enthusiastic about developing your knowledge of surveying, valuation and the wider property profession. You will be committed to your personal and professional development, proactively seeking opportunities to build the skills, experience and technical expertise required to succeed in the role and support your progression towards Chartered Surveyor (MRICS) status through the Assessment of Professional Competence (APC).

Essential Requirements

We are looking for candidates who meet the below eligibility criteria:

  • Exhibit sound analytical skills with the ability to evaluate information, drawing on evidence to make reasoned decisions, solve problems and reach balanced conclusions.
  • Be able to communicate complex information clearly and effectively both vernally and in writing, adapting your approach to different audiences and building positive working relationships with a range of people.
  • Have well - developed organisational skills, with the ability to prioritise competing demands, demonstrating personal responsibility, attention to detail and the ability to deliver high-quality outcomes to agreed timescales.
  • Demonstrate the ability to work effectively with colleagues and stakeholders, contributing to shared goals, supporting others, and maintaining a professional, customer-focused approach in all interactions.
  • Have a genuine interest in property, valuation or the built environment, with a commitment to developing new skills and knowledge, and a strong motivation to achieve Chartered Surveyor (MRICS) status through the APC programme.
  • A full UK driving licence is essential to this role. A provisional licence is accepted at time of application however a FULL licence must be attained and evidenced within 6 months of take up date. However, if you are considered disabled under the Equality Act 2010 and do not hold a full driving licence, we will consider your application. Please contact resourcingteamvo@hmrc.gov.uk before you start/submit your application with your details to discuss this further.
  • Be willing and able to travel on a regular basis to undertake property inspection or attend training, including potential overnight stays.

In addition, you must hold one of the following:

Undergraduate Eligibility Criteria

  • Hold a RICS accredited Real Estate or Valuation degree at 2:2 or above OR will expect to hold one by 30th July 2027.

Please note your qualification must be fully complete and awarded by this date.

OR

Post Graduate Eligibility Criteria

  • Hold a RICS accredited Masters in Real Estate or Valuation

Please note applications are also welcome from candidates who will be in their final trimester and awaiting full award confirmation at the time of anticipated start. In such cases this must be supported by a transcript of results received up to that date with only the final credit outstanding.

For both undergraduate and post graduate degrees, it is essential you confirm your degree meets the eligibility criteria. Please check it is listed here , filtering on the Valuation pathway or any of the pathways listed below:

  • Commercial Real Estate
  • Residential
  • Planning and Development
  • Rural
  • Property Finance and Investment
  • Corporate Real Estate

Please note: As part of the application process, you will be required to answer a series of mandatory eligibility questions, including providing details of your degree and /or masters qualifications. Please ensure that all requested information is provided accurately and in full. Applications from candidates who do not meet the qualification requirements, or who fail to provide the required information, will not be progressed.

Licences

Hold a full UK / EU driving licence – a provisional licence is accepted at the time of application, however a FULL licence must be attained and evidenced within 6 months of take up date.
If you are considered disabled under the Equality Act 2010 and do not hold a full driving licence, we will consider your application. Please contact resourcingteam@voa.gov.uk before you start/submit your application , with your details to discuss this further.

Qualifications

Hold a RICS accredited Real Estate or Valuation degree at 2:2 or above OR will expect to hold one by 30th July 2027.

Please note your qualification must be fully complete and awarded by this date.

OR

Hold a RICS accredited Masters in Real Estate or Valuation

Behaviours

We'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:

  • Communicating and Influencing
  • Making Effective Decisions
  • Working Together
  • Leadership

Technical skills

We'll assess you against these technical skills during the selection process:

  • At the Assessment Centre you will be required to conduct a 10-minute presentation where we will assess your technical and presentation skills. Information on the presentation topic will be provided to you if you are shortlisted for the next stage.

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £32,500, HM Revenue and Customs contributes £9,415 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

HMRC operates both Flexible and Hybrid Working policies, allowing you to balance your work and personal commitments. We welcome applications from those who need to work a more flexible arrangement and will agree to requests where possible, considering our operational and customer service needs.

We offer a generous leave allowance that starts at 25 days, increasing by a day for every year of qualifying service up to a maximum of 30 days and a Civil Service Pension with an average employer contribution of 28.97%.

  • Pension - We make contributions to our colleagues’ Alpha pension equal to at least 28.97% of their salary.
  • Family friendly policies.
  • Personal support.
  • Coaching and development.

To find out more about HMRC benefits and find out what it’s really like to work for HMRC hear from our insiders or visit Thinking of joining the Civil Service.

    Things you need to know

    Artificial intelligence

    Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

    Selection process details

    This vacancy is using Success Profiles (opens in a new window), and will assess your Behaviours, Strengths, Experience and Technical skills.

    How to apply

    If you can meet our person requirements above, we are keen to hear from you. To apply for this post, you must complete an online application with the following:

    A Personal Statement (maximum 750 words). Please outline your suitability and alignment to the role. Please include reference to:

    • Any skills, knowledge or experience you may have either directly from your academic studies and/or any work experience you may have undertaken.
    • Showcase your alignment to the opportunity to complete your APC and interest in the surveying profession.

    Sifting will take place between 9 October - 6 November 2026

    Please note these dates are provisional and may be subject to change.

    We will assess you on your Personal Statement and Qualifications.

    Interviews will take place Face to Face via our Assessment Centres between 31 November - 3 December 2026

    Please note these dates are provisional and may be subject to change. These will be confirmed & further details will be provided should you be invited to interview.

    Before the Assessment Centre

    Shortlisted candidates will be invited to attend an Assessment Centre, where we will assess the behaviours outlined in the job description, together with your strengths, technical knowledge and skills. The assessment will consist of a range of activities, including an interview, presentation and group exercise. The assessment will include technical elements relevant to the role, providing you with an opportunity to demonstrate your knowledge, skills and understanding.

    Assessment Centres will take place week commencing Monday 30 November 2026. Further details regarding venues and booking arrangements will be provided to candidates who are successful at the sift stage.

    As part of the Assessment Centre, you will be required to deliver a 10-minute presentation. This will enable us to assess both your technical knowledge and your ability to communicate information clearly and effectively. Details of the presentation topic will be provided in advance.

    Please note that, due to data security requirements, IT equipment will not be available on the day. If you wish to use slides or other visual aids as part of your presentation, please bring sufficient printed copies for each member of the assessment panel.

    It is important to us that everyone feels able to participate in our selection process. We are committed to helping cover travel and accommodation costs for anyone invited to attend one of our assessment centres. Further detail on what our support package covers will be provided along with your assessment centre invite. Our team will be available to help make sure you’re supported in accessing the right level of assistance for you.

    In exceptional circumstances only, we many need to conduct some elements of the assessment centre remotely via an online platform.

    During the Assessment Centre

    You will have an opportunity to meet the Development and Surveying Profession Teams to find out more about the programme and the wider VO. You’ll get a sense of what your work environment could be like as your assessment centre will take place in one of our regional hubs.

    The assessment itself will include:

    A presentation – further detail will be provided with your invite to the assessment centre to help you prepare.

    A group exercise – where we will assess you on the behaviours shown below in real time.

    A short individual interview - where we will assess your technical knowledge and your strengths.

    The behaviours tested will be: Communicating and Influencing, Making Effective Decisions, Working Together and Leadership. You can find out more about these here Success Profiles: Civil Service behaviours - GOV.UK, you’ll be assessed against the HEO level definitions.

    Please be aware that the take up duty date for this role will be Monday 6th September 2027.

    Eligibility

    Please take extra care to tick the correct boxes in the eligibility sections of your application form. Mistakes sometimes happen but if you contact us later than two working days (Monday-Friday) before the vacancy closes, we may not be able to reopen your application for you.

    If you do make a mistake with your eligibility form, or have withdrawn yourself in error and need your application reinstated whilst the campaign is still live, please contact us via: resourcingteamvo@hmrc.gov.uk – Use the subject line to insert appropriate wording for example – ‘Please re-open my application – [insert vacancy ref] & vacancy closing date [insert date]’.

    To check that you are eligible to apply for this role, please review the eligibility information before submitting your application.

    Application Hints and Tips

    For more information on Success Profiles, tips on how to write a successful application and find out more about what’s involved in the application process please visit About the application process , Civil Service Careers (civil-service-careers.gov.uk).

    Further information

    Please be aware that the take up duty date for this role will be Monday 6 September 2027

    Whilst we try take personal circumstances into account wherever possible, successful candidates must be willing and able to work at least 30 hours per week to meet the requirements of the programme.

    Sponsorship

    We have assessed this role against both Home Office and HMRC criteria and we are unable to offer sponsorship for a Skilled Worker Visa. This means the vacancy is not open to applicants who require visa sponsorship.

    Hybrid working at HMRC

    HMRC is an office-based organisation, and colleagues are expected to spend 60% of their working time in the office. Our offices provide opportunity for interaction, collaboration which aids learning and development and a sense of community. Where the role allows it, and where the home environment is suitable, colleagues can work from home for up to 2 days a week, averaged over a calendar month (or a proportionate amount of time for colleagues who work less than full time).

    Reasonable Adjustments

    We want to make sure no one is put at a disadvantage during our recruitment process. To assist you with this, we will reduce or remove any barriers where possible and provide additional support where appropriate.

    If you need a change to be made so that you can make your application, you should:

    Contact the UBS Recruitment Team via resourcingteamvo@hmrc.gov.uk as soon as possible before the closing date to discuss your needs.

    Complete the “Assistance required” section in the “Additional requirements” page of your application form to tell us what changes or help you might need further on in the recruitment process. For instance, you may need wheelchair access at interview, or if you’re deaf, a Language Service Professional.

    Criminal Record Check

    Applications received from candidates with a criminal record are considered fairly in accordance with the DBS Code of Practice and the Recruitment of ex-offenders Policy.

    Locations

    As part of the application process, you will be asked to tell us which of the locations available you can work in.

    This role can be undertaken at any of the locations listed above. You will be asked to select up to two preferred locations as part of your application. You should only select locations that you can commit to working in long term. If you can only commit to one location , please provide one location preference only..

    Details of our office locations can be found at the top of the advert.

    Offers will be made in overall merit order, with candidates being considered against their preferred locations. To support recruitment across a range of locations, initial offers will be made to the highest-scoring candidate for each location until all 20 vacancies have been filled. Any remaining successful candidates will be placed on a reserve list and may be offered future vacancies in their preferred location based on business need.

    If you accept a role in one of your preferred locations you will automatically be removed from any other merit list.

    Successful candidates must select one of the locations noted in this advert as their base office and will be expected to undertake regular travel to this location under HMRC hybrid working policy.

    Wembley and Canary Wharf

    Due to the way the CS Jobs system is set up, when choosing your preferred locations, you will find that the Wembley & Canary Wharf locations will not appear on the list of options.

    Should you wish to choose Wembley as a location then please select Harlesden.

    Should you wish to choose Canary Wharf as a location then please select Tower Hamlets.

    Transitional Sites Information

    If your location preference is for the following sites, it’s important to note that this is not long-term site for HMRC and we will require you to move to a new building in the future, subject to our location strategy and the applicable employee policies at that time.

    These sites are:

    • Benton Park View, Newcastle - moving to Pilgrims Quarter, Newcastle.
    • Civic Centre, Oystermouth Road, Swansea – moving to Sandringham Park, Swansea.

    Terms and Conditions

    The Civil Service values honesty and integrity and expects all candidates to abide by these principles. The evidence you provide in your application must relate to your own experiences.

    Any instances of plagiarism or other forms of cheating will be investigated and, if proven, the relevant application(s) will be withdrawn from the process.

    Recording of interviews is prohibited unless explicit agreement is sought in line with the UK General Data Protection Regulations.

    Questions relating to an individual application must be emailed as detailed later in this advert.

    Applicants who are successful at interview will be, as part of pre-employment screening, subject to a check on the Internal Fraud Database (IFD). This check will provide information about employees who have been dismissed for fraud or dishonesty offences. This check also applies to employees who resign or otherwise leave before being dismissed for fraud or dishonesty had their employment continued. Any applicant’s details held on the IFD will be refused employment.

    A candidate is not eligible to apply for a role within the Civil Service if the application is made within a 5 year period following a dismissal for carrying out internal fraud against government.

    Please note that, if you are applying for roles on a part-time basis, the salary agreed will be pro-rata, reflective of the working hours agreed within your contract.

    If you experience accessibility problems with any attachments on this advert, please contact the email address in the 'Contact point for applicants' section.

    Reserve Lists

    If we have more successful candidates than available vacancies, we will hold a 6-month reserve list. During that time, we may use the list to fill the same, or similar roles with closely matching essential criteria, without further testing of merit. Any appointments from the Reserve list will be made in strict merit order.

    Concerns/Complaints

    If you feel your application has not been treated in accordance with the values in the Civil Service Code and/or if you feel the recruitment has been conducted in such a way that conflicts with the Civil Service Commissioner’s Recruitment Principles, you may make a complaint, by contacting the Central Recruitment Team at the following address: resourcingteamvo@hmrc.gov.uk.

title: Night Front Office All Rounder (Night Audit)
description:
What we ask of you:

  • A genuinely warm & welcoming demeanour
  • Personable communication skills
  • Energising motivation - its infectious - no job is too big or too small
  • A passion for the industry, a want to be the best in service
  • Australian Working Rights
  • New South Wales Responsible Service of Alcohol certificate/card

POSITION SUMMARY

  • Process all guest check-ins by confirming reservations, assigning room, and issuing and activating room key.
  • Process all payment types such as room charges, cash, checks, debit, or credit.
  • Process all check-outs including resolving any late and disputed charges.
  • Answer, record, and process all guest calls, messages, requests, questions, or concerns.
  • Coordinate with Housekeeping to track readiness of rooms for check-in.
  • Communicate parking procedures to guests/visitors and dispatch bell staff or valet staff as needed.
  • Supply guests with directions and information regarding property and local areas of interest.
  • Run daily reports (number of arrivals, departures), identify any special requests, and check reports for accuracy.
  • Complete designated cashier and closing reports in the computer system.
  • Cash guests' personal checks and traveler's checks.
  • Count bank at the beginning and end of shift. Balance and drop receipts according to Accounting specifications.
  • Follow all company safety and security policies and procedures; report accidents, injuries, and unsafe work conditions to manager.
  • Follow all company policies and procedures; ensure uniform and personal appearance are clean and professional; maintain confidentiality of proprietary information; protect company assets.
  • Welcome and acknowledge all guests according to company standards; anticipate and address guests’ service needs; assist individuals with disabilities; thank guests with genuine appreciation.
  • Speak with others using clear and professional language; answer telephones using appropriate etiquette.
  • Develop and maintain positive working relationships with others.
  • Comply with quality assurance expectations and standards. Stand, sit, or walk for an extended period of time.
  • Move, lift, carry, push, pull, and place objects weighing less than or equal to 10 pounds without assistance.
  • Perform other reasonable job duties as requested by Supervisors.

Perks, Rewards, Motivations

  • Team-spirited co-workers
  • Encouraging leadership
  • Discounted room rates on hotels worldwide
  • Discount on food and beverages at participating Marriott International hotels worldwide
  • Recognition programs to keep you motivated
  • Wellbeing & mindfulness programs to ensure you stay healthy
  • Paid birthday leave
  • Training and development

At Marriott International, we are dedicated to being an equal opportunity employer, welcoming all and providing access to opportunity. We actively foster an environment where the unique backgrounds of our associates are valued and celebrated. Our greatest strength lies in the rich blend of culture, talent, and experiences of our associates. We are committed to non-discrimination on any protected basis, including disability, veteran status, or other basis protected by applicable law.

title: Deputy Director - Strategic Change
company: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs
description:
• Job grade: SCS Pay Band 1
  • Contract type: Permanent
  • Business area: Strategy and Change Group
  • Type of role: Project Delivery, Senior leadership, Strategy
  • Working pattern: Full-time, Job share
  • Number of jobs available: 1

Location

Bristol, London, Newcastle-upon-Tyne, York

About the job

Job summary

The post holder will lead an ambitious change agenda at the heart of the department. This is an exciting role for somebody to make a substantial impact on the development and delivery of strategic change at Defra. The role provides strategic direction, specialist change delivery capability and strong leadership, to drive the successful design and implementation of Defra’s change agenda.

Job description

The role works at the centre of the Department working closely with strategy, policy and delivery colleagues to ensure that change across the Defra group is coherent and supports delivery of Defra’s outcomes. The Deputy Director leads a team of people to enable delivery of a series of organisational shifts that will put Defra in the best possible position to successfully delivery its outcomes, ensuring change is aligned to the Future Civil Service Programme. The successful candidate also leads a portfolio of change projects and programmes to deliver Defra’s efficiency targets, identifying and implementing interventions that ensure the department operates within its spending envelope.

The Deputy Director will engage senior colleagues across Defra group to ensure change is impactful and delivers its intended outcomes. They will work closely with senior colleagues responsible for delivering specific projects and programmes, and functional directors and their teams delivering organisational change. They will build excellent relationships in order to enable and facilitate the delivery of others, whilst at the same time assuring and challenging the delivery of change to ensure it is both ambitious and feasible.

Key responsibilities of the role will include:

  • Translate policy intent into strategic design to deliver change that is meaningful and impactful
  • Work closely with colleagues across Defra to lead the delivery of a series of organisational change initiatives designed to make Defra more modern, agile and effective, and better placed to successfully deliver its outcomes
  • Oversight of the efficiencies portfolio to ensure that projects are managed effectively to deliver the required outcomes, efficiencies and organisational benefits and that Defra is on-track to deliver its efficiencies targets
  • Establish and manage a wide range of relationships and key strategic alliances with stakeholders including ALBs Change and Transformation Directors, functional colleagues and delivery partners to ensure change is effectively cohered and delivered
  • Develop, deliver and lead change functional governance and reporting, ensuring governance and reporting informs effective decision making
  • Lead work to understand the effectiveness of change delivery at Defra, providing insights to senior colleagues and making recommendations for improvement - be bold and able to set an ambitious strategy for change at Defra with the ability to oversee its successful delivery
  • Lead work to consider the role of business design in Defra and take forward the preferred approach for business design standards and guardrails to inform the development of the policies and services we deliver
  • Work closely with Defra’s Executive Committee - use simple language and cut through complex responsibilities to communicate with impact

Person specification

Essential Criteria

Candidates will be assessed against the following behaviors and essential criteria:

  • Seeing the big picture: Demonstrable ability to interpret policy intent into strategy and delivery in a way that delivers meaningful change. Ensuring plans are adjusted as needed to reflect wider contextual changes, maintaining alignment between Defra and wider government priorities and the work of their team.
  • Changing and improving: Experience operating at a senior level in complex organisations, providing evidence-based advice and constructive challenge to senior leaders on organisational change, strategy, business priorities or transformation.
  • Delivering at pace: Demonstrable ability to deliver high-quality outcomes at pace; setting clear priorities, managing risks and proactively removing blockers, whilst making timely decisions and responding quickly when circumstances change.
  • Communicating and influencing: Experience of communicating complex issues clearly and persuasively to influence senior stakeholders and support effective decision making.
  • Leadership: Outstanding people leadership skills and experience in leading across organisational boundaries to develop multidisciplinary teams in complex or changing environments; creating inclusive conditions in which people feel empowered to deliver, supported to reach their potential and proud of their work.
  • Working together: Experience of building collaborative relationships at a system level and across organisational boundaries to deliver shared outcomes.
