About the Wales Office:

The Wales Office is the face of the UK Government in Wales and the voice of Wales in Westminster. We support the Secretary of State for Wales and the Ministerial team in representing Wales at the heart of Government. We work in partnership with other Government Departments and other stakeholders to deliver a stronger Wales within a strong United Kingdom.

Our departmental values are Commitment, Collaboration and Quality. These shape how we operate in a challenging, demanding, and fast paced environment which requires flexibility, transparency and professionalism.

The Wales Office has two sites, one in Cardiff and one in Whitehall. The successful candidate will be based in Cardiff or London, but travel between sites and elsewhere may be required in order to build relations with colleagues and stakeholders.

About the team:

The Wales Office Communications Team is a high-performing team that helps connect people across Wales with the work of the UK Government. We provide strategic communication advice to ministers and senior officials, manage media relations, deliver digital and social media content, and support ministerial visits and events.

Working at the heart of government, we collaborate closely with colleagues across Whitehall and the Government Communication Service to ensure UK Government delivery is communicated clearly, effectively and in ways that matter to Welsh audiences. We combine insight, evaluation, creativity and strong news judgement to deliver communication that is audience-focused, evidence-led and impactful.

The team is ambitious about modern government communications. Alongside supporting ministers and managing daily media activity, we are increasingly focused on direct-to-citizen communication, using digital channels and partnerships to tell authentic stories about the impact of UK Government policies and investment in communities across Wales.

As part of a small team, you will have the opportunity to work across multiple communication disciplines, take ownership of significant projects and develop strong relationships with senior decision-makers. No two days are the same, making this an ideal role for a communicator who enjoys variety, challenge and the chance to make a visible impact.

About the Role:

The Wales Office is seeking an experienced integrated communicator to play an important role in developing and delivering strategic communication that supports UK Government priorities across Wales.

You will develop expert communication advice for ministers and senior officials, helping to shape and deliver integrated communication strategies that build understanding of UK Government priorities and their impact across Wales.

This is a varied role spanning strategic communication, media relations, campaigns, digital communication and reputation management. You will work across disciplines to ensure communication activity is insight-driven, audience-focused and aligned with wider UK Government objectives.

A key aspect of the role will be supporting the Head of Communication to develop and deliver longer-term communication strategies across Wales Office priority policy areas. The successful candidate will lead the development of thematic communication plans, ensuring activity is informed by audience insight, aligned to ministerial priorities and evaluated to demonstrate impact and continuous improvement.

By joining a communications team, you will become a member of the Government Communication Service, a profession of over 7,000 communicators working in government departments, agencies and arm’s length bodies. You’ll benefit from continuous professional development from our new learning and development curriculum, a network of skilled communicators sharing best practice, mentoring opportunities, and more.

For more information on how becoming a part of the Communications Profession can support your career and development please visit the GCS careers page.

Key Responsibilities

We are looking for motivated and creative individual to join us and embark on an exceptional career in government communications.

Your key responsibilities will include:

  • Strategic communication – support the Head of Communications in developing and delivering long-term communication strategies across priority policy and thematic areas, ensuring communication activity supports ministerial objectives and organisational priorities.
  • Insight and evaluation – lead the development of audience insight, evaluation and communication performance reporting. Use evidence and data to shape communication activity, identify opportunities and provide strategic recommendations to senior leaders.
  • Press office resilience and reputation management – provide expert media handling support, contribute to proactive and reactive communications activity, support major announcements and issues management, and provide resilience during periods of high operational demand, including participation in the out-of-hours rota.
  • Relationships – develop and maintain strong working relationships with ministers, private offices, special advisers, senior officials, journalists, stakeholders and other government departments.
  • Prioritising – understand government, departmental and ministerial priorities so you can communicate key messages clearly, accurately and creatively.
  • Each member of the team takes part in an on-call system, for which there is an allowance, to take calls out-of-hours from the media. This is done on a rotational basis, and full training will be given.

The job description is not intended to be exhaustive, and it is likely that duties may be altered from time to time in the light of changing circumstances and after consultation with the postholder.

Person Specification

Please evidence how closely you match the essential criteria in your Statement of Suitability, which is up to 750 words.

Essential:

  • Experience of developing strategic communication strategies that support organisational and ministerial objectives.
  • Experience of using audience insight, research, evaluation and performance data to develop communication activity and measure success.
  • Experience of providing strategic communication advice to senior stakeholders.
  • Ability to identify emerging risks and opportunities and translate complex issues into effective communication approaches.
  • Excellent understanding of the national news agenda, social media landscape and communication handling; strong news judgement and political awareness.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with experience producing high-quality content for a range of audiences and channels
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills - producing high-quality written content such as statements, press releases and briefings, for a range of different stakeholders and audiences.
  • Strong organisational and planning skills, comfortable managing multiple priorities and working to tight deadlines.
  • Strong networking skills with the confidence in building and maintaining a network of internal and external contacts.
  • Strong team collaboration skills, work effectively as part of a team; contributing to shared goals, supporting colleagues and fostering a positive team environment.

Desirable:

  • An ability to speak and write proficiently in the Welsh language is desirable for this post.

  • Seeing the Big Picture (Lead Behaviour) (Application & Interview)

In the event of a high volume of applicants, we will sift only on the lead behaviour to create a shortlist for interview.

Technical Skills

  • Impact: Evaluating communication activity and using evidence to improve future performance.

Additional Information

The Wales Office is not an employer in its own right and staff recruited to work at the Wales Office will be employees of the Ministry of Justice who provide employment services on our behalf.

This role requires SC level clearance. Applicants for National Security Clearance (SC) must be resident in the UK for 5 years immediately prior to their application for Security Clearance. About the job

Job summary

Are you someone who thrives in a problem-solving environment and would love a varied, dynamic and rewarding role?

Are you highly resilient with the ability to remain calm and professional in pressurised situations?

Do you hold a Vessel Traffic Services (VTS) Operator Qualification or have the willingness to work towards achieving this once in post?

If so, we'd love to hear from you!

Joining our department comes with many benefits, including:

  • Employer pension contribution of 28.97% of your salary. Read more about Civil Service Pensions here
  • 25 days annual leave, increasing by 1 day each year of service (up to a maximum of 30 days annual leave), plus 8 bank holidays a privilege day for the King’s birthday.
  • Flexible working options where we encourage a great work-life balance.

Read more in the Benefits section below!

Find out more about what it's like working at Maritime and Coastguard Agency - Department for Transport Careers

Job description

Based at our Coastguard Operations Centre in Falmouth, we have a fantastic opportunity for a number of Vessel Traffic Services Operators (VTSO) to join our dynamic team providing a crucial VTS Traffic Information and Navigational Assistance Service in accordance with current national doctrine and the International Association of Marine Aids to Navigation and Lighthouse Authorities (IALA) recommendations.

As a VTSO your day will include taking mandatory ship reports from vessels navigating within the service area, gathering key information in relation to cargo, passengers and vessel damage or defects to ensure they are compliant with both national and international maritime regulations and able to safely continue their passage.

This is a dynamic role in which you’ll be faced with a multitude of interesting and varied situations – from a compliant vessel just passing through to ships that have run aground, a passenger ferry dealing with a fire, loss of pollutant cargo overboard or even managing vessels safely around swimmers in the English Channel.

Your responsibilities will include, but aren’t limited to:

  1. Delivery of a vessel traffic service as defined by IALA recommendations and guidelines to vessels navigating in the service area to ensure compliance with all local, national and international regulations
  2. Working as part of a team to manage day-to-day operations to provide a high and effective standard of VTS service delivery
  3. Planning, prioritising and managing work based on dynamic risk assessments, and ensuring resources are available for both forecast and actual demand
  4. Balancing work against resource and recommending additional staff or assistance from other teams to provide suitable coverage
  5. Implementing sound leadership, management and direction within a team, and ensuring safe working practices are maintained

Great line management is important to us as an organisation, and we will equip and support line managers to develop the skills they need. We aim to empower line managers to create teams where people can flourish and deliver excellent outcomes for the public.

For further information on the role, please read the role profile. Please note that the role profile is for information purposes only - whilst all elements are relevant to the role, they may not all be assessed during the recruitment process. This job advert will detail exactly what will be assessed during the recruitment process.

Person specification

Applicants are required to demonstrate a willingness to work towards and obtain a VTS C0103-1 qualification – (eligibility to enrol for this qualification requires English as a first language or an English Language certification to the equivalent of IELTS level 5.0)

To be successful in this role you will need to have the following experience:

  • be confident and proficient in the use of multiple IT systems
  • combining auditory and visual information
  • demonstrating spatial and situational awareness
  • demonstrating alertness and decisiveness when required
  • carrying out several tasks simultaneously (multi-tasking)
  • carrying out routine work without losing situational awareness
  • prioritising and deciding what situations require immediate action
  • show initiative and make decisions whilst working within a framework of standards, regulations and structured procedures
  • demonstrating effective participation as a member of a team
  • working within a busy, high-pressure environment
  • communicating with a range of stakeholders, both verbally and in writing.

Additional Information

Please note that this is a uniformed role and uniform will be required to be worn at all times when on duty.

Successful candidates will be expected to undertake a physical medical and mental health questionnaire for this role. Please see the attached document for further information.

Operational Delivery Profession (ODP) is the largest and most diverse professional community across the Civil Service. Many of us will have an association with several professional communities or specialisms, ODP applies to all public facing roles / or a role that is primarily aligned to supporting the work of those with public facing roles. All critical to the delivery of UK public services.

This role is not suitable for hybrid working and will require the successful candidate to work solely from their designated workplace (one of the locations cited in the advert) or, when required for business reasons, from other offices/work locations/visiting stakeholders.

If your employment ceases within 24 months of completing your training course, you will be required to reimburse the MCA any associated training fees based on the length of your employment.

The role requires occasional travel to attend ongoing training courses, meetings and working groups which will involve some time away from home and the regular workplace.

This role is full-time only and you will be required to work a 12-hour shift pattern (both day and nightshifts) to allow HMCG to provide its 24 hour emergency service to the public, 365 days a year. On average the shift pattern equates to 37 duty hours per week over a 12-month period. As such, this position attracts a number of allowances to reflect the shift working and unsociable hours.

Appointment to this role is subject to meeting Health Standards, please see attached document.

For more information please Vessel traffic service operators , HM Coastguard UK

Visa Sponsorship

Please note that we will only offer sponsorship for a skilled worker visa where a role has been deemed to be business critical. This role does not meet that category, and we will not sponsor a visa. Therefore, this role is not open to applications from those who require sponsorship – candidates must ensure they have the appropriate right to work in the UK before applying. Should you apply for this role and be found to require sponsorship, your application will be rejected and any provisional offer of employment withdrawn.

Behaviours

We'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:

Benefits

Being part of our brilliant Civil Service means you will have access to a wide range of fantastic benefits:

  • 25 days annual leave, increasing by 1 day each year of service (up to a maximum of 30 days annual leave).

Things you need to know

Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Selection process details

How to apply:

As part of the application process, you will be asked to complete a CV and personal statement. Further details around what this will entail are listed on the application form.

Pre-employment Checking

If your application is successful but you have been dismissed from the Civil Service, your application could be removed at the pre-employment checking stage depending on the nature of the dismissal.

Applicants who are successful at interview will be, as part of pre-employment screening, subject to a check on the Internal Fraud Database (IFD). This check will provide information about employees who have been dismissed for fraud or dishonesty offences. This check also applies to employees who resign or otherwise leave before being dismissed for fraud or dishonesty had their employment continued. Any applicant’s details held on the IFD will be refused employment. A candidate is not eligible to apply for a role within the Civil Service if the application is made within a 5-year period following a dismissal for carrying out internal fraud against government.

All external applicants and current employees of accredited non-departmental public bodies (NDPBs) will be required to undergo a Social Media Check. A Social Media Check is a review of your publicly available online activity, typically across platforms like LinkedIn, Facebook, X (formerly Twitter), Instagram, and others. The purpose is to identify any public posts or content that could raise concerns for employers, such as:

  • Hate speech or discriminatory behaviour
  • Threats or acts of violence
  • Illegal activity or substance misuse

Importantly, this check does not involve hacking into your accounts or accessing private messages. It only considers content you have chosen to make public. Employers use this kind of screening to help ensure their workplace remains safe, inclusive, and aligned with company values. It’s not about judging your personality or lifestyle - it’s about checking for potential red flags that might affect the role or company culture. title: Executive Creative Director
description:
Workplace: White City, London - 2 days a week in the office

The role

ITV Creative is ITV’s in-house creative agency, responsible for promoting our shows and building the reputation of the ITV brand. As part of the marcomms team, we create attention grabbing, strategic ideas to help ITV compete with the best of the broadcasters and streamers. Our output ranges from 360 campaigns to imagery on ITVX and everything in between. We have a high performing team of 70 people, made up of creatives, designers, editors, a full production team, strategists & campaign managers.

The ECD has 4 Creative Directors that report into them (Commercial, Imagery, Performance & Campaigns)

The last two years have been focussed on transforming how we work with Marketing, Media and Programme PR - collaboration is at the heart of how we work together, enabling everybody to leverage their skills and expertise but on a level playing field and not ‘in service’ to any department. This has proven to be incredibly effective in delivering brave work, with excellent results.

Main responsibilities

Leading the creative output:

  • Setting the vision, the standard and being the ultimate decision maker on everything that goes out into the world creatively from ITV Creative.
  • Working side by side with the Head of Creative Strategy and Head of Production to ensure our output is consistently on brief and well crafted.
  • Driving best in class creativity within the creative department, with quality to rival any broadcaster/streamer or brand.
  • This year we have launched our brand platform, There’s No Place Like ITV and it feels like we’re just getting started! There’s opportunity to continue to build on that as part of the Marketing Priority plan for 2027 and beyond.
  • Outside of delivering the Marketing plan, the ECD is also ultimately responsible for the creative output our Creative Commercial team delivers (sponsorship and partnership campaigns for our advertisers).
  • Overall responsible for the quality of our imagery across ITVX and our partner platforms.
  • Ensuring our owned channels are branded visually and utilising Continuity in the right way.
  • Leading the charge on creative innovation alongside the Head of Post Production & Creative Operations.
  • Supporting the Head of Brand Experiences when required for creative quality across internal and external activations and events.
  • Ultimately leading award winning effective creative work across multiple touchpoints.

Creative Champion within the business:

  • The driver for brilliant and brave creative ideas that deliver against the strategy and brief.
  • Fostering meaningful relationships with key senior stakeholders across Marketing and Commissioning to get ideas made. As well as within the product and editorial team to ensure the brand is represented in the right way across our platform (ITVX).
  • Being the ITV Creative voice in the room with production companies and commissioners where required.
  • Supporting the Director of Creative in presenting and roadshowing the skillset and output of the team at internal and external events.

Management:

  • Running the creative department (30 people plus freelancers), ensuring the teams and individuals have the right opportunities and training to thrive.
  • Line Management duties for x4 direct reports; Creative Director Campaigns, Creative Director Performance Marketing, Creative Director Imagery, Creative Director Commercial (including but not limited to setting objectives, reviews, ensuring high performance and good results, pastoral support).
  • Providing stability, leadership and guidance through practical and pastoral support for the wider creative team.
  • Working closely with the Creative Resource Manager and relevant CDs to allocate teams and creatives to projects and campaigns.
  • As part of the Creative Leadership Team (CLT) alongside Head of Creative Strategy, Head of Production and Head of Post Production & Creative Ops you will support the Director of Creative in the day to day running of ITV Creative.
  • Alongside your CLT duties the role also sits within the ‘Heads Of’ group that spans ITV Creative, Marketing, Media, Programme Publicity and Delivery where your role is to have a voice in the overall planning of activity and WoW across the departments alongside your peers.

Skills you’ll need (minimum criteria)

  • Experience within a creative agency at Creative Director level or above (this can be a broadcaster, in-house or external agency).
  • Examples of campaigns that have delivered against set KPIs and proved to work effectively, that have been generated/led by the candidate.
  • Proven Leadership skills (running/developing a team)
  • Demonstrated experience leading multi-channel 360° integrated campaigns across AV, digital, social, out-of-home, and digital platform imagery.
  • Proven track record of developing, expanding, or embedding long-term brand platforms.
  • Experience working to a commercial agenda, ensuring quality creative at varying cost levels
  • Experience collaborating alongside senior Strategy, Production, and Operations leads to manage department resourcing and workflows.

Other things we’re looking for (key criteria)

  • Good interpersonal and stakeholder management skills (part of this role is around building relationships within ITV Creative as well as other people/stakeholders within the organisation at varying levels of seniority).
  • Excellent communication skills - seeing everyone at eye level.
  • Good interpersonal and stakeholder management skills (part of this role is around building relationships within ITV Creative as well as other people/stakeholders within the organisation at varying levels of seniority).
  • A love of TV/content/entertainment!

title: Sastre
description:

Mend, repair, and alter guest clothing and employee uniforms by hand stitching, applying adhesive patches, or using a sewing machine. Distribute clean uniforms to personnel according to company specifications. Send damaged uniforms to appropriate location (e.g., seamstress, Housekeeping, outside vendor) for repair. title: Kitchen Steward
description:
The Tasman, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Hobart is located just steps from Hobart’s waterfront and the city’s top restaurants and attractions. The Tasman is a unique combination of Modern Contemporary, Art Deco and Heritage architecture. Presenting 152 luxuriously appointed guest rooms and suites with carefully restored features and adorned with exclusive art pieces from local artists, The Tasman reflects the true spirit of the destination.

The Opportunity

We are seeking a reliable and motivated Kitchen Steward to join our Culinary team. In this role, you will play a vital part in maintaining a clean, safe, and efficient kitchen environment, ensuring our chefs have the equipment and support they need to deliver exceptional dining experiences.

Working closely with the Culinary and Food & Beverage teams, you will be responsible for maintaining cleanliness across all kitchen and back-of-house areas, operating dishwashing equipment, and ensuring compliance with food safety and hygiene standards. Your contribution will be essential to the smooth operation of the kitchen and the overall success of our service.

Key Accountabilities

  • Maintain the cleanliness and organisation of all kitchen, stewarding, and back-of-house areas.
  • Operate commercial dishwashing equipment to clean crockery, cutlery, glassware, kitchen utensils, and cooking equipment.
  • Ensure kitchen equipment is cleaned, sanitised, and stored correctly.
  • Assist with the removal of rubbish, recycling, and waste in accordance with hotel procedures.
  • Support chefs with basic kitchen cleaning and operational tasks as required.
  • Ensure adequate stock of clean kitchen equipment is available throughout service periods.
  • Maintain high standards of food safety, hygiene, and workplace cleanliness in line with hotel policies.
  • Safely handle cleaning chemicals and equipment in accordance with WHS guidelines.
  • Assist with receiving and storing deliveries when required.
  • Contribute to a positive, professional, and team-focused working environment.

Profile

  • Previous experience in a stewarding, kitchen hand, or hospitality role is preferred.
  • Understanding of food safety, hygiene, and safe work practices.
  • Ability to work efficiently in a fast-paced, high-volume environment.
  • Strong work ethic with a proactive and reliable attitude.
  • Physically capable of manual handling, standing for extended periods, and lifting kitchen equipment.
  • Excellent teamwork and communication skills.
  • Strong attention to cleanliness and organisation.
  • Flexibility to work a rotating roster, including early mornings, evenings, weekends, and public holidays.
  • Full working rights in Australia.

Rewards for work, benefits for your lifestyle

  • Join a supportive, progressive, and highly experienced team
  • Be part of something truly unique within The Tasman experience
  • Access generous benefits and discounts for yourself, family, and friends across over 9000+ Marriott properties worldwide
  • Extensive career development, learning, and growth opportunities
  • Wellbeing programs and initiatives designed to support you personally and professionally
  • Enjoy a relaxed lifestyle with easy access to world-class events and experiences across Tasmania

Marriott International is an equal opportunity employer. We believe in hiring a diverse workforce and sustaining an inclusive, people-first culture. We are committed to non-discrimination on any protected basis, such as disability and veteran status, or any other basis covered under applicable law.

title: Vice President, Consumer Brand, Sports Portfolio - Burson
description:
Who we are:

Burson, part of WPP, is the global communications leader built to create value for clients through reputation. With highly specialized teams, industry-leading technologies and breakthrough creative, we help brands and businesses redefine reputation as a competitive advantage so they can lead today and into the future. When you work at Burson, you are part of a global community of lifelong learners who thrive at the edge of innovation.

WPP (LSE/NYSE: WPP) is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. For more information, visit WPP.com

For more information visit and follow us on LinkedIn and Instagram.

More about the role:

The Consumer Brand team partners with some of the world's most recognized sports brands, properties, leagues, and organizations to create culturally relevant communications programs that drive conversation, engagement, and business impact. We operate at the intersection of sports, earned media, entertainment, influencer engagement, athlete partnerships, and brand storytelling to help clients connect with consumers through compelling narratives, strategic partnerships, and integrated communications campaigns.

We are seeking a Vice President, Consumer Brand Sports to serve as a senior communications leader responsible for developing and executing integrated earned media and brand communications programs for a diverse portfolio of sports clients. This role will lead strategic communications initiatives that generate meaningful earned media results, elevate brand reputation, and connect clients with consumers through sports, culture, talent, and experiences across diverse consumer audiences.

The ideal candidate brings established relationships with key media outlets, publishers, journalists, producers, influencers, and industry stakeholders, along with expertise in athlete marketing, sponsorship activation, sports business trends, and culturally relevant storytelling that helps brands authentically engage consumers.

This individual will lead in the development and execution of campaigns, athlete and brand partnership programs, experiential events, press trips, and other integrated communications initiatives. They will serve as a trusted counselor to senior clients, delivering strategic recommendations, executive communications support, and compelling presentations while building long-term relationships and driving client growth.

The Vice President will manage and mentor team members, collaborate across agency disciplines, and contribute to agency growth through business development, client expansion, innovative communications strategies, and thought leadership.

The preferred locations for this role are Los Angeles (Hybrid), Southern California (Remote), or San Francisco (Hybrid).

What you'll do:

Lead Client Communications Programs

  • Develop and execute integrated earned media and communications programs for leading brands, sports properties, and entertainment clients.
  • Serve as a trusted strategic advisor to clients, providing senior-level counsel on media strategy, reputation management, athlete partnerships, sponsorship activations, and brand storytelling.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with key client stakeholders while proactively identifying opportunities to deepen partnerships and grow business.

Drive Earned Media Excellence

  • Leverage deep knowledge of key sports, consumer, lifestyle, entertainment, and business media outlets, publishers, journalists, podcasts, newsletters, broadcast partners, and emerging media platforms.
  • Develop media strategies that generate earned coverage, cultural relevance, and audience engagement across traditional, digital, social, and emerging channels.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with sports, consumer, lifestyle, entertainment, and business media.

Lead Athlete Activations and Experiential Programming

  • Develop and execute athlete activation programs that align with client business objectives and brand narratives.
  • Identify and manage athlete, ambassador, influencer, and talent partnerships that drive visibility and engagement.
  • Lead the planning and execution of press trips, media tours, product launches, experiential activations, sporting event programs, and marquee consumer experiences.
  • Partner closely with talent agencies, athlete representatives, leagues, teams, and industry partners to maximize program impact.

Provide Team Leadership

  • Manage, mentor, and develop account teams while fostering an inclusive, collaborative, and high-performance culture.
  • Provide ongoing coaching and career development support to junior and mid-level team members.
  • Lead cross-functional teams across strategy, creative, social, influencer, analytics, and production disciplines to deliver integrated client solutions.

Contribute to Agency Growth

  • Play an active role in business development, including prospecting, pitch strategy, proposal development, and presentation delivery.
  • Contribute to new business opportunities by developing communications strategies and presenting recommendations to prospective clients.
  • Identify opportunities to expand existing client relationships through strategic counsel and innovative programming.
  • Partner with account leadership to identify organic growth opportunities, support account planning and resource management efforts, and contribute to the overall financial success of the business.
  • Represent Burson as a subject matter expert in sports communications, athlete partnerships, consumer brand marketing, and integrated communications.

Experience that contributes to success:

  • 10+ years of experience in sports communications, consumer brand marketing, earned media, public relations, or integrated communications, preferably within an agency environment.
  • Deep understanding of the consumer sports landscape, including major leagues, teams, athletes, media ecosystems, sponsorship trends, fan engagement strategies, and cultural moments that drive conversation.
  • Proven relationships with leading sports, consumer, lifestyle, business, and entertainment media outlets, publishers, and journalists.
  • Demonstrated success developing and executing integrated earned media campaigns that generate impactful coverage and measurable results.
  • Significant experience planning and executing press trips, media events, product launches, experiential activations, and large-scale event communications programs.
  • Proven success leading athlete activations, sponsorship campaigns, endorsement programs, and talent-driven consumer marketing initiatives.
  • Strong client-facing presence with exceptional presentation, storytelling, and executive communication skills.
  • Experience counseling senior executives and marketing leaders on communications strategy, media engagement, and reputation management.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead integrated teams and collaborate effectively across disciplines to deliver business results.
  • Experience attracting, managing, mentoring, and developing high-performing teams in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong understanding of agency business operations, including account management, staffing, financial oversight, and resource planning.
  • Proven success supporting and winning new business opportunities, including developing pitch strategies, presenting recommendations, and building relationships with prospective clients.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, strong attention to detail, and sound judgment in high-pressure situations.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining a strategic mindset and delivering exceptional client service.
  • A passion for sports, culture, communications, and storytelling, with a pulse on emerging trends and opportunities shaping the industry.

Burson is an equal opportunity employer and considers applicants for all positions without discrimination or regard to particular characteristics. We are committed to fostering a culture of respect in which everyone feels they belong and has the same opportunities to progress in their careers.

#LI-MG1

Individual compensation varies based on job-related factors, including location, business needs, level of responsibility, experience, and qualifications. We offer a competitive benefits package; click here for more details: .

The base salary for this position at the time of this posting may range between:
$75,000—$180,000 USD

You belong at Burson:

Our vision is for Burson to be the leading ‘academy company’ for creative communications professionals and emerging leaders. We provide a dynamic environment where ambitious colleagues come to elevate their skills, expand their networks, and ultimately, produce the best solutions for today’s leading brands. Our commitment to your growth is reflected in our robust benefits and people programs, which include professional development opportunities, mentorship programs with industry leaders, a vibrant and inclusive company culture fostering collaboration and innovation and packages designed to reward and retain top talent. About the job

Job summary

On the Property Fast Stream, you’ll be part of building a modern, sustainable public estate that benefits the whole of the UK.

The specific towns and cities depend on the department you are posted to and its office locations. The Fast Stream evolves continually, so postings can vary from year to year.

As an indication, in 2026 new fast streamers were posted to government offices in the following regions: Greater London, North East, North West, Scotland, South East, South West, West Midlands, and Yorkshire and the Humber.

On occasion, some individuals may need to move location. We aim to align postings with your preferences whenever possible; however, final decisions must support our wider business needs. Please note that Fast Streamers cannot choose their department or their specific role.

Job description

The Government Property Professionals work on the UK’s largest and most varied estate. Across government, we occupy around 2% of the land area of the entire UK, worth half a trillion pounds, costing over £20 billion each year to run the estate alone.

The numbers are huge, and so are the opportunities. As a Property fast streamer, you’ll be at the heart of making our properties more sustainable, better suited to the needs of the UK population and adaptable to reflect the way people want to work in the future.

Property is not just about bricks and mortar; it’s about people too. We want to invest in you, to give you the broad property knowledge and the essential leadership and management skills to be a future property leader in government. As a Property fast streamer, you will work across a broad range of central government departments and agencies throughout the UK. You will be involved with developing strategy, planning and delivering projects that will build a better, more sustainable estate for delivering public services. Not only that, but you’ll gain vast property experience working with teams of experts in a variety of different specialisms.

Here is an insight of the exciting work you may be involved with during the 4-year programme:

Experiencing how the government values, acquires, sells, and lets buildings
Understanding how important the workplace is to delivering a modern Civil Service
Procuring or managing contracts and services to ensure buildings are safe and fit for purpose
Delivering huge projects ranging from building new prisons, to refurbishing historic buildings and improving the delivery of essential services
Being part of a sustainability drive that will see the UK achieving carbon net zero emissions by 2050
In addition to this, we will also support you on your journey to accreditation with either the Chartered Institute of Building (CIOB), Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (RICS) or the Institute of Workplace and Facilities Management (IWFM). Promotion and successful completion of the scheme will see you earn up to £55k


We aim to put all successful candidates through Security Clearance (SC). However, if you are ineligible for SC, please do not be deterred from applying; we have plenty of exciting roles available that only require standard Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) pre-employment checks. You can find more information about vetting clearance levels here: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/united-kingdom-security-vetting-clearance-levels

Person specification

You must be eligible to work in the UK
You need to have or be oon track to receive a 2:2 or higher in any degree subject including degree apprenticeships
Existing civil servants can apply without a degree

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £31,554, Fast Stream and Emerging Talent contributes £9,141 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).
You’ll have a unique chance to work on issues that really matter, whilst at the same time gaining a qualification and professional accreditation. It’s the best foundation for promotion and long term career progression, and will set you up for a varied and exciting career in government property.

Other benefits include the Civil Service Pension Scheme, flexible working, season ticket loans, sports and social activities, childcare vouchers and more.

Artificial intelligence

Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Selection process details

Application Process

There are several phases in the Fast Stream application process. Some of these assessments are multimedia in that they present information in video, audio, graphical or visual formats, as well as text. We hope you find it an engaging process and one that gives you a real insight into the role of a fast streamer.

At the initial application stage you will be asked to complete some background information which will include some diversity questions - which are for monitoring purposes only and will have no bearing on selection outcomes - along with the opportunity to identify your preferences in terms of the different Fast Stream schemes. You can choose up to three.

When you apply please register with a personal email address, and not a work or university email address.

Assessment Phases

There are 2 online tests:

Work-based scenarios - This test measures interpersonal skills, utilising video based scenarios and you are required to assess the effectiveness of various responses.

Case Study assessment - In this test you are required to take work based scenarios on an imaginary role, learning and responding to a series of challenges and situations and adapting to the changes you are presented with.

Additional information - depending on the schemes you have chosen, there may be additional information to be completed, or an intermediate sift process. More information on the schemes that require additional information can be found https://www.civil-service-careers.gov.uk/fast-stream/fs-how-to-apply/fs-additional-information/

Fast Stream Assessment Centre - if you pass the above stages you'll be invited to attend a half day assessment centre. This will be conducted virtually online. The Fast Stream Assessment Centre (FSAC) reflects some of the key elements of a Fast Stream role and will consist of a written exercise, oral briefing exercise and a personal development conversation. Information will be presented via an app that you will be able to access remotely.

Final Selection Board - most schemes will then require a Final Selection Board . We'll ask you to attend this final assessment if you reach the required standard at FSAC. More information on the Final Selection Boards can be found https://www.civil-service-careers.gov.uk/fast-stream/fs-how-to-apply/fs-final-selection-board/

The Civil Service Fast Stream is committed to supporting you through the application process by offering a range of reasonable adjustments. For further information about reasonable adjustments through the Fast Stream application process, please visit our dedicated page - https://www.civil-service-careers.gov.uk/fast-stream/fs-how-to-apply/fs-reasonable-adjustments/

If you need to contact us, please submit a request for help https://fsetatso.freshdesk.com/support/home



Feedback will only be provided if you attend an interview or assessment.

  • UK nationals

Working for the Civil Service

The Civil Service embraces diversity and promotes equal opportunities. As such, we run a Disability Confident Scheme (DCS) for candidates with disabilities who meet the minimum selection criteria.

description:
Job description:

Position Summary

The General Manager is the business leader of the restaurant, responsible for driving financial performance, building high-performing teams, and ensuring operational excellence. This role owns full accountability for sales, profitability, and execution, operating as the “CEO of the store.”

The GM sets the standard for leadership, culture, and results developing future leaders, delivering exceptional guest experiences, and executing strategic initiatives that drive long-term growth.

Business & Operational Leadership

  • Own total restaurant performance, including operations, profitability, and team execution
  • Lead all daily operations with full accountability for results
  • Ensure consistent execution of Quality, Service, and Cleanliness (QSC) standards
  • Conduct regular self-audits and operational walkthroughs
  • Ensure all systems, checklists, and processes are executed consistently

Financial Performance & Cost Control

  • Own and manage prime cost (labor + food) performance
  • Maintain labor targets (~20%) and food cost targets (~31%)
  • Analyze daily sales, labor reports, and key performance metrics
  • Forecast sales and build strategic schedules to maximize efficiency
  • Oversee payroll, cash handling, deposits, and financial accuracy
  • Manage inventory, truck orders, and product levels
  • Identify and prevent waste, variance, and loss

Sales Growth & Business Development

  • Drive top-line sales and execute growth strategies
  • Analyze trends and guest feedback to identify opportunities
  • Lead upselling and in-store performance initiatives
  • Execute Local Store Marketing (LSM) strategies and community engagement
  • Act as a brand ambassador within the local market
  • Manage online reputation, including guest reviews and feedback
  • Execute company promotions and initiatives with consistency

Team Leadership & Development

  • Recruit, hire, and retain a strong, engaged team
  • Develop Assistant Managers and Shift Leaders into future leaders
  • Build and maintain a leadership bench for growth
  • Conduct performance evaluations and hold team members accountable
  • Foster a positive, high-performance culture focused on results and development
  • Create clear pathways for internal promotion and career growth

Scheduling & Labor Strategy

  • Build and manage schedules aligned with sales forecasts
  • Ensure proper staffing levels across all dayparts
  • Adjust labor in real time to meet business demands
  • Hold leadership team accountable to labor performance and productivity

Guest Experience & Brand Protection

  • Deliver consistent, high-quality guest experiences on every visit
  • Monitor and improve guest satisfaction metrics
  • Resolve escalated guest concerns quickly and professionally
  • Identify and eliminate recurring service or operational issues

Compliance & Safety

  • Ensure full compliance with food safety, health, and sanitation standards
  • Maintain all required certifications, including ServSafe
  • Conduct routine safety checks and ensure equipment functionality
  • Prepare for and pass all audits and inspections

Administrative & Organizational Leadership

  • Maintain accurate and timely documentation across all systems
  • Lead regular team meetings to communicate goals and expectations
  • Oversee ordering of supplies, uniforms, and operational needs
  • Ensure inventory processes follow established standards (PAR levels and product mix)
  • Partner with leadership and support teams to drive business results

Work schedule

  • Monday to Friday
  • Weekend availability
  • 12 hour shift
  • 10 hour shift
  • 8 hour shift

Supplemental pay

  • Bonus pay

Benefits

  • Flexible schedule
  • Paid time off
  • Health insurance
  • Dental insurance
  • Vision insurance
  • Employee discount

Pay: $50,000.00 - 55,000.00 per year

About the job

Job summary

The Government Actuary’s Department (GAD) is a well-established non-ministerial department in the heart of government, which uses statistical analysis and probabilistic financial models to assess a wide range of risks facing the public sector. Using these techniques, we aim to enhance the stewardship of public sector finances by providing expert advice to government departments in areas including pensions, contingent risks, insurance, and social security.

Examples of our work include: (1) the regular assessment of approximately £1 trillion of public service pension schemes liabilities, covering around 15 million people; and (2) the ongoing appraisal of the financial positions of social security frameworks together with recommendations on how to manage them.

For further information about the role and GAD, please see the following pack: Project Management Lead - Project Management Lead

Job description

This role is an excellent opportunity to help shape the project management of such complex, important and often interdependent projects, and to support GAD in delivering high quality projects.

The successful applicant will be a project management professional with significant relevant experience and a proven track record of successfully delivering strategically important projects with senior stakeholders. You will have a desire to learn and understand how this relatively specialist department and its actuarial professionals operate. You will be able to adapt quickly to changing priorities and establish effective working relationships with all business areas.

At GAD we embrace diversity and believe that it builds a stronger and more effective organisation. It is therefore important to us that we recruit from a wide range of professional and personal backgrounds, bringing varying perspectives and experiences to our work. All our recruitment is made on merit, on the basis of open and fair competition.

1. Driving the effective use of Project Management across the Organisation by supporting our Business Units to

  • Implement project initiation and kick-off activity in line with wider best practice
  • Effectively manage projects with a focus on budgeting, planning, monitoring and delivery management
  • Proactively manage risk, issue and stakeholders

2. Working in partnership with Heads of Teams to:

  • understand the landscape of projects and support required
  • ensure the application of best practice in the delivery of projects
  • help build a culture focused on prioritisation and addressing issues resolutely and promptly
  • provide training and support across a wide range of different Project Management tools and techniques
  • develop, monitor and report on key project management performance indicators

3. Setting out the Project Management framework for the Department including central materials, training opportunities and communication channels

4. Ensuring that the project management processes, tools and documentation used within GAD are appropriate.

5. Ensuring that we adhere to the Governments Project Delivery Functional Standard.

About the job

Job summary

On the Fast Stream Yorkshire and the Humber scheme you will undertake a variety of different roles and develop a breadth of policy-making and delivery skills and experience. The scheme will include a secondment to local government or wider public service, providing you valuable experience in working in both local and central government.

Based in Yorkshire and the Humber for your entire Fast Stream journey you will have the opportunity to be a change maker across both local and national issues, building long standing networks and fostering greater collaboration with regional and local government, working together to innovate and deliver better outcomes for citizens across the country.

Roles will predominantly be based in the cities of Leeds, York and Sheffield.

Job description

The scheme offers the opportunity to work on national and local issues that really make a difference to people’s lives in Yorkshire and the Humber.
Throughout your time on the scheme, you will work across a range of departments and roles giving you exposure to a breadth of experience within the public sector.
Over the course of the three postings, you will work in a variety of roles ensuring you have the capability and skills needed to build networks and collaborate across sectors to solve complex problems at scale.
It will also include a secondment to local government or wider public service during your second year on the scheme, ensuring policy and delivery are better integrated.
You will have access to a range of learning that will equip you with the underpinning knowledge, tools and skills you need for your postings and future career. This could include training linked to AI, Policy, Operational Delivery and Leadership and Management.
You will have a buddy as you begin the scheme and there will be lots of opportunities to collaborate across your cohort of fast streamers.
The skills you will develop on the scheme are highly transferable across a broad range of government departments and local government, leaving you equipped to shape the career that you choose.


We aim to put all successful candidates through Security Clearance (SC). However, if you are ineligible for SC, please do not be deterred from applying; we have plenty of exciting roles available that only require standard Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) pre-employment checks. You can find more information about vetting clearance levels here: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/united-kingdom-security-vetting-clearance-levels

Person specification

You must be eligible to work in the UK
You need to have or be on track to receive, a 2:2 or higher in any degree subject including degree apprenticeships
Existing civil servants can apply without a degree before starting the scheme, all Cyber Fast Streamers must secure SC clearance

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £31,554, Fast Stream and Emerging Talent contributes £9,141 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).
The programme provides a solid foundation for promotion and long-term career progression and offers many advantages, which include:

Responsibility and autonomy in a variety of roles at the heart of the Civil Service

Excellent training and development opportunities

Close contact with senior civil servants and the opportunity to join a valuable network of future leaders

Enhanced support as you off-board from the scheme into your permanent role

Potential earning opportunities between £45k and £62k upon successful completion of the scheme

Further employment benefits include a generous annual leave offer starting at 25 days plus national holidays, access to the highly competitive Civil Service Pension Scheme, flexible working opportunities, season ticket loans, sports and social activities, childcare assistance and more.

Selection process details

Application Process

There are several phases in the Fast Stream application process. Some of these assessments are multimedia in that they present information in video, audio, graphical or visual formats, as well as text. We hope you find it an engaging process and one that gives you a real insight into the role of a fast streamer.

At the initial application stage you will be asked to complete some background information which will include some diversity questions - which are for monitoring purposes only and will have no bearing on selection outcomes - along with the opportunity to identify your preferences in terms of the different Fast Stream schemes. You can choose up to three.

When you apply please register with a personal email address, and not a work or university email address.

Assessment Phases

There are 2 online tests:

Work-based scenarios - This test measures interpersonal skills, utilising video based scenarios and you are required to assess the effectiveness of various responses.

Case Study assessment - In this test you are required to take work based scenarios on an imaginary role, learning and responding to a series of challenges and situations and adapting to the changes you are presented with.

Additional information - depending on the schemes you have chosen, there may be additional information to be completed, or an intermediate sift process. More information on the schemes that require additional information can be found https://www.civil-service-careers.gov.uk/fast-stream/fs-how-to-apply/fs-additional-information/

Fast Stream Assessment Centre - if you pass the above stages you'll be invited to attend a half day assessment centre. This will be conducted virtually online. The Fast Stream Assessment Centre (FSAC) reflects some of the key elements of a Fast Stream role and will consist of a written exercise, oral briefing exercise and a personal development conversation. Information will be presented via an app that you will be able to access remotely.

Final Selection Board - most schemes will then require a Final Selection Board . We'll ask you to attend this final assessment if you reach the required standard at FSAC. More information on the Final Selection Boards can be found https://www.civil-service-careers.gov.uk/fast-stream/fs-how-to-apply/fs-final-selection-board/

If you need to contact us, please submit a request for help https://fsetatso.freshdesk.com/support/home

title: Compliance and Risk Management Director
company: The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center
description:
The Director of Compliance and Risk Management (Director) oversees and administers OSUMT’s Compliance and Risk Management Programs (Programs) and is responsible for ensuring their effectiveness in identifying, preventing, detecting, and correcting potential or actual noncompliance with applicable laws and regulations and for leading efforts in risk identification, event review, and trend analysis. The Director oversees and administers the organization’s Compliance Plan and Risk Management Plan, serves as a subject matter expert to leadership and staff, and provides independent oversight of compliance and risk management activities. The Director ensures alignment with applicable laws, regulations, organizational policies and procedures, and the Code of Conduct. To maintain the integrity of the Programs, the Director serves as an independent resource with direct access to the Board and the authority to raise concerns, provide recommendations, and oversee compliance activities free from undue influence or conflicts of interest.

The Director provides strategic leadership for the Compliance Program. Responsibilities include: 1) overseeing compliance related activities; 2) providing strategic direction regarding compliance risk identification, assessment, mitigation, and reporting; 3) coordinating and integrating compliance activities across the organization; 4) monitoring and responding to the evolving regulatory and enforcement environment; and 5) promoting a culture of compliance, safety, ethics, accountability, and integrity through ongoing communication, education, and leadership engagement.

In administering the Risk Management Program, the Director collaborates with clinical and operational leaders to evaluate events, conduct investigations, and implement corrective action plans to reduce risk exposure and prevent recurrence. The Director oversees insurance renewals and claims tracking and assists with medical malpractice matters, including coordination with legal counsel and preparation for interviews or depositions.

The Director promotes a robust safety culture and ensures compliance with federal, state, and accreditation requirements. Strong communication, analytical ability, and organizational skills are essential to effectively lead committees, educate staff, and support high-reliability practices across the organization.

Education:

  • Bachelors degree required - Healthcare Administration, Public Health, Nursing, Business, Legal Studies, Risk Management, or related field.
  • Post Graduate Degree – viewed favorably (MHA, MPH, MBA, MS in Risk/Compliance)

License / Certification: CPHRM, CHC, CHPC, CPHO viewed favorably

Experience: 3-5+ years, prefer experience in healthcare field, hospital systems, or other highly regulated industry.

title: Head Coach - Women's Soccer
description:
The USF Department of Intercollegiate Athletics is an integral part of USF and its mission by sponsoring a diverse and nationally competitive Division I athletic program. The program serves several significant constituencies, including its student-athletes, who are students first. The most important priority of the program is the progress of the student-athletes toward graduation. Other priorities include the health, fitness and emotional development of student-athletes at USF.

Intercollegiate Athletics provide a sense of collegiality, allegiance, and pride for students, staff, faculty, alumni, boosters and the greater Tampa Bay community at large and serves as a focal point for their support. Within the framework of competitive excellence, Intercollegiate Athletics at USF are also a contact vehicle leading supporters to a greater awareness of the University's mission, academic programs and prominence as an educational institution.

  • Recruiting: The ability of the head coach to go wherever necessary off campus to games, tournaments, championships and identify prospective student-athletes with the talent and skill level to be successful at the highest level of athletic competition, while also possessing the academic ability to achieve academic success at USF. After identifying the prospective student-athlete, managing the recruitment process itself. The sending of materials and e mails to the prospect. Visiting the prospects home and parents. Setting up official visits and finally signing the prospective student-athlete to a scholarship. This is all done within the constraints of the budget that is allocated by the athletic department.
  • Training and preparation for the highest level of competition. Planning, organizing, scheduling, motivating and monitoring the student-athletes athletic progress towards successful competition. This entails the supervision of the playing (traditional season) and the non-traditional (spring) season. The traditional season is more intensive with competition and team training. While the spring season, must emphasize continual progress in strength and conditioning and individual skill improvement. Throughout both seasons individual and team meetings are held to communicate the goals of the individual and the team and how they are to be met. Assessment of individual and team progress are monitored constantly, allowing for adjustments to be made through instruction in preparation or changes to the program. This would include post-game analysis, scouting, videotaping training to show improvement and goal setting for again the individual and the team.
  • Academic progress: Monitor the academic progress of the student-athlete. This entails monitoring their grade progress, attendance and tutoring sessions. Constantly reviewing the consistency of effort made by the student-athlete being matched with the proper resources of the Academic Enrichment Center.
  • Budgeting: Creating, monitoring, and overseeing the program's budget. This would include but not be limited the major areas of recruiting, scholarships, travel, and equipment.
  • Community relations: Going out into the community and participating in programs that help represent USF in the best possible manner.
  • Fundraising: Providing opportunities to raise funds to support areas that need to be funded at a higher level. i.e. scholarships
  • Supervise the women's soccer coaching staff and integrate the other departments that pertain to the women's soccer program; including but not limited to sports information, strength and conditioning, NCAA compliance, academic staff (counselor, tutors, advisors) , and other departments or personnel as needed. Monitoring, motivating, and assessing the areas handled by the assistant coaches and their assigned areas of responsibility. ( i.e. training, tape analysis of game opponents, scouting, monitoring of study hall and tutoring hours)
  • Minimum Qualifications: This position requires a Master's degree in an appropriate area of specialization and one year of coaching experience at the high school level or above; or a bachelor's degree in an appropriate area of specialization and three years experience at the high school level or above. Successful experience as a graduate assistant or intern in an athletic program is acceptable for up to one year of the required experience.
  • Senate Bill 1310- The Florida Senate (https://www.flsenate.gov/Session/Bill/2023/1310) is conditional upon meeting all employment eligibility requirements in the U.S.
    • SB 1310: Substitution of Work Experience for Postsecondary Education Requirements
    • A public employer may include a postsecondary degree as a baseline requirement only as an alternative to the number of years of direct experience required, not to exceed:
    (a) Two years of direct experience for an associate degree;
    (b) Four years of direct experience for a bachelor’s degree;
    (c) Six years of direct experience for a master’s degree;
    (d) Seven years of direct experience for a professional degree; or
    (e) Nine years of direct experience for a doctoral degree
    • Related work experience may not substitute for any required licensure, certification, or registration required for the position of employment as established by the public employer and indicated in the advertised description of the position of employment.
    • Minimum Qualifications that require a high school diploma are exempt from SB 1310
  • Criminal History Background Check - Level 1

The University of South Florida is a top-ranked research university serving approximately 50,000 students from across the globe at campuses in Tampa, St. Petersburg, Sarasota-Manatee and USF Health. In 2025, U.S. News & World Report recognized USF with its highest overall ranking in university history, as a top 50 public university for the seventh consecutive year and as one of the top 15 best values among all public universities in the nation. U.S. News also ranks the USF Health Morsani College of Medicine in the highest tier, placing it as one of the top 16 medical schools in the nation and inside the top 10 among public universities. USF is a member of the Association of American Universities (AAU), a group that includes only the top 3% of universities in the U.S. With an all-time high of $750 million in research funding in 2025 and as a top 20 public university for producing U.S. patents, USF uses innovation to transform lives and shape a better future. The university generates an annual economic impact of nearly $10 billion for the state of Florida. USF’s Division I athletics teams compete in the American Conference. Learn more at www.usf.edu .

title: Head of Digital Business Partnering
company: Department of Health and Social Care
description:
• Job grade: Grade 6

  • Type of role: Business Management and Improvement, Digital, Information Technology, Strategy
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time, Job share, Part-time

Location

Leeds, London

About the job

Job summary

In the Department of Health and Social Care, we are proud of our purpose – to enable everyone to live more independent, healthier lives for longer. To achieve this, and create a great place to work, we have four values: we are inclusive, we constantly improve, we challenge, and we are agile. If this sounds like an environment you would like to work in, we would love to hear from you.

The DHSC Digital Transformation team works with the national health and care system to realise the benefits of digital, data and technology, to deliver better end to end services for their users and for the professionals who provide them.

We don’t manage live digital services; our role is more strategic. We partner with policy and commissioning teams to deliver user centred, design-led change, and to act as a bridge between policy and digital delivery teams. We support the Department and its arms' length bodies in a range of different ways - from providing short-term consultancy advice and digital training, to running full discoveries and alphas, and embedding team members in wider beta or live delivery teams.

We champion standards, user-centred design and accessibility in everything that we do.

Job description

As Head of Digital Business Partnering, you will lead a digital engagement and business partnering function that strengthens relationships between DHSC and senior digital, data and technology stakeholders across the wider healthcare system. You will build trusted relationships with senior leaders, provide strategic leadership for external engagement, and support work that improves collaboration across organisational boundaries. Working closely with Chief Digital and Information Officers (CDIOs) and senior stakeholders, you will help identify opportunities to share expertise, reduce duplication and improve outcomes through more joined-up digital, data and technology activity.

This is a highly visible leadership role operating at the intersection of strategy, engagement and delivery. You will provide leadership across digital business partnering activity, oversee key engagement forums and communities, and help ensure that organisations are better connected, informed and equipped to tackle shared digital, data and technology challenges together.

Person specification

Role responsibilities

  • Lead and develop a digital business partnering function, providing strategic direction, people leadership and fostering a high-performing, inclusive culture.
  • Build and maintain trusted relationships with senior digital leaders, CDIOs and stakeholders across DHSC and partner organisations, acting as a senior lead for outward-facing digital engagement.
  • Lead and support work to strengthen collaboration, visibility and digital capability across organisational boundaries.
  • Identify and manage strategic opportunities, risks, dependencies and emerging priorities across the digital, data and technology landscape, supporting informed decision-making and greater coordination between organisations.
  • Establish and lead engagement mechanisms that support collaboration across organisations, including senior leadership forums, working groups, communities of practice and strategic partnerships.
  • Provide strategic advice, challenge and briefing to senior stakeholders, helping shape digital, data and technology priorities across DHSC and partner organisations.

We are looking for an experienced and credible leader who can operate confidently in complex stakeholder environments and build strong relationships across organisational boundaries.

You will be comfortable engaging with senior leaders, translating strategic priorities into practical action and influencing without formal authority. You will bring strong digital awareness, excellent judgement and a passion for helping organisations work more effectively together.

You will enjoy working across organisational boundaries, understanding different perspectives and identifying opportunities where collaboration can deliver better outcomes. Most importantly, you will be motivated by helping others succeed and by improving how digital, data and technology are used to support shared priorities.

This role will include line management responsibilities.

Key skills and experience required for the role

Essential

  • Demonstrable experience of leading and developing high-performing teams, creating an inclusive environment where people can thrive and perform at their best.
  • Strong stakeholder management and relationship-building skills, with the ability to influence, challenge and build credibility with senior leaders across complex organisations.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with experience facilitating discussions, brokering agreement and communicating complex information to diverse audiences.
  • Broad knowledge of technology, digital and data delivery, together with significant practical experience in at least one digital specialism such as product management, delivery management, architecture, data, user-centred design or engineering.
  • Experience of planning and prioritising across multiple programmes, products, portfolios or organisations, with the ability to identify dependencies, risks and opportunities and translate these into practical action.
  • Knowledge and understanding of the public sector, with experience of business partnering, stakeholder engagement or relationship management, ideally within digital, technology, health or wider government settings.

Desirable

  • Experience working with public bodies, partner organisations or senior external stakeholders within a complex delivery environment.
  • Experience leading or contributing to cross-organisational transformation, collaboration initiatives, communities of practice or networks.
  • Knowledge of the health and care system, including the role of technology, digital and data in supporting organisational and system-wide priorities.

Behaviours

We'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:

  • Seeing the Big Picture
  • Leadership
  • Communicating and Influencing
  • Working Together

We only ask for evidence of these behaviours on your application form:

  • Seeing the Big Picture

Technical skills

We'll assess you against these technical skills during the selection process:

  • Knowledge of standards and ability to communicate technical concepts clearly.

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £73,559, Department of Health and Social Care contributes £21,310 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).
  • Learning and development tailored to your role

Artificial intelligence

Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. If you will be doing this, please advise Government Recruitment Service of your intention by emailing Pre-EmploymentChecks.grs@cabinetoffice.gov.uk stating the job reference number in the subject heading.

New entrants are expected to join on the minimum of the pay band.

Applicants who are successful at interview will be, as part of pre-employment screening, subject to a check on the Internal Fraud Database (IFD). This check also applies to employees who resign or otherwise leave before being dismissed for fraud or dishonesty had their employment continued. Any applicant’s details held on the IFD will be refused employment.

A candidate is not eligible to apply for a role within the Civil Service if the application is made within a 5 year period following a dismissal for carrying out internal fraud against government.

This role is being advertised on a permanent basis. Terms and Conditions

Candidates should note that DHSC’s Terms and Conditions of employment changed from 1 October 2013. It is the candidate’s responsibility to ensure they are aware of the terms and conditions they will adopt should they be successful.
