title: Director, School of Hospitality and Sport Management
description:
The Muma College of Business is one of fewer than 200 institutions worldwide with separate AACSB accreditation in both business and accounting. The College enrolls more than 9,000 students across seven schools: the Kate Tiedemann School of Business and Finance; the Lynn Pippenger School of Accountancy; the School of Hospitality and Sport Management; the School of Information Systems; the School of Management; the School of Marketing and Innovation; and the Baldwin Group School of Risk Management and Insurance.

In spring 2025, the college released a ten-year strategic plan centered on four priorities: student success, impactful research, community engagement, and expanded reach. Muma also has a long history of working with Tampa Bay businesses and organizations to create talent pipelines, support workforce development, and connect students with applied learning.

The School of Hospitality and Sport Management (SHSM) prepares students for leadership in hospitality, tourism, sport, and entertainment management. Launched in fall 2025, the School brought together the former School of Hospitality and Tourism Management and the Vinik Sport & Entertainment Management program. SHSM serves students on the Tampa and St. Petersburg campuses and is led by Interim Director Michelle Harrolle, who has directed the Vinik program since 2013.

The University of South Florida seeks an entrepreneurial academic leader to serve as Director of the School of Hospitality and Sport Management at the Muma College of Business. Reporting to the Dean, the Director will lead the School’s research, teaching, and outreach across USF’s Tampa and St. Petersburg campuses and serve as a visible ambassador for the School in Tampa Bay and beyond.

  • Lead externally. Serve as a highly visible ambassador who builds consequential relationships with hotel companies, professional sports franchises, venue operators, tourism organizations, developers, restaurateurs, entrepreneurs, alumni, donors, and civic leaders.
  • Raise the resources. Make fundraising and resource development a central responsibility: articulate the School’s vision, cultivate transformational gifts, secure corporate investment, and work closely with the Dean and advancement team on major fundraising initiatives.
  • Make Tampa Bay the classroom. Expand experiential learning through internships, residencies, executive-led courses, applied research, consulting projects, major-event experiences, and partnerships connected to the stadium, Uptown Landing, and the broader region.
  • Develop talent and the workforce. Make the School a preferred talent partner for the region’s hospitality, tourism, sports, and entertainment industries while preparing students for national and global leadership roles.
  • Lead innovation. Keep the curriculum and research responsive to artificial intelligence, data analytics, customer experience, sports technology, revenue optimization, food innovation, and new models of fan and guest engagement, and foster entrepreneurship.
  • Champion teaching, research, and student success. Foster a collaborative environment within the School and across the College that supports faculty research, teaching excellence, strong advising, career outcomes, and alumni engagement.
  • Lead the academic enterprise. Direct strategic planning aligned with the College’s ten-year plan; recruit, evaluate, develop, and expand the faculty and staff; manage the budget and course scheduling; unite the School’s programs into a coherent portfolio; and sustain accreditation standards, including AACSB.

Minimum Qualifications:

  1. A terminal degree (Ph.D. or equivalent) in hospitality management, sport management, or a related field, preferably from an AACSB-accredited institution or international equivalent.
  2. Outstanding accomplishments in teaching, research, and engagement that meet USF standards for appointment with tenure at the associate or full professor level.

Preferred Qualifications:

  1. Bold, entrepreneurial leadership with an appreciation for the nuances of guiding an academic enterprise; demonstrated vision, execution, and strategic planning, and the drive to build something new.
  2. Ability to develop and lead strategic and tactical plans in collaboration with stakeholders.
  3. A keen understanding of, and contacts within, the hospitality, tourism, sport, and entertainment industries.
  4. A compelling fundraiser with a demonstrated ability to cultivate major gifts and corporate investment, and a record of building external partnerships.
  5. Strong people-management skills, including the ability to recruit, retain, and develop outstanding faculty and staff, and evidence of sound financial and operational management.
  6. An inclusive, collaborative, and persuasive communicator who can unite previously separate programs.

The University of South Florida is a top-ranked research university serving approximately 50,000 students from across the globe at campuses in Tampa, St. Petersburg and USF Health. In 2025, U.S. News & World Report recognized USF with its highest overall ranking in university history, as a top 50 public university for the seventh consecutive year and as one of the top 15 best values among all public universities in the nation. U.S. News also ranks the USF Health Morsani College of Medicine in the highest tier, placing it as one of the top 16 medical schools in the nation and inside the top 10 among public universities. USF is a member of the Association of American Universities (AAU), a group that includes only the top 3% of universities in the U.S. With an all-time high of $750 million in research funding in 2025 and as a top 20 public university for producing U.S. patents, USF uses innovation to transform lives and shape a better future. The university generates an annual economic impact of nearly $10 billion for the state of Florida. USF’s Division I athletics teams compete in the American Conference. Learn more at .

description:

Location

Cambridge Lab - Addenbrooke’s Hospital Pathology Block

About the job

Job summary

The Clinical Microbiology and Public Health Laboratory (CMPHL) at Cambridge is part of the UKHSA Clinical Network Laboratory division and provides services to Cambridge University Hospital (Addenbrooke’s) and Royal Papworth Hospital NHS Trusts, the surrounding district, and other NHS Laboratories. It has active research and epidemiological interests. The laboratory undergoes assessment against UKAS ISO 15189 standards and has strong teaching interests. Set on the outskirts of the university city of Cambridge, within the Cambridge Biomedical Campus, Addenbrooke’s Hospital is one of the top hospitals in the UK and a thriving NHS Foundation Trust. Addenbrooke’s is closely associated with leading educational providers including the University of Cambridge and is a major centre for biomedical research and education.

Working for your organisation

We pride ourselves as being an employer of choice, where Everyone Matters promoting equality of opportunity to actively encourage applications from everyone, including groups currently underrepresented in our workforce.

UKHSA ethos is to be an inclusive organisation for all our staff and stakeholders. To create, nurture and sustain an inclusive culture, where differences drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our workforce and wider communities. We do this through celebrating and protecting differences by removing barriers and promoting equity and equality of opportunity for all.

Please visit our careers site for more information https://gov.uk/ukhsa/careers

Job description

CMPHL undertakes a wide range of manual and automated routine and specialist microbiological and molecular investigations, for clinical and public health service delivery.

The Laboratory Services Manager will contribute to planning, leading, organising and controlling the operation of the laboratory service in line with the operational direction of the Regional Head of Laboratory Operations and clinical direction of Clinical Services Lead. They will be responsible for ensuring and improving the performance, quality, efficiency and safety of laboratory operations through the implementation of effective methods and strategies.

The post holder is expected to act independently and is accountable for his / her own actions and those of others, line managed by the UKHSA Regional Head of Laboratory Operations and clinically accountable to the relevant Lead Consultants, through the Clinical Services Director.

  • To lead, coordinate and monitor the work of the provision of clinical and public health microbiology laboratory services, managing workflows and staffing to maximise service quality and timeliness
  • Deputise for the Regional Head of Laboratory Operations
  • Contribute to the development of and manage effective business continuity and resilience arrangements.
  • Management of employee productivity, coordinating workforce availability, including rostering, training planning, skills development and succession planning.
  • Oversee laboratory equipment and consumables, including supplier liaison regarding equipment maintenance, performance and fault resolution.
  • Support the relevant Lead Consultants to develop and integrate diagnostic and analytical techniques into appropriate patient pathways.
  • Contribute to the planning and implementation of integrated multi sectional service developments.

Management and Organisation

  • Within the framework laid down by the Regional Head of Laboratory Operations and under the clinical leadership of the Clinical Services Director/Lead undertake the management and organisation of the laboratory service.
  • Ensure the development and maintenance of Standard Operating Procedures, policies and working practices in accordance with a programme agreed by the Regional Head of Laboratory Operations, Clinical Services Director and other members of the Management Team.
  • Analyse and interpret any new guidance from relevant sources and to then provide advice for the development of departmental and service-wide policies and procedures.

Finance and Resources

  • Ensure an adequate and economic local supply of reagents and non-capital equipment
  • Review consumables and non-capital equipment used by the laboratory and identify opportunities for development and improvement in quality and cost effectiveness.
  • Manage departmental budgets and delegated finances
  • Contribute to costing of services, ensuring that service change control includes full financial review

Asset and Buildings Management

  • Work with UKHSA leads to manage procurement process of the capital equipment programmes and asset management
  • Ensure maintenance and service contracts are in place and local asset management is documented and current within the Quality Management system
  • Liaise with the Estates Departments for maintenance of building and services
  • Take a lead role in the future planning of new accommodation and alterations to existing premises.
  • Be responsible for facilities and environmental aspects within the laboratory.

Service Development

  • Lead in the review, development and implementation of business and strategic plans
  • Facilitate the introduction and development of new technologies, methodologies and systems of work for service improvement and in compliance with quality standards
  • Review practices through policies, audits, benchmarking, LEAN working and continuous improvement.

Scientific and Clinical

  • Be actively involved in scientific and technical duties within the department which may include delivering specialist technical advice to service users.
  • Accountable for the direct service delivery of a high standard of professional competence in the performance of tests and investigations across the Clinical Microbiology and Public Health service
  • Analyse, interpret, technically validate and report on routine complex and specialist tests.

Health and Safety

  • Ensure compliance with local and national Health and Safety legislation and recommendations and implement required changes.
  • Ensure the notification of all dangerous occurrences within the department/site to appropriate bodies and reporting on UKHSA systems
  • Ensure staff receive training in Health and Safety practices

Quality Assurance

  • In collaboration with the Quality manager, develop a clear accountability framework for the service in respect of quality assurance.
  • Ensure that the laboratory complies with ISO 15189, IDPS and HTA standards and HCPC/IBMS requirements and adheres to the principles and requirements of sound Clinical Governance
  • Ensure participation in appropriate External Quality Assurance schemes, monitor departmental performance in such schemes and implement corrective actions

Please note that UKHSA is exploring options for the future of the Clinical Network Laboratories service and that further information will be shared as the review progresses.

Person specification

Essential role criteria

  • Registration with Healthcare Professions Council (Biomedical Scientist)
  • Postgraduate level qualification in Infection Sciences subjects equivalent to Fellowship of the Institute of Biomedical Sciences or MSc
  • Recent technical and managerial experience in an Infection Sciences diagnostic laboratory In depth post graduate technical experience and scientific knowledge of Microbiology gained including within a service management role
  • High level knowledge of laboratory policies, regulatory standards, Standard Operating Procedures, codes of practice, legislation and professional guidelines including those relating to Health and Safety
  • Knowledge and experience of staff management techniques (e.g. recruitment, training, supervision, organisational, appraisal, performance management, grievance and disciplinary)
  • High level of theoretical and practical knowledge of microbiological techniques and procedures and their clinical applications, and be technically competent at specimen processing and interpretation
    Robust understanding of the Public Health requirements of a clinical microbiology laboratory

Benefits

  • Learning and development tailored to your role
  • An environment with flexible working options
  • A culture encouraging inclusion and diversity
  • A Civil Service pension with an employer contribution of 28.97%

Things you need to know

Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Selection process details

This vacancy will be assessed using a competency-based framework which will assess your qualifications, knowledge and experience and / or skills and abilities outlined in the essential criteria

Stage 1 : Application

You will be required to complete an application form. You will be assessed on the listed essential criteria, and this will be in the form of a :

  • Application form (‘Employer/ Activity history’ section on the application)
  • 1,500 word Supporting Statement

This should outline how you consider your skills, experience and knowledge provide evidence of your suitability for the role, with reference to the essential criteria

You will receive a joint score for your application form and statement. The application form is the kind of information you would put into your CV. Please be advised you will not be able to upload your CV. Please complete the application form in as much detail as possible. Please do not email us your CV

Longlisting

In the event of a large number of applications we will longlist into 3 piles of:

  • Meets all essential criteria
  • Meets some essential criteria
  • Meets no essential criteria

If used, the pile(s) ‘Meets all essential criteria’ and will proceed to shortlisting.

Shortlisting

In the event of a large number of applications we may conduct an initial sift, on the lead criteria of :

  • Registration with Healthcare Professions Council (Biomedical Scientist)

If you are successful at this stage, you will progress to interview. Feedback will not be provided at this stage

Stage 2: Interview

You will be invited to a (single ) face to face interview at Addenbrooke’s Hospital Pathology Block, Microbiology Department

If face to face interviews are planned, in exceptional circumstances, we may be able to offer a remote interview

Knowledge , Experience Skills & abilities will be tested at interview

Open to all external applicants (anyone) from outside the Civil Service (including internal applicants)

For meaningful National Security Vetting checks to be carried out individuals need to have lived in the UK for a sufficient period of time. You should normally have been resident in the United Kingdom for the last 3 years as the role requires Counter Terrorism Check (CTC) clearance. In exceptional circumstances UK residency less than the outlined periods may not necessarily bar you from gaining national security vetting and applicants should contact the Vacancy Holder/Recruiting Manager listed in the advert for further advice

UKHSA is investing in a new state-of-the-art National Biosecurity Centre in Harlow, Essex, which will eventually bring together teams currently based at Canary Wharf, Colindale and Porton Down. For more details, please see: Huge biosecurity centre investment to boost pandemic protection - GOV.UK.

The new facilities will start becoming operational in the mid-2030s, with full completion by 2038. Staff will move in phases as facilities become available. If you're appointed to a role currently based at Canary Wharf, Colindale or Porton Down, please note that we'll continue investing in these sites for the next decade. As we get closer to the transition, we'll provide full information about relocation support available to staff.

This is separate to the Disability Confident Scheme. title: Data, Analytics and AI - Product Manager
description:
• Job grade: Grade 7
  • Contract type: Permanent
  • Business area: CO - Public Sector Fraud Authority
  • Type of role: Analytical
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time, Job share
  • Number of jobs available: 1

Location

Glasgow, London, Manchester, Newcastle-upon-Tyne, York

About the job

Job summary

Cabinet Office supports the Prime Minister and ensures the smooth running of government - from developing policy, to modernising public services. We welcome talented people from all backgrounds with the skills and the commitment to build a career in the Civil Service.

The Cabinet Office Purpose is:

  • to maintain the integrity of the Union, coordinate the security of the realm and sustain a flourishing democracy;
  • to support the design and implementation of HM Government’s policies and the Prime Minister’s priorities; and
  • to ensure the delivery of the finest public services by attracting and developing the best public servants and improving the efficiency of government.

As an organisation of approximately 7,000 employees, the Cabinet Office is a vibrant, modern and exciting place to work, attracting a diverse workforce which represents the people we serve. Our main offices are in London, Glasgow, Newcastle, York and Manchester, but we have staff based around the UK.

At the heart of this are our Cabinet Office values. To deliver our Purpose and help make Cabinet Office a great place to work, we all commit to:

  • treating everyone with Respect;
  • actively Collaborate, and
  • build Trust.

We have an aspiration to become the most inclusive employer across the Civil Service. We have a number of staff benefits, including flexible working, and access to a number of staff support networks to ensure we meet this.

This role offers an unparalleled opportunity to work at the very heart of government. The Public Sector Fraud Authority is at the cutting edge of government’s response to tackling fraud against the public sector and builds on the internationally recognised reputation of the Counter Fraud Function as a world-leader in tackling fraud and corruption in the public sector. Working with us, you will be placed at the forefront of shaping policy that will have an impact across the breadth of the public sector, as well as building cutting edge data drive tools to deliver counter fraud savings for government.

Right now, fraud represents a cost to the government which is estimated at £29bn-£52bn per year. At PSFA, we play an instrumental role in spearheading the Government's response to fraud by developing innovative policies and initiatives to counter this threat with the mission of funnelling real, tangible financial benefits back to the public.

Job description

This is an exciting opportunity to join a pivotal team at the heart of public sector innovation.

The Public Sector Fraud Authority (PSFA) works with departments and public bodies to better understand and reduce the impact of fraud against the public sector. As part of its mandate, it provides data analytics services and access to technology solutions to find and prevent fraud using the latest tools.

As a Product Manager, you will play a crucial role in developing and delivering our product roadmap and managing the delivery of data and AI products throughout their entire lifecycle. You will work closely with technical experts from the Digital, Data, and Technology (DDaT) profession, including Data Engineers, Data Scientists, Business Analysts, and more. These technical roles are integral to our mission of deploying advanced analytics and AI tools across government to counter fraud.

The Role

The Product Manager within the Public Sector Fraud Authority’s Data Analytics Service is responsible for developing and delivering a range of data and AI products to enable public bodies to detect and prevent fraud. You will work with multidisciplinary teams and lead on the delivery of our products through their entire lifecycle, from discovery to alpha-stage development, and beta service implementation, ensuring they deliver measurable outcomes and maximise financial benefits for the public. This role requires the job holder to balance the needs of anti-fraud operations with user requirements and technical feasibility, while advocating for a user-centred, and data-informed approach.

Product Strategy and Vision

  • Strategic Ownership: Develop and articulate a clear product vision and strategy for data, analytics, and AI capabilities, ensuring alignment with PSFA’s mission to counter fraud and the wider Cabinet Office/Government priorities.
  • Managing Product Outcomes: Define, track, and regularly report on Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and success metrics that measure product value, performance, and impact on counter-fraud savings. Use trusted data and rigorous analysis to inform product decisions and drive continuous improvement.
  • Creating Value for Money: Estimate the value of product features and capabilities, and compare this against the effort and cost of delivery. Actively identify opportunities for the reuse of data or components to maximise value for money.

Delivery and Life Cycle Management

  • Product Management: Own and prioritise the product roadmap and backlog, working with the team to investigate and validate what adds value now and what could add value in the future.
  • Agile and Lean Practices: Select and apply the most appropriate delivery methods (e.g., Agile, Lean) for the team, fostering a culture of experimentation, reflective practice, and continuous adaptation to improve ways of working.
  • Life Cycle Management: Manage the product through all phases of the life cycle (discovery, alpha, beta, live, retirement), ensuring the product is developed and maintained in line with appropriate service standards.

User and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Applying User-Centred Insights: Advocate for and ensure continuous user research is conducted to deeply understand the needs of anti-fraud analysts, investigators, and other operational users. Use these insights to represent users in all internal discussions and determine priorities.
  • Stakeholder Relationship Management: Proactively identify and manage relationships with a complex stakeholder environment, including policy teams, operational leads, technical partners, and other government departments. Develop communication strategies to ensure transparency, manage expectations, and build long-term strategic relationships.
  • Product Leadership: Advocate for the product and a product-led approach across the organisation. Consult, mediate, and negotiate with stakeholders, while protecting the development team from unnecessary distractions to focus on delivery.

title: In-Room Dining Telephone Service Agent (Evenings & Overnight)
description:
POSITION SUMMARY

Telephone Service Agent - InRoom Dining
(IRD Order Taker - Evenings & Overnight)

**This position is for an Evenings and Overnight Shift.

Food and beverage enthusiast who really enjoys making guests feel at home and talking guests through menus. This role requires the ability to know the finest details of the menu and to share this expertise with guests and answer any menu questions. Food and Beverage Server allows guests to experience warm greetings, flawless table settings, precise food and beverage service, and friendly engaging demeanor through their experience, providing each guest with a dining experience that will be remembered long after their stay.

Communicate with the kitchen regarding menu questions, and product availability. Be knowledge in dietary restrictions and allergies. Diligently communicate additional meal requirements, allergies, dietary needs, and special requests to the kitchen. Check in with guests throughout their experience to ensure satisfaction with each food course and/or beverages. Maintain cleanliness of work areas, china, glass, etc., throughout the day. Complete closing duties, including restocking items etc. Present physical and accurate check to guest and process payment.

The ideal candidate will have:

  • 2-3 year’s previous food and beverage serving experience required
  • Must be customer and team oriented
  • Ability to multi-task and work in a fast pace environment
  • Serve food and beverages to guests making recommendations if needed
  • Excellent guest service skills and communication skills (English required)
  • Must be able to work flexible working hours, weekends and holidays
  • Demonstrates knowledge and proficiency of all applicable food & beverage laws and regulations
  • Demonstrate Excellent knowledge of Food & Beverage especially meats & Wine knowledge
  • Hospitality Graduate or Certified Service Professional required.
  • Experience with working with POS system (Oracle Hospitality Symphony desirable)
  • Move, lift, carry, push, pull, and place objects weighing less than or equal to 50 pounds without assistance
  • Stand and work at an extended period of time.
  • Able to work outdoors in the elements of the Caribbean weather
  • Must be 18 years of age or older

Take room service orders over the phone. Answer questions on menu selections, and check with kitchen staff. Answer guest questions or concerns regarding the origin, vintage, and style of various wines. Place and log call back for room service order. Notify guests and management of delays in service delivery. Communicate additional meal requirements, allergies, dietary needs, and special requests to the kitchen. Maintain cleanliness of work areas throughout the day. Record transaction in MICROS system at time of order. Complete all closing reports, including MICROS reports. Process all payment methods.

Follow all company and safety and security policies and procedures; report accidents, injuries, and unsafe work conditions to manager; and complete safety training and certifications. Ensure uniform and personal appearance are clean and professional, maintain confidentiality of proprietary information, and protect company assets. Welcome and acknowledge all guests according to company standards, anticipate and address guests’ service needs, assist individuals with disabilities, and thank guests with genuine appreciation. Speak with others using clear and professional language, and answer telephones using appropriate etiquette. Develop and maintain positive working relationships with others, and support team to reach common goals. Ensure adherence to quality expectations and standards. Stand, sit, or walk for an extended period of time. Move, lift, carry, push, pull, and place objects weighing less than or equal to 10 pounds without assistance. Perform other reasonable job duties as requested by Supervisors.

Education: High school diploma or G.E.D. equivalent.

title: FLEX OSR Enterprise Program Support Services – Project Manager
description:

Drawing upon expertise in Rooms Operations, Food & Beverage Operations, or both, this role provides training, consulting, operational assessments, project management, and hands-on coaching designed to strengthen service culture, improve operational execution, enhance system adoption, and elevate the overall guest experience across Marriott-managed and franchise hotels.

The EPSS Project Manager partners with hotel leaders, associates, owners, franchisees, and internal stakeholders to assess operational needs, facilitate workshops, deliver training, implement operational and system-related initiatives, and develop tailored solutions that drive measurable and sustainable performance improvement. Success in this role requires the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously, adapt to varying hotel environments and business needs, and build strong relationships across a diverse stakeholder group.

Programs supported may include PMS Systems + Guest Experience, Operational Impact Support, Post Opening Hotel Operational Refresh, F&B Refinement, Midscale OSR Support Initiatives, and other enterprise programs and performance improvement initiatives as assigned.

title: Senior Governance & Change Manager (f/m/d)
description:
About the Role

We are looking for a Senior Governance & Change Manager to help shape and continuously improve how Digital Technology operates within E.ON Energy Markets (EMDT).

This role sits at the intersection of governance, transformation, operational excellence and organizational effectiveness. You will work closely with Digital Leadership, Product Teams, Enterprise Architects, Controllers and stakeholders across E.ON Energy Markets and Digital Technology to drive transparency, improve execution and ensure that strategic priorities are translated into measurable outcomes.

As E.ON Energy Markets continues to evolve its Digital Technology operating model, this role will play a central part in shaping how change is governed, how performance is managed and how cross-functional initiatives are delivered. You will challenge the status quo, identify opportunities for improvement and help create an environment that enables high-quality delivery in a fast-moving trading technology landscape.

This role goes beyond traditional project coordination or PMO activities. We are looking for someone who combines strong governance and organizational skills with an understanding of digital technology and energy trading, can challenge stakeholders constructively and is able to drive outcomes across organizational boundaries without formal authority.

What You Will Own

Governance and Change Management

  • Own and continuously evolve the EMDT change management process within our SAFe/DevOps approach
  • Drive improvements to governance, efficiency and delivery quality across the change lifecycle and ensure transparency across decisions, priorities, dependencies and organizational risks. Establish governance mechanisms that balance agility, quality and operational stability while adapting to AI-native product DevOps.
  • Close collaboration with Energy Markets Business

Performance Management and Leadership Support

Own the preparation, coordination and continuous improvement of Performance Dialogues for EMDT and work closely with the digital leadership team to transform operational data management insights and prepare respective decision-ready content.

  • Challenge assumptions, identify root causes and help ensure that actions result in measurable outcomes.
  • Track commitments, actions and outcomes to strengthen accountability across the organization.

Operational Strategy Alignment

  • Support the consolidation of product and domain-level strategies into a coherent operational target picture for Digital Technology.
  • Work closely with Enterprise Architects, Domain Leads and Product Teams to identify synergies, dependencies and alignment opportunities.
  • Facilitate cross-domain discussions and help ensure consistent execution against agreed priorities.
  • Maintain transparency on strategic progress, risks and interdependencies.

Cross-Functional Management and Disaster Recovery

  • Drive initiatives across teams (Product teams, Finance, Strategy) with different objectives, priorities and perspectives.
  • Lead activities related to Disaster Recovery and Business Continuity Management. This includes ensuring that recovery objectives, documentation and governance requirements are understood, maintained and monitored, as well as supporting the identification and resolution of recovery gaps.
  • Contribute to the further development of resilience capabilities as an increasingly important pillar of Energy Markets Digital Technologies’ operational excellence.

What We Are Looking For

Required

  • 10+ years of experience in IT governance, organizational effectiveness, operational excellence, transformation or comparable roles with a minimum of 5 years experience in C-level stakeholder management
  • Knowledge of Energy Markets, Energy Trading and Trading Technologies
  • Strong hands-on knowledge of AI technologies & tools, familiarity with AI-native product development
  • High degree of resilience, ownership and organizational awareness.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities with the ability to translate complex situations into structured decisions processes and actions.
  • Excellent communication skills in English (German is a plus), facilitation and stakeholder management skills

Preferred

  • Strong understanding of software delivery organizations
  • Experience in collaborating with architects, developers as well as financial and business analyst functions.
  • Understanding of IT-Infrastructure, Business Continuity Management and Disaster Recovery concepts.
  • Experience preparing senior management material and facilitating decision-making processes.

What Success Looks Like

You will help build a Digital Technology organization that is:

Transparent in its governance. Efficient in its execution. Accountable in its delivery. Resilient in its operations. And continuously improving in the way it manages change.

You will be recognized as a trusted partner who enables leaders and teams to focus on delivering value by creating clarity, driving accountability and helping turn strategic ambition into operational reality.

title: Workplace Technology Engineer
description:
• Job grade: Grade 7
  • Contract type: Fixed term, Loan
  • Length of employment: 12 months
  • Business area: DSIT - Digital, Technologies and Telecoms
  • Type of role: Operational Delivery
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time, Job share, Part-time
  • Number of jobs available: 1

Location

London, Manchester

About the job

Job summary

The UK AI Security Institute (AISI) exists to make frontier AI systems secure, trustworthy, and beneficial for society. We work at the heart of the UK government with direct lines to No. 10, advancing our understanding of how to evaluate and govern advanced AI systems so they can be deployed safely and responsibly.

Our mission is to strengthen state technical capacity in AI security research to support both government and global partners in managing the risks and harnessing the opportunities of this transformative technology.

Job description

You'll join AISI's Workplace Technology team, a sub-team of Business Operations, which is part of the Talent & Operations directorate. Business Operations looks at how AISI runs as an organisation and how to improve it, and we're its technical arm.

AISI needs to keep pace with the frontier AI labs it works with. We're also part of government, so we carry a public body's legal duties and security obligations, and much of our infrastructure is shared with other departments. Bringing in a new tool can need sign-off from several approval boards and changes to identity, devices and networking, each owned by a different provider.

Our job is to close that gap while keeping AISI secure and accountable. We don't think anyone in government has fully cracked this yet, and we find it an exciting problem to work on. We have three missions:

  • Identify and strategise. Work out what software and systems AISI needs, and how they should be run and governed.
  • Procure, build and integrate. Buy or build the tools AISI needs, get them through government security and assurance, and automate the workflows that cause the most friction.
  • Enable and upskill. Help staff adopt new tools and ways of working, and raise the quality of AI use across AISI.

AISI is also deciding how much of its technology it should own and run itself, and you'd help shape that.

We're a close group (4-5) of curious problem-solvers who care about each other. We like messy problems and we're honest with each other when something isn't working. If that sounds like you, we'd love to hear from you.

What you'll do: examples from the team's current work

This is what the team is working on at the moment, to give you a flavour of the job. The work is varied, and most weeks involve some coding, some time with stakeholders and some strategy work.

  • Connecting AI assistants to everyday work tools. We're securely linking our in-house AI assistant platform to staff email, calendars, Teams and documents in Microsoft 365, and building the controls needed for data protection sign-off.
  • Improving our AI assistant platform, which staff across AISI use every day. We ship new features and UX improvements, and we're fixing findings from a recent independent security test.
  • Automating identity and access. We're designing an Okta-based setup, backed by a single reliable source of people data, so that joiners, movers and leavers get (and lose) the right access automatically.
  • Rebuilding operational workflows. We've replaced spreadsheet and email processes in Finance and Grants with Airtable systems, and we're building small web apps with proper approvals and dashboards for other teams.
  • Evaluating and deploying new AI tooling. Scanning the market for emerging AI productivity and agentic tooling, assessing options against AISI's security, data protection and operational requirements, and taking the strongest candidates through evaluation, governance and rollout.
  • Fixing tech issues that cause a lot of friction. We recently worked with our IT provider and a vendor to diagnose a network security issue that kept cutting off engineers' remote development sessions.
  • Shaping AISI's long-term technology. We're working out how AISI's devices, identity, Microsoft 365 and software should be run and governed in future, and how much of that AISI should own itself. That means mapping dependencies and weighing up options with senior leaders.

Person specification

We're flexible on the exact profile. We expect strong candidates will meet many of the criteria below, but not all of them.

Essential

  • Has solid software engineering experience. Has worked 2+ years as a software engineer and/or equivalent academic or production experience. Comfortable writing Python or TypeScript, working in shared codebases with peer review and CI, and debugging integrations from logs and documentation. Experience in infrastructure engineering and building in environments with stronger security needs highly appreciated.
  • Enjoys improving the way people work. Cares about the person stuck with a clunky process and enjoys turning painful workflows into ones that work.
  • Thinks in systems and works well within constraints in a resourceful way. Looks beyond symptoms to understand root causes, dependencies and trade-offs. When there are challenges, whether it's from a stakeholder perspective or a security perspective, can come up with creative and pragmatic solutions.
  • Prioritises well and follows through. Can identify what matters most, make sensible trade-offs, and focus effort where it will have the greatest impact. Sees important work through to completion rather than leaving it 80% done.
  • Communicates clearly, in writing and in the room. Can write concise documents for senior leaders, explain workflows in plain language, and discuss design decisions confidently with an architectural review board.
  • Exercises good judgement about risk. Handles sensitive data appropriately, knows when something needs additional scrutiny.
  • Uses AI critically as part of day-to-day work. Day-to-day workflow integrates latest AI tools and models, whilst reviewing their outputs critically.
  • Builds trust within and across teams. Works effectively with operators, engineers, security colleagues and external providers. Keeps people informed, takes concerns seriously, and makes collaboration straightforward.

Desirable

  • Experience with enterprise IT or platforms, such as identity and access management (Okta, Entra), Microsoft 365 administration or integration, device management, or cloud platforms.
  • Experience in government or a similar environment, such as another public body or a regulated industry, where decisions go through formal governance and you've had to work within it.

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £56,850, Department for Science, Innovation & Technology contributes £16,469 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

The Department for Science, Innovation and Technology offers a competitive mix of benefits including:

  • A culture of flexible working, such as job sharing, homeworking and compressed hours.
  • Automatic enrolment into the Civil Service Pension Scheme, with an employer contribution of 28.97%.
  • A minimum of 25 days of paid annual leave, increasing by 1 day per year up to a maximum of 30.
  • An extensive range of learning & professional development opportunities, which all staff are actively encouraged to pursue.
  • Access to a range of retail, travel and lifestyle employee discounts.

Office attendance

The Department operates a discretionary hybrid working policy, which provides for a combination of working hours from your place of work and from your home in the UK. The current expectation for staff is to attend the office or non-home based location for 40-60% of the time over the accounting period.

Things you need to know

Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Selection process details

As part of the application process you will be asked to complete a CV and personal statement. In the event of high volume applications we will sift on cv only.

Further details around what this will entail are listed on the application form.

Applications will be sifted on the CV and personal statement.

Please use your personal statement (in no more than 750 words) for the following:

Tell us why you want to join AISI's Workplace Technology team as an engineer, and what you'd bring. Please include:

One concrete example of a product, internal tool or automation you've shipped: the problem, what you built (be specific about the design, architecture, APIs or low-code platforms used), the outcome, and what you'd do differently.

And answer to one of these two:

What motivates you to come into work everyday? What gives you a sense of fulfilment in work?

What's a product, tool or solution that you particularly admire. Whether it is in its design, in the way it solves a problem elegantly or efficiently, or changes how people interact with a system or task, or something you wished you had built yourself.

Interviews

  • Interview 1: Short screening interview about your motivation for joining AISI and this role
  • Interview 2: Task-based interview

title: Engineering Manager
description:
JOB SUMMARY

Manages all engineering/maintenance operations, including maintaining the building, grounds and physical plant with particular attention towards safety, security and asset protection. Accountable for managing the budget, capital expenditure projects, preventative maintenance and energy conservation. Responsible for maintaining regulatory requirements. Assists in leading the emergency response team for all facility issues. Helps to increase guest and employee satisfaction through effective communications and training.

CANDIDATE PROFILE

Education and Experience

• High school diploma or GED; 4 years experience in the engineering and maintenance or related professional area; technical training in HVAC-R/electrical/plumbing.

OR

• 2-year degree from an accredited university in Building and Construction, Engineering, Mechanics, or related major; 2 years experience in the engineering and maintenance or related professional area; technical training in HVAC-R/electrical/plumbing.

CORE WORK ACTIVITIES

Managing Engineering Operations and Budgets

• Manages the physical plant including equipment, refrigeration, HVAC, plumbing, water treatment and electrical systems.

• Ensures regulatory compliance to facility regulations and safety standards.

• Manages and controls heat, light and power and recommends current best methods for energy conservation and economical facility operations.

• Develops specifications and requirements for service contracts and administers such contracts to support building needs.

• Distributes preventive maintenance and repair work orders and monitors timeliness and quality of completion.

• Oversees and directs the maintenance of grounds, guestrooms, public space, restaurants, property vehicles and recreational facilities.

• Develops a long term plan for preventative maintenance and asset protection and overseeing execution of plan.

• Develops project plans in accordance with renovation or new construction needs.

• Contacts contractors for bids and supervising construction to ensure timely completion of projects within budgetary guidelines.

• Builds positive relationships with external customers such as city building/zoning department, fire prevention bureau and vendors.

• Ensures fire crew has complete understanding of all procedures, equipment and alarms.

• Performs monthly property inspection to ensure buildings and grounds are maintained in excellent condition.

• Conducts guest room and common area inspection to ensure guest satisfaction.

• Inspects and evaluates the physical condition of facilities in order to determine the type of work required.

• Recommends or arranges for additional services such as painting, repair work, renovations, and the replacement of furnishings and equipment.

• Selects and orders or purchasing new equipment, supplies, and furnishings.

• Manages parts and equipment inventory.

Maintaining Property Standards

• Ensures building and equipment licenses and certifications are current.

• Maintains property life safety systems (fire fighting equipment, sprinkler systems and alarm systems).

Ensuring Exceptional Customer Service

• Displays leadership in guest hospitality, exemplifying excellent customer service and creating a positive atmosphere for guest relations.

• Reviews comment cards, guest satisfaction results and other data to identify areas of improvement.

• Shares plans with property leadership and ensuring corrective action is taken to continuously improve guest satisfaction.

• Strives to improve service performance.

Conducting Human Resources Activities

• Supervises staffing levels to ensure that guest service, operational needs and financial objectives are met.

• Helps train employees in safety procedures.

• Assists in training other department employees in fire protection, safety and evacuation procedures.

• Provides feedback to employees based on observation of service behaviors.

• Assists in performing operational activities as necessary.

HM Courts & Tribunals Service (HMCTS) is responsible for the administration of criminal, civil and family Courts and Tribunals in England and Wales. Our roles support our service users and colleagues within HMCTS, where people and businesses access potentially life-changing justice. We’re looking for individuals who are committed to public service and making a difference in people’s lives to deliver justice. You will be based in the Crown Court and provide support to the Jury. This is a predominantly customer facing role, which includes public speaking in a court setting. You will have regular contact with court users, including members of the Judiciary and the legal profession.

Alongside your public facing duties, you will be assigned to teams to carry out a variety of general administrative duties to progress cases through the court system or provide administrative support to other functions within HMCTS.

Working as part of a flexible team, you will be expected to undertake a range of the functions and responsibilities specified.

Job summary

The Home Office works to build a safe, fair and prosperous UK. We achieve this through our work on counter-terrorism, policing, crime, drugs policy, immigration and passports.

Home Office Digital, designs, builds and develops services for the rest of the department and for government. Every year our systems support up to 3 million visa applications, checks on 100 million border crossings, up to 8 million passport applications and deliver 140 million police checks on people, vehicles and property.

Job description

An Infrastructure Engineer supports and maintains infrastructure solutions and services as directed and according to departmental policy and Home Office strategy.

You will work in a team of Infrastructure Engineers ensuring services are delivered and supported as required. You will work with and support third parties to provide infrastructure services and with technical architects to translate architectural designs into operations.

Your main day to day responsibilities will be:

  • Building, configuring, transitioning, administering, and supporting enterprise toolsets used for monitoring the health and performance of the Home Office compute, storage, networking, physical and cloud infrastructure using commercial off the shelf (COTS) and open-source packages and solutions.
  • Implementing and supporting event management solutions, toolsets, and methods of event aggregation from multiple sources and integrations with the IT Operations Management Solution.
  • Proactively managing alerts & thresholds for monitored infrastructure and services, ensuring that technical solutions continue to meet business requirements.
  • Responding to and supporting the resolution of incidents, problem analysis, root cause identification and fix; monitor resolution activities and progress updates to users.
  • Using logical designs created by technical architects and required standards, methods & tools (including prototyping tools where appropriate) to build and implement enterprise tooling solutions.
  • Working in cooperation with testing to ensure the integrity & quality of enterprise toolsets and solutions.
  • Create, update, and maintain technical documentation, work instructions and guidance notes for supported toolsets.
  • Build and test simple interfaces between systems or work on more complex integration as part of a wider team.

Due to the business requirements of this role, it is only available on a full-time basis. However, compressed hours are available.

• Understanding of core technical concepts, techniques and methods related to enterprise tools and ability to implement and support tooling solutions and offerings.

• Implementing and supporting event management solutions, toolsets, and methods of event aggregation from multiple sources.

• The use of IT Operations Management (ITOM) suites such as ServiceNow for supporting Event, Incident, Problem and Change Management.

• Troubleshooting and resolving issues involving technologies across a variety of platforms.

• Awareness of emerging technologies and how they could be applicable to the current business.

• Effectively communicating at different levels, across support and engineering, business users, architecture, and suppliers.

• Working within an ITIL Framework.

The essential criteria listed above are reflective of the Home Office Government Digital and Data Profession Career Framework (based on the industry standard SFIA framework).

  • The allowance values are set by the Home Office, subject to remaining in a qualifying role. This allowance is non-contractual, non-pensionable, subject to an annual review and could be withdrawn at any time. Please see the Home Office Digital Recruitment and Retention Allowance Careers page for more information.

description:

  • Type of role: Other
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time

10 South Colonnade, Canary Wharf London, E14 4PU

About the job

Job summary

We are currently looking for a Regulation and Policy Lead, AI for Medicines Safety to join our Benefit Risk Evaluation I Function within the Safety & Surveillance Group.

This is a full-time opportunity, on a permanent basis. The role will be based in 10 South Colonnade, Canary Wharf London, E14 4PU.

Government departments and agencies are working towards implementing a minimum 60% attendance in office sites.

We are currently implementing a flexible, hybrid way of working, with a minimum of 8 days per month working on site to enable the collaboration and contact with partners and stakeholders needed to deliver MHRA business. Attendance on site is driven by business needs so depending on the nature of the role, this can flex up to 12 days a month, with the remainder of time worked either remotely or in the office. Some roles will need to be on site more regularly. Remote working is potentially available for some specific roles. Please discuss this with the recruiting manager before accepting an appointment.

The Safety and Surveillance (S&S) Group brings together into a single integrated structure expertise on the safety of all medical products with enforcement capabilities. These functions are supported by the Agency’s data and evidence generating capabilities, complementing our signal generating abilities.

Against this background and the drive to improve treatment availability for patients, safety remains at the heart of all our decision making across the product life cycle. The central mission of the Safety & Surveillance portfolio is to protect the public by appropriately identifying, assessing and managing the risks associated with medical products. In every aspect of this work, we harness the best science, technology, information and professional practice to protect patients in new and impactful ways.

The core purpose of Benefit Risk Evaluation is to deliver a robust assessment of potential safety signals using data from a range of sources along with technical, scientific, clinical and regulatory knowledge, and practical experience. The team conducts benefit-risk evaluations for medicines and medical device across a broad spectrum of therapeutic areas to guide actions that protect patient safety. The team is responsible for:

  • Signal detection of emerging safety issues
  • Evaluating the benefit risk of signals and developing effective and measurable risk mitigation measures
  • Using data and embracing new technologies to develop the evidence to support our actions and understand their impact

Job description

Role Purpose

This is an exciting opportunity to play a lead regulatory and policy role in the delivery of the MHRA's “Beyond ADMET: AI for Medicines Safety” regulatory sandbox. This unique regulatory science initiative will explore how artificial intelligence can improve the prediction of absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion and toxicity (ADMET) outcomes and integrate clinical and real-world data to support safer, faster and more efficient medicines development.

Working closely with the Head, AI for Medicines Safety and the Technical Lead, the postholder will provide specialist regulatory and policy expertise across the programme, ensuring that sandbox activities are aligned with current regulatory frameworks and helping to assess the implications of emerging AI-enabled approaches for medicines development and safety assessment.

The postholder will support the identification and interpretation of emerging regulatory, scientific and policy developments relating to artificial intelligence, computational methods and non-clinical medicines development. They will work collaboratively with colleagues across the MHRA, government, industry, academia and international regulatory networks to support evidence generation, regulatory learning and policy development arising from the programme.

Initially focused on supporting delivery of the “Beyond ADMET: AI for Medicines Safety” regulatory sandbox programme, the postholder will also contribute to the MHRA's broader ambitions in AI-enabled regulatory science and innovation, with opportunities to apply their expertise across other priority areas as organisational needs evolve.

The role offers a unique opportunity to contribute to the future development of AI-enabled medicines regulation while helping strengthen the MHRA's position as a global leader in regulatory innovation and patient safety.

Key responsibilities

Regulatory and Policy Leadership

  • Lead on all aspects of regulatory and policy advice on AI-enabled approaches in medicines development, safety assessment and related scientific areas.
  • Shape the MHRA's regulatory thinking on emerging AI methodologies and technologies, ensuring outputs from the sandbox inform future regulatory approaches and policy development. Drive horizon scanning and strategic assessment of UK and international regulatory, policy and scientific developments relevant to AI, toxicology, pharmacology, ADMET prediction and medicines development.
  • Lead the interpretation and application of current legislation, regulatory frameworks and guidance relevant to programme activities.

Programme Delivery

  • Work closely with the Head, AI for Medicines Safety, Technical Lead and Programme Manager to ensure effective integration of regulatory, scientific and operational considerations across the programme.
  • Provide regulatory and policy leadership on programme planning, delivery and evaluation activities.
  • Develop programme outputs including reports, recommendations, briefings, workshops and publications.

Stakeholder Engagement

  • Build effective relationships with stakeholders across the MHRA, government departments, academia, industry, healthcare organisations and international regulatory networks.
  • Represent the programme in regulatory and policy discussions with internal and external stakeholders, communicating regulatory and policy considerations clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.

Regulatory Science and Governance

  • Lead on the development of future regulatory frameworks, guidance and policy approaches where appropriate. Identify opportunities to strengthen MHRA capability and leadership in AI-enabled regulation.
  • Ensure regulatory activities are delivered in accordance with MHRA governance requirements, quality standards and best practice. Maintain accurate documentation and evidence to support programme outputs and recommendations.

General

  • While the immediate focus of this role is the successful delivery of the “Beyond ADMET: AI for Medicines Safety” regulatory sandbox, the postholder will be expected to contribute regulatory and policy expertise across the Agency's evolving AI and regulatory science agenda.
  • Champion the MHRA values and Civil Service behaviours, promoting an ethical, positive and inclusive working environment.

The duties and responsibilities outlined above are not intended to be exhaustive and may be reviewed or amended from time to time in consultation with the postholder to meet organisational needs.

Person specification

Essential Criteria:

  • Experience working in regulatory affairs, regulatory policy, regulatory science or a related discipline within healthcare, life sciences or a related sector - Lead
  • Experience interpreting and applying regulatory frameworks to new technologies, scientific approaches, products or services.
  • Experience advising on regulatory or policy issues and translating complex information into practical recommendations.
  • Experience contributing to regulatory guidance, policy development, standards development or regulatory science initiatives.
  • Experience engaging effectively with stakeholders across government, academia, industry, healthcare organisations or regulatory bodies.
  • Experience working collaboratively within multidisciplinary projects, programmes or teams.

Qualifications

Degree in a relevant scientific, healthcare, policy or regulatory discipline (or equivalent experience).

Behaviours

We'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:

  • Communicating and Influencing
  • Working Together
  • Making Effective Decisions

Technical skills

We'll assess you against these technical skills during the selection process:

  • Degree in a relevant scientific, healthcare, policy or regulatory discipline (or equivalent experience).
  • Understanding of medicines regulation, non-clinical assessment and emerging technologies.
  • Knowledge of regulatory policy development processes and regulatory science principles.
  • Ability to critically evaluate scientific evidence and assess regulatory implications.
  • Understanding of artificial intelligence and machine learning concepts and their application within healthcare and life sciences.
  • Awareness of UK and international regulatory approaches relating to AI-enabled technologies.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including preparation of briefings, reports and recommendations for senior audiences.

We only ask for evidence of these technical skills on your application form:

  • Understanding of medicines regulation, non-clinical assessment and emerging technologies.

  • Mobility: Mobility clause in contracts allowing staff to be mobile across the Civil Service
  • Civil Service Pension Scheme. Please see the link for further information For enquiries relating to the Civil Service Pension Schemes please contact MyCSP's Pension Service Centre directly on 0300 123 6666

title: Fire Alarm Technician
description:
JOB SUMMARY:

The purpose of the Fire Alarm Technician position is to install, troubleshoot, service and repair fire alarm systems, and other fire and life safety products with minimal supervision.

ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES:

  • Troubleshoot fire alarm systems to determine faults, including ground faults.
  • Repair or replace damaged fire alarm components such as FACP, power supplies, and alarm‑initiating devices.
  • Demonstrate knowledge of various manufacturers’ clean agent and high‑pressure suppression systems.
  • Properly use tools and test equipment (e.g., multimeter, megger, programming laptop, lifts) to repair or replace fire alarm and suppression components.
  • Maintain comprehensive working knowledge of fire alarm codes and standards.
  • Apply programming and software skills across multiple fire alarm platforms when removing or replacing components.
  • Safely follow procedures for handling, removing, and replacing explosive actuators such as squibs and gas cartridge actuators.
  • Communicate professionally with internal and external customers and offsite monitoring companies.
  • Arrive punctually to assigned work locations and complete scheduled projects in a timely manner.
  • Use Field Service Lightning to track work orders, materials, and time on the job.
  • Complete all required documentation on work orders.
  • Understand and follow SFP’s Safety Program, SDS Book, and Hazard Communication Program. Participate in weekly toolbox talks and maintain awareness of all safety documentation for each project.
  • Maintain company‑provided vehicle in clean and compliant condition.
  • Participate in on‑call rotation as required to support emergency service requests.
  • Attend periodic seminars and training sessions to stay current with technology, codes, and standards.
  • Train service technician trainees in applicable fire protection tasks.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS

The qualifications listed below are representative of the elements required to perform the job successfully, however in some cases, an equivalent combination of Education, Training, Certifications and Experience may meet the job qualifications.

Education, Training, Certifications:

  • High School Diploma or equivalent, required.
  • NICET or state specific certification, preferred.

Experience, Knowledge, Skill Requirements:

  • 2 years’ experience in Fire Life Safety Industry experience, specifically in Fire Alarm, required.
  • NICET Level 1 Fire Alarm Certification, strongly preferred

Communication Skills:

  • Must have the ability to effectively read, write and communicate in English with employees and customers.

Systems and Software Skills:

  • 2 years using business intelligence systems, Sage 300 CRE, or similar, preferred.
  • 2 years of professional computer skills, preferred

Other Qualifications:

  • Valid driver’s license with acceptable driving record required.
  • Must be able to comply with SFP’s Drug and Alcohol policy and Background screening requirements, which may also include customer specific requirements based on contractual agreement.
  • Occasional travel up to 20%.

PHYSICAL & WORK ENVIRONMENT REQUIREMENTS

Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform Essential Job Duties.

Physical Requirements:

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to bend, ascend and descend step stools, ladders and stairs, kneel, lift >50lbs, reach above and below shoulders, stand and walk for extended periods of time. Employee is required to see in color, close and far distances, peripheral, depth, and adjust focus. Employee will occasionally be required to balance, crouch, drive, kneel, lift >50lbs, sit, stoop, twist, and work at heights.

Work Environment:

Employees will regularly be required to work outside, and be exposed to hot/cold temperatures, dust, fumes, chemicals, electrical hazards and noise. Employee will occasionally be required to work indoors in an office setting, work alone and with others. Employee must consistently wear all appropriate personal protective equipment, as required by company safety policies while visiting locations.

We are fully committed to equal opportunities for employment to all individuals regardless of race, national origin, gender, religion, sexual orientation, disability, familial status, and any other classification protected under the law. We are an Equal Opportunity, Affirmative Action employer.

title: General Manager, Reconditioning - Fairburn
description:
At Carvana, we sell cars but we aren’t car salesmen. Our promise is simple: we won’t sell a car to a customer that we wouldn’t sell to our own Mom. Period. To make sure our car’s are in first-rate condition, we’ve built multiple vehicle Reconditioning Centers around the country, where our cars are inspected, perfected, and photographed before reaching the Carvana website. Using our Carvana Certified 150-point inspection process, we’re able to verify that every vehicle meets our rigorous mechanical and cosmetic standards.

We strive to provide only the highest quality vehicles to our customers in our mission to deliver a no-hassle, better car buying experience. We are actively looking for passionate and talented individuals who can help us deliver on that promise.

Think you’ve got what it takes to join our team? Keep reading below to see what we’re looking for!

About the team and position

The Inspection Center General Manager is responsible for the overall performance of the center. Providing leadership for up to 500 associates working multiple shifts in a lean manufacturing environment. Maintaining a culture of continuous improvement and high associate engagement while ensuring the facility meets quality, production, and cost objectives.

What you’ll be doing

Leadership 30%

  • Leads strategic planning to ensure the facility will have the capability to meet future demands.
  • Provides strategic vision and guidance to the location
  • Ensures management beliefs and behaviors are in line with the Carvana culture
  • Frequent visits to the shop floor to ensure connection with the realities of the business and model leadership behaviors throughout the organization
  • Positively challenge and engage the team to continuously improve quality production and cost performance
  • Live the Carvana values

Production Management 30%

  • Lead production planning for the Inspection Center
  • Ensure the Inspection Center has adequate capacity to meet production targets
  • Oversee weekly performance review meetings for each area and report out on the Inspection Centers performance
  • Identify problems impacting the Inspection Center’s performance. Prioritize problems, allocate resources, and ensure the resolution of issues
  • Ensure operating standards such as standardized work, operating rules, 5S, and visual management tools are consistently executed
  • Ensure compliance with all health and safety and loss prevention guidelines

People Management 30%

  • Participate in the selection and hiring process, ensure a pipeline of associates to fill current and future positions
  • Maintain a bench of candidates for each leadership position
  • Ensure progression path training and certification process is consistently executed
  • Model effective teamwork and ensure it’s embraced at all levels of the organization
  • Provide competency-based feedback and ensure leaders throughout the organization are also providing appropriate feedback
  • Mentor reconditioning managers

Continuous Improvement 10%

  • Lead the selection of continuous improve events, allocate resources to support events, and hold the team accountable for results
  • Participate in and lead continuous improvement efforts
  • Train and mentor reconditioning managers on problem-solving
  • Other duties as assigned.

What you should have

  • Minimum of 8 years of management experience either in automotive or a lean manufacturing environment leading multiple work groups
  • A valid driver’s license
  • Valid unrestricted driver’s license with a clean driving record in the last 3 years
  • Knowledge of lean manufacturing principles
  • Proven track record of leading and developing associates
  • Proven ability to obtain project deliverables and company metrics
  • Ability to work a flexible work schedule
  • An ability to work in a fast-paced, ever-changing production environment while sometimes being exposed to excessive weather conditions (heat/cold)
  • Excellent communications skills, oral and written
  • Ability to work with and through teams to achieve results
  • Strong analysis and decision making ability
  • Proficient computer skills

What we’ll offer in return

  • Full-Time Position with a competitive salary
  • Medical, Dental, and Vision benefits
  • 401K with company match
  • A multitude of perks including student loan payments, discounts on vehicles, benefits for your pets, and much more
  • A great wellness program to keep you healthy and happy, both physically and mentally
  • Access to opportunities to expand your skillset and share your knowledge with others across the organization
  • A company culture of promotions from within, with a start-up atmosphere allowing for varied and rapid career development
  • A seat in one of the fastest-growing companies in the country

Other requirements

To be able to do your job at Carvana, there are some basic requirements we want to share with you.

  • Must be able to read, write, speak and understand English
  • Must be at least 18 years of age
  • Must have a valid driver's license
  • A clean driving record with no more than two moving violations or DUI’s in the last three years
  • The physical environment requires the employee to work both inside and outside in heat/cold, wet/humid, and dry/arid conditions
  • Will be required to use personal protective equipment to prevent exposure to hazardous materials
  • May be requested to work overtime and weekends for special programs and events.
  • Frequent standing and sitting with varying periods of each
  • May at times require working different shifts
  • Lift up to 40 pounds frequently
  • Walk up to three miles each day

Of course, we’ll make any reasonable accommodations for those with disabilities to perform the essential functions of their jobs.

Legal stuff

Hiring is contingent on passing a complete background check. This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

Carvana is an equal employment opportunity employer. All applicants receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, national origin, age, mental or physical disability, protected veteran status, or genetic information, or any other basis protected by applicable law. Carvana also prohibits harassment of applicants or employees based on any of these protected categories.
