title: Group Housing Coordinator
description:
POSITION SUMMARY

Assign room according to guest request and preferences whenever possible. Pre-register designated guests and prepare key packets. Organize and coordinate check-in/pre-registration procedures for arriving groups. Review/Track/Accommodate requests for room/check-out changes when possible; communicate status to appropriate staff. Confirm reservations and cancellations. Review out-of-order rooms daily. Ensure rates match market codes and document exceptions. Verify and adjust billing for guests. File guest paperwork or documentation. Set up/process all guest check-ins/check-outs. Activate room keys. Secure valid payment. Identify any over-commitments. Perform duplicate reservation checks; block rooms. Run daily reports. Follow up with guests to ensure their requests or problems have been met to their satisfaction. Receive, record, and relay messages accurately, completely, and legibly.

Follow all company policies and procedures; ensure uniform and personal appearance are clean and professional; maintain confidentiality of proprietary information; protect company assets. Welcome and acknowledge all guests according to company standards; anticipate and address guests’ service needs; assist individuals with disabilities; thank guests with genuine appreciation. Speak with others using clear and professional language; prepare and review written documents accurately and completely; answer telephones using appropriate etiquette. Coordinate tasks and work with other departments. Serve as a departmental role model. Develop and maintain positive working relationships with others; support team to reach common goals. Comply with quality assurance standards. Stand, sit, or walk for an extended period of time. Enter and locate information using computers and/or POS systems. Move, lift, carry, push, pull, and place objects weighing less than or equal to 10 pounds without assistance. Perform other reasonable job duties as requested by Supervisors.

On the Government Operational Research Service (GORS) Fast Stream, you’ll use scientific and mathematical techniques to find better solutions to government policy making and resolve complex management problems. This is a fast track leadership programme for the Operational Research profession.

The specific towns and cities depend on the department you are posted to and its office locations. The Fast Stream evolves continually, so postings can vary from year to year.

As an indication, in 2026 new fast streamers were posted to government offices in the following regions: Greater London, North East, North West, Scotland, West Midlands, and Yorkshire and the Humber.

On occasion, some individuals may need to move location. We aim to align postings with your preferences whenever possible; however, final decisions must support our wider business needs. Please note that Fast Streamers cannot choose their department or their specific role.

Job description

Operational Research is the discipline of applying advanced analytical methods to help make better policy decisions.

You’ll do this using techniques ranging from quick calculations to complicated systems dynamics models, forecasting, simulation and analytics.

Different techniques can be used to objectively assess the current situation and how different changes might affect it. The work at the Operational Research Fast Stream brings government policy to life and has an impact on everyone in the UK.


We aim to put all successful candidates through Security Clearance (SC). However, if you are ineligible for SC, please do not be deterred from applying; we have plenty of exciting roles available that only require standard Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) pre-employment checks. You can find more information about vetting clearance levels here: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/united-kingdom-security-vetting-clearance-levels

Person specification

You must be eligible to work in the UK
You need to have or be on track to receive, a 2:1 or higher, degree apprenticeship in a highly numerate degree subject
or 2:2 with a highly numerate postgraduate degree (subjects like maths, statistics and physics; for mixed degrees, at least 50% should be in a highly numerate subject)

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £31,554, Fast Stream and Emerging Talent contributes £9,141 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).
You’ll have a unique chance to work on issues that really matter, and to gain experience internally and externally. It’s the best foundation for promotion and long term career progression.

Other benefits include the Civil Service Pension Scheme, professional qualifications, flexible working, season ticket loans, sports and social activities, childcare assistance and more.

Things you need to know

Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Selection process details

Application Process

There are several phases in the Fast Stream application process. Some of these assessments are multimedia in that they present information in video, audio, graphical or visual formats, as well as text. We hope you find it an engaging process and one that gives you a real insight into the role of a fast streamer.

At the initial application stage you will be asked to complete some background information which will include some diversity questions - which are for monitoring purposes only and will have no bearing on selection outcomes - along with the opportunity to identify your preferences in terms of the different Fast Stream schemes. You can choose up to three.

When you apply please register with a personal email address, and not a work or university email address.

Assessment Phases

There are 2 online tests:

Work-based scenarios - This test measures interpersonal skills, utilising video based scenarios and you are required to assess the effectiveness of various responses.

Case Study assessment - In this test you are required to take work based scenarios on an imaginary role, learning and responding to a series of challenges and situations and adapting to the changes you are presented with.

Additional information - depending on the schemes you have chosen, there may be additional information to be completed, or an intermediate sift process. More information on the schemes that require additional information can be found https://www.civil-service-careers.gov.uk/fast-stream/fs-how-to-apply/fs-additional-information/

Fast Stream Assessment Centre - if you pass the above stages you'll be invited to attend a half day assessment centre. This will be conducted virtually online. The Fast Stream Assessment Centre (FSAC) reflects some of the key elements of a Fast Stream role and will consist of a written exercise, oral briefing exercise and a personal development conversation. Information will be presented via an app that you will be able to access remotely.

Final Selection Board - most schemes will then require a Final Selection Board . We'll ask you to attend this final assessment if you reach the required standard at FSAC. More information on the Final Selection Boards can be found https://www.civil-service-careers.gov.uk/fast-stream/fs-how-to-apply/fs-final-selection-board/

The Civil Service Fast Stream is committed to supporting you through the application process by offering a range of reasonable adjustments. For further information about reasonable adjustments through the Fast Stream application process, please visit our dedicated page - https://www.civil-service-careers.gov.uk/fast-stream/fs-how-to-apply/fs-reasonable-adjustments/

If you need to contact us, please submit a request for help https://fsetatso.freshdesk.com/support/home



Feedback will only be provided if you attend an interview or assessment.

Security

Successful candidates must undergo a basic (or equivalent) criminal record check.
People working with government assets must complete baseline personnel security standard (opens in new window) checks.

Nationality requirements

This job is broadly open to the following groups:

  • UK nationals

  • nationals of the EU, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein and family members of those nationalities with settled or pre-settled status under the European Union Settlement Scheme (EUSS) (opens in a new window)

  • Turkish nationals, and certain family members of Turkish nationals, who have accrued the right to work in the Civil Service
Further information on nationality requirements (opens in a new window)

Working for the Civil Service

The Civil Service Code (opens in a new window) sets out the standards of behaviour expected of civil servants.

We recruit by merit on the basis of fair and open competition, as outlined in the Civil Service Commission's recruitment principles (opens in a new window).
The Civil Service embraces diversity and promotes equal opportunities. As such, we run a Disability Confident Scheme (DCS) for candidates with disabilities who meet the minimum selection criteria.
The Civil Service also offers a Redeployment Interview Scheme to civil servants who are at risk of redundancy, and who meet the minimum requirements for the advertised vacancy.

Diversity and Inclusion

The Civil Service is committed to attract, retain and invest in talent wherever it is found. To learn more please see the Civil Service People Plan (opens in a new window) and the Civil Service Diversity and Inclusion Strategy (opens in a new window).

title: Engineering Coordinator
description:
POSITION SUMMARY

Engineering Coordinator

Coordinate purchasing, receiving, storage, inventory control, and distribution of hotel engineering materials, spare parts, tools, equipment, and supplies. Process approved purchase requests, obtain quotations, prepare and track purchase orders, follow up with vendors, and support timely delivery. Receive and inspect goods against purchase orders, invoices, and packing slips for quantity, specification, condition, and price. Maintain secure, clean, labeled, and organized storerooms; issue materials against approved requisitions; monitor minimum and maximum stock levels; conduct inventory counts; and maintain accurate purchasing, receiving, warranty, and stock records. Coordinate with Engineering, Purchasing, Receiving, Finance, and hotel departments to resolve discrepancies, returns, credits, urgent requirements, and delivery delays.

The Engineering Coordinator is responsible for driving the reduction of utility consumption throughout the hotel by implementing policies and ensuring adherence to The Ritz-Carlton standards. This role monitors energy usage, performs trend analysis, and supports the development of strategic energy plans in collaboration with the Director of Engineering and third-party consultants.

The Engineering Coordinator coordinates and monitors external vendors to resolve large-scale engineering issues (e.g., HVAC, internet, and telephone systems). The role also involves receiving, distributing, and tracking maintenance of work orders, maintaining accurate records and files, and ensuring easy access to purchasing information and order status. Familiarity with engineering terminology is essential to effectively process orders and request services.

The Ideal Candidate Will Have:
• High school diploma/G.E.D. equivalent; diploma or certificate in Purchasing, Supply Chain, Inventory Control, Business Administration, or Industrial Engineering is preferred.
• At least 2 years of related purchasing, receiving, inventory, or storekeeping experience; hotel engineering experience is strongly preferred.
• Ability to complete Energy Technician certification classes
• Knowledge of energy conservation and previous experience in a similar role

• Experience with computer-based software systems, including but not limited to Excel, Windows, PowerPoint, and facsimile machines
• Ability to operate standard office equipment
• Strong organizational skills with the ability to maintain high standards of cleanliness and safety
• Ability to work under pressure and meet deadlines
• Strong communication skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and effectively with hotel guests, suppliers, and employees
• Experience with procurement systems such as Hotshop, BirchStreet, invoicing processes, and logistics/warehouse coordination
• Availability to work flexible shifts, including weekends and holidays, as required

Coordinate with other departments using telecommunications devices in order to respond to requests and resolve maintenance issues and to put rooms needing maintenance out of order. Coordinate and schedule with other departments in the event of major system shut down or major repair or improvement. Maintain purchase orders log and file purchase orders upon payment, ensuring that orders match packing slips.

Follow all company and safety and security policies and procedures; report maintenance problems, safety hazards, accidents, or injuries; complete safety training and certifications; and properly store flammable materials. Ensure uniform and personal appearance are clean and professional, maintain confidentiality of proprietary information, and protect company assets. Welcome and acknowledge all guests according to company standards, anticipate and address guests’ service needs, assist individuals with disabilities, and thank guests with genuine appreciation. Speak with others using clear and professional language; prepare and review written documents accurately and completely; answer telephones using appropriate etiquette. Develop and maintain positive working relationships with others; listen and respond appropriately to the concerns of other employees. Ensure adherence to quality expectations and standards. Visually inspect tools, equipment, or machines. Move, lift, carry, push, pull, and place objects weighing less than or equal to 35 pounds without assistance. Read and visually verify information in a variety of formats (e.g., small print). Enter and locate work-related information using computers and/or point of sale systems. Perform other reasonable job duties as requested by Supervisors.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

Education: High school diploma or G.E.D. equivalent.

Related Work Experience: At least 2 years of related work experience.

Supervisory Experience: No supervisory experience.

License or Certification: None

Our greatest strength lies in the rich blend of culture, talent, and experiences of our associates. We are committed to non-discrimination on any protected basis, including disability, veteran status, or other basis protected by applicable law.

title: Senior Medical Entomologist
description:
• Job grade: Senior Executive Officer
  • Contract type: Fixed term, Loan, Secondment
  • Length of employment: Fixed Term Appointment/Loan/Secondment until 27/10/2028
  • Type of role: Science, Other
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time, Job share, Part-time
  • Number of jobs available: 1

Location

Scientific Campus, Porton, Salisbury

About the job

Job summary

The Medical Entomology & Zoonoses Ecology (MEZE) group assess, prepare, and respond to current and emerging vector-borne disease threats in the UK. The team provide entomological expertise on vector issues through research and surveillance activities, primarily on ticks and mosquitoes. The team also work internationally on vectors and vector-borne diseases to deliver European funded projects and to support the development and delivery of surveillance systems in the UK Overseas Territories. Research and surveillance activities are translated into expert advice for UKHSA, the Department of Health and related sister agencies and departments, contributing to policy, contingency planning, and public health preparedness on vector-borne diseases. We are seeking an additional team member with experience in medical entomology to support the delivery of our expanding research and surveillance portfolio on vectors and vector-borne diseases.

Working as part of a multidisciplinary team and with external and internal collaborators within and outside UKHSA, the post holder will provide medical entomological and vector-borne disease expertise (particularly on tick-borne diseases) within a team responsible for the delivery of the scientific and technical activities of the Medical Entomology & Zoonoses Ecology group. This will include the development, design and delivery of specific projects and resources such as UKHSA’s National vector surveillance programmes of ticks and mosquitoes.

We are keen to hear from candidates with experience in entomology, as well as candidates with experience in innovation, prototyping and the application of emerging technologies to address real-world challenges.

Job description

The postholder will contribute specialist scientific expertise to the delivery of research, surveillance and health protection activities relating to vector-borne diseases of public health importance. Working within the Medical Entomology and Zoonoses Ecology team, they will support UKHSA's understanding of current and emerging vector-borne disease threats through the generation, analysis and interpretation of scientific evidence.

The postholder will:

  • Critically analyse and interpret complex scientific data from research studies, surveillance systems, incident investigations and funded projects, identifying trends, assessing risks and drawing evidence-based conclusions to inform public health decision-making.
  • Lead and deliver research and surveillance projects relating to vectors and vector-borne diseases, ensuring activities are completed to agreed quality standards and timescales.
  • Design and undertake field, laboratory and desk-based investigations using appropriate scientific, epidemiological and entomological methodologies.
  • Develop and support surveillance activities for vectors of public health importance, including mosquitoes, ticks and other arthropods relevant to human disease transmission.
  • Plan and undertake fieldwork, including vector collection, species identification, habitat assessment and environmental investigations.
  • Analyse surveillance and research data using appropriate analytical and statistical approaches.

Scientific Leadership and Research

  • Review and interpret scientific literature, surveillance data and intelligence on emerging vector-borne diseases, assessing implications for UK public health.
  • Maintain expertise in medical entomology, vector ecology and disease epidemiology to support programme development and innovation.
  • Produce technical reports, publications, presentations, funding applications and briefings for a range of audiences.
  • Contribute to research opportunities, partnerships and externally funded projects that strengthen UKHSA evidence and surveillance capabilities.
  • Ensure compliance with governance, quality and health and safety requirements.
  • Contribute to team and divisional objectives.

Project Delivery and Team Leadership

  • Plan, manage and monitor research and surveillance projects, balancing priorities and delivering outputs to agreed timescales.
  • Coordinate colleagues and external partners, maintain project records and support reporting, resource management and budgets.
  • Supervise, mentor and develop staff, students and visiting researchers.
  • Support recruitment, induction and workforce development activities.
  • Promote collaborative working and knowledge sharing.
  • Deputise for senior colleagues and represent the team at relevant meetings and forums.

Stakeholder Engagement and Communication

  • Build effective relationships with UKHSA colleagues, government, academia and partner organisations.
  • Provide specialist advice on vector surveillance, ecology and disease risks.
  • Prepare and present evidence, briefings and reports for scientific, operational and policy audiences.
  • Contribute to publications, government-facing products and communications that translate complex evidence for non-specialist audiences.

Health Protection

  • Support the assessment and management of vector-borne disease threats.
  • Contribute scientific expertise to risk assessments, surveillance investigations, incidents and public health responses.
  • Support horizon scanning, evaluation of control measures and development of evidence-based guidance.
  • Deliver training and technical guidance on vector-borne diseases.

Professional Development

  • Maintain professional knowledge through continuing development, appraisal, mandatory training and compliance with UKHSA policies and standards

This list is not exhaustive.

Person specification

Essential Criteria

  • PhD in medical entomology or MSc and postgraduate experience or degree with substantial relevant experience and significant experience in medical entomology including identification of arthropods, field and laboratory-based techniques, public health communication, risk assessment and statistical analyses
  • Experience of contributing to large scale vector surveillance programmes with experience of developing and co-ordinating complex field-based research projects in potentially challenging environments with potentially changing priorities/tight deadlines
  • Demonstration of an active research profile through peer review publication record and knowledge of the key public health issues surrounding vector-borne diseases and experience of drafting briefing papers, presentations, and correspondence for internal and external stakeholders for project meetings and/or training purposes and evidence of continuing professional development with high degree of self-motivation .
  • Ability to prepare and produce evidence based scientific material for dissemination to a broad range of stakeholders, including non-specialists, as required with ability to identify scientific issues drawn from multiple sources, undertake comprehensive literature reviews, assess materials with conflicting states and interpret detailed documents that may include legislation
  • Demonstrated capability to act upon incomplete information, using experience to make inferences and decisions

Desirable Criteria

  • Experience of staff recruitment, selection and supervision
  • Experience of contributing to successful research proposals

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £41,983, UK Health Security Agency contributes £12,162 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).
  • Learning and development tailored to your role
  • An environment with flexible working options
  • A culture encouraging inclusion and diversity
  • A Civil Service pension with an employer contribution of 28.97%

We pride ourselves as being an employer of choice, where Everyone Matters promoting equality of opportunity to actively encourage applications from everyone, including groups currently underrepresented in our workforce.

UKHSA ethos is to be an inclusive organisation for all our staff and stakeholders. To create, nurture and sustain an inclusive culture, where differences drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our workforce and wider communities. We do this through celebrating and protecting differences by removing barriers and promoting equity and equality of opportunity for all.

Things you need to know

Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Selection process details

This vacancy will be assessed using a competency-based framework which will assess your qualifications, knowledge and experience and / or skills and abilities outlined in the essential criteria.

Stage 1: Application & Sift

Competency Based

You will be required to complete an application form. You will be assessed on the listed 5 essential criteria, and this will be in the form of a:

  • Application form (Employer/ Activity history’ section on the application)
  • 1500 word supporting statement.

This should outline how you consider your skills, experience and knowledge provide evidence of your suitability for the role, with reference to the essential criteria.

You will receive a joint score for your application form and statement. (The application form is the kind of information you would put into your C.V –please be advised you will not be able to upload your CV. Please complete the application form in as much detail as possible). Please do not email us your CV.

Healthjobs UK has a word limit of 1500.

Longlisting:

In the event of a large number of applications, we will longlist into 3 piles of:

  • Meets all essential criteria
  • Meets some essential criteria
  • Meets no essential criteria

If used, the pile(s) that meets ALL essential criteria’ will proceed to shortlisting.

Shortlisting:
In the event of a large number of applications we will conduct an initial sift, on the lead criteria of:

  • PhD in medical entomology or MSc and postgraduate experience or degree with substantial relevant experience and significant experience in medical entomology including identification of arthropods, field and laboratory-based techniques, public health communication, risk assessment and statistical analyses
  • Experience of contributing to large scale vector surveillance programmes with experience of developing and co-ordinating complex field-based research projects in potentially challenging environments with potentially changing priorities/tight deadlines
  • Demonstration of an active research profile through peer review publication record and knowledge of the key public health issues surrounding vector-borne diseases and experience of drafting briefing papers, presentations, and correspondence for internal and external stakeholders for project meetings and/or training purposes and evidence of continuing professional development with high degree of self-motivation.

Desirable criteria may be used in the event of a large number of applications/large amount of successful candidates.

If you are successful at this stage, you will progress to interview & assessment.

Feedback will not be provided at this stage.

Stage 2: Interview

Competency Based

You will be invited to a single face to face interview at our Scientific Campus, Porton.

When face to face interviews are planned, in exceptional circumstances, we may be able to offer a remote interview.

Knowledge, experience, skills & abilities will be tested at interview in the form of questions.

There will be a Presentation.

  • Please prepare a 10-minute presentation on the following topic: Identify one current challenge relating to vector-borne diseases (VBDs) in the UK and explain how you would approach addressing it.

Interview dates are yet to be confirmed.

Eligibility Criteria

External - This vacancy is open to all external applicants (anyone) from outside the Civil Service as well as internal applicants.

Location

This role is being offered as hybrid working based at our Scientific Campus in Porton.

We offer great flexible working opportunities at UKHSA and operate using a hybrid working model where business needs allow. This provides us with greater flexibility about how and where we work, to get the best from our workforce. As a hybrid worker, you will be expected to spend a minimum of 60% of your contractual working hours (approximately 3 days a week pro rata, averaged over a month) working at our campus.

Security Clearance Level Requirement Please

Successful candidates must pass a basic disclosure and barring security check before they can be appointed.

Successful candidates must meet the security requirements before they can be appointed. The level of security needed is Counter-Terrorist Check.

When based at our scientific campus, you will be required to have a minimum of a Counter Terrorism Check security vetting check as a minimum. For meaningful National Security Vetting checks to be carried out individuals need to have lived in the UK for a sufficient period of time. You should normally have been resident in the United Kingdom for the last 3 years as the role requires Counter Terrorism Check (CTC) clearance. In exceptional circumstances UK residency less than the outlined periods may not necessarily bar you from gaining national security vetting and applicants should contact the Vacancy Holder/Recruiting Manager listed in the advert for further advice.

Salary Information

If you are successful at interview, and are moving from another government department, NHS, or Local Authority, the relevant starting salary principles for level transfers or promotions will apply. Otherwise, roles are offered at the pay scale minimum for the grade, but in exceptional circumstances there may be flexibility if you are able to demonstrate you are already in receipt of an existing, higher salary. Pay increases are through the relevant annual pay award for the role and terms. Please be aware that the salary is based on the office location.

If this role is fixed term and you are not currently a Civil Servant, you will take up the post on a Fixed Term appointment; you may be able to take this role up as a Secondment. If you are an existing Civil Servant, based outside of UKHSA, you will take up the post as a loan which you will need your department to agree. Loans are normally agreed for a period of two years. However, this may be extended where required, subject to agreement between UKHSA and your home department. You cannot take the post up as a fixed term. If you are an existing UKHSA member of staff, you will take up the post as either a level transfer or a temporary promotion as per the UKHSA’s Pay policy. If this role is permanent, it may also be available as a loan (for existing Civil Servants only) or secondment arrangement, subject to business need and agreement from the hiring manager and, where applicable, the employee's home organisation.

Reserve List

If more than the required number of suitable candidates pass the interview criteria, you may be kept on a reserve list for 12 months subject to your agreement. You may be contacted, in merit-order, if similar roles with closely matching essential criteria become available and the department choose to appoint from a reserve list. The panel will assess if candidates meet the requirement of the role first, using a specific benchmark system. If you are interviewed for the post and do not meet the required threshold for the specified grade, your application may be assessed against a similar, lower grade role and you may be offered the post should one be available.

Incident Response Activity

From time to time, the role holder may be required to support UKHSA’s incident response activity by contributing their appropriate expertise within an Incident Cell; during such periods, supported by the line manager, this work will take priority over normal day-to-day responsibilities, commensurate with their grade, skills and experience.

Qualifications and Registrations

For roles where specific qualifications or registrations are required, successful applicants will be asked to provide appropriate evidence. Employment cannot
commence until satisfactory documentation has been received and verified.

Future location

UKHSA is investing in a new state-of-the-art National Biosecurity Centre in Harlow, Essex, which will eventually bring together teams currently based at Canary Wharf, Colindale and Porton Down. For more details, please see: Huge biosecurity centre investment to boost pandemic protection - GOV.UK. The new facilities will start becoming operational in the mid-2030s, with full completion by 2038. Staff will move in phases as facilities become available. If you're appointed to a role currently based at Canary Wharf, Colindale or Porton Down, please note that we'll continue investing in these sites for the next decade. As we get closer to the transition, we'll provide full information about relocation support available to staff.

Reasonable Adjustments

The Civil Service is committed to making sure that our selection methods are fair to everyone. To help you during the recruitment process, we will consider any
reasonable adjustments that could help you. An adjustment is a change to the recruitment process or an adjustment at work. This is separate to the Disability Confident Scheme. If you need an adjustment to be made at any point during the recruitment process you should contact the recruitment team in confidence as soon as possible to discuss your needs. You can find out more information about reasonable adjustments across the Civil Service here: https://www.civil-service-careers.gov.uk/reasonable-adjustments/

International Police check

Internal Fraud Check

If successful for this role as one aspect of pre-employment screening, applicant’s personal details – name, national insurance number and date of birth - will be checked against the Cabinet Office Internal Fraud Hub, and anyone included on the database will be refused employment unless they can show exceptional circumstances. Currently this is only for external candidates to the Civil Service.

Security

See our vetting charter (opens in a new window).

Location

About the job

Job summary

From healthcare to artificial intelligence, energy to national security, we provide legal advice to government departments on nation-changing subjects.

At Government Legal Department we have a vital, single-minded purpose: to help the Government govern well within the rule of law. This is complemented by our exciting vision to be an outstanding legal organisation, committed to the highest standards of service and professionalism and a brilliant place to work where we can all thrive and fulfill our potential.

Our work touches almost every aspect of public life. We are the largest provider of legal services across government, working on high profile matters.

Our respected professionals are involved in everything from regulation and litigation to advice on drafting legislation. They provide expertise to the full range of government departments. We are at the heart of delivering the government’s priorities and our success depends on our people.

GLD is a non-ministerial government department headed by the Treasury Solicitor, our Permanent Secretary, and employs nearly 4000 people, including nearly 3000 legal professionals. We have offices nationwide, in Bristol, Leeds, inner and outer London and Manchester. Our lawyers can also be located within other departments and overseas.

GLD also depends on a range of cross-functional professionals to provide our corporate services. There are nearly 1000 colleagues playing an essential part in helping GLD to achieve its purpose and truly deliver much more than law.

This is an exciting time to join GLD, with cutting edge legal work on global issues and a transformation agenda which is ensuring the Department exemplifies the Modern Civil Service.

To find out more about what we do you can view our introductory film. On our website you can hear from team members, find out how to apply and learn about the benefits of working for GLD. You can also read more about the future vision for GLD in our GLD Strategy 2024 – 2027.

Job description

About MODLA and BISTLA

Ministry of Defence Legal Advisers (MODLA)

The Ministry of Defence Legal Advisers (MODLA) has a Business Management team and four legal teams providing advice to the Ministry of Defence on a wide range of issues. The Ministry of Defence is a large and influential Ministerial Department with global reach. The Department works to protect the people of the UK, its territories, values and interests at home and overseas, through strong armed forces, to ensure the UK’s security and prosperity and support its national interests.

The teams in MODLA advise across the full range of MOD business and interests. This includes advice on service justice, the service police, matters that relate to membership of the Armed Forces, operational engagement, the development of the international legal framework to meet new challenges and artificial intelligence.

MODLA is a place where:

  • Our people are confident, professional and resilient.
  • Our team is kind, welcoming and inclusive.
  • Everyone can feel empowered and enthusiastic about their work and their career development.

The MODLA directorate is made up of around 40 lawyers and business support staff headed by Jennifer Morrish.

Business, Innovation Science and Trade Legal Advisers (BISTLA)

We provide legal support to the Department for Business Innovation Science and Trade (BIST) across the full range of its work, helping deliver the UK’s trade, investment, business, economic security, and growth objectives. BIST Legal is part of the Government Legal Department (GLD) and brings together specialist legal teams covering international trade, trade defence, investment disputes, competition and consumer policy, products and regulation, employment rights, corporate and insolvency, subsidy control, intellectual property, national security and investment, and science and space matters.

As a Directorate we:

  • Provide expert, practical and solution-focused legal advice.
  • Advise on international trade agreements and wider international economic policy and participate in trade negotiations.
  • Advise on competition, consumer, employment, corporate, insolvency, product regulation and intellectual property matters.
  • Advise on investment, national security, subsidy control, industrial strategy and wider business policy issues.
  • Handle trade and investment disputes, judicial reviews and other litigation for BIST.
  • Advise on and support the development of policy, legislation and regulatory frameworks.
  • Supports staff in meetings with ministers, stakeholders and other government departments.
  • Instruct external counsel through specialist legal services frameworks.
  • Runs GLD’s Centre of Excellence to support lawyers across government in relation to trade law issue.

GLD’s Business Management (BM) teams provide an expert service to support legal teams in the delivery of their work, using professional knowledge of the client department and the working context to ensure the team runs smoothly.

Each BM team is lead by a Head of Business Management, Christopher Dyas for MODLA and Hayley Devine for BISTLA, delivering strategic support to Directors. Acting as relationship managers with clients and GLD they have oversight of all services provided. Business managers support the Head by overseeing the operational, day-to-day running of the team.

The Role

This is an exciting opportunity to undertake a fast-paced, varied and challenging role. The Business Manager (HEO) role sits within the Business Management team offering a range of interesting work where ‘no one day is the same’. It would particularly suit someone looking to embed and enhance their leadership/people management and organisational change skills while working closely with their Head of Business Management, Director, Deputy Directors and legal colleagues.

We are looking for self-motivated people with the following key attributes:

  • Drive and energy - capable of driving delivery, initiating, and developing new ideas and processes and taking people along with them.
  • Decision-making – not afraid to make the right decisions and use evidence to come to conclusions.
  • Resilience and practical disposition – display a positive and can-do attitude.
  • Flex – able to respond and adapt to changing circumstances and manage a diverse workload with the ability to multi-task and prioritise when faced with competing deadlines.
  • Ownership - operate with a high degree of personal autonomy.
  • Committed to promote diversity, inclusion and equality of opportunity, respecting difference and external experience.

The successful candidates will lead the day-to-day services of their team, line manage staff and be provided with interesting and challenging work, along with developmental opportunities.

Individuals are expected to participate in wider corporate activities. This provides an opportunity to work with colleagues in the broader Business Management function and across GLD to deliver corporate tasks and activities.

About the job

Job summary

The Government Property Agency is the largest property holder in government, with more than £2.1 billion in property assets and over 55% of the government’s office estate.

We are transforming the way the Civil Service works by creating great places to work, leading the largest commercial office programme in the UK, working towards halving carbon emissions from government offices, and achieving greater value for taxpayers. And we are looking for innovative, solutions-focused people to join our team.

Representing the best covenant in the UK – His Majesty’s Government – we are leading significant transformational programmes such as the Government Hubs Programme, Whitehall Campus Programme and Net Zero Programme. We are also delivering cost- effective property services such as asset management, lifecycle replacement and workplace services.

Innovation and progress underpin our behaviours. We foster a culture of lifelong learning, where curiosity and self-improvement are encouraged. Our four core values are at the heart of everything we do. They shape our culture and guide how we work, lead and grow together:

  • Striving for excellence - We always aim to deliver great results
  • Empowering through respect - We insist on fair treatment for all, always
  • Acting with integrity - We consistently do the right thing
  • Succeeding together - We rely on each other to achieve success

The GPA is committed to representing the communities we serve by making Diversity, Equality and Inclusion part of everything we do.

To ensure that we are always recruiting and retaining a diverse mix of talent, we are particularly inviting applications from candidates who are disabled, ethnically or gender diverse, and people who identify as being part of the LGBTQ+ community.

Join our dynamic and diverse team that leads with purpose, improving sustainability, nurturing social value, driving inclusivity and flexibility, and kickstarting economic growth. We are driven by purpose, and you can be part of it too: where you make a meaningful impact; where you influence; where your voice really matters; where you help to shape our future direction.

Job description

This is a new role for an established, experienced Change Manager to join the newly established Business Integration team, situated in the Workplace Portfolio Management team of the Government Property Agency’s (GPA) Workplace Services (WS) Directorate. As a founding member of the team, you will help shape the processes and systems of change utilised to deliver cross directorate change. Offering a genuine opportunity to build our operational change capability from the ground up, this role will be instrumental in shaping our change frameworks, impact assessment tools, delivery methods, and reporting rhythms.

Reporting to the Head of Business Integration, you will lead the people, process and cultural change across the WS directorate. As one of the largest directorates in the GPA, WS is regionally distributed and operates across five distinct functional areas, each led by a Deputy Director. You will play a central role in delivering major transformation initiatives (including digital workplace platforms, estate moves, service delivery models, and operational assurance frameworks) to ensure initiatives and changes land safely without disrupting daily building operations.

In doing so, you will build change capability, embed sustainable new ways of working, and ensure both frontline operational teams and our commercial supply chain partners are supported to absorb change seamlessly. As part of establishing this new capability, you will also recruit, onboard, and line-manage an SEO Change Support Lead to build out your core team.

Key Responsibilities

As Change and Integration Manager you will lead and coordinate change management activity across Workplace Services’ key strategic programmes and initiatives. You will work collaboratively across teams and with senior stakeholders to ensure that people, process and organisational change is effectively planned, communicated and embedded. More specifically you will:

  • Design Change Frameworks & Systems: Establish standard processes, impact assessment templates, and digital tracking tools inside our Customer Service Portal and IWMS systems to map, sequence, and manage incoming cross-directorate change.
  • Lead Strategic Change Programmes & Project Gabriel: Develop and execute structured change management strategies for key strategic initiatives, most notably Project Gabriel (a three-year strategic initiative to redefine Facilities Management across the GPA estate by establishing innovative, resilient, and data-driven service models), IWMS rollouts, and delivery and assurance workstreams.
  • Flex to Emerging SLT Priorities & New Initiatives: Provide agile change leadership for new, emerging transformation initiatives as they arise, adapting delivery focus and change management frameworks to align with the shifting strategic priorities of the Workplace Services SLT and wider GPA.
  • Assess Change Readiness & Gate Control: Measure change saturation and operational capacity across teams and FM suppliers, conducting readiness assessments to provide evidence-based recommendations for formal "Go / No-Go" stage-gate decisions.
  • Drive Training & Capability Building: Conduct Directorate-wide Training Needs Analyses (TNA) and support the design of targeted learning interventions to build staff and contractor capability for new ways of working.
  • Drive Digital & Data Adoption: Lead behavioural and cultural change campaigns to embed data habits, data quality, and standardised tool usage across Customer Service Portals, CRM, PowerBI, Pilgrim, and AI platforms.
  • Lead Communications & Mixed-Economy Engagement: Design and deliver engaging communication strategies, stakeholder impact plans, and collaboration forums tailored for both internal civil servants and third-party commercial FM suppliers.
  • Represent WS in the GPA Change Champion Network: Stand up regional feedback loops and actively represent Workplace Services on the wider GPA Change Network, synthesising ground-level insights to resolve adoption bottlenecks.
  • Build and Manage the Team: Lead the recruitment campaign for an SEO Change Support Lead, setting clear performance objectives, supporting their professional development, and managing daily team workload.
  • Track Benefits, Govern Risks & Deputise: Monitor risks, dependencies, programme milestones, and benefits realisation, escalating blockers through governance channels, reporting updates to the SLT, and deputising for the Head of Business Integration as required.
  • Champion Continuous Improvement & Innovation: Instigate change initiatives and foster an inclusive culture of continuous improvement, innovation, and organisational learning throughout Workplace Services.

Person specification

We are seeking an established Change Lead with a proven track record of designing change frameworks and establishing operational capabilities from scratch. You will demonstrate experience operating as the lead change authority across complex, multi-stakeholder organisations and mixed-economy supply chains.

  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and communication skills – you can build open, collaborative relationships and flex your style to suit your audience.
  • Proven ability to manage a broad and diverse group of stakeholders with varied priorities and interests, outside your immediate team.
  • Ability to take responsibility for resolution of risks and issues, and to escalate where appropriate with sound judgement.
  • Strong persuasive and influencing skills, with the confidence to constructively challenge at senior levels.
  • Strategic thinking – you can identify opportunities, anticipate risks and develop practical mitigations.
  • Comfortable working in fast-paced, ambiguous environments where priorities may shift and adaptability is key.

Experience and Technical Skills

Essential criteria:

  • Substantial Change Leadership Experience: An extensive, proven track record as an established Change Manager leading complex, end-to-end transformation across large, multi-site public, private, or commercial organisations.
  • Framework Design & Capability Building: Demonstrable experience of designing, implementing, and embedding new change frameworks, impact assessment tools, and governance rhythms from scratch whilst integrating them into established routines.
  • Team Leadership & Development: Proven experience in line management or team leadership, with the capability to recruit, onboard, and develop direct reports while directing multi-workstream change delivery.
  • Senior Stakeholder Influence & Constructive Challenge: Substantial experience engaging, influencing, and constructively challenging senior executive stakeholders (SLT/ExCo levels) and commercial supply chain leadership.
  • Mixed-Economy & Partner Integration: Proven experience driving process, cultural, and digital change across mixed-economy environments comprising both internal staff and external commercial supply chain vendors.
  • Change Readiness & Gate Control: Deep practical experience conducting Training Needs Analyses (TNA), measuring organisational change saturation, tracking benefits realisation, and evaluating "Go / No-Go" stage-gate operational readiness.

Desirable criteria:

  • Property & Facilities Management Sector Experience: Experience supporting property, real estate, infrastructure, facilities management, or operational transformation programmes.
  • Enterprise Systems & Digital Change: Familiarity with enterprise software implementations (such as IWMS, ERP, or Customer Support Portals), large-scale digital transformation projects, and behavioural technology adoption frameworks.
  • Delivery & Assurance Knowledge: Experience working in or alongside operational delivery and assurance functions, or knowledge of public sector project delivery frameworks.
  • Professional Qualifications (GPA Gold Standard): A recognised Change Management certification (such as APMG Change Management, Prosci, or CCMP) or Project Management qualification (such as PRINCE2, Agile, or MSP).

Qualifications and Accreditations

Desirable Criteria:

  • A recognised Change Management certification (such as APMG Change Management, Prosci, or CCMP), or a willingness to work towards achieving one, is desirable.
  • A recognised Project or Programme Management qualification (such as PRINCE2, Agile, or MSP) is advantageous but not essential.

About the job

Job summary

Can you solve the puzzles of government?

Can you be the architect of a better tomorrow?


If you enjoy applying statistical theories to assess risks and estimate the odds of future outcomes—and have a passion for presenting your findings—a rewarding career as a Graduate Trainee Actuary in the heart of government could be the perfect fit for you!

About us

The Government Actuary’s Department (GAD) are at the centre of actuarial expertise within government. We enable government to better understand and quantify risk and uncertainty and in turn help shape better outcomes for the UK public. We do this on our core work by diving into client challenges and ensuring our advice enables success. We identify critical challenges to co-create solutions with our partners so that actuarial expertise can have more impact on significant policy initiatives.

We are an inclusive organisation that values the unique perspectives and strengths of a diverse team, supported through our staff networks and active Diversity and Inclusion strategy, we ensure everyone has the opportunity to thrive. We are seeking motivated individuals to join our analytical team, where your contributions will be valued, and your voice heard.

Job description

As a Graduate Trainee Actuary, we will support your development to become a future Actuary in Government who is able to produce high quality, impactful advice and analysis for government and adapt to emerging societal challenges.

This will include participation in our rotation programme which includes:

Analytical Focussed Placement: Apply theoretical actuarial concepts and modern techniques to actuarial processes to deliver accurate analysis efficiently. As time progresses, take on more responsibility for the validity of your work and others as well as delegating and developing junior colleagues.

Consulting Focussed Placement: Work with actuaries to turn analysis into impactful advice through drafting communications and presenting to clients. Build relationships with stakeholders (internal and external) to support effective delivery of advice. As time progresses, build relationships with clients, support scoping of actuarial advice and business development.

Specialised Focussed Placement: Build upon experience of previous placements to try a new actuarial area in GAD or continue specialising within a certain domain to take on more ownership of advice and/or analysis.

Throughout the rotation programme, secondment opportunities exist to work directly with clients in government.

A significant proportion of GAD’s actuarial advice is either pensions or emerging policy areas. Therefore, during the rotation programme, all trainees will be exposed to typical pensions work (such as delivering actuarial valuations and other pension calculations, managing costs and risks associated with public service pension schemes or providing advice on funded pension schemes) as well as working in a different area to develop adaptability to new problems.

GAD works across a wide range of actuarial areas and we would look to provide opportunities for you to get involved in areas of interest where business needs allow.

Person specification

  1. Have an inquisitive and open mind to learn and apply new concepts
  2. Produce actuarial analysis to inform GAD’s advice to government departments, across areas of insurance, investments, pensions, and risk.
  3. Consider the validity of your, or others’, analysis through self-checks and communicate areas of concerns to senior colleagues.
  4. Support client engagement by drafting reports and advice as well as providing support in meetings and presentations.
  5. Manage your time to deliver your work to time and budget. You may also be responsible for assisting with broader project management and development of junior staff.
  6. Proactively develop your knowledge and understanding of actuarial methods and analysis, data science, the issues and risks facing government as well as how GAD can best provide advice to our clients.
  7. Identify and suggest new ways of working, innovative solutions, modern outputs and new areas where GAD can provide advice.
  8. Work within GAD’s and Actuarial professional standards and departmental procedures and guidance notes.
  9. Use MS Office and advanced tools like R, Python or our Pension Valuation Software to carry out analysis and prepare advice for clients.
  10. With materials and time provided, independently work towards actuarial qualification through exams and Personal Professional Development requirements.

  • Working Together
  • Developing Self and Others
  • Making Effective Decisions
  • Delivering at Pace
  • Communicating and Influencing

Technical skills

  • Achieved or on target to achieve a 2:2 or above in a degree with a high mathematical content. (Essential)

Alongside your salary of £37,768, Government Actuary's Department contributes £10,941 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

As well as competitive salaries, we offer a substantial package of benefits:

  • Exceptional learning and development opportunities that you can explore alongside your day-to-day work.
  • 25 days annual leave per year, increasing to 30 days after 5 years’ service. In addition, we offer 9 days public and privilege days leave per year (pro rata for part time staff)
  • A Civil Service pension with an employer contribution of 28.97%
  • 5 days of paid volunteering leave
  • Up to 9 months maternity leave on full pay + generous paternity and adoption leave
  • Staff reward and recognition bonuses that operate throughout the year.
  • Occupational sick pay
  • Family-friendly policies such as help with caring responsibilities, special leave, generous paid maternity, paternity, and adoption leave.
  • Access to employee assistance programme which offers staff 24/7 confidential support and resources such as counselling, debt guidance and management advice.
  • The opportunity to join a trade union.
  • A working culture which encourages inclusion and diversity.
  • Salary advances for travel costs, including annual season tickets and cycle-to-work schemes.
  • Access to the Edenred employee benefits system which offers discounts to popular retailers and access to various useful resources such as financial and savings advice.
  • Complimentary BUPA health check.

About the job

Job summary

Please see job description

Job description

HMP Liverpool Futures Campaign

Sponsorship is not guaranteed, and applicants are responsible for ensuring they have, and can maintain, the appropriate right to work in the UK.

Skilled Worker visa sponsorship may be available for this role, subject to eligibility and in line with the UK Immigration Rules in force at the time of application. However, due to current immigration requirements and recruitment timescales, candidates who require Skilled Worker visa sponsorship are unlikely to be sponsored if applying to this campaign.

Applicants are strongly encouraged to consider their right to work in the UK carefully before applying. You can read more about Skilled Worker visas and eligibility criteria at .

The Department will continue to comply with UK Immigration Rules applied in the UK and Civil Service.

Applying for your first prison officer role and happy to relocate? Get your career off to a great start, gaining valuable experience working at HMP Full Sutton, nr york for 23 months before returning to HMP Liverpool Permanently.

We are recruiting not just for officers who are needed today, but for prison officers to fill vacancies at HMP Liverpool in years to come. We need officers now to fill vacancies at other prisons and that is why we are recruiting to this special futures scheme that guarantees you a prison officer role at HMP Liverpool permanently but for the first 23 months of your service you will be working at HMP Full Sutton.

It's a great opportunity. You will benefit from a greater variety of experience, you will also get help towards your accommodation costs paid for up to 23 months, receive a recruitment and retention payment paid at 12 months and 23 months and a paid monthly trip home. You won’t be on your own and you will be with other new officers who, like you will be returning to HMP Liverpool at the end of their 23 month deployment.

What’s on offer?

  • We will pay your accommodation costs (up to £750 per month) for up to 23 months
  • You will be able to reclaim the cost of a monthly trip between HMP Full Sutton and HMP Liverpool
  • You will also be paid a recruitment and retention bonus of £1500 after the first 12 month and 23-month period

As the prisons on First time prison officer recruitment scheme list have an ongoing need for prison officers, you should be able to start your paid training sooner than you would if you applied via our standard application process.

An extraordinary job. Done by someone like you.

Prison officers protect the public and help make an impact on prisoners' lives.

If you have the integrity, skills and strength of character we’re looking for, this fast-paced role could be the start of a successful career. No two shifts or situations are ever the same. And, as you gain experience, you’ll find a range of opportunities to grow and develop into.

Someone like you

There’s no such thing as a typical prison officer. Our officers come from different walks of life, just like the offenders they work with. Whether you’re a parent, a teacher, have worked in retail, the armed forces, or just feel like you’re a natural people person, you’ll have the empathy, self-confidence, great communication skills and resilience we want.

No matter the challenge, you’ll take the time to build constructive, positive and professional relationships with prisoners who could be at the lowest point in their lives.

Teamwork plays a vital role in this environment, so you’ll need to be fully committed to supporting your colleagues and understand the importance of acting as one team to keep the prison, prisoners and everyone who works here safe.

You will be required to work various shifts and some weekends.

An extraordinary job

In this unique career, you’ll have the opportunity to carry out many different roles in any one day. One minute you’re a peacekeeper, the next you’re a counsellor or a teacher. You’ll work directly with prisoners in a unique environment, helping to protect the public and make a positive impact.

Job details

Eligibility

To become a prison officer, you will need to:

· be at least 18 years old at the point you commence employment
· meet the Civil Service Nationality requirements (see nationality section below)
· as this is a physically active job, you will need to pass a medical and fitness assessment as part of the application process
· meet the required eyesight standard in both eyes (both with and without corrective lenses)
· For safety reasons, everyone training to be a prison officer needs a suitable standard of hearing (without the use of hearing aids)
· Whilst tattoos are permitted, including those that are visible, they must not be deemed as offensive, discriminatory, violent, or intimidating in any way. Facial tattoos are generally not acceptable, except where this is for cultural, religious, or medical reasons.

Travel to Work

Some prison establishments are situated in rural locations with limited public transport options; therefore, a driving licence and own transport is beneficial but is not an essential requirement of the role (unless specified). Please note that shift start, and finish times are fixed, and it is your responsibility to get to and from your place of work on time for the start of your shift. Please carefully consider the location of this vacancy and your transport options before applying.

Nationality requirements

This job is broadly open to the following groups:

  • UK nationals
  • nationals of the Republic of Ireland
  • nationals of Commonwealth countries who have the right to work in the UK
  • nationals of the EU, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein and family members of those nationalities with settled or pre-settled status under the European Union Settlement Scheme (EUSS)
  • nationals of the EU, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein and family members of those nationalities who have made a valid application for settled or pre-settled status under the European Union Settlement Scheme (EUSS)
  • individuals with limited leave to remain or indefinite leave to remain who were eligible to apply for EUSS on or before 31 December 2020
  • Turkish nationals, and certain family members of Turkish nationals, who have accrued the right to work in the Civil Service

Further information on nationality requirements .

Essential skills

You don’t need qualifications to become a prison officer. Personal qualities are more important. You need to show:

· communication and influencing skills
· commitment to quality
· effective decision-making
· care and understanding

Pay

Your pay will depend on which prison you work at and your weekly shift hours. The figures below are based on a 37 hour contract which you will remain on until you have completed your initial training. You can then choose to increase your hours to 39 or 41 hours a week.

Salaries quoted include an unsocial hours allowance - 37 hours

Starting Salary - £34,928 - HMP Full Sutton**

**Due to the security status of these prisons a Counter-Terrorism Check (CTC vetting) will need to be undertaken. Proof that you have been a resident in the UK for the last 3 years is needed to complete the CTC vetting process. Applicants who do not meet the residency requirement will not be able to take up post at this prison. (please refer to CTC section below)

You will also get:

  • your accommodation costs paid (up to £750 per month) for up to 23 months.
  • the cost of a monthly trip home.
  • The cost is 1 trip home per month (deployed prison to permanent prison)

Prisons operate 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. This means you will have to cover various shift patterns that will include evenings, some nights, weekends and public holidays (these days are added to your holiday allowance).

You may also have opportunities to work additional paid hours.

Total length of deployment 23 months, after which you will return to HMP Liverpool, your permanent prison.

Benefits

· 25 days’ annual holiday (rising to 30 days after 10 years’ service)
· paid time off for public holidays and 1 extra privilege day
· Civil Service pension of up to 20% of your salary
· cycle to work scheme, travel loans and other benefits

Prison officer rewards & benefits , HM Prison & Probation Service (prisonandprobationjobs.gov.uk)

Assessment Process

During the recruitment process you will be assessed on the behaviours, strengths and abilities you need to become an effective prison officer. These include:

  • communicating and influencing
  • managing a quality service
  • making effective decisions
  • caring

Your natural strengths are assessed to find out what motivates and energises you. We will also assess your numerical, written English and spoken English abilities.

Online Test

Once you have completed your initial application form, you will be invited to complete stage 1 of the online test, to see if you have the basic judgement and numerical skills expected of a prison officer.

If you are successful, we will invite you to the stage 2 online test (values-based assessment). We use this assessment to understand how well you demonstrate the values needed to be an effective prison officer.

If you were unsuccessful at the stage 2 online test in the last 6 months, you can now re‑apply.

The online assessment centre (OAC)

If you pass the online test, we will invite you to an online assessment centre.

We test to see if you have the abilities, behaviours and strengths to be a prison officer.

Once you’ve successfully completed the online assessment centre, we will invite you to complete a medical and fitness test. This will cover an eyesight test, hearing test and basic health screening, including a blood pressure check.

Read more about the application process.

The rewards aren’t all you’ll gain from a role in the Prison Service. There’s the sense of achievement you feel when you’ve helped a prisoner to get their life back on track - the kind of experience you simply won’t find anywhere else.

High security prisons requiring CTC vetting

If your application is successful, you will need to undergo and clear pre-employment checks. This will include His Majesty’s Prison and Probation Service Enhanced Level 2 vetting, and due to the security status of the establishment Counter-Terrorism Check (CTC vetting) is also required. Proof that you have been a resident in the UK for the last 3 years is needed to complete the CTC vetting process. The residency requirements refer to the period immediately before an application is made, and not any other three-year period, or any other accumulation of time spent in the UK.

If you have been out of the country for a significant period of time (usually up to one year) and maintained your UK residency you may still be considered for vetting clearance. For example:

■ spent a significant period of time overseas without returning to the UK, but intend to return in the future

■ taken a gap year before or following university

■ travelled for a year

■ spent time overseas visiting family

This is not an exhaustive list.

Candidates must be able to provide correct and up to date documentation when requested during the application process.

Job offers: merit vacancy

This is a merit job vacancy. If you are successful at the online assessment centre, you will be added to a merit list based on your score.

When all applicants have completed the assessment centre, the prison will make job offers to individuals with the highest scores first when positions become available.

You can stay on the merit list for 12 months. After this, you’ll need to apply again.

Your successful pass from assessment centre will be valid for 12 months if you want to apply for vacancies at other prisons.

If your application is unsuccessful at the sift/Interview stage, a six month waiting period will be applied during which time you will not be allowed to submit any further applications for prison officer positions.

title: Lead R&O Maint Technician (2nd Shift)
description:
In this role, you will impact the overall operational uptime and safety of our manufacturing and production facilities by ensuring all equipment is maintained to the highest standards, reducing downtime and supporting continuous production flow.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Lead and coordinate maintenance and repair activities for production equipment and facilities.
  • Troubleshoot mechanical, electrical, and hydraulic systems to identify and resolve issues promptly.
  • Supervise and mentor maintenance technicians to ensure adherence to safety and quality standards.

YOU MUST HAVE

  • Proven experience in maintenance and repair of industrial equipment with at least 6+ years in a similar role.
  • Strong knowledge of mechanical, electrical, and hydraulic systems maintenance and troubleshooting.
  • Expertise in preventive and corrective maintenance practices to optimize equipment reliability.
  • Experience with maintenance management systems and safety compliance standards.

WE VALUE

  • Associate degree or technical certification in Industrial Maintenance, Electrical, Mechanical, or related field.
  • Experience leading and mentoring maintenance teams.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and ability to work under pressure.
  • Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement methodologies.
  • Commitment to workplace safety and regulatory compliance.

BENEFITS OF WORKING FOR HONEYWELL AEROSPACE

In addition to a competitive salary, leading-edge work, and developing solutions side-by-side with dedicated experts in their fields, Honeywell Aerospace employees are eligible for a comprehensive benefits package. This package includes employer-subsidized Medical, Dental, Vision, and Life Insurance; Short-Term and Long-Term Disability; 401(k) match, Flexible Spending Accounts, Health Savings Accounts, EAP, and Educational Assistance; Parental Leave, Paid Time Off (for vacation, personal business, sick time, and parental leave), and 12 Paid Holidays. For more information visit: click here

The application period for the job is estimated to be 40 days from the job posting date; however, this may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates. Posting Date: September 25th,2026.

U.S. PERSON REQUIREMENTS

Due to compliance with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidate must be a U.S. Person, which is defined as, a U.S. citizen, a U.S. permanent resident, or have protected status in the U.S. under asylum or refugee status.

ABOUT HONEYWELL AEROSPACE

Join a company that's reintroducing itself to the aviation community we've helped advance for more than a century. At Honeywell Aerospace (NASDAQ: HONA), we're launching as an independent, publicly traded aerospace and defense company built on a legacy of operational excellence and mission-focused execution.

Our new brand identity pairs that heritage with real momentum, as we build technology that helps pilots navigate with confidence, aircraft operate more efficiently, and operators stay ahead of change. With our systems on board 90% of the world's aircraft, your work here has reach that's rare to find anywhere else.

Focusing on our customers, investing in innovation, and building a culture of accountability and performance is how we're shaping what comes next.

Every horizon. Every mission. Every day.

THE BUSINESS UNIT

Honeywell Aerospace products and services are found on aircraft across commercial aviation, defense and space. We operate through three business areas:

Electronic Solutions develops the avionics, navigation systems, sensors and electromagnetic defense technology on board 90% of the world's aircraft

Engines & Power Systems provides the propulsion, auxiliary power and electrical systems that keep those aircraft flying

Control Systems supplies the thermal and motion control systems that support takeoff, landing and the safety of everyone on board

With approximately 58,000 employees worldwide and net sales of $17.4B in 2025, we are also advancing systems for autonomous and supersonic platforms — bringing the same focus on safety and efficiency to the next era of flight. Explore our businesses:

Honeywell Aerospace is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will be considered without regard to age, race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, marital status, affectional or sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, disability, nationality, sex, religion, or veteran status.
