Alongside your salary of £60,390, Crown Prosecution Service contributes £17,494 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

Join the Crown Prosecution Service and find your purpose.

The Crown Prosecution Service is passionate about ensuring that we're a top performing organisation and a great place to work. We're a committed equal opportunities employer, creating a culture where you can bring your whole self to work, and individuality is truly appreciated.

This culture of inclusion is underpinned by our staff networks covering disability, faith and belief, LGBTQI+, race, social mobility alongside our mental health first aiders programme and wellbeing sessions.

Clearance

title: Quarry Operations Intern
description:
Internship for Summer 2027

Build Your Career. Build America’s Future.

Vulcan Materials Company is the nation’s largest producer of construction aggregates and a major producer of aggregates-based construction materials including asphalt and ready-mixed concrete. When you join Vulcan, it’s more than starting an exciting career – you get to make a difference for millions of people every day across the country.

When you join Vulcan, you join a dynamic culture in which career development is encouraged, excellence is rewarded, and diversity is valued. No matter the role or the location across the country, every member of the Vulcan team lives through the Vulcan Way: doing the right thing, the right way, at the right time.

Qualifications - External

Skills You’ll Need:

Experience. Previous experience is not required for internships. However, experience working in an industrial environment and or prior experience tied to aggregate mining operations is preferred.

Integrity and Decision-Making. Must display the highest commitment to ethical decision-making and integrity.

Interpersonal Skills. Must be an excellent motivator and team builder. Must be able to form strong social relationships and effectively communicate with both internal and external audiences.

What You’ll Like About Us:

Great Company Culture. Our people share a competitive drive for excellence, in an environment of trust, teamwork, open-mindedness and communication.

Safe. Industry leader in health and safety standards. We are committed to creating a safe work environment and protecting all employees and customers.

Meaningful Work. What sets up apart is the work we do impacts daily lives – and every employee contributes. Our aggregates produced are used to build roads, schools, hospitals, airports, and housing throughout the United States.

Prepare for the Future. 401(k) with company match and contribution.

Training and Development. We see our development programs, and helping our employees meet their goals, as a key part of our business.

What You’ll Do:

Grow your Career. No matter your passion or whether you’re looking to make a career move or are a new graduate from high school or college, there’s more than a job at Vulcan. There’s a career path to take you as far as you want to go.

Learn the Business. Start your career by understanding our industry, the materials we sell, our sales methodology, territory management, day-to-day duties of many departments, and the importance of collaboration. Transition into a role that best suits your talents and interests upon successful completion of the program.

Get Hands On. There’s no limit to the impact our interns can have. All employees are taught best practices in safety, health, and excellence so they can receive hands-on training in one of the many departments across the company in order to maximize their experience and learning.

Explore Different Career Paths. From Sales to Operations, Engineers to Equipment Operators, and many other occupations in between. Interns at Vulcan Materials Company get insights into the range of work happening across our company allowing them to identify their strengths and passions, and aligning them with different departments to have the most impact.

Additional Responsibilities. Other duties as assigned.

Hourly Rate: The compensation range for this role is between $23-24.This position is eligible for overtime. When determining a candidate's compensation, we consider several factors, including, without limitation, skillset, experience, job scope, and current market data.

Vulcan Materials Company is committed to employing a diverse workforce. You will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, veteran status, or disability. You also have the right to be free from discrimination for medical needs arising from pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions.


NOTICE TO TEMPORARY STAFFING AGENCIES, PLACEMENT SERVICES AND PROFESSIONAL RECRUITERS

Vulcan Materials Company has an internal recruiting department. Please review our policy as it relates to the use of temporary staffing agencies, placement services and professional recruiters.

Please note that Caxton House, London is only available to existing DWP employees already based at Caxton House or Sanctuary Buildings, London. All other locations are available to all candidates.

About the job

Job summary

Working towards sustainable futures. Championing diversity in the workplace. At the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP), it’s all in a day’s work. From HR to Finance, Policy to Communications, this is work that sustains and supports, where everyone’s voice is heard, and our customers are at the heart of everything we do. For a career packed with possibility, a comprehensive benefits package, where we live by our values and have the opportunity to improve the lives of people across the country, look no further.

Supporting people who need it most. That’s our purpose. Start your own career today.

The Departmental Planning and Performance division (DPP) is at the forefront of DWP’s agenda to improve how we plan and monitor performance across the department to support decision makers including the Permanent Secretary, the Executive Team (ET) and the Secretary of State. The division’s role is to develop a single cross-departmental strategic overview and plan to ensure the whole department is working towards the same outcomes and to keep delivery on track.

The post holders will join an energetic, vibrant, and collegiate team which plays a vital role in developing, maintaining and communicating a deliverable departmental plan (the Strategic Plan). You will work closely with our performance colleagues who assess how well it is delivered throughout the year.

These are challenging and exciting roles in a fast-paced and dynamic environment, working with senior officials in the organisation to strengthen strategic alignment and decision-making. We are a small team and individual accountability for delivering to a high standard is critical.

Places for Growth and Social Mobility

As part of the Places for Growth Programme, we are committed to delivering a more geographically diverse Civil and Public Service that will better serve the public and ministers.

As part of this initiative, we are continuously reviewing how we recruit into each location.

Job description

These are high profile and stretching roles which will offer the postholder a wide range of developmental opportunities to lead on key elements of the Division’s work to set and embed DWP’s future vision.

Strategic Planning Lead

The main responsibilities include:

  • Managing the Strategic Plan production cycle including developing the timeline, commissioning contributions, and drafting coherent, evidence‑based content to ensure a clear, balanced narrative that reads with a single departmental voice.
  • Leading the development and maintenance of Strategic Plan tracking tools ensuring they provide clear oversight of progress, risks and interdependencies, and acting as the primary project management and audit tools for the team.
  • Planning and coordinating stakeholder engagement across all relevant groups to ensure timely and effective involvement. This includes proactively managing the clearance process with Directors, Directors General, the Permanent Secretary, SpAds, HMT/CO, junior ministers and SoS to secure alignment and sign off.
  • Leading sections of the Strategic and Delivery Plans, building and maintaining strong relationships with policy and delivery leads, and applying negotiation, influence and constructive challenge to ensure the plan content is accurate, outcome focused, and strategically aligned.
  • Supporting continuous improvement of the strategic planning process, ensuring lessons are learned, good practice implemented, and opportunities for streamlining and enhancing strategic decision-making are captured, tracked and embedded through existing processes, governance and improvement mechanisms.
  • Coordinating communication and engagement for the Strategic Plan, ensuring timely, consistent and well informed messaging across the department. This includes developing tailored messages, working with Strategic Communications to create high quality communication products, and collaborating with communications leads across the department to maintain coherent priorities and messaging. Preparing key launch materials - including drafting speaking notes for the Permanent Secretary and Director General and developing supporting packs.
  • Contributing to and supporting the wider work of DPP, creating tools and products that help manage the work of the division and support the senior leadership team to ensure delivery of our objectives. This could include supporting on cross-team initiatives or championing structured and effective stakeholder management strategies.

You will need to be proactive, a confident communicator, very comfortable working in ambiguity and a keen problem solver who isn’t afraid of suggesting possible solutions.

Deliverability Manager

The main responsibilities include:

  • Support the provision of timely deliverability assessments of DWP activities to inform internal and external senior decision-making and Plan changes. These include of the draft Strategic Plan, group or other level plans or proposed new/changed activities arising from fiscal events (e.g. Autumn Budget) and ministerial requests i.e. our responses to the Milburn and Timm’s reviews and the devolution White Paper. This will be achieved through targeted and clear commissioning of our Planning and deliverability community following agreed procedures, adapting where appropriate, analysing and synthesizing returns.
  • Supporting Planning and Deliverability Leads and Private Offices to complete the budget allocations return and to input into deliverability assessments through supporting the running a Planning and Deliverability Community and other routine and ad hoc engagement.
  • Supporting effective cross-DWP strategic planning and the annual production of an affordable and deliverable Strategic Plan. Your focus will be on securing robust deliverability considerations through the Strategic Finance-led design of budget allocations commission, products and quality control of returns. You will also support maturing DWP’s planning approach, in particular prioritisation.
  • Supporting strategic planning decision-making by DGs, ET, DB and Investment Committee and ministers through the provision of timely, concise advice utilising deliverability assessments. Wherever possible/appropriate this will be in co-ordination with PFER, People Resourcing, Policy and Business Strategy and Risk.
  • Contributing to and supporting wider work of the DPP, occasionally providing cover for other leads and working flexibly across team boundaries and identifying synergies with the performance team within DPP.

Hybrid working

These roles may be suitable for hybrid working, which is where an employee works part of the week in their DWP office and part of the week from home. This is a voluntary, non-contractual arrangement and your office will be your contractual place of work.

If a hybrid working arrangement is suitable for the role and for you, you will normally be required to spend a minimum of 60% of your contracted working hours from your DWP office.

If you have a disability, caring responsibilities, or other circumstances that may affect your ability to meet the minimum office attendance requirement, please discuss this with us using the contact details in this advert.

These roles can only be carried out in the UK.

Visa Sponsorship

For these vacancies, we strongly recommend that applicants consult with an immigration specialist or qualified advisor to assess their eligibility for Visa Sponsorship before deciding to apply. Please note that while we consider sponsorship requests in accordance with current DWP guidance and Home Office policy, sponsorship cannot be guaranteed.

Locations

You will be asked for your preference for up to 3 locations these will tell us where you would prefer to work if you are successful. Please do not select a location unless you are prepared to accept a role in that location.

Please note that for candidates requesting to work in Newcastle, Blackpool, Sheffield & London, these locations will be changing:

Newcastle Benton Park View will move to Newcastle Pilgrim Place in Autumn 2027

Sheffield Hartshead Square will move to Sheffield 1 West Bar Hub in 2028

Blackpool, Peel Park will move to Blackpool, Fylde View in April 2028

London Caxton House will move to London Sanctuary Building in Summer 2027

Selection for appointment to the Civil Service is on merit, on the basis of fair and open competition, as outlined in the Civil Service Commission's Recruitment Principles here.

Successful candidates will be posted in merit order based on your location preferences, where appropriate, and the geographical requirements of the business. Dependent on your position on the merit list, if none of your location preferences remain at the point we make a job offer DWP may offer you a role at an alternative advertised location. If we are unable to offer you a role in any of your preferred locations, and you are unable to accept a role at an alternative advertised location, we will add you to the reserve list if one is being held.

Some travel may be required, but individuals’ circumstances will be taken into account.

Person specification

The successful candidate must be able to demonstrate their knowledge, experience and skills against the following essential criteria:

  • Lead Criteria: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to adapt style to ensure maximum impact. Experience of drafting publications, advice and/or reports to senior managers/Ministers. The ability to summarise and explain technical issues in a clear and straightforward way for internal and/or external audiences, helping to inform strategic discussions and/or decision making.
  • Excellent stakeholder management skills, with experience of developing and maintaining strong and influential relationships with senior stakeholders both internally and/or externally to achieve results. Able to provide effective challenge to others, to draw out key messages and themes while responding to stakeholder feedback.
  • A strong track record of managing substantial workloads and competing priorities to deliver high quality outputs requiring close attention to detail, sometimes to very short deadlines. Able to operate with a high degree of autonomy and personal accountability. Able to manage information from multiple stakeholders, tracking and utilising, keeping a clear audit trail. Awareness of project management techniques, including approaches to planning and risk management (although formal qualifications are not required).
  • Experience of manging and interpreting large volumes of complex and sometimes ambiguous information and clearly communicating findings to stakeholders. Able to use knowledge of organisational priorities and insights to make timely recommendations that improve ways of working and/or support credible decisions.

Behaviours

We'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:

  • Communicating and Influencing
  • Delivering at Pace
  • Working Together
  • Making Effective Decisions

Technical skills

We'll assess you against these technical skills during the selection process:

  • Please outline your skills and experience demonstrating how you meet the Lead Essential Criteria listed for this position in no more than 250 words

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £44,447, Department for Work and Pensions contributes £12,876 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

DWP have a broad benefits package built around your work-life balance which includes:

  • Working patterns to support work/life balance such as job sharing, term-time working, flexi-time and compressed hours.
  • Generous annual leave – at least 23 days on entry, increasing up to 30 days over time (pro–rata for part time employees), plus 9 days public and privilege leave.
  • Support for financial wellbeing, including interest-free season ticket loans for travel, a cycle to work scheme and an employee discount scheme.
  • Health and wellbeing support including our Employee Assistance Programme for specialist advice and counselling and the opportunity to join HASSRA a first-class programme of competitions, activities and benefits for its members (subscription payable monthly).
  • Family friendly policies including enhanced maternity and shared parental leave pay after 1 year’s continuous service.
  • Funded learning and development to support progress in your role and career. This includes industry recognised qualifications and accreditations, coaching, mentoring and talent development programmes.
  • An inclusive and diverse environment with opportunities to join professional and interpersonal networks including Women’s Network, National Race Network, National Disability Network (THRIVE) and many more.

Things you need to know

Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Selection process details

This vacancy is using Success Profiles (opens in a new window), and will assess your Behaviours, Strengths, Experience and Technical skills.

Sift stage:

Initial sift – Lead Criteria

As part of the application process, you will be asked to provide evidence of no more than 250 words against the Lead Essential Criteria listed under person specification.

We are interested in what you did and how you did it, and what was the outcome, as part of your example. Please note due to system restrictions you may be asked to complete your personal statement ahead of the lead criteria on the application form.

Further details around what this will entail are listed on the application form.

Only candidates who pass the initial sift on the Lead Criteria will be progressed to full sift of your CV and Personal Statement.

Full sift:

You will be required to provide an up‑to‑date CV clearly outlining your employment history, outlining your skills and experience for the role. You will be asked to input this into the application and you are NOT required to attach as a document.

You will also need to complete a Personal Statement of up to 750 words, addressing the remaining Essential Criteria outlined in the application form. Please note that references to the Lead Criteria do not need to be included in this section. Further guidance on what is expected is available within the application form.

The sift panel will assess your suitability based on the information provided in your CV and Personal Statement. You will only receive a score for your Personal Statement and CV if you pass the initial sift. Each element will be individually scored.

Interview stage:

If you have been successful in sift stage, you will be invited to an online interview via MS Teams. You will need to produce evidence of ID at the interview.

The interview will take a blended approach, and you will be assessed against the behaviours outlined in the job advert, as well as strength-based questions.

Further information will be provided to those who are invited to interview, and feedback will only be provided if you attend an interview or assessment.

Application sift is planned to be carried out week commencing: 9th November 2026

Interviews are planned to be carried out week commencing: 30th November 2026

Please be advised that the above dates are indicative only and are subject to change.

DWP may consider increasing the overall pass mark at sift or interview stage in order to manage applications and outcomes.

Further Information​

At the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) we value diversity and inclusion and actively encourage and welcome applications from everyone, including those that are underrepresented in our workforce.

This is an exciting opportunity to join the Met Office on a 12-month Year in Industry placement, commencing at the start of July 2027, developing your skills and knowledge and ensuring you gain the most value possible from your experience with us.

You will have the opportunity to network with our cohort of Industrial Placements all over the Met Office and understand what career opportunities are on offer at the Met Office after you graduate.

We’re looking for a Broadcast Graphics Industrial Placement to help us make a difference to our planet.

As our Broadcast Graphics Industrial Placement, the job may be suitable for hybrid working, which is where an employee works part of the week in the office and part of the week from home. This is a voluntary, non-contractual arrangement and the location advertised will be your contractual place of work. As an Industrial Placement, we would expect you to attend the office once a week as a minimum.

Our opportunity is full time, 37 hours per week. Our people are at the heart of what we do and we'll do our best to agree a working pattern that works for everyone.

World changing work

From science to technology, from meteorology to management, and from planning to communication, our expertise helps us stand out as the authority on weather accuracy and climate prediction. We help individuals, industries and government to make better decisions to stay safe and thrive. This is the Met Office. This is who we are.

  • We’re a force for good - focusing on our environmental and social impact

  • We live and breathe it - putting our purpose at the heart of decision-making

Our Industrial Placement scheme offers ambitious and capable undergraduates the opportunity to gain valuable experience working alongside diverse and highly skilled experts in their field. You’ll be working on projects that really matter and will make a difference.

This role sits within our Broadcast Graphics DevOps team. We develop, configure and support the broadcast graphics software used by internal Met Office media services to produce weather graphics for the Met Office, as well as for a range of external media customers. You may already have seen this software in action on the Met Office website and social media channels, where it helps broadcast weather forecasts. As part of this team, you will contribute to software that supports high-profile, real-world services.

Your key duties

Our software is an exciting, high-profile product, and the results of your work will be used widely to help make a positive difference for real people.

As our IT Broadcast Graphics Industrial Placement, your key responsibilities will include:

  • Developing applications that support our broadcast graphics software.
  • Supporting internal media customers by helping to investigate and troubleshoot issues with the broadcast graphics software.
  • Working in an agile DevOps team to support and maintain the Met Office broadcast graphics estate.
  • Testing the integrity of the broadcast graphics software and its supporting applications.

Exploring new capabilities and contributing ideas for future improvements

Essential Criteria, skills and experience:

  1. Studying for an undergraduate degree with a significant numeracy, science and/or IT element which MUST incorporate a placement year (i.e. sandwich course). Lead Criteria

title: Policy Adviser - Special Situations
location: This post can be based in London (1 Horse Guards Road) or Darlington (Feethams House).
description:

  • Contract type: Permanent
  • Business area: HMT - Companies and Economic Security
  • Type of role: Policy
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time, Part-time
  • Number of jobs available: 1

Location

This post can be based in London (1 Horse Guards Road) or Darlington (Feethams House).

About the job

Job summary

Working at HM Treasury puts you at the heart of government, making a difference to the UK economy and ultimately to people’s lives right across the UK.

Jobs at the Treasury are fast-paced, fun and can offer unparalleled perspective – not least the opportunity to advise Ministers on the decisions which directly determine the UK’s prosperity. Deep in our DNA is a commitment to empowering our people: maximising individual and collective impact, with interesting work no matter your role or seniority.

Day-to-day you could be supporting Ministers to decide the right level of a specific tax or line of government spending; helping maintain the stability of financial markets; analysing the long-term trends impacting the future of the economy; or enabling this work as part of our vital corporate functions.

We are a high-performing department and proud to have outstanding staff from a wide range of backgrounds. We are also a friendly, inclusive and sociable workplace that prides itself on fostering great team spirit. Our two largest offices are 1 Horse Guards Road in London, opposite St James’ Park, and the Darlington Economic Campus, which also contains eight other departments. We work seamlessly across all our sites, including Norwich, Birmingham and Leeds, as one Treasury.

We are both a 1,000-year-old institution and dynamic, forward-looking economics and finance ministry, with a strong direction set by our organisational strategy, the Future Treasury Vision. The 21st century offers huge opportunities and poses new challenges for the UK. Working at the Treasury is your chance to help the country chart the right course.

Job description

This post sits with in the Special Situations and Steel team and is an excellent opportunity to work on high profile projects which combine government policy with corporate finance issues and commercial negotiations. This is an exciting policy environment with a high-level of political interest, often requiring collaborating across departments.

The work of the team will continue to respond to ministerial priorities and the requirements of urgent situations as they arise, but the successful candidate will undertake the following activities:

  1. Lead on situations where companies encounter financial difficulties for HM Treasury, using corporate financial information to inform decision making, often at pace. You may be assigned responsibility for company distress cases, or oversee specific workstreams within larger and more complex negotiations. You will provide recommendations to ministers that reflect the best interests of the UK and its taxpayers.
  2. Build strong relationships and communicate effectively with colleagues across government - including the Department for Business and Trade, No.10, Cabinet Office, UK Government Investments, and other relevant bodies - to represent HM Treasury’s interests in company interventions.
  3. Collaborate with internal and external partners, including Treasury spending teams, external advisers, and wider government, to develop high-quality advice on commercial matters, including whether government should intervene in companies facing financial difficulties or seeking to disinvest from the UK.
  4. Supporting the strategic oversight of active casework, ensuring regular updates are provided to the Chancellor, ministers, and senior officials across government. This involves supporting the ongoing development of tools such as the cross-Whitehall company distress casework digital tracker (in partnership with No.10).
  5. Oversee our active company distress casework pipeline and processes, working effectively across HM Treasury and wider government to develop and explain best practice for considering commercial interventions in financially distressed companies. This includes developing policies, providing training and advice, and signposting colleagues to relevant sources of expertise.
  6. Working across the Treasury and Whitehall on the long-term approach to areas affected by sectoral or company distress, policies affecting various sectors of the economy, as well as individual companies and their finances. Projects will be driven by senior and ministerial priorities; for example, other team members have contributed to the government’s Industrial Strategy.

We work in a fast-moving part of HMT and sometimes we need to work outside our core responsibilities to support policy development and implementation across a range of growth policy issues. Our branches work closely together and flexibly, so the successful candidate can expect the opportunity to be involved in other policy projects across the team.

Candidate Drop-In Session

The hiring manager will be running a candidate drop-in session to give you greater insight about the role and HM Treasury, and ask any questions you might have. If you would like to join us, use the link below to join the call at the right time.

Thursday 22nd October 11:30-12:00


If you would like to speak to the hiring manager informally prior to the closing date, please contact Daniel Lawson, Daniel.Lawson@hmtreasury.gov.uk.

Application Stage

Application Form

Applications should consist of a CV including your employment history, and a 250-word statement demonstrating evidence of each of the below shortlisting criteria. Your CV and employment history won’t be scored. It’s used to give context to your application and support discussions at interview.

The panel will review applications and invite those that best demonstrate evidence of the shortlisting criteria below for interview. Please keep this in mind when writing your application.

Please note that only applications submitted through Civil Service Jobs will be accepted.

  1. Making Effective Decisions: The ability to weigh up incomplete and/or conflicting evidence, and strategic considerations, to reach sound judgements on complex often competing issues, often involving corporate finance.
  2. Working Together: Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to work confidently across teams to develop effective working relationships and influence a wide range of internal and external stakeholders.
  3. Seeing the Bigger Picture: Ability to understand how individual policy issues contribute to wider strategic objectives and use this understanding to support effective decision-making.
  4. Communicating and Influencing: Ability to communicate complex issues clearly, build effective relationships and influence senior stakeholders to support delivery of shared objectives.

The lead criterion is: Making Effective Decisions

If we receive a high volume of applications, we’ll first sift using the lead criterion only. Those meeting the minimum score will then be assessed against all remaining criteria.

If you are successful at the application stage, you will be invited to interview where you will be assessed against the following criteria:

  • Behaviours:

Hybrid working: HM Treasury operates an office based working approach across all Treasury sites. There is an expectation of a minimum of 60% attendance in the office. Please be aware that this role can only be worked in the UK and not overseas.

title: Senior Product Manager
description:
About Taskrabbit:

Taskrabbit is a marketplace platform that conveniently connects people with Taskers to handle everyday home to-do’s, such as furniture assembly, handyman work, moving help, and much more.

At Taskrabbit, we want to transform lives one task at a time. As a company we celebrate innovation, inclusion and hard work. Our culture is collaborative, pragmatic, and fast-paced. We’re looking for talented, entrepreneurially minded and data-driven people who also have a passion for helping people do what they love. Together with IKEA, we’re creating more opportunities for people to earn a consistent, meaningful income on their own terms by building lasting relationships with clients in communities around the world.

Taskrabbit is a hybrid company with employees distributed across the US and EU and a Built In — Best Places to Work (2022, 2023, 2024, 2025) continually ranked across multiple national and regional categories. Join us at Taskrabbit, where your work will be meaningful, your ideas valued, and your potential unleashed!

This role operates on a hybrid schedule requiring two days of in-office collaboration per week in our San Francisco office (130 Sutter Street).

About the Role:

As Senior Product Manager for Commerce, you will own Taskrabbit's global commerce platform, which covers how clients pay for their tasks and how Taskers get paid for their work. The Commerce team's goals are to make it easy for clients around the world to book and pay, get Taskers their earnings quickly and reliably, reduce what we spend to process payments, and keep our payments platform compliant and reliable in every market we operate in. As the PM for the team, you will propose, shape, and execute the initiatives that move us toward these goals. You'll lead a team made up mainly of backend engineers and partner with Finance, Accounting, Tax, Support, Risk, and Legal to identify problems, prioritize the work that matters most, and deliver it.

We're looking for someone who knows the payments landscape well and can lead independently from day one. You don't need marketplace experience. What matters more is that you care about the people on both sides of a payment, you dig into problems until you understand why they happened, and you're comfortable going deep into how payments systems work behind the scenes.

What You'll Work On:

  • Own the global commerce platform, including client payments (e.g., payment methods, booking experience) and Tasker money movement (e.g., payouts and earnings) across every market we operate in.
  • Improve how payments work for our users, e.g., launching new payment methods that increase booking conversion in different markets, reducing payout delays for Taskers, and removing friction from checkout.
  • Investigate payment issues end to end. When something goes wrong (a spike in declines, a delayed payout, numbers that don't match what Finance sees), you'll find the root cause using every tool available, including AI tools to explore data and system behavior.
  • Plan and sequence the team's initiatives with your engineering lead and drive them to delivery, balancing user-facing improvements, cost reduction, compliance requirements, and platform health.
  • Prioritize ruthlessly. There will always be more work than the team can take on, so you'll decide what moves the needle and be clear about what we won't do.
  • Partner closely with Finance, Accounting, Tax, Support, Risk, and Legal, and communicate the roadmap and outcomes to Taskrabbit senior leadership.

Your Areas of Expertise:

  • Payments experience: You have deep experience building B2C payments products (e.g., integrating with payment processors, adding payment methods like PayPal, BNPL, or SEPA, managing payouts), and you know the landscape well enough to lead with minimal supervision from day one. Global payments experience is a strong plus.
  • Product sense for payments: You understand how the payment experience shapes user behavior and business outcomes, and you can tell which improvements will actually move conversion, retention, or cost. You track metrics like authorization and decline rates, and you know where to look when they move.
  • User champion: You care about the problems users run into with payments, and you don't stop at the first answer. You keep asking why until you get to the root cause. You don't need to write code or SQL, but you're comfortable using AI tools to query data, understand how our systems behave, and get to answers yourself rather than waiting on someone else.
  • Systems-level understanding: You understand how payments work under the hood (e.g., auth and capture flows, ledgers, reconciliation, processor and bank interactions), or you're eager to learn our backend setup in detail. The more you know about the system, the better the products you'll build, and the more effectively you'll work with a backend-heavy engineering team.
  • Prioritization: You have a strong sense of what moves the needle, and you make tradeoffs with conviction. You're comfortable saying no, explaining why, and keeping the team focused on the highest-impact work with limited resources.
  • Stakeholder relationships: You build trust with partners across the company, gather input from many sources, and turn it into a clear plan. You've worked with Finance, Accounting, Tax, Support, Risk, and Legal teams and understand what each of them needs from a payments platform.
  • Execution and communication: You get things done, remove blockers, and roll up your sleeves when needed. You communicate clearly in writing and in person.

Compensation & Benefits:

At Taskrabbit, our approach to compensation is designed to be competitive, transparent, and equitable. Total compensation consists of base pay + bonus + benefits + perks. The base pay range for this position is $140,000 - $185,000. This range is representative of base pay only, and does not include any other total cash compensation amounts, such as company bonus or benefits. Final offer amounts may vary from the amounts listed above and will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, relevant experience, qualifications, geography, and level.

You’ll love working here because:

  • Taskrabbit is a Hybrid Company. We value flexibility and choice but also stay committed to regular in-person connection.
  • The People. You will be surrounded by some of the most talented, supportive, smart, and kind leaders and teams -- people you can be proud to work with!
  • The Diverse Culture. We believe that we make better decisions when our workforce reflects the diversity of the communities in which we operate. Women make up half of our leadership team and our diversity representation is above that of the tech industry average.
  • The Perks. Taskrabbit offers our employees with employer-paid health insurance and a 401k match with immediate vesting for our US based employees. We offer all of our global employees generous and flexible time off with 2 company-wide closure weeks, Taskrabbit product stipends, wellness + productivity + education stipends, IKEA discounts, reproductive health support, and more. Benefits vary by country of employment.

Taskrabbit’s commitment to Diversity and Inclusion:

An Active Commitment to Equity within our Company and Platform. We are an inclusive community where all who share our mission and values belong. Our diverse team represents the communities we serve, breaking down systemic barriers, and transforming lives- one action at a time.

Taskrabbit is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, marital status, military/veteran status, or disability status. Taskrabbit is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodation to applicants with physical and mental disabilities. Taskrabbit will consider for employment all qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable law.

AI-Assisted Prescreening Notice [US Based Candidates Only]: As part of our hiring process, we may use artificial intelligence tools to assist with the initial prescreening of applications and responses. This tool does not make hiring decisions — every application and response is reviewed by a member of our recruiting team to determine fit for the role. If you would prefer not to have your application processed using this tool, you may opt out by selecting 'opt out' in the application form or by emailing talentacquisition@taskrabbit.com, and your application will be reviewed manually with no impact on your candidacy.

title: Mission Integration Engineer, Mission and Ground Systems - Top Secret Clearance
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

MISSION INTEGRATION ENGINEER, MISSION AND GROUND SYSTEMS - TOP SECRET CLEARANCE

As a member of our Mission Management team, you will help tackle new technical problems from initial requirements verification through rapid prototyping, integrated test, and operational deployment.

You’d work within a team of other Mission Integration Engineers and Mission Managers, on the same program and across related efforts, to ensure total alignment of your work. You would also work closely with disciplines across SpaceX such as software, information technology, and payload integration to ensure safe and successful mission completion.

You’ll contribute to the performance and execution of programs within the special programs portfolio while specifically focusing on the mission specific systems that drive, manage, and provide user insight into those programs. Based on customer requirements and SpaceX’s system capabilities, you’ll develop system specifications, interface control documentation, and infrastructure plans. This work will cover a number of technical disciplines including space system command and control, operational planning, data processing, compute and networking infrastructure, integrated mission planning, payload integration, and the secure implementation and execution of each of these discipline areas. Our ideal candidate is a self-starter and is hungry to do work that matters.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Serve as the customer interface at meetings, tests, and reviews to develop operations plans, design missions, and participate in real world operations.
  • Ensure contract deliverables are completed on-time and distill customer requirements into actionable development objectives.
  • Work with internal and external stakeholders to drive development. Collaborate with subsystem representatives across team boundaries to consider all necessary trades and ensure end-to-end mission success.
  • Support all phases of the program from development, initial proposal, through successful test, flight, and on-orbit commissioning. This will include educating the customer on our designs and methodologies.
  • Own ground segment interface and architecture design, including compute infrastructure, network architecture, and software systems.
  • Support in-person integration efforts (forward deployed engineering) with external stakeholders and customers.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in a engineering or science discipline.
  • 1+ years of software engineering or electrical engineering, working hands-on with hardware or software technical projects.
  • Active Top Secret, Top Secret SCI, or DOE Level Q Clearance.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Familiarity with USG processes and software systems.
  • Experience coordinating hardware or infrastructure deployments, including in classified or government-controlled environments.
  • Familiarity with networking fundamentals (e.g. IP networking, switching/routing concepts, etc).
  • Demonstrated ability to work under pressure and deliver reliable and expeditious results across multiple parallel priorities.
  • Highly detail oriented, hardworking, and professional with excellent written and verbal technical communication skills.
  • Spacecraft mission design, development, integration, and/or test experience.
  • Strong penchant for innovation in process improvement and system design.
  • Capacity to balance conflicting opinions and manage expectations between multiple teams and customers.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay Range:
Level 1: $100,000.00 - $130,000.00
Level 2: $115,000.00 - $160,000.00

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees accrue paid sick leave pursuant to Company policy which satisfies or exceeds the accrual, carryover, and use requirements of the law.

Those with an active clearance will receive a 10% differential, up to an additional $20,000 annually, once officially briefed into a classified program.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

  • To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Chief Construction Inspector, Public Improvement Construction
description:
The Chief Construction Inspector (CCI) is a first-line supervisory position within Public Improvement Construction responsible for supervising and overseeing Inspectors and Construction Representatives assigned to public improvement projects. The CCI serves as the primary field interface with company organizations, municipal agency representatives, and contractors; supports constructability reviews and project turnover; reviews project scope, field conditions, documentation, invoices, and payment support; monitors safety, training, schedules, expenditures, accruals, appropriations, and RAP funding; and ensures that work affecting company facilities is properly documented, supported, protected, and constructed in accordance with applicable layouts, specifications, procedures, and regulatory requirements. This position requires field leadership, sound judgment, timely communication, and the ability to coordinate multiple priorities across internal and external stakeholders.

This position does not provide employment pursuant to the terms of a STEM OPT Training Plan.

Core Responsibilities
  • Supervise and oversee the work of Public Improvement Inspectors and Construction Representatives assigned to municipal and agency construction projects.
  • Serve as the primary interface between the Public Improvement field organization, company field organizations, agency representatives, municipal contractors, and other project stakeholders.
  • Attend and collaborate with Public Improvement Engineering during constructability reviews; provide field-based input on feasibility, potential conflicts, community impacts, design refinements, and accommodation decisions.
  • Review project packages, engineering layouts, proposed work areas, and field conditions to identify scope gaps, interferences, conflicts, constructability concerns, and impacts to company facilities and the surrounding community.
  • Review and approve eFARs submitted by Inspectors and Construction Representatives by the required deadline, and verify that all field documentation is accurate, complete, and sufficient.
  • Review and verify Daily Activity Reports, Field Activity Reports, applications, mileage reports, cut dimensions, gas cost sharing documentation, photographs, sketches, measurements, selected work items, and quantities for work performed.
  • Review and verify contractor invoices, required backup documentation, payment support, and invoice discrepancies; ensure appropriate documentation is available to justify payment or non-payment.
  • Ensure contractor invoices are entered and processed in MAXIMO and the Public Improvement Invoice Tracking System, required fields are completed correctly, and information requests or discrepancies are addressed timely.
  • Discuss and document changes to field data forms; ensure inspector concurrence where required and record applicable changes in the deviation section of the eFAR.
  • Ensure work is constructed in accordance with applicable design documents, layouts, drawings, and specifications, and ensure changes or alterations are supported by field data, evidence, and accurate as-constructed documentation where applicable. Review and audit Inspector applications, mileage reports, time entry, and other administrative submissions; review and approve time entry for assigned Inspectors and Construction Representatives. Perform other related tasks and assignments as required.
Required Education/Experience
  • Bachelor's Degree and 2 years of full-time business/field construction experience or
  • Associate's Degree and 4 years of full-time business/field construction experience or
  • High School Diploma/GED and 5 years of full-time business/field construction experience.
Preferred Education/Experience
  • Bachelor's Degree in Engineering or Architecture and 2 years of busines full-time/field construction experience.
Relevant Work Experience
  • Demonstrated ability to supervise field personnel, review field documentation, and oversee construction activities involving company facilities on municipal or agency projects. Required
  • Knowledge of Public Improvement construction, utility interference work, company facilities, and electric, gas, steam, or transmission operations. Required
  • Working knowledge of eFAR/eDAR, MAXIMO/CworX, invoice tracking, field documentation, and payment support processes. Required
  • Ability to interface effectively with municipal agencies, contractors, internal operating groups, engineering, estimating, FP&A, and other stakeholders. Required
  • Strong leadership, communication, documentation, problem-solving, planning, and decision-making skills. Required
  • Knowledge of applicable construction safety, environmental, Code 753, permitting, and company procedural requirements. Required
  • Ability to review project scope, layouts, contractor invoices, field quantities, supporting documentation, accruals, appropriations, and RAP funding needs. Required
  • Knowledge of contract administration, invoice resolution, construction inspection, cost control, and field change documentation. Required
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and preferred knowledge of MAXIMO/CworX, eFAR/eDAR, PIITS, project tracking systems, ProjectWise, AutoCAD, MicroStation, Microsoft Project, Primavera, and/or Oracle Work Management System. Preferred
Licenses and Certifications
  • Driver's License Required
Physical Demands

  • Stand, walk, lift, climb, bend, kneel, stoop, and/or reach for the duration of the workday
  • Use personal vehicle(s), and be able to transport, store, and secure company laptops and other job-related equipment in vehicle. Acknowledge that reimbursement for use of personal vehicle is available through the company mileage procedure
Additional Physical Demands

title: Director, Budgets
description:
POSITION SUMMARY

The Budget Director supports the Deputy Chief in the development, administration, forecasting and monitoring of CHA’s annual operating budget and the capital needs plan. The position directs the day-to-day work of Budget team staff; oversees budget monitoring, financial analysis, and executive reporting; coordinates required HUD budget and funding submissions; and monitors the allocation and use of operating and capital resources.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Directly supervises assigned Budget team staff and is responsible for assigning and reviewing work, providing training and guidance, monitoring performance and completing performance evaluations.

  • Coordinates the preparation and submission of required budget document and funding forms to HUD.

  • Leads Budget team activities with the transition from Lawson to Yardi, including implementation and ongoing use of budget, forecasting, capital-planning, workflow, and reporting function.

  • Manages Yardi Jobs request, review, approval, and revision workflows to ensure adherence to CHA policy, appropriate funding allocation, and accurate tracking of all capital funding sources and uses; includes migration into Yardi Forecast IQ for operating budget management, compilation, and reporting.

  • Directs the development of revenue and expenditure forecasts for CHA programs and coordinates monthly variance analysis and explanations with budget staff and user groups.

  • Directs the development and updating of the five-year capital needs plan using information provided by leadership and applicable user departments.

  • Assigns capital funding sources to projects and provide monthly reporting that include budget versus actual, commitment & spend status of various capital funds, and other ad hoc reporting needs.

  • Supervises and directs day-to-day departmental activities to ensure smooth and efficient operations. Oversee processes to ensure that expenditures have proper approval and have been budgeted.

  • Directs the preparation and review of monthly budget to actual reports, forecasts, and financial analyses for executive leadership and operating departments.

  • Participates in and directs strategic planning initiatives to ensure overall goals and objectives of the departments are met.

  • Oversees preparation of program applications related to operating subsidy and capital grants and assists in completing budget-related portions of HUD Annual Plan and Report submissions.

  • Monitors available financial resources and anticipates future funding requirements for review with the Deputy Chief of Budgets.

  • Monitors relevant trends, developments, and federal regulations to ensure accurate maintenance of budgets authority-wide.

  • Reviews program contract agreements relative to financial issues to ensure funds are allocated accordingly.

  • Performs other related duties consistent with the purpose and level of the position.

QUALIFICATIONS

This position requires considerable knowledge of accounting and budget practices and procedures, knowledge of HUD budget and accounting regulations, financial reporting practices, effective analytical, problem-solving, and communications skills, and a general working knowledge of manual and automated accounting and budget maintenance systems. Familiarity with Yardi ERP would be a plus.

This position also requires a bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Mathematics, or Business Administration, and a minimum of seven (7) years’ progressive, responsible experience in an accounting environment or the equivalent of education and related work experience. CPA or MBA preferred.

BENEFITS AT-A-GLANCE

  • Vacation, Sick and Personal, competitive PTO package

  • Medical (HMO, PPO, and No employee cost High-Deductible PPO) Dental, Vision, and Life Insurance

  • Short-Term and Long-Term Disability Insurance

  • Long-Term Care Insurance

  • Pet Insurance

  • Parking Transit

  • Prepaid Legal Services

  • Brightstar 529 College Savings Plan

  • Identity Theft Protection

  • Hospital Indemnity Insurance

  • Voluntary Critical Illness Insurance

  • Deferred Compensation Plan: Empower 457/401(a) with a 3% employer match

  • Pension Plan: CHA makes contributions on behalf of the employee, along with the employee's 3% contribution; 100% vesting occurs after 6 years of continuous employment or opt-out of CHA's Retirement Plan and continues to participate in the Municipal Employees Annuity and Benefit Fund of Chicago

  • Hybrid work schedule (position specific) This position may be eligible for remote work following a successful completion of a 90-day probationary period according to CHA’s established policies and procedures.

Location

Your permanent duty station can be any MOD site within reasonable travel distance from MOD Main Building, London & MOD Bristol Abbey Wood, as there is a requirement to attend here 2-3 days a month. Frequent UK travel as required.

About the job

Job summary

Thank you for your interest in the Director Strategy, Governance & Communications role at National Armaments Director group:

The Director Strategy, Governance & Communications plays a critical role as part of the MOD strategic capability, operating within and across the National Armaments Director (NAD) Group. The NAD group bring together 27, 000 people focussing on delivering major programmes, projects and services that directly support and enable the military front line. In this role you will provide a critical interface with the rest of Defence, Whitehall and Industry to enable the NAD Group to be the UK’s strategic interlocutor for defence capability preparedness – to ensure the UK has the capabilities and services needed to execute defence plans and operations, while igniting economic growth.

You will lead on providing strategic organisational direction, prioritisation and stakeholder engagement, setting organisational performance, long-term reputational improvement and internal communications. The role oversees the NAD Group’s strategy, governance, communications and policy secretariat teams. Their key interlocutors are the Directors of Strategy and Communications in Department of State, Military Strategic Head Quarters and Defence Nuclear Enterprise – as well as the Director leads for industrial, international and innovation strategies in the NAD Group.

The NAD Group has a significant undertaking to deliver the Strategic Defence Review, Defence Industrial Strategy, Defence Investment Plan and Defence Reform at pace. You would play an influential role in the oversight and implementation of these departmental and ministerial priorities by creating the conditions for the rest of the NAD Group to succeed – both internally and externally. The Director Strategy, Governance & Communications operates at the heart of the NAD Group, working alongside its executive leadership – both as it designs itself for the future and operates as a single integrated organisation, within a wider Defence context. You would work closely with the NAD Chief of Staff who is responsible for the day-to-day coherence of strategic activity.

Job description

The Director Strategy, Governance & Communications has the following areas of responsibility:

  • Using wider context of global threats, the defence enterprise and departmental and Ministerial direction to set strategy, communications, and strategic engagements across Defence.

  • Defining the NAD Group’s vision, high-level change agenda and strategic priorities, while aligning these to departmental strategy and the MOD’s Strategic Cycles, particularly the Strategic Planning Cycle.

  • Provide leadership of the organisation’s governance framework, ensuring robust corporate oversight, effective assurance, and high-quality decision-making that enables the delivery of strategic objectives.

  • Setting the strategic performance framework for the NAD Group, which measures progress against the outcomes, benefits and priorities set out in its strategy and plan.

  • Oversee the NAD Group’s Strategic Centre, bringing together strategy, communications, governance, policy secretariat and performance reporting from across the entire 27,000-strong NAD Group to support decision-making and strategic engagements across Defence.

  • Lead implementation and reporting of Strategic Defence Review recommendation.

  • Enable the delivery of effective communications, in support of the NAD Group, their partnerships, and into wider cross-Defence campaigns, and ensure effective communications to meet business needs through the effective utilisation of communication and policy professionals.

  • Support DG Corporate in the effective design, mobilisation and long-term implementation of the Strategy Directorate work in line with Defence Reform – and by optimising the interfaces with wider-Defence at Director level.

  • Represent the NAD Group and DG executive team at external strategic events, to set out the NAD Group vision and future direction for partners in industry, international and innovation communities.

Person specification

Essential Criteria
To be successful with your application, you’ll need to be able to demonstrate the following 5 essential criteria (please reference each of these in your supporting statement):

  • Proven ability to translate strategic intent, policy development, and innovative thinking into tangible delivery outcomes, ensuring effective implementation at pace while adapting to shifting priorities, complex organisational change and leading teams to embrace new ways of working.

  • Proven ability to quickly establish credibility and trusted relationships with senior stakeholders up to ministerial level (or equivalent), while ensuring ministerial and senior priorities are effectively implemented and providing robust evidence-based advice that leverages a strong understanding of the wider political landscape.

  • Proven ability to translate insights and analysis from a complex operating environment, and the implications of government and departmental direction, into strategic priorities and tangible action.

  • Demonstrable experience of managing a business area responsible for the strategic delivery of corporate services, including at least one of these policy areas: governance, communications and policy secretariat.

  • Demonstrable experience of translating strategic policy and organisational vision into executable delivery plans, leading complex programmes from concept through implementation to achieve measurable outcomes in a dynamic and politically sensitive environment.​

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £135,000, Ministry of Defence contributes £39,109 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).
  • Learning and development tailored to your role
  • An environment with flexible working options
  • A culture encouraging inclusion and diversity
  • A Civil Service pension with an employer contribution of 28.97%

Things you need to know

Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Selection process details

HOW TO APPLY

This is an external competition, and we welcome applications from candidates in both the public or private sector. To apply for this post, you will need to submit the following documents, via the apply button by 23:55 on Sunday 8th November 2026.​

  • A copy of your CV preferably in MS Word format setting out your career history, with key responsibilities and achievements. Please ensure you have provided reasons for any gaps.​​
  • A Supporting Statement of no more than 1200 words (font Arial, size 11), outlining how you consider your personal skills, leadership attributes, qualities and experience match the essential criteria listed above.​ Applications that exceed the word limit will not be considered. For assistance with Supporting Statements or if you experience any technical issues with submitting your application, please do reach out to the recruitment team prior to the closing deadline. Late submissions will not be considered.

AFTER YOU’VE APPLIED

Shortlist​

All submissions will receive an email acknowledgement upon application. If you do not receive confirmation of receipt of your application 3 working days post-closing date, please contact us at DESHR-SCSRecruitment@mod.gov.uk. The panel will consider the evidence you have provided against the essential criteria set out above to determine their shortlist. ​

Assessments

If you are shortlisted for interview, you will be asked to complete an online Leadership Assessment and take part in a staff engagement exercise. These will be held virtually. These assessments are not pass/fail and are designed only to provide more insight into you as a leader and support the panel’s decision.​

Interview​

Shortlisted candidates will be asked to attend a panel interview for an in-depth discussion of your previous experience and professional competence in relation to the essential criteria. Full details of the interview process will be made available to shortlisted candidates. The Panel will consist of Patricia Gallan (Civil Service Commissioner), Nina Cope (DG Corporate), Dominic Wilson (DG Strategy).

Offer​

We will notify all candidates of their outcome, as soon as possible after the final interview. We reserve the right to make any offer of appointment conditional upon references and satisfactory conclusion of security enquiries. In the event that you meet the requirements for the role, but you are not offered the position, we will be pleased to retain your application for a 12-month period in case another suitable role arises. ​

description:

Location

This role is available on a remote, hybrid or office basis. Initially, all DBS employees' contracts are office-based at one of our two sites (Liverpool and Darlington). Employees can apply for remote or hybrid work from day one. If approved, the arrangement will start after six months for transfers from Home Office or after completing probation for new joiners. Requests will be considered based on business needs and role requirements. Informal hybrid working arrangements are also available from day one, subject to business needs and role requirements and will be discussed further following any job offer.

About the job

Job summary

About the Department:

DBS was established under the Protection of Freedoms Act 2012 on 1 December 2012, working from two sites, which are Liverpool and Darlington. We operate on behalf of government delivering Disclosure functions in England, Wales, Jersey, Guernsey and the Isle of Man, and Barring functions for England, Wales, and Northern Ireland. We function within a framework of legal and regulatory requirements and that includes work with a range of external organisations including other government departments, regulators, and trade bodies.

We provide a service that enables organisations in the public, private and voluntary sectors to make better informed, safer recruitment and other decisions. We do this by providing information to enable them to determine whether individuals are unsuitable or unable to undertake certain work, particularly with occupations involving regular contact with vulnerable groups, including children.

Our Strategy:

Our current Strategy sets out our purpose, vision, and the impacts we want to achieve. Our strategy was co-created with our staff and has been supported by insight from our various partners, and throughout, you will find our ambitions to be achieved. Everything that we do within DBS, from developing our strategic intent, to the day-to-day operational delivery of our services, is underpinned by constant considerations of safeguarding, quality, sustainability, value for money, and diversity and inclusion. Our strategic objectives aim to enhance our effectiveness, influence, and customer satisfaction while fostering a supportive environment for everyone.

Equality, Diversion, and Inclusion at DBS

DBS is committed to fostering an environment that values individual differences and ensures fair treatment to unlock the full potential of staff and better support customers. Equality, diversity, and inclusion (EDI) are core to driving organisational success and we have developed specific equality objectives for DBS.

Every decision and activity will be considered through an EDI lens, aiming to build an inclusive culture, improve policies and practices, gain external assurances, and become a leading voice of good practice in EDI.

Read More:

For further information, please see below for a collection of DBS strategies and business plans:

Job description

The post of Associate Director - Commercial (Technology and Innovation) is primarily responsible leading the T&I Contracts side of the Commercial team and for partnering with stakeholders across the organisation to understand the business needs.

As a key member of the Finance and Commercial Leadership team, the post holder will work collaboratively with colleagues to ensure customer and stakeholder needs are met, and that all commercial activity is delivered compliantly with public accountability expectations, the procurement regulations (including the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 and regulations that pertain to the Procurement Act 2023 as appropriate), government policy and professional standards.

As the DBS is a member of the Home Oﬃce family, you will work closely with other members of the Home Office Finance community. Building relationships with people in Home Oﬃce will be key to ensuring DBS and Home Oﬃce expectations, systems and processes are aligned.

You will play a pivotal role in the development of the DBS Commercial Roadmap and associated Category plans, to support delivery of the DBS 2028 Strategy and will lead and support a team of 7 in implementing a T&I Commercial Business Partnering Model to ensure effective resource capacity and capability is in place to support the delivery of these strategies.

Corporate Duties:

As an Associate Director for Commercial, you will lead the development and management of senior relationships to support the organisation in reducing unnecessary spend and delivering Value for Money through commercial activities. You will be responsible for liaising at appropriate levels across the organisation to offer early-stage specific advice to assist in managing commercial activity.

  • Proactively building effective and influential relationships with senior stakeholders including Directors and DMTs both within DBS and across the Home Office and Cabinet Office commercial community, to support the provision of clear and considered advice on organisational, commercial and procurement matters, policy, planning and strategy and the development of innovative routes to market.
  • Develop and implement the DBS Commercial Roadmap, a variety of Category plans and development and implementation of a multi-year strategic procurement strategy with associated assurance methodologies to set the commercial direction in alignment with the organisation’s strategy; devise the appropriate communication strategy to enable G7s and below to drive awareness in the business.
  • Drive the Commercial Teams development in understanding service supply markets, categories and business context, enabling innovation in approach; providing options and opportunities for new ways of working from a commercial perspective.
  • Plan, lead and oversee the procurement of services across all relevant categories, ensuring effective commercial management of key suppliers compliantly with Disclosure Barring Services, Home Office and Cabinet Office policies and assurance processes ensuring full compliance with the Procurement Regulations, the Procurement Act 2023 and any applicable EU procurement law.
  • Lead the team in developing and implementing procurement strategies, defining and negotiating contract terms, and engaging the market in delivery Category plans, including the future technology category.
  • Lead the team in identifying and mitigating contractual risk, reducing the risk of service failure and reputational damage. Developing the G7s to engage with other Commercial professionals across Government on broader supplier and market risks to understand broader exposure and mitigate risks, by leading through example. Ensure escalations to SCS across the DBS, Home Office and Cabinet Office commercial community are managed appropriately.
  • Setting the strategic direction to commercial activities around the commercial life cycle including leading the team’s approach to strategic planning and timetabling, market development, market engagement, tender document preparation, tender period management, tender evaluation and price analysis, award recommendations and governance.
  • Managing and overseeing the mobilisation of new contracts from a commercial perspective; handing over to SSRM, T&I and contract management teams in accordance with the Contract Management Professional Standards.
  • Support G7s in driving awareness of and compliance with any developments in procurement law, government accounting and best commercial and procurement practice as identified by government policy, standards and toolkits.
  • Support G7s in ensuring that the Commercial teams maintain a Commercial pipeline of procurement activity, forecast and enable savings; and identify and manage all commercial and contract risks to protect DBS from risks of service failure and reputational risk.
  • Ensuring positive relationships with relevant internal, pan government and external stakeholders, including suppliers are developed and maintained; building and maintaining effective working relationships at strategic, organisational leadership levels with key suppliers.
  • Ensure compliance to and awareness of developments in procurement law, government accounting and best commercial and procurement practice as identified by government toolkits; lead compliance with all Departmental, Home Office and Cabinet Office Commercial Controls for DBS that relate to commercial practice and otherwise, including strict adherence to their delegated authorities, governance, legislation, and policy as appropriate.
  • Act corporately and make a contribution to Pan Government Commercial Function Agendas and wider objectives.
  • Analysing and resolving escalated contractual issues, where strategic management of the resolution is required; otherwise oversee G7 and SEO/HEO management of issues.
  • Providing leadership, management and guidance to an integral internal team of commercial professionals.

Person specification

The successful applicant will need to be able to demonstrate the below ability and experience:

Essential Criteria

Ability

  • Ability to design strategic MI required from a variety of sources for the purposes of DBS/Supplier meetings/negotiations and DBS, HO and CO governance. Skilled in understanding senior stakeholders MI needs.
  • Skilled at balancing conflicting demands; to prioritise strategically to ensure DBS strategic objectives and corporate priorities are met and/or influence corporate re-prioritisation for the team.
  • Effectively communicates with all levels of stakeholders both within DBS; with suppliers and with broader government; able to influence Senior Stakeholders.
  • Able to flex leadership and communication style in line with strategic situational leadership thinking; leads team members, peers and senior stakeholders by example in Subject Matter Expert specific areas.
  • Resilient under pressure able to work alone on strategic priorities/outcomes and/or lead the team to deliver successful outcomes at pace, against a backdrop of changing priorities both within the function and across the business.

Experience

  • Strategically led complex portfolios/programmes involving novel and non-standard commercial and contractual mechanisms, with the ability to identify improvements that deliver greater commercial outcomes.
  • Experience in leading the most strategic and key procurements and contracts for an organisation, delivering with and through others; reducing/mitigating potential reputational risk, ensuring security of supply and a focus in managing costs and driving best value.
  • Experience in building optimal relationships with all levels of stakeholders and the most senior managers across the organisation and across government in a complex and strategic commercial environment, through highly effective communication skills, gravitas and personal impact.
  • Experienced in developing and leading multiple teams to support organisational delivery, managing complex intra-team relationships.

Qualifications/Membership

  • CIPS (Chartered Institute of Procurement & Supply) membership, qualified to Level 6 Diploma.

Desirable Criteria

  • Experienced in managing compliance with the Gov.uk Sourcing Playbook, the Contract Management Professional Standards and all associated policies.
  • Knowledge of MS Office based products specifically Excel, Outlook and SharePoint, whilst also demonstrating skills in utilising digital tools to support delivery of wider objectives.
  • A decisive individual; uses judgement in prioritising for the function and DBS as a whole; helps develop DBS thinking at a strategic level and influences both commercial and broader organisational strategy.
  • You can drive functional teams or teams of peers to seek continuous improvement and have experience in re-modelling strategic approaches to delivering outcomes and objectives; able to design and/or re-design business processes to support improvements.
