Job summary

As a member of the Digital, Data and Technology function the post-holder will work closely with colleagues across the Commission in a multidisciplinary team and be responsible for the design of the end-to-end journey of a service. This helps a user complete their goal and the Charity Commission to deliver on its responsibilities. In this role, your work will involve the creation of, or change to, transactions, products and content across both digital and offline channels provided by the Charity Commission.

A service designer is a confident and competent designer who can develop designs based on evidence of user needs and organisational outcomes.

You will:

  • Be trusted to make good decisions
  • Recognise when to ask for further guidance and support
  • Contribute to the development of design concepts
  • Interpret evidence-based research and incorporate this into your work

Job description

Key Responsibilities

    Design communication

    • Clearly explain problems and design ideas to others
    • Clearly explain design decisions to others using appropriate tools and methods

    Designing for everyone

    • Work with others to design and deliver inclusive, accessible and environmentally sustainable content or services that meet the needs of all users
    • Ensure a design meets appropriate standards, for example accessibility regulations, with support

    Designing strategically

    • Align your design work to both the goals and vision of your team and the strategic objectives of your organisation
    • Identify potential risks and use design to mitigate them
    • Identify opportunities and use design to take advantage of them
    • Contribute to the development of design patterns and components

    Designing together

    • Effectively plan and run a design session with your team, users or internal and external stakeholders
    • Identify and engage the right people throughout the design process
    • Give and receive constructive design feedback

    Evidence-based design

    • Analyse, synthesise and clearly explain evidence relevant to users or a service, for example, web analytics data
    • Work with researchers or analysts to use evidence to inform, develop and test a design idea

    Iterative design

    • Apply iterative design principles and agile methodologies to your work
    • Iterate and improve a design based on successive rounds of research
    • Prototype your ideas at different fidelities to explore and test designs
    • Use a range of design tools and techniques
    • Use and iterate design patterns and components

    Leading design

    • Lead and coordinate design work in your team, with support
    • Communicate the value of user-centred design to your team
    • Support other designers
    • Work with digital and data leaders in your organisation, when needed

    Problem solving

    • Draw together and present reasoned solutions based on a wide range of complex evidence and data - able to act or decide even when details are not clear.
    • Recognise patterns and trends from a wide range of evidence / data and draw key conclusions, outlining benefits, risks and design opportunities.
    • Identify the main issues in complex problems; clarify understanding or expectations to discover opportunities to create value to users and the business.
    • Influence internal and external stakeholders and senior leaders through your analysis and make use of qualitative and quantitative evidence to inform design decisions.

    Decision-making

    • Present findings and related design / business recommendations to key decision makers.
    • Work within clear criteria and timescales laid down by colleagues.
    • Plot timelines and manage your workload to suit your own capacity and the project/business need.
    • Make day to day operational decisions relating to the co-ordination of user research activity within the Commission.

    Essential criteria

    Ability:

    • Understanding of a range of user centred service design and delivery practices
    • Ability to understand what problem your team is trying to solve, and align design activities to inform decision making and action

    • Ability to utilise of a range of techniques for analysis of research data, synthesis of findings, and presentation of clear findings that colleagues can understand and use
    • A good understanding of the social and technological context, , and the ability to align service design activities to help the team understand changing user behaviour
    • Ability to use research and analytics to understand user needs, identify service failures and test different designs
    • Ability to champion accessibility and inclusion, consider the impact of new technologies and make sure that designs meet accessibility, legal and security requirements
    • Able to use evidence to challenge assumptions, negotiate with product owners and rationalise design decisions based on user research and established best practices.

    • Proven experience of prototyping and designing for web-based services
    • Proven experience of designing and facilitating collaborative design activities
    • Proven experience within a research and digital design environment
    • Demonstrable knowledge, experience in and passion for user centred design practices for web, service and software development

title: Advanced Hardware Design Engineer
description:
As an Advanced Hardware Engineer at Honeywell Aerospace, you will play a key role in designing and developing sophisticated hardware solutions that advance the future of aerospace technology. You will apply deep technical expertise to create innovative, high-reliability hardware that contributes to safer, more efficient, and more dependable aerospace products.

In this role, you will support Honeywell Aerospace's Integrated Flight Deck Systems (IFS) organization and contribute to the development of the next generation of Honeywell Anthem™ Displays. Working under minimal supervision, you will collaborate with world-class engineers to design, test, validate, and transition complex hardware from prototype through production. You will also serve as a technical mentor, supporting the growth of junior engineers and contributing to the success of complex engineering programs.

You will report directly to our Sr Engineering Manager, and you’ll work out of our Phoenix, AZ location on a Hybrid work schedule. External hires will begin with 90 days on site before transitioning to a 3/2 hybrid schedule.

  • Lead the design and development of advanced hardware systems from concept through production.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to define hardware requirements and ensure seamless integration with software and systems engineering.
  • Perform schematic capture, PCB design support, and comprehensive hardware validation to ensure performance, reliability, and compliance.
  • Conduct troubleshooting, debugging, and root-cause analysis during development and qualification phases.
  • Provide technical leadership and mentorship to junior engineers and support continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Interface with internal and external stakeholders to ensure products meet customer and regulatory requirements.
  • Stay current with emerging hardware technologies and aerospace industry trends to drive innovation in product designs.

YOU MUST HAVE

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in a technical discipline such as science, technology, engineering, mathematics
  • 5+ years of experience in hardware engineering and project leadership
  • Comprehensive knowledge in hardware design, implementation, and troubleshooting
  • U.S. citizenship or permanent residency due to export control and ITAR requirements.
  • Strong expertise in schematic capture, hardware testing methodologies, and design verification.
  • In-depth knowledge of analog and digital circuit design, signal integrity, and power management.
  • Experience with hardware validation, debugging tools, and compliance with aerospace standards.

WE VALUE

  • Experience with modern processing technologies, including microprocessors, FPGAs, memory, and high‑speed I/O.
  • Experience designing module-level analog/linear circuits such as signal conditioning and data conversion (ADC/DAC).
  • Demonstrated experience performing Product/LRU and Printed Board Assembly (PBA) design verification and qualification.
  • Working knowledge of DO‑254 (Design Assurance for Airborne Electronic Hardware) and RTCA DO‑160 qualification guidelines.
  • Proven ability to design, simulate, analyze, and verify hardware performance against requirements.
  • Proficiency with Mentor Graphics Xpedition (or similar design tools), Mathcad, LTspice, and Microsoft Excel.
  • Test engineering experience, including requirements‑based verification.
  • Familiarity with the avionics development lifecycle and strong troubleshooting/debug capabilities.

U.S. PERSON REQUIREMENT

Due to compliance with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidate must be a U.S. Person, which is defined as, a U.S. citizen, a U.S. permanent resident, or have protected status in the U.S. under asylum or refugee status or have the ability to obtain an export authorization.

BENEFITS

Beyond a performance-driven salary, you'll work alongside dedicated experts on technology that's advancing aviation. As a Honeywell Aerospace employee, you're eligible for a comprehensive benefits package that includes:

  • Employer-subsidized medical, dental, vision and life insurance
  • Short-term and long-term disability coverage
  • 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts and health savings accounts
  • Employee assistance program and educational assistance
  • Parental leave and 12 paid holidays
  • Paid time off for vacation, personal and sick time

Explore your benefits:

ABOUT HONEYWELL AEROSPACE

Join a company that's reintroducing itself to the aviation community we've helped advance for more than a century. At Honeywell Aerospace (NASDAQ: HONA), we're launching as an independent, publicly traded aerospace and defense company built on a legacy of operational excellence and mission-focused execution.

Our new brand identity pairs that heritage with real momentum, as we build technology that helps pilots navigate with confidence, aircraft operate more efficiently, and operators stay ahead of change. With our systems on board 90% of the world's aircraft, your work here has reach that's rare to find anywhere else.

Focusing on our customers, investing in innovation, and building a culture of accountability and performance is how we're shaping what comes next.

Every horizon. Every mission. Every day.

THE BUSINESS UNIT

Honeywell Aerospace products and services are found on aircraft across commercial aviation, defense and space — from engines and cockpit electronics to cabin systems, mechanical components and connectivity solutions. Our technology helps operators fly more safely, reduce fuel consumption, improve on-time performance and deliver a better experience for the people on board.

As aviation continues to evolve, we're also developing systems to support autonomous and supersonic platforms, bringing the same focus on safety and efficiency to the next era of flight. With approximately 36,000 employees worldwide and net sales of $17.4B in 2025, Honeywell Aerospace is one of the largest dedicated aerospace companies in the world. Explore our businesses:

Electronic Solutions develops the avionics, navigation systems, sensors and electromagnetic defense technology that help aircraft perform safely and with precision. Our systems are on board 90% of the world's aircraft — serving commercial aviation, defense and space operators from integrated flight deck platforms with 30-plus years in service to radiation-hardened systems trusted for human spaceflight.

title: MRB Analysis Engineer, Fury
description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM
The Air Dominance and Strike Aerostructures Engineering Team is responsible for designing and analyzing advanced structural parts for Group 5 air vehicles and missile platforms. Air Dominance and Strike Structures Engineers own the full development lifecycle, from conceptual to detailed design and analysis of primary and secondary structures, ensuring high-performance, resilient, and scalable mechanical systems that meet the demands of complex, contested environments.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Serve as the engineering authority dispositioning Material Review Board (MRB) non-conformances for metallic and composite primary and secondary structures on Group 5 air vehicles
  • Perform structural substantiation analysis — static strength, fatigue, damage tolerance, and buckling — using first-principle hand calculations and finite element methods to support use-as-is, repair, and scrap dispositions
  • Write clear, defensible disposition packages that restore airworthiness and meet program certification requirements
  • Develop and continuously improve MRB work methods, tools, and standard dispositions to scale the process as production rates increase
  • Monitor trends in recurring non-conformances and drive root cause and corrective action (RCCA) efforts with Quality, Manufacturing Engineering, and Materials & Processes (M&P)
  • Coordinate directly with Quality Assurance, Manufacturing, Design, and M&P to resolve non-conformances quickly without compromising structural integrity
  • Conduct trade studies to evaluate repair versus rework versus scrap decisions, balancing schedule, cost, and performance
  • Provide on-the-floor engineering support during builds, including occasional travel to manufacturing and integration sites

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or equivalent experience
  • 5+ years of experience in aerospace structural analysis, with direct experience dispositioning non-conformances (MRB, liaison, or stress engineering)
  • Strong understanding of static strength, fatigue, damage tolerance, and load path analysis for metallic and composite structures
  • Proficiency with finite element analysis tools (NASTRAN or equivalent) and classical hand-calculation methods
  • Experience analyzing and substantiating repairs for both metallic and composite aircraft structures
  • Excellent written communication skills — able to produce clear, technically rigorous disposition packages under schedule pressure
  • Self-driven with strong autonomy and adaptability in a fast-paced, dynamic environment
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance
  • Ability to travel up to 50% to vendors, production, and test sites as needed to support hardware builds and troubleshoot issues directly

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Prior MRB signature/delegated authority on a production aerospace program
  • Experience with high-rate or rapidly scaling production environments
  • Familiarity with military airworthiness and structural substantiation standards (e.g., MIL-HDBK-5, MIL-STD-1530)
  • Experience with composite laminate fastened and bonded structure repair
  • CATIA or Siemens NX proficiency
  • Hands-on experience in an aircraft manufacturing or depot repair environment
  • Broad experience across a range of aircraft or missile programs
US Salary Range
$132,000—$175,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

  • No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

  • Please always verify communications:
    • Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.
    • Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

  • Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

  • What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit .

title: Principal Software Engineer, Data Platform — Data Trust & AI Context
location: WA - Seattle; UT - Cottonwood Heights; CA - San Francisco
description:
Employee Applicant Privacy Notice

Who we are:

Shape a brighter financial future with us.

Together with our members, we’re changing the way people think about and interact with personal finance.

We’re a next-generation financial services company and national bank using innovative, mobile-first technology to help our millions of members reach their goals. The industry is going through an unprecedented transformation, and we’re at the forefront. We’re proud to come to work every day knowing that what we do has a direct impact on people’s lives, with our core values guiding us every step of the way. Join us to invest in yourself, your career, and the financial world.

The Role:

SoFi’s ability to deliver trusted member experiences, manage risk, meet regulatory obligations, and scale enterprise AI depends on data that is reliable, governed, understandable, and available when it is needed.

As a Principal Software Engineer in the Data Platform Group, you will provide hands-on technical leadership within the Data Trust pillar. Working alongside the Senior Manager and other Principal Engineers, you will design, build, and operate the distributed systems and reusable platform primitives that make data quality, privacy, metadata, lineage, access, and reliability enforceable by construction across the enterprise.

Your work will span three connected areas: establishing shared Data Trust capabilities, raising the reliability of data across batch and low-latency environments, and applying those foundations to a semantic context layer for trusted analytics and AI. By making business meaning, ownership, provenance, quality, freshness, and access policies machine-readable, you will help end users and AI systems work from consistent, governed context.

This is an individual contributor role with broad organizational impact. You will personally contribute code, prototypes, architecture, and operational improvements while setting technical direction across engineering, data, security, privacy, legal, risk, analytics, and product teams. You will build reusable enterprise capabilities and reference patterns that partner teams can adopt, while domain teams retain ownership of their application-specific use cases and serving paths.

What you will own:

  • Data Trust architecture and strategy: Define and execute the technical direction for data contracts, metadata and catalog modernization, lineage, data quality, privacy, and access controls. Translate business, regulatory, and engineering requirements into a coherent platform strategy and sequence investments for long-term impact.
  • Declarative enforcement primitives: Build platform services, libraries, and reference patterns that make contracts, quality rules, privacy policies, and access requirements versioned, testable, observable, and automatically enforceable across the data lifecycle.
  • Semantic context for analytics and AI: Establish the technical foundations for a governed semantic context layer that connects business definitions, metadata, lineage, ownership, quality, freshness, and access policy. Enable trusted discovery, analytics, and AI-assisted or agentic experiences without turning this role into a model-development function.
  • Reliability across batch and streaming data: Lead the evolution of Data Trust capabilities across Snowflake, AWS data services, Kafka-based ingestion, and other batch or low-latency environments. Establish explicit SLOs, failure modes, correction paths, and operational ownership, supported by automated detection, containment, remediation, and recovery.
  • Mission-critical operational rigor: Raise the standard for production data systems through observability, integrity checks, audit evidence, incident learning, and safe automation. Help move the organization from reactive troubleshooting and manual compliance activity toward proactive, measurable control.
  • Cross-organizational technical leadership: Drive multi-quarter initiatives across teams and functions, earning alignment on difficult architectural tradeoffs and investment decisions. Serve as a trusted technical authority for Data Trust while mentoring senior engineers, strengthening design and implementation practices, and raising the broader engineering bar.

What success looks like in the first 12–18 months:

  • A clear enterprise architecture and delivery path exists for Data Trust primitives spanning contracts, metadata, lineage, quality, privacy, and reliability.
  • Priority data domains have materially improved coverage, observability, SLOs, and automated enforcement.
  • The platform provides production-ready patterns for governing data in both batch and low-latency environments.
  • Initial semantic context capabilities are operating in production and provide more reliable, traceable context for analytics and AI use cases.
  • Manual investigation, recurring data failures, and compliance evidence-gathering are measurably reduced.
  • Engineering and partner teams have adopted reusable standards and capabilities rather than creating isolated point solutions.

What you’ll need:

  • Experience & Education: 15+ years of software or data engineering experience (or 13+ years with a Master’s degree) with a proven track record of designing, building, and operating distributed data platforms at enterprise scale.
  • Platform Architecture Expertise: Deep experience designing horizontal, multi-tenant platform services that other engineering teams depend on. You understand the failure modes of distributed systems, eventual consistency, and how to balance latency, availability, and cost.
  • Data Trust & Governance Depth: Practical, battle-tested experience building or managing components of the modern data trust stack, such as data contracts, metadata catalogs, data quality frameworks, end-to-end lineage, and fine-grained access control (RBAC/ABAC).
  • Batch & Streaming Mastery: Advanced knowledge of modern data ecosystems, specifically Snowflake, Kafka (or similar streaming platforms), and AWS data services. You know how to govern data in motion just as effectively as data at rest.
  • Hands-On Engineering: Mastery of one or more core programming languages (e.g., Python, Java, Go) and advanced SQL. You are comfortable writing production-grade code, conducting rigorous code reviews, and building declarative infrastructure (Terraform, CI/CD).
  • Cross-Organizational Leadership: A history of successfully driving multi-team, cross-functional technical initiatives. You know how to build consensus across Engineering, Security, Privacy, and Product teams, translating compliance and risk requirements into frictionless engineering primitives.
  • Operational Rigor: Experience managing Tier-0/mission-critical infrastructure. You build systems with a "trust but verify" mindset—relying on automated testing, drift detection, and circuit breakers rather than manual processes.

Nice to have:

  • FinTech / Regulated Industry Experience: Prior experience operating in a highly regulated environment where auditability, data privacy (CCPA/GDPR), and data integrity are architectural requirements, not afterthoughts.
  • AI Infrastructure Exposure: Experience building semantic layers, knowledge graphs, or context engines that ground LLMs and autonomous agents in governed enterprise data.
  • Open Source Contributions: Contributions to relevant open-source data or metadata projects (e.g., Apache Iceberg, OpenMetadata, DataHub, Amundsen).

title: Senior Manager, Learning Delivery and Pre-Openings
description:
JOB SUMMARY

The Senior Manager, Learning Delivery and Pre-Openings is responsible for leading the delivery, coordination, and continuous improvement of Learning and Development (L+D) programs & projects across Asia Pacific Excluding China (APEC), including foundational leadership development, enterprise mindset workouts, train-the-trainer programs, talent development programs, pre-opening workshops, and ad hoc learning initiatives.

This role facilitates learning programs for property and above-property associates & leaders, while supporting the ongoing capability development of Property L+D Leaders, the International Management Trainer Network (IMTN), and other future Market Champion programs.

The role will balance direct program delivery with efforts to strengthen local learning capability across the continent. The Senior Manager independently leads assigned projects and initiatives, supports the localization and deployment of global programs, and identifies opportunities to improve processes, leverage technology, and enhance the effectiveness and scalability of learning delivery across APEC.

This position is posted in Singapore; however, the location may be flexible within major APEC markets, depending on the successful candidate’s suitability and location.

CANDIDATE PROFILE

Experience

  • Demonstrated leadership experience, preferably as a member of a hotel Executive Committee or in a comparable senior leadership role.
  • Experience leading and developing people, preferably through direct people leadership responsibilities, including coaching, delegation and developing leadership capability.
  • Broad hotel, hospitality, or related field experience and exposure across multiple disciplines
  • Strong facilitation, presentation, and public speaking skills, with experience delivering training, leading workshops, or engaging senior leadership audiences.
  • Experience managing projects, programs, or initiatives involving multiple stakeholders and competing priorities.
  • Ability to build credibility and trusted relationships with senior stakeholders & senior program audiences.
  • Strong business acumen and an enterprise mindset, with the ability to balance property, market, continent, and organizational priorities.
  • Experience supporting organizational change, capability building, or talent development initiatives preferred.
  • Demonstrated ability to embrace new technology and innovative approaches to improve effectiveness, simplify processes, and enhance learning outcomes.
  • Experience working in a multicultural and geographically dispersed environment preferred.

CORE WORK ACTIVITIES

Learning Delivery & Program Operations

  • Coordinates and delivers a broad range of L+D programs, including leadership & talent development programs, enterprise mindset workouts, train-the-trainers, pre-opening alignment workshops and other continent or market learning initiatives.
  • Oversees the planning and execution of assigned programs, ensuring materials, communications, enrollments, participant requirements, and logistics are effectively managed.
  • Supports the localization, adaptation, translation, and deployment of global learning programs to meet the needs of APEC audiences.
  • Ensures learning programs deliver a high-quality participant experience and achieve intended business and development outcomes.

Property L+D, Market Champion and IMTN Capability Building

  • Supports the onboarding, engagement, and development of Property L+D Leaders, IMTNs and Market Champions through onboarding, education webinars, engagement, and capability-building initiatives.
  • Encourages collaboration and sharing of best practices across IMTNs and Market Champion programs.
  • Provides guidance, resources, and support to Market Champions to strengthen local delivery capability and program sustainability.
  • Supports the continuous improvement of capability-building programs and resources across the region.

Program and Project Leadership

  • Independently manages assigned learning, talent development, capability-building, and pre-opening projects from planning through implementation.
  • Coordinates stakeholders, timelines, communications, resources, and deliverables to ensure successful execution of assigned initiatives.
  • Identifies opportunities to improve programs, processes, and participant experiences while supporting evolving business and talent priorities.
  • Provides practical recommendations and solutions to address learning, capability, and operational challenges.

Innovation and Continuous Improvement

  • Identifies opportunities to simplify, standardize, and improve learning and development processes and ways of working.
  • Leverages technology, automation, AI, and digital tools to improve efficiency, scalability, and the learner experience.
  • Supports process redesign initiatives that strengthen operational effectiveness and reduce administrative complexity.

title: Biomedical Engineer - Surgery
description:
The Biomedical Engineer is responsible for technical support of the equipment in the Open Heart Surgery suites, CSICU and other Intensive and Critical Care Units including the setting up, maintaining and repairing of the equipment, rendering technical advice and assistance to surgeons, OR staff and nursing personnel. Ensures electrical safety of the equipment for the patient, as well as medical and nursing personnel.

  • Maintains patient care monitoring equipment including Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump subsequent to appropriate vendor training and all other patient related instrumentation.
  • Informs the Biomedical Engineering Department of any defective equipment and participates in repair and maintenance.
  • Orders necessary parts, accessories, and supply items for all related equipment
  • Constantly interacts with outside vendors and the BIMC Engineering Department regarding periodic maintenance, repairs, and closely monitors and coordinates those activities
  • Ensures electrical safety and performance of equipment by means of periodic checks and preventive maintenance procedures, and maintains necessary documentation for Federal, State and City regulatory compliance requirements
  • Interacts with outside vendors and the BIMC Engineering Department regarding periodic maintenance, repairs, and closely monitors and coordinates those activities
  • Trains other staff of the Biomedical Engineering Department for cross coverage purposes
  • Other duties as assigned

Basic knowledge of anatomy and physiology, knowledge of medical electronic technology and instrumentation acquired through completion of appropriate training, with a highly preferred certification from AAMI or other similar organizations

Non-Bargaining Unit, 862 - Surgery - ISM, Icahn School of Medicine

title: Program Manager
description:
Join a company that's reintroducing itself to the aviation community we've helped advance for more than a century. At Honeywell Aerospace (NASDAQ: HONA), we're launching as an independent, publicly traded aerospace and defense company built on a legacy of operational excellence and mission-focused execution.

Our new brand identity pairs that heritage with real momentum, as we build technology that helps pilots navigate with confidence, aircraft operate more efficiently, and operators stay ahead of change. With our systems on board 90% of the world's aircraft, your work here has reach that's rare to find anywhere else.

Focusing on our customers, investing in innovation, and building a culture of accountability and performance is how we're shaping what comes next.

Every horizon. Every mission. Every day.

Honeywell Aerospace products and services are found on aircraft across commercial aviation, defense and space. We operate through three business areas:

Electronic Solutions develops the avionics, navigation systems, sensors and electromagnetic defense technology on board 90% of the world's aircraft

Engines & Power Systems provides the propulsion, auxiliary power and electrical systems that keep those aircraft flying

Control Systems supplies the thermal and motion control systems that support takeoff, landing and the safety of everyone on board

As a Program Manager here at Honeywell, you will plddttay a crucial role in guiding and managing Aerospace and Defense Programs. Your ability to define project scope and deliverables in collaboration with cross-functional teams will help align projects with business goals and customer requirements. By developing and implementing project plans, including timelines, budgets, and resource allocation, you will ensure efficient project execution and delivery. Monitoring project progress and ensuring adherence to timelines and budgets will help maintain project efficiency and cost-effectiveness. Your expertise in identifying and mitigating risks and issues that may impact project delivery will contribute to successful project outcomes.

You will report directly to our Customer Business Manager and you'll work out of one of our Aerospace locations.

In this role, you will impact the successful execution and delivery of production projects, driving operational excellence, and fostering a culture of continuous improvement and innovation.

Job tasks also include extensive communications and direction of supporting functions such as contracts, program planning & control and finance. This position also requires travel to assist in interfacing with key customers and major suppliers/partners.

Responsibilities for Internal Candidates

Key Responsibilities

  • Manages matrixed program team(s) to achieve business objectives of the Defense & Space Lockheed Martin (DSLM) CBT Lead and manage programs to ensure successful execution and delivery
  • Define project scope, objectives, and deliverables in collaboration with cross functional teams
  • Develop and implement project plans, including timelines, budgets, and resource allocation
  • Monitor project progress and ensure adherence to timelines and budgets
  • Identify and mitigate risks and issues that may impact project delivery
  • Coordinate and communicate with stakeholders to provide project updates and address concerns
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives to enhance project management processes and practices

WE VALUE

  • Strong thoughtful and problem-solving abilities
  • Ability to work collaboratively in cross-functional teams
  • Attention to detail and ability to prioritize tasks effectively
  • Adaptability and flexibility to manage changing project requirements
  • Passion for innovation and continuous learning

This position requires Project Management Professional (PMP) or Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM) certification, which certification of the two will be determined by the level of the position & meeting the minimum experience requirements of the certification. Candidates who do not currently hold the certification required for their position level must obtain the applicable certification within six (6) months of hire. The company will cover the cost of required training, certification, and/or recertification.

Due to compliance with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidate must be a U.S. Person, which is defined as, a U.S. citizen, a U.S. permanent resident, or have protected status in the U.S. under asylum or refugee status or have the ability to obtain an export authorization.

BENEFITS

Beyond a performance-driven salary, you'll work alongside dedicated experts on technology that's advancing aviation. As a Honeywell Aerospace employee, you're eligible for a comprehensive benefits package that includes:

  • Employer-subsidized medical, dental, vision and life insurance
  • Short-term and long-term disability coverage
  • 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts and health savings accounts
  • Employee assistance program and educational assistance
  • Parental leave and 12 paid holidays
  • Paid time off for vacation, personal and sick time

Explore your benefits:

POSTING TIMELINE

The application period for the job is estimated to be 40 days from the job posting date; however, this may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates.

title: Casework Admin Manager
description:
• Job grade: Executive Officer
  • Contract type: Permanent
  • Business area: CPS - Thames & Chiltern
  • Type of role: Administration / Corporate Support, Operational Delivery
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time, Job share, Part-time
  • Number of jobs available: 1

Location

St Albans

About the job

Job summary

CPS Thames & Chiltern are delighted to advertise a Casework Admin Manager position.

As a Casework Admin Manager for Thames and Chiltern, you need to be self-motivated and organised to manage the daily workflow on the Operational Team. You work collaboratively with other managers to ensure that tasks are completed as per our Standard Operating Procedures to meet the high-quality casework standards. You also contribute to the delivery of maintaining professional relationships with internal and external stakeholders and have line management responsibilities of Casework Assistants.

Regular office attendance is a fundamental aspect of this role, as it enables you to offer direct, on-site support to your team. Therefore, is an expectation as part of the role.

The work is varied and fast paced, offering the opportunity to work across multiple work streams.

The Crown Prosecution Service is based in England and Wales. If you’re applying for this role and live in Scotland or Northern Ireland, you must let us know when accepting this offer as you need permission to work from your home address if hybrid working is part of your role. There’s no guarantee that we will grant this approval.

You must be aged 18 before starting in this role. The start date is expected to be 8-12 weeks after the application deadline.

As part of this role, you are expected to undertake direct line management responsibilities.

Job description

Your roles and responsibilities:

  • Line Manage Casework Assistants
  • Allocate administrative duties to the team taking into account the priority of work and the deployment or availability of resources.
  • Monitor compliance with systems and processes to ensure that casework and administrative functions are delivered efficiently and effectively by Casework Assistants
  • Ensure Performance and Development Review appraisals and Probation reports for Casework Assistants are completed within designated timeframes, in accordance with the Personnel Management Manual.
  • Quality Assurance monitoring for the Case Management System (CMS), dealing promptly with any issues arising from these reviews and ensuring cases progress through to finalisation.
  • Ensure the effective management of the Unit’s Custody Time Limits (CTL) system.
  • In partnership with the Paralegal Business Manager (PBM) and Unit Head/District Crown Prosecutor analyse performance data to ensure effective case progression.
  • To use the CPS Case Management System and other IT tools to communicate and conduct CPS business.
  • To deal with general correspondence as well as more complex enquires.
  • Represent the CPS effectively to outside agencies and the public.

A copy of the full job description is attached.

Person specification

GCSE and A-Level results won't hold you back. We know that some people find their skills and passions when they leave school, so we won't take these into account.

Behaviours

We'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:

  • Leadership
  • Communicating and Influencing
  • Delivering at Pace
  • Making Effective Decisions

We only ask for evidence of these behaviours on your application form:

  • Leadership
  • Communicating and Influencing
  • Delivering at Pace

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £32,110, Crown Prosecution Service contributes £9,302 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

Join the Crown Prosecution Service and find your purpose.

The Crown Prosecution Service is passionate about ensuring that we're a top performing organisation and a great place to work. We're a committed equal opportunities employer, creating a culture where you can bring your whole self to work, and individuality is truly appreciated.

This culture of inclusion is underpinned by our staff networks covering disability, faith and belief, LGBTQI+, race, social mobility alongside our mental health first aiders programme and wellbeing sessions.

The Crown Prosecution Service commits to offer its employees the following experience.

  • You can do impactful, purposeful work that’s making a difference to your local communities.
  • You are able to learn and grow, with access to the right opportunities and resources.
  • We care about your wellbeing.
  • We want you to feel valued, trusted and included.

We also offer the following range of benefits:

  • Civil Service contributory pension of up to 28.9%
  • 25 days’ leave, increasing to 30 days after 5 years
  • £350 each year to spend on personal development
  • lawyer training programme for all new prosecutors
  • an extra privilege day to mark the King's birthday
  • competitive maternity, paternity and parental leave
  • flexible working including flexitime, and a family friendly approach to work
  • Cycle2Work scheme, employee savings.

Diversity at the Crown Prosecution Service is about inclusion, embracing differences and ensuring our workforce truly reflects the communities we serve. We want you to feel that you belong and can thrive, whatever your background, identity or culture. As a Disability Confident employer, we're happy to support requests for reasonable adjustments and improve your recruitment experience. If you'd like any reasonable adjustments made to our recruitment process, let us know within your application or contact ben.savage@cps.gov.uk

The Crown Prosecution Service has fixed rates for its Executive Officer grade – a developing rate (the starting salary) and a spot rate (the maximum salary). Applicants typically join us on the developing rate and, after completing a 15-month development period, move to the spot rate if your line manager confirms you’re performing the role to a satisfactory standard.

If you’re joining the Crown Prosecution Service on a lateral transfer from another government department, you should contact us about the impact on your salary and the implications of any time you’ve already spent at that grade before applying or accepting an employment offer. Your salary may be adjusted if your location changes when you join us. This adjustment also takes into account any existing allowances that may have previously been consolidated into your basic pay – there’s no guarantee that you can retain these when you transfer.

We want to ensure our employees can thrive at work and home and offer a range of support to achieve a balance. This includes flexibility of working hours, flexibility to support caring responsibilities and a flexible approach to deployment. We offer a hybrid working policy. You must spend at least 40% of your contracted hours over a four-week period at court, in an office or another official workplace depending on business need and the kind of work you're doing.

The Crown Prosecution Service also has a range of development programmes to support all aspiring, new and experienced managers with developing the skills, behaviours and knowledge to build their confidence and capability. Our Manager Induction Programme is mandatory for all newly appointed managers. This is a fantastic opportunity to support all our new Crown Prosecution Service managers with the tools required to perform effectively in their roles.

Things you need to know

Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Selection process details

This vacancy is using Success Profiles (opens in a new window), and will assess your Behaviours, Strengths and Experience.

Recruitment process

The recruitment process consists of an online application, interview and assessment. These are expected to take place on 24 and 25 November 2026 at 4th Floor Verulam Point, Station Way, St Albans AL1 5HE.

A member of our recruitment team will be in touch with guidance. If you have any queries about this, contact ben.savage@cps.gov.uk

You should keep these dates free or notify us if you're not available. We'll make every effort to accommodate your date preferences but we can't guarantee it.

Assessment

We ask you to complete an assessment as part of the recruitment process for this role. We will provide details immediately before your interview.

Behaviours

You are asked to complete a statement of no more than 250 words for each behaviour setting out how you consider your personal skills, qualities and experience match the specified behaviours and requirements.

  1. Leadership (Lead Behaviour)
  2. Communicating and Influencing
  3. Delivering at Pace

You also need to demonstrate the Crown Prosecution Service or Civil Service values.

The panel has the right to assess the lead behaviour ‘Leadership’ first. If the standard on this behaviour isn’t met, the other behaviours won’t be considered and your application won’t progress. The panel also has the right to raise the minimum standard pass mark. The panel may also refer to the lead behaviour at the interview stage to determine merit order.

Interview/Assessment

We use behaviours to help us understand your experience, to see if you're a good fit for the role. You are assessed against EO in the Civil Service success profiles behaviours framework. We are assessing 4 behaviours at interview / assessment stage:

  1. Leadership - interview
  2. Communicating and Influencing - interview
  3. Delivering at Pace - interview
  4. Making Effective Decisions - assessment

CV

You’re not required to upload your CV. However, when submitting your application there is a ‘CV section’. You are required to provide information about your employment and/or academic history for the past three years. The CV section will be used as supporting evidence, it won’t be assessed.

It’s your responsibility to provide the specified information in the requested format to ensure that you're considered for the post.

If you're unable to cover three years through employment or academic history, you must provide a character reference for clearance purposes.

Strengths

Strengths are tested at interview stage - the strengths tested are not shared before the interview.

Online tests

Before submitting your application, you’re invited to complete an online Civil Service judgment test. You must successfully complete the test to progress to the next stage. Please complete the online test as soon as possible – we recommend within 24-48 hours. The closing date for the test is 27 August 2026.

We send you an invitation to take the test and provide full instructions about how to complete it. The test can’t be taken on mobile phones or tablets.

For more guidance about the online Civil Service tests, please see the GOV.UK website: Civil Service online tests - GOV.UK (www.gov.uk)

Other

This is a full-time post. We do consider requests for flexible, part-time working and job share, always considering the operational needs of the department.

Please note that the CPS is unable to offer visa sponsorship. Therefore, if you require visa sponsorship to work in the UK, you will not meet the eligibility criteria for this role.

Clearance

If successful, you are required to secure a Disclosure and Barring Service check, for which you must have a current valid UK address.

If successfully appointed, we ask you to complete a character enquiry form, and nationality and immigration questionnaire

If you're a Crown Prosecution Service member of staff, you won’t need to do a Disclosure and Barring Service check as you already hold this clearance.

The job you’re applying for is covered by Article 3(a) of the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 (Exceptions) Order 1975, consequently Section 4(2) of that Act doesn’t apply. You’re required to disclose all previous convictions and cautions including spent convictions. Failing to make a full declaration will result in withdrawing your offer of employment if our checks reveal convictions that haven’t been disclosed.

Reserve list

If you're recommended by the selection panel but not appointed to the current vacancy, you’re put on a reserve list for 12 months. You may be offered another Casework Administration Manager post in CPS Thames & Chiltern if a vacancy comes up during this period. We may also approach candidates on the waiting list to fill other roles that require similar knowledge and experience.

Fraud check

The Crown Prosecution Service provides a Fair Processing Notice to all new applicants after they’ve been successful at interview. These candidates are informed that, as one aspect of pre-employment screening, their personal details – name, National Insurance number and date of birth – are checked against the Internal Fraud Database. The Strategic Resourcing team in the Crown Prosecution Service will, on behalf of the vacancy holder, inform applicants when they are refused employment because of their inclusion in the Internal Fraud Database.

title: Assistant Director of Events - JW Marriott Venice Resort & SPA
description:
Job Summary
The Assistant Director of Events provides strategic leadership for the planning and delivery of contracted corporate and social events, as well as catering enquiries with or without guest rooms. The role leads, delegates, coaches and develops the Events team, building the capability and confidence of managers, supervisors, coordinators and trainees to take ownership of their programmes and deliver consistently at luxury-service standards. Maintaining oversight from sales handover through post-event follow-up, the position sets clear priorities, strengthens workflows, anticipates operational and financial risks, and ensures effective cross-functional coordination. With a strong commercial and business-development focus, the role trains the team to maximise total-event revenue and leads the creation of new social, corporate, offsite-catering and Marquee business solutions, including the Marquee’s catering-only proposition, market positioning, pricing approach and operating model.
Core Work Activities
• Drive a strong commercial mindset across the department by training the team to identify and convert relevant upselling opportunities across food and beverage, venues, audiovisual, spa, recreation, transportation and resort experiences.
• Lead the development of new business solutions for the Marquee, including a clear catering-only proposition, market positioning, lead-routing process, pricing approach, operating model and commercial follow-up.
• Create and implement innovative social, corporate, offsite-dinner and offsite-catering concepts in partnership with Culinary, Food & Beverage, Operations, Finance, Sales, Revenue and approved external partners.
• Build a structured business-development plan for catering and event opportunities, strengthen relationships with planners and partners, and convert client feedback into repeat, referral and new-business potential.
• Establish clear ownership for event documentation, financial follow-up and recaps; review performance with the team and ensure discrepancies, risks and lessons learned are addressed promptly.
• Act as the strategic link between clients, the Events team and property leadership, remaining visible during key moments while enabling team members to lead day-to-day planning and client communication with confidence.
• Provide visible, strategic leadership to the Events team, setting clear priorities, service expectations and commercial objectives aligned with the property’s business plan.
• Delegate confirmed events and new catering enquiries according to team capability, workload, programme complexity and development needs, while maintaining clear accountability for results.
• Coach, train and empower managers, supervisors, coordinators and trainees to take ownership of their files, make sound decisions and deliver consistently at luxury-service standards.
• Build individual development plans, provide regular feedback and create structured learning opportunities through file reviews, shadowing, cross-training and progressive delegation.
• Develop Supervisors’ capability to lead large groups, complex programmes and full or partial buyouts, intervening directly only where senior leadership or strategic support adds value.
• Review and improve workflows, tools and standards across the full event journey to reduce unnecessary workload, strengthen efficiency and enable the team to focus on high-value client and commercial activities.
• Ensure the team understands all contractual commitments, commercial conditions and client objectives before planning begins, and coach associates to resolve outstanding points proactively.
• Maintain strategic oversight of the event portfolio from turnover through post-event follow-up, using regular reviews to anticipate operational risks, programme conflicts, financial exposure and service opportunities.
• Empower the team to translate client requirements into clear operational plans and lead cross-functional coordination with Food & Beverage, Culinary, Banquets, Rooms, Spa, Engineering, Loss Prevention, Transportation and other resort teams.
Leadership and Business Responsibilities
• Create a high-performance team culture built on Marriott values, luxury-service standards, clear accountability and confident ownership of each event programme.
• Lead through structured delegation, coaching and progressive development, using workload allocation, individual development plans, file reviews, shadowing and cross-training to strengthen capability at every level.
• Build strong cross-functional and external partnerships to develop commercially viable social, corporate, offsite-catering and Marquee solutions, in line with property procurement, approval and operating requirements.
• Translate event performance, client feedback, market intelligence and financial results into business-development priorities, improved processes and measurable revenue opportunities, with particular focus on the Marquee and catering-only business.
Candidate Profile
• High school diploma or equivalent with substantial experience in luxury hotel event management, food and beverage, catering sales or a related professional area; OR a degree in Hotel and Restaurant Management, Hospitality, Business Administration or a related discipline with relevant leadership experience.
• Demonstrated success leading the planning and delivery of complex luxury events, including large groups, social programmes, buyouts, catering-only events and high-value food-and-beverage experiences.
• Proven people leader with experience delegating effectively, coaching different levels of talent, building development plans and empowering team members to take ownership and make sound decisions.
• Strong commercial and business-development experience, with the ability to shape new event and catering propositions, assess market potential, support pricing decisions and convert opportunities into measurable revenue.
• Strategic understanding of event operations, contractual commitments, financial follow-up, upselling, workflow improvement and cross-functional coordination within a luxury resort environment.
• Working knowledge of hotel event, sales and property-management systems; Marriott systems experience is preferred.
• Fluent professional English; Italian and additional international languages are an advantage. Eligibility to work in Italy is required.
Core Competencies
• Strategic leadership, sound judgement and visible team direction
• Delegation, coaching, training and talent development
• Commercial acumen, business development and total-event revenue growth
• Concept development, market positioning and entrepreneurial thinking
• Operational anticipation, risk management and decisive problem-solving
• Cross-functional influence, stakeholder engagement and partnership building
• Performance management, process improvement and financial accountability
Marriott Culture, Safety and Inclusion
• Model Marriott service values and create an environment in which associates feel welcomed, supported and accountable.
• Follow all company, property, safety, security, confidentiality and data-protection policies and procedures.
• Maintain a professional appearance and communicate clearly and respectfully with guests, clients, partners and colleagues.
• Perform other reasonable job duties as requested by leadership to support business needs.

At Marriott International, we are dedicated to being an equal opportunity employer, welcoming all and providing access to opportunity. We actively foster an environment where the unique backgrounds of our associates are valued and celebrated. Our greatest strength lies in the rich blend of culture, talent, and experiences of our associates. We are committed to non-discrimination on any protected basis, including disability, veteran status, or other basis protected by applicable law.

title: Software Developer Industrial Placement 2027
description:
• Job grade: Industrial
  • Contract type: Temporary
  • Length of employment: 12 months
  • Type of role: Digital, Information Technology
  • Working pattern: Full-time
  • Number of jobs available: 2

Location

Exeter, South West England, EX1 3PB

About the job

Job summary

The Met Office is delighted to open our advertising for Industrial Placements 2027.

This is an exciting opportunity to join the Met Office on a 12-month Year in Industry placement, commencing at the start of July 2027, developing your skills and knowledge and ensuring you gain the most value possible from your experience with us.

You will have the opportunity to network with our cohort of Industrial Placements all over the Met Office and understand what career opportunities are on offer at the Met Office after you graduate.

We’re looking for a Software Developer Industrial Placement to help us make a difference to our planet.

As our Software Developer Industrial Placement, the job may be suitable for hybrid working, which is where an employee works part of the week in the office and part of the week from home. This is a voluntary, non-contractual arrangement and the location advertised will be your contractual place of work. As an Industrial Placement, we would expect you to attend the office once a week as a minimum.

Our opportunity is full time, 37 hours per week. Our people are at the heart of what we do and we'll do our best to agree a working pattern that works for everyone.

World changing work

From science to technology, from meteorology to management, and from planning to communication, our expertise helps us stand out as the authority on weather accuracy and climate prediction. We help individuals, industries and government to make better decisions to stay safe and thrive. This is the Met Office. This is who we are.

  • We’re a force for good - focusing on our environmental and social impact
  • We’re experts by nature - always learning and developing to do things better
  • We live and breathe it - putting our purpose at the heart of decision-making
  • We’re better together - understanding partnerships and inclusivity make us greater
  • We keep evolving - pushing boundaries to make tomorrow better for our customers

Job description

About the job

Job summary

Do you have substantial senior leadership experience with a track record of leading corporate Governance, Planning and Performance?

Are you able to translate organisational strategy into coherent business plans?

If so, this is an exciting opportunity to join the Food Standards Agency (FSA) as our Deputy Director of Governance, Planning and Performance, and we’d love to hear from you!

The FSA is a non-ministerial department of over 1600 people. We play a critical role in protecting public health and consumers’ wider interests in food across England, Wales and Northern Ireland. Our vision is an important one - to drive change, delivering “food you can trust” and working towards a healthier and more sustainable food system.

Job description

This is a new senior leadership role at the heart of the Food Standards Agency, offering the opportunity to strengthen how the organisation makes decisions, delivers its priorities and demonstrates accountability. As Deputy Director of Governance, Planning and Performance, you will bring together governance, planning, performance, risk, and audit, into a coherent organisational approach.

Working across the Agency, you will provide trusted advice to the Chief Executive, Chair, Board and the Executive Management Team (EMT). Through visible and inclusive leadership of a multidisciplinary division, you will help create the structures, insight and accountability needed to support the Agency’s mission of food you can trust.

You will oversee corporate reporting, risk management, business planning, Private Office and senior Committee Secretariat services. You will lead the production and review of the Agency’s annual and multi-year plans, working with finance, people and strategy colleagues to ensure that priorities are ambitious, deliverable and supported by effective performance measures.

You will provide senior oversight of assurance and performance information, delivering high-quality challenge and data-led insight to senior boards. You will resolve complex delivery issues through collaboration and influence, build productive relationships across the wider Civil Service and promote continuous improvement. You will also line manage senior functional leaders, develop organisational capability and ensure workloads and resources are managed effectively.

title: Maritime Advisor
description:
• Job grade: Executive Officer
  • Contract type: Permanent
  • Business area: UKHO - Operations Content
  • Type of role: Analytical, Defence Operations, Operational Delivery
  • Working pattern: Full-time
  • Number of jobs available: 3

Location

Taunton, Somerset, South West

About the job

Job summary

The UK Hydrographic Office (UKHO) is a world leading centre for hydrography, specialising in marine geospatial data to support safe, secure and thriving oceans.

As a trading fund of the Ministry of Defence, we support defence, safe maritime navigation and marine development around the UK and worldwide.

We are looking for maritime professionals to join our team. If you have the maritime qualifications and experience required for the role and want to apply your skills to support the maritime community, then this role is for you.

The purpose of the Maritime Advisor role is to assess new data to maintain our Sailing Directions Volumes, providing essential information to support port entry and coastal navigation for all classes of ships at sea.

Quality is paramount and the role is to ensure the volumes of Sailing Directions (SDs) are safe, accurate, clear to users, whilst remaining comprehensive, and up-to-date including Section IV Notice to Mariners supporting the maritime customer.

Post holders also provide navigational and maritime input for existing and emerging UKHO products and services, often acting as the “voice of the customer” due to their Maritime expertise.

You would be joining this team as we move towards producing digital SD volumes.

If you are successful, you will undertake a programme of development and will be measured against a defined skills and competency framework and, once the required level is reached, normally within 12 – 18 months, post holders will become B2 Maritime Advisors.

Selection Process:

Candidates who pass the sift will be invited to undertake a technical test, which will be undertaken virtually. If the pass mark is achieved, you will then be invited to an interview hosted on MS Teams. Please note these stages will happen in a relatively short timeframe.

Hybrid Working

The Maritime Advisor Teams work in a hybrid way, with ways of working agreed in discussion with the Line Manager. There will be a requirement to attend the Taunton site daily for the first 2 weeks after joining for initial training. There may then be further onsite training requirements – these will be discussed and agreed with appropriate notice. The Teams ordinarily meet onsite in Taunton once a month all together, dates are agreed in advance.

Hybrid working is a non contractual and voluntary arrangement.

Job description

On starting, Maritime Advisors will undertake the following activities:

› Assess new information for its impact on Sailing Directions (SDs) and maintain in steady state maintenance

› Recommend Notice to Mariner action for SDs

› Provide mariner's input to product development

› Pro-actively seek information for SD content from external sources

› Prepare, amend and technically edit Sailing Directions volumes for publication.

Once assessed as competent in these tasks, post holders will progress to undertake the following tasks:

› Verify assessment decisions relating to new information and recommendations of Notice to Mariners action; providing feedback and guidance to support colleagues.

› Collaborate with others to share knowledge providing the mariners’ perspective on New Charts, New Editions and new chart schemes at specification stage.

Additional tasks undertaken by Maritime Advisors may include:

› Provide navigational expertise in response to queries from both internal and external customers.

› Provide mariners perspective/advise to other areas of the business when required.

› Continually develop own skills and provide clear coaching and mentoring for the development of the team.

› Use own expertise to play an active role in development and implementation of new processes and working practices and review and update process documentation.

Person specification

In this role you will have the opportunity to share your external user experience to contribute to and support the development of our products and services to meet current and future customer needs. We are looking for team players, with a proactive approach to identifying and taking forward improvements to ways of working. An eye for detail and the ability to use clear written English to produce user focused sailing directions are key requirements for the role.

Qualifications

Officer of the Watch CoC (Unlimited) or Navy Equivalent (Minimum)

Behaviours

We'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:

  • Delivering at Pace
  • Communicating and Influencing
  • Making Effective Decisions

Technical skills

We'll assess you against these technical skills during the selection process:

  • Strong understanding of passage planning techniques including the use of nautical publications and charts
  • Relevant experience in practical navigation, as a senior/sole watchkeeper.

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £33,448, UK Hydrographic Office contributes £9,689 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

At the UK Hydrographic Office, it's very important to us that our people feel valued.

We offer a huge range of benefits such as training and development, well-being support, flexible/ homeworking, a fantastic state of the art building, high spec equipment, and so much more.

See our attached Candidate Information Pack for more details.

Things you need to know

Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Selection process details

This vacancy is using Success Profiles (opens in a new window), and will assess your Behaviours, Experience and Technical skills.

How to Apply:

Apply by clicking 'Apply Now' and enter the requested information from your CV including job history and full qualifications and upload evidence of the qualification being considered at pre-sift. You will also be asked to enter a Statement of Suitability of up to 1000 words which will be scored against the "Experience" criteria listed below.

Timeline:

  • Advert Closes for applications: 01/11/2026
  • Shortlisting date: Week commencing 02/11/2026
  • Tests will be conducted: 09/11/2026 and 10/11/2026 (these dates may be subject to change)
  • Interviews will take place: Week commencing 16/11/2026

We will try to meet the dates set out in the advert. There may be occasions when these dates change. You will be provided with sufficient notice of the confirmed dates.

PRE-SIFT:

Only applications from candidates who have the qualification of Officer of the Watch CoC (Unlimited) or Navy Equivalent (Minimum) will be considered at sift. You will need to upload copies of your certificates to evidence this and include your qualification details in your CV. If your application does not this pre-sift criteria, it will not be taken through to the Sift/Shortlist as noted below.

SIFT/SHORTLIST CRITERIA:

All applications are processed anonymously. Please note the information required from your CV, as above, will not be scored. Your Statement of Suitability will be short-listed against the following criteria:

Experience:

Your sea-going experience. Please include:

    Chronological details of the names, types and sizes of vessels you have sailed on, time onboard, rank sailed as, geographical areas operated in and whether you were a sole/senior watchkeeper on that vessel.

    Passage Planning. Please describe your experience of passage planning, and your specific responsibility for preparing/executing the plan.

    Practical Navigation. Please describe your experience of practical navigation, in particular coastal navigation and port approach, as a senior/sole watchkeeper.

    If you have any other experience within the maritime sector that you feel is relevant to the role, please detail this in your statement.

    NB. Attention to detail and standard of written English within your application will be considered and scored in the sift.

    Test Criteria

    Candidates who meet the requirements at sift will be invited to undertake a 60 minute virtual technical test and an untimed follow up recruitment question form. Only those who pass the test will be invited to an interview.

    The test will be scored against the below criteria:

    • Making Effective Decisions (Civil Service Behaviour EO Level). There will also be an interview question.
    • Technical knowledge in relation to the role
    • Attention to detail.
    • Clear written English

    Interview Criteria:

    You will be interviewed against the following essential criteria:

title: Associate- Asset Management (Hospitality)
description:
Job Overview

The Associate, Hospitality acts as the primary representative for ownership, providing strategic oversight of third-party managed hotel assets. This role is responsible for maximizing the financial performance and long-term value of the hospitality portfolio. The individual will manage the relationship with third-party operators, lead financial underwriting for potential transactions, and coordinate joint venture relationships. By blending operational audit with high-level financial analysis, the Asset Manager ensures that each property aligns with ownership’s investment objectives and the company’s mission of delivering extraordinary experiences.

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage relationship with third-party hotel operators
  • Create financial models for potential transactions as part of the underwriting process
  • Assist with and support joint venture relationships across all sectors
  • Produce and assist with reporting as it relates to all assets, JVs, and budgeting process
  • Assist with all aspects of transaction pursuit and due diligence including preparation of Investment Committee materials, due diligence coordination, and other activities
  • Perform sensitivity analysis and discounted cash flow analysis
  • Monitor and report on performance at asset and portfolio level to maximize returns for investors
  • Perform other duties as assigned
  • Any other financial and joint venture relations activity that may become necessary through the day to day

Qualifications

  • 3 – 4 years’ experience in commercial real estate hospitality asset management
  • Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, business or mathematics preferred
  • Must want to continuously learn and develop
  • Must have a positive, can-do attitude and be able to fuel growth and innovation
  • Advanced skills in Microsoft Word and Excel
  • Experience working with Yardi and ARGUS preferred
  • Exceptional analytical skills
  • Must be highly credible and trustworthy, and operate with high degree of integrity
  • Must hold oneself and others accountable and strive for a high level of excellence
  • Must be customer-focused and results-oriented
  • Exceptional oral and written communication, active listening, and organizational skills
  • Ability to establish strong working relationships with others in team setting
  • Ability to multitask and prioritize tasks with a strong attention to detail in a fast-paced environment
  • Self-directed and able to work independently, with minimal supervision

Benefits

- Competitive Salary with Bonus Potential

Career Development
- Opportunities for Advancement within our expanding portfolio
- Annual Professional Development Funds to fuel your growth

- Parental Leave Program
- Enjoy a Friendly Work Environment that values collaboration
