Job summary

Power SPPA’s cloud-first operational excellence with your expertise!

The Scottish Public Pensions Agency (SPPA) administers pensions for Scottish Teachers, Police, Firefighters' and National Health Service employees on behalf of the Scottish Government. We’re responsible for protecting the financial futures of over half a million people - that’s around 1 in 10 people in Scotland. If you’re looking for meaningful work, a supportive environment and a career with purpose, you’ll find it at the SPPA. Our office is based in Tweedbank in the Scottish Borders, the train station is a short two-minute walk away and offers regular services to and from Edinburgh Waverley, making it a convenient and well-connected location for commuters. The surrounding area offers access to green space, walking routes and a strong sense of local community, supporting wellbeing both in and outside of work. Our modern office building is designed to support flexible and collaborative working, with spaces for teamwork, quiet focus and hybrid working. Colleagues benefit from a comfortable, welcoming environment that reflects our commitment to wellbeing and inclusion.

As the Senior Infrastructure Engineer, you will be central to enabling SPPA’s secure, reliable and modern cloud services by leading the design, implementation and ongoing management of critical infrastructure across Azure and wider platforms. Working closely with colleagues, suppliers and partners, you will drive the development of scalable, secure solutions using modern standards, scripting tools (such as Python and DevOps platforms) and infrastructure-as-code approaches, while ensuring robust governance, effective problem resolution, system integration and continuous improvement across SPPA’s technology landscape.

Job description

  • Lead and line manage the SPPA Infrastructure/Cloud Engineering team.
  • Build and maintain knowledge and awareness of best practice of cloud and IT infrastructure management. An in-depth knowledge of MS Azure is critical to this role, as is knowledge of the wider Microsoft product suite and Linux. Oracle knowledge, or the ability to acquire it rapidly, would be advantageous to the postholder. Knowledge of securely integrating MS Azure with other cloud platforms is essential.
  • Work closely with SPPA colleagues, suppliers, and managed service providers to deliver the design, implementation and ongoing maintenance of critical cloud services. This should include a deep cloud expertise, including key IaaS, PaaS and SaaS technologies such as IAM, Networking, Storage, Compute and Governance.

  • Use information security practices and available security controls to contribute to protecting solutions and services.
  • Shape contributions to IT Change and Architecture Boards in the capacity of trusted advisor, and/or present to them, to ensure compliant and secure services are developed in line with best practice and architectural principles.

About the job

Job summary

Data Product Manager
£57,000 per annum
Bedford
Permanent
Hybrid Working

Join us at the Money and Pensions Service (MaPS) as a Data Product Manager. This role offers an opportunity to make a significant impact by shaping, delivering and continuously improving data products that support the National Pensions Connection Service, the Pensions Dashboard and MoneyHelper Pensions Dashboard programmes. You will be responsible for helping turn complex service, reporting, analytics and performance needs into trusted data products that enable informed decision-making across the pensions dashboards ecosystem, delivering value for internal users and key external stakeholders including senior leaders, regulators, government departments, delivery partners and dashboard providers.

You will lead the product direction for data products that provide a single, trusted and authoritative view of service performance. Working closely with Data Engineering, BI, Product, Operations and external suppliers, you will define user needs, shape roadmaps and backlogs, prioritise delivery, and ensure reporting, analytics and monitoring capabilities are robust, scalable and aligned to organisational and regulatory requirements. A key aspect of the role will be applying strong product management discipline to data and insight capabilities: ensuring products are evidence-led, user-centred, governed appropriately and designed to support service performance, continuous improvement, regulatory reporting and benefits realisation across a piece of national digital infrastructure.

Job description

Key Responsibilities:

Role Overview

The Data Product Manager will report directly to the Lead Data Product Manager within the Technology & Change directorate within the Data and Analytics team. In this role, you will be responsible for:

Key Responsibilities:

  • Product Development: Lead iterative development of data products aligned with user needs and organisational goals.
  • Collaboration: Work closely with BI analysts, UI/UX designers, delivery managers, and engineers to enhance usability and accessibility.
  • Stakeholder Engagement: Communicate effectively with diverse stakeholders, including those with varying levels of technical understanding.
  • Adaptability: Be comfortable working with ambiguity and evolving requirements in a fast-paced environment.
  • Governance & Compliance: Address legal, privacy, and governance issues early in the product lifecycle.
  • Evidence-Based Decisions: Use product usage data and evidence to guide prioritisation and lifecycle decisions.
  • External Value: Ensure products are accessible and valuable to external bodies including government and regulators.
  • Product Management: Maintain roadmaps and backlogs; translate user needs into product outcomes.
  • Community Contribution: Actively contribute to the wider product community at MaPS.

Person specification

Essential Skills and Experience:

  • Product management – experience managing data products or services such as business intelligence dashboards.
  • Agile and Lean practices – applying Agile principles and tools to support delivery.
  • Applying user-centred insights – using stakeholder insights to improve product outcomes.
  • Creating value for money – identifying opportunities for reuse and efficiency.
  • Life cycle management – understanding product lifecycle phases.
  • Managing product outcomes – identifying priority outcomes and using baseline data.

Benefits

About Us
The Money and Pensions Service (MaPS) is based in Bedford, in a recently renovated modern office. This is a wonderful opportunity for you to become an integral part of a dynamic organisation, working to help people across the UK.

At the heart of the Money and Pensions Service are our values – caring, connecting, and transforming, which are the foundation of our success. They permeate every area of our work and define all our business relationships and the way we work with each other. We’re not only looking for the best people to come and work for us, but we need people who align themselves with our values:

  • Caring
    We care about our colleagues and the people whose lives we are here to transform.
  • Connecting
    We will transform lives through our ability to make positive connections.
  • Transforming
    We are committed to transforming lives and making a positive societal impact.

Our Inclusive Working Environment
By fostering our values, we are immensely proud of the inclusive working environment that we have created. The diversity of our people is a strength that we embrace and wish to build upon, so we are committed to attracting people of all backgrounds. We work hard to ensure that we have a progressive approach to inclusion, equity, and belonging. We really do want our colleagues to “bring their whole selves to work.”

Our colleague and ally networks encompass LGBTQ+, neurodiversity, women’s health, men’s health, ethnicity, and diversity.

What We Offer

  • Generous Annual Leave – 30 days plus Bank Holidays
  • Pension scheme – contributions matched 2 to 1 (employer contribution up to 10% of your salary)
  • Interest-free loan for season tickets for buses and trains
  • Cycle to work Scheme

  • PAM Assist and PAM Life scheme (Wellbeing)
  • Enhanced family and sick pay
  • Paid volunteering (2 days a year)
  • Recognition Scheme
  • Discounts portal to numerous retailers

Flexible Working
At MaPS, we take pride in our flexible approach to work. As standard, we work on a hybrid basis with a minimum of 2 days in the office per month. Hybrid working is a voluntary, non-contractual arrangement and our headquarters in Bedford will be your contractual place of work. The number of days that anyone will be able to work at home will be determined primarily by business needs, but personal and other relevant circumstances will also be considered. If you are successful, any opportunities for hybrid working, including whether a hybrid working arrangement is suitable for you, will be discussed with you prior to you taking up your post.

description:

About the job

Job summary

We're currently accepting applications from candidates based in the South West area of England. If you live outside of the South West area we're unable to progress your application on this occasion.

Make a difference

Every role at CQC contributes to our mission, and if you’re looking for a new role in Operations that gives a true sense of purpose, then you’ve found it. As a Hospitals, Secondary and Specialist Care Inspector, you’ll help make sure people receive safe, effective and high-quality care.

Picture this

Each day brings new insight. One moment you may be visiting a hospital ward, the next you’re analysing information that helps shape safer services for thousands of people. As a Hospitals, Secondary and Specialist Care Inspector, you might get the chance to work on:

  • Reviewing care concerns raised by patients, families or staff and using this insight to trigger urgent assessment activity that protects people.
  • Leading an on‑site inspection that identifies risks, supports improvement, and ensures a provider is held to account where safety standards aren’t met.

Job description

The role

You’ll be key in helping us deliver our work. In this role, you’ll:

  • Lead regulatory assessments: Carry out on‑site and off‑site assessments, develop inspection plans, and analyse information from many sources to build a clear picture of quality and safety.
  • Guide and support others: Work with inspection teams, specialist advisors, and colleagues across the organisation to share insight, understand risks, and build strong relationships with providers and stakeholders.
  • Use evidence to drive decisions: Record findings clearly, analyse data to spot trends, and make fair, risk‑based decisions that support people’s safety and wellbeing.

Person specification

Show us
We’ll be looking for the following in your application:

title: Staffing Specialist, China Grove - Full Time
description:
About

Macy’s is proudly America’s Department Store. There’s a reason we’ve been around for 160 years. Customers come to us for fashion, value, and high-quality products. Now is an exciting time to join Macy’s. The face of retail is changing, and change requires innovation.

Online sales are booming at Macy’s. Our Distribution Center teams are key to our success in the modern retail landscape. They make sure that products arrive at our stores - and each customer’s doorstep - on time, in perfect condition. Behind the scenes, a lot goes into getting products to customers. When a shopper makes an online purchase, we plan, prep, and package the merchandise to get it delivered as quickly and efficiently as possible – across the country and around the world. It takes a lot of smart people working together to make that happen, and so there are many roles you can play, including (but not limited to): material handlers, equipment drivers, inventory control, packers, quality assurance, safety specialists, asset protection, and many more. Whatever role you play – we value you as a colleague. Choose the challenge that’s right for you!

Job Overview

The Staffing Specialist is responsible for maintaining and ensuring the proper staffing and scheduling levels for the Macy's Distribution Centers. The role is also responsible for expense analysis related to staffing and ensuring compliance with the financial components of the Corporate Audit.

Essential Functions

  • Work with Operations management team to ensure appropriate staffing
  • Partner with operations to create week out staffing schedule with daily updates.
  • Analyze current staffing levels vs. projected workload to determine correct FT/PT staffing ratios in order to maximize productivity
  • Partner with HR to provide staffing recommendations
  • Follow company work rules/guidelines for calling in associates
  • Run weekly query to ensure min/max hours are sustained for each associate
  • Validate accurate timekeeping in Kronos, confirm schedules and make corrections to clockings
  • Ensure associates book to correct GL account
  • Maintain Learning Matrix-cross training spreadsheet for all part-time associates
  • Maintain overtime and average hours reports
  • Review and maintain expense controls
  • Provide information necessary to complete ROF, and assist with seasonal/annual budget planning.
  • Monitor and review monthly expenditures vs. budget and provide meaningful variance analysis, as directed by Finance Manager.
  • Assist in closing process to ensure timely and accurate booking of expense and allocations
  • Other functions deemed necessary by management.

Qualifications and Competencies

  • 2 Year / Associate Degree
  • 2-5 Years Experience
  • Must be able to:
    • Understand, communicate effectively and present information to customers, co-workers, and all levels of management
    • Read and understand employment policies and safety rules/procedures in English
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Excellent organizational skills and analytical skills
  • Sound judgment & decision making skills
  • Displays leadership qualities
  • PC skills – MS Word, Excel, Kronos
  • Ability to work independently
  • Excellent training and follow up skills
  • Good problem solver
  • Flexible work schedule
  • Excellent motivational skills
  • Provide accurate reporting and analysis.
  • Team player
  • Maintain confidentiality
  • Sense of urgency

Essential Physical Requirements

  • Position requires prolonged periods of standing/walking around store or department
  • May involve reaching, crouching, kneeling, stooping, climbing ladders, depth perception and color vision
  • Frequent use of computers and other technology necessary to perform job duties, including handheld electronic equipment
  • Frequently lift/move up to 25lbs.

Supply Chain Only and Colleagues Working in a Supply Chain Facility except in locations governed by a Collective Bargaining Agreement:

Random drug testing for all colleagues will be conducted on a monthly or semi-monthly basis, depending upon factors including but not limited to the size of the facility and the number of colleagues on roll. Colleagues will be randomly selected for testing by a third party. Testing must be completed on the same workday the colleague is informed of selection for testing, absent extenuating circumstances. In all circumstances, testing must be completed within 24 hours of notification

This job description is not all-inclusive and may not apply to colleagues covered by a collective bargaining agreement. Macy's Inc. reserves the right to amend this job description at any time. Macy's Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to an inclusive work environment.

title: Service Manager
description:
• Job grade: Higher Executive Officer
  • Contract type: Permanent
  • Business area: FCDO Services - Global Services
  • Type of role: Project Delivery, Quality
  • Working pattern: Full-time
  • Number of jobs available: 1

Location

Hanslope, South East England, MK19 7BH

About the job

Job summary

At FCDO Services we protect the UK’s interests at home and overseas. We design and construct secure government buildings and courier diplomatic packages worldwide, safeguard government tech and a whole lot more. Our work is as varied and vital as it gets, but we never lose sight of our people. Their skills, aspirations and growth mean as much as the global mission we’re on. In our world, it all matters.

Job description

Our Service Management community works with global customers, delivery experts and other stakeholders to ensure our services are of the very highest quality. Committed to meeting agreed outcomes, offering great value for money and aligning with business needs, we’re flexible, efficient and always ready to listen and adapt to the needs of our customers. Now, you’ve got the opportunity to join them.

Supporting customers globally.

Developing new ways of working.

Making an impact internationally.

It all matters.

Support, manage and develop a portfolio of vital services

When you join us as a Service Manager, you’ll be responsible for supporting a defined portfolio, and be committed to ensuring the services we offer are delivered with a strong customer focus and to the highest standards. Monitoring risks, providing clear insights, ensuring consistent day-to-day delivery and ready to make an ongoing contribution to continuous improvement, you’ll work collaboratively and flexibly as you promote consistency, resilience, knowledge sharing and best practice. Developing positive relationships with customers, suppliers, stakeholders and operational teams as you support our organisation’s ambitious plans, you’ll also ensure that the services you focus on are managed in accordance with agreed policies, standards, governance and contractual obligations.

You’ll have a wide range of additional tasks – these include monitoring performance, risks, compliance obligations and customer outcomes, contributing to improved efficiency, satisfaction and service quality, and maintaining accurate documentation, records, management information and performance reporting. Working to coordinate service change and transformation activities, and investigating any issues, risks or challenges that arise, we’ll expect you to make an active contribution to our capabilities by sharing knowledge and helping to build a collaborative and resilient Service Management community. In addition, you’ll respond to changing business priorities and support our overall resilience by operating flexibly across a range of customer portfolios and service areas.

Use all your skills as you work to defend the UK’s security interests

To be a success in this vital role you’ll have proven experience of building positive working relationships with a diverse range of colleagues, the ability to work in a high volume, complex service delivery environment, and be ready to support, encourage and coach other members of your team. Capable of contributing to change activities, service improvements and process updates, and of applying sound judgement while handling escalations and monitoring service performance, you should also possess the writing skills necessary to produce clear reports, reviews and operational updates for your senior colleagues.

You should hold – or being willing to attain – an ITIL Foundation qualification, and in addition to evidence of ongoing professional development, you should have a good awareness of service management principles, quality assurance frameworks and customer-focused service design. It’s important that you possess excellent numeracy and digital capabilities, and in addition to an understanding of risk, compliance and audit expectations linked to service delivery, you should have good knowledge of performance management, KPIs and how data supports operational decisions. In addition to these skills, a Lean, Six Sigma, Agile, PRINCE2 or similar qualification would be desirable, as would knowledge of digital or workflow management systems and financial processes such as budgeting or cost controls.

Discover the support you need to grow your career further

But we’re always looking to improve – just like you. That’s why when you join us, expect to receive a competitive salary, generous holiday entitlement and a Civil Service Pension. Along with this, you’ll also have access to training and other development opportunities to help grow your career with us. Our offices have an on-site gym, nursery, café, and restaurant, and we offer interest-free loans on season tickets and bikes to help you get there. It's a great set of benefits made to support all you do, and all you need.

Want to see your future team’s work in action? Step into our Virtual Embassy and select a guide to take you round to see how we deliver for government customers and how you could help. Explore the embassy now at virtual-embassy.fcdoservicescareers.co.uk

Every single colleague must be security cleared before joining us. If you’re successful in your application, we’ll ask you to undergo our vetting process. You can find out more about this at fcdoservicescareers.co.uk/how-to-apply/

To find out more about our benefits and our organisation, please visit fcdoservicescareers.co.uk.

It takes a diverse team to protect a diverse world

The vital work we do takes an incredible community of colleagues, with different skills, backgrounds, cultures and identities. We support every individual, so that you always know you’re welcome and valued. It’s what makes us a Disability Confident employer. And why we’re recognised as a ‘Carer Confident’ workplace. And it’s how you know you’re joining an inspiring, inclusive organisation.

Person specification

We are looking for people with:

Qualifications

  • ITIL Foundation qualification (or willingness to achieve).
  • Evidence of ongoing professional development related to service delivery, operations or organisational processes.
  • Good literacy, numeracy and digital capability in an operational environment.

Knowledge

  • Awareness of service management principles and quality assurance frameworks.
  • Understanding of risk, compliance and audit expectations linked to service delivery.
  • Basic understanding of performance management, KPIs and how data supports operational decisions.
  • Awareness of continuous improvement and customer‑focused service design.

Experience

  • Experience building effective working relationships across teams.
  • Operational experience within a service delivery environment, ideally high volume or complex.
  • Experience supporting team delivery or coaching colleagues (formal line management not essential).
  • Experience contributing to change activity, service improvements or process updates.
  • Experience handling escalations and applying sound judgement within policy.
  • Experience producing clear reports or operational updates for managers.
  • Experience monitoring service performance and contributing to service reviews, reporting, or governance activities.

Behaviours

We'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:

  • Managing a Quality Service
  • Communicating and Influencing

Technical skills

We'll assess you against these technical skills during the selection process:

  • Awareness of service management principles and quality assurance frameworks.
  • Experience building effective working relationships across teams.
  • Experience contributing to change activity, service improvements or process updates.

Alongside your salary of £39,865, FCDO Services contributes £11,548 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

title: Division Head, Pediatric Pain & Palliative Care - Full Time - Hartford, CT
description:
The Division Head of Pain & Palliative responsibilities will include a combination of administrative, clinical, research and educational duties. The Division head is responsible for the overall day to day management of a broad range of clinical and educational activities, administrative and strategic efforts. This role will provide visionary and innovative leadership to guide the division into the next phase of growth and development while ensuring the delivery of superior and comprehensive fetal care.

The Division Head will be expected to recruit and develop a team of Physicians, Advanced Practice Providers and health care staff of the Division and work collaboratively with other Divisions in carrying out the mission of the Organization. Additionally, the Division Head will be responsible for encouraging academic advancement within the Division as well as monitoring overall divisional budget, strategy and fostering an environment of professionalism.

The position may also be considered for a part-time FTE, depending on the candidate’s needs and primary area of specialty.

Leadership and Management Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute a strategic vision for the division while building and enhancing the division's clinical enterprise.
  • Work collaboratively with administration and other divisions to build the fetal care center
  • Provides leadership, medical oversight, clinical supervision and implementation of exceptional health care delivery systems for the hospital.
  • Develops and implements departmental goals, plans, and standards consistent with the clinical, administrative, legal, and all Joint Commission, and DPH Health Care Quality standards.
  • Works collaboratively, mentors and oversees the medical director, if the division has a medical director
  • Implements systems and/or programs that address quality while supporting quality improvement projects that are consistent with Joint Commission standards.
  • Foster collaboration within the department and interdepartmentally.
  • Fosters collaboration and strategic relationships with regional hospital systems and providers
  • Create and foster an environment that encourages the professional growth, development and success of faculty including utilizing mentoring, coaching and training.
  • Participate in education of students, residents, and fellows, including their development.
  • Participate in clinical, research and mentor other faculty in research pathways.
  • Plans and monitors staffing activities, including retaining, evaluating, engagement, recognition, disciplinary actions, hiring of diverse faculty and staff and continuing education initiatives.
  • Ensures that medical staff and other employees adhere to appropriate billing and coding procedures.
  • Participates as an active member in all appropriate Hospital administrative and clinical care
    committees as assigned.
  • Maintain fiscal responsibility and financial growth.
  • Maintain the requirements for an academic appointment at the University of Connecticut School of Medicine.

Clinical Responsibilities

  • Perform clinical duties of a Pain & Palliative Physician.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Supervisory Responsibilities:
Yes

Education and/or Experience Required:

  • Graduate from accredited school of medicine required.
  • MD or DO Degree.
  • Greater than 10 years of progressively complex administrative experience in an academic medical center setting.
  • 7 years leadership experience in population-based high quality care, medical management, complex system management, clinical quality improvement and strategic planning.
  • Outstanding record of achievement in an academic medical center as a clinician, educator, investigator and academic medical administrator.

License and/or Certification Required:

  • Must possess current unrestricted license to practice in the State of CT and must be maintained thereafter.
  • DEA with Controlled Substance required and must be maintained thereafter.
  • Board certified/board eligible in Pediatric Pain Medicine, Palliative Care.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Required:

Knowledge of:

  • Posses strong clinical and academic background.
  • Possess knowledge, understanding and advancement of medical science, education, and the provision of healthcare for medically ill patients.
  • Maintain CME units based on the requirements of the specifying Board, as well as maintain all licensure requirements
  • Strong leadership experience and proven commitment to investigation.

Skills:

  • Outstanding clinical and teaching skills.
  • Communication skills needed to present goals clearly.
  • Strong oral and written communication skills.
  • Apply current knowledge to the interpretation and organization of data gathered through the assessment process.

Ability To:

  • Be team-oriented.
  • Ability to work effectively with patients from diverse social, cultural and economic groups.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with a multidisciplinary team.
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively with children, adolescents, and families.
  • Passion for developing state-of-the-art services and research activities.
  • Strong business sense and ability to responsibly manage the human, material, and financial resources.

title: Senior Public Appointments Advisor
company: Department for Culture, Media and Sport
description:
• Job grade: Senior Executive Officer
  • Contract type: Fixed term, Loan, Secondment
  • Length of employment: 2 years
  • Business area: DCMS - Private Office - Corporate Strategy and Private Office
  • Type of role: Administration / Corporate Support
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time, Job share
  • Number of jobs available: 1

Location

Manchester

About the job

Job summary

DCMS is responsible for 44 public bodies, delivering important public functions at arm’s length from government. They include some of the UK’s most high-profile cultural, media and sporting organisations, such as the V&A, Tate, the British Museum, the BBC, BFI, UK Sport and Sport England, as well as regulators and advisory bodies.

The Appointments Team manages more than 450 appointments to the boards of these organisations. Public appointments are regulated and highly scrutinised, and the team works closely with Ministers, No.10, Cabinet Office, senior leaders and our public bodies to deliver fair and effective appointment processes.

Our role is to attract and appoint talented people from a diverse range of backgrounds, helping to ensure DCMS public bodies have strong boards that can deliver for people across the UK.

Job description

We are seeking a proactive and highly motivated individual to lead high-profile public appointment campaigns for some of DCMS’s most important public bodies.

You will oversee complex campaigns, support colleagues and provide high-quality advice to Ministers, No.10 and senior stakeholders. You will also lead key areas of the team’s wider work, including risk management, background checks and Parliamentary correspondence, while supporting continuous improvement across the team.

This is a varied and interesting role, offering the opportunity to work across the breadth of the DCMS portfolio and build relationships with a wide range of stakeholders across DCMS, our public bodies and wider government. You will work on high-profile issues, often at pace, and play an important role in ensuring our public appointment processes are efficient, effective and able to withstand external scrutiny.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead high-profile and strategically important public appointment campaigns, ensuring they are delivered effectively and can withstand external scrutiny.
  • Support innovation and continuous improvement across the Public Appointments Team, including the automation of routine tasks.
  • Review and improve internal processes in line with Ministerial and Cabinet Office requirements.
  • Lead the team’s work on BPSS and due diligence checks, Parliamentary Questions and risk management.

Person specification

The ideal candidate would have the following key skills and experience, please note that desirable skills will only be used in the vent of tied candidates:

Essential requirements:

  • Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and adapt flexibly to shifting high-level strategic and senior stakeholder priorities.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to deliver clear, accurate advice and manage workloads effectively to meet tight deadlines.
  • Ability to build and maintain effective relationships with a wide range of stakeholders.
  • A commitment to continuous improvement and delivering a positive stakeholder experience.

Desirable Skills:

  • Experience of public appointments or working with public bodies.
  • Experience of risk management.
  • Line management experience.

We are running an information session where prospective applicants can find out more about the role. This will be hosted by Aidan Teare, and will take place on:

  • 12:30pm Thursday 22 October 2026

The session will be an opportunity to hear more about the role, the team and wider directorate and the department. It will also be an opportunity for you to ask any questions.

Please register your interest by filling out this Registration form and you will be sent an invitation. Invites will only be sent after this deadline has passed.

Please note that the session will not be recorded and will not focus on the DCMS recruitment process - please direct any queries that you have on this topic (timelines, reasonable adjustments, onboarding etc) to resourcing.team@dcms.gov.uk

Behaviours

We'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:

  • Delivering at Pace
  • Seeing the Big Picture
  • Communicating and Influencing
  • Making Effective Decisions

We only ask for evidence of these behaviours on your application form:

  • Communicating and Influencing

Benefits

DCMS values its staff and offers a wide range of benefits to everyone who works here. We’re committed to developing talent, and supporting colleagues to have great careers in our department. To support with that, some of the benefits we offer include:

  • Flexible working arrangements and hybrid working - DCMS staff work on a flexible basis with time spent in offices, and time spent working from home

  • 26.5 days annual leave on entry, increasing to 31.5 days after 5 years’ service

  • A Civil Service pension with an employer contribution of 28.97%

  • Access to the Edenred employee benefits system which offers discounts to popular retailers and access to various useful resources such as financial and savings advice

  • 3 days of paid volunteering leave

  • Up to 9 months maternity leave on full pay + generous paternity and adoption leave

  • Staff reward and recognition bonuses that operate throughout the year

  • Occupational sick pay

  • Access to the Employee Assistance Programme which offers staff 24/7 confidential support and resources such as counselling, debt guidance and management advice

  • Active and engaged staff networks to join including the LGBT+, Ethnic Diversity, Mental Health and Wellbeing and Gender Equality Networks

  • Exceptional learning and development opportunities that you can explore alongside your day to day work

  • Season ticket loan, cycle to work scheme and much more!

Terms and conditions at SCS grades will vary. Those applying for SCS roles should refer to the candidate information pack for more information on terms and conditions.

Things you need to know

Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Selection process details

This vacancy is using Success Profiles (opens in a new window), and will assess your Behaviours, Strengths and Experience.

To apply for this vacancy, you will need to submit the following documents which will assessed against the experience success profile:

  • A CV setting out your career history, with key responsibilities and achievements. Please ensure you provide employment history that relates to the essential and desirable criteria, and that any gaps in employment history within the last 2 years are explained. The CV should not exceed more than 2 x A4 pages and you should insert your CV into the "Job History" section on the Civil Service Jobs application form.

  • A Statement of Suitability (max 750 words) explaining how you consider your personal skills, qualities and experience provide evidence of your suitability for the role in reference to the essential requirements highlighted. You may also choose to reference the desirable skills listed however these will not be considered in the assessment of your application except in circumstances where there are a high number and calibre of candidates.

  • A Behaviour Statement (max 250 words) detailing an example of when you have used Communicating and Influencing.

For the shortlist, we will select applicants demonstrating the best fit for the role by considering the evidence provided in your application.

In the event of a large number of applicants, an initial sift will be conducted on the behaviour statement. Those who are successful in the initial sift will then be scored on all elements of the application.

For support in writing your application and interviewing, please refer to the ‘Application and Interview Guidance’ document attached to the job advert.

The interview process will assess behaviours and strengths.

The behaviours to be tested at interview are:

  • Delivering at Pace
  • Seeing the Big Picture
  • Communicating and Influencing
  • Making Effective Decisions

Prior to the interview you will be sent the behaviour questions in advance.

You will also be required to prepare a presentation. Full details of this, including the topic, length of time, and whether or not you will need to use visual aids, will be sent to you prior to your interview.

You will not be made aware of the strengths being assessed prior to your interview.

Your interview will take place remotely via Teams.

For indicative sift and interview dates please refer to the attached Candidate Information Pack.

Further Information

If the vacancy is offered as FTA/Loan, existing Civil Servants must join on a Loan basis only. Prior agreement to be released on loan must be obtained before commencing the application process. In the case of Civil Servants, the terms of the loan will be agreed between the home and host department and the Civil Servant. This includes grade on return.

Any move to Department for Culture, Media and Sport from another employer will mean you can no longer access childcare vouchers. This includes moves between government departments. You may however be eligible for other government schemes, including Tax Free Childcare. Determine your eligibility at

New entrants are expected to join on the minimum of the pay band.

DCMS has a London and a National pay scale. For more information on this, including the circumstances in which each pay scale will apply, please see the ‘Candidate Information Pack’ attached.

If successful and transferring from another Government Department a criminal record check may be carried out.

In order to process applications without delay, we will be sending a Criminal Record Check to Disclosure and Barring Service on your behalf. However, we recognise in exceptional circumstances some candidates will want to send their completed forms direct. If you will be doing this, please advise Government Recruitment Service of your intention by emailing Pre-EmploymentChecks.grs@cabinetoffice.gov.uk stating the job reference number in the subject heading.

Applicants who are successful at interview will be, as part of pre-employment screening, subject to a check on the Internal Fraud Database (IFD). About the job

Job summary

Accurate financial reporting is essential to understanding how Britain’s energy networks perform and ensuring they deliver value for consumers. Ofgem is looking for a Regulatory Financial Reporting Analyst to develop their financial expertise whilst supporting effective regulation and investment across the energy sector.

Ofgem is Great Britain’s independent energy regulator. We’re at the forefront of change across the energy sector, driving toward Net Zero whilst protecting energy consumers – especially vulnerable people.

This is a permanent opportunity for a finance professional looking to take their career in an exciting new direction. You’ll have the chance to contribute to important work that supports investment across Britain’s energy networks, making a meaningful difference whilst building your experience in a regulatory environment.

You’ll join a friendly and inclusive team of financial experts, gaining exposure to a wide range of knowledge, skills and professional backgrounds. With the opportunity to learn from experienced colleagues and get involved in varied and engaging work, you’ll be enabled to broaden your capabilities, develop new perspectives and build a strong foundation for your future career.

Job description

We’re looking for a finance professional who holds or is working towards a recognised qualification, such as CCAB, CFA or an MSc in Finance, or has relevant finance or commercial experience demonstrated through previous performance and achievements. You’ll bring good quantitative and qualitative financial analytical skills, including the ability to analyse complex situations and policy decisions, alongside knowledge of accounting statements and interpreting financial information. Experience of building internal and external relationships at all levels and the ability to communicate complex financial information to different audiences will also be essential.

In return, you’ll have the opportunity to build your skills and experience in a supportive environment, making a meaningful contribution whilst developing your career. Alongside this, you’ll enjoy a rewarding package of benefits designed to support your wellbeing, work-life balance and future.

We have a critical purpose to protect energy consumers whilst enabling vital investment across the sector. Join us and help ensure financial reporting provides the clarity, scrutiny and evidence needed to support sound regulatory decisions.

Ofgem can offer you a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes; 30 days annual leave after 2 years; Excellent training and development opportunities; The opportunity to join the generous Civil Service pension which also includes a valuable range of benefits; hybrid working (currently 1 day a week in the office but this is kept under review), flexible working hours and family friendly policies. Plus lots of other benefits including clean and bright offices based centrally, engaged networks and teams and an opportunity to contribute to our ambitious and important targets of establishing a Net Zero energy system by 2050. This exciting blend of professional challenge and personal reward identifies career opportunities at Ofgem as something to get excited about.

About the Electoral Commission

The Electoral Commission is the UK’s independent body overseeing elections and regulating political finance. Everything we do is about ensuring trust, participation, and integrity in the democratic process.

As we enter a bold new chapter under our five-year Corporate Plan, we are increasing our workforce and transforming how we plan and deliver core services. This post plays a central role in that journey.

Job description

About the role

We are looking for a skilled content designer to play an important role in improving the content on our website, making it clearer, more consistent and easier for people to use.

You will design content that enables everyone to take part in democracy, ensuring it is user‑centred, accessible and inclusive.

A key part of your role will be redesigning content and user journeys as part of our website improvement project. This will involve reviewing, redesigning and restructuring content so it’s based on evidence, user needs and data.

Working closely with the content team, subject-matter experts and external partners, you will help to modernise how content is created, managed and governed across the website.

You will:

  • Lead the design, testing and iteration of high‑quality website content
  • Use analytics, research and user insight to guide content decisions
  • Collaborate with teams across the Commission to improve complex information
  • Help establish content standards, patterns and governance for the website
  • Mentor colleagues and champion user‑centred content design across the organisation

This is an exciting and high‑impact role where your expertise will directly shape how millions of people access trusted, democratic information.

About the team

You will join our Digital Communications team; a collaborative and forward-thinking group committed to delivering user-centred digital services. We value creativity, inclusivity, and continuous improvement.

You’ll also be working alongside the Commission’s first in house digital service delivery team, who are building our postcode lookup service. This is a fantastic opportunity collaborate, share skills and learn as part of a multidisciplinary team working on a service used by over 40 million people.

We’re looking for someone who can combine strong content design skills with the ability to build good relationships and influence others. You’ll be confident using user research and data to shape decisions and explain your thinking clearly.

You’ll enjoy being part of a small, supportive team, working on a range of projects, and helping to drive positive change across the organisation.

Essential skills and experience include:

  • Experience delivering user‑centred content for large, public‑facing websites

title: Sr. Systems Reliability Engineer
description:
At Zone 5 Technologies, we're redefining what's possible in unmanned aircraft systems. Our team of engineers and innovators is developing cutting-edge autonomous solutions that push the boundaries of UAS technology - solving complex challenges that matter.

We're building the future of UAS capabilities, and we're looking for exceptional talent to join us. If you're driven by hard problems, energized by rapid innovation, and ready to make an impact on next-generation flight systems, you belong here.

We are seeking a Senior Systems Reliability Engineer to lead Reliability & Maintainability (R&M) activities across the product lifecycle. This role focuses on R&M architecture, data-driven analysis, comprehensive documentation, and test planning for reliability verification. You will engage directly with customer counterparts on R&M reviews and milestone events, including Reliability Scoring Conferences, Corrective Action Boards, and Milestone B/C Design Reviews.

Key Responsibilities:

Reliability & Maintainability Architecture

  • Develop and maintain the R&M Program Plan and reliability architecture documentation, including the RAM-C (Reliability, Availability, Maintainability-Cost) Rationale Report
  • Lead Failure Modes, Effects, and Criticality Analysis (FMEA/FMECA), Fault Tree Analysis (FTA), and Reliability Block Diagram (RBD) development across system architecture
  • Develop R&M allocations and apportion reliability and maintainability requirements to lower-level items; support R&M requirements analysis and trade studies
  • Draft Reliability Predictions (per MIL-HDBK-217 and related methods) and Maintainability Analyses; maintain traceability between R&M requirements, predictions, and demonstrated performance
  • Lead Reliability-Centered Maintenance (RCM) and Level of Repair Analysis (LORA); support Testability and Built-In Test (BIT) analysis

Data, Documentation & Test Planning

  • Establish and own the Failure Reporting, Analysis, and Corrective Action System (FRACAS); maintain closed-loop failure data collection and trending from design through test, production, and sustainment
  • Develop Failure Definitions and Scoring Criteria (FDSC) and reliability test plans tied to program milestones
  • Lead reliability growth planning and execution of reliability growth and demonstration testing, including Environmental Stress Screening (ESS) and HALT/HASS where applicable
  • Support Qualification Test Plan development, all-up-round testing, and flight and live-fire test reliability assessments
  • Develop technical documentation including R&M standards, specifications, procedures, and user guides
  • Review ground test, flight test, and live-fire test data to confirm R&M requirements compliance

Customer Engagement & Reviews

  • Serve as primary point of contact with customers on R&M matters
  • Present R&M analyses, RAM-C Rationale Report updates, and risk posture at Milestone Reviews (A/B/C) and design reviews (PDR, CDR, TRR, PRR)
  • Lead Reliability Scoring Conferences and Corrective Action Boards (CAB) with customer participation
  • Coordinate responses to customer R&M data item deliverables and support In-Service Reviews

Risk Management & Process Improvement

  • Lead Root Cause and Corrective Action (RCCA) investigations for failures identified through FRACAS
  • Host corrective action reviews and ensure lessons learned are implemented across the program
  • Coordinate R&M risk mitigation with Manufacturing Engineering, Logistics, Quality, and System Safety, including DMSMS/obsolescence and shelf-life and aging surveillance considerations
  • Apply digital engineering and AI-enabled tools (predictive maintenance, digital twins, automated FRACAS analytics) to R&M processes
  • Ensure compliance with MIL-STD-785, MIL-HDBK-217, GEIA-STD-0009, and other applicable R&M standards

Basic Qualifications:

  • 7+ years as a Reliability Engineer, R&M Engineer, or equivalent reliability-critical engineering role
  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Aerospace, Systems, or Electrical Engineering, or Physics
  • Expertise with MIL-STD-785, MIL-HDBK-217, and related R&M standards
  • Experience owning FRACAS, including failure tracking, root cause analysis, and corrective action closure
  • Proven experience developing and executing reliability test plans, including growth testing, demonstration testing, and Environmental Stress Screening
  • Experience engaging with customers on R&M reviews and milestone/design reviews (PDR, CDR, Milestone B/C)
  • Strong system architecture knowledge and R&M requirements decomposition and allocation
  • Extensive FMEA/FMECA, FTA, and RBD experience
  • Failure investigation with proven corrective action implementation
  • Technical writing for R&M program plans, rationale reports, procedures, and documentation
  • Design review experience (PDR, CDR, MRR) with strong presentation skills
  • Data collection, analysis, and trending for R&M metrics
  • U.S. Citizenship

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master's degree in engineering or related field
  • 10+ years progressive R&M experience
  • ASQ Certified Reliability Engineer (CRE) or equivalent certification
  • DoD or Navy R&M programs experience, aligned with SECNAV Reliability and Maintainability Engineering guidance
  • Quantitative reliability growth modeling (e.g., Crow-AMSAA) and Weibull analysis
  • Maintainability, Testability/BIT, LORA, and RCM experience
  • Missile, hypersonic, or munitions systems experience, including all-up-round reliability, environmental stress screening, and shelf-life/stockpile surveillance programs
  • Digital engineering and AI-enabled R&M tools (predictive maintenance, digital twins, automated FRACAS analytics)
  • Active U.S. Security Clearance or ability to obtain

About the job

Job summary

Homes England is looking for a Content Designer to create, evaluate, update and review content across the end-to-end user journey on GOV.UK and other digital platforms. You will join the User Centred Design team, a passionate and highly skilled group dedicated to improving how Homes England delivers content on GOV.UK, within a fast-growing national organisation with a strong social purpose.

Job description

This is a hands-on content design role that combines technical skill with a strong user-centred approach, ensuring that everything we publish is clear, accessible and effective in helping people understand and act on our services and policies. Working with key stakeholders, policy teams and regional teams, you will help ensure publications are efficient, consistent and effective, meeting accessibility and Government Digital Service standards and supporting Homes England's wider commitment to inclusive communications. You will apply content standards and style guidelines consistently and contribute to the wider cross-government content community.

You will support the design and delivery of key strategic projects, including the National Housing Bank, the Social and Affordable Homes Programme, the Cladding Safety Scheme and the Capital Funding Guide. This is a role focussed on developing guidance and organisational information content as opposed to service screens and requires experience working in Whitehall Publisher CMS.

Please review the full job description in the supporting documents before applying for the role.

Person specification

You'll be comfortable supporting the agency with complex publishing issues, and committed to making content available in an easy-to-understand, plain English and accessible way.

You'll be proficient in the principles of content design, confident using evidence, data and research to inform content decisions, and skilled at building relationships across the agency with a focus on user needs. You'll also engage with and contribute to the wider cross-government content community.

Delivering on a mission as bold as ours isn't always easy, so you'll be resilient and comfortable managing stakeholders, with a good understanding of the operational impact of what we do as a Communications Team. You'll enjoy working in an innovative, fun and engaging way, and be confident negotiating and persuading others.

As an experienced content design professional, you'll know how to guide and support colleagues, and demonstrate that you can work with others as part of a team in a collaborative, inclusive way.

You will have experience in...

Creating, evaluating, updating and reviewing content across end to end journeys

Working on content in GOV.UK

Applying a user centred approach to content design

Working on complex publishing issues

Working in Whitehall publisher CMS

Benefits

Homes England is an executive non-departmental public body with its own terms and conditions, benefits and pension scheme. We are a government agency working in partnership with the private sector and want to employ and retain great people. In return we offer a range of excellent benefits, some of the key benefits include:

Holiday - Homes England offers all staff 33 days annual leave per year in addition to 8 statutory bank holidays.

Working Flexibly - At Homes England we have a strong culture of flexible working and encourage all employees to have a healthy work/life balance. We offer a wide range of potential working patterns, including part time, job share and compressed hours.

Health and Wellbeing - We offer health screening with Nuffield Proactive Health Clinics, a free Employee Assistance Programme which offers confidential support 24 hours a day, 7 days a week as well as access to Occupational Health.

Professional Development - At Homes England we are committed to your continued professional and personal development with learning as one of our core values. We pay for one job-related professional membership subscription per year for our employees.

We also offer an excellent range of family friendly benefits, for example, maternity, paternity, shared parental leave.

Every year our systems support up to 3 million visa applications, checks on 100 million border crossings, up to 8 million passport applications and deliver 140 million police checks on people, vehicles and property.

As a Senior Response Manager within the Home Office Cyber Security Operations Centre (CSOC) you will be expected to plan, implement and operate capabilities to detect, contain and remediate incidents, identify opportunities to improve detection, response and automation capabilities. You will also support organisational readiness through co-ordinating preparedness exercises and red team activity. The Response function also advises product and service owners on potential mitigations and supports the continuous improvement of security operations through monitoring, detection and standardisation of security practices.

You’ll be joining an expert team of cyber professionals, committed to reducing the exposure to cyber-attack of new and existing digital systems. You’ll be aided in your role by a diverse and supportive organisational culture, and a commitment to further your continuous development.

Where business needs allow, some roles may be suitable for a combination of office and home-based working. Where this is the case, employees will be expected to spend a minimum of 60% of their working time in the office. Applicants can raise any queries to the email address at the bottom of the advert.

Watch this short video to hear from members of Home Office Digital talking about the projects they work on and their experience of working here: Working for Home Office Digital.

Job description

We are seeking a Senior Response Manager to join the Cyber Security Operations Centre (CSOC) as a Senior SOAR & Detection-as-Code (DaC) Analyst. This role focuses on improving cyber detection, response and automation capabilities through security automation, response playbooks and Detection-as-Code practices. You will design, develop, test, maintain and improve security automation workflows, response playbooks and integrations using SOAR platforms or comparable automation technologies, while applying structured and repeatable DaC methodologies.

You will work with SOC teams and other business areas to improve incident handling, implement complex solutions for emerging threats, contribute to relevant standards and process improvements, and reduce operational effort and future risk.

As a Senior Response Manager your main responsibilities will be to;

  • Carry out security monitoring, detection and response activities in line with agreed standards, providing advice on mitigation, escalation and risk reduction.
  • Identify, analyse and investigate indicators of malicious activity across networks, systems and applications, supporting effective threat detection and incident response.
  • Triage security events and alerts, supporting investigations and recommending improvements to monitoring controls, detection coverage and overall security posture.
  • Support incident response activities, including red teaming and threat hunting exercises, communicating investigation outcomes and contributing to lessons learned and post-incident reviews.
  • Develop, review and continuously improve monitoring use cases, detection content and alert effectiveness across a range of security technologies.
  • Define and enhance processes, tooling and security controls to identify emerging threats, strengthen detection capabilities and implement effective mitigation strategies.
  • Drive service and process improvements by applying industry best practice, sound judgement and problem-solving skills to support efficient security operations and investigations.

Working Pattern

This role is available on a full-time basis with the option of compressed hours working. This role is also suitable for part-time working hours, with a minimum requirement to work 4 days/ 30 hours per week due to business requirements.

Person specification

Essential Skills

You will have a demonstrable passion for Cyber Security, Detection and Response with the following skills, knowledge or experience;

  • Conducting investigations and working in a ‘Security Operations Centre’ environment, supporting security operations and incident response activities.
  • Designing, developing, testing maintaining and improving security automation workflows, response playbooks and integrations using SOAR platforms or comparable automation technologies, while applying DaC methodologies.
  • Communicating in a verbal and written manner, and a good understanding of the use of different channels and formats for different audiences.
  • Building strong partnerships with peers across an organisation and navigating the complex landscape of technologies, 3rd party suppliers, and other teams.
  • Managing a team in a technical environment.

    2. Personal statement - this should present a clear and coherent narrative explaining why you are applying, what you would bring to the role, and how your experience meets the essential criteria. description:

Location

About the job

Job summary

At FCDO Services we protect the UK’s interests at home and overseas. We design and construct secure government buildings and courier diplomatic packages worldwide, safeguard government tech and a whole lot more. Our work is as varied and vital as it gets, but we never lose sight of our people. Their skills, aspirations and growth mean as much as the global mission we’re on. In our world, it all matters.

Job description

The success of a government project can depend on secure, timely shipments and our Logistics team always deliver the goods. From dedicated drivers to King's Messengers, they've delivered to over 250 destinations worldwide, moving over a million kilograms of freight annually across land, air, and sea. Now, you've got the opportunity to join them.

Delivering globally.

Dispatching each shipment with care.

Seeing your impact go further.

It all matters.

Support the teams of couriers and messengers that keep the UK safe and secure

When you join us in this important role you’ll take the lead on the day-to-day organisation of our London Car Service, managing and processing bookings and requests, allocating drivers and vehicles, and working with the finance team to ensure that timings are recorded accurately. Taking responsibility for you and your team’s training and development, and defining roles, recruiting suitable personnel, managing performance and coaching your less experienced colleagues, whilst responding efficiently, discreetly and professionally to all the communications you receive.

Prioritising, annotating, flagging and forwarding correspondence that comes into the office, and responding quickly to your customers’ requests, you’ll ensure scheduled maintenance work is carried out to the fleet’s vehicles, daily check sheets are completed, and ad hoc work is handled correctly. We’ll also expect you to make sure the members of your team keep their professional qualifications up to date, maintain productive relationships with all the stakeholders you work with, and hold regular team meetings to address any issues that impact on you and your colleagues’ responsibilities.

Use all your skills of discretion and diplomacy as you support our global mission

To be a success in this significant and busy role you must be highly organised, possess strong line management experience within a time critical and high-pressure environment, and be a clear and confident communicator. With well developed judgement, tact and diplomatic skills, and able to handle sensitive information with discretion and confidentiality, you should also be capable of maintaining the confidence of your colleagues at all levels of our organisation. It’s important that you have previous experience of fleet resource scheduling and the planning skills to maximise utilisation, while an understanding of London and the UK’s road network, and airside and freight forwarding operations would be desirable.

It goes without saying that excellent customer service and team leadership skills area essential, and if you don’t already hold it, you must be prepared to gain DV level security clearance. A highly proficient user of Microsoft Office and SharePoint, you’ll be at an advantage if you hold Lean Six-Sigma Yellow Belt certification and possess some knowledge and understanding of the structure and key personnel within FCDO and FCDO Services. Candidates should also be aware that while working with Ministerial Private Offices, the King’s Messengers and a number of other high profile customers, we’ll expect you to be available for out of hours calls and requests.

Discover the support you need to grow your career further

But we’re always looking to improve – just like you. That’s why when you join us, expect to receive a competitive salary, generous holiday entitlement and a Civil Service Pension. Along with this, you’ll also have access to training and other development opportunities to help grow your career with us. Our offices have an on-site gym, nursery, café, and restaurant, and we offer interest-free loans on season tickets and bikes to help you get there. It's a great set of benefits made to support all you do, and all you need.

Want to see your future team’s work in action? Step into our Virtual Embassy and select a guide to take you round to see how we deliver for government customers and how you could help. Explore the embassy now at virtual-embassy.fcdoservicescareers.co.uk

Every single colleague must be security cleared before joining us. If you’re successful in your application, we’ll ask you to undergo our vetting process to achieve Developed Vetting (DV) clearance. You can find out more about vetting at fcdoservicescareers.co.uk/how-to-apply/

To find out more about our benefits and our organisation, please visit fcdoservicescareers.co.uk

It takes a diverse team to protect a diverse world

The vital work we do takes an incredible community of colleagues, with different skills, backgrounds, cultures and identities. We support every individual, so that you always know you’re welcome and valued. It’s what makes us a Disability Confident employer. And why we’re recognised as a ‘Carer Confident’ workplace. And it’s how you know you’re joining an inspiring, inclusive organisation.

  • Clear and concise communication skills – written and verbal to be able to communicate with colleagues at all levels.
  • Good judgement, tact and diplomatic skills – ability to deliver difficult messages and maintain the confidence of colleagues at all levels, handling sensitive information with discretion and confidentiality.

title: Associate Director for Assessment Integrity and Innovation
company: Ofqual (Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation)
description:
• Job grade: Grade 6
  • Contract type: Permanent
  • Business area: OFQUAL - Strategy
  • Type of role: Senior leadership, Strategy, Other
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time, Job share, Part-time
  • Number of jobs available: 1

Location

Coventry, West Midlands (England), CV1 2GN

About the job

Job summary

Ofqual is the independent qualifications regulator for England. We currently regulate 200+ awarding organisations, and approx. 11,600 certified qualifications.

These include GCSEs, AS and A levels, and a broad range of vocational and technical qualifications.

For more information about the work we do please visit our website and our Careers Pages and

The Assessment Integrity and Innovation team works on some of the most important and fast-moving issues facing qualifications and assessment. Our work spans artificial intelligence and emerging technologies, assessment integrity and test security, and innovation across the qualifications sector.

We are a collaborative and forward-looking team, working across Ofqual and with government, awarding organisations, regulators, technology providers and external experts. We bring together different perspectives and expertise to understand emerging opportunities and risks and help shape proportionate, evidence-led regulatory responses.

It is an exciting time to join us. Technology is developing rapidly, creating new possibilities for how qualifications are designed and delivered, alongside new challenges for maintaining assessment integrity, standards and public confidence.

Job description

As Associate Director for Assessment Integrity and Innovation, you will take a leading role in shaping Ofqual’s response to these challenges and opportunities.

You will lead high-profile strategic projects covering AI, emerging technology, assessment integrity and innovation, turning complex and developing issues into clear regulatory approaches. You will advise senior leaders and Board, build relationships with experts and organisations across the sector, and work with colleagues across Ofqual to tackle complex, strategic issues.

We are looking for someone who enjoys tackling complex problems, can see the bigger picture and is comfortable working in areas where the answers are not always obvious. You will be able to build strong relationships, bring different perspectives together and communicate complex ideas clearly and persuasively.

You do not need to have followed one particular career path to succeed in this role. We value different experiences, perspectives and ways of thinking, and we want someone who is curious, collaborative and excited by the opportunity to help shape the future of qualifications and assessment.

Person specification

Please refer to the job description attached for a full list of essential criteria to support your application.

Qualifications

A level 6 qualification such as an honours degree or experience in a similar role, demonstrating the ability to apply specialist knowledge and expertise

Behaviours

We'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:

  • Seeing the Big Picture
  • Communicating and Influencing
  • Working Together
  • Delivering at Pace

Technical skills

We'll assess you against these technical skills during the selection process:

  • Understanding of the evolving potential and use of technology in assessment
  • Understanding of the role of regulation to both safeguard the use of technology, while enabling effective innovation

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £71,262, Ofqual (Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation) contributes £20,644 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

As a Civil Servant, you will benefit from a leading, modern employment offer which includes flexible working arrangements that support people at different stages in their lives, and pensions among the best available in the UK, as well as generous annual leave entitlements.

Other benefits you can enjoy include:

  • Organisational performance related bonus
  • Cycle-to-work scheme
  • Regular professional development
  • Health and wellbeing initiatives such as mini-medicals, flu vaccinations
  • Employee assistance programme and occupational health
  • Free eye tests and contribution towards lenses/spectacles for VDU users, if appropriate
  • Family friendly policies
  • Interest free rail season ticket loan
  • Access to exclusive discounts
  • Free car parking

We are committed to promoting Equality, Diversity, Inclusion and Wellbeing throughout the organisation. We are proud of the action we are taking to support this. We welcome applications from individuals from all backgrounds to support our ethos of creating a diverse culture that is reflective of both our employees and the learners we support.

Due to our continued commitment and focus in relation to Equality, Diversity and Inclusion, our inclusion and fair treatment score based on the Civil Service 2024 annual people survey ranks us joint 5th out of 104 participating departments.

Ofqual is a rewarding, dynamic place to work. We offer employees the opportunity to develop within their role and progress through the organisation via a number of Learning and Development opportunities and activities.

Ofqual has a highly engaged workforce. Our 2024 Civil Service People Survey score on engagement was 71%, against 64% for the whole Civil Service, and was the joint 12th highest of the 104 participating CS departments.

About the job

Job summary

Across government, the adoption of artificial intelligence is reshaping how organisations design services, make decisions and deliver outcomes. As AI capabilities expand, the need for robust architectural design becomes critical to ensure solutions are scalable, secure and aligned with both organisational strategy and ethical standards. Ofgem plays a vital role in the UK’s energy system, protecting consumers and enabling a more secure, fair and sustainable energy future, and the responsible use of AI is central to delivering this mission.

Ofgem is on an ambitious transformation journey. Within the Digital, Data and Security Services (DDSS) directorate, we are building a modern data and AI capability to support innovation, improve decision-making and enhance service delivery. This includes designing and deploying AI-driven solutions that are integrated into wider enterprise architecture and governed by strong standards around security, transparency and ethics.

As a Senior Solution Architect (AI), you will lead the design and assurance of AI and data-driven solutions across a range of programmes and services. You will work closely with data scientists, engineers and business stakeholders to ensure that AI systems are scalable, secure and aligned with organisational goals. You will also play a key role in shaping architectural standards and governance, ensuring that AI is implemented responsibly and effectively.

This is a senior role requiring a strong blend of technical expertise, architectural thinking and stakeholder engagement. You will operate across multiple initiatives, balancing strategic direction with hands-on design and assurance responsibilities.

Job description

You will be responsible for:

  • Leading the architectural design and assurance of AI and machine learning solutions, ensuring they meet standards for scalability, security and performance.
  • Ensuring alignment between AI solutions and Ofgem’s enterprise architecture, promoting interoperability and reuse across systems and platforms.
  • Defining and maintaining architecture artefacts and documentation using recognised frameworks such as TOGAF and modern data modelling approaches.
  • Working closely with stakeholders, including data scientists, engineers and business teams, to translate requirements into effective technical designs.
  • Providing architectural governance and assurance, identifying and mitigating risks across multiple programmes and delivery teams.
  • Evaluating emerging AI technologies and recommending solutions that enhance capability while ensuring compliance with ethical and governance frameworks.
  • Supporting the development of AI architecture standards and best practice, promoting responsible and explainable AI across the organisation.
  • Communicating complex architectural concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences, influencing decision-making at senior levels.
  • Coaching and supporting other architects, contributing to capability development and consistency across architecture practices.

We are looking for:

A technically strong and strategically minded architect who can design and assure AI solutions within a complex organisation. You will bring experience of solution architecture, alongside an understanding of AI and data-driven systems, and the ability to influence across a wide range of stakeholders.

You may come from a solution architecture, data architecture or AI engineering background, but you will demonstrate:

  • Experience designing and assuring AI or data-driven solutions within an enterprise environment
  • Strong understanding of enterprise architecture principles and frameworks
  • Knowledge of AI governance, ethical AI and data management considerations
  • The ability to balance technical design with business requirements and strategic priorities
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to influence senior stakeholders and translate complex concepts clearly

Relevant certifications such as Azure AI Engineer, AI Solutions Architect or equivalent architectural qualifications are expected (or willingness to obtain).

Experience designing AI solutions in Azure environments, including tools such as Azure Machine Learning, Copilot Studio or AI Foundry, would be beneficial.

This is an opportunity to play a key role in shaping how Ofgem designs and delivers AI solutions. You will ensure that AI adoption is architecturally sound, scalable and responsible, supporting innovation while maintaining strong governance and trust.

Person specification

Essential Criteria

  • Demonstrates proven experience in designing and assuring AI technical solutions that align with enterprise architecture principles and business objectives. (Lead Criteria)
  • Demonstrates understanding of ethical AI, data governance, and explain ability frameworks within enterprise or public sector contexts. (Lead Criteria)
  • Applies sound understanding of responsible and explainable AI principles to ensure solutions are ethical, secure, and transparent in their operation and outcomes.

Holds or can obtain the following certifications or equivalent within 6 months:

  • Formal Architectural Qualification such as Microsoft Certified Azure AI Engineer Associate, Microsoft Certified Agentic AI Business Solutions Architect or IBM Applied AI Professional.

Desirable Criteria

  • Experienced in designing or deploying AI and machine learning services on Azure, such as Azure Machine Learning Co-pilot, Co-pilot studio and AI foundry.
