Location

London, Manchester

About the job

Job summary

This vacancy is for the recruitment of 3 x SCS Pay band 2 Directors in the Public Safety Group;

  1. Strategy and Operations Director
  2. Policing Policy Director
  3. Crime Director

Please indicate on your application which role you are specifically applying for, or if you would like to be considered for more than 1 role.

You will only be required to submit 1 application and attend 1 interview.

Job description

We are pleased to advise you that Sarah Swinford – Director- Public Safety Group will be hosting a Townhall Event for these roles for prospective candidates on Tuesday 3rd November 2026 at 11:30.

Whilst this is an optional event, all candidates are encouraged to join Sarah to gain an insight into the role(s) . You can join this event by registering at;

Candidate Information session – Public Safety Group, Directors x3 Tickets, Tuesday 3 November • 11:30 AM - 12 PM GMT , Eventbrite

If you have any role related questions that can be reviewed and addressed at the event, please submit these to;

PublicSafetyDG@homeoffice.gov.uk by 5pm on Friday 30th October 2026.

Role 1:

Strategy and Operations Director;

  • The PSG Strategy and Operations Director is a critical member of the leadership team. The post holder will need to have a strong working relationship with central finance, central strategy and HR. Specific responsibilities include:Leadership of the central strategy, risk, corporate and co-ordination functions in PSG and its “route to moderate”.
  • Strengthen alignment between PSG strategy, finance and people to ensure ongoing deployment of resources against the highest priority work. Lead Director for PSG's Spending Review work.
  • Deliver spend within budget and within 1% of P6 forecast (across an overall PSG budget of c.£14bn) and achieving workforce targets.
    Improve PSG compliance with key departmental metrics.
  • Shape and cohere PSG’s key strategic discussions and products including the Permanent Secretary Stocktake process, the PSG Board, risk oversight, strategic finance and workforce oversight.
  • Provide PSG locally delivered corporate functions (security, accommodation, health and safety etc).
    Delivery of key and high-profile elements of the Police Reform portfolio: national police capabilities, police efficiency targets, police performance.
  • The post holder will have 6-7 SCS1 direct reports.
  • Contribute to PSG and the Department’s wider corporate aims and objectives, including membership of the PSG Board and the Home Office senior leadership team. This will include providing out of hours cover as Director on call.

Role 2:

Policing Policy Director;

  • Oversight and responsibility for the governance, accountability and structures of policing, including the role and powers of the Home Secretary and setting her national priorities for policing.
  • Ensure the police have the powers and tools to maintain public order, and that they are used proportionately and appropriately. Implementation of the recommendations from Lord Macdonald’s review of public order and hate crime legislation to address concerns about two-tier policing.
  • Direct personal accountability (SRO) for the Neighbourhood Policing Programme, the government’s flagship commitment to strengthen neighbourhood policing, improve outcomes through the neighbourhood policing guarantee, and increase neighbourhood policing personnel by 13,000.
  • Policy and delivery of reforms to local policing structures including abolition of Police and Crime Commissioners, design and implementation of new local policing governance, and sponsorship of the Independent Review of Force Structures, and delivery of the Police Reform Bill.
  • Oversee the PSG Emergency Response Team, which provides a single information picture and assurance for the Department, Ministers and senior leaders, for all significant emergency incidents impacting upon Public Safety Group areas as well as overseeing preparedness.
  • Responsible for police workforce and professionalism policy, including delivering a new workforce strategy for policing, responding to Lord Blunkett’s Leadership Commission; ensure the wellbeing of the police workforce through the Police Covenant; and supporting Ministers’ decisions on police pay and pensions.
  • Sponsorship of an end-to-end review of the police misconduct system to make it more targeted and effective; delivery of key manifesto commitments to improve trust in policing through strengthening standards such as vetting; handle the Government response to current serious misconduct cases and issues of public concern including the Orgreave Inquiry, and act as a core participant in the Undercover Policing Inquiry.
  • Responsibility for the funding of the 43 police forces in England and Wales, including leading the next spending review for policing, and reform of the police funding formula used to distribute c.£10bn of government funding to align to the changing local and national police structures.
  • Lead the Government’s relationship with national policing bodies including the College of Policing, the Independent Office for Police Conduct; the National Police Chiefs’ Council; the Association of Police and Crime Commissioners; and staff associations.
  • Contribute to PSG and the Department’s wider corporate aims and objectives, including membership of the PSG Board and the Home Office senior leadership team. This will include providing out of hours cover as Director on call.

Role 3:

Crime Director;

  • Leadership of the Government’s strategic approach to reducing crime and protecting the public, driving critical government priorities to reduce crime, improve public safety and build public confidence in our response. Build and lead effective cross-government and external partnerships to deliver a coherent, system-wide approach, championing a transformative approach using all available tools and data.
  • Drive forward the Government’s commitment to halve knife crime over the next decade, including delivery of the most impactful interventions and ensuring public confidence in our approach.
  • Lead on tackling neighbourhood and visible crime, including around anti-social behaviour, street crime, retail crime and our response to prolific offenders. Ensure a coordinated approach across government, policing, and local partners.
  • Focus on crime prevention, in particular for young people, to prevent individuals from entering or becoming trapped in a cycle of offending.
  • Lead the Home Office’s strategic approach to drugs, ensuring a coherent response to drug-related harm and strong alignment with wider government priorities on crime and public safety.
  • Respond rapidly to high profile crime incidents – working together with Ministers and other senior officials to ensure that both short-term and long-term implications are addressed.
  • Ensure effective performance, risk, and financial management across the crime portfolio, using data and evidence to monitor delivery, understand impact and ensure resources are targeted effectively.
  • Be a proactive member of the Public Safety Group Board, contributing to the strategic direction of the Group and ensuring budgetary responsibilities are met and risks are effectively managed.
  • Provide strong leadership to the Crime Directorate, developing a high-performing and inclusive team. Champion continuous improvement and digital capability – including strengthened use of data and AI. The post holder will have six SCS1 direct reports.
  • Contribute to PSG and the Department’s wider corporate aims and objectives, including membership of the PSG Board and the Home Office senior leadership team. This will include providing out of hours cover as Director on call.

Person specification

Essential Criteria:

The successful candidate will need to demonstrate:

  • First rate strategic and systems leadership skills with exceptional political judgement and the ability to build strong relationships with ministers.
  • Experience of delivering and leading at pace and getting things done under pressure.
  • An excellent communicator who is able to inspire and lead staff at all levels.
  • Exceptional stakeholder and partnership management skills. Excellent personal impact, resilience and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build sustainable relationships with a diverse range of partners and influence in order to achieve goals.
  • A significant track record of visible and results-focused leadership which inspires, develops and motivates staff to deliver and thrive.
  • Strong awareness of finance management and delivering value for money, with a demonstrable ability to engage effectively with both finance professionals and senior leaders.
    Experience of acting as the Senior Responsible Owner (SRO) for a major, high-profile programme or portfolio with personal accountability for delivering strategic outcomes, benefits realisation, governance, risk management and successful delivery across complex organisational and stakeholder environments.

Desirable Criteria:

  • Experience of policing, crime and criminal justice issues and operating in a highly scrutinised public environment.
  • Experience of leading in crisis

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £105,000, Home Office contributes £30,418 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).
  • Learning and development tailored to your role
  • An environment with flexible working options
  • A culture encouraging inclusion and diversity
  • A Civil Service pension with an employer contribution of 28.97%

title: Senior Specialist  BESS Economics and Analysis (2L)
description:
The Utility Dispatch Rights (UDR) Procurement team at Con Edison conducts competitive procurements with third party battery energy storage system developers to enter into contracts for up to 15 years during which Con Edison will have the right to dispatch the batteries into NYISO wholesale energy markets. In this role, the chosen candidate would have the opportunity to:

1) Build and run analytical simulations in Excel and other tools and platforms to assess the economics of potential projects for Con Edison, including analysis to help support forecasts and scenarios of wholesale markets.

2) Create models to evaluate tariff rates, wholesale markets and perform other data analysis tasks to support the program.

3) Develop and support subject matter expertise related to:

a. Wholesale market rules, principles, practices and policies.

b. Regulatory frameworks governing infrastructure including energy storage deployment and operation in New York State as well as applicable FERC policies.

c. Roles and use cases for energy storage to enable the clean energy transition.

4) The use and evaluation of company storage evaluation tools.

The chosen candidate will have a unique opportunity to explore the role of batteries authorized under the Utility Dispatch Rights framework in New York. This work will require extensive quantitative work, provide opportunity to develop innovative program structures to assess the value of assets, and to explore how grid, policy, and market constraints may influence asset opportunities. This is a unique and exciting role sitting at the intersection of many key utility functions including storage development, interconnection, operations, strategy, wholesale market scheduling, accounting, engineering, and policy-oriented teams.

  • Analyze the economic value of proposed storage projects using company models and optimization tools and collaborating with company SMEs that schedule assets in NYISO markets

title: Park Ranger - Part time (Parks & Recreation Department)
description:
• New Hires Hourly Starting Rate -$19.21

POSITION SUMMARY:

Park Rangers enforce park ordinances and related regulations, provide park visitors with information and directions, protect park resources, and ensure a positive visitor experience. The Park Ranger is responsible for all safety, security, visitor services, and resource protection in the parks.

POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES:

Essential Functions

The duties and responsibilities of this position include, but are not necessarily limited to:

  • Conducts individual patrols by vehicle, utility vehicle, bicycle, and on foot in various weather conditions.
  • Educates the public about park ordinances and associated regulations, issuing warnings as necessary.
  • Issue warnings or tickets/citations for serious or continuous violations.
  • Preparing for patrol, calling on, obtaining log sheets and any information from the office, gathering necessary equipment, cleaning off and fueling vehicles, and completing all logs, reports, and hours sheets.
  • Present environmental education programming to varied groups of park visitors.
  • Miscellaneous tasks or duties as assigned

MINIMUM EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

  • High School Diploma or (GED).
  • Minimum age of 18 years old
  • Preferred: one year of job-related experience and/or training (i.e., parks & recreation, law enforcement, resource management, education, emergency medicine, and/or customer service).
  • Previous Police, Ranger, or Security experience preferred.
  • Possession of a valid Pennsylvania driver’s license is required.
  • Must possess or can possess current CPR/First Aid certification.
  • Experience with departmental equipment.

MINIMUM KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

  • Excellent positive public relations and customer service skills.
  • Knowledge or the ability to become familiar with PA Criminal Code, Vehicle Code, Parks Code, Civil Law, Labor Law relations, PA Fish and Boat Code, and PA Game Laws
  • Knowledge of EMS, MSDS, fire safety, and environmental issues is an asset.
  • Ability to communicate effectively verbally and grammatically.
  • Ability to recognize liabilities for the County and take immediate action.
  • Adaptability to changing departmental needs and priorities.
  • Ability to deal with potentially dangerous individuals, criminal behavior, resistant individuals, and people with varying mental or physical abilities.
  • Ability to work independently or as part of a team.
  • Basic IBM-compatible skills with Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint.
  • Must obtain PA Act 153 Clearances.
  • Ability to handle stress.
  • Physical presence in the facilities is required.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

  • Ability to work extended hours – sometimes 12-16 hours.
  • Ability to lift 25 lbs., bend, stoop, climb, and reach.
  • Walking, hiking, bicycling at various intervals
  • Ability to aid or lift people in need.
  • Required to wear a department-issued ballistic vest while on patrol.

WORKING ENVIRONMENT:

  • Potential for working in highly hazardous situations when dealing with enforcement issues.
  • Responds to calls in low- or no-light conditions and is usually working alone.
  • Will be required to work outside 80 – 85% of the time (depending on the season) and will be exposed to variable weather conditions.
  • Will work varied shift patterns to ensure park coverage throughout the year, including weekends, holidays, and evenings.

Location

This role is available on a remote, hybrid, or office basis.

Initially, all DBS employees' contracts are office-based at one of our two sites (Liverpool and Darlington). Employees can apply for remote or hybrid work from day one. If approved, the arrangement will start after six months for transfers from Home Office or after completing probation for new joiners. Requests will be considered based on business needs and role requirements. Informal hybrid working arrangements are also available from day one, subject to business needs and role requirements and will be discussed further following any job offer.

About the job

Job summary

The Technology Delivery Office will operate as the Technology &Innovation (T&I) interface to DBS’s corporate demand, portfolio, governance and assurance arrangements.

The Head of Technology Delivery Office will establish and lead the T& I Technology Office, providing a single, consistent approach to managing T&I’s technical delivery commitments and contribution to organisational change. The role will provide clear visibility and control of technical demand, priorities, delivery, resources, dependencies, risks and performance, ensuring that T&I has the capacity and capability to deliver its commitments effectively.

The role will bring together change activity across T&I into a coherent portfolio, supporting proportionate governance, standards and reporting while providing leaders with the insight needed to make informed decisions about priorities, sequencing and resource allocation. Working across T&I and with wider corporate portfolio and change functions, the Head of Technology Office will strengthen technical delivery discipline, identify and resolve constraints, and ensure that technical activities are appropriately planned, resourced, governed, costed and tracked through to successful delivery.

Job description

  • Lead the T&I Technology Office, providing oversight and control of all change activity for which T&I is responsible.
  • Maintain an integrated view of T&I’s delivery commitments, technical pipeline and emerging demand, ensuring demand is understood, assessed, prioritised and aligned to the corporate portfolio plan.
  • Support the T&I Intelligent Client Function (ICF), coordinating functions to establish the requirements, feasibility, impacts, dependencies, costs, risks and resources needed to deliver change
  • Provide T&I leadership and the corporate portfolio function with advice on technical sequencing, delivery constraints, capacity, feasibility, risk and technology investment implications.
  • Maintain an integrated T&I delivery view of technical milestones, resources, dependencies, risks, issues, benefits and technical delivery confidence, providing early intervention where delivery is at risk.
  • Work in partnership with CMBI, using established corporate governance, assurance, reporting and change control arrangements rather than duplicating them.
  • Ensure appropriate business cases, assurance and governance are in place, and that T&I provides the evidence required to support investment and delivery decisions.
  • Lead technology delivery performance and reporting, providing T&I leadership with clear evidence of progress, constraints, emerging risks and decisions required.
  • Establish effective resource and capacity management within T&I, identifying capability gaps and advising on allocation or reprioritisation of resources across the technology portfolio.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships across T&I, CMBI and the wider organisation, resolving cross cutting issues and ensuring clear accountability for delivery.
  • Develop the Technology Delivery Office's management capability, standards and ways of working, aligned to Government Functional Standard

Person specification

Essential Criteria

ABILITY

  • Ability to build effective relationships and work collaboratively with senior leaders, delivery teams, corporate functions and external partners.
  • Ability to lead, motivate and develop multidisciplinary teams, creating clear accountability and a strong focus on delivery.
  • Ability to analyse complex technology delivery information and communicate clear, evidence-based advice, recommendations and decisions to senior audiences.
  • Ability to remain resilient, calm and decisive when managing competing priorities, ambiguity and delivery pressures.
  • Ability to prioritise and sequence change activity, balance demand against capacity, and direct resources to the highest-value outcomes.
  • Ability to identify and resolve technical dependencies, risks, resource constraints and delivery issues through timely intervention and constructive challenge.

EXPERIENCE

  • Demonstrable senior-level experience leading a portfolio, programme or change management office within a large and complex organisation.
  • A strong track record of establishing and applying proportionate governance, assurance, reporting and change controls across a complex portfolio.
  • Experience of managing technical demand and pipelines coordinating the technical assessment of demand, including feasibility, architecture, security, cost, sourcing, dependencies, technical capacity and delivery implications.
  • Experience of providing senior leaders with clear, evidence-based information on technology delivery performance, technical delivery confidence, investment, dependencies, risks and resource allocation.
  • Proven experience of leading and developing multidisciplinary teams to deliver high-quality outcomes and reporting.
  • Experience of maintaining an integrated view of technology delivery commitments, milestones, capacity, costs, dependencies, risks, issues and technical delivery confidence.

TECHNICAL

  • A recognised qualification, accreditation or equivalent professional expertise in technology delivery, digital delivery, portfolio, programme or project management. Strong knowledge and practical application of technology delivery planning and control, technical dependency management, delivery risk and issue management, capacity planning, delivery performance reporting and technical assurance
  • Strong technical knowledge and practical application of portfolio governance, assurance, planning and control, risk and issue management, benefits management, and resource and capability management.

Desirable Criteria

ABILITY

  • Ability to influence and constructively challenge senior stakeholders when priorities, resources or delivery confidence are unclear.
  • Ability to translate complex technical delivery information into clear options and implications for non-technical decision-makers
  • Ability to negotiate priorities and broker solutions across teams with competing demands.

EXPERIENCE

  • Experience of operating within a government, public sector or similarly complex and politically sensitive environment.
  • Experience of working in a safeguarding, regulatory or other high-assurance environment.

TECHNICAL

title: Manager, Data Quality
description:
About Care Access

Care Access is working to make the future of health better for all. With hundreds of research locations, mobile clinics, and clinicians across the globe, we bring world-class research and health services directly to communities that often face barriers to care. We are dedicated to ensuring that every person has the opportunity to understand their health, access the care they need, and contribute to the medical breakthroughs of tomorrow.

With programs like Future of Medicine, which makes advanced health screenings and research opportunities accessible to communities worldwide, and Difference Makers, which supports local leaders to expand their community health and wellbeing efforts, we put people at the heart of medical progress. Through partnerships, technology, and perseverance, we are reimagining how clinical research and health services reach the world. Together, we are building a future of health that is better and more accessible for all.

To learn more about Care Access, visit .

How This Role Makes a Difference

The Manager, Data Quality leads a centralized team of Data Coordinators responsible for accurate, timely, and complete clinical research data across the Care Access site network. The role turns study, sponsor, and organizational requirements into clear operating practices that protect data integrity and reduce administrative burden for site teams.

The Manager guides the team, plans workload, monitors quality, and partners across functions to identify discrepancies early, resolve issues quickly, and keep data reliable for research decisions.

How You'll Make An Impact

  • People Leadership and Team Development: Lead and support Data Coordinators by setting clear expectations, assigning work, coaching performance, and building team capability through training, feedback, and knowledge sharing.
  • Operational Oversight and Capacity Management: Set daily and weekly priorities across assigned studies and sites, balancing team capacity with participant visits, sponsor timelines, monitoring activity, and database milestones. Identify risks early and adjust plans to maintain service levels.
  • Data Quality and Compliance Governance: Maintain quality control practices for source review, EDC/CRF transcription, reconciliation, and documentation. Review performance trends and confirm activities align with protocol, GCP, sponsor requirements, and Care Access procedures.
  • Query and Issue Escalation Management: Track open, aging, and high-risk queries; remove barriers to resolution; and coordinate escalations with site teams, investigators, sponsors, CROs, and internal quality and operational compliance partners. Ensure decisions and follow-up actions are documented in approved systems.
  • Process Improvement and Reporting: Define and monitor site-level metrics for quality, timeliness, workload, and recurring issues. Standardize best practices, improve workflows, and communicate performance trends and risks to leadership.
  • Cross-Functional Partnership: Work with Clinical Operations, Operational Compliance, site leadership, and study teams to align data coordination activities with study requirements and network priorities. Join sponsor, monitoring, and internal operational meetings as needed.
  • Other Responsibilities:
    • Support the rollout of new studies, tools, reports, and process changes.
    • Contribute to audit and inspection readiness by reviewing follow-up items, trends, and quality issues.
    • Take on other duties and special projects that align with the role.

The Expertise Required

  • Strong understanding of clinical research data workflows, including source documentation, EDC/CRF entry, query management, reconciliation, and documentation practices.
  • Ability to lead and develop a remote team, set accountability, and manage competing priorities.
  • Working knowledge of GCP, protocol compliance, sponsor expectations, and quality management principles.
  • Ability to analyze data, identify trends and risks, and lead practical process improvements.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with site teams, investigators, sponsors, CROs, and internal stakeholders.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and clinical research systems, including EDC platforms and quality management systems.

Certifications/Licenses, Education, and Experience

  • Minimum Education:
    • High school diploma or GED required; bachelor’s degree in life sciences, healthcare, clinical research, or a related field preferred.
  • Minimum Experience:
    • Five or more years of experience in clinical research, clinical data management, site coordination, or a related area required, including at least two years leading, coaching, or coordinating the work of others.
    • Experience supporting multi-site clinical research operations and sponsor-facing data activities preferred.
    • Experience reviewing, entering, reconciling, or maintaining structured data in electronic systems, spreadsheets, trackers, or databases.

description:
• Job grade: SCS Pay Band 1
  • Contract type: Permanent
  • Business area: Regions and Cities Partnerships and Delivery Directorate
  • Type of role: Senior leadership
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time, Job share, Part-time
  • Number of jobs available: 1

Location

Birmingham, Leeds or London
We particularly welcome applications from candidates based in Birmingham or Leeds. Where candidates are equally scored at the relevant stage, priority may be given to candidates based in Leeds or Birmingham over London-based candidates

About the job

Job summary

The Directorate oversees major devolved transport funding and delivery relationships at a time of significant change in how central government works with Mayors, Mayoral Strategic Authorities and local leaders. The successful candidates will need to combine delivery grip with finely tuned political judgement, and the ability to operate confidently with Ministers, senior officials, HM Treasury, No.10 North and senior local politicians to secure progress, manage risk and maintain confidence across government and places.

One postholder will focus primarily on delivery of CRSTS and TCR portfolios. The postholder will work with Strategic Authorities to agree delivery plans and investment priorities, build a shared understanding of delivery progress, risk and confidence, and provide assurance and support to help secure successful delivery and benefits realisation across devolved transport portfolios.

The second postholder will focus primarily on sponsorship of retained major infrastructure schemes within the CRSTS and TCR portfolio. A central feature of the role will be the West Yorkshire Mass Transit (WYMT) programme, which is expected to account for around 50-75% of the postholder's time. Acting as the Department's sponsor for WYMT, the postholder will work closely with West Yorkshire Combined Authority and partners to provide assurance, challenge and support as the programme progresses through business case development, approvals and delivery planning.

The Directorate's operating model continues to evolve in response to the Government's devolution agenda and ongoing organisation design work. While each role has a distinct area of emphasis, both postholders will be expected to help shape the development of the Directorate's future approach to delivery, assurance and sponsorship. Sponsorship responsibilities for retained schemes within the TCR portfolio will be shared across both roles. The precise distribution of responsibilities between the two posts may continue to evolve as the organisation design develops, and in light of the experience, strengths and interests of the successful candidates.

Candidates will be asked to indicate a preference for one role, or to be considered for either. Final appointments will take account of candidate preference, assessment evidence and business need.

Job description

Responsibilities of the role include:

  • Provide visible senior leadership across the Directorate’s delivery and sponsorship responsibilities, helping to build a strengthened, complementary delivery capability that preserves place insight, improves resilience and aligns resources to strategic priorities.
  • Build strong, trusted relationships with senior colleagues in Mayoral Strategic Authorities, local transport bodies and across government, including Ministers, senior officials, HM Treasury, No.10 North and senior local politicians, exercising support, collaboration, constructive challenge and finely judged political handling.
  • Design and operate proportionate, risk-based reporting, assurance and governance arrangements that reflect the scale, complexity, delivery risk and organisational maturity of the relevant portfolio, based on transparency and accountability for public money.
  • Drive delivery across the CRSTS and TCR portfolio, ensuring delivery plans, performance information, risks, dependencies, benefits and affordability issues are surfaced, understood and managed effectively.
  • Invest substantial time face to face with local authority and delivery body teams to strengthen understanding of delivery confidence, portfolio health and investment risk.
  • Ensure Departmental sponsorship, assurance and governance arrangements are aligned to each scheme or portfolio, balancing value for money, accountability, benefits realisation and the Government’s ambition for deeper devolution.
  • Commission expert advice and independent assurance where needed, and navigate internal Departmental, cross-government and HM Treasury approval processes.
  • Work collaboratively across the Regions, Cities and Devolution Directorate, the Department and wider government to align around effective local delivery, maximise wider benefits, inform future support and targeted interventions, and ensure public investment delivers tangible economic and social outcomes for communities.
  • For the postholder leading the Department's approach to sponsorship of retained major infrastructure schemes, dedicate a substantial proportion of time to the West Yorkshire Mass Transit programme, acting as the Department’s senior sponsor and ensuring the programme has clear governance, proportionate assurance, effective business case progression, and robust engagement with West Yorkshire Combined Authority, HM Treasury and other key partners.

Person specification

You will need to be able to show, through your application, that you have the professional skills, breadth of experience and personal qualities for this post, as well as the leadership skills to succeed at Deputy Director level in the Senior Civil Service.

  • Proven senior leadership in sponsoring, overseeing or leading complex infrastructure projects, programmes or place-based funding settlements ideally involving delivery through local authorities, Strategic Authorities or other devolved delivery arrangements. You will bring the judgement to shape proportionate oversight that reflects investment scale, delivery risk, organisational maturity and the Government’s ambition for deeper devolution [lead competency].
  • Proven leadership of high-performing teams in complex and evolving environments, including developing capability, leading through ambiguity, working effectively across organisational boundaries and contributing to wider directorate leadership.
  • Finely tuned political judgement, including direct experience of operating effectively in politically sensitive environments and navigating competing priorities involving Ministers, Mayors, senior local politicians and senior Government officials to secure delivery outcomes.
  • Outstanding stakeholder engagement, communication and influencing skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships across diverse interests, explain complex delivery issues clearly, secure alignment across organisations, provide constructive challenge and influence partner organisations without direct authority.
  • Ability to assess competing delivery, sponsorship and governance options, weighing value for money, affordability, assurance, benefits realisation and accountability in a devolved delivery context.

Desirable

  • Evidence of working with and factoring in the wider cross-government and political context for programme delivery, including aligning strategic and operational coordination across the Department, wider Government, and delivery partners to support successful delivery outcomes.

Experience of public sector funding, governance and accountability frameworks, including an understanding of Managing Public Money principles and their application within devolved delivery environments.

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £86,000, Department for Transport contributes £24,914 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

Whatever your role, we take your career and development seriously, and want to enable you to build a really successful career with the Department and wider Civil Service.

It is crucial that our employees have the right skills to develop their careers and meet the challenges ahead, and you’ll benefit from regular performance and development reviews to ensure this development is ongoing. As a Civil Service employee, you’ll be entitled to a large range of benefits.

Equality, Diversity & Inclusion

The Civil Service values and supports all its employees.

We have strong and pro-active staff networks, special leave policies for hospital appointments, reasonable adjustments put in place for those who need them, and diversity talent programmes to help everyone irrespective of background, to achieve their potential.

Pension

Your pension is a valuable part of your total reward package.

A competitive contributory pension scheme that you can enter as soon as you join where we will make a significant contribution to the cost of your pension; where your contributions come out of your salary before any tax is taken; and where your pension will continue to provide valuable benefits for you and your family if you are too ill to continue to work or die before you retire. Visit Civil Service Pension Scheme for more details. >

Generous Annual Leave and Bank Holiday Allowance

25 days annual leave on entry, increasing on a sliding scale to 30 days after 5 years’ service (allowance is pro rata for part-time employees). This is in addition to 8 public holidays.

This will be complimented by one further day paid privilege entitlement to mark the King’s Birthday.

Staff Wellbeing

Flexible working including part-time or term-time working and access to Flexible Working Schemes allowing you to vary your working day as long as you work your total hours.

Generous paid maternity and paternity leave which is notably more than the statutory minimum offered by many other employers.

Childcare benefits (policy for new employees as of 5 April 2018): The government has introduced the Tax-Free Childcare (TFC) scheme. Working parents can open an online childcare account and for every £8 they pay in, the government adds £2, up to a maximum of £2000 a year for each child or £4000 for a disabled child. Parents then use the funds to pay for registered childcare. Existing employees may be able to continue to claim childcare vouchers, so please check how the policy would work for you here. Any move to the DfT from another employer will mean you can no longer access childcare vouchers. This includes moves between government departments.

Onsite facilities Opportunity to use onsite facilities including fitness centres and staff canteens (where applicable).

Things you need to know

Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Selection process details

Application

Veredus are managing this competition on behalf of the Department for Transport. To apply, please submit the following through the Veredus website at Opportunities , Veredus quoting reference 1416 by no later 9am Monday 2nd November 2026

The application will include:

  • A CV setting out your career history, with key responsibilities and achievements. Please ensure you have provided reasons for any gaps within the last two years.
  • A Statement of Suitability (no longer than 1,000 words) explaining how you consider your personal skills, qualities and experience provide evidence of your suitability for the role, with particular reference to the criteria in the person specification.

Failure to submit both documents will mean the panel only have limited information on which to assess your application against the criteria in the person specification.

As part of the online application process, you will also be required to complete the following:

  • Diversity Monitoring Form - All monitoring data will be treated in the strictest confidence, will not be provided to the selection panel and will not affect your application in any way. If you do not wish to provide a declaration on any of the particular characteristics, you will have the option to select 'prefer not to say’ (via this link) DIVERSITY MONITORING FORM – Fill in form
  • Candidate Supporting Information Form (via this link) CANDIDATE SUPPORTING INFORMATION FORM – Fill in form

If applicable, please also download from our website, complete and submit the following forms;

  • Disability Confident Scheme Form
  • Veteran’s Scheme Form

Should you encounter any issues with your application or wish to have a confidential discussion, please contact our recruitment advisers at Veredus::

Julian.Middleton@veredus.co.uk or Laura.Spurgin@veredus.co.uk

Longlist

The panel will assess your application to select those demonstrating the best fit with the role by considering the evidence you have provided against the essential criteria set out in the ‘Person Specification’ section. Failure to address any or all of these may affect your application. ​

The timeline later in this pack indicates the date by which decisions are expected to be made, and all candidates will be advised of the outcome as soon as possible thereafter. Candidates selected for longlisting will be invited for a preliminary discussion with Laura Spurgin to further explore their skills and experience.​

Candidates applying under the Disability Confident, Redeployment or Veterans Scheme who meet the minimum selection criteria in the job specification are guaranteed an interview. Please complete the relevant parts in the application system if applying under these schemes.

Shortlist
The panel will review reports on those longlisted and will select a shortlist of candidates whose applications best demonstrate suitability for the role, by considering the evidence provided against the essential criteria set out in the Personal Specification

Assessment
If you are shortlisted you will be asked to take part in the following assessments :

  • Individual Leadership Assessment – a combination of psychometric assessments
  • Staff Engagement Exercise - a presentation and Q&A with a representative staff group from across the DfT.

These assessments will not result in a pass or fail decision. Rather, they are designed to support the panel’s decision making and highlight areas for the panel to explore further at interview.

Informal Discussions
Shortlisted candidates will have the opportunity to speak to John Hall prior to the final interview. This is an informal discussion to allow candidates to learn more about the role and is not part of the assessment process

Interview
You will be asked to attend a panel interview where you will be asked to give a presentation and then have a more in-depth discussion of your previous experience and professional competence in relation to the criteria set out in the Person Specification.

Interviews are expected to take place face to face in our London offices, SW1P 4DR.

Outcome and Feedback

Expected Timeline

If your application is successful but you have been dismissed from the Civil Service, your application could be removed at the pre-employment checking stage depending on the nature of the dismissal.

Applicants who are successful at interview will be, as part of pre-employment screening, subject to a check on the Internal Fraud Database (IFD). This check will provide information about employees who have been dismissed for fraud or dishonesty offences. This check also applies to employees who resign or otherwise leave before being dismissed for fraud or dishonesty had their employment continued. Any applicant’s details held on the IFD will be refused employment. A candidate is not eligible to apply for a role within the Civil Service if the application is made within a 5-year period following a dismissal for carrying out internal fraud against government.

All external applicants and current employees of accredited non-departmental public bodies (NDPBs) will be required to undergo a Social Media Check. A Social Media Check is a review of your publicly available online activity, typically across platforms like LinkedIn, Facebook, X (formerly Twitter), Instagram, and others. The purpose is to identify any public posts or content that could raise concerns for employers, such as:

  • Hate speech or discriminatory behaviour
  • Threats or acts of violence
  • Illegal activity or substance misuse
  • Sexually explicit material
  • Extremist views or affiliations

Importantly, this check does not involve hacking into your accounts or accessing private messages. It only considers content you have chosen to make public. Employers use this kind of screening to help ensure their workplace remains safe, inclusive, and aligned with company values. It’s not about judging your personality or lifestyle - it’s about checking for potential red flags that might affect the role or company culture. If you have questions or concerns about the social media check, we would be happy to explain in more detail what’s being looked at and how your data is handled securely and fairly.

title: Internal Controls Consulting, Experienced
description:
Your Role

The Internal Controls Advisory Services team provides objective consulting and advisory services designed to add value and assist management with establishing and maintaining an effective system of internal controls. The team helps Blue Shield of California accomplish its objectives through a systematic, disciplined approach to evaluating and improving risk management and control processes. The Internal Controls, Experienced position will report to the Principal, Internal Controls Advisory Services and will work under the guidance of senior team members to support internal controls assessments, advisory engagements, and remediation activities.

Our leadership model is about developing great leaders at all levels and creating opportunities for our people to grow – personally, professionally, and financially. We are looking for leaders that are energized by creative and critical thinking, building and sustaining high-performing teams, getting results the right way, and fostering continuous learning.

Your Work

In this role, you will:

  • Demonstrate professionalism, objectivity, and integrity in completing assigned work, and escalate issues to senior team members as appropriate
  • Support assigned phases of healthcare operational process assessments under the direction of the Principal, including planning support, walkthroughs, fieldwork, control testing, and finding validation
  • Execute and document control testing using established test procedures and the COSO framework, and help document various documents such as process flows, risk and control matrices (RCMs)
  • Review policies, procedures, and supporting evidence against established requirements, and raise potential gaps or improvement opportunities to the engagement team
  • Assist in identifying root causes of findings and drafting recommendations for review by senior team members
  • Prepare accurate, well-organized workpapers, status trackers, and draft deliverables in line with team standards
  • Request and track documentation from process owners, and follow up on open items to keep assigned work on schedule
  • Assist with internal and external audit requests by gathering supporting documentation and tracking responses
  • Track remediation activities and review supporting evidence for completed corrective actions, escalating delays or concerns to senior team members
  • Coordinate meetings with business partners and stakeholders, including scheduling, preparing supporting materials, tracking follow-up items, and facilitating timely completion of requested activities.
  • Gather, organize, and validate data and information used in executive and leadership reporting, working with appropriate stakeholders to resolve questions, discrepancies, and incomplete information.
  • Reconcile supporting details and data across source information, status trackers, and reporting materials to help ensure executive reporting is accurate, complete, and consistent.
  • Assist in preparing recurring and ad hoc executive reporting by consolidating updates, validating supporting information, and maintaining reporting documentation.
  • Participate in internal controls training, knowledge sharing, special projects, and team initiatives as assigned

Your Knowledge and Experience

  • Requires a Bachelor’s degree or High School Diploma/GED and 4 years of additional relevant experience in lieu of a degree
  • Requires a minimum of 3 years of prior relevant experience in internal audit, internal controls, risk advisory, compliance, SOX, or a related field
  • Working knowledge of internal controls, risk assessment, process documentation, and control testing
  • Ability to analyze information, identify issues, and communicate observations clearly and professionally
  • Strong organization and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple assignments and meet deadlines
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with team members and business partners in a dynamic, hybrid environment
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint
  • CPA, CIA, CISA, or progress toward a relevant certification preferred
  • Experience in the health insurance or healthcare industry preferred

Hybrid

This role requires employees to be in-office based on our hybrid workplace model, balancing purposeful in-person collaboration with flexibility. For most teams, this means coming into the office two days each week. Employees living more than 50 miles from an office location will work with their manager to determine in-office time based on business need.

About the job

Job summary

Academi Wales is transitioning to Arwain - Wales National School for Government, supporting the development of confident, capable and connected leaders across One Welsh Public Service. Through leadership programmes, conferences, schools, coaching, board development and collaborative learning, Arwain brings together public service leaders from across Wales to improve outcomes for citizens and communities.

The Leadership Engagement and Events Teams are responsible for planning and delivering leadership training and a portfolio of high-profile national events and leadership programmes, including Summer School, Winter School, board leadership events, conferences, leadership forums and development programmes.

The Leadership Engagement and Events Officers will play a pivotal role in the planning, coordination and delivery of leadership events and learning programmes across Wales.

Job description

Working as part of a small and agile team, postholders will ensure events are professionally organised, accessible, bilingual and customer-focused, providing an excellent participant experience from initial enquiry through to post-event evaluation.

The role combines event management, stakeholder engagement, customer service, financial administration and operational delivery.

We are actively seeking leadership engagement and event specialists, with an ability to contribute effectively within a high performing team. You will be involved in designing, developing and delivering engagement activities (online and in person) which will support leaders to develop in a range of leadership and development models, programmes and workshops. The successful candidates will be expected to work across Wales; this will include overnight stays.

The ideal candidate will be enthusiastic, self-motivated, innovative and creative, with the ability to inspire leaders from diverse backgrounds to develop through our engagement activities and events. They will be an excellent communicator who can multitask in a dynamic environment with changing demands, including finance and procurement, application processing and sifting, developing literature and online resources, communications and marketing. They will need to be both proactive and responsive before, during and after engagement activities and events, determining what support is needed in the moment. They will also provide feedback and insights to the wider Academi Wales team to inform future business planning.

Person specification

Postholders will undertake a range of the responsibilities below, depending on the requirements of the team to which they are assigned. They may not be responsible for every task listed, but priorities can change according to business needs:

  • Coordinate the end-to-end delivery of multiple leadership events, conferences, programmes and engagement activities simultaneously.
  • Manage event logistics, including venues, digital platforms, accessibility requirements and supplier arrangements.
  • Support the design and delivery of impactful leadership events for diverse audience groups across the Welsh public service and third sector.
  • Develop and coordinate event literature, promotional materials and participant information that is accurate, accessible and bilingual.
  • Contribute to service improvements, new initiatives and more effective ways of working.

Stakeholder and Partner Engagement

  • Build and maintain effective relationships with public service organisations, partners, facilitators and suppliers.
  • Promote events and engagement opportunities to maximise participation and impact.
  • Act as a key contact for stakeholder enquiries, providing professional and timely support.
  • Support marketing and engagement campaigns to increase awareness of leadership development opportunities.

Programme Coordination, Administration and Financial Management

  • Deliver efficient administrative support for leadership events and engagement activities, including liaising with suppliers and contractors to ensure services are delivered effectively.
  • Maintain accurate records, databases and booking systems
  • Coordinate meetings, prepare documentation and support programme governance activities.
  • Liaise with the business team to process purchase orders, invoices and payments in accordance with organisational procedures, monitoring event expenditure and supporting value-for-money delivery.
  • Ensure collection of participant and stakeholder feedback to measure event effectiveness, to support continuous improvement and future planning.

Network Development

  • Build stakeholder and participant networks with partners to strengthen engagement across the Welsh public service and third sector.
  • Support the development of leadership networks and alumni engagement activities collaborating with Customer Insights.
  • Facilitate opportunities for collaboration, knowledge sharing and peer learning across sectors.

About the job

Job summary

The Social Housing Quality and Residents division leads on work to improve the quality of social homes and landlord services, and to empower residents to have a strong voice and hold their landlord to account. The division sponsors the Housing Ombudsman Service and also manages a Resident Panel through which residents engage directly with officials and Ministers. We are recruiting two SEOs to deliver this work. The first position will be for the guidance lead of the Decent Homes Standard. The Decent Homes Standard is being updated to reflect modern expectations of the minimum standard of rented housing. We are looking for a high-performing, autonomous, and well-organised individual to oversee inputs into this publication. They will also be responsible for the policy development and drafting of specific elements. This will be a stretching role working on a ministerial priority that will materially impact both the lives of renters and the ability of landlords to deliver good quality homes.

The second position is for a Senior Policy Advisor focused on energy efficiency in the social rented sector. This is a rewarding role which will involve leading the development of guidance to support social housing providers make homes cheaper to heat, more comfortable and less susceptible to damp and mould. The Government has published new Minimum Energy Efficiency Standards (MEES), setting long term ambitions to make homes warmer and cheaper to heat with lower carbon emissions. This will form part of an updated Decent Homes Standard (DHS).

Social housing providers will only have a few years to bring more than a million homes up to the new standard and they urgently need advice about how to meet it, what government ambitions mean in practice, where homes will be exempt from parts of the standard and how it will be enforced. This will help landlords to begin work on improving their stock more quickly develop investment plans for the next decade. You will need to work quickly to develop a package in tandem with social housing providers and other housing stakeholders, working closely with DESNZ and other teams across MHCLG.

Job description


Key Responsibilities

Decent Homes Standard Guidance Lead


  • Act as the primary owner of the Decent Homes Standard guidance, ensuring the delivery of a high-quality product that enables landlords to provide better quality social housing with greater certainty and consistency.
  • Lead the coordination and management of contributions from internal and external stakeholders, ensuring the guidance reflects the latest policy thinking, evidence and expertise from across government and the housing sector.
  • Monitor progress against delivery plans, identifying risks and issues early and taking action to keep development on track.
  • Lead the drafting of key sections of guidance that will help shape housing standards across England and support the effective implementation of future regulatory requirements.

Social Housing Energy Efficiency Lead

  • Lead the implementation of policy relating to Minimum Energy Efficiency Standards (MEES) within the social rented sector, developing guidance and supporting materials that provide clear and practical advice to social housing providers.
  • Develop and refine policy positions on complex and cross-cutting issues, drawing on evidence and stakeholder engagement to address implementation challenges and support informed decision-making.
  • Work collaboratively with colleagues across MHCLG, the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ), and the Regulator of Social Housing to ensure policy proposals are aligned, deliverable and achieve intended outcomes.
  • Build strong relationships with stakeholders across government and the housing sector to support the successful implementation of energy efficiency improvements in social housing.

Responsibilities for Both Roles

  • Prepare high-quality briefing and advice for Ministers and senior officials, clearly setting out options, risks and recommendations, and drawing together complex and sometimes conflicting evidence.
  • Build and maintain effective relationships with a wide range of internal and external stakeholders to support policy development and delivery.
  • Work at pace to deliver high-profile ministerial priorities while managing competing demands and tight deadlines.
  • Contribute positively to the culture and performance of the team, supporting continuous improvement and undertaking corporate responsibilities to help maintain a collaborative, inclusive and high-performing working environment.



Person specification

We are looking for individuals who can demonstrate strong policy, project management and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to deliver high-quality outcomes in a fast-paced and high-profile environment. This is a policy area that attracts ministerial interest and as such the post holder may need to respond to changing priorities.

Successful candidates will be organised, adaptable and collaborative, with the confidence to lead complex pieces of work and build effective relationships across a wide range of stakeholders.

Essential Criteria

  • Strong organisational and project management skills, with the ability to coordinate and deliver complex work involving multiple stakeholders, priorities and competing deadlines.
  • Experience of policy development and analysis, with the ability to interpret evidence, assess options and develop practical solutions to complex challenges.
  • Strong leadership and influencing skills, including the ability to work independently and engage effectively with senior stakeholders, building productive relationships across organisational boundaries to deliver shared objectives.
  • Excellent written communication skills, with the ability to synthesise detailed and sometimes conflicting information into clear, concise and compelling briefings, guidance and advice for a range of audiences.
  • Strong strategic thinking skills, with the ability to understand how individual policy decisions interact with wider government priorities, objectives and delivery considerations.
  • Knowledge of or experience working in housing policy, energy efficiency, or a related policy area.
  • Experience of working with external stakeholders, regulators or delivery partners to support policy development and implementation.

description:

The Nelson Poynter Memorial Library is an active partner in the teaching, research, and learning of the University of South Florida St. Petersburg’s students, faculty, and staff. We promote student-centered learning and research in an inviting, creative, and collaborative environment.

Position Summary

The Student Assistant’s primary job function is to provide front desk coverage and library support. The student assistant may be asked to assist staff with patron counts and other general duties in support of the overall operation of the campus library. This position reports to the USF St Petersburg campus library Manager, Library Operations, Access Services.

  • Provide front desk information support: answers questions about library and campus; helps patrons search the online catalog, locates and checks-out materials, study room keys and accessories; sorts and shelves library materials.
  • Must be consistently reliable to cover assigned desk shift
  • Provides excellent customer service to the USF community and library patrons, both in-person and by telephone.
  • Educates users about library services and policies when appropriate
  • Refers users’ questions to appropriate department or staff
  • Learns Library Classification system, Library of Congress and Dewey.

  • Other duties as assigned

Minimum Qualifications

  • This position requires a high school diploma.

  • Enrolled in minimum 1 credit hour at USF

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience providing excellent customer service, preferably in a library environment

  • Experience with MS Office products

  • Ability to work independently after initial training

  • Flexibility to adapt to new technologies, workflows, and emerging service models

  • Able to sit & stand for extended periods. Ability to lift up to 25 lbs. and push up to 50 lbs.

The University of South Florida is a top-ranked research university serving approximately 50,000 students from across the globe at campuses in Tampa, St. Petersburg and USF Health. In 2025, U.S. News & World Report recognized USF with its highest overall ranking in university history, as a top 50 public university for the seventh consecutive year and as one of the top 15 best values among all public universities in the nation. U.S. News also ranks the USF Health Morsani College of Medicine in the highest tier, placing it as one of the top 16 medical schools in the nation and inside the top 10 among public universities. USF is a member of the Association of American Universities (AAU), a group that includes only the top 3% of universities in the U.S. With an all-time high of $750 million in research funding in 2025 and as a top 20 public university for producing U.S. patents, USF uses innovation to transform lives and shape a better future. About the job

Job summary

Can you help shape how one of the UK's largest organisations adopts AI responsibly, effectively and at scale?

Do you have the vision to combine behavioural science, user insight and evaluation to influence the future of work across the Department for Transport?

If so, we’d love to hear from you!

The Head of Human Centred AI formulates and leads a high-impact programme to provide evidence and insight into how AI can be effectively and responsibly developed and deployed across DfT. They lead a team to design and implement social, behavioural and user research projects aligned to departmental priorities, collaborating with colleagues within DfT, across government and with external partners.

ivotal role in the delivery of AI in DfT, applying their skills and insights to shape the portfolio of work and identify opportunities. They apply rigorous and innovative social and behavioural science methodologies to aid the development and deployment of AI.

Job description

Our aim is for DfT to be a leading department in the use of AI. We want to expand our reach across the Department, its agencies and delivery bodies, and make better use of the full spectrum of data science techniques and advances in AI to realise the ambition set out by our Secretary of State in the Transport AI Action Plan.

Your responsibilities will include, but aren’t limited to:

        • Designing and leading a behavioural science, social and user research programme to support the safe and effective adoption of AI across the department.
        • Leading the Evaluation programme, on the effectiveness, impact and value of AI tools using mixed-method approaches to assess impacts on quality, time-saving and user satisfaction.
        • Applying research findings and insight to shape the design and delivery of AI projects, including identifying opportunities, supporting the design and evaluation of training and communication activities, and advocating for the user perspective.
        • Working closely with the AI & data science teams, HR and other colleagues to inform organisational readiness for AI, aligning social and behavioural evidence with training, change management and workforce strategy.
        • Developing and maintaining a knowledge base of AI-related social and behavioural research and evaluation evidence to inform ongoing decision-making.
        • Acting as an ambassador for social and behavioural science and evaluation in AI across the department, government and external networks.
        • Developing research collaborations within DfT, other government departments and academia.
        • Building and sustaining positive relationships with senior stakeholders, demonstrating the value of user-centred and evidence-led decision-making.
        • Drive standards of research quality, inclusivity and ethical practice, offering mentorship and hands-on support to ensure high performance within your team.
        • Lead the Social and Behavioural Science and Evaluation for AI function in collaboration with peers across GSR and other professions to grow and embed capability and foster a culture of innovation and continuous improvement.

About the job

Job summary

The Office for National Statistics (ONS) is the UK’s largest producer of official statistics, covering a range of key economic, social and demographic topics. These include measuring changes in the value of the UK economy, estimating the size, geographic distribution and characteristics of the population, and providing indicators of price inflation, employment, earnings, crime and migration.

The Reward team sits within the People and Places Directorate (PPD) and provides strategic leadership, specialist advice and high-quality delivery across delegated pay, Senior Civil Service pay, reward and recognition, allowances and related policy. The team works closely with Finance, Pay Unit, HR Business Partners, trade unions, People Analytics and leaders across ONS, as well as Cabinet Office, HM Treasury and pay professionals across government.

Job description

This is a strategic leadership role responsible for shaping how pay, reward and recognition support ONS to attract, retain and motivate the workforce it needs. The postholder will lead implementation of the ONS Pay Strategy, own its ongoing development and bring forward evidence-based recommendations that respond to organisational priorities, workforce risks and emerging government policy.

You will combine strong pay and reward expertise with strategic thinking, political awareness and the ability to lead change. As ONS’s lead professional for pay and reward, you will provide trusted advice and recommendations to senior leaders, establish influential relationships across government and lead engagement and negotiations with trade unions. You will use workforce analytics, external insight and professional judgement to help shape a deliberate, targeted and evidence-led approach to pay and reward.

Alongside this strategic focus, you will ensure the Reward team delivers high-quality annual pay activity, policy advice, reward and recognition services and governance. You will lead through the team, setting direction and maintaining responsibility for the quality and impact of its delivery.

Key Responsibilities

Pay Strategy and Organisational Outcomes

  • Lead implementation of the ONS Pay Strategy and own its ongoing evolution, ensuring pay, reward and recognition remain aligned with organisational priorities and workforce needs.
  • Translate recruitment, retention, skills and pay competitiveness challenges into clear strategic options and recommendations for senior leaders.
  • Lead the development of future pay proposals, including annual pay approaches and potential flexibility initiatives, ensuring recommendations reflect workforce needs, business priorities and wider Civil Service requirements.
  • Challenge existing arrangements constructively, testing whether pay and reward interventions remain fair, effective and proportionate and whether they are delivering the intended impact.
  • Lead the team in delivering pay and reward initiatives, remaining responsible for successful implementation and embedding while drawing on wider organisational expertise and support.

Strategic Advice, Evidence and Governance

  • Provide clear, balanced and evidence-based pay and reward advice and recommendations to senior leaders and decision-making forums, including the HR Leadership Team and Remuneration Committee, and contribute to advice and recommendations for ExCo and People Committee.
  • Bring together pay, recruitment, retention, workforce, skills and market evidence to improve the quality of strategic decisions and business cases.
  • Present complex policy, evidence, risks, constraints and trade-offs in a clear and compelling way, with practical recommendations for senior and non-specialist audiences.
  • Ensure appropriate governance, assurance, equality consideration and evaluation are built into pay and reward decisions and initiatives.

Relationships, Influence and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with Cabinet Office, HM Treasury and Heads of Pay across other government departments, representing ONS and bringing relevant policy developments, insight and best practice back into the organisation.
  • Lead the Reward team’s contribution to engagement, consultation and negotiations with departmental trade unions, building constructive relationships and providing the specialist pay expertise needed to navigate challenging issues and competing priorities.
  • Build effective partnerships across ONS so that pay and reward decisions bring together business priorities, workforce evidence, policy expertise, robust modelling and financial implications, while recognising Finance’s accountability for affordability.
  • Navigate the wider Civil Service policy and political environment, anticipating implications for ONS and shaping timely, credible responses.

Leadership and Delivery through the Team

  • Act as a senior leader within PPD and ONS, demonstrating collective leadership, contributing to directorate and corporate priorities, and working collaboratively across teams to deliver organisational outcomes and the wider People Plan.
  • Set a clear strategic direction for the Reward team, translating priorities into deliverable plans and focusing resources on the highest-value outcomes.
  • Ensure effective delivery of delegated and Senior Civil Service pay activity, reward and recognition, allowances, pay policy, pay gap reporting and associated governance in line with relevant frameworks.
  • Lead, develop and empower a high-performing specialist team, building capability, professional standards, resilience and accountability for delivery.
  • Maintain oversight of operational performance, delivery risks and dependencies, intervening or escalating where required.
  • Foster an inclusive, collaborative and continuous-improvement culture in which evidence, learning and constructive challenge are valued.
